children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 1.1]

children.text: jayati sa dainyagadākulam akhilam idaṃ paśyato jagad yasya /
children.translated_text: Victorious is He who, seeing this entire world afflicted by the disease of wretchedness,

children.text: hṛdayasthaiva galitvā jātā rasarūpiṇī karuṇā // GRht_1.1 //
children.translated_text: whose compassion, in the form of <s>rasa</s> (mercury/essence), arose by melting [with sympathy] while remaining in His heart. // GRht 1.1 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Obeisance to the glorious great Lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>)!
Having bowed to Him who is skilled in protecting from the fear of worldly existence, [the commentator] composes the <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s> —
a commentary on the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>, well-applied, proceeding with straightforward meaning, [composed by] the trustworthy one. // GRhtCM 1.1:1 //
In the family of <s>Guṇavāridhi</s> (ocean of virtues), [there was] <s>Harihara Miśra</s>, renowned for his established greatness;

children.text: tatputro bhuvi mahito maheśa iti nāmavikhyātaḥ // GRhtCM_1.1:2 //
children.translated_text: his son, honored on earth, was famous by the name <s>Maheśa</s>. // GRhtCM 1.1:2 //
In that lineage, endowed with the spirit of <s>Bhāratī</s> (the goddess of speech), his son, the master, [speaks] with accomplished words,
<s>Caturbhuja</s>, whose mind contemplates realized states, by virtue of the distinction of the family into which he was born. // GRhtCM 1.1:3 //

children.text: jyeṣṭho'bhūd bhuvi pārijātakataruḥ khaṇḍelavālānvaye tatputraḥ kila nāthaballavasudaḥ prāṇair yaśo'rthānvitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The eldest was like the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree on earth, in the <s>Khaṇḍelavāla</s> lineage; his son, indeed, was <s>Nāthaballa</s>, the giver of wealth, endowed with life, fame, and purpose.

children.text: tatputreṇa ca sāvareṇa patinā bandhasya dharmārthinā gīrvāṇāśu rugoñcajena satataṃ tenātra yatnaḥ kṛtaḥ // GRhtCM_1.1:4 //
children.translated_text: By his son <s>Sāvare</s>, a master seeking <s>dharma</s> and the goals [of life], effort was constantly made here, with <s>Rugoñcaja</s> [?] serving the divine ones swiftly. // GRhtCM 1.1:4 //

children.text: iha śāstrārambhe ācāryaśrīmadgovindapādāḥ śiṣṭasamayaparipālanārthe śāstrasya deśayato gurupādasya bhagavato vastunirdeśarūpaṃ maṅgalam ācaranti jayatītyādi // GRhtCM_1.1:5 //
children.translated_text: Here, at the commencement of the treatise, the <s>Ācārya</s>, the illustrious <s>Govindapāda</s>, in order to maintain the convention of the learned, performs an auspicious invocation (<s>maṅgala</s>) in the form of indication of the subject matter (<s>vastunirdeśa</s>), [as befitting] the blessed <s>guru</s> who teaches the treatise — [beginning with] '<s>jayati</s>' ('is victorious') and so forth. // GRhtCM 1.1:5 //

children.text: maṅgalalakṣaṇaṃ yathā āśīr namaskriyā vastunirdeśo maṅgala iti // GRhtCM_1.1:6 //
children.translated_text: The definition of <s>maṅgala</s> (auspicious invocation) is: a benediction (<s>āśīḥ</s>), an act of obeisance (<s>namaskriyā</s>), or an indication of the subject matter (<s>vastunirdeśa</s>) — these are [the forms of] <s>maṅgala</s>. // GRhtCM 1.1:6 //

children.text: vastunirdeśaḥ pañcadhā yathāsti bhāti priyaṃ rūpaṃ nāma cetyaṃśapañcakam // GRhtCM_1.1:7 //
children.translated_text: The indication of the subject matter (<s>vastunirdeśa</s>) is fivefold: existence (<s>asti</s>), consciousness (<s>bhāti</s>), dearness (<s>priyam</s>), form (<s>rūpam</s>), and name (<s>nāma</s>) — these are the five aspects. // GRhtCM 1.1:7 //

children.text: ādyaṃ trayaṃ brahmarūpaṃ śaktirūpaṃ tato dvayam iti // GRhtCM_1.1:8 //
children.translated_text: The first three are of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>; the latter two are of the nature of <s>Śakti</s> (power). // GRhtCM 1.1:8 //

children.text: sa haro jayati sarvotkarṣeṇa vartate // GRhtCM_1.1:9 //
children.translated_text: 'He' — <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) — '<s>jayati</s>' — exists with supreme excellence. // GRhtCM 1.1:9 //

children.text: akhilaṃ jagat paśyata iti vastunirdeśābjayaddraṣṭā // GRhtCM_1.1:10 //
children.translated_text: 'Seeing the entire world' — by the indication of the subject, the victor is the seer. // GRhtCM 1.1:10 //

children.text: tathā ca śrutiḥ apāṇipādo javano grahītā // GRhtCM_1.1:11 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic scripture) [says]: 'Without hands and feet, He grasps and moves swiftly.' // GRhtCM 1.1:11 //
'He sees without eyes, He hears without ears;

children.text: sa vetti vedyaṃ na ca tasya vettā tamāhur agryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam iti // GRhtCM_1.1:12 //
children.translated_text: He knows all that is to be known, but none knows Him — Him they call the foremost, the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person).' // GRhtCM 1.1:12 //

children.text: yasya hṛdayasyaiva rasarūpiṇī karuṇā ghṛṇā jātā prādurbhūtā // GRhtCM_1.1:13 //
children.translated_text: 'Whose' — from whose heart alone, compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) in the form of <s>rasa</s> (mercury/essence) arose, was born. // GRhtCM 1.1:13 //

children.text: kiṃbhūtvā galitvādravitvā galitasya sthānāccyutir iti yuktam // GRhtCM_1.1:14 //
children.translated_text: In what manner? 'By melting' (<s>galitvā</s>) — by becoming liquid; 'melting' means falling from one's [original] place — this is appropriate. // GRhtCM 1.1:14 //
This [compassion] remains 'in the heart itself.' // GRhtCM 1.1:15 //
The word '<s>eva</s>' (itself/alone) is an indeclinable that negates [residence in] another place. // GRhtCM 1.1:16 //

children.text: rasarūpiṇīti rasaḥ pāradastatsvarūpaṃ yasyāḥ sā // GRhtCM_1.1:17 //
children.translated_text: 'In the form of <s>rasa</s>' — <s>rasa</s> means mercury (<s>pārada</s>); that which has this as its essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>). // GRhtCM 1.1:17 //
And the [lexical] statement [is]:

children.text: raso jalaṃ raso harṣo rasaḥ śṛṅgārapūrvakaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Rasa</s>' means water, '<s>rasa</s>' means joy, '<s>rasa</s>' means the erotic sentiment and its predecessors,

children.text: svādvādiṣu ca niryāse pārade'pi raso viṣe /
children.translated_text: and in [the context of] sweet tastes and the like, in extracts, in mercury, and in poison — '<s>rasa</s>' [has these meanings].
Thus it is a word of many meanings. // GRhtCM 1.1:18 //

children.text: sāmānyatastadrūpaṃ dravatvaṃ viśeṣato rasarūpaṃ sarvopakāritvam // GRhtCM_1.1:19 //
children.translated_text: In general, its nature is fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>); specifically, the nature of <s>rasa</s> is its capacity to benefit all. // GRhtCM 1.1:19 //
And the statement in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:
'The sole fire for burning away sins committed since birth; having the form of a lion [that destroys] the elephant of the suffering of poverty.' // GRhtCM 1.1:20 //

children.text: kiṃbhūtasya harasya dainyagadākulaṃ jagat saṃsāraṃ paśyataḥ dainyayaṃ ca gadāśca tair ākulaṃ vyāptaṃ dainyaṃ dīnabhāvo dāridryaṃ gadā vyādhaya iti // GRhtCM_1.1:21 //
children.translated_text: 'Of what nature is <s>Hara</s> (Śiva/mercury)? — seeing the world, the cycle of existence, afflicted by wretchedness and disease (<s>dainya-gada-ākulam</s>). <s>Dainya</s> means the state of being wretched, poverty; <s>gadāḥ</s> means diseases.' // GRhtCM 1.1:21 //
'<s>Akhilam</s>' (entire) is a word meaning 'all-pervading.' // GRhtCM 1.1:22 //
As stated by [the author of] the <s>Mañjarī</s>:

children.text: yasya rogasya yo yogastenaiva saha dāpayet /
children.translated_text: 'For whatever disease, whatever preparation [is appropriate] — one should administer it along with that [preparation].
<s>Rasendra</s> (mercury, the king of essences) removes the diseases of men, elephants, and horses.' // GRhtCM 1.1:23 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 1.1:24 //
And another opinion:
'Without the <s>bhasma</s> (calcinated ash) of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), the procedure of the <s>saṃhitā</s> (compendium) is described;
even what is not explicitly stated should be understood in the relevant contexts for the pacification of [disease in specific] body parts.' // GRhtCM 1.1:25 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 1.1:26 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 1.2]
Wearing a yellow garment, conqueror of <s>Bali</s>, destroyer of serpents, of intense passion, riding <s>Garuḍa</s> —

children.text: jayati sa haririva harajo vidalitabhavadainyaduḥkhabharaḥ // GRht_1.2 //
children.translated_text: victorious is that <s>Haraja</s> (born from Hara/mercury), like <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) Himself, who has shattered the burden of the wretchedness and suffering of worldly existence. // GRht 1.2 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
'<s>Pīta</s>-' and so forth. // GRhtCM 1.2:1 //

children.text: anena padyena kavirharajasya hareśca samatvaṃ sūcayati // GRhtCM_1.2:2 //
children.translated_text: By this verse, the poet indicates the equivalence of <s>Haraja</s> (mercury/son of Śiva) and <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu). // GRhtCM 1.2:2 //

children.text: sa purāṇakavivarṇito harajo jayati sarvotkarṣeṇa vartate harādīśvarājjāto harajaḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:3 //
children.translated_text: That <s>Haraja</s>, described by the ancient poet, is victorious, existing with supreme excellence. '<s>Haraja</s>' — born from <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), the lord of lords. // GRhtCM 1.2:3 //

children.text: sa utprekṣyate haririva viṣṇur iva // GRhtCM_1.2:4 //
children.translated_text: He is figuratively compared (<s>utprekṣyate</s>) to <s>Hari</s>, i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // GRhtCM 1.2:4 //

children.text: kiṃbhūto hariḥ pītāmbaraḥ pīte ambare vastre yasya saḥ dukūlayugmatvāt // GRhtCM_1.2:5 //
children.translated_text: Of what nature is <s>Hari</s>? '<s>Pītāmbara</s>' — He whose garment (<s>ambara</s>) is yellow (<s>pīta</s>); because of [His wearing] a pair of silk garments. // GRhtCM 1.2:5 //

children.text: punaḥ kimbhūto balijit baliṃ balināmānaṃ daityaviśeṣaṃ jayatīti tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:6 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what nature? '<s>Balijit</s>' — He who conquers <s>Bali</s>, the specific demon named <s>Bali</s>; He is so called. // GRhtCM 1.2:6 //

children.text: punaḥ kiṃbhūtaḥ nāgakṣayetyādi nāgānāṃ śeṣādīnāṃ kṣayāya nāśāya bahalarāgo bahuprīto yo 'sau garuḍaḥ khageśvaraḥ tatra carati gacchati tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:7 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what nature? '<s>Nāgakṣaya</s>-' etc. — He who has great affection (<s>bahalarāga</s>) for the destruction (<s>kṣaya</s>) of <s>nāgas</s> (serpents) such as <s>Śeṣa</s> and others, that <s>Garuḍa</s>, the lord of birds — He moves (<s>carati</s>) upon him; He is so called. // GRhtCM 1.2:7 //

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ vidalitetyādiḥ viśeṣaṇena dalito dūrīkṛto bhavasya saṃsārasya duḥkhabharo yena saḥ dainyaṃ dāridryaṃ duḥkhaṃ vyādhirūpaṃ tayorbharo bāhulyam iti // GRhtCM_1.2:8 //
children.translated_text: Further, possessing what quality? 'Having shattered (<s>vidalita</s>)' — by the qualifier, 'shattered' means 'removed'; '<s>bhava</s>' means worldly existence (<s>saṃsāra</s>); the 'burden of suffering' — <s>dainya</s> means poverty, <s>duḥkha</s> means disease-form [of suffering]; '<s>bhara</s>' means their abundance. // GRhtCM 1.2:8 //

children.text: adhunā harajaṃ viśeṣayati kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ pītāmbaraḥ pītāmbaraḥ pūrvārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:9 //
children.translated_text: Now [the commentary] qualifies <s>Haraja</s> (mercury): Of what quality? '<s>Pītāmbara</s>' — yellow-clad; the meaning is as before. // GRhtCM 1.2:9 //

children.text: kathaṃ yuktaḥ tamarthe spaṣṭayatyanena sūtarājenāpi catvāri vāsāṃsi dhṛtāni viprādivarṇabhedāt // GRhtCM_1.2:10 //
children.translated_text: How is this appropriate? To clarify this meaning: Even by the king of mercury (<s>sūtarāja</s>), four garments are worn, according to the distinction of <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and other castes. // GRhtCM 1.2:10 //
As in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:
'White, red, yellow, and black are the mercuries [corresponding to] <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the [other castes].' // GRhtCM 1.2:11 //

children.text: brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrāḥ śvetaraktapītakṛṣṇavastradhāriṇo jñātavyāḥ na tv eṣāṃ svarūpam iti // GRhtCM_1.2:12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s> [varieties of mercury] should be known as wearing white, red, yellow, and black garments [respectively]; but this is not their intrinsic nature. // GRhtCM 1.2:12 //
As in the <s>Rasamañjarī</s>:

children.text: antaḥ sunīlo bahirujjvalo yo madhyāhnasūryapratimaprakāśaḥ iti // GRhtCM_1.2:13 //
children.translated_text: 'Internally dark-blue, externally brilliant, with a luster like the midday sun.' // GRhtCM 1.2:13 //
'Internally' refers to its intrinsic nature; 'externally' to its coverings — this is the tradition. // GRhtCM 1.2:14 //
'<s>Atha</s>' (now) is used in the sense of aggregation. // GRhtCM 1.2:15 //
'<s>Atha</s>' is used in [the senses of] auspiciousness, [introducing] what follows, commencement, question, time, one's own qualification, assertion, and aggregation. // GRhtCM 1.2:16 //

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ balijit balīn jayatīti baliścarma jarākṛtam // GRhtCM_1.2:17 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what quality? '<s>Balijit</s>' — he who conquers <s>bali</s>; and <s>bali</s> [also means] wrinkled skin [caused by] old age. // GRhtCM 1.2:17 //
Thus it is a word of many meanings. // GRhtCM 1.2:18 //

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ nāgakṣayetyādi nā puṃsvarūpaḥ punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ gamyate 'neneti gaḥ pakṣayor gaḥ gakṣaye pakṣanāśe sati bahalarāgo bahurāgavān yaḥ sa rasaḥ tena garuḍa iva cāryate iti // GRhtCM_1.2:19 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what quality? '<s>Nāgakṣaya</s>-' etc. — '<s>nā</s>' means the man-form [of mercury]; further, of what quality? '<s>ga</s>' — that by which one goes; in the pair of wings (<s>pakṣa</s>), '<s>ga</s>' [means wing]; when the wings (<s>pakṣa</s>) are destroyed (<s>kṣaya</s>), [mercury] having intense color (<s>bahularāga</s>), that is <s>rasa</s> (mercury); by it, [mercury] moves like <s>Garuḍa</s>. // GRhtCM 1.2:19 //

children.text: kiṃ pāradaḥ pakṣanāśe sati ākāśagamanaṃ dadātīti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:20 //
children.translated_text: Does mercury, when its wings are destroyed, grant the power of flying through the sky? — this is the intended meaning. // GRhtCM 1.2:20 //
As in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:
'When killed, it kills old age and death; when calcined (<s>mūrchita</s>), it destroys diseases;

children.text: datte ca khe gatiṃ baddhaḥ ko 'nyaḥ sūtāt kriyākaraḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:21 //
children.translated_text: when bound, it grants movement through the sky — who else but mercury (<s>sūta</s>) is such an agent of [these] actions?' // GRhtCM 1.2:21 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 1.2:22 //

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ vidalitetyādiḥ pūrvārthaḥ karuṇāparatvena dainyaduḥkhahāritvaṃ sūcayati // GRhtCM_1.2:23 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what quality? 'Having shattered' etc. — the meaning is as before; by [its quality of] being supreme in compassion, it indicates the removal of wretchedness and suffering. // GRhtCM 1.2:23 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 1.3]

children.text: mūrchitvā harati rujaṃ bandhanamanubhūya muktido bhavati /
children.translated_text: Having been calcined (<s>mūrchita</s>), it removes disease; having undergone binding (<s>bandhana</s>), it becomes the giver of liberation (<s>mukti</s>);

children.text: amarīkaroti sumṛtaḥ ko 'nyaḥ karuṇākaraḥ sūtāt // GRht_1.3 //
children.translated_text: when well-killed (<s>sumṛta</s>), it makes one immortal (<s>amara</s>) — who else but mercury (<s>sūta</s>) is so compassionate? // GRht 1.3 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: yaḥ pūrvaviśiṣṭo harajas tasmādanyaḥ karuṇāparo dayāvān kaḥ na ko 'pi yato rujaṃ śarīravyathāṃ harati // GRhtCM_1.3:1 //
children.translated_text: Other than the previously described <s>Haraja</s> (mercury), who is so compassionate (<s>karuṇāpara</s>), so full of mercy? No one. Because it removes bodily affliction (<s>ruja</s>). // GRhtCM 1.3:1 //
In what manner? 'Having been calcined (<s>mūrchitvā</s>)' — having become <s>mūrchita</s> (calcined/solidified). // GRhtCM 1.3:2 //
The definition of <s>mūrchita</s> (calcination) in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:
'When mercury (<s>sūta</s>), abandoning its dense restlessness,

children.text: dṛśyate 'sau tadā jñeyo mūrchitaḥ sūtarāḍbudhaiḥ // GRhtCM_1.3:3 //
children.translated_text: appears like <s>kajjala</s> (lampblack), then it should be known by the wise as <s>mūrchita</s> (calcined), the king of mercuries.' // GRhtCM 1.3:3 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 1.3:4 //

children.text: punarbandhanamanubhūya dhṛtvā muktido bhavati muktiṃ dadātīti // GRhtCM_1.3:5 //
children.translated_text: Further, 'having undergone binding' (<s>bandhana</s>) — having been held [in a fixed state], it becomes the giver of <s>mukti</s> (liberation), i.e., it gives liberation. // GRhtCM 1.3:5 //

<s>Mukti</s> (liberation) is described as fourfold: by the distinction of <s>sālokya</s> (dwelling in the same world), <s>sārūpya</s> (having the same form), <s>sāmīpya</s> (proximity), and <s>sāyujya</s> (union). // GRhtCM 1.3:6 //

children.text: bandhanaṃ ca mukhyatayā dvividham avāntaravyāpāreṇa ca caturvidham // GRhtCM_1.3:7 //
children.translated_text: And <s>bandhana</s> (binding) is primarily of two kinds, and by subsidiary processes, of four kinds. // GRhtCM 1.3:7 //
Now, the enumeration of the two [primary] kinds of binding: <s>nirbīja-baddha</s> (bound without seed) and <s>bīja-baddha</s> (bound with seed). // GRhtCM 1.3:8 //
<s>Nirbīja-baddha</s> (seedless binding), as in the <s>Rasamañjarī</s>:
'Mercury, digested with a quarter-portion of gold, made into a paste,
and fired in successive stages with equal portions of sulphur — is called <s>nirbīja</s> (seedless), the remover of all diseases.' // GRhtCM 1.3:9 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 1.3:10 //
And <s>bīja-baddha</s> (seeded binding), as:
'That which is processed with <s>bījas</s> (seed-metals) — the essence of mica (<s>abhra-sattva</s>), gold (<s>hema</s>), silver (<s>tārā</s>), sun-stone (<s>arka-kānta</s>) —
and then combined with six-fold sulphur powder — that has even greater potency in the seeded binding.' // GRhtCM 1.3:11 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 1.3:12 //
The enumeration of the four subsidiary types of binding, as:

children.text: poṭaḥ khoṭo jalaukā ca bhasmatvaṃ ca caturvidham /
children.translated_text: '<s>Poṭa</s> (flake-binding), <s>khoṭa</s> (lump-binding), <s>jalaukā</s> (leech-binding), and <s>bhasmatva</s> (ash-form) — [these are] the fourfold
binding of mercury, to be known by the best of physicians.' // GRhtCM 1.3:13 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 1.3:14 //
Their characteristics, in the <s>Saṃketakalikā</s>:
'<s>Poṭa</s> is the flake-binding (<s>parpaṭī-bandha</s>); the paste-solidification is <s>khoṭaka</s>.

children.text: dhmāto druto bhavetkhoṭas tv āhataścūrṇatāṃ vrajet // GRhtCM_1.3:15 //
children.translated_text: When blown [by bellows] and melted, it becomes <s>khoṭa</s>; when struck, it turns to powder.' // GRhtCM 1.3:15 //

children.text: punardhmāto drutaḥ khoṭa iti khoṭasya lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Again blown and melted, [it is] <s>khoṭa</s>' — this is the characteristic of <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: jalaukā pāṭabandhaśca bhasma bhasmanibhaṃ bhavet // GRhtCM_1.3:16 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Jalaukā</s> is the slab-binding (<s>pāṭa-bandha</s>); <s>bhasma</s> becomes ash-like.' // GRhtCM 1.3:16 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 1.3:17 //
Further, 'being well-killed (<s>sumṛta</s>), it makes [one] immortal (<s>amara</s>).' // GRhtCM 1.3:18 //

children.text: sumṛta iti suḥ iti pūjāyāṃ yathā vidagdhamukhamaṇḍanabahirlāpikāyām /
children.translated_text: '<s>Sumṛta</s>' — '<s>su</s>' is used in the sense of 'worshipful/excellent'; as in the <s>Vidagdhamukhamaṇḍana-bahirlāpikā</s>:

children.text: pūjāyāṃ kiṃ padaṃ proktam astanaṃ ko bibhartyuraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What word is said [to convey] worship? What bears the bone upon its chest?
Who is known as the weapon of the enemy of the demon <s>Pralamba</s>?' // GRhtCM 1.3:19 //
'<s>Su-nāsīra</s>' — that which is worshipful. // GRhtCM 1.3:20 //
'<s>Mṛta</s>' (killed) has a specific meaning. // GRhtCM 1.3:21 //
The definition of '<s>mṛta</s>' (killed mercury):

children.text: ārdratvaṃ ca ghanatvaṃ ca cāpalyaṃ gurutaijasam /
children.translated_text: 'That in which moisture, density, restlessness, heaviness, and luster

children.text: yasyaitāni na vidyante taṃ vidyānmṛtasūtakam // GRhtCM_1.3:22 //
children.translated_text: are no longer found — that should be known as killed mercury (<s>mṛta-sūtaka</s>).' // GRhtCM 1.3:22 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 1.3:23 //
'Worshipful' — as in the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s>:

children.text: abaddhasūtaṃ tu hataṃ pramādāt karoti kaṣṭaṃ prabalaṃ rasendraḥ // GRhtCM_1.3:24 //
children.translated_text: 'Mercury that is unbound (<s>abaddha</s>) and killed (<s>hata</s>) carelessly causes severe harm, [even though it is] the king of essences.' // GRhtCM 1.3:24 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 1.3:25 //

children.text: mūrchanādibandhanaparamparayā yo mṛtaḥ sa pūjyo nānyathā // GRhtCM_1.3:26 //
children.translated_text: That which is 'killed' (<s>mṛta</s>) through the sequence of calcination (<s>mūrchanā</s>) and binding (<s>bandhana</s>) and the rest — that alone is worshipful (<s>pūjya</s>), not otherwise. // GRhtCM 1.3:26 //
As also in the <s>Rasamañjarī</s>:

children.text: ajīrṇaṃ cāpyabījaṃ ca sūtakaṃ yastu ghātayet /
children.translated_text: 'He who kills mercury that is undigested (<s>ajīrṇa</s>) and unseeded (<s>abīja</s>) —

children.text: brahmahā sa durācārī mama drohī maheśvari // GRhtCM_1.3:27 //
children.translated_text: he is a killer of <s>Brahman</s>, an evildoer, and an offender against me, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>!' // GRhtCM 1.3:27 //
This meaning is appropriate. // GRhtCM 1.3:28 //
Being supreme in compassion is the innate nature of the virtuous. // GRhtCM 1.3:29 //
As [the saying goes]:

children.text: chede'pi candanataruḥ surabhayati mukhaṃ kuṭhārasya iti // GRhtCM_1.3:30 //
children.translated_text: 'Even when cut, the sandal tree perfumes the mouth of the axe.' // GRhtCM 1.3:30 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 1.4]
That which arises from the mass of sins of killing gods, <s>gurus</s>, cows, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — [a disease] said to be incurable —

children.text: tadapi ca śamayati yasmāt ko 'nyas tasmāt pavitrataraḥ // GRht_1.4 //
children.translated_text: even that it pacifies; who then is more purifying than this [mercury]? // GRht 1.4 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
'<s>Sura</s>-' and so forth. // GRhtCM 1.4:1 //

children.text: tasmāt sūtarājāt anyo dvitīya pavitratara atiśayena pavitraḥ kaḥ kila śrūyate na ko 'pi // GRhtCM_1.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Other than the king of mercuries (<s>sūtarāja</s>), who is a second entity that is more purifying (<s>pavitratara</s>), exceedingly pure? '<s>Kila</s>' — it is heard — no one at all. // GRhtCM 1.4:2 //

children.text: yasmāddhetoḥ apīti niścayena asādhyaṃ rujaṃ śamayati sarvarūpānvitamasādhyaṃ divyauṣadhibhir api karmavipākenāpi sādhyate tacca kiṃviśiṣṭam asādhyaṃ suretyādiḥ surāś ca guravaś ca gāvaś ca dvijāś ca teṣāṃ yā hiṃsā hananam avamānanaṃ vātād utpanno yaḥ pāpakalāpo duṣkṛtapaṭala etasmād udbhavatīti // GRhtCM_1.4:3 //
children.translated_text: Because, with certainty [indicated by] 'api' (even), it cures (<s>śamayati</s>) incurable disease — disease of every form that is incurable (<s>asādhya</s>) — which cannot be achieved even by divine herbs or by the ripening of <s>karma</s>. And what characterizes this [incurable disease]? Beginning with 'sura' (gods) etc.: <s>suras</s> (gods), <s>gurus</s> (teachers), <s>gāvas</s> (cows), and <s>dvijas</s> (brāhmaṇas) — their <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence), killing, and dishonoring — the mass of sins, the collection of evil deeds (<s>duṣkṛta-paṭala</s>) arising from [such offenses] born of [karmic] wind — it arises from this.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 1.5

children.text: tasya svayaṃ hi sphurati prādurbhāvaḥ sa śāṃkaraḥ ko 'pi /
children.translated_text: Of that [mercury], indeed, there spontaneously manifests a certain emergence (<s>prādurbhāva</s>) which is of the nature of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva);

children.text: kathamanyathā hi śamayati vilasanmātrācca pāparujam // GRht_1.5 //
children.translated_text: for how else could it cure the disease of sin by its mere radiance (<s>vilasanmātra</s>)?
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
'Of that' (<s>tasya</s>) etc.
By this, the poet establishes through inference (<s>anumāna</s>) what is commonly known to people.

children.text: yaḥ pūrvoktaḥ sūtarājas tasya ko 'pyanirvacanīyaḥ sa sarvadeśīyatvena śāṃkaraḥ prādurbhāvaḥ śamayatīti duḥkhamupaśamayatīti śaṃ prasādaḥ śaṃ karotīti śaṃkaraḥ tasyāyaṃ śāṃkaraḥ duḥkhopaśamāyāyaṃ prādurbhavatīti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.5:3 //
children.translated_text: The aforementioned king of mercury (<s>sūtarāja</s>) — of that, a certain indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) emergence (<s>prādurbhāva</s>), which is of the nature of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) due to being universal, cures — that is, alleviates suffering (<s>duḥkham upaśamayati</s>). '<s>Śam</s>' means grace (<s>prasāda</s>); he who creates '<s>śam</s>' is '<s>Śaṅkara</s>' — it manifests for the alleviation of suffering: this is the purport.

children.text: duḥkhamādhivyādhyātmakena dvividhaṃ punar ādhibhautikādhidaivikādhyātmikabhedācca trividham // GRhtCM_1.5:4 //
children.translated_text: Suffering is of two kinds due to the distinction of physical and mental (<s>ādhi-vyādhi</s>); again, it is of three kinds due to the distinction of <s>ādhibhautika</s> (caused by beings), <s>ādhidaivika</s> (caused by fate/gods), and <s>ādhyātmika</s> (caused by oneself).

children.text: sa punarasya sūtarājasya svayaṃ sphurati prakāśata iti // GRhtCM_1.5:5 //
children.translated_text: And this [emergence] of this king of mercury manifests by itself — that is, it shines forth (<s>prakāśate</s>).

children.text: anyathā anyaprakāreṇa śāṃkaraprādurbhāvaṃ vinā pāparujaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ suragurugodvijahiṃsāpāpakalāpodbhavaṃ kathaṃ śamayati // GRhtCM_1.5:6 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, by another means — without the emergence of <s>Śaṅkara's</s> [nature] — how could it cure the disease of sin (<s>pāpa-ruj</s>), [namely] leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), which arises from the mass of sins born of violence against gods, teachers, cows, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>?
How? By mere radiance (<s>vilasanmātra</s>) — that is, by merely coming within the range of sight.
As stated in the <s>Rasendra-maṅgala</s>:
The merit [obtained] by performing a hundred horse-sacrifices (<s>aśvamedha</s>), by donating ten million cows, by [giving] ten million elephants,

children.text: suvarṇabhūdānasamānadharme naro labhet sūtakadarśanena iti // GRhtCM_1.5:8 //
children.translated_text: equal to the merit of gifting gold and land — a person obtains [all this] by merely seeing mercury (<s>sūtaka</s>).
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 1.6

children.text: rasabandhaśca sa dhanyaḥ prārambhe yasya satatamiva karuṇā /
children.translated_text: And blessed is the binding of mercury (<s>rasabandha</s>), at whose commencement compassion [arises] perpetually, as it were;

children.text: siddhe rase kariṣye mahīmahaṃ nirjarāmaraṇam // GRht_1.6 //
children.translated_text: 'When mercury is perfected, I shall make the earth free from old age and death.'
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: mūrchitabaddhamṛtasyāvasthayā trividhaṃ sūtarājasya bandhanaṃ praśaṃsati kaviḥ rasa ityādi // GRhtCM_1.6:1 //
children.translated_text: The poet praises the binding of the king of mercury in its three states — <s>mūrchita</s> (swooned), <s>baddha</s> (bound), and <s>mṛta</s> (killed) — beginning with 'rasa' etc.

children.text: bho janāḥ rasabandhaḥ pāradabandhanaṃ dhanyaḥ yasya prārambhe satataṃ nirantaraṃ karuṇā jāyata iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_1.6:2 //
children.translated_text: O people! The binding of mercury (<s>rasabandha</s>) — the fixation of mercury (<s>pārada</s>) — is blessed (<s>dhanya</s>), at whose commencement, perpetually, without interruption, compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) arises — this is the completion [of the sentence].

children.text: kiṃrūpā ahaṃ govindanāmā rase siddhe sati samyagbandhanatvaṃ prāpte sati mahīṃ medinīṃ nirjarāmaraṇaṃ yathā tathā kariṣye // GRhtCM_1.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what nature? I, named <s>Govinda</s>, when mercury is perfected (<s>siddha</s>) — that is, when it has attained the state of proper fixation — I shall make the earth (<s>medinī</s>) free from old age and death (<s>nirjarāmaraṇa</s>).
Due to extreme proximity [of the event], the present tense (<s>laṭ</s>) [is used] even for [what is essentially] a future action.
'<s>Nirjarāmaraṇam</s>' is a qualifier of the action (<s>kriyā-viśeṣaṇa</s>).

children.text: jarā pālityaṃ maraṇaṃ prāṇatyāga ābhyāṃ rahitaṃ yathā mahyāṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ na yuktam // GRhtCM_1.6:6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jarā</s> (old age) means graying of hair; <s>maraṇa</s> (death) means the departure of the life-breath — free from both, such that old age and death would not be fitting for me.

children.text: atra mahīpadena mahīmadhikṛtya nivasanti ye manujādayas ta eva lakṣaṇāvṛttitvāt // GRhtCM_1.6:7 //
children.translated_text: Here, by the word '<s>mahī</s>' (earth), through metonymy (<s>lakṣaṇā-vṛtti</s>), what is indicated is the humans and others who dwell upon the earth.

children.text: punā rasāyanavaśājjarāniṣedho bhaved iti yuktam // GRhtCM_1.6:8 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, through the power of <s>rasāyana</s> (mercurial elixir), the prevention of old age is indeed reasonable.
As in the <s>Hitopadeśa</s>:
That medicine which destroys old age and disease is called <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy);

children.text: ādye vayasi madhye vā śuddhakāyaḥ samācared /
children.translated_text: one whose body is purified should practice it in the first or middle stage of life.
Thus.

children.text: maraṇaniṣedhaḥ kathamauṣadhena anyauṣadhiśaktihrāsato na yuktaḥ raseśvaraśaktyādhikyād yuktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.6:10 //
children.translated_text: How can death be prevented by medicine? By other medicines, [it is] not reasonable due to the diminishment of [their] power. But by the superior power of the lord of mercury (<s>raseśvara</s>), it is reasonable.
As in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:

children.text: mṛtyorjarāviṣadharasya ca vainateya tubhyaṃ namāmi suravanditasūtarāja /
children.translated_text: O king of mercury, worshiped by the gods, [you who are] the <s>Vainateya</s> (Garuḍa) against the serpent of death and old age — I bow to you!
Thus.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 1.7
And those who, without abandoning the body, have obtained a body born of the creation of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) and <s>Gaurī</s> (Pārvatī) —

children.text: vandyāste rasasiddhā mantragaṇāḥ kiṃkarā yeṣām // GRht_1.7 //
children.translated_text: those <s>rasasiddhas</s> (mercury-adepts) are to be worshiped; hosts of <s>mantras</s> are their servants.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: jarāmaraṇaniṣedhatvena kimādhikyaṃ tadāha ya ityādi // GRhtCM_1.7:1 //
children.translated_text: 'What is superior to the prevention of old age and death?' — to that he says, beginning with 'ye' (those who).

children.text: ye evaṃvidharasasiddhāste vandyā abhivādanayogyāḥ stutyāśca // GRhtCM_1.7:2 //
children.translated_text: Those who are <s>rasasiddhas</s> (mercury-adepts) of this kind are worthy of veneration (<s>vandya</s>), worthy of respectful salutation, and worthy of praise.
'<s>Vadi</s>' [is used in the sense] of salutation and praise.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭā atyaktaśarīrāḥ na tyaktaṃ śarīraṃ yaiste jīvanmuktā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.7:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? '<s>Atyaktaśarīrāḥ</s>' — those who have not abandoned the body; they are <s>jīvanmuktas</s> (liberated while living) — this is the meaning.

children.text: śarīraṃ dvividhaṃ sthūlasūkṣmabhedāt pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśātmakaṃ sthūlaṃ kośatrayātmakaṃ sūkṣmam // GRhtCM_1.7:5 //
children.translated_text: The body is of two kinds, due to the distinction of gross (<s>sthūla</s>) and subtle (<s>sūkṣma</s>): the gross [body] consists of earth, water, fire, air, and space; the subtle [body] consists of three sheaths (<s>kośa-traya</s>).
As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

children.text: vijñānamayaṃ manomayaṃ prāṇamayam etat kośatrayaṃ militaṃ sūkṣmaśarīramutpadyate // GRhtCM_1.7:6 //
children.translated_text: 'The <s>vijñānamaya</s> (knowledge-sheath), <s>manomaya</s> (mind-sheath), and <s>prāṇamaya</s> (breath-sheath) — these three sheaths combined give rise to the subtle body.'
Others [define] the subtle body differently.
And the <s>rasasiddhas</s> who [achieved perfection] without abandoning the body are named [as follows]:

<s>Manthānabhairava</s>, the <s>yogī</s>; <s>Siddhabuddha</s>; and <s>Kanthaḍī</s>;
<s>Koraṇṭaka</s>; <s>Surānanda</s>; <s>Siddhapāda</s>; and <s>Carpaṭī</s>;
<s>Kaṇerī</s>; <s>Pūjyapāda</s>; <s>Nityanātha</s>; <s>Nirañjana</s>;
<s>Kapālī</s>; <s>Bindunātha</s>; <s>Kākacaṇḍīśvara</s>; <s>Gaja</s>;
<s>Āllama</s>; <s>Prabhudeva</s>; <s>Ghoḍācolī</s>; and <s>Ṭhiṇṭhinī</s>;

children.text: bhālukir nāgadevaśca khaṇḍī kāpālikas tathā // GRhtCM_1.7:10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāluki</s>; <s>Nāgadeva</s>; <s>Khaṇḍī</s>; and <s>Kāpālika</s> as well.
These and other great <s>siddhas</s> (perfected ones), by the grace of the enjoyment of mercury (<s>rasabhoga</s>),

children.text: khaṇḍayitvā kāladaṇḍaṃ trilokyāṃ vicaranti te // GRhtCM_1.7:11 //
children.translated_text: having shattered the rod of Death (<s>Kāla</s>), wander in the three worlds.
Thus.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ tanuṃ prāptāḥ śarīraṃ grahītāraḥ // GRhtCM_1.7:13 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what quality? 'Having obtained a body' — that is, bearers of a [new] body.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāṃ tanuṃ haragaurīsṛṣṭijāṃ haro mahādevaḥ gaurī pārvatī tayoḥ sṛṣṭiḥ sarjanaṃ maithunasaṃyogas tajjātā putrā evetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.7:14 //
children.translated_text: What kind of body? 'Born of the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>' — <s>Hara</s> is <s>Mahādeva</s> (Śiva); <s>Gaurī</s> is <s>Pārvatī</s>; their creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>) means procreation, sexual union; those born from that are [their] sons — this is the meaning.

children.text: punaryeṣāṃ mantragaṇāḥ kiṃkarāḥ mantrasamūhā ājñākarā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.7:15 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, 'whose servants are hosts of <s>mantras</s>' — assemblies of <s>mantras</s> are their obedient servants — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 1.8-9

children.text: sukṛtaphalaṃ tāvadidaṃ sukule yajjanma dhīśca tatrāpi /
children.translated_text: This is the fruit of good deeds (<s>sukṛta</s>): birth in a good family, and intelligence (<s>dhī</s>) in addition to that;

children.text: sāpi ca sakalamahītalatulanaphalā bhūtalaṃ ca suvidheyam // GRht_1.8 //
children.translated_text: and that [intelligence], whose fruit is the weighing of the entire earth — and the earth, too, is to be well mastered.
The fruit of mastery over the earth is wealth (<s>artha</s>); and those [riches] bear the fruit of various enjoyments;

children.text: bhogāḥ santi śarīre tadanityamaho vṛthā sakalam // GRht_1.9 //
children.translated_text: enjoyments exist in the body — but that [body] is impermanent! Alas, all is in vain!
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: tāvaditi sākalye yāvattāvad ityetau sākalyāvadhimānavadhāraṇeṣv iti prasādataḥ // GRhtCM_1.8-9:1 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Tāvat</s>' (so far/to that extent) [is used] in the sense of totality; '<s>yāvat-tāvat</s>' is used in [expressions of] totality, limit, and restriction — [as explained] by [the grammarian] <s>Prasāda</s>.

children.text: idaṃ sukṛtaphalaṃ suvihitakarmaphalam idaṃ kiyat sukṛte śubhānvaye janma svatantrā dhīḥ svādhīnabuddhir ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.8-9:2 //
children.translated_text: 'This fruit of good deeds' — the fruit of well-performed actions. How much [comes from] good deeds? Birth in a good lineage (<s>śubhānvaya</s>); independent intelligence (<s>svādhīna-buddhi</s>) — this is the meaning.
'Api' (indeed/even) [is used] in the sense of certainty.

children.text: sā buddhiḥ sakalamahītalatulanaphalā sakalasya niravaśeṣasya mahītalasya tulanaṃ phalaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā // GRhtCM_1.8-9:4 //
children.translated_text: That intelligence, 'whose fruit is the weighing of the entire earth' — that whose fruit is the measurement of the entire, complete earth — is so described.

children.text: tulanam iti tulayā svatantrabuddhirūpayā sakalamahītalasya tulanaṃ bhavatyeveti yuktaṃ kimākārā kiyanmānā kaiḥ śritā kair dhṛtā ca bhūr iti jyotiṣasiddhāntavidhānād adṛṣṭāntā bhūr buddhyopalakṣyate // GRhtCM_1.8-9:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Weighing' — by means of the scale that is independent intelligence, the measuring of the entire earth indeed occurs. Of what form, of what measure, by whom supported, by whom sustained is the earth? — through the methods of <s>jyotiṣa-siddhānta</s> (astronomical science), the earth, which is beyond example, is comprehended by the intellect.

children.text: punaḥ sukulajanmasvatantrabuddhibhyāṃ bhūtalaṃ suvidheyaṃ pūjyaṃ jñātavyam // GRhtCM_1.8-9:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, through birth in a good family and independent intelligence, the earth is to be well mastered — to be honored, to be known.

children.text: ekadeśagrahaṇāt sarvaṃ grāhyaṃ mahāntastokā bhūtalaṃ bahu īdṛśā mahānto yatra tiṣṭhanti tatsthānaṃ pūjyaṃ vettumaśakyatvāt sarvamiti // GRhtCM_1.8-9:7 //
children.translated_text: By mentioning one part, the whole is to be understood. [Whether] great [or] small, the earth [is] vast; places where such great ones dwell are worthy of worship; because it is impossible to know [them all], [the word] 'all' [is used].
The connection with birth in a good family is explained, beginning with '<s>bhūtale</s>' (on the earth).

children.text: bhūtalavidheyatāyāḥ bhūtale pṛthivīmaṇḍale yā vidheyatā sarvakarmapravīṇatā tasyā arthāḥ kāryāṇi kathaṃbhūtāḥ vividhabhogaphalāḥ vividhāśca te bhogāśca vividhabhogāḥ nānābhogāḥ phalaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ // GRhtCM_1.8-9:9 //
children.translated_text: 'Mastery over the earth' — the proficiency in all actions on the earth, the terrestrial sphere; its 'purposes' (<s>artha</s>) are its effects; of what nature? 'Bearing the fruit of various enjoyments' — various and manifold enjoyments — <s>vividha-bhogāḥ</s> — meaning diverse enjoyments; those whose fruit [consists of] these are so called.
Those are of the nature of fruit.
Enjoyments exist in the body — they come into being [there].

children.text: kutaḥ yato vedāntasūtraṃ prārabdhakarmaphalabhogāyatanaṃ śarīram iti // GRhtCM_1.8-9:12 //
children.translated_text: Why? Because of the <s>Vedānta-sūtra</s>: 'The body is the locus for the enjoyment of the fruits of <s>prārabdha-karma</s> (previously initiated actions).'

children.text: ata eva bhogānām āśrayāḥ śarīram // GRhtCM_1.8-9:13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the body is the support of enjoyments.

children.text: aho iti kaṣṭe āścarye vā // GRhtCM_1.8-9:14 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Aho</s>' — [an exclamation] of distress or wonder.
But this body is the most excellent of all — this is the purport.

children.text: sā muktiḥ piṇḍapātane iti vacanāt // GRhtCM_1.8-9:16 //
children.translated_text: Because of the statement: 'That liberation [occurs] at the fall of the body (<s>piṇḍapātana</s>).'
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 1.10
Thus, having considered wealth, body, and enjoyments to be impermanent, one should always strive

children.text: muktau sā ca jñānāt taccābhyāsāt sa ca sthire dehe // GRht_1.10 //
children.translated_text: for liberation; and that [comes] from knowledge; and that [knowledge comes] from practice; and that [practice is possible] in a stable body.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: sarvasādhanaṃ śarīraṃ matvābhimataṃ diśati bho janāḥ sadā sarvasmin kāle aharniśaṃ yatanīyam kiṃ kṛtvā dhanaśarīrabhogān anityān naśvarān matvā yatanīyam iti // GRhtCM_1.10:1 //
children.translated_text: Having considered the body as the means of all [attainments], [the author] directs his view. O people! At all times, day and night, one should strive. Having done what? Having considered wealth, body, and enjoyments to be impermanent, perishable — one should strive.

children.text: kiṃ yathā śarīraṃ nityasthāyi bhavati śarīre nitye sarvaṃ nityam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.10:2 //
children.translated_text: For what? So that the body becomes permanently enduring; when the body is permanent, everything is permanent — this is the meaning.

children.text: tasya śarīrasya nityasya jñānāt sarvotkṛṣṭenānenaiva śarīraṃ nityaṃ bhaved ityavabodhāt tasyaivābhyāsācca muktir bhavati // GRhtCM_1.10:3 //
children.translated_text: From the knowledge of that [supreme mercury] — from the understanding that by this most excellent [substance] alone the body would become permanent — and from the practice of that very [knowledge], liberation comes about.

children.text: kva sati sthire dehe sati // GRhtCM_1.10:4 //
children.translated_text: When? When the body is stable (<s>sthira</s>).

children.text: manaso dharmaiḥ śarīrāśritaiḥ ṣaṅkikāraś ca dehāsthiratvam etanniṣedhatvaṃ dehasthiratvaṃ mokṣaḥ // GRhtCM_1.10:5 //
children.translated_text: By the properties of the mind that are body-dependent, there is doubt (<s>ṣaṅkikāra</s>) and instability of the body; the negation of this — the stability of the body — is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).
That very thing is stated — the words of the <s>guru</s> to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: na mokṣo nabhasaḥ pṛṣṭhe na pātāle na bhūtale /
children.translated_text: Liberation is not on the surface of the sky, nor in the netherworld, nor on the earth;

children.text: sarvāśāsaṃkṣayaś cetaḥ śamo mokṣam itīkṣate iti // GRhtCM_1.10:6 //
children.translated_text: the extinction of all desires, the tranquility of the mind — that is regarded as liberation.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 1.11

children.text: tatsthairyaṃ na samarthaṃ rasāyanaṃ kimapi mūlalohādi /
children.translated_text: For that stability [of the body], no <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir/rejuvenation) — whether any root, metal, or the like — is capable,

children.text: svayamasthirasvabhāvaṃ dāhyaṃ kledyaṃ ca śoṣyaṃ ca // GRht_1.11 //
children.translated_text: [for these are] by nature unstable, combustible, liquefiable, and desiccable.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: tasya dehasya sthairyeṇa sthirabhāvena kṛtvā rasāyanaṃ jarāvyādhināśanaṃ prati samarthaṃ kārakataram // GRhtCM_1.11:1 //
children.translated_text: For the stability — the state of firmness — of that body, as a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy) — for the destruction of old age and disease — [what is] capable, most efficacious?
'Api' (indeed/even) [is used] in the sense of certainty.

children.text: kiṃ sūtalohādiḥ sūtaḥ pāradaḥ lohāḥ svarṇādayo navakāḥ kṛtrimākṛtrimabhedayuktāḥ rājarītikharparīghoṣāḥ kṛtrimāḥ svarṇatāratāmranāgavaṅgalohā akṛtrimāḥ ādiśabdānmahārasā uparasāśca jñātavyāḥ // GRhtCM_1.11:3 //
children.translated_text: What? Mercury-metal and the like: '<s>sūta</s>' means mercury (<s>pārada</s>); '<s>lohas</s>' means the nine [metals] such as gold etc., endowed with the distinction of artificial (<s>kṛtrima</s>) and natural (<s>akṛtrima</s>); <s>rājaritikharparī-ghoṣa</s> are the artificial ones; gold, silver, copper, lead (<s>nāga</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), and iron (<s>loha</s>) are the natural ones. By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), the <s>mahārasas</s> (great mineral substances) and <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals) should be understood.
Who are these? As in the <s>Rasāvatāra</s>:

Cinnabar (<s>hiṅgūla</s>), red lead (<s>tāpya</s>), clear [mica] (<s>vimala</s>), mountain-born [mineral] (<s>acala</s>), loadstone (<s>sasyakānta</s>), <s>vaikrānta</s>, and 'lords of birds' (<s>pakṣi-pati</s> = orpiment/realgar) — these are the <s>mahārasas</s>;

Antimony (<s>sauvīra</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), arsenic (<s>śilā</s>), red chalk (<s>laviraṅga</s>), mineral substances (<s>dhātu</s>), <s>kāsīsa</s>, and <s>kāṅkṣī</s> — the <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals) have been enumerated by the knowers of mercury.

children.text: athavā sthairyeṇa samarthe tat dehaṃ prati rasāyanaṃ kiṃ sūtalohādi // GRhtCM_1.11:5 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively: for stability, as a capable [agent] toward that body, what <s>rasāyana</s> [is there]? Mercury-metal and the like.

children.text: sūte yadabhivyāptaṃ grāsamānena lohādi tattathoktaṃ sūte iti abhivyāpake // GRhtCM_1.11:6 //
children.translated_text: That which is permeated by mercury — the metals and the like consumed by it — are so called; '<s>sūte</s>' [is used] in the sense of 'permeating.'
The seventh [case-ending] is in the locative sense.

children.text: taddehaṃ svayamasthiram asthirībhāvatvabhāvaṃ punar dāhyaṃ dagdhuṃ śakyaṃ punaḥ kledyam ārdrībhāvena śīrṇayituṃ śakyaṃ punaḥ śodhyaṃ śoṣayitum agnijalānilaiḥ dāhyaṃ kledyaṃ śoṣyaṃ ca śarīramityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.11:8 //
children.translated_text: That body is by nature unstable — having the character of instability; furthermore, combustible — capable of being burned; furthermore, liquefiable — capable of being dissolved through moisture; furthermore, desiccable — capable of being dried up — by fire, water, and wind [respectively], the body is combustible, liquefiable, and desiccable — this is the meaning.

children.text: sūtalohādinā dehamanityaṃ nityaṃ bhavet ayameva yatna iti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.11:9 //
children.translated_text: By means of <s>sūta</s> (mercury), metals, and so forth, [one can make] the impermanent body permanent — this is indeed the effort [intended]. This is the purport. // GRhtCM_1.11:9 //
START GRht 1.12-13
<Dissolution of plants → immortality>

children.text: kāṣṭhauṣadhyo nāge nāgaṃ vaṅge vaṅgamapi līyate śulve /
children.translated_text: Wooden herbs [dissolve] in <s>nāga</s> (lead), <s>nāga</s> dissolves in <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), <s>vaṅga</s> too dissolves in <s>śulva</s> (copper),

children.text: śulvaṃ tāre tāraṃ kanake kanakaṃ ca līyate sūte // GRht_1.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>śulva</s> in <s>tāra</s> (silver), <s>tāra</s> in <s>kanaka</s> (gold), and <s>kanaka</s> dissolves in <s>sūta</s> (mercury). // GRht_1.12 //
Just as in the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), the dissolution of all beings is certain,
so that one <s>Rasarāja</s> (King of Mercury) makes the body free from old age and death. // GRht_1.13 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: pūrvaśloke sūtalohādikamuktaṃ tatrādhivyāpakādhikaraṇasya kramaṃ darśayati kāṣṭhauṣadhya ityādi // GRhtCM_1.12-13:1 //
children.translated_text: In the previous verse, <s>sūta</s> (mercury), metals, and so forth were mentioned; now he shows the sequence of the pervading substratum — 'wooden herbs' and so forth. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:1 //

children.text: kāṣṭhauṣadhyaḥ kumārikādayaḥ nāge līyante tannāgaṃ vaṅge līyate tadvaṅgamapi śulbe tāmre līyate tacchulbaṃ tāre līyate tattāraṃ rūpyaṃ kanake suvarṇe līyate tatkanakaṃ sūte pārade līyate iti // GRhtCM_1.12-13:2 //
children.translated_text: Wooden herbs such as <s>kumārikā</s> (aloe) and others dissolve in <s>nāga</s> (lead); that <s>nāga</s> dissolves in <s>vaṅga</s> (tin); that <s>vaṅga</s> also dissolves in <s>śulva</s>, i.e., <s>tāmra</s> (copper); that <s>śulva</s> dissolves in <s>tāra</s> (silver); that <s>tāra</s>, i.e., silver, dissolves in <s>kanaka</s>, i.e., <s>suvarṇa</s> (gold); that <s>kanaka</s> dissolves in <s>sūta</s>, i.e., <s>pārada</s> (mercury). Thus. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:2 //

children.text: kathaṃ līyate vidhānata ekaikena yuktaṃ samudāyenāpi ca // GRhtCM_1.12-13:3 //
children.translated_text: How does it dissolve? By the prescribed method — each individually and also in combination. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:3 //

children.text: dhātūnām arivargatvān mahārasoparasānām api yogam apiśabdāśca // GRhtCM_1.12-13:4 //
children.translated_text: Because the metals have the nature of being enemies [to each other], the <s>mahārasas</s> (great mineral substances) and <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals) are also [applicable]; and the word 'also' [implies further substances]. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:4 //
He describes them as a totality — 'just as in the <s>Paramātman</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:5 //

children.text: asau eko dhātvādyantarbhūto rasarājaḥ śarīramajarāmaraṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitaṃ kurute // GRhtCM_1.12-13:6 //
children.translated_text: That one [mercury], subsuming metals and other substances within it, is the <s>Rasarāja</s> (King of Mercury) [and] makes the body free from old age and death, devoid of aging and dying. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:6 //

children.text: rasair mahārasoparasair antarbhūto rājate śobhate vā prakāśate iti rasarājaḥ athavā raseṣu mahārasoparaseṣu anādarībhūteṣu satsu rājata iti viśeṣārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.12-13:7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasarāja</s>: among the <s>rasas</s> (mercurial substances), <s>mahārasas</s>, and <s>uparasas</s>, it is subsumed and shines, or it radiates — hence '<s>Rasarāja</s>.' Alternatively, when the <s>rasas</s>, <s>mahārasas</s>, and <s>uparasas</s> are disregarded, it alone reigns supreme — this is the specific meaning. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:7 //

children.text: tathā ca sūtraṃ ṣaṣṭhīsaptamyau cānādare iti athavā rasānāṃ mahārasoparasadhātūnāṃ rājā teṣu mukhyatvenopadiṣṭaḥ mukhyatvenāsya grahaṇamityupalakṣaṇam // GRhtCM_1.12-13:8 //
children.translated_text: And thus the grammatical rule: 'The sixth and seventh cases [are used] also in the sense of disregard.' Alternatively, the king of <s>rasas</s> — of <s>mahārasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, and metals — is taught as the principal one among them; its acceptance as principal is implied. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:8 //
By this alone, the inclusion of all [substances] should be understood. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:9 //
The particle '<s>iva</s>' is in the sense of comparison. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:10 //

children.text: ātmani brahmaṇi niyataṃ niścitaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ sakalajīvānāṃ layo bhavati layo'ntarbhāvaḥ vā tasminsarve // GRhtCM_1.12-13:11 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>Ātman</s>, i.e., <s>Brahman</s>, certainly, definitively, the dissolution of all beings (<s>sattvas</s>), of all living entities, takes place — dissolution means absorption; in that [<s>Brahman</s>], all // GRhtCM_1.12-13:11 //

children.text: sattvā līnā eva tiṣṭhantītyātmānaḥ taṭasthasvarūpataitallakṣaṇadvayam uktam // GRhtCM_1.12-13:12 //
children.translated_text: beings indeed abide in a dissolved state — thus, the marginal characteristic (<s>taṭastha-lakṣaṇa</s>) of the Self, and its two defining marks, have been stated. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:12 //

children.text: tathā rasarāje'pi darśayati kāṣṭhauṣadhīdhātumahārasoparasādīnāṃ layo jñeyaḥ taṭasthalakṣaṇena layasya krama upadiṣṭaḥ // GRhtCM_1.12-13:13 //
children.translated_text: He shows that the same applies to <s>Rasarāja</s> (mercury): the dissolution of wooden herbs, metals, <s>mahārasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, and so forth should be understood; the sequence of dissolution is taught by means of the marginal characteristic. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:13 //

children.text: svarūpalakṣaṇenauṣadhīdhātumahārasoparasādayaḥ pṛthaktvena sthitā api guṇairantarbhūtā eva jñātavyāḥ yataḥ sarveṣāṃ guṇāntarbhūtaḥ sūtas tato 'nantaguṇa ācāryair upavarṇitaḥ // GRhtCM_1.12-13:14 //
children.translated_text: By means of the essential characteristic (<s>svarūpa-lakṣaṇa</s>): the herbs, metals, <s>mahārasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, and so forth, even though existing separately, should be understood as subsumed within [mercury] through their qualities; since the qualities of all are subsumed in <s>sūta</s> (mercury), it is described by the masters as having infinite qualities. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:14 //
Through the specific manner of dissolution, the equality of both [<s>Paramātman</s> and <s>Rasarāja</s>] — this is the secret. // GRhtCM_1.12-13:15 //
START GRht 1.14

children.text: amṛtatvaṃ hi bhajante haramūrtau yogino yathā līnāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>yogins</s>, dissolved in the body of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), attain immortality,
so too metals such as gold, [dissolved] in <s>Rasarāja</s> (mercury) that has swallowed <s>gagana</s> (mica/sky-metal). // GRht_1.14 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
To make all [things] equivalent, he says 'immortality' and so forth. // GRhtCM_1.14:1 //

children.text: te svātmanā ātmanā saha yogakartṛkā yogino yathā haramūrtau mahādevaśarīre līnāḥ santaḥ amṛtatvaṃ bhajante muktatvaṃ prāpnuvanti // GRhtCM_1.14:2 //
children.translated_text: Those <s>yogins</s>, performing yoga with their own selves, when dissolved in the body of <s>Hara</s>, i.e., the body of <s>Mahādeva</s>, attain immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>), i.e., they achieve liberation (<s>muktatva</s>). // GRhtCM_1.14:2 //

Liberation, isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>), extinction (<s>nirvāṇa</s>), welfare (<s>śreyas</s>), supreme welfare (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), immortality (<s>amṛta</s>) — thus [says] <s>Amara</s> [<s>Amarakośa</s>]. // GRhtCM_1.14:3 //

children.text: tadvattenaiva prakāreṇa rasarāje pārade kavalitagagane grāsīkṛtābhrake sati hemalohādyā līnāḥ santa amṛtatvaṃ pīyūṣabhāvaṃ bhajante amarīkaraṇayogyā bhavanti // GRhtCM_1.14:4 //
children.translated_text: In the same manner, in <s>Rasarāja</s>, i.e., in <s>pārada</s> (mercury), when <s>gagana</s> (mica) has been devoured, i.e., when <s>abhraka</s> (mica) has been consumed, gold, metals, and so forth, being dissolved, attain the state of immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>), i.e., the state of elixir (<s>pīyūṣa-bhāva</s>), and become fit for conferring immortality (<s>amarīkaraṇa</s>). // GRhtCM_1.14:4 //

children.text: hema ca lohaśca hemalohau ādyau yeṣāṃ vā hemasaṃjñako loha ādyo yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ // GRhtCM_1.14:5 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Hema</s>' and '<s>loha</s>' — '<s>hema-loha</s>' [means] gold and metal; '<s>ādya</s>' (and so forth): or [it means] the metal designated as '<s>hema</s>' (gold) comes first — those [substances are] thus described. // GRhtCM_1.14:5 //

children.text: abhrake kavalite sati cāraṇā syānnānyatheti // GRhtCM_1.14:6 //
children.translated_text: When <s>abhraka</s> (mica) has been devoured, [the process of] <s>cāraṇā</s> (perambulation/transmutation) is possible, not otherwise. // GRhtCM_1.14:6 //
START GRht 1.15
One with a stabilized body, through practice having attained knowledge endowed with the eightfold qualities,
attains the state of <s>Brahman</s>, without the suffering of repeated existence. // GRht_1.15 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: adhunā sthiradehasya phalaṃ vyanakti sthiretyādi // GRhtCM_1.15:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he reveals the fruit of having a stabilized body — 'stabilized' and so forth. // GRhtCM_1.15:1 //

children.text: pūrvoktasyaiva rasarājasyābhyāsāt sevanāddhetoḥ sthiradehaḥ pumān brahmapadaṃ prāpnoti // GRhtCM_1.15:2 //
children.translated_text: Through the practice of, i.e., through the service of, the aforementioned <s>Rasarāja</s> (mercury), a man with a stabilized body attains the state of <s>Brahman</s>. // GRhtCM_1.15:2 //
The state of <s>Brahman</s> is the nature of supreme bliss (<s>paramānanda-svarūpa</s>). // GRhtCM_1.15:3 //
Having done what? Having attained knowledge. // GRhtCM_1.15:4 //

What kind of knowledge? Endowed with the eightfold qualities — endowed with the eight <s>siddhis</s> (perfections) beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (ability to become infinitely small). // GRhtCM_1.15:5 //
How does one attain the state of <s>Brahman</s>? // GRhtCM_1.15:6 //

children.text: yathā punaraprathamaṃ bhavāvāsaduḥkhe saṃsāranivāsanatāpatrayātmakakaṣṭe na patatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.15:7 //
children.translated_text: Such that one does not fall again, for the first time, into the suffering of worldly existence (<s>bhavāvāsa-duḥkha</s>), i.e., the triple misery (<s>tāpatraya</s>) that constitutes the pain of dwelling in <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_1.15:7 //
Having attained knowledge, one attains the state of <s>Brahman</s>. // GRhtCM_1.15:8 //
How so? Because without knowledge, there is no liberation. // GRhtCM_1.15:9 //

children.text: anyacca kiṃ mokṣatarorbījaṃ samyagjñānaṃ kriyāsahitam iti praśnottararatnamālāyām // GRhtCM_1.15:10 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore: 'What is the seed of the tree of liberation? Right knowledge accompanied by action' — thus in the <s>Praśnottara-ratnamālā</s>. // GRhtCM_1.15:10 //
START GRht 1.16

children.text: ekāṃśena jaganti ca viṣṭabhyāvasthitaṃ paraṃ jyotiḥ /
children.translated_text: With one part pervading all the worlds, the Supreme Light stands established;
that immortal [state] is easily attainable by three feet [of practice], not by mere detachment alone. // GRht_1.16 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He describes <s>Brahman</s> that is accessible through knowledge — 'with one part' and so forth. // GRhtCM_1.16:1 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ prakāśasvarūpaṃ tatparaṃ jyotir jaganti saṃsārāṇi svargamṛtyupātālādīni viṣṭabhya vyāpya sthitaṃ kena ekāṃśena anekabrahmāṇḍanāyakatvāt ekaikasmin brahmāṇḍe bahūni saṃsārāṇi vartante ata ekāṃśenetyuktaṃ punas tatparaṃ jyotīrūpam amṛtaṃ tribhiḥ pādair abhyāsasthiradehajñānasaṃjñakaiḥ sulabhaṃ sukhena labhyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.16:2 //
children.translated_text: What kind of <s>Brahman</s>? The Supreme Light, whose nature is radiance — that Supreme Light pervades and stands established in the worlds, i.e., the planes of existence such as heaven, mortal realm, netherworld, and so forth — with one part, since it is the ruler of innumerable cosmic eggs (<s>brahmāṇḍas</s>), and in each <s>brahmāṇḍa</s> there are many planes of existence, hence 'with one part' is said. Furthermore, that Supreme Light in the form of immortality (<s>amṛta</s>) is easily attainable (<s>sulabha</s>), i.e., easily obtained, by three feet, namely by the three [means] designated as practice, stabilized body, and knowledge — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_1.16:2 //
First, practice is one cause for the easy attainability of immortality. // GRhtCM_1.16:3 //

children.text: heturekaḥ sthiradehaś ca dvitīyo hetur jñānaṃ tṛtīyaheturmokṣe yathāvākyaṃ na viraktimātram // GRhtCM_1.16:4 //
children.translated_text: The stabilized body is the second cause; knowledge is the third cause for liberation — as the text states — not mere detachment alone. // GRhtCM_1.16:4 //
START GRht 1.17
For with a body afflicted by disease, old age, death, and suffering,
perishable in an instant — it is not possible to worship that subtle <s>Brahman</s>. // GRht_1.17 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: pūrvāparābhyāmabhyāsajñānābhyāṃ sthiradeho heturgarīyāniti sūcayannāha netyādi // GRhtCM_1.17:1 //
children.translated_text: Indicating that the stabilized body is the weightiest cause among the two flanking [causes] of practice and knowledge, he says 'not' and so forth. // GRhtCM_1.17:1 //

children.text: ubhayoḥ sādhakatvāt tādṛśadehavyatiriktaṃ kathaṃcidapi kiṃcin na sidhyatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.17:2 //
children.translated_text: Because both [practice and knowledge] are means to accomplishment, without such a [stabilized] body, nothing whatsoever can be accomplished — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_1.17:2 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭena vyādhijarāmaraṇaduḥkhavidhureṇa vyādhirāmayaḥ jarā pālityaṃ maraṇaṃ prāṇatyāgaḥ duḥkhaṃ mohaśokādikam etair vidhuraṃ tāḍitaṃ vyadha tāḍane ityasya ghāto rūpaṃ vidhuram urapratyayāntam // GRhtCM_1.17:3 //
children.translated_text: With what kind [of body]? Afflicted by disease, old age, death, and suffering: disease means illness; old age means greying; death means the departure of the vital breath; suffering means delusion, grief, and so forth; '<s>vidhura</s>' (afflicted) means struck — '<s>vyadha</s>' means striking — its form is '<s>vidhura</s>,' ending with the suffix '<s>ura</s>.' // GRhtCM_1.17:3 //

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭena kṣaṇabhaṅgureṇa kṣaṇavināśinā dehena tadbrahma cidghanānandasvarūpam upāsituṃ sevituṃ kathaṃ kena prakāreṇa śakyaṃ kuto yataḥ sūkṣmam indriyāgrāhyatvāt // GRhtCM_1.17:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with what kind? Perishable in an instant (<s>kṣaṇa-bhaṅgura</s>), i.e., destructible in a moment — with such a body, how, by what means, can one worship that <s>Brahman</s>, i.e., serve [it]? Why? Because it is subtle (<s>sūkṣma</s>), i.e., beyond the grasp of the senses. // GRhtCM_1.17:4 //
START GRht 1.18
Even the name of yogic perfection — who could grasp it without the body?

children.text: yadyogagamyamamalaṃ manaso'pi na gocaraṃ tattvam // GRht_1.18 //
children.translated_text: That truth which is attainable through yoga, pure, beyond even the reach of the mind. // GRht_1.18 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: sarvopāyena śarīraṃ sthiraṃ kāryam ityāha nāmetyādi // GRhtCM_1.18:1 //
children.translated_text: The body must be made stable by every means — thus he says 'even the name' and so forth. // GRhtCM_1.18:1 //

children.text: dehasiddheḥ śarīravibhūteḥ nāmāpyabhidhānamapi ko gṛhṇīyānna ko 'pītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.18:2 //
children.translated_text: Of bodily perfection (<s>deha-siddhi</s>), i.e., the glory of the body — even its very name, its designation — who could grasp it? No one — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_1.18:2 //

children.text: kena vinā śarīreṇa śarīramantareṇa siddhirastu paraṃ tannāma kenāpi na gṛhyate śarīranāmagrahaṇamiti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.18:3 //
children.translated_text: Without what? Without the body, i.e., without the body. Let perfection exist as something supreme, but its very name cannot be grasped by anyone without a body — the grasping of the body's name — this is the purport. // GRhtCM_1.18:3 //

children.text: anaśvaraṃ śarīraṃ bhavatu cet tad amalaṃ nirañjanaṃ tattvaṃ brahmāvaśyaṃ prāpyate // GRhtCM_1.18:4 //
children.translated_text: If the body becomes imperishable, then that pure, stainless truth (<s>tattva</s>), <s>Brahman</s>, is necessarily attained. // GRhtCM_1.18:4 //

children.text: tattattvaṃ manaso'pi na gocaraṃ cittenāpi na gamyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.18:5 //
children.translated_text: That truth is beyond even the reach of the mind — not accessible even by thought — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_1.18:5 //

children.text: tarhi kena gamyam ubhayor melanam ekīkaraṇaṃ yogastenaiva prakṛtipuruṣayor ekīkaraṇenetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.18:6 //
children.translated_text: Then by what is it accessible? The union (<s>yoga</s>) of both — the unification, the joining — is yoga; by that alone, i.e., by the unification of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_1.18:6 //
START GRht 1.19
From sacrifice, from charity, from austerity, from the study of the <s>Vedas</s>, from self-restraint, from righteous conduct —
supremely greater indeed is self-realization (<s>ātma-saṃvitti</s>) by the power of yoga. // GRht_1.19 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: adhunā yogasya sarvakarmabhya utkṛṣṭatvaṃ darśayati yajñād ityādi // GRhtCM_1.19:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he shows that yoga is superior to all [other] practices — 'from sacrifice' and so forth. // GRhtCM_1.19:1 //

children.text: atyantaṃ śreya iti adhikatarakalyāṇaṃ sarvopadravanivāraṇātmakaṃ bhaved ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_1.19:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Supremely greater' means 'more beneficial' — the prevention of all calamities; '[it] would be' is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_1.19:2 //

children.text: kutaḥ yajñādaśvamedhādeḥ na kevalaṃ yajñāt punardānāt dhanasyārpaṇāt pātreṣu punastapasaḥ kṛcchrātikṛcchracāndrāyapasaṃcāgnitapanādeḥ punarvedādhyayanāt vedānām ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvaṇāṃ adhyayanaṃ pāṭhākramastataḥ punardamāt vedāntānusāreṇa damastāvat bāhyendriyāṇāṃ tadvyatiriktaviṣayebhyo manasā nirvartanaṃ tadvyatiriktaṃ śravaṇādivyatiriktaṃ tataḥ punaḥ sadācārāt brāhmamuhūrtam ārabhya prātaḥsaṃgavamadhyāhnāparāhṇasāyāhnādiṣu śayanaparyantaṃ vedabodhito vidhiḥ sadācārastata iti samudāyaḥ śreyaskaro nātmasaṃvittikaraḥ punarātmasaṃvittiḥ brahmavedanaṃ yogavaśādeva syāt yogaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.19:3 //
children.translated_text: From what? From sacrifice such as the <s>Aśvamedha</s> and others — not from sacrifice alone; furthermore, from charity, i.e., the offering of wealth to worthy recipients; furthermore, from austerity such as <s>Kṛcchra</s>, <s>Atikṛcchra</s>, <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s>, fire-heating, and so forth; furthermore, from the study of the <s>Vedas</s>, i.e., the sequential recitation of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Atharva</s> Vedas; furthermore, from self-restraint (<s>dama</s>), which according to <s>Vedānta</s> is the withdrawal of the external senses from objects other than [those pertaining to] hearing and so forth; furthermore, from righteous conduct (<s>sadācāra</s>), the Vedically prescribed routine from the <s>brāhma-muhūrta</s> (pre-dawn hour) through the morning, forenoon, midday, afternoon, and evening periods up to bedtime — the aggregate of all that is merit-producing but does not produce self-realization. Self-realization, i.e., the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, comes about only through the power of yoga — yoga as previously described. // GRhtCM_1.19:3 //
START GRht 1.20
With abundant false cognitions having fallen away, devoid of all [worldly] purposes — consciousness-bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>),
though manifest, what does it do for the multitude of beings whose bodies remain unmanifest? // GRht_1.20 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: yasya jīvasya yogavaśātsaṃvittirjātā sa kīdṛśa ityāha galitetyādi // GRhtCM_1.20:1 //
children.translated_text: The living being for whom self-realization has arisen through the power of yoga — what is he like? He says 'having fallen away' and so forth. // GRhtCM_1.20:1 //

children.text: galitānalpavikalpa iti galito dūrībhūto 'nalpo bahutaro vikalpo mithyājñānaṃ yasya īdṛk syāt // GRhtCM_1.20:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Galitānalpa-vikalpa</s>' — '<s>galita</s>' means having receded; '<s>analpa</s>' means abundant, numerous; '<s>vikalpa</s>' means false knowledge — one for whom this [condition] obtains. // GRhtCM_1.20:2 //

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛk sarvārthavivarjitaḥ sarve ca te arthāśca tair vivarjitāḥ samyagrahito bhavati kāryāṇāṃ smaraṇakaraṇayorabhāva ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.20:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, what is he like? 'Devoid of all purposes' — all those purposes, by them he is devoid, i.e., completely freed; meaning: there is an absence of both remembering and performing actions. // GRhtCM_1.20:3 //

children.text: punaḥ kathaṃbhūtaḥ cidānandaś cidā prakāśena ānandaḥ sukhasampattir yasya sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.20:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what nature? '<s>Cidānanda</s>' — by <s>cit</s>, i.e., by luminous awareness, there is <s>ānanda</s>, i.e., the wealth of bliss — one who has that is thus described. // GRhtCM_1.20:4 //

children.text: prakāśahetunā ānandatā bhavet jaḍahetunā tadviparyayaḥ // GRhtCM_1.20:5 //
children.translated_text: Through the cause of luminous awareness, bliss arises; through the cause of inertness, the opposite. // GRhtCM_1.20:5 //

children.text: īdṛk saḥ sphurito'pi prakāśamāno'pi asphuritatanorjantuvargasya aprakāśaśarīrasya jīvasamūhasya kiṃ karoti pṛcchāṃ karoti // GRhtCM_1.20:6 //
children.translated_text: Such a one, though manifest, i.e., though shining forth — for the multitude of beings whose bodies are unmanifest, i.e., for the mass of living entities whose bodies lack [that] radiance — what does he do? He makes an inquiry. // GRhtCM_1.20:6 //
'<s>Kim</s>' is used in the senses of inquiry and contempt — thus is the derivation. // GRhtCM_1.20:7 //

children.text: pṛcchati ca hasati ca roditi pramattavan mānavo'pi tallīna iti // GRhtCM_1.20:8 //
children.translated_text: He inquires and laughs and weeps, like one intoxicated — yet the human being too is absorbed in that [state]. // GRhtCM_1.20:8 //
START GRht 1.21
That which, situated between the two eyebrows, pure like a peacock's lightning, illuminates the world —

children.text: keṣāṃcit puṇyakṛtām unmīlati cinmayaṃ jyotiḥ // GRht_1.21 //
children.translated_text: for some who have performed meritorious deeds, the light that is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>) opens forth. || GRht 1.21 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: ātmasaṃvitter viralatvaṃ sūcayann āha bhrūyugetyādi // GRhtCM_1.21:1 //
children.translated_text: Indicating the rarity of self-realization, he says 'between the brows' and so forth. || GRhtCM 1.21:1 ||

children.text: yat bhrūyugamadhyagataṃ bhrūdvayāntargataṃ sat prakāśate tatra dṛṣṭiṃ nidhāya yoginaḥ paśyanti khecaryā mudrayā haṭhapradīpikāyāṃ padyam /
children.translated_text: That which is situated between the pair of brows (<s>bhrūyuga</s>), being within the two eyebrows, shines forth — fixing the gaze there, <s>yogins</s> perceive [it] through the <s>khecarī mudrā</s>. A verse in the <s>Haṭhapradīpikā</s>:
The tongue, having entered the cavity of the skull, turned upward,

children.text: bhruvor antargatā dṛṣṭirmudrā bhavati khecarī // GRhtCM_1.21:2 //
children.translated_text: the gaze directed between the brows — that <s>mudrā</s> is called <s>khecarī</s>. || GRhtCM 1.21:2 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 1.21:3 ||

children.text: punaḥ śikhividyutsu vahnisaudāminīṣu nirmalaṃ sat yatprakāśate punaryat jagadbhāsi jagat saṃsāraṃ prakāśate tat cinmayaṃ prakāśapracuraṃ jyotiḥ keṣāṃcit puṇyakṛtāṃ suvihitakarmakartḥṇām unmīlati prādurbhavati na tu sarveṣāṃ yato nirmalaṃ prakāśaṃ dhyātvā vipulapuṇyena nirmalatvāya jāyate ataḥ prakāśo yuktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.21:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that which shines forth as pure amidst the lightnings of peacock [feathers] — i.e., amidst the lightnings of fire — and which again illuminates the world, i.e., illuminates <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) — that light which is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>), abundant in luminosity, opens forth, i.e., manifests, for some who have performed meritorious deeds, those who have performed proper actions — but not for all, because by meditating on the pure luminosity with abundant merit, one is born unto purity. Therefore the luminosity is fitting. || GRhtCM 1.21:4 ||
START GRht 1.22
Consisting solely of supreme bliss, of the nature of the supreme light, free from conceptual construction (<s>avikalpa</s>),
from which all afflictions have fallen away — it is to be known as peaceful, self-luminous. || GRht 1.22 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: pūrvavarṇitaṃ cinmayaṃ viśeṣayannāha paramānandaikamayam ityādi // GRhtCM_1.22:1 //
children.translated_text: Qualifying the previously described consciousness-nature (<s>cinmaya</s>), he says 'consisting solely of supreme bliss' and so forth. || GRhtCM 1.22:1 ||

children.text: tadbrahma īdṛśaṃ jñeyaṃ paramānandaikamayamiti parama utkṛṣṭo 'sāv ānandaḥ paramānandaḥ sa eva eko 'dvitīyas tātprācuryaṃ yasmiṃs tathoktaṃ punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ paramaṃ jyotiḥsvabhāvaṃ paramaṃ yajjyotiḥ tatsvabhāvaḥ svarūpaṃ yasya tad aśarīratvātsvaprakāśitvācca punaḥ avikalpaṃ mithyājñānaśūnyaṃ punarvigalitasarvakleśaṃ vigalitā viśeṣeṇa dūrīkṛtāḥ sarvakleśāḥ duḥkhāni yasmāt tat svarūpatvāt punaḥ śāntaṃ śamamayaṃ punaḥ svayaṃvedyam anyena veditum aśakyam ātmanaiva vedyaṃ tasmānnāparo'stīti bhāvāt // GRhtCM_1.22:2 //
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahman</s> is to be known as such: 'consisting solely of supreme bliss' — 'supreme' means exalted, and that itself is bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) — hence 'supreme bliss'; that alone is one, non-dual — such abundance exists in which, thus it is said. Furthermore, of what character? 'Of the nature of the supreme light' — that whose nature, whose essence, is the supreme light — [so called] because of its being incorporeal and self-luminous. Furthermore, 'free from conceptual construction' (<s>avikalpa</s>) — devoid of false knowledge. Furthermore, 'from which all afflictions have fallen away' — all afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), i.e., sufferings, have especially been removed from which — that, because of its being of that nature. Furthermore, 'peaceful' — consisting of tranquility (<s>śama</s>). Furthermore, 'self-luminous' (<s>svayaṃvedya</s>) — unable to be known by another, knowable only by oneself — because there is no other [than it], such is the purport. || GRhtCM 1.22:2 ||
START GRht 1.23
Placing the mind upon that, perceiving the entire world as shining forth,
one whose bondage of <s>karma</s> has ceased attains <s>Brahman</s>-hood in this very [life]. || GRht 1.23 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the instruction regarding what is to be known, saying 'upon that' and so forth. || GRhtCM 1.23:1 ||

children.text: tasminnādhāyeti pūrvanirūpite tasminnevātmani mana ādhāya saṃsthāpya pumān utsannakarmabandho bhavet tyaktakarmapāśaḥ syāt // GRhtCM_1.23:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Placing upon that' — placing, i.e., establishing the mind upon that very <s>Ātman</s> (Self) described previously, a person would become one whose bondage of <s>karma</s> has ceased, i.e., one who has cast off the fetters of action. || GRhtCM 1.23:2 ||

children.text: sa ihaiva janmani brahmatvaṃ prāpnotīti viśeṣaḥ brahmavid brahmaiva bhavati iti śruteḥ // GRhtCM_1.23:3 //
children.translated_text: He attains <s>Brahman</s>-hood in this very birth — this is the distinction. As the <s>Śruti</s> says: 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself.' || GRhtCM 1.23:3 ||
That person places the mind [thus]. || GRhtCM 1.23:4 ||

children.text: kiṃ kurvan san akhilaṃ jagat sarvasaṃsāraṃ cinmayaṃ prakāśasvarūpaṃ cidvikāraṃ paśyan avalokamāno manaścakṣuṣā kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ jagat sphurat adhyāropāpadeśena dedīpyamānam // GRhtCM_1.23:5 //
children.translated_text: While doing what? Perceiving the entire world, all of <s>saṃsāra</s>, as being of the nature of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>), of the essence of luminosity, a modification of consciousness — observing with the eye of the mind. Of what character is the world? 'Shining forth' (<s>sphurat</s>) — by way of superimposition (<s>adhyāropa</s>), blazing forth. || GRhtCM 1.23:5 ||
And thus the word of the Lord (<s>Bhagavad-vacana</s>):

children.text: karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction,

children.text: sa buddhimānmanuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt // GRhtCM_1.23:6 //
children.translated_text: he is the wise one among men; he is disciplined, the performer of all actions. || GRhtCM 1.23:6 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 1.23:7 ||

children.text: he pārtha sa pumān manuṣyeṣu buddhimān // GRhtCM_1.23:8 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Pārtha</s>, that person is the wise one among men. || GRhtCM 1.23:8 ||
By this, the general applicability is stated. || GRhtCM 1.23:9 ||

children.text: viśeṣaśca yathā rajjau sarpabhramo yathā śuktau rajatajñānaṃ yathā gandharvanagaraṃ yathā marusthale vāri tathaiva saṃsāro nāsīt nāsti na bhaviṣyatīti advaitavādānmithyaiva // GRhtCM_1.23:10 //
children.translated_text: And the specific [illustration] is as follows: just as the illusion of a snake upon a rope, just as the cognition of silver in a shell, just as a celestial city (<s>gandharva-nagara</s>), just as water in a desert — so too <s>saṃsāra</s> never existed, does not exist, and will not exist — from the standpoint of <s>Advaita</s> (non-dualism), it is merely false. || GRhtCM 1.23:10 ||
START GRht 1.24
Sense objects indeed set, through the union of <s>prāṇa</s> and the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>);

children.text: sphuraṇaṃ nendriyatamasāṃ nātaḥ sphurataśca duḥkhasukhe // GRht_1.24 //
children.translated_text: there is no manifestation of the senses and darkness — and therefore neither suffering nor happiness manifests. || GRht 1.24 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
For one whose bondage of <s>karma</s> has ceased, sense objects set (disappear). || GRhtCM 1.24:1 ||

children.text: prāṇāntaḥkaraṇasaṃyogāt na indriyāṇāṃ sphuraṇaṃ bhavet // GRhtCM_1.24:2 //
children.translated_text: Through the union of <s>prāṇa</s> and the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), there would be no manifestation of the senses. || GRhtCM 1.24:2 ||

children.text: tathā ca nyāyaśāstre ātmā manasā saṃyujyate mana indriyeṇa indriyamarthenetīndriyāṇāṃ vastuprāpyaprakāśakāritvaniyamād iti // GRhtCM_1.24:3 //
children.translated_text: And thus in the <s>Nyāya-śāstra</s>: 'The <s>Ātman</s> is conjoined with the mind (<s>manas</s>), the mind with the sense organ, and the sense organ with the object' — because of the rule that the senses illuminate only upon reaching the object. || GRhtCM 1.24:3 ||

children.text: ato hetośca duḥkhasukhe na sphurataḥ // GRhtCM_1.24:4 //
children.translated_text: And for this reason, neither suffering nor happiness manifests. || GRhtCM 1.24:4 ||

children.text: ātmanaḥ prakāśāt prāṇāntaḥkaraṇānāṃ prakāśaḥ prāṇāntaḥkaraṇāni tameva prakāśaṃ prāpyendriyāṇi prakāśayanti // GRhtCM_1.24:5 //
children.translated_text: From the luminosity of the <s>Ātman</s>, the luminosity of <s>prāṇa</s> and the inner organs [arises]; <s>prāṇa</s> and the inner organs, having attained that very luminosity, illuminate the senses. || GRhtCM 1.24:5 ||
Therefore, for both [senses and darkness], there is only dependent illumination (<s>para-prakāśa</s>). || GRhtCM 1.24:6 ||

children.text: tadvad gahanatama agrāhyamandhakāraṃ cidbhinnaṃ prakāśena prakāśitaṃ syāditi // GRhtCM_1.24:7 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the most profound, incomprehensible darkness, being different from consciousness, would be illuminated by luminosity. || GRhtCM 1.24:7 ||
Since darkness is a non-existent entity (<s>abhāva-padārtha</s>), the senses and darkness share the same nature of inertness (<s>jaḍatva</s>). || GRhtCM 1.24:8 ||
START GRht 1.25
Those persons who are free from attachment (<s>rāga</s>) and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), of truthful conduct, devoid of falsehood,
become impartial in all things, through contact with the consciousness-<s>Brahman</s> (<s>cid-brahma</s>). || GRht 1.25 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: adhunā antaḥkaraṇānāṃ pravṛttiṃ darśayati rāgetyādi cidbrahmasaṃsparśāditi cidbrahmaṇi prakāśasvarūpe ātmani yaḥ sparśaḥ tanniṣṭhā tato hetoḥ puruṣā rāgadveṣaviyuktāḥ snehaśatrutvavirahitāḥ syuḥ // GRhtCM_1.25:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he shows the activity of the inner organs, saying 'attachment' and so forth. 'Through contact with the consciousness-<s>Brahman</s>' — contact with the consciousness-<s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is luminosity, i.e., the Self — devotion to that; from that cause, persons become free from attachment and aversion, i.e., devoid of affection and enmity. || GRhtCM 1.25:1 ||

children.text: punaḥ satyaḥ ācāraḥ pravṛttidharmo yeṣāṃ te punarmṛṣārahitāḥ atyācārādyasatyavarjitā ityarthaḥ punaḥ sarvatra nirviśeṣāḥ sarvasmin mānāpamānayoḥ samāḥ tathā ca bhagavadvacanam /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, those whose conduct is truthful, whose active duty (<s>pravṛtti-dharma</s>) [is truth] — furthermore, 'devoid of falsehood,' meaning free from misconduct, untruth, and the like — this is the meaning. Furthermore, 'impartial in all things' — equal in honor and dishonor in everything. And thus the word of the Lord: 'Equal toward enemy and friend, and likewise in honor and dishonor.' || GRhtCM 1.25:2 ||

children.text: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ // GRhtCM_1.25:2 //
children.translated_text: And so forth. || GRhtCM 1.25:3 ||
START GRht 1.26
Endowed with <s>aṇimā</s> and other [powers], with radiant bodies, always blissful with joy,
those who have attained the immortal state of <s>Brahman</s>-realization dwell as ones who have fulfilled all purposes. || GRht 1.26 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing the attainment of liberation through contact with the Self, he says 'they dwell' and so forth. || GRhtCM 1.26:1 ||
