children.text: ye brahmabhāvamamṛtaṃ muktisārūpyatvaṃ prāptāste kṛtakṛtyāḥ kṛtasarvakāryāḥ pūrṇatāṃ prāptā ityarthaḥ punaste aṇimādiyutā aṇimādibhiryutā iha jagati tiṣṭhantīti aṇimādayo yathā /
children.translated_text: Those who have attained the immortal state of <s>Brahman</s>-realization, i.e., the state of identity with the liberated form, they have fulfilled all purposes, meaning they have attained completeness. Furthermore, they, endowed with <s>aṇimā</s> and other [powers], dwell in this world. The <s>aṇimā</s> and other [powers] are as follows: '<s>Aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>mahimā</s> (greatness), and then <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), <s>garimā</s> (heaviness) likewise,

children.text: aṇimā mahimā cātha laghimā garimā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>prāpti</s> (obtaining), <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will), <s>īśitva</s> (sovereignty),
and <s>vaśitva</s> (subjugation) — these are the eight <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers).' || GRhtCM 1.26:2 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 1.26:3 ||

children.text: punarvilasaddehāḥ tejaḥprāyaśarīrāḥ punaḥ sadānandāḥ kena mudā harṣeṇa sadā sarvasminkāle ānando yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ paramānande magnatvāt // GRhtCM_1.26:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, 'with radiant bodies' — having bodies predominantly of brilliance. Furthermore, 'always blissful' — by what? With joy (<s>mudā</s>), with delight, at all times; those whose bliss is constant — they are called thus, because of being immersed in supreme bliss. || GRhtCM 1.26:4 ||
START GRht 1.27
The abode of all sciences, the root of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) —

children.text: śreyaḥ paraṃ kimanyat śarīramajarāmaraṃ vihāyaikam // GRht_1.27 //
children.translated_text: what other supreme welfare is there, aside from this one body that is free from old age and death? || GRht 1.27 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Stating that everything is to be known as rooted in the body, he says 'the abode' and so forth. || GRhtCM 1.27:1 ||

children.text: ekam ajarāmaraṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitaṃ śarīraṃ vihāya tyaktvā anyat paramutkṛṣṭaṃ śreyaḥ kalyāṇasvarūpaṃ kiṃ na kim apītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.27:2 //
children.translated_text: Setting aside, i.e., abandoning, the one body that is free from old age and death — free from old age and death — what other supreme, exalted welfare (<s>śreyas</s>), of the nature of auspiciousness, is there? There is none — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 1.27:2 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ śarīram āyatanaṃ vidyānāṃ vyākaraṇādicaturdaśasaṃkhyākāṅgānāṃ nivāsasthānaṃ punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ mūlaṃ dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ caturṇāṃ padārthānāṃ mūlaṃ hetuḥ dharmādayaś catvāraḥ pratītā eva // GRhtCM_1.27:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what character is the body? 'The abode of sciences' — the dwelling place of the fourteen sciences including grammar and others. Furthermore, of what character? 'The root of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>' — the root, i.e., the cause of the four objects of human pursuit. <s>Dharma</s> and the other four are well-established. || GRhtCM 1.27:3 ||
START GRht 1.28
He who does not know <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) even through the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) such as direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>),

children.text: adṛṣṭavigrahaṃ devaṃ kathaṃ jñāsyati cinmayam // GRht_1.28 //
children.translated_text: how will he know the Lord (<s>deva</s>) who is of the nature of consciousness, whose form is invisible? || GRht 1.28 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: ātmano 'vekṣayā sūte sugamatvaṃ sūcayannāha pramāṇata ityādi // GRhtCM_1.28:1 //
children.translated_text: Indicating the ease of approach through examination of the Self, he says 'through the means of valid knowledge' and so forth. || GRhtCM 1.28:1 ||

children.text: yaḥ puruṣaḥ sūtakaṃ rasendraṃ na jānāti kutaḥ pramāṇataḥ pramākaraṇaṃ pramāṇaṃ pramitisādhanaṃ vā tataḥ kimbhūtāt pramāṇataḥ pratyakṣāc cakṣurindriyagrāhyarūpāt sa pumān cinmayam atisūkṣmam ātmānaṃ kathaṃ jñāsyati na katham apītyarthaḥ indriyāgocaratvāt // GRhtCM_1.28:2 //
children.translated_text: The person who does not know <s>sūtaka</s>, i.e., mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) — from where? Through the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), which is the instrument of valid cognition or the means of knowledge — from what kind of <s>pramāṇa</s>? From direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), that which is apprehensible by the sense organ of sight — that person, how will he know the Self (<s>Ātman</s>) which is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>), extremely subtle? He cannot in any way — that is the meaning — because it is beyond the reach of the senses. || GRhtCM 1.28:2 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭam anādivigraham ādiśca vigrahaṃ ca ādivigrahe te na vidyete yatra saḥ taṃ utpattiśarīrayorabhāvāt sthūlajñānābhāva iti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.28:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? 'Whose form is without beginning' (<s>anādi-vigraha</s>) — 'beginning' and 'form' (<s>ādi</s> and <s>vigraha</s>) — these do not exist in which — that; because of the absence of origination and a [physical] body, the purport is the absence of gross knowledge. || GRhtCM 1.28:3 ||
START GRht 1.29-30
That [body] which is worn out by old age, subject to the sufferings of cough, asthma, and the like,
is not fit for <s>samādhi</s>, its intellect and sense-faculties being obstructed. || GRht 1.29 ||
A child until sixteen years, after that enamored of the relishing of sense pleasures,
with discrimination arising [only] in old age — how can a mortal attain liberation? || GRht 1.30 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: śarīrasya vayovibhāgenāsthiratvaṃ darśayannāha bāla ityādi // GRhtCM_1.29-30:1 //
children.translated_text: Showing the instability [of the body] through the division of ages, he says 'a child' and so forth. || GRhtCM 1.29-30:1 ||

children.text: ṣoḍaśavarṣa iti ṣoḍaśa varṣāṇi yasya vayasi sa ṣoḍaśābdo bāla ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.29-30:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Of sixteen years' — one who has sixteen years in age is [called] 'of sixteen years,' meaning a child. || GRhtCM 1.29-30:2 ||
In other texts, even within childhood, there are divisions of age. || GRhtCM 1.29-30:3 ||
As the verse says:
Up to the fifth [year] is <s>kaumāra</s> (early childhood), <s>paugaṇḍa</s> (boyhood) up to nine years,

children.text: ā ṣoḍaśācca kiśoro yauvanaṃ ca tataḥ param // GRhtCM_1.29-30:4 //
children.translated_text: up to the sixteenth is <s>kiśora</s> (adolescence), and <s>yauvana</s> (youth) thereafter. || GRhtCM 1.29-30:4 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 1.29-30:5 ||
A child is incapable of knowing reality. || GRhtCM 1.29-30:6 ||

children.text: punaḥ ṣoḍaśavarṣebhyaḥ paraḥ viṣayarasāsvādalampaṭo bhavati viṣayāḥ śabdasparśarūparasagandhā rasāḥ śṛṅgārahāsyakaruṇaraudravīrabhayānakabībhatsādbhutaśāntāḥ // GRhtCM_1.29-30:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, after the sixteenth year, one becomes enamored of the relishing of sense pleasures. The sense objects (<s>viṣayas</s>) are sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. The <s>rasas</s> are: <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrifying), <s>bībhatsa</s> (odious), <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous), and <s>śānta</s> (peaceful). || GRhtCM 1.29-30:7 ||

children.text: kecit śāntaṃ rasaṃ na bruvanti nirvikāratvāt eteṣām āsvādaḥ svādas tatra lampaṭo vyāsaktaḥ atha vā viṣayānantaraṃ snehastatreti // GRhtCM_1.29-30:8 //
children.translated_text: Some do not include <s>śānta</s> (peaceful) as a <s>rasa</s>, because of its being without modification. The relishing (<s>āsvāda</s>) of these — 'enamored' means attached to that. Or alternatively, attachment following upon sense objects. || GRhtCM 1.29-30:8 ||

children.text: ataḥ parato jātaviveko bhavati utpannavicāro bhavati // GRhtCM_1.29-30:9 //
children.translated_text: After that, discrimination (<s>viveka</s>) arises; [the person] develops the capacity for inquiry. || GRhtCM 1.29-30:9 ||

children.text: tadā vṛddho'kṣamaḥ paraṃ manuṣyaḥ muktiṃ kaivalyaṃ katham āpnuyāt na kathamapītyartho vayasyupaplavabhāvāt // GRhtCM_1.29-30:10 //
children.translated_text: Then, being old and incapable, a mortal — how can he attain liberation (<s>mukti</s>), i.e., <s>kaivalya</s>? He cannot in any way — that is the meaning — because of the deterioration of faculties in [old] age. || GRhtCM 1.29-30:10 ||
START GRht 1.31

children.text: asminn eva śarīre yeṣāṃ paramātmano na saṃvedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who have no realization (<s>saṃveda</s>) of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) in this very body,
for them, after the abandoning of the body, that <s>Brahman</s> becomes even more distant. || GRht 1.31 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: pūrvapadyābhiprāyaṃ vicārya muktiprāptau praśaṅkitaḥ prāhāsminn ityādi // GRhtCM_1.31:1 //
children.translated_text: Having considered the purport of the previous verse and being apprehensive regarding the attainment of liberation, he says 'in this' and so forth. || GRhtCM 1.31:1 ||

children.text: asmin śarīre vartamāne kṣetrarūpe yeṣāṃ puṃsām ātmasaṃvedo na jātaḥ brahmajñānaṃ na jātaṃ teṣāṃ puṃsāmeva dehatyāgād ūrdhvaṃ śarīrotsargataḥ paścāt tadbrahma dūrataraṃ dūrāddūrataram ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.31:2 //
children.translated_text: In this body, while it is present, in this field-like [body] — for those persons in whom Self-realization has not arisen, in whom knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> has not arisen — for those very persons, after the abandoning of the body, i.e., after the casting off of the body, thereafter, that <s>Brahman</s> becomes even more distant, meaning more distant than distant. || GRhtCM 1.31:2 ||
START GRht 1.32

children.text: brahmādayo yajante yasmin divyāṃ tanuṃ samāśritya /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and others worship in which, having resorted to a divine body;
and other sages, liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>), endure until the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle). || GRht 1.32 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: adhunā pūrvamataṃ draḍhayati brahmādaya ityādi // GRhtCM_1.32:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he strengthens the previous view, saying '<s>Brahmā</s> and others' and so forth. || GRhtCM 1.32:1 ||

children.text: yasmin brahmādayo viṣṇurudrendrādayo brahmavido yajante saṃgatiṃ kurvanti samāpnuvantītyarthaḥ yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu atra saṃgatikaraṇam artho darśitaḥ // GRhtCM_1.32:2 //
children.translated_text: In which <s>Brahmā</s> and others, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and other knowers of <s>Brahman</s> worship — meaning they form an association, they attain [it]. [The root] <s>yaj</s> [is used] in the senses of worship of deities, forming association, and giving; here the sense of 'forming association' is indicated. || GRhtCM 1.32:2 ||

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā prāpnuvanti divyāṃ tanuṃ paramāṃ samāśritya samprāpya tebhyo brahmādibhyo 'pyanye apare munayo nāradādayo jīvanmuktā yajante saṃgatiṃ kurvanti // GRhtCM_1.32:3 //
children.translated_text: What having done do they attain? Having resorted to, having attained the divine body (<s>divyā tanu</s>) — the supreme [body] — other sages beyond even those <s>Brahmā</s> and others, namely <s>Nārada</s> and others who are <s>jīvanmuktā</s> (liberated while living), worship, form association [with it]. || GRhtCM 1.32:3 ||

children.text: te 'pi kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ kalpāntasthāyinaḥ pralayānte'pi tiṣṭhantīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_1.32:4 //
children.translated_text: What characterizes even them? They endure until the end of the <s>kalpa</s> — the meaning is that they persist even at the time of dissolution. || GRhtCM 1.32:4 ||
<s>Brahmā</s> and others simply persist. || GRhtCM 1.32:5 ||
[START GRht 1.33]
Therefore, by the <s>yogin</s> who aspires to liberation while living (<s>jīvanmukti</s>), first
a divine body must be fashioned, through the union of the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>. || GRht 1.33 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: iti bahudhā vicāryeṣṭavastustutim āha tasmād ityādi // GRhtCM_1.33:1 //
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated in many ways, he states the praise of the desired substance, beginning with 'therefore' and so forth. || GRhtCM 1.33:1 ||

children.text: yato brahmādayo jīvanmuktāś cānye divyāṃ tanuṃ vidhāya muktiṃ prāptās tasmāddhetor yoginā yogayuktena prathamaṃ divyā tanur vidheyā dṛḍhaśarīraṃ kāryam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.33:2 //
children.translated_text: Since <s>Brahmā</s> and others, as well as the other <s>jīvanmuktas</s>, having fashioned a divine body, attained liberation — therefore, for that reason, by a <s>yogin</s> who is endowed with <s>yoga</s>, first a divine body must be fashioned — meaning a firm body must be made. || GRhtCM 1.33:2 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭena yoginā jīvanmuktiṃ samīhamānena yoginā divyā tanur vidheyā // GRhtCM_1.33:3 //
children.translated_text: By a <s>yogin</s> of what qualification? By a <s>yogin</s> who aspires to <s>jīvanmukti</s>, a divine body must be fashioned. || GRhtCM 1.33:3 ||
By what means? Through the union of the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>. || GRhtCM 1.33:4 ||

children.text: umeśvarasṛṣṭo rasendras tasya sevanād ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.33:5 //
children.translated_text: The king of <s>rasas</s> (mercury) created by <s>Umā</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> — through its service, that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 1.33:5 ||

children.text: dṛḍhaśarīreṇa vāñchitaṃ sādhyate na tv anyathā // GRhtCM_1.33:6 //
children.translated_text: With a firm body, the desired goal is accomplished — but not otherwise. || GRhtCM 1.33:6 ||
[START GRht 1.34]
In the procedural method for its preparation too, by the wise person, the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory processes), which are flawless in each operation, must first
be known with effort. || GRht 1.34 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: divyatanorhetutvād rasendrasya sādhanavidhau sādhanopadeśe sudhiyā pūjyamatinā puṃsā prathamam aṣṭādaśasaṃskārāḥ prayatnena jñātavyāḥ // GRhtCM_1.34:1 //
children.translated_text: In the procedural instruction for the preparation of the king of <s>rasas</s>, which is the cause of the divine body — by a wise person, one of reverential disposition, the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> must first be known with effort. || GRhtCM 1.34:1 ||
That which is purified (<s>saṃskriyante</s>) — [those processes] are <s>saṃskāras</s>. || GRhtCM 1.34:2 ||

children.text: puṃsyapi garbhādhānādayaḥ ṣoḍaśa saṃskārā vartante ata eva saṃskārair ubhayoḥ sāmyaṃ doṣābhāvatvaṃ guṇavattvaṃ ca syāt // GRhtCM_1.34:3 //
children.translated_text: For a person too there exist sixteen <s>saṃskāras</s> beginning with <s>garbhādhāna</s> (conception rite); therefore, through the <s>saṃskāras</s>, there is equality between the two [mercury and a person] — freedom from defects and possession of good qualities would result. || GRhtCM 1.34:3 ||
Thus there would be [the equivalents of] <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>. || GRhtCM 1.34:4 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ saṃskārāḥ pratikarmanirmalāḥ karma karma prati nirdoṣāḥ // GRhtCM_1.34:5 //
children.translated_text: Of what character are the <s>saṃskāras</s>? They are flawless in each operation — faultless with respect to each procedure. || GRhtCM 1.34:5 ||
[START GRht 2.1-2]
<The 18 <s>saṃskāras</s>>
<s>Svedana</s> (sweating), <s>mardana</s> (grinding), <s>mūrcchana</s> (swooning), <s>utthāpana</s> (raising), <s>pātana</s> (distillation), <s>nirodhana</s> (confinement), <s>niyama</s> (restraint),
<s>dīpana</s> (kindling), <s>gagana</s> (sublimation into space), <s>grāsa</s> (swallowing), <s>pramāṇa</s> (proportioning), and then the procedure of <s>cāraṇa</s> (roaming). || GRht 2.1 ||
<s>Garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction), <s>bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction), <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation), <s>rasarāga</s> (coloring of mercury), <s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing), and also
<s>krāmaṇa</s> (pervading), <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) — [these along with] <s>bhakṣaṇa</s> (ingestion) [make] eighteen: thus are the operations on mercury. || GRht 2.2 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He whose fame is relied upon, whose very association is [cherished] by the gods —

children.text: sa śrīmān kārayāmāsa vṛttiṃ mugdhāvabodhinīm // GRhtCM_2.1-2:1 //
children.translated_text: that illustrious one caused the commentary named <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s> to be composed. || GRhtCM 2.1-2:1 ||
By the pair of <s>āryā</s> verses, the enumeration of the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> of mercury has been made. || GRhtCM 2.1-2:2 ||
[START GRht 2.3]
<1. <s>Svedana</s> (Sweating)>

With <s>āsurī</s> (mustard), <s>paṭu</s> (rock salt), the three pungents (<s>kaṭukatraya</s>), <s>citraka</s> (leadwort), fresh ginger (<s>ārdraka</s>), and radish (<s>mūlaka</s>), in portions of one-sixteenth,

children.text: sūtasya kāñjikena tridinaṃ mṛduvahninā svedaḥ // GRht_2.3 //
children.translated_text: the sweating of mercury [should be done] with <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) for three days over a gentle fire. || GRht 2.3 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: adhunā saṃskārāṇāṃ sādhane lakṣaṇam āha // GRhtCM_2.3:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the defining characteristic for accomplishing the <s>saṃskāras</s>. || GRhtCM 2.3:1 ||

children.text: tatra prathamoddiṣṭasya svedanasaṃskārasya sādhanaṃ spaṣṭayannāha āsurītyādi // GRhtCM_2.3:2 //
children.translated_text: Therein, clarifying the method for accomplishing the <s>svedana-saṃskāra</s> (sweating process), which was first enumerated, he says beginning with '<s>āsurī</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 2.3:2 ||

children.text: sūtasya pāradasya tridinaṃ dinatrayaparimāṇaṃ yathā syāttathā mṛduvahninā svalpāgninā svedaḥ svedanaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_2.3:3 //
children.translated_text: The sweating of mercury (<s>pārada</s>) should be performed for three days — meaning for the duration of three days — over a gentle fire, meaning with a small flame. || GRhtCM 2.3:3 ||
With what? With <s>kāñjika</s>, that is, <s>sauvīra</s> (a type of fermented gruel). || GRhtCM 2.3:4 ||
Together with what? Together with <s>āsurī</s>, <s>paṭu</s>, the three pungents, <s>citraka</s>, fresh ginger, and radish. || GRhtCM 2.3:5 ||

children.text: āsurī rājikā paṭu saindhavaṃ lavaṇaviśeṣaḥ kecitpaṭuśabdena kṣāramapi vyācakṣate kaṭukatrayaṃ śuṇṭhīmaricapippalyaḥ citrakaṃ pratītam ārdrakaṃ kandaviśeṣo nāgarahetuḥ mūlakaṃ kandaviśeṣaḥ prasiddhaḥ // GRhtCM_2.3:6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Āsurī</s> is <s>rājikā</s> (mustard); <s>paṭu</s> is <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), a particular type of salt — some explain <s>paṭu</s> as also meaning alkali (<s>kṣāra</s>); <s>kaṭukatraya</s> (the three pungents) are dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>), black pepper (<s>marica</s>), and long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>); <s>citraka</s> is well-known [as leadwort]; <s>ārdraka</s> is a particular tuber, the source of dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>); <s>mūlaka</s> is a well-known particular tuber [radish]. || GRhtCM 2.3:6 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭairetaiḥ kalāṃśaiḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśaiḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśaḥ pratyekaṃ saṃyujyate // GRhtCM_2.3:7 //
children.translated_text: Of what specification are these? In portions of one-sixteenth (<s>kalāṃśa</s>) — one-sixteenth part is combined for each [ingredient]. || GRhtCM 2.3:7 ||
This explanation is agreed upon by all. || GRhtCM 2.3:8 ||

children.text: atra viśeṣaḥ kāñjike sarvadhānyāmlasaṃdhānaṃ tuṣavarjye tu kārayet // GRhtCM_2.3:9 //
children.translated_text: Here a specification: the <s>kāñjika</s> should be prepared as a fermentation of all grains with sour [agents], excluding husks. || GRhtCM 2.3:9 ||

children.text: uragā triphalā krāntā laghuparṇī śatāvarī // GRhtCM_2.3:10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Uragā</s>, <s>triphalā</s> (the three fruits), <s>krāntā</s>, <s>laghuparṇī</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s> — || GRhtCM 2.3:10 ||

children.text: tena yuktaṃ rasasvinnaṃ tridinaṃ mṛduvahninā // GRhtCM_2.3:11 //
children.translated_text: with that, the mercury being sweated for three days over a gentle fire — || GRhtCM 2.3:11 ||
by means of the <s>dolā-yantra</s> (swinging apparatus), vigorously grinding again and again —
thus from the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s>. || GRhtCM 2.3:12 ||

children.text: kṣārāmlair oṣadhair vāpi dolāyantre sthitasya hi /
children.translated_text: The cooking of [mercury] placed in the <s>dolā-yantra</s> with alkalis, sour substances, or herbs —
that is called <s>svedana</s> (sweating), which causes the loosening of impurities.
Thus the definition. || GRhtCM 2.3:13 ||
Having filled a vessel to half its belly with liquid substances,
and having carefully made two openings on both sides of its mouth — || GRhtCM 2.3:14 ||
one should place a rod across its top, and in the middle of that, having tied a pouch of mercury,
one should sweat it — this is known as the <s>dolā-yantra</s> (swinging apparatus).
Thus the definition of the <s>dolā-yantra</s>. || GRhtCM 2.3:15 ||
[START GRht 2.4]
<2. <s>Mardana</s> (Grinding)>
With jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), burnt wool (<s>dagdhorṇā</s>), and salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>), together with <s>mandira</s> (temple soot?), smoke-brick (<s>dhūmeṣṭakā</s>), and mustard (<s>āsurī</s>),
in measures of one-sixteenth of the mercury, with <s>kāñjika</s>, the grinding [should be done] for three days. || GRht 2.4 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: dvitīyoddiṣṭasya mardanasya sādhanaṃ spaṣṭayannāha guḍetyādi // GRhtCM_2.4:1 //
children.translated_text: Clarifying the method for accomplishing <s>mardana</s> (grinding), which was enumerated second, he says beginning with '<s>guḍa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 2.4:1 ||

children.text: etair auṣadhair dinatrayaṃ parimāṇaṃ rasasya mardanaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_2.4:2 //
children.translated_text: With these medicinal substances, the grinding of mercury should be done for a duration of three days. || GRhtCM 2.4:2 ||

children.text: etaiḥ kaiḥ guḍadagdhorṇālavaṇaiḥ guḍa ikṣuvikāraḥ prasiddhaḥ dagdhorṇā dagdhā cāsau ūrṇā ceti samāsaḥ ūrṇā pratītā meṣaromanicayam ityarthaḥ lavaṇaṃ saindhavamekaṃ guḍadagdhorṇārajanī iti vā pāṭhaḥ tatra haridrā grāhyā na saindhavam // GRhtCM_2.4:3 //
children.translated_text: With what are these? With jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), burnt wool (<s>dagdhorṇā</s>), and salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>). <s>Guḍa</s> is the well-known product of sugarcane; <s>dagdhorṇā</s> is a compound: 'burnt' and 'wool' — <s>ūrṇā</s> is well-known as the collection of sheep's hair, that is the meaning; <s>lavaṇa</s> is rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) alone. An alternative reading is '<s>guḍa-dagdhorṇā-rajanī</s>' — in that case, turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>) should be taken, not rock salt. || GRhtCM 2.4:3 ||
In measures of one-sixteenth of mercury — meaning in proportions of one-sixteenth relative to mercury. || GRhtCM 2.4:4 ||
The word 'portion' (<s>aṃśa</s>) has a connection with each [ingredient] individually. || GRhtCM 2.4:5 ||

children.text: viśeṣaścātra vastraiścaturguṇair baddhaḥ sūtaḥ sthāpyaḥ śubhe 'hani // GRhtCM_2.4:6 //
children.translated_text: And the specification here: the mercury, bound in cloth folded four times, should be placed on an auspicious day. || GRhtCM 2.4:6 ||

children.text: lohārkāśmajakhalve tu tapteṣveva tu mardayet // GRhtCM_2.4:7 //
children.translated_text: One should grind in a mortar made of iron, copper, or stone — and only when heated. || GRhtCM 2.4:7 ||
Together with the enumerated medicinal herbs and all sour substances including <s>kāñjika</s>,

children.text: peṣaṇaṃ mardanākhyaṃ syāttadbahirmalanāśanam iti paribhāṣā // GRhtCM_2.4:8 //
children.translated_text: the grinding is called <s>mardana</s> — it destroys the external impurities. Thus the definition. || GRhtCM 2.4:8 ||

children.text: atra yantraṃ tu khalvākhyaṃ jñeyam // GRhtCM_2.4:9 //
children.translated_text: The apparatus here should be known as the mortar (<s>khalva</s>). || GRhtCM 2.4:9 ||

children.text: tallakṣaṇaṃ tu khalvayogyā śilā nīlā śyāmā snigdhā dṛḍhā guruḥ // GRhtCM_2.4:10 //
children.translated_text: Its defining characteristic: the stone suitable for the mortar should be blue-black, dark, smooth, firm, and heavy. || GRhtCM 2.4:10 ||
Sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in height and nine <s>aṅgulas</s> in breadth. || GRhtCM 2.4:11 ||
The defining characteristic of the stone suitable for the mortar has been stated incidentally. || GRhtCM 2.4:12 ||

children.text: utsedhena navāṅgulaḥ khalu kalātulyāṅgulāyāmavān vistāreṇa daśāṅgulo 'tha munibhir nimnas tathaivāṅgulaiḥ // GRhtCM_2.4:13 //
children.translated_text: Nine <s>aṅgulas</s> in height, the mortar is as long as a digit-measure (<s>kalā</s>) in <s>aṅgulas</s>, ten <s>aṅgulas</s> in breadth; then, according to the sages, the same [number of] <s>aṅgulas</s> in depth; || GRhtCM 2.4:13 ||

children.text: pālyāṃ hy aṅgulavistaraśca masṛṇo 'tīvārdhacandropamo gharṣo dvādaśakāṅgulaśca tadayaṃ khalvo mato mardane iti // GRhtCM_2.4:14 //
children.translated_text: the rim is one <s>aṅgula</s> wide, very smooth, shaped like a half-moon; the pestle is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> — this mortar is considered [appropriate] for grinding. || GRhtCM 2.4:14 ||
[START GRht 2.5-6]
<3. <s>Mūrchana</s> (Swooning)>
Named <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>śikhi</s> (fire [= internal heat]), and <s>viṣa</s> (poison), these are the three natural defects of mercury.

children.text: mūrchāṃ malena kurute śikhinā dāhaṃ viṣeṇa mṛtyuṃ ca // GRht_2.5 //
children.translated_text: Due to <s>mala</s>, it causes <s>mūrcchā</s> (fainting/stupor); due to <s>śikhi</s> (fire), burning; and due to <s>viṣa</s> (poison), death. || GRht 2.5 ||

children.text: gṛhakanyā harati malaṃ triphalāgniṃ citrakaśca viṣam /
children.translated_text: <s>Gṛhakanyā</s> (aloe vera) removes the impurity; <s>triphalā</s> (the three fruits) [removes] the fire; and <s>citraka</s> (leadwort) [removes] the poison.

children.text: tasmād ebhir miśrair vārān saṃmūrchayetsapta // GRht_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, mixed with these, one should perform <s>mūrchana</s> seven times. || GRht 2.6 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: rasasya pāradasya doṣās trayo vartante // GRhtCM_2.5-6:1 //
children.translated_text: Mercury (<s>pārada</s>) has three defects. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:1 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ malaśikhiviṣābhidhānāḥ malaśca śikhī ca viṣaṃ ca tānyevābhidhānaṃ nāma yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:2 //
children.translated_text: Of what nature? Named <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>śikhi</s> (fire), and <s>viṣa</s> (poison) — impurity, fire, and poison: those which have these as their names are so-called. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:2 ||

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ naisargikāḥ nisarga utpattis tatsambandhinaḥ sahajā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:3 //
children.translated_text: And of what further nature? Natural (<s>naisargika</s>) — <s>nisarga</s> means birth/origin; related to that, meaning innate. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:3 ||

children.text: viśeṣaścātra malādyāḥ pañcadoṣāḥ syur bhūjādyāḥ saptakañcukāḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:4 //
children.translated_text: And the specification here: 'the five defects beginning with <s>mala</s>, and the seven sheaths (<s>kañcuka</s>) beginning with <s>bhūja</s>' — || GRhtCM 2.5-6:4 ||

children.text: kuṣṭānaṣṭau rasāntaḥsthā rase te 'nantadoṣadāḥ iti rasasaṃketakalikāyām // GRhtCM_2.5-6:5 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kuṣṭha</s> and <s>anaṣṭa</s> residing within mercury — they produce endless defects in mercury.' Thus in the <s>Rasa-saṅketa-kalikā</s>. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:5 ||

children.text: yadyapi rasendramaṅgale pañca malādayo naisargikā doṣāḥ kathitās tathāpyatra traya eva anye dve gurutvacapalatve naisargikadoṣarūpe kuto na staḥ tribhiḥ svedanamardanamūrchanātmakaiḥ saṃskārair anivṛtteḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:6 //
children.translated_text: Although in the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s> five natural defects beginning with <s>mala</s> are described, nevertheless here only three are [mentioned]. Why are not the other two — heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>) and fickleness (<s>capalatva</s>) — which are also natural defects, [mentioned]? Because they are not removed by the three <s>saṃskāras</s> of <s>svedana</s>, <s>mardana</s>, and <s>mūrchana</s>. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:6 ||

children.text: naisargikagrahaṇād vaikārikāṇām api grahaṇaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_2.5-6:7 //
children.translated_text: By the mention of 'natural,' the acquired (<s>vaikārika</s>) [defects] would also be included. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:7 ||

children.text: atra naisargikā uktā vaikārikāḥ kuto noktāḥ vaikārikāṇāṃ bhāvābhāvāt // GRhtCM_2.5-6:8 //
children.translated_text: Here the natural [defects] are stated — why are the acquired ones not stated? Because of the potential presence or absence of the acquired [defects]. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:8 ||

children.text: raso doṣatrayāvṛtaḥ prāśyamānaḥ kiṃ karoti malena maladoṣeṇa mūrchām indriyamohaṃ kurute śikhinā vahninā dāhaṃ viṣeṇa mṛtyuṃ maraṇaṃ ceti samuccaye // GRhtCM_2.5-6:9 //
children.translated_text: Mercury, enveloped by the three defects, when consumed — what does it cause? Due to <s>mala</s>, the defect of impurity, it causes <s>mūrcchā</s> (stupor of the senses); due to <s>śikhi</s> (fire), burning; and due to <s>viṣa</s> (poison), <s>mṛtyu</s> (death) — the conjunction [of all three is implied]. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:9 ||
The purport is that the removal of these must be carried out. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:10 ||
The reduction to powder (<s>piṣṭitva</s>) through the destruction of [mercury's] inherent form —

children.text: vidvadbhir jitasūto 'sau naṣṭapiṣṭaḥ sa ucyate // GRhtCM_2.5-6:11 //
children.translated_text: learned ones say that mercury so conquered is called <s>naṣṭa-piṣṭa</s> (destroyed-powdered). || GRhtCM 2.5-6:11 ||
That which causes the <s>naṣṭa-piṣṭa</s> state through the medicaments prescribed for <s>mardana</s> —

children.text: tanmūrchanam iti proktaṃ doṣatrayavināśanam iti // GRhtCM_2.5-6:12 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>mūrchana</s>, which destroys the three defects. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:12 ||

children.text: yantram atra khalvam eva pūrvoktaṃ yat // GRhtCM_2.5-6:13 //
children.translated_text: The apparatus here is the mortar (<s>khalva</s>) itself, which was previously described. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:13 ||
He states the removal of the three defects and <s>mūrchana</s> beginning with '<s>gṛhakanyā</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:14 ||

children.text: gṛhakanyā gṛhakumārikā malaṃ prathamaṃ doṣaṃ harati // GRhtCM_2.5-6:15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gṛhakanyā</s> (aloe vera, lit. 'house-maiden') removes <s>mala</s> (impurity), the first defect. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:15 ||

children.text: punastriphalā trayāṇāṃ phalānāṃ samāhāraḥ triphalā agniṃ dvitīyaṃ doṣaṃ harati samāhāro yathā ekā harītakī yojyā dvau ca yojyau vibhītakau /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>triphalā</s>, the aggregate of three fruits, removes <s>agni</s> (fire), the second defect. The aggregate is as follows: one <s>harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan) is to be used, and two <s>vibhītaka</s> (beleric myrobalan),
and four <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry) — this is declared to be <s>triphalā</s>.
Thus. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:16 ||

children.text: punaścitrako'gniḥ viṣaṃ tṛtīyaṃ doṣaṃ harati dūrīkarotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:17 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>citraka</s> (<s>agni</s>, leadwort) removes <s>viṣa</s> (poison), the third defect — meaning it drives it away. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:17 ||

children.text: tasmāddhetor ebhis tribhir gṛhakanyātriphalācitrakair miśritair ekīkṛtai rasaṃ sapta vārānmūrchayet vidhivanmūrchanaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_2.5-6:18 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, for that reason, with these three — <s>gṛhakanyā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>citraka</s> — mixed together, made into one, one should perform <s>mūrchana</s> on mercury seven times, carrying out the <s>mūrchana</s> according to the prescribed method. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:18 ||
And the specification here:
The <s>mūrchana</s> of the king of <s>rasas</s> should always be performed by practitioners —
first with poisons and <s>triphalā</s>, and likewise with <s>bṛhatī</s> (nightshade) and <s>upaviṣa</s> (sub-poisons), || GRhtCM 2.5-6:19 ||
with <s>karkoṭī</s>, with alkali (<s>kṣāra</s>) and <s>kanda</s> (tuber), with <s>citraka</s>, and with <s>gṛhakanyā</s> —

children.text: ekenāpyatha saṃmardyo yāmamekaṃ tu pāradaḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:20 //
children.translated_text: with even one of these, the mercury should be ground for one <s>yāma</s> (three-hour period). || GRhtCM 2.5-6:20 ||
Taking the <s>kiṃnara-yantra</s> (a specific apparatus), one should coat its base with the herb;
the mercury, combined with fresh <s>tāra</s> (silver), should be placed in the middle of the apparatus. || GRhtCM 2.5-6:21 ||

children.text: dadyād rasopari śarāvaṃ saṃdhilepaṃ dṛḍhaṃ mṛdā /
children.translated_text: One should place a lid (<s>śarāva</s>) over the mercury, [and apply] joint-paste (<s>saṃdhilepa</s>) firmly with clay;

children.text: lavaṇena ca sampūrya dvāraṃ saṃrudhya yatnataḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:22 //
children.translated_text: and having filled with salt and carefully blocked the opening — || GRhtCM 2.5-6:22 ||
'Place upon the furnace (<s>cuhlī</s>) and the wise one should kindle a blazing fire;

children.text: yāmaikena taduttārya kartavyaḥ śītalo rasaḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:23 //
children.translated_text: after one <s>yāma</s> (three hours), remove it and make the mercury cool.' // GRhtCM 2.5-6:23 //
'Having carefully extracted the mercury from the apparatus, sublimate the calcined (<s>mūrchita</s>) [mercury];

children.text: amūrchitas tadā deyaḥ kalāṃśaṃ mūrchite rasaḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:24 //
children.translated_text: when it is uncalcined, one should add a fractional portion of [calcined] mercury to the [uncalcined] mercury.' // GRhtCM 2.5-6:24 //

children.text: sindhūtthaṭaṅkaṇābhyāṃ ca mardayen madhusaṃyutaṃ dolāyantre tataḥ svedyaḥ kṣārāmlalavaṇaiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: 'Grind with borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>) derived from <s>Sindh</s> salt, mixed with honey; then steam it in a swing-apparatus (<s>dolā-yantra</s>) together with alkalis, sour substances, and salts.
Then sublimate and calcine the lord of mercuries (<s>raseśvara</s>) again and again;
the sublimation should be performed twenty-one times.' // GRhtCM 2.5-6:25 //
Thus [ends the citation] from the <s>Rasasāra</s>. // GRhtCM 2.5-6:26 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 2.7]
<Processing: Sublimation (<s>utthāpana</s>)>
By this grinding, indeed, thoroughly purified, freed from lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>),
the mercury, sublimated in a distillation apparatus (<s>pātana-yantra</s>), [rises] from the decoction of sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>). // GRht 2.7 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: sūto nāgavaṅgaparimukto bhavati nāgavaṅgābhyāṃ doṣābhyāṃ virahitaḥ pārado bhavatītyarthaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ san samutthitaḥ san // GRhtCM_2.7:1 //
children.translated_text: The mercury becomes freed from lead and tin — separated from the defects of lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), the mercury becomes [pure] — this is the meaning. Of what quality? Having been sublimated (<s>samutthita</s>). // GRhtCM 2.7:1 //
In the distillation apparatus (<s>pātana-yantra</s>) — in the sealed junction of two vessels — properly raised by the [correct] procedure. // GRhtCM 2.7:2 //

children.text: kasmāt kāñjikaṃ sauvīraṃ pūrvavarṇitaṃ tatkvāthasaṃyogād ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.7:3 //
children.translated_text: From what? '<s>Kāñjika</s>' means <s>sauvīra</s> (sour gruel), as previously described; from the combination with its decoction — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 2.7:3 //
'<s>Hi</s>' (indeed) — with certainty. // GRhtCM 2.7:4 //

children.text: amunā virecanena uktaśodhanena sūtaḥ suviśuddho bhavet viśeṣaśuddho bhaved ityutthāpanam // GRhtCM_2.7:5 //
children.translated_text: By this purging — by the stated purification — the mercury becomes thoroughly purified, specially pure — this is <s>utthāpana</s> (sublimation). // GRhtCM 2.7:5 //

children.text: anena vidhinā hiṅgulasthasya sūtasyāpi utthāpanaṃ bhavati // GRhtCM_2.7:6 //
children.translated_text: By this method, the sublimation of mercury present in cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>) is also accomplished. // GRhtCM 2.7:6 //
'The restoration to its own essential form through the process of steaming and the like —
that is called <s>utthāpana</s> (sublimation), the destruction of the ill-effects of calcination (<s>mūrchā</s>).' // GRhtCM 2.7:7-8 //
'<s>Ut</s>' (upward) + '<s>sthāpana</s>' (placing) = <s>utthāpana</s> (sublimation/upward-placing). // GRhtCM 2.7:9 //
The apparatus for this:
'With a circumference of eight <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths) and a height of ten <s>aṅgulas</s>,
with a depth of four <s>aṅgulas</s>, a water-reservoir [placed] one <s>aṅgula</s> below — // GRhtCM 2.7:10 //
the mouth of the lower vessel, and [the mouth] of the upper vessel,
should be inserted into [a vessel] whose back is sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> wide, at the opening. // GRhtCM 2.7:11 //
On the sides, smear with buffalo milk, [grain] powder, frog [essence], and molasses (<s>phāṇita</s>). // GRhtCM 2.7:12 //

children.text: vilipya śoṣayet saṃdhiṃ jalādhāre jalaṃ kṣipet /
children.translated_text: After smearing, dry the joint; pour water into the water-reservoir;
place this upon the stove — this is called the distillation apparatus (<s>pātana-yantra</s>).' // GRhtCM 2.7:13 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 2.7:14 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 2.8]
<Processing: Distillation (<s>pātana</s>) — Upward distillation (<s>ūrdhvapātana</s>)>
Having made a paste with copper (<s>śulba</s>), it is distilled, [freeing it] from the suspicion of lead and tin;

children.text: tasmindoṣān muktvā nipatati śuddhas tathā sūtaḥ // GRht_2.8 //
children.translated_text: having released those defects, the purified mercury falls down. // GRht 2.8 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Clarifying the distillation process (<s>pātana-saṃskāra</s>) described as the fifth [process], [the author] says 'having made' and so forth. // GRhtCM 2.8:1 //

children.text: tu punaḥ utthitaṃ sūtaṃ śulbapiṣṭiṃ kṛtvā śulbena tāmreṇa saha tayormelanaṃ yathā syāttathā peṣaṇaṃ vidhāya tasmin pātanayantre nipātyate karmavideti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_2.8:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Tu</s>' (further/again) — having made the sublimated mercury into a paste with copper (<s>śulba</s>), i.e., with copper (<s>tāmra</s>), the grinding being done so as to effect their combination — the person skilled in procedure distills it in that distillation apparatus; the rest [of the sentence is implied]. // GRhtCM 2.8:2 //
From what [defect]? From the suspicion of lead and tin — weakened by the defects of lead and tin. // GRhtCM 2.8:3 //

children.text: tathā uktavidhānena nipatati sati pātanakarmaṇi kṛte sati śuddhaḥ sūto bhavet // GRhtCM_2.8:4 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Tathā</s>' (thus) — by the stated method, when it falls [in the distillation], when the act of distillation is performed, the mercury becomes pure. // GRhtCM 2.8:4 //

children.text: vāramityanukte granthāntare trisaptaikaviṃśativāraṃ pātanakarmaṇi kṛte sati samyak nāgavaṅgaśaṅkā naśyatīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_2.8:5 //
children.translated_text: Though the number of repetitions is not stated [in the root text], in other texts, the suspicion of lead and tin is destroyed when the distillation is performed twenty-one times, i.e., three times seven — this is the purport. // GRhtCM 2.8:5 //
And the specifics for the distillation apparatus:
'Two parts of purified mercury combined with one part of copper;

children.text: viṃśāṃśaṃ lavaṇaṃ dattvā piṣṭīkuryācca sundaram // GRhtCM_2.8:6 //
children.translated_text: add one-twentieth [part] of salt, and make a fine paste. // GRhtCM 2.8:6 //
The lower vessel is eight <s>aṅgulas</s> wide, ten <s>aṅgulas</s> in length;
with a water-reservoir made four <s>aṅgulas</s> [deep] all around below the neck. // GRhtCM 2.8:7 //
The mouth of the inner vessel enters within; its own lip-edge is submerged in water;
on top, a flat-bottomed pot (<s>ciṇṭī-ghaṭī</s>) is placed, sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> wide at its belly. // GRhtCM 2.8:8 //
In that lower-upper vessel [assembly], when distilled, freed from all defects,

children.text: sutarāṃ bhavati rasendro jīrṇagrāso'pi pātyo'sau // GRhtCM_2.8:9 //
children.translated_text: the king of mercuries (<s>rasendra</s>) becomes exceedingly [pure]; even [mercury] that has consumed its dose should be distilled.' // GRhtCM 2.8:9 //

children.text: adha ūrdhvaṃ tathā tiryak pātastrividha ucyate /
children.translated_text: 'Downward, upward, and oblique — distillation (<s>pāta</s>) is declared to be threefold;

children.text: yatra tiṣṭhati sūtendro vahnis tatrānyathā jalam // GRhtCM_2.8:10 //
children.translated_text: where the king of mercuries sits, there is fire; on the other [side], water.' // GRhtCM 2.8:10 //
'The expulsion — upward, downward, or obliquely — of mercury ground with the stated herbs
and placed in the apparatus, is called <s>pātana</s> (distillation); it destroys the skin-covering produced by the contact of tin and lead (serpent).' // GRhtCM 2.8:11 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 2.8:12 //

children.text: ūrdhvapāte rasasyordhvagamanaṃ tatrādhaḥpātre vahniḥ jalamūrdhvapātre adhaḥpāte tu rasasyādhastādgamanaṃ bhavati yantraṃ tadeva paraṃ tu agnijalayorvyatyāsaḥ jalam atrādhaḥpātre agnirūrdhvapātre tiryakpāte tu rasastiryak patati tatraikapātrapṛṣṭhe jalam anyapātrādho vahniḥ // GRhtCM_2.8:13 //
children.translated_text: In upward distillation (<s>ūrdhva-pāta</s>), the mercury moves upward; there, fire is below and water in the upper vessel. In downward distillation (<s>adhaḥ-pāta</s>), the mercury moves downward; the apparatus is the same, but the fire and water are reversed — water is in the lower vessel, fire in the upper. In oblique distillation (<s>tiryak-pāta</s>), the mercury falls sideways; there, water is on the back of one vessel, and fire is beneath the other. // GRhtCM 2.8:13 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 2.9-16]
<Distillation apparatus (<s>pātana-yantra</s>)>
The lower vessel is eight <s>aṅgulas</s> wide, ten <s>aṅgulas</s> in length;
with a water-reservoir raised four <s>aṅgulas</s> [deep] below the neck. // GRht 2.9 //
The mouth of the inner vessel enters within; its own lip-edge is submerged in water;
on top, a flat pot (<s>cipiṭa-ghaṭī</s>) is placed, sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> wide at its belly. // GRht 2.10 //
In that upper vessel, when distilled, freed from all defects,

children.text: sutarāṃ bhavati rasendro dravye ca rasāyane yogyaḥ // GRht_2.11 //
children.translated_text: the king of mercuries (<s>rasendra</s>) becomes exceedingly [pure] — fit for use in [alchemical] substances and in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). // GRht 2.11 //
<Downward distillation (<s>adhaḥpātana</s>)>
Having made an ash-paste (<s>naṣṭa-piṣṭi</s>) with <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>śikhi</s> (chitraka), <s>śigru</s> (horseradish tree), mustard (<s>rājikā</s>), and sharp [substances],
smear it in the upper vessel; with a kindled fire of one <s>pala</s> [of fuel], it should be distilled downward. // GRht 2.12 //
Alternatively, when distilled in a lamp-apparatus (<s>dīpaka-yantra</s>), [it is] freed from all defects.
<Oblique distillation (<s>tiryakpātana</s>)>
The king of mercuries should be distilled by the method of oblique distillation. // GRht 2.13 //
A sheet of finely prepared mica (<s>abhra-dala</s>), combined with the king of mercuries (<s>rasendra</s>), along with sour gruel (<s>aranāla</s>),

children.text: khalve dattvā mṛditaṃ yāvat tannaṣṭapiṣṭatām eti // GRht_2.14 //
children.translated_text: placed in a mortar and ground until it attains the state of an ash-paste (<s>naṣṭa-piṣṭa</s>). // GRht 2.14 //
One should make the mercury distilled by the oblique method; gradually, over steady fire,

children.text: saṃsvedya pātyate'sau na patati yāvaddṛḍhaścāgniḥ // GRht_2.15 //
children.translated_text: it is steamed and distilled — it does not fall [back] as long as the fire is steady. // GRht 2.15 //
<Confinement (<s>nirodhana</s>)>
Weakened by grinding, calcination, and distillation, from having been overly processed, it attains feeble potency;

children.text: sṛṣṭyambujair nirodhāllabdhāpyāyo na ṣaṇḍhaḥ syāt // GRht_2.16 //
children.translated_text: [but] by confinement (<s>nirodhana</s>) with excretory substances (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>) and lotuses (<s>ambuja</s>/salt), having regained its nourishment, it should not become impotent (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>). // GRht 2.16 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Clarifying the confinement process (<s>nirodhana-saṃskāra</s>) described as the sixth, [the author] says 'by grinding' and so forth. // GRhtCM 2.9-16:1 //

children.text: etair mardanamūrchanapātaiḥ saṃskāraviśeṣaṃ kṛtvā mandavīryatvāt kadarthito bhavati // GRhtCM_2.9-16:2 //
children.translated_text: By these — grinding, calcination, and distillation — having undergone a special treatment, [mercury] becomes weakened due to feeble potency. // GRhtCM 2.9-16:2 //

children.text: kutsitavidhānena kadarthito bhavatītyarthaḥ punaḥ sūtaḥ sṛṣṭyambujaiḥ saha mardanānantaraṃ nirodhāt mūṣādvayasampuṭe kūpikāyāṃ vā nirodhāt rundhanāt labdhāpyāyaḥ prāptabalaḥ san na ṣaṇḍhaḥ syāt na śukrarahito bhavati // GRhtCM_2.9-16:3 //
children.translated_text: It becomes oppressed by inferior procedure — this is the meaning. Further, the mercury, after grinding with excretory substances and salts (<s>ambuja</s>), by confinement (<s>nirodhana</s>) — in a sealed junction of two crucibles (<s>mūṣā</s>) or in a flask (<s>kūpikā</s>) — by confinement, by sealing — having regained its nourishment (<s>labdhāpyāya</s>), having obtained [renewed] strength, it should not become impotent (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>), should not become devoid of semen (<s>śukra</s>). // GRhtCM 2.9-16:3 //

children.text: sṛṣṭiḥ mūtraśukraśoṇitarūpā ambujaṃ lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ kamalam iti mandāḥ // GRhtCM_2.9-16:4 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Sṛṣṭi</s>' (excretory substances) is of the form of urine, semen, and blood; '<s>ambuja</s>' (lotus) means salt, rock-salt (<s>saindhava</s>), or lotus — according to the less-informed commentators. // GRhtCM 2.9-16:4 //
The definition of <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (excretory substances):
'The urine and semen and blood of cows, goats, sheep, men, and women —
this is declared to be <s>sṛṣṭi</s>, the destroyer of the defect of impotency (<s>ṣaṇḍha-doṣa</s>).'
From the <s>Śaktyavatāra</s>. // GRhtCM 2.9-16:5 //
The apparatus, as follows:
'With red rock-salt forming the lump-binding (<s>khoṭa</s>), one should prepare a pair of crucibles (<s>mūṣā</s>);

children.text: tatsampuṭe rasaṃ kṣiptvā navasāraṃ sanimbukam // GRhtCM_2.9-16:6 //
children.translated_text: placing mercury into that sealed junction, along with sal ammoniac (<s>navasāra</s>) and lemon (<s>nimbuka</s>) — // GRhtCM 2.9-16:6 //
seal the joint of the sealed junction carefully with the best [sealant];
taking <s>vajra-mṛtsnā</s> (adamantine clay), wrap it around with care. // GRhtCM 2.9-16:7 //
Having dried it in the shade, then place it in a pit in the ground;
eight <s>aṅgulas</s> above the crucible, fill [the pit] there. // GRhtCM 2.9-16:8 //
For a period of twenty-one days, maintain a cow-dung fire;

children.text: dine dine prakartavyā mūṣā saindhavanūtanā // GRhtCM_2.9-16:9 //
children.translated_text: day by day, the crucible should be freshly [sealed] with rock-salt. // GRhtCM 2.9-16:9 //
Steam it carefully, then place it in the underground pit;
alternatively, [place] the mercury combined with rock-salt inside a flask (<s>kūpikā</s>). // GRhtCM 2.9-16:10 //
It should then be placed in the underground pit for a period of twenty-one days;

children.text: ayaṃ nirodhako nāmnā mahāmukhakaro rase // GRhtCM_2.9-16:11 //
children.translated_text: this [process] is called <s>nirodhaka</s> (confinement) by name — it is the great mouth-opening agent (<s>mahā-mukha-kara</s>) for mercury.' // GRhtCM 2.9-16:11 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 2.9-16:12 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 2.17]
<7. Restraint (<s>niyamana</s>)>

children.text: iti labdhavīryaḥ samyak capalo'sau saṃniyamyate tadanu /
children.translated_text: Thus, having properly obtained potency, that restless [mercury] is thereafter restrained
by steaming with <s>phaṇī</s> (betel), garlic, lotus/salt (<s>ambuja</s>), <s>mārkava</s> (Bhṛṅgarāja), <s>karkoṭī</s> (a bitter gourd), and tamarind (<s>ciñcikā</s>). // GRht 2.17 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Clarifying the processing described as the seventh, [the author] says 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM 2.17:1 //

children.text: iti pūrvoktavidhānena yantraṇādinā tadanu rodhanānantaram asau capalaścañcalo raso niyamyate karmavidā saṃniyamanaṃ kriyate // GRhtCM_2.17:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus' — by the previously described method, by the apparatus and the rest, 'thereafter' — after the confinement — that restless, fickle mercury is restrained; the restraint process (<s>saṃniyamana</s>) is performed by the skilled practitioner. // GRhtCM 2.17:2 //

children.text: kasmāt phaṇīlaśunāmbujamārkavakarkoṭīciñcikāsvedāt phaṇī tāmbūlaṃ laśunaṃ rasonaḥ ambujaṃ lavaṇaṃ mārkavaḥ bhṛṅgarājaḥ karkoṭīti pratītā vandhyā ciñcikā amlikā etābhiḥ saha yaḥ svedaḥ yantre agnitāpaḥ tasmāt // GRhtCM_2.17:3 //
children.translated_text: By what? By steaming with betel (<s>phaṇī</s> = <s>tāmbūla</s>), garlic (<s>laśuna</s> = <s>rasona</s>), salt (<s>ambuja</s> = <s>lavaṇa</s>), <s>mārkava</s> (= <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>), <s>karkoṭī</s> (a well-known barren [gourd variety]), and tamarind (<s>ciñcikā</s> = <s>amlikā</s>); the steaming with these — the heating by fire in an apparatus — by that. // GRhtCM 2.17:3 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ samyak labdhavīryaḥ prāptabalo vīryavān rasaḥ capalatvanivṛttaye niyamyata ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.17:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? 'Having properly obtained potency' — having obtained strength, the potent mercury is restrained for the cessation of its restlessness — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 2.17:4 //

children.text: viśeṣaścātra kācakūpīṃ mṛdā lipya raso madhye vimucyate /
children.translated_text: And the specifics here: 'A glass flask (<s>kāca-kūpī</s>) is smeared with clay, and the mercury is released inside;

children.text: kalāṃśaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ dattvā madhye kiṃcit pradīyate // GRhtCM_2.17:5 //
children.translated_text: a fractional amount of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>) is added, and a little [material] is placed inside. // GRhtCM 2.17:5 //
A firm door-seal should be made with adamantine clay (<s>vajra-mṛttikā</s>);

children.text: bhūgarbhe kūpikāṃ sthāpya sitayā garbhapūraṇam // GRhtCM_2.17:6 //
children.translated_text: having placed the flask in an underground pit, fill the interior with white [material]. // GRhtCM 2.17:6 //
A cow-dung fire should be maintained for a period of twenty-one days;
this [process] is called <s>niyāmaka</s> (the restrainer) by name — it counteracts [excessive] fire.' // GRhtCM 2.17:7 //
'For the restraint of restlessness in [mercury] that has obtained potency through confinement,

children.text: kriyate yo rasasvedaḥ proktaṃ niyamanaṃ hi tat // GRhtCM_2.17:8 //
children.translated_text: the steaming of mercury that is performed — that is declared to be <s>niyamana</s> (restraint).' // GRhtCM 2.17:8 //
Thus. // GRhtCM 2.17:9 //
The characteristics of the apparatus:
'Holding four <s>prasthas</s> (measures) of water, with a neck-opening of four <s>aṅgulas</s> —

children.text: ghaṭayantramidaṃ proktaṃ tadāpyāyanakaṃ smṛtam iti // GRhtCM_2.17:10 //
children.translated_text: this is declared to be the pot-apparatus (<s>ghaṭa-yantra</s>), also known as the nourishment apparatus (<s>āpyāyanaka</s>).' // GRhtCM 2.17:10 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 2.18]
<8. Kindling (<s>dīpana</s>)>

With earth-substance (<s>bhū</s>), bird-substance (<s>khaga</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), pepper (<s>marica</s>), salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>), <s>āsurī</s> (mustard), <s>śigru</s> (horseradish tree), and sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), for three days,

children.text: svedena dīpito'sau grāsārthī jāyate sūtaḥ // GRht_2.18 //
children.translated_text: by steaming, the kindled (<s>dīpita</s>) [mercury] becomes desirous of a morsel (<s>grāsa</s>) — thus the mercury is [ready]. // GRht 2.18 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: aṣṭamoddiṣṭasya dīpanasaṃskārasya vidhiṃ spaṣṭayannāha bhūkhagetyādi // GRhtCM_2.18:1 //
children.translated_text: Clarifying the procedure for the kindling process (<s>dīpana-saṃskāra</s>) described as the eighth, [the author] says '<s>bhūkhaga</s>-' and so forth. // GRhtCM 2.18:1 //

children.text: asau pūrvasaṃskṛtarasa etair auṣadhais tridinaṃ nirantaraṃ yathā syāt tathā svedena dīpitaḥ kṣutpīḍitaḥ san grāsārthī kavalābhilāṣī jāyate // GRhtCM_2.18:2 //
children.translated_text: That previously processed mercury, by steaming with these herbs for three days continuously, without interruption, [becomes] kindled (<s>dīpita</s>), i.e., stimulated by hunger, and becomes desirous of a morsel (<s>grāsārthī</s>), i.e., desiring to swallow [metals]. // GRhtCM 2.18:2 //

children.text: etair oṣadhaiḥ bhūkhagaṭaṅkaṇamaricaiḥ na kevalam etaiḥ punar lavaṇāsurīśigrukāñjikaiḥ // GRhtCM_2.18:3 //
children.translated_text: With these herbs: '<s>bhūkhaga</s>,' borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), pepper (<s>marica</s>) — not only these, but also salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>), <s>āsurī</s> (mustard), <s>śigru</s> (horseradish tree), and sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>). // GRhtCM 2.18:3 //

children.text: bhūḥ tuvarī khagaḥ kāsīsaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ maricam ūṣaṇam etaiḥ // GRhtCM_2.18:4 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhū</s>' means pigeon-pea (<s>tuvarī</s>); '<s>khaga</s>' means green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>); '<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>' means borax (<s>saubhāgya</s>); '<s>marica</s>' means long pepper (<s>ūṣaṇa</s>) — with these. // GRhtCM 2.18:4 //

children.text: punaḥ lavaṇaṃ saindhavam āsurī rājikā śigruḥ saubhāñjanaṃ vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ kāñjikaṃ pūrvoktam amlībhūtam etaiśceti // GRhtCM_2.18:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, 'salt' means rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>); '<s>āsurī</s>' means mustard (<s>rājikā</s>); '<s>śigru</s>' is a variety of tree called <s>saubhāñjana</s> (drumstick tree); '<s>kāñjika</s>' is the aforementioned [substance that has become] sour. 'By these' — thus.
And the specific [procedure] here:
The sweating (<s>svedana</s>) of the king of mercury [is performed] with alkalines, sours, poisons, and wines.
One should take a citron (<s>bījapūra</s>), remove the stalk, and prepare [it thus]:
In its center, one should place mercury combined with a portion of alkali;

children.text: dvāraṃ nirudhya yatnena vastramadhye nibandhayet // GRhtCM_2.18:7 //
children.translated_text: closing the opening carefully, one should tie it in a cloth.
The swing-sweating (<s>dolā-sveda</s>) should be performed for up to twenty-one days;

children.text: dine dine prakartavyaṃ nūtanaṃ bījapūrakam // GRhtCM_2.18:8 //
children.translated_text: day by day, a fresh citron should be used.
Licking up the metals and compressed by hunger,
by this very [method], the stimulation (<s>dīpana</s>) of the king of mercury should be performed.
Three days, or seven days, or fourteen, or twenty-one —

children.text: saṃskāraḥ sūtarāje tu kramāt kramataraṃ varam // GRhtCM_2.18:10 //
children.translated_text: the processing (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of the king of mercury, progressively more is better.
Thus.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 2.19
<s>Cāraṇa</s> (making mercury consume substances)>
Thus stimulated and purified, [shining] like a thousand flashing lightning-streaks,

children.text: bhavati yadā rasarājaś cāryo satvādi tadā bījam // GRht_2.19 //
children.translated_text: when the king of mercury becomes [ready], the <s>cāraṇa</s> [process] with <s>sattva</s> (essence) and the like becomes the seed [of transmutation].
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: kṛtāṣṭasaṃskārasya pāradasya saṃskārāntarasiddhāṃ parīkṣām āha itītyādi // GRhtCM_2.19:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the test for mercury that has undergone the eight <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory processes), and the accomplishment of a further process, beginning with 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) etc.

children.text: iti pūrvoktaprakāreṇa rasarājo dīpitaḥ san kṣudutpīḍitaḥ san viśuddho bhavati // GRhtCM_2.19:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the aforementioned method, the king of mercury, having been stimulated — being afflicted with hunger — becomes purified.

children.text: yadīdṛśo bhavati rasarājastadā cāryaḥ cāraṇakarma kāryam // GRhtCM_2.19:3 //
children.translated_text: When the king of mercury becomes of such [quality], then the <s>cāraṇa</s> operation — the action of making [it] consume — should be performed.

children.text: kīdṛk pracalitavidyullatāsahasrābhaḥ prakarṣeṇa calatyaś calanaśīlā yā vidyutastāsāṃ sahasrasyeva bhā dīptir yasya sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_2.19:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what appearance? 'Like a thousand flashing lightning-streaks' — those which move with intensity, which are of a restless nature — the lightning bolts; the radiance (<s>bhā</s>) of a thousand of these — he whose [brilliance] is thus is so described.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā cāryaḥ idamagre vakṣyamāṇaṃ kiṃcit dhātūparasamahārasaratnasaṃjñakaṃ dvitīyaṃ rasarājasambandhinaṃ dattvā saṃyojyetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.19:5 //
children.translated_text: Having done what, is it ready for <s>cāraṇa</s>? This will be stated ahead: having given — that is, having combined — a certain second substance related to the king of mercury, designated as metal, subsidiary mineral, great mineral, or gem — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 2.20
<s>Cāraṇa</s>: with 'face' (<s>samukha</s>) and without 'face' (<s>nirmukha</s>)>

children.text: pītakriyāsu pītaṃ śvetaṃ tārakriyāsu mukham ādau /
children.translated_text: For gold-operations, gold [is given as the] 'face' (<s>mukha</s>); for silver-operations, silver; first the 'face' should be given;

children.text: deyaṃ khalve ghṛṣṭo divyauṣadhibhiḥ sa nirmukhaś carati // GRht_2.20 //
children.translated_text: ground in a mortar with divine herbs, [mercury] without a 'face' consumes [substances].

Thus ends the second chapter (<s>avabodha</s>), dealing with the purification of mercury, in the <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Govindabhagavatpāda</s>, the <s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya</s> (supreme wandering ascetic-teacher).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: kiṃ dvitīyamityāśaṅkya taṃ spaṣṭayannāha pītetyādi // GRhtCM_2.20:1 //
children.translated_text: Anticipating [the question] 'What is the second [substance]?', he clarifies, beginning with '<s>pīta</s>' (gold/yellow) etc.

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ mukhaṃ vidheyam ityadhyāhāraḥ pāradasya mukhaṃ kāryamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.20:2 //
children.translated_text: 'First' — initially, the 'face' (<s>mukha</s>) should be assigned — this is the implied supplement; the 'face' of mercury should be made — this is the meaning.

children.text: tataścetpītakriyā bhavanti svarṇasambandhīni kāryāṇi bhavanti tadā pītaṃ svarṇaṃ deyam // GRhtCM_2.20:3 //
children.translated_text: Then, if gold-operations (<s>pīta-kriyā</s>) are to be performed — that is, if tasks related to gold are [intended] — then gold (<s>pīta</s>) should be given [as the face].

children.text: śvetakriyāsu śvetaṃ deyaṃ śvetaṃ tāram ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.20:4 //
children.translated_text: For silver-operations, silver should be given; 'silver' (<s>śveta</s>) means <s>tāra</s> (silver) — this is the meaning.

children.text: svarṇatārādikaṃ khalve dattaṃ kṛtamukho rasaścarati // GRhtCM_2.20:5 //
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, and the like being placed in the mortar, mercury with a [prepared] 'face' consumes [them].

children.text: punarnirmukho rasaḥ akṛtamukho rasaḥ khalve ghṛṣṭo gharṣitaḥ san pūrvoktaṃ carati bhakṣayati // GRhtCM_2.20:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, mercury 'without a face' (<s>nirmukha</s>) — mercury without a prepared face — being ground in a mortar, consumes [substances] as described before.

children.text: kābhiḥ saha divyauṣadhībhir vakṣyamāṇābhiḥ saha // GRhtCM_2.20:7 //
children.translated_text: With what? With divine herbs (<s>divyauṣadhi</s>) — those that will be described [later].
As [stated in] a verse:

children.text: sāsyo rasaḥ syātpaṭuśigrututthaiḥ sarājikair vyoṣaṇakais trirātram /
children.translated_text: Mercury becomes 'faced' (<s>sāsya</s>) [by processing] with mustard, drumstick, blue vitriol (<s>tuttha</s>), with mustard seeds (<s>rājikā</s>), and <s>vyoṣaṇa</s> (the three pungents) for three nights;

children.text: piṣṭastataḥ svinnatanuḥ suvarṇamukhānayaṃ khādati sarvadhātūn // GRhtCM_2.20:8 //
children.translated_text: ground [thus], then sweated, it devours all metals with a gold-face.
Thus.
And 'without a face': one should grind [mercury] combined with the sour group, using whatever is available;
mercury with an 'impression-face' (<s>vāsanā-mukha</s>) consumes mica (<s>abhraka</s>) and other [substances].
For mercury of this quantity, the measure of the edible substance [is specified];
such-and-such a quantity is stated — that which is called the 'consumption measure' (<s>grāsamāna</s>).
This is the technical definition (<s>paribhāṣā</s>).

children.text: iti śrīmatkuralakulapayodhisudhākaramiśramaheśātmajacaturbhujamiśraviracitāyāṃ mugdhāvabodhinyāṃ rasahṛdayaṭīkāyāṃ rasaśodhanātmako dvitīyo'vabodhaḥ // GRhtCM_2.20:13 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter (<s>avabodha</s>), dealing with the purification of mercury, in the <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s> commentary on the <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s>, composed by <s>Caturbhuja Miśra</s>, son of <s>Maheśa</s> (who is) the moon of the ocean of the illustrious <s>Kurala</s> family.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 3.1
Those who, having performed <s>cāraṇa</s> without <s>ghana</s> (mica) as the seed, are satisfied with the attainment of [mere] leaf-[transmutation] and the like —
they are wretches, like those who, having reached the ocean, are content with [finding] a cowrie shell.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
'Its consumption-<s>sattva</s> [brings forth] the moon-born [silver], and the delight of the lotus [gold];</s>
and its powers (<s>vibhūti</s>) bring joy to virtuous people.'

children.text: anena padyena granthasya guṇādhikyaṃ saṃmatatvaṃ ca varṇayannāha ghanetyādi // GRhtCM_3.1:2 //
children.translated_text: By this verse, while describing the excellence and the authoritative nature of the text, he says, beginning with '<s>ghana</s>' etc.

children.text: ye evaṃvidhāḥ puruṣāste kṛpaṇā eva // GRhtCM_3.1:3 //
children.translated_text: Those persons of such [limited] kind are wretches indeed.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ ghanarahitabījacāraṇasamprāptadalādidravyakṛtakṛtyāḥ ghanenābhrakeṇa rahitaṃ varjitaṃ yad bījacāraṇam anyadhātvādīnāṃ bījakavalanaṃ tena yatprāptaṃ dalādidravyaṃ pattrarañjanavarṇavṛddhitārakṛṣṭī melāpakādikaṃ vastu tena ye kṛtakṛtyāḥ pūrṇāḥ ātmānaṃ manyante ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_3.1:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? 'Satisfied with the leaf-substances and the like obtained through seed-<s>cāraṇa</s> without mica (<s>ghana</s>)' — <s>cāraṇa</s> that is devoid of — that is, lacking — mica (<s>abhraka</s>), and the seed-consumption, the swallowing of other metals and the like by [mercury]; the leaf-substances and other things obtained thereby — leaf [transmutation], coloring, color-enhancement, silver-extraction, <s>melāpaka</s> (conjunction), and so forth — those who consider themselves fulfilled by these — this is the implied supplement.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ kṛpaṇāḥ samudraṃ prāpya ratnākaraṃ labdhvā varāṭikālābhasaṃtuṣṭāḥ kapardikālābhena saṃtuṣṭiṃ prāptaḥ daridrabhāvāditi bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.1:5 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality are these wretches? Having reached the ocean — having obtained the jewel-mine — they are content with the acquisition of a cowrie shell (<s>kapardikā</s>); [this is] due to their impoverished condition — this is the import.

children.text: tathā evaṃvidhāḥ kṛpaṇā idaṃ śāstraṃ ratnākararūpaṃ bahuratnaṃ prāpya dalādidravyeṇa kṛtakṛtyāḥ // GRhtCM_3.1:6 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, such wretches, having obtained this treatise, which is in the form of a jewel-mine containing many gems, are satisfied with [mere] leaf-substances and the like.

children.text: śāstrasamudrayor guṇaratnaiḥ sāmyaṃ varāṭikādalādirdravyayoḥ sāmyaṃ tucchatayā yata ubhāv api nikṛṣṭāv eva // GRhtCM_3.1:7 //
children.translated_text: The treatise and the ocean share equality in [their respective] gem-like qualities; the cowrie shell and the leaf-substance share equality in worthlessness, since both are indeed inferior.

Because this treatise bestows much: it grants the [methods for] <s>mudrikā-vedha</s> (ring-transmutation), <s>sparśa-vedha</s> (touch-transmutation), <s>dhūma-vedha</s> (smoke-transmutation), <s>śabda-vedha</s> (sound-transmutation), <s>dhāmya-vedha</s> (blowing-transmutation), and <s>adhāmya-dhātu-vedha</s> (non-blowing metal-transmutation).
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 3.2
Others, however — the great ones — having disdained <s>Lakṣmī</s> (wealth-goddess), the king of elephants (<s>Airāvata</s>), the <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem], and the like,

children.text: avadhīrya labdhavantaḥ parāmṛtaṃ cāmarā jātāḥ // GRht_3.2 //
children.translated_text: having obtained the supreme nectar (<s>parāmṛta</s>), have become immortal.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: punaratra granthe guṇādhikyaśataṃ ca varṇayannāhānye ityādi // GRhtCM_3.2:1 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, describing the hundredfold excellence of this text, he says, beginning with 'others' (<s>anye</s>) etc.

children.text: punar ity aprathamaviśeṣaṇayor iti prasādaḥ // GRhtCM_3.2:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Punar</s>' [is used here] in the sense of a distinguishing qualifier — [as explained by the grammarian] <s>Prasāda</s>.
Here, '<s>punar</s>' [functions as] a distinguishing qualifier.
Others, greater than the aforementioned [wretches], exist.

children.text: kiṃ kurvantaḥ parāmṛtaṃ labdhavantaḥ santa amarā jātā maraṇarahitā jīvanmuktā jātā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.2:5 //
children.translated_text: Doing what? Having obtained the supreme nectar (<s>parāmṛta</s>), they have become immortal (<s>amara</s>) — free from death, <s>jīvanmuktas</s> (liberated while living) — this is the meaning.

children.text: paraṃ ca tadamṛtaṃ ceti samāsaḥ mokṣam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.2:6 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Para</s>' (supreme) and 'that <s>amṛta</s>' (nectar) — [this is] a compound; it means liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā lakṣmīkarirājakaustubhādīni avadhīrya avahelanaṃ vidhāya lakṣmīrharipriyā karirāja airāvata indravāraṇaḥ kaustubho harermaṇiḥ ityādīni caturdaśaratnāni // GRhtCM_3.2:7 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having disdained — having shown contempt for — <s>Lakṣmī</s> (the beloved of <s>Hari</s>), the king of elephants (<s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Indra's</s> elephant), the <s>Kaustubha</s> (<s>Hari's</s> gem), 'and the like' — the fourteen [cosmic] jewels.

children.text: satām ayameva svabhāvaḥ daridrāṇāṃ kṛpaṇānāṃ pūrvavat // GRhtCM_3.2:8 //
children.translated_text: This is the very nature of the noble; for the wretched and miserly, [it is] as before.
Therefore, this treatise serves as a touchstone (<s>nikaṣa</s>) for [distinguishing] the wretched and the great.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 3.3
By alkalines, herbs, pungents, and sours, the awakening of hunger [occurs]; [then] coloring and binding [come] from sweating;

children.text: na punaḥ pakṣacchedo dravatvaṃ vā vinā gaganam // GRht_3.3 //
children.translated_text: but without <s>gagana</s> (mica), there is no wing-clipping [i.e., immobilization] or [removal of] fluidity.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the means for the supreme process of mica-consumption, beginning with '<s>kṣāra</s>' (alkaline) etc.

children.text: kṣudbodho rasarājasya jāyate iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.3:2 //
children.translated_text: The awakening of hunger of the king of mercury occurs — this is the completion [of the sentence].

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā kṣārauṣadhipaṭvamlaiḥ kṣārauṣadhayo 'himārādayaḥ paṭu saindhavam amlam amlavetasādi etaiḥ kṣudutpattir bhaved ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.3:3 //
children.translated_text: By what means? By alkalines, herbs, pungents, and sours. Alkaline herbs are <s>ahimāra</s> and others; 'pungent' means rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>); 'sour' means <s>amlavetasa</s> (sour tamarind) and the like. By these, the generation of hunger occurs — this is the meaning.
The alkaline herbs are as follows:
<s>Ahimāra</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, combined with <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> (amaranth),
milkweed (<s>snuhī</s>), swallow-wort (<s>arka</s>), oleander (<s>karavīra</s>), <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>kṣīrakanda</s> (milky tuber);
<s>Karkoṭī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, bottle-gourd (<s>tumbā</s>), <s>palāśa</s> (flame-of-the-forest), and <s>agnimanthaka</s> (fire-churning tree);

children.text: karīraṃ citrakaṃ śigruṃ varuṇaṃ vetasaṃ vaṭam // GRhtCM_3.3:5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Karīra</s> (caper), <s>citraka</s> (leadwort), drumstick (<s>śigru</s>), <s>varuṇa</s> (three-leaved caper), <s>vetasa</s> (cane), and banyan (<s>vaṭa</s>);
Pointed gourd (<s>paṭolī</s>), <s>arjuna</s>, pumpkin (<s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>), plantain (<s>kadalī</s>), and <s>vajrakandaka</s> (adamantine tuber);

children.text: aśvatthaṃ sūraṇaṃ jālīṃ dahet kandān anekaśaḥ // GRhtCM_3.3:6 //
children.translated_text: sacred fig (<s>aśvattha</s>), elephant-yam (<s>sūraṇa</s>), <s>jālī</s> — one should burn the tubers in many ways.
By means of the inner smoke, all [these] and also <s>devadālī</s> should be burned;
this group is called the 'herb-alkaline' (<s>auṣadhi-kṣāra</s>).
Thus.
The sours are as follows:
Sour tamarind (<s>amlavetasa</s>), lemon (<s>jambīra</s>), bread-fruit (<s>lakuca</s>), citron (<s>bījapūraka</s>),

children.text: cāṅgerī caṇakāmlaṃ ca nāraṅgaṃ tittiḍī tathā // GRhtCM_3.3:9 //
children.translated_text: wood-sorrel (<s>cāṅgerī</s>), sour chickpea-water (<s>caṇakāmla</s>), orange (<s>nāraṅga</s>), and tamarind (<s>tittiḍī</s>);
<s>Ambaṣṭhā</s>, <s>karamarda</s> (Carissa), wood-apple (<s>kapittha</s>), <s>karaṇa</s>, and the like;
or combined with the five sours (<s>pañcāmla</s>) — [this] is declared as the sour group.
Among all [sours], sour chickpea-water (<s>caṇakāmla</s>) alone is praised;
or sour tamarind (<s>amlavetasa</s>) alone — the supreme among all.
Thus.

children.text: ityetaiḥ kṣārauṣadhipaṭvamlaiḥ kṣudbodho bhavet rāgabandhane ca bhavetāṃ rāgo rañjanaṃ bandhanaṃ pūrvam upavarṇitam // GRhtCM_3.3:13 //
children.translated_text: By these — alkalines, herbs, pungents, and sours — the awakening of hunger occurs; and coloring (<s>rāga</s>) and binding (<s>bandhana</s>) — binding has been previously described — would [also] occur.

children.text: kuto hetoḥ etaiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ karaṇarūpaiḥ svedāt // GRhtCM_3.3:14 //
children.translated_text: From what cause? From sweating (<s>sveda</s>) by means of the aforementioned [substances] in the form of instruments.
'<s>Punar</s>' [is used here] as a distinguishing qualifier.

children.text: pakṣacchedaḥ rasapakṣāpakartanaṃ yathā sthiro bhavati dravyatvaṃ guṇavattvaṃ vā gaganamabhrakaṃ vinā na bhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.3:16 //
children.translated_text: 'Wing-clipping' (<s>pakṣaccheda</s>) means the cutting of mercury's 'wings' — that is, [making it] stable; 'fluidity' (<s>dravatva</s>) means the quality of being fluid — without mica (<s>gagana</s> = <s>abhraka</s>), [these] do not occur — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 3.4

children.text: abhrakajīrṇo balavān bhavati rasastasya cāraṇe proktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury that has digested mica (<s>abhrakajīrṇa</s>) becomes powerful; for its <s>cāraṇa</s> (consumption-process) are prescribed
<s>saṃdhāna</s> (fermentation), <s>vāsanā-auṣadhi</s> (impression-herbs), <s>nirmukha</s> (faceless), <s>samukha</s> (faced) — these great procedures (<s>mahā-yogas</s>).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states [the attainment of] substantiality (<s>dravyatva</s>) through mica, beginning with '<s>abhrakajīrṇa</s>' (having digested mica) etc.
When [mercury] is devoid of strength and the hunger-awakening is excessive, impotence (<s>ṣaṇḍhatā</s>) results.
As [stated]:
Due to coldness, due to lack of grinding, due to the digestion of impure metal,
due to giving an excess of <s>viḍa</s> (a type of salt), or [when mercury] consumes [substances] in indigestion after previous digestion —
due to excessive heat, due to lack of food, or for one lacking <s>krāmaṇa</s> (progressive treatment) —

children.text: ityetā vikriyā jñeyā aṣṭabhiḥ ṣaṇḍhatāṃ vrajet // GRhtCM_3.4:4 //
children.translated_text: these defects should be known; by [any of] these eight, [mercury] attains impotence (<s>ṣaṇḍhatā</s>).
Thus.

children.text: ato raso'ṣṭasaṃskārānantaram abhrakajīrṇaḥ kartavyaḥ yato'bhrakajīrṇaṃ balavān bhavati // GRhtCM_3.4:6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, after the eight <s>saṃskāras</s>, mercury should be made to digest mica (<s>abhrakajīrṇa</s>), because [only] mercury that has digested mica becomes powerful.

children.text: abhrakajīrṇe grāsanyāye na jāritaṃ yasmin sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_3.4:7 //
children.translated_text: In mica-digestion, according to the rule of consumption (<s>grāsa</s>), that in which [mica] has not been digested is so described.

children.text: tasyābhrajāraṇāyogyasya rasasya cāraṇe kevalakavalane ete proktāḥ // GRhtCM_3.4:8 //
children.translated_text: For that mercury suitable for mica-digestion, in the <s>cāraṇa</s> — the mere consumption [process] — these [procedures] are prescribed.

children.text: ete ke saṃdhānavāsanauṣadhinirmukhasamukhā eva mahāyogāḥ mahaddravyatvakārakāḥ saṃdhānaṃ sarvadhānyānām aṣṭauṣadhyādīnāṃ ca saṃdhānaṃ yathā sarvadhānyāni nikṣipya āranālaṃ tu kārayet // GRhtCM_3.4:9 //
children.translated_text: Which are these? <s>Saṃdhāna</s> (fermentation), <s>vāsanā-auṣadhi</s> (impression-herbs), <s>nirmukha</s> (faceless), and <s>samukha</s> (faced) — these are the great procedures (<s>mahā-yogas</s>), the producers of great substantiality. <s>Saṃdhāna</s> (fermentation) [is prepared] from all grains, the eight herbs, and the like. The fermentation [is] as follows: 'Having placed all grains, one should prepare sour gruel (<s>āranāla</s>).'
'One should place therein the herbs with their leaves and roots.'
'With earth-salt (<s>kṣitikāsīsa</s>), sea-salt (<s>sāmudra</s>), rock salt (<s>sindhu</s>), the three pungents (<s>tryuṣaṇa</s>), and mustard seeds (<s>rājikā</s>),
combined — one should prepare that, kept in a warm place for seven days.'
'That, combined with sour gruel (<s>āranāla</s>), should be fermented in a copper vessel' —
thus [is prepared] the fermentation (<s>saṃdhāna</s>) for the purpose of mica-<s>cāraṇa</s>.
The impression-herbs (<s>vāsanā-auṣadhi</s>) are as follows:
'The group of herbs should be known as stated in the treatises.'

children.text: jalajaṃ sthalajaṃ caiva samyak jñātvā tu kārayet // GRhtCM_3.4:13 //
children.translated_text: Knowing properly both the aquatic and terrestrial [plants], one should employ them. // GRhtCM_3.4:13 //

children.text: jalajā utpalī padmā sthalajā ca prasāriṇī /
children.translated_text: The aquatic ones are: <s>utpalī</s> (water lily), <s>padmā</s> (lotus); and the terrestrial one is <s>prasāriṇī</s>;
<s>jālinī</s>, <s>abhracandrā</s>, <s>citraparṇī</s>, <s>triparṇikā</s>,
<s>rasacandra</s>, <s>aukasa</s>, and likewise <s>jalamūlaka</s>,

children.text: samaṅgā vāribhūtā ca apāmārgo jalodbhavā // GRhtCM_3.4:14 //
children.translated_text: <s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>vāribhūtā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>jalodbhavā</s>. // GRhtCM_3.4:14 //
<s>Ajamārī</s>, <s>upāmbu</s>, <s>kumbhikā</s>, <s>jalapippalī</s>,

children.text: jalapūrvāmbusītā ca kumārī nāginī tathā // GRhtCM_3.4:15 //
children.translated_text: <s>jalapūrvā</s>, <s>ambusītā</s>, <s>kumārī</s> (aloe), <s>nāginī</s> likewise. // GRhtCM_3.4:15 //
<s>Sitajaṅghā</s>, <s>svara</s>, and likewise <s>sarpa</s>, <s>sugandhikā</s>,

children.text: vṛddhā ca bṛhatī tadvanmūrtir mārjārapādikā // GRhtCM_3.4:16 //
children.translated_text: <s>vṛddhā</s> and <s>bṛhatī</s>, likewise <s>mūrti</s>, <s>mārjārapādikā</s>. // GRhtCM_3.4:16 //
Likewise <s>jalacakorī</s>, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, <s>ahilocanā</s>,

children.text: jayāṃvica varāhī ca apattrā īśvarī tathā // GRhtCM_3.4:17 //
children.translated_text: <s>jayā</s>, <s>vica</s>, <s>varāhī</s>, <s>apattrā</s>, <s>īśvarī</s> likewise. // GRhtCM_3.4:17 //
<s>Kurkurī</s>, <s>halinī</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>vajrakandaka</s>,

children.text: musalī vanamālā ca vidārī mohinī tathā // GRhtCM_3.4:18 //
children.translated_text: <s>musalī</s>, <s>vanamālā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>mohinī</s> likewise. // GRhtCM_3.4:18 //

children.text: māṇḍūkī lavaṇā caiva ugrā ca uttamā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Māṇḍūkī</s>, <s>lavaṇā</s>, <s>ugrā</s>, and <s>uttamā</s> likewise,
<s>śikhipādī</s>, <s>kapotī</s>, <s>nandinī</s>, <s>vṛścikālikā</s>,

children.text: haṃsapādī śikhā caiva sārivā vāyasī tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>haṃsapādī</s>, <s>śikhā</s>, <s>sārivā</s>, <s>vāyasī</s> likewise,

children.text: dantī gojihvikā caiva garuḍī hemapuṣpikā // GRhtCM_3.4:19 //
children.translated_text: <s>dantī</s>, <s>gojihvikā</s>, <s>garuḍī</s>, <s>hemapuṣpikā</s>. // GRhtCM_3.4:19 //
<s>Samaṅgā</s>, <s>jalajā</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>pāṣāṇabhedikā</s>,
<s>alambuṣā</s>, <s>meghanādā</s>, <s>śukanādā</s>, <s>kapotikī</s>. // GRhtCM_3.4:20 //

children.text: kṣīrikā tulasī dhānyā meṣikā ca vanārjakā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣīrikā</s>, <s>tulasī</s>, <s>dhānyā</s>, <s>meṣikā</s>, <s>vanārjakā</s>,

children.text: vārāhī caṇakāyāsī tathā ca aparājitā // GRhtCM_3.4:21 //
children.translated_text: <s>vārāhī</s>, <s>caṇakāyāsī</s>, and likewise <s>aparājitā</s>. // GRhtCM_3.4:21 //
This group of sixty-four herbs is declared.
By means of the sixty-eight procedure, one should not bring about [their] transformation. // GRhtCM_3.4:22 //
Thus. // GRhtCM_3.4:23 //
This group of herbs is also applicable in the <s>saṃdhāna</s> (fermentation/joining) process. // GRhtCM_3.4:24 //

children.text: saṃdhānaṃ ca vāsanauṣadhayaśca tābhiḥ kṛtvā ye nirmukhasamukhā eva yogāḥ akṛtamukhakṛtamukhā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.4:25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃdhāna</s> and the processing herbs (<s>vāsana-oṣadhis</s>) — by means of them, those preparations that are <s>nirmukha</s> (without mouth/opening) and <s>samukha</s> (with mouth/opening) are the procedures; meaning: those with an unprepared opening and those with a prepared opening. // GRhtCM_3.4:25 //
START GRht 3.5
<mica: preparation for <s>cāraṇā</s> (transmutation)>

children.text: niścandrikaṃ hi gaganaṃ kṣārāmlairbhāvitaṃ tathā rudhiraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Moonless <s>gagana</s> (mica), treated with alkalis, acids, and also with blood,
ground with the <s>sṛṣṭitraya</s> (triple creation fluids), <s>nīrakaṇā</s> (water pepper), and <s>tumburu</s> juice — it is transmuted. // GRht_3.5 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the method of <s>abhraka-cāraṇā</s> (mica transmutation) by the <s>nirmukha</s> (without-mouth) method — 'moonless' and so forth. // GRhtCM_3.5:1 //

children.text: hi niścitaṃ yadgaganamabhrakaṃ niścandrikaṃ candrarahitaṃ bhavati vajrasaṃjñakam ityarthaḥ tadgaganaṃ rucirair nirdoṣair manoramair vividhaiḥ kṣārāmlair bhāvitaṃ plāvitaṃ kāryaṃ kṣārā yavakṣārasvarjikṣāraṭaṅkaṇakṣārādayo 'mlā amlavetasajambīrādyāḥ pūrvoktāḥ // GRhtCM_3.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Indeed certainly: that <s>gagana</s>, i.e., <s>abhraka</s> (mica), which is <s>niścandrika</s> (moonless, i.e., lusterless), means it is the variety called <s>vajra</s> (diamond-type) — this is the meaning. That <s>gagana</s> should be treated, i.e., soaked, with pure, faultless, beautiful, various alkalis and acids.
