The alkalis are: <s>yava-kṣāra</s> (barley alkali), <s>svarji-kṣāra</s> (borax alkali), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa-kṣāra</s> (borax), and so forth. The acids are: <s>amlavetasa</s> (tamarind), <s>jambīra</s> (citron), and others as previously mentioned. // GRhtCM_3.5:2 //

children.text: nanu kṣārā rucirāḥ kathaṃ bhavanti ucyate yathā sarjikācūrṇabhāgaikaṃ viṃśadbhāgaṃ jalasya ca // GRhtCM_3.5:3 //
children.translated_text: Now, how do alkalis become pure? It is said: One part of <s>sarjikā</s> (soda ash) powder with twenty parts of water — // GRhtCM_3.5:3 //

children.text: tāvatkvāthyaṃ kṣiped bhāṇḍe yāvatphenaṃ sitaṃ bhavet // GRhtCM_3.5:4 //
children.translated_text: boil that much and pour into a vessel until a white foam appears. // GRhtCM_3.5:4 //

children.text: kṣīṇe kṣīṇe jalaṃ dattvā śvetaphenaṃ ca gṛhyate // GRhtCM_3.5:5 //
children.translated_text: As [the water] reduces, add more water and collect the white foam. // GRhtCM_3.5:5 //
Then, by means of a <s>ḍeka-yantra</s> (distillation apparatus), one should liquefy it by the application of fire. // GRhtCM_3.5:6 //
The liquefaction should be performed twenty-one times (three times seven), combined with urine. // GRhtCM_3.5:7 //
This one named <s>svarjikā-kṣāra</s> (borax alkali) is considered supreme in liquefaction. // GRhtCM_3.5:8 //
Thus is the special procedure. // GRhtCM_3.5:9 //

children.text: evamatyuttamāḥ kṣārāḥ syuḥ sampakvāḥ himāḥ // GRhtCM_3.5:10 //
children.translated_text: In this way, the alkalis that are fully prepared become supremely excellent and cool [in potency]. // GRhtCM_3.5:10 //

children.text: punaḥ sṛṣṭitrayanīrakaṇātumbarurasamarditaṃ go'jāvinārīṇāṃ mūtraṃ śukraṃ ca śoṇitaṃ sṛṣṭitrayaṃ nīrakaṇā jalapippalī paṭuriti loke tumburu pratītaṃ jalakaṇā ca tumbaruśca anayo rasaḥ sṛṣṭitrayaṃ ca jalakaṇātumbarurasaśca tābhyāṃ mardanaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_3.5:11 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, 'ground with <s>sṛṣṭitraya</s>, <s>nīrakaṇā</s>, and <s>tumburu</s> juice': the <s>sṛṣṭitraya</s> (triple creation) is the urine, semen, and blood of cows, goats, sheep, and women. <s>Nīrakaṇā</s> is <s>jalapippalī</s> (long pepper), known in common parlance as '<s>paṭu</s>.' <s>Tumburu</s> is well-known [by that name] in common parlance. <s>Jalakaṇā</s> and <s>tumburu</s> — by these, and [by] <s>sṛṣṭitraya</s>, <s>jalakaṇā</s>, and <s>tumburu</s> juice — grinding should be done. // GRhtCM_3.5:11 //

children.text: rasaḥ pāradaḥ nirmukho'pi evaṃvidhaṃ gaganaṃ carati grāsīkaroti // GRhtCM_3.5:12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s>, i.e., <s>pārada</s> (mercury), even without a mouth (<s>nirmukha</s>), transmutes (<s>carati</s>), i.e., devours, <s>gagana</s> (mica) of this kind. // GRhtCM_3.5:12 //
The [detailed] procedure is found in other texts:
The three milks, <s>kumārī</s> (aloe) juice, <s>gaṅgāputra</s> (Gangetic clay?), three urines,
banyan shoot-tips, goat's blood — <s>abhraka</s> (mica) well-ground with these, // GRhtCM_3.5:13 //
even when calcined a hundred times, becomes like a ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>).

children.text: niścandrikaṃ mṛtaṃ tv abhraṃ vṛddhadehe rasāyanam // GRhtCM_3.5:14 //
children.translated_text: Moonless, dead <s>abhraka</s> (calcined mica) is a rejuvenating elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>) for aged bodies. // GRhtCM_3.5:14 //
It destroys the pride and arrogance of women, [and] is prescribed for those suffering from impotence.
Thus. // GRhtCM_3.5:15 //
START GRht 3.6
<mercury: <s>abhraka-cāraṇā</s> (mica transmutation)>
Calcined with <s>yavaciñcikā</s> (tamarind) water, [then] mixed with its root, <s>śatāvarī</s> (asparagus), and <s>gadā</s> (kuṣṭha),
treated with the juice of <s>ghanarava</s> (amaranth), <s>śigru</s> (drumstick), and <s>punarnava</s> (hogweed) — the <s>abhraka</s> (mica) is transmuted. // GRht_3.6 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states an alternative method — 'barley' and so forth. // GRhtCM_3.6:1 //

children.text: punarabhrakaṃ yavaciñcikāmbupuṭitaṃ kāryaṃ yavaciñcikā pratītā yavaciñciketi loke tasyā ambudravaḥ tena puṭitam ātapayogena bhāvitam // GRhtCM_3.6:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>abhraka</s> (mica) should be calcined (<s>puṭita</s>) with <s>yavaciñcikā</s> water. <s>Yavaciñcikā</s> is known as '<s>yavaciñcikā</s>' in common parlance; its '<s>ambu</s>' means liquid/juice; '<s>puṭita</s>' by that means treated through sun-drying. // GRhtCM_3.6:2 //

children.text: punastanmūlaśatāvarīgadākulitaṃ kāryaṃ tasyā yavaciñcikāyā mūlaṃ tanmūlaṃ śatāvarī śatapād gadaḥ kuṣṭhaḥ etair ākulaṃ vyāptaṃ pariplutam // GRhtCM_3.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, it should be mixed with <s>tanmūla</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, and <s>gadā</s>. '<s>Tanmūla</s>' — the root of that [<s>yavaciñcikā</s>], that is '<s>tanmūla</s>.' <s>Śatāvarī</s> is '<s>śatapād</s>' (centipede plant). <s>Gadā</s> is <s>kuṣṭha</s> (costus). Mixed with these means pervaded, saturated. // GRhtCM_3.6:3 //
When fresh juicy herbs are unavailable, then this procedure [applies]: // GRhtCM_3.6:4 //
Taking the dry substance, when fresh juices are unavailable,
one should prepare it in eight times [its weight of] water, and collect when reduced to one-quarter. // GRhtCM_3.6:4 //
Thus. // GRhtCM_3.6:5 //

children.text: punar ghanaravaśigrupunarnavarasabhāvitaṃ kāryaṃ ghanaravas taṇḍulīyakaḥ śigru saubhāñjanaṃ suhijanā iti loke punarnavā varṣābhūḥ pratītā eteṣāṃ rasena bhāvitaṃ pariplutam ātapayogena śoṣyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.6:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, it should be treated with the juice of <s>ghanarava</s> (amaranth, i.e., <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>), <s>śigru</s> (<s>saubhāñjana</s>, drumstick tree, known as '<s>suhijanā</s>' in common parlance), <s>punarnava</s> (<s>varṣābhū</s>, known in common parlance) — treated means saturated with their juice and dried in sunlight — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_3.6:6 //
Mica of this kind is transmuted by <s>rasa</s> (mercury). // GRhtCM_3.6:7 //

children.text: nirmukhena bhāvanāśabdena śatavāraṃ jñātavyaṃ granthāntarasāmyāt // GRhtCM_3.6:8 //
children.translated_text: By the <s>nirmukha</s> (without-mouth) [method], the word '<s>bhāvanā</s>' (saturation) should be understood as [repeated] a hundred times, by analogy with other texts. // GRhtCM_3.6:8 //
Here is a special [procedure]: // GRhtCM_3.6:9 //
Having ground [the mica] in <s>somavallī</s> juice, one should give it three calcinations (<s>puṭas</s>);
with <s>somavallī</s> juice itself, one should saturate it seven times. // GRhtCM_3.6:10 //
One should place it in an earthen vessel, combined with <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
One should grind the root of <s>śarapuṅkhā</s> with cow's milk,

children.text: kalkena melayet sūtaṃ gaganaṃ tadadhaūrdhvagam // GRhtCM_3.6:11 //
children.translated_text: [and] with that paste, combine <s>sūta</s> (mercury) [and] <s>gagana</s> (mica), placed below and above. // GRhtCM_3.6:11 //
One should place it in sunlight; the <s>nirmukha</s> (mouthless mercury) devours [the mica] in an instant.

children.text: jāyate piṣṭikā śīghraṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // GRhtCM_3.6:12 //
children.translated_text: A pellet (<s>piṣṭikā</s>) forms quickly — there should be no doubt about this. // GRhtCM_3.6:12 //
Thus. // GRhtCM_3.6:13 //
And another [method]:
Having taken the juice of <s>tilaparṇī</s>, one should treat <s>gagana</s> (mica) with it.

children.text: mardanājjāyate piṣṭī nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // GRhtCM_3.6:14 //
children.translated_text: By grinding, a pellet forms — there should be no doubt about this. // GRhtCM_3.6:14 //
Thus. // GRhtCM_3.6:15 //
And another [method]:
One should repeatedly pour <s>nāga</s> (lead) in <s>muṇḍī</s> exudate.

children.text: tenābhrakaṃ tu saṃyojya bhūyo bhūyaḥ paṭe dahet // GRhtCM_3.6:16 //
children.translated_text: Having combined <s>abhraka</s> (mica) with that, one should burn [it] again and again on cloth. // GRhtCM_3.6:16 //
With the roots of <s>citraka</s> and <s>ārdraka</s> (ginger), each one separately, seven times,
the powder of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) and <s>abhraka</s> (mica) should be carefully soaked. // GRhtCM_3.6:17 //
<s>Nāga</s> (lead) cast in <s>muṇḍī</s> exudate, treated with sour <s>rasaluṅga</s> (?),
should be added in one-sixteenth proportion; in a <s>dolā-yantra</s> (swinging apparatus), the mercury transmutes [it]. // GRhtCM_3.6:18 //
Thus is the <s>nirmukha-cāraṇā</s> (mouthless transmutation). // GRhtCM_3.6:19 //
START GRht 3.7-9
<s>āranāla</s> (fermented gruel) for <s>jāraṇā</s> (assimilation)>
<s>Sarjī</s> (soda ash), earth (<s>kṣiti</s>), <s>khaga</s> (green vitriol), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and salt combined, in a copper vessel for three days,
fermented <s>āranāla</s> (sour gruel) is excellent for the treatment of <s>gagana</s> (mica) and other [substances]. // GRht_3.7 //
Having melted pure <s>nāga</s> (lead) in that [<s>āranāla</s>], one should pour it a hundred times.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ vā tāravidhau rasāyane naiva tadyojyam // GRht_3.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaṅga</s> (tin) is suitable in the procedure for <s>tāra</s> (silver); in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), it should not be employed. // GRht_3.8 //
<s>Gagana</s> (mica), <s>rasa</s> (mercury), <s>uparasa</s> (subsidiary minerals), <s>amṛta</s> (mica?), <s>loha</s> (metals), <s>rasāyasa</s> (iron compounds), and other powders —

children.text: sarvamanena ha bhāvyaṃ yatkiṃcit cāraṇāvastu // GRht_3.9 //
children.translated_text: everything should be treated with this [<s>āranāla</s>], whatever substance is intended for <s>cāraṇā</s> (transmutation). // GRht_3.9 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He describes the <s>samukha-cāraṇā</s> (with-mouth transmutation) — '<s>sarjī</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:1 //

children.text: āranālaṃ svedanasaṃskāre yaduktaṃ kāñjikaṃ tat // GRhtCM_3.7-9:2 //
children.translated_text: The <s>āranāla</s> is the <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented rice-water) that was mentioned in the <s>svedana-saṃskāra</s> (sweating preparation). // GRhtCM_3.7-9:2 //
'In a copper vessel' means in a <s>tāmra-pātra</s> (copper pot). // GRhtCM_3.7-9:3 //
For three days — for that long one should prepare the fermentation (<s>saṃdhānīkaraṇa</s>). // GRhtCM_3.7-9:4 //

children.text: kīdṛgvidham āranālaṃ sarjīkṣitikhagaṭaṅkaṇalavaṇānvitaṃ sarjī pratītā sājīti loke kṣitiḥ sphaṭikā khagaḥ kāsīsaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ sohāgā iti loke lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ tadabhāve lavaṇāṣṭakeṣu yatra yallabhyaṃ tadeva yojyaṃ lavaṇoddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: What kind of <s>āranāla</s>? Combined with <s>sarjī</s>, <s>kṣiti</s> (earth), <s>khaga</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and <s>lavaṇa</s> (salt). <s>Sarjī</s> is known as '<s>sājī</s>' in common parlance. <s>Kṣiti</s> is <s>sphaṭikā</s> (alum). <s>Khaga</s> is <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol). <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax), '<s>sohāgā</s>' in common parlance. <s>Lavaṇa</s> is <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt); in its absence, whichever is available among the eight types of salt should be used — this is the indication for '<s>lavaṇa</s>.'

children.text: saindhavaṃ rucakaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ viḍaṃ sāmudram audbhidam /
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>rucaka</s> (black salt), <s>kṛṣṇa</s> (black salt), <s>viḍa</s> (foul salt), <s>sāmudra</s> (sea salt), <s>audbhida</s> (earth salt),

children.text: romakaṃ pāṃśujaṃ ceti lavaṇāṣṭakam ucyate // GRhtCM_3.7-9:5 //
children.translated_text: <s>romaka</s> (Sindh salt), and <s>pāṃśuja</s> (sandy salt) — these are called the eight salts. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:5 //

children.text: iti etair anvitaṃ militaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_3.7-9:6 //
children.translated_text: Combined with these, i.e., mixed — one should do so. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:6 //

children.text: tadāranālaṃ gaganādikabhāvane abhrakādiplāvane śastaṃ pradhānam abhrakādikā agre vakṣyamāṇāḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:7 //
children.translated_text: That <s>āranāla</s> is excellent, i.e., foremost, for the treatment (<s>bhāvana</s>), i.e., saturation, of <s>gagana</s> (mica) and other [substances]. The <s>abhraka</s> and other substances will be described ahead. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:7 //

children.text: nirmukhā samukhā ceti dvividhā cāraṇā matā nirmukhā cāraṇā proktā bījādhānena bhāgataḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Cāraṇā</s> (transmutation) is considered to be of two kinds: <s>nirmukha</s> (without mouth) and <s>samukha</s> (with mouth). <s>Nirmukha cāraṇā</s> is described as [proceeding] without the addition of a seed (<s>bīja</s>). // GRhtCM_3.7-9:8 //

children.text: śuddhaṃ svarṇaṃ ca rūpyaṃ ca bījam ityabhidhīyate // GRhtCM_3.7-9:9 //
children.translated_text: Pure gold and silver are called the 'seed' (<s>bīja</s>). // GRhtCM_3.7-9:9 //
The addition of the seed in one-sixty-fourth proportion is called the 'mouth' (<s>mukha</s>). // GRhtCM_3.7-9:10 //

children.text: evaṃ kṛte raso grāsalolupo mukhavān bhavet /
children.translated_text: When done thus, the mercury becomes greedy to devour, endowed with a mouth (<s>mukhavān</s>);

children.text: kaṭhinānyapi lohāni kṣamo bhavati bhakṣaṇe // GRhtCM_3.7-9:11 //
children.translated_text: it becomes capable of consuming even hard metals. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:11 //

children.text: iyaṃ hi samukhā proktā cāraṇā varavārttikaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This is declared to be the <s>samukha</s> (with-mouth) <s>cāraṇā</s> by the best among commentators.
Thus. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:12 //

children.text: abhrakādyapadhātūnāṃ nirmukhacāraṇaṃ hemādidhātūnāṃ samukhacāraṇam iti viveko jñeyaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:13 //
children.translated_text: The <s>nirmukha-cāraṇā</s> (mouthless transmutation) is for <s>abhraka</s> (mica) and other subsidiary metals (<s>apadhātus</s>); the <s>samukha-cāraṇā</s> (with-mouth transmutation) is for gold and other metals (<s>dhātus</s>) — this distinction should be known. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:13 //

children.text: rasāyane śarīrakārye nāgavaṅgau na cāraṇīyau kiṃtu svarṇādikaṃ bījaṃ cāraṇīyam iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:14 //
children.translated_text: In <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation for the body), <s>nāga</s> (lead) and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) should not be transmuted; rather, gold and other [noble] seeds should be transmuted — this is the purport. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:14 //

children.text: ādiśabdena nāgavaṅgayor adhikāraviśeṣam āha tasminnityādi // GRhtCM_3.7-9:15 //
children.translated_text: By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), he states the specific domain [of application] for <s>nāga</s> and <s>vaṅga</s> — 'in that' and so forth. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:15 //

children.text: tasmin pūrvoktasaṃdhāne śuddhaṃ nirmalīkṛtaṃ nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ pradrāvya jalarūpaṃ vidhāya vahniyogāt iti śeṣaḥ niṣecayet niṣekaḥ kartavyaḥ vā tatraiva saṃdhāne vaṅgaṃ raṅgaṃ pradrāvya niṣecayet // GRhtCM_3.7-9:16 //
children.translated_text: In that aforementioned <s>saṃdhāna</s> (preparation), having melted pure, i.e., purified, <s>nāga</s> (<s>sīsaka</s>, lead) and made it liquid by application of fire — this is the remainder — one should pour it, i.e., the pouring should be done; or in that same preparation, having melted <s>vaṅga</s> (<s>raṅga</s>, tin), one should pour it. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:16 //

children.text: kativārān śataṃ vārān pratiśatam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:17 //
children.translated_text: How many times? A hundred times — meaning a hundred times each. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:17 //

children.text: tadvaṅgaṃ tāravidhau rūpyavidhāne yojyaṃ rasena saha militaṃ kāryam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:18 //
children.translated_text: That <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) is to be employed in the <s>tāra-vidhi</s> (silver procedure), i.e., in the preparation of silver — it should be combined with <s>rasa</s> (mercury) — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:18 //

children.text: āsyām āryāyāṃ svarṇādhikāre'nuktamapi nāgaṃ granthāntarāt samāyojyam iti viśeṣārthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:19 //
children.translated_text: In this <s>āryā</s> verse, though unstated in the context of gold, <s>nāga</s> (lead) should be supplied from other texts — this is the specific meaning. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:19 //

children.text: tannāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca rasāyane śarīrasiddhinimittaṃ na yojyamiti yato nāgavaṅgaprabhavāv aupādhikau doṣau galabandhagulmadau kathitau etannāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca grāsārthe yojyamiti yuktaṃ yata etenāntargatenānyadapi grāhyaṃ dravyaṃ grasatīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:20 //
children.translated_text: That <s>nāga</s> (lead) and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) should not be employed in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation for bodily perfection), because the defects arising from lead and tin — throat-obstruction (<s>galabandha</s>), abdominal tumor (<s>gulma</s>), and so forth — are described as adventitious faults. This <s>nāga</s> and <s>vaṅga</s> should be employed for the purpose of [mercury's] devouring (<s>grāsa</s>), since through their being assimilated internally, other substances too are consumed — this is the purport. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:20 //
A specification regarding <s>vaṅga</s> (tin):

children.text: khurakaṃ miśrakaṃ ceti dvividhaṃ vaṅgam ucyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaṅga</s> is said to be of two kinds: <s>khuraka</s> (hoof-type) and <s>miśraka</s> (mixed type).

children.text: khurakaṃ guṇataḥ śreṣṭhaṃ miśrakaṃ na rase hitam // GRhtCM_3.7-9:21 //
children.translated_text: <s>Khuraka</s> is superior in qualities; <s>miśraka</s> is not beneficial for <s>rasa</s> (mercury). // GRhtCM_3.7-9:21 //
Thus, the [type] suitable for silver-work should be selected. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:22 //
Explaining the sequence beginning with <s>gagana</s> (mica), he says '<s>gagana</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_3.7-9:23 //

children.text: anena pūrvoktasaṃdhānena sarvaṃ sakalaṃ bhāvyaṃ bhāvitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_3.7-9:24 //
children.translated_text: By the aforementioned <s>saṃdhāna</s> (conjunction process), everything, all [substances], should be processed (<s>bhāvita</s>). || GRhtCM 3.7-9:24 ||

'Everything' means what? The powders of <s>gagana</s> (mica), mercury (<s>rasa</s>), <s>uparasas</s> (semi-metals), <s>amṛta</s> (nectar/poison), metals, iron-compounds, and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.7-9:25 ||

children.text: gaganamabhrakaṃ vajrasaṃjñikaṃ rasā mahārasā hiṅgulasvarṇamākṣikarūpyamākṣikaśilājatucapalacumbakavaikrāntakharparagairikasphaṭikakāsīsasaṃjñakā amṛtaṃ viṣaṃ vā amṛtalohā na mṛtā amṛtā amṛtāśca te lohāś ca dhāvata iti rasāḥ pūrvoktāḥ āyasā lohās teṣāṃ saṃyogajāni yāni cūrṇāni kalkāni śulbābhrādīni // GRhtCM_3.7-9:26 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gagana</s> is mica (<s>abhraka</s>), also known as <s>vajra</s>. <s>Rasas</s> (minerals) and <s>mahārasas</s> (great minerals) are: <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold pyrite), <s>rūpyamākṣika</s> (silver pyrite), <s>śilājatu</s> (bitite), <s>capala</s> (bismuth), <s>cumbaka</s> (magnetite), <s>vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline), <s>kharpara</s> (zinc carbonate), <s>gairika</s> (red ochre), <s>sphaṭika</s> (quartz crystal), and <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol). <s>Amṛta</s> means poison; or <s>amṛta-lohas</s> are those metals that are not dead (<s>amṛta</s>), i.e., living [metals]; and 'those metals run (<s>dhāvata</s>).' <s>Rasas</s> are as previously stated. <s>Āyasa</s> means metals; the powders (<s>cūrṇas</s>) and pastes (<s>kalkas</s>) born from their combination, such as copper-mica compounds and the like. || GRhtCM 3.7-9:26 ||
By the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), the <s>uparasas</s> (semi-metals) are also included. || GRhtCM 3.7-9:27 ||

children.text: na kevalametānyeva saṃdhānena bhāvyāni kiṃtvanyad api yat kiṃcic cāraṇāvastu cāraṇayogyaṃ dravyaratnādikaṃ tadapyetena saṃdhānena bhāvyaṃ cāraṇārtham // GRhtCM_3.7-9:28 //
children.translated_text: Not only these are to be processed by the conjunction — but also whatever else is a substance suitable for <s>cāraṇa</s> (ingestion by mercury), such as gems and the like — that too is to be processed by this conjunction for the purpose of <s>cāraṇa</s>. || GRhtCM 3.7-9:28 ||
START GRht 3.10

children.text: ādau khalve mṛditāṃ piṣṭīṃ hemnaśca tāṃ rasaścarati /
children.translated_text: First, having ground the paste (<s>piṣṭī</s>) of gold in a mortar, mercury consumes (<s>carati</s>) it;

children.text: tārasya tārakarmaṇi dattvā sūte tato gaganam // GRht_3.10 //
children.translated_text: for silver-work, having added silver to the mercury, then [add] mica (<s>gagana</s>). || GRht 3.10 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specific procedure for gold and silver, saying 'first' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.10:1 ||

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ hemnaḥ svarṇasya piṣṭīṃ khalve mṛditāṃ vakṣyamāṇena iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.10:2 //
children.translated_text: Then, the paste (<s>piṣṭī</s>) of gold (<s>hema</s>), ground in a mortar — by the method to be described — thus the remainder [is to be supplied]. || GRhtCM 3.10:2 ||
Mercury consumes (<s>carati</s>) that paste. || GRhtCM 3.10:3 ||

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā piṣṭīṃ dadyāt ādau prathamataḥ sūteśvare gaganamabhrakaṃ dattvā // GRhtCM_3.10:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what, should one add the paste? First, having added mica (<s>gagana</s>), i.e., <s>abhraka</s>, to the lord of mercury (<s>sūteśvara</s>). || GRhtCM 3.10:4 ||
The procedure for gold has been shown. || GRhtCM 3.10:5 ||

children.text: hemakarmaṇi hemaiva tārakarmaṇi tārameva dadyāt // GRhtCM_3.10:6 //
children.translated_text: For gold-work, one should add gold itself; for silver-work, silver itself. || GRhtCM 3.10:6 ||
The distinction regarding gold:
Gold is said to be of five kinds: natural (<s>prākṛta</s>), innate (<s>sahaja</s>), and fire-born (<s>agnija</s>);
these three [kinds of] gold are to be used [when] of sixteen <s>varṇas</s> (carats). || GRhtCM 3.10:7 ||
Mined (<s>khanija</s>) and produced by alchemical transmutation (<s>rasavādottha</s>), well-leafed and purified —
that, endowed with fourteen <s>varṇas</s>, destroys diseases of humans. || GRhtCM 3.10:8 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.10:9 ||
The distinction regarding silver as well:

children.text: kailāse sahajaṃ rūpyaṃ khanijaṃ kṛtrimaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Silver found on <s>Kailāsa</s> is innate (<s>sahaja</s>); [then] mined (<s>khanija</s>) and artificial (<s>kṛtrima</s>) likewise.

children.text: vyutkrameṇa guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ nāgottīrṇe rase hitam // GRhtCM_3.10:10 //
children.translated_text: In reverse order, each is superior in qualities; in mercury freed from lead (<s>nāgottīrṇa</s>), it is beneficial. || GRhtCM 3.10:10 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.10:11 ||
Silver too should be processed with the previous <s>varṇa</s> [standard]. || GRhtCM 3.10:12 ||
START GRht 3.11
Having added bit by bit (<s>truṭiśaḥ</s>), grinding in a steel mortar — mica, gold, metal, and such —
the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) consumes [them], with the acids of earth[-born plants], <s>khaga</s> (bird-like plant), willow (<s>vetasa</s>), citron (<s>bījapūra</s>). || GRht 3.11 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the substances and instruments for grinding the paste, saying 'bit by bit' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.11:1 ||

children.text: abhrahemalohādīni abhramabhrakaṃ pratītaṃ hema kanakaṃ tadeva lohaḥ abhrakaṃ ca hemalohaśca tāv ādī yasya tat // GRhtCM_3.11:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Mica, gold, metal, and such' — <s>abhra</s> is mica, which is well-known; <s>hema</s> is gold; that itself is the metal; mica and gold-metal — these two being the initial ones of which, that. || GRhtCM 3.11:2 ||

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ dravyaṃ kṣitikhagavetasabījapūrāmlaiḥ kṣitiśca khagaś ca vetasaṃ ca bījapūraś ca kṣitikhagabījapūrāḥ bījapūro mātuluṅgaḥ teṣāṃ trayāṇāmamlāḥ tair mṛditaṃ gharṣitaṃ sat rasendraś carati // GRhtCM_3.11:3 //
children.translated_text: Such a substance — with the acids of earth[-born], <s>khaga</s>, willow (<s>vetasa</s>), and citron (<s>bījapūra</s>): <s>kṣiti</s> (earth) and <s>khaga</s> (bird) and <s>vetasa</s> and <s>bījapūra</s> — <s>bījapūra</s> is citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>); the acids (<s>amla</s>) of those three — having been ground, i.e., rubbed with those, the lord of mercury consumes [the substances]. || GRhtCM 3.11:3 ||

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā mṛditaṃ truṭiśo 'lpamātraṃ dattvā // GRhtCM_3.11:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what — ground? Having added bit by bit (<s>truṭiśaḥ</s>), in small measure. || GRhtCM 3.11:4 ||
In what? In a steel (<s>sāra</s>) mortar. || GRhtCM 3.11:5 ||
Of steel — of the sharp (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) type — this is the steel; in such a [mortar]. || GRhtCM 3.11:6 ||
The distinction regarding steel:

children.text: muṇḍaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tathā kāntaṃ bhedāstasya trayodaśa /
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍa</s> (cast iron), <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (wrought iron), and <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron) — its varieties are thirteen.

children.text: mṛdu kuṇṭhaṃ ca kaḍāraṃ trividhaṃ muṇḍamucyate // GRhtCM_3.11:7 //
children.translated_text: Soft (<s>mṛdu</s>), blunt (<s>kuṇṭha</s>), and tawny (<s>kaḍāra</s>) — <s>muṇḍa</s> is said to be threefold. || GRhtCM 3.11:7 ||

children.text: kharasāraṃ ca hannālaṃ tārāvartaṃ viḍaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kharasāra</s> (coarse-grained), <s>hannāla</s>, <s>tārāvarta</s> (star-whirl), <s>viḍa</s> (acid-treated),

children.text: kālalohaṃ gajākhyaṃ ca ṣaḍvidhaṃ tīkṣṇamucyate // GRhtCM_3.11:8 //
children.translated_text: <s>kālaloha</s> (black iron), and <s>gajākhya</s> (elephant-named) — <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is said to be sixfold. || GRhtCM 3.11:8 ||

children.text: kāntaṃ lohaṃ caturdhoktaṃ romakaṃ bhrāmakaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> (magnetic) iron is said to be fourfold: <s>romaka</s> (hairy), <s>bhrāmaka</s> (rotating),

children.text: cumbakaṃ drāvakaṃ ceti guṇās tasyottarottarāḥ // GRhtCM_3.11:9 //
children.translated_text: <s>cumbaka</s> (kissing/attracting), and <s>drāvaka</s> (melting) — each subsequent one has superior qualities. || GRhtCM 3.11:9 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.11:10 ||
The mortar (<s>khalva</s>) is as follows:
The mortar should be made of stone and the like, without cracks, with a basin two finger-breadths [deep],

children.text: aṣṭāṅgulāvaṭī kāryā dīrghā vā vartulā tathā // GRhtCM_3.11:11 //
children.translated_text: and a cavity of eight finger-breadths, either oblong or circular. || GRhtCM 3.11:11 ||
With a pestle twelve finger-breadths long and four finger-breadths [wide],

children.text: mukhaṃ vṛttaṃ tu kartavyaṃ darpaṇodarasaṃnibham // GRhtCM_3.11:12 //
children.translated_text: the face should be made round, resembling the surface of a mirror. || GRhtCM 3.11:12 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.11:13 ||
'Of stone and the like' — it should be understood [to include] those made of stone, iron, and sun-stone (<s>arka</s>). || GRhtCM 3.11:14 ||
START GRht 3.12-13

children.text: samukhaṃ nirmukhamathavā tulyaṃ dviguṇaṃ caturguṇaṃ vāpi /
children.translated_text: With the face (<s>samukha</s>) or without the face (<s>nirmukha</s>), or equal, or double, or fourfold,
or eightfold, or sixteenfold, or multiplied by thirty-two — || GRht 3.12 ||

children.text: iti pattrābhrakam uktaṃ tena vidhānena cārayetsūtam /
children.translated_text: thus the leaf-mica (<s>pattrābhraka</s>) has been described; by that method one should make mercury consume [it].
<s>cāraṇa</s> (ingestion process)

children.text: grāsaḥ piṣṭī garbhastrilakṣaṇā cāraṇā bhavati // GRht_3.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Grāsa</s> (swallowing), <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste-formation), and <s>garbha</s> (impregnation) — the <s>cāraṇa</s> has three characteristics. || GRht 3.13 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: dhātvādīnāṃ cāraṇāyāṃ parimāṇamāha samukham ityādi // GRhtCM_3.12-13:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the measure for the <s>cāraṇa</s> (ingestion) of metals and such, saying 'with the face' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.12-13:1 ||

children.text: iti pūrvoktaṃ pattrābhrakam uktaṃ pattrābhrakacāraṇam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.12-13:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus the previously described leaf-mica is stated — the meaning is: the <s>cāraṇa</s> of leaf-mica. || GRhtCM 3.12-13:2 ||

children.text: samukhaṃ mukhasahitaṃ cāraṇaṃ bhavatu vātha nirmukhaṃ mukhavarjitaṃ cāraṇaṃ bhavatu ubhayatrāpi tulyaṃ samānaṃ sūtaṃ cārayet dhātvādīniti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.12-13:3 //
children.translated_text: Let the <s>cāraṇa</s> be 'with the face,' i.e., accompanied by the face (opening), or let it be 'without the face,' i.e., devoid of the opening — in both cases, one should make mercury consume metals and the like in equal proportion — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 3.12-13:3 ||

children.text: atra vikalpo dviguṇaṃ sūtād dviguṇitaṃ cārayed vā caturguṇitaṃ sūtāccaturguṇitaṃ vā aṣṭaguṇaṃ sūtādaṣṭaguṇitaṃ vā ṣoḍaśaguṇaṃ sūtāt ṣoḍaśaguṇitaṃ vā dvātriṃśatāguṇitaṃ sūtād dvātriṃśadguṇitaṃ cārayet // GRhtCM_3.12-13:4 //
children.translated_text: Here is the alternative: double — twice the amount of mercury; or fourfold — four times the mercury; or eightfold — eight times the mercury; or sixteenfold — sixteen times the mercury; or thirty-two times — thirty-two times the mercury — one should make [it] consume. || GRhtCM 3.12-13:4 ||

children.text: tena vidhānena pūrvoktena vidhānena truṭiśo dattvetyādinā // GRhtCM_3.12-13:5 //
children.translated_text: By that method — by the previously stated method, i.e., by adding bit by bit and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.12-13:5 ||

children.text: cāraṇā trilakṣaṇā bhavati trīṇi lakṣaṇāni cihnāni yasyāṃ sā tathoktā // GRhtCM_3.12-13:6 //
children.translated_text: The <s>cāraṇa</s> has three characteristics — that which has three distinguishing marks is so called. || GRhtCM 3.12-13:6 ||

children.text: kathaṃ grāsaḥ abhrakasya grāsanaṃ nirmukhatvena samukhatvena vāparā piṣṭī rasenābhrāder melanaṃ punargarbho rasasya garbhe rasarūpaṃ gaganaṃ tiṣṭhatīti // GRhtCM_3.12-13:7 //
children.translated_text: How? <s>Grāsa</s> (swallowing) — the swallowing of mica, either without the face or with the face. The second, <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste) — the amalgamation of mica and such with mercury. Again, <s>garbha</s> (impregnation) — the mica remains in the womb of mercury, in the form of mercury. || GRhtCM 3.12-13:7 ||
Being a pair due to the syntactic connection of the two verses. || GRhtCM 3.12-13:8 ||
START GRht 3.14-15
<wrong ideas about <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion process)>
Those who, by the <s>dolana</s> (swinging) method, [use] mica prepared with various <s>bhaṅga</s> (breaking/levigation) processes,

children.text: cāraṇavidhau pradiṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ noddhūyamānaṃ taiḥ // GRht_3.14 //
children.translated_text: prescribed in the <s>cāraṇa</s> procedure — it is seen that [the mica] is not sublimated by them. || GRht 3.14 ||
Others too, of worthless intellect, [use] sulphur paste, copper paste, and powder;
sublimated by the <s>dolana</s> method, they think that to be mercury-digested (<s>rasa-jīrṇa</s>). || GRht 3.15 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: iti gaganādigrāsapramāṇaṃ kathitam atha cāraṇāvidhānamāha dolanavidhinetyādi // GRhtCM_3.14-15:1 //
children.translated_text: Thus the measure of mica-swallowing has been stated. Now he describes the method of <s>cāraṇa</s>, saying 'by the <s>dolana</s> method' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:1 ||

children.text: gaganamabhrakaṃ yair auṣadhaiḥ piṣṭaṃ peṣitaṃ bhavati tair evauṣadhair nālpamānair bahumānair nānāvidhabhaṅgasaṃskṛtaṃ kuryāditi śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.14-15:2 //
children.translated_text: The mica (<s>abhraka</s>) that has been ground, i.e., levigated, with certain medicinal substances — with those very substances, not in small but in large measure, one should prepare it processed with various <s>bhaṅga</s> (breaking) treatments — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:2 ||

children.text: nānāvidhā anekaprakārā ye bhaṅgās taraṃgā āgamābdhijātās taiḥ saṃskṛtam upaskṛtam // GRhtCM_3.14-15:3 //
children.translated_text: The various, i.e., manifold, <s>bhaṅgas</s> (wave-like processes) born from the ocean of scripture — processed, i.e., treated with those. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:3 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ gaganaṃ māraṇavidhinā pañcatvavidhānena uddiṣṭam uddeśitam /
children.translated_text: Of what character is the mica? Prescribed by the <s>māraṇa</s> (killing/calcination) method, i.e., indicated by the process of reducing to the five [elements].

children.text: evaṃvidham api gaganaṃ dolanavidhinā cāraṇāyāṃ yojyamiti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.14-15:4 //
children.translated_text: Even such mica should be employed in <s>cāraṇa</s> by the <s>dolana</s> (swinging) method — this is the purport. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:4 ||
Now he states the view of those of small intellect, saying 'others' and so forth.

children.text: anye mahadbhyo 'pare tucchamatayas tucchā stokā matirbuddhiryeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ alpabuddhaya iti yāvat // GRhtCM_3.14-15:5 //
children.translated_text: Others — those different from the great ones — of worthless intellect, i.e., those whose intellect (<s>mati</s>), i.e., understanding (<s>buddhi</s>), is trivial (<s>tuccha</s>) — so called, meaning of little intelligence. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:5 ||

children.text: rasaṃ jīrṇaṃ jāraṇasaṃskāropapannaṃ rasaṃ manyante iti // GRhtCM_3.14-15:6 //
children.translated_text: They think, i.e., consider, the mercury to be digested (<s>jīrṇa</s>), i.e., endowed with the <s>jāraṇa</s>-processing. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:6 ||

children.text: kiṃ gandhakaniṣpiṣṭiśulbapiṣṭirajo gandhakena yā niṣpiṣṭiḥ piṣṭībhūtā śulbena yā piṣṭiḥ piṣṭībhūtā tāmrapiṣṭītyarthaḥ gandhakaniṣpiṣṭiśca śulbapiṣṭiśca tayoryadrajaḥ pāṃśuḥ gandhakapiṣṭī yathā /
children.translated_text: What [is used]? 'Sulphur paste, copper paste, and powder' — the paste (<s>niṣpiṣṭi</s>) made with sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), the paste made with copper (<s>śulba</s>) — meaning a copper paste — the powder (<s>rajas</s>), i.e., the dust, of the sulphur paste and copper paste. The sulphur paste is as follows:
The powder of sulphur-stone (<s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>),

children.text: bhāvayetsaptavāraṃ tu strīraktena ca saptadhā // GRhtCM_3.14-15:7 //
children.translated_text: should be soaked seven times with the juice of chickpea, and seven times with menstrual blood. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:7 ||
One <s>pala</s> (measure) of purified mercury should then be placed in a <s>kharpara</s> (saucer);
the soaked sulphur should be added, combined with a <s>narapiṇḍa</s> (human-shaped bolus). || GRhtCM 3.14-15:8 ||

children.text: dolāyantre'pi tāpena piṣṭikā bhavati kṣaṇāt // GRhtCM_3.14-15:9 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swinging apparatus), through heating, a paste forms instantly. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:9 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:10 ||
Likewise, a paste is also produced from copper. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:11 ||
Of what character is the sulphur-paste-copper-paste powder? Produced by the <s>dolana</s> method, i.e., generated by the procedure of the swinging apparatus. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:12 ||
What has thus been stated — that is improper. Such is the purport. || GRhtCM 3.14-15:13 ||
START GRht 3.16
<s>golakamukha</s> (bolus-opening method)>
When mercury is heated with oil and the like, through the <s>golaka-mukha</s> (bolus-opening) of gold, silver, and such,

children.text: carati ghanaṃ rasarājo hemādibhir eti piṇḍatvam // GRht_3.16 //
children.translated_text: the king of mercury (<s>rasarāja</s>) consumes the dense [mica], and with gold and other [metals] attains the state of a solid mass (<s>piṇḍatva</s>). || GRht 3.16 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing the <s>vāsanā-mukha</s> (aromatic-opening) <s>cāraṇa</s>, which is included within the 'with-face' (<s>samukha</s>) <s>cāraṇa</s>, he says 'with oil' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.16:1 ||

children.text: rasarājaḥ pārado hāṭakatārādi svarṇarūpyādi dhātudravyaṃ kṛtrimākṛtrimātmakanavasaṃkhyākaṃ pūrvamuktaṃ carati bhakṣati // GRhtCM_3.16:2 //
children.translated_text: The king of mercury (<s>rasarāja</s>), i.e., <s>pārada</s> (mercury), consumes, i.e., ingests, the metallic substances of gold, silver, and so forth — the nine [metals], both natural and artificial, previously stated. || GRhtCM 3.16:2 ||
By what means? Through the <s>golaka-mukha</s> (bolus-opening). || GRhtCM 3.16:3 ||

children.text: golakaśca mukhaviśeṣaḥ tena viḍasya golakenetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.16:4 //
children.translated_text: The <s>golaka</s> is a particular type of opening (<s>mukha</s>); through that, meaning through the bolus of <s>viḍa</s> (acid-treated substance) — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 3.16:4 ||
Under what condition? When the mercury has been heated with oil and the like. || GRhtCM 3.16:5 ||

children.text: tailam ādiḥ yeṣāṃ te tailādikās tailavasāmūtraśukrapuṣpāḥ etaistapto yo rasa uṣṇatvaṃ nīto yo 'sau pāradastasmin satyevaṃ ghanamabhrakaṃ carati rasendraḥ // GRhtCM_3.16:6 //
children.translated_text: Those whose initial [ingredient] is oil are called 'oil and the like' — [namely] oil, fat (<s>vasā</s>), urine (<s>mūtra</s>), semen (<s>śukra</s>), and menstrual fluid (<s>puṣpa</s>). The mercury (<s>pārada</s>) that has been heated, i.e., brought to a state of warmth, with these — when that [condition] exists, thus the king of mercury consumes the dense mica. || GRhtCM 3.16:6 ||
Furthermore, having swallowed the nine [metals] beginning with gold, it attains the state of a solid mass (<s>piṇḍatva</s>), i.e., reaches a state of compactness. || GRhtCM 3.16:7 ||
The oils are as follows:
Produced from <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus paniculatus), <s>tumbinī</s>, <s>ghoṣā</s>, <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia pinnata), and <s>śrīphala</s> (Aegle marmelos);
from <s>kaṭu</s> (pungent [mustard]), <s>vātāri</s>, <s>siddhārtha</s> (white mustard), <s>somarājī</s> (Vernonia anthelmintica), and <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica); || GRhtCM 3.16:8 ||
from linseed (<s>atasī</s>), <s>mahākālī</s>, neem (<s>nimba</s>), and sesame (<s>tila</s>) likewise;
<s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera), <s>devadālī</s>, <s>dantī</s> (Baliospermum), castor (<s>tumbaru</s>), and <s>vigraha</s>; || GRhtCM 3.16:9 ||
oils produced from the fruits of <s>aṅkola</s> (Alangium), datura (<s>unmatta</s>), and marking-nut (<s>bhallāta</s>, Semecarpus anacardium).
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.16:10 ||
The fats (<s>vasā</s>) are as follows:
The fat of goat (<s>aja</s>), camel (<s>uṣṭra</s>), donkey (<s>khara</s>), and ram (<s>meṣa</s>), and of buffalo (<s>mahiṣa</s>) likewise.
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.16:11 ||
The urine, menstrual fluid, and semen are as follows:
The urines of elephant, young elephant (<s>karabha</s>), she-buffalo, donkey, and horse;

children.text: striyaḥ puṃsas tathā mūtraṃ puṣpaṃ vīryaṃ ca yojayet /
children.translated_text: the urine of woman and man likewise; menstrual fluid (<s>puṣpa</s>) and semen (<s>vīrya</s>) should be employed.
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.16:12 ||
START GRht 3.17
<s>mukha</s> (opening method): <s>śukapicchamukha</s> (parrot-feather opening)>

children.text: anye svacchaṃ kṛtvā śukapicchamukhena cārayanti ghanam /
children.translated_text: Others, having purified [mercury], make it consume the dense [mica] through the parrot-feather opening (<s>śukapiccha-mukha</s>),
by the method taught by the <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected masters) — with a moist swallowing, not with a dry one. || GRht 3.17 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
On that same topic, he states another view, saying 'others' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.17:1 ||

children.text: eke uktavidhānena cāraṇāṃ kurvanti anye apare rasaṃ pāradaṃ svacchaṃ kṛtvā svedanādyaṣṭasaṃskāropasaṃskṛtaṃ vidhāya vā hiṅgulotthaṃ ghanam abhrakaṃ cārayanti abhrakasya cāraṇāṃ kurvanti // GRhtCM_3.17:2 //
children.translated_text: Some perform <s>cāraṇa</s> by the stated method. Others, i.e., different [practitioners], having made the mercury (<s>pārada</s>) pure (<s>svaccha</s>), i.e., having prepared it as refined through the eight <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory processes) beginning with <s>svedana</s> (sweating), or [using mercury] derived from cinnabar (<s>hiṅgulottha</s>), make it consume the dense mica — i.e., perform the <s>cāraṇa</s> of mica. || GRhtCM 3.17:2 ||

children.text: kena śukapicchamukhena śukapicchaṃ saṃdhānaviśeṣaḥ mukhaṃ viśeṣo yeṣāṃ saṃdhānānāṃ tena // GRhtCM_3.17:3 //
children.translated_text: By what? By means of the <s>śukapicchamukha</s> — <s>śukapiccham</s> is a particular type of flux (<s>saṃdhāna</s>); that which has this flux as its foremost [agent], by that. || GRhtCM 3.17:3 ||

children.text: kva sati cārayanti āśitagrāse sati bhuktakavale sati punaś cāryam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.17:4 //
children.translated_text: Under what condition do they perform <s>cāraṇa</s> (roaming/assimilation)? When the morsel has been consumed (<s>āśitagrāse sati</s>) — meaning when the previous bolus has been eaten, then another <s>cāraṇa</s> should be performed: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 3.17:4 ||

children.text: kena siddhopadeśavidhinā siddhā rasasiddhā nityanāthavīranāthādayaḥ pūrvoktāḥ teṣāṃ ya upadeśavidhis tena // GRhtCM_3.17:5 //
children.translated_text: By what method? By the method of instruction of the <s>Siddhas</s> — the <s>Siddhas</s>, those perfected in mercury-work such as <s>Nityanātha</s>, <s>Vīranātha</s>, and others previously mentioned — by their method of instruction. || GRhtCM 3.17:5 ||

children.text: na śuṣkeṇa saṃdhānenārdrībhāvāt nīrasatāṃ prāptena punaścāraṇā na syāt // GRhtCM_3.17:6 //
children.translated_text: Not with a dried-out flux — [because] having become moist, when it has reached a juiceless state, <s>cāraṇa</s> cannot be performed again. || GRhtCM 3.17:6 ||
The <s>śukapiccham</s> (parrot-feather [flux]) is as follows:
Having mixed ash, alkalis, very dry [substances], [more] alkalis, and salts

children.text: āloḍya hy amlavargeṇa śulbabhāṇḍe nidhāpayet // GRhtCM_3.17:7 //
children.translated_text: by stirring with the sour group [of substances], one should deposit [them] in a copper vessel. || GRhtCM 3.17:7 ||
And when the mica becomes [colored] like a parrot's feather, one should treat [the mercury] with it —
mercury swallows it at that very instant, and a ball (<s>golaka</s>) is formed. || GRhtCM 3.17:8 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.17:9 ||
[START GRht 3.18]
<Mercury: <s>cāraṇa</s> (assimilation)>
Alternatively, <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) [combined with] <s>gagana</s> (mica) in equal parts, combined with <s>paṭu</s> (rock salt), cooked —
having placed [it] in an iron vessel, after steaming, [the mercury] assimilates the black mica. || GRht 3.18 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Presenting an alternative method from another school of thought, he says beginning with 'alternatively' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.18:1 ||

children.text: pūrvoktaṃ vidhānaṃ kuryāt athavā pakṣāntare idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_3.18:2 //
children.translated_text: One should perform the previously stated procedure, or alternatively, in the other option, one should perform what is about to be described. || GRhtCM 3.18:2 ||

children.text: mākṣikagaganamiti mākṣikena yuktaṃ gaganam abhrakaṃ samabhāgaṃ dvayaṃ tulyabhāgaṃ puṭitaṃ bhāvitaṃ yat paṭu saindhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ śāstrāntarasāmyād amlavargeṇa puṭitaṃ tena yutaṃ militaṃ sat pakvaṃ vahnipuṭitaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.18:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣikagaganam</s>: <s>gagana</s> (mica) combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite); <s>samabhāgam</s>: the two in equal proportions; <s>paṭu</s> is <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) — from the correspondence with other treatises, [it should be] processed with the sour group; combined with that (<s>yutam</s>), meaning mixed; <s>pakvam</s>: cooked by fire-treatment — one should do so: this is the completion [of the sentence]. || GRhtCM 3.18:3 ||

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā lohapātre muṇḍādibhājane prakṣipya madhye sthāpya // GRhtCM_3.18:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having placed [it] in a metal vessel such as an iron pot (<s>muṇḍa</s>) — having deposited [it] in the middle. || GRhtCM 3.18:4 ||

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ kṛṣṇābhraṃ svedāntarvahnitāpamadhye rasaḥ pāradaś carati grasati mākṣikasaṃyogāt kṣipram iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.18:5 //
children.translated_text: Such black mica — amidst the heat of fire (<s>svedāntar</s>) — mercury, <s>pārada</s>, assimilates [it], swallows [it] — quickly, due to the combination with <s>mākṣika</s>: this is the purport. || GRhtCM 3.18:5 ||
[START GRht 3.19]
I shall teach that instruction by which the entry of sulphur and mica [into mercury takes place],

children.text: pakṣachinnaś ca raso yogyaḥ syād rasarasāyanayoḥ // GRht_3.19 //
children.translated_text: and the mercury, with its wings clipped, becomes fit for both <s>rasa</s> (therapeutic mercury) and <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). || GRht 3.19 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the method of instruction, beginning with 'that' and so forth.

children.text: yenopadeśena gandhābhrakapraveśanaṃ gandhapāṣāṇasaṃyogād yadabhrapraveśena bhavati abhrasya pāradāntaḥpraveśo bhavati tamupadeśamahaṃ kavir vakṣyāmi kathayiṣye // GRhtCM_3.19:1 //
children.translated_text: By which instruction the entry of sulphur and mica occurs — by the combination with <s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s> (sulphur-stone), by which entry of mica takes place, the mica enters inside mercury — that instruction I, the poet, shall declare, shall tell. || GRhtCM 3.19:1 ||
Due to extreme proximity [in time], the present tense [<s>laṭ</s>] is used [for a future action]. || GRhtCM 3.19:2 ||
<s>Tu</s> means 'furthermore.' || GRhtCM 3.19:3 ||

children.text: pakṣachinnaśca raso rasarasāyanayor yogyaḥ rase jvarādiroganāśake jvarāṅkuśādau rasāyane ca jarāvyādhināśane prayoge yogyaḥ samarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.19:4 //
children.translated_text: And the mercury, with its wings clipped (<s>pakṣacchinna</s>), becomes fit for both <s>rasa</s> and <s>rasāyana</s> — for <s>rasa</s>, meaning in the destruction of diseases such as fever, in preparations like <s>jvarāṅkuśa</s>; and for <s>rasāyana</s>, meaning in the application that destroys old age and disease — fit, capable. || GRhtCM 3.19:4 ||
As [stated] in the <s>Mañjarī</s>:
Killed (<s>mārita</s>) [mercury is] for the purpose of bodily purification; swooned (<s>mūrchita</s>) [mercury] destroys diseases.

children.text: rasabhasma kvacidroge dehārthe mūrchitaṃ kvacit // GRhtCM_3.19:5 //
children.translated_text: Mercury-ash (<s>rasabhasma</s>) [is used] in some diseases; the swooned [mercury] for bodily purposes in some [cases]. || GRhtCM 3.19:5 ||

children.text: baddhaṃ dvābhyāṃ prayuñjīta śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā // GRhtCM_3.19:6 //
children.translated_text: The bound (<s>baddha</s>) [mercury] should be employed for both [purposes], through procedures prescribed in the treatises. || GRhtCM 3.19:6 ||
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.19:7 ||

children.text: gandhābhrakapraveśena pakṣachinno 'calo bhaved iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.19:8 //
children.translated_text: Through the entry of sulphur and mica, [mercury] with wings clipped becomes immobile (<s>acala</s>): this is the purport. || GRhtCM 3.19:8 ||
[START GRht 3.20]
<Sulphur: special role in alchemy>
Sulphur gives color (<s>rāga</s>) to the king of <s>rasas</s> (mercury), is capable of cooking and assimilating metals (<s>bīja</s>),
clips the wings of mercury — in the binding of mercury, sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) is so declared. || GRht 3.20 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He characterizes sulphur further, beginning with '<s>rasarāja</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.20:1 ||

children.text: rasabandhane pāradabandhane gandhako 'bhitaḥ lelinakaḥ sarvotkṛṣṭaḥ // GRhtCM_3.20:2 //
children.translated_text: In the binding of mercury (<s>rasabandhana</s>) — in the fixation of <s>pārada</s> — sulphur is declared supreme, the most excellent of all [agents]. || GRhtCM 3.20:2 ||

children.text: kuto yataḥ sūtakapakṣacchedī gandhakaḥ sūtasya pāradasya pakṣau chinatti // GRhtCM_3.20:3 //
children.translated_text: Why? Because sulphur clips the wings of mercury (<s>sūtaka</s>) — it cuts the wings of <s>pārada</s>. || GRhtCM 3.20:3 ||

children.text: punaḥ kuto rasarājarāgadāyī rasarājaḥ pāradaḥ tasya rāgaṃ rañjanaṃ dadātīti // GRhtCM_3.20:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, why? It gives color (<s>rāga</s>) to the king of <s>rasas</s> — to <s>rasarāja</s>, that is <s>pārada</s>: it gives coloring (<s>rañjana</s>). || GRhtCM 3.20:4 ||

children.text: punaḥ kuto bījānāṃ pākajāraṇasamarthaḥ pākaśca jāraṇaṃ ca pākajāraṇe // GRhtCM_3.20:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, why? It is capable of cooking and assimilating metals (<s>bīja</s>) — 'cooking' and 'assimilation' [form a compound] <s>pākajāraṇa</s>. || GRhtCM 3.20:5 ||
[START GRht 3.21-25]
<Mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (calcination), <s>pakṣacheda</s> (wing-clipping)>

children.text: dattvā khalve truṭiśo gandhakam ādau rasaṃ ca truṭiśo'pi /
children.translated_text: Having placed in a mortar sulphur bit by bit (<s>truṭiśas</s>), and mercury also bit by bit,

children.text: tāvacca mardanīyaṃ yāvatsā piṣṭikā bhavati // GRht_3.21 //
children.translated_text: one should grind for as long as it takes until that [mixture] becomes a paste (<s>piṣṭikā</s>). || GRht 3.21 ||

children.text: tadanu ca drutabalivasayā samabhāganiyojitaṃ tathā gaganam /
children.translated_text: Then, with the melted fat (<s>drutabalivasā</s>), mica (<s>gagana</s>) combined in equal portion —

children.text: truṭiśo rasaṃ ca dattvā kurvīta yathepsitāṃ piṣṭim // GRht_3.22 //
children.translated_text: having added mercury bit by bit, one should make the desired paste. || GRht 3.22 ||
And that [paste] is then dropped downward in the <s>dīpikā-yantra</s> (lamp apparatus) by means of heated stones.
Thereafter, freed from impurity, with wings clipped, by means of mica and sulphur — || GRht 3.23 ||

children.text: bhasmākāraś ca raso hemnā saha yujyate sa ca dvaṃdve /
children.translated_text: the mercury becomes ash-like, and it unites with gold in the <s>dvaṃdva</s> (paired compound).

children.text: gandhakābhrakābhyāṃ rasapakṣāpakartanaṃ yathā syāttathāha dattvetyādi // GRhtCM_3.21-23:1 //
children.translated_text: He explains how the clipping of mercury's wings by sulphur and mica should be done, beginning with 'having placed' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:1 ||

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ khalve lohārkāśmamaye gandhakaṃ truṭiśo dattvā alpamātraṃ vāraṃ vāraṃ gandharasau dattvā tāvanmardanīyaṃ yāvat sā piṣṭikā ekaśarīratā bhavati kajjaliketi vyaktārthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.21-23:2 //
children.translated_text: First, having placed in a mortar made of iron, copper, or stone, sulphur bit by bit — in small quantities, repeatedly — having placed both sulphur and mercury, one should grind until that paste, the state of being one body (<s>ekaśarīratā</s>), becomes a <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulphide of mercury): this is the clear meaning. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:2 ||

children.text: tadanu tatpaścāt rasagandhakapiṣṭīkaraṇānantaraṃ tatra rasagandhakapiṣṭyā gaganam abhrakaṃ samabhāganiyojitaṃ gandharasābhyāṃ tulyāṃśaṃ militaṃ kāryam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.21-23:3 //
children.translated_text: Then, after that — after making the paste of mercury and sulphur — therein, mica (<s>gagana</s>) combined in equal portion with the mercury-sulphur paste should be mixed in equal parts with the sulphur and mercury: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:3 ||

children.text: kayā kṛtvā drutabalivasayā drutā dravībhūtā yā balivasā bhekamatsyakarkaṭaśiśumārāṇāṃ tailarūpā śarīrajātā tayā // GRhtCM_3.21-23:4 //
children.translated_text: With what? With melted fat (<s>drutabalivasā</s>) — <s>balivasā</s> is the oil-form fat produced from the bodies of frogs, fish, crabs, and crocodiles (<s>śiśumāra</s>); with that which has been liquefied. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:4 ||

children.text: samabhāgābhrakaniyojanānantaraṃ balivasayā mardanaṃ kāryamiti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.21-23:5 //
children.translated_text: After combining mica in equal portion, grinding with the fat should be performed: this is the essential meaning. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:5 ||
The <s>balivasā</s> (animal fat) is as follows:
That which comes from frogs, fish, or the fat of crabs, or alternatively,

children.text: bhāvyam ebhiḥ kramādgandhaṃ śiśumāravasāpi vā // GRhtCM_3.21-23:6 //
children.translated_text: the sulphur should be treated with these in sequence, or also with the fat of crocodile (<s>śiśumāra</s>). || GRhtCM 3.21-23:6 ||
Any one of these fats (<s>balivasā</s>) properly binds mercury
and also produces coloring, according to the procedure involving <s>maṇimūṣā</s> (jewel-crucible). || GRhtCM 3.21-23:7 ||
This is [what is] called <s>balivasā</s> — it binds mercury in an instant.
Thus. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:8 ||
One should make a paste of mercury, sulphur, and mica: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:9 ||

children.text: sā pūrvoktā rasagandhābhrapiṣṭir athetyanantaraṃ dīpikāyantre 'dhaḥpātane raso nirmuktamalas tyaktadoṣo bhavati // GRhtCM_3.21-23:10 //
children.translated_text: The previously mentioned paste of mercury, sulphur, and mica — then, after that, in the <s>dīpikā-yantra</s> (lamp apparatus) by downward distillation, the mercury becomes freed from impurity (<s>nirmuktamala</s>), that is, with defects removed. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:10 ||

children.text: tasminnirmuktamale sati nikṛntapakṣaḥ chinnapakṣo bhavati // GRhtCM_3.21-23:11 //
children.translated_text: When it is freed from impurity, it becomes one with wings clipped (<s>nikṛntapakṣa</s>), that is, with wings cut. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:11 ||

children.text: kābhyām abhragandhābhyām abhraṃ ca gandhaśca abhragandhau tābhyāṃ gandhakāntaḥ saṃyogāt sukhaṃ rasābhrapiṣṭirbhavet yato gandhako dvaṃdvamelanasamarthaḥ kiṃ punarbalivasayeti tṛtīyaślokārthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.21-23:12 //
children.translated_text: By what two? By mica and sulphur (<s>abhragandha</s>). Through the internal combination with sulphur, the paste of mercury and mica is easily [formed]; since sulphur is capable of pairing (<s>dvaṃdvamelana</s>) [them] — how much more so with the [addition of] fat: this is the meaning of the third verse. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:12 ||
[This is] a verse-cluster (<s>kulaka</s>). || GRhtCM 3.21-23:13 ||
He states the form and the accomplishment of another purpose of the previously processed mercury, beginning with 'ash' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:14 ||
<s>Ca</s> means 'furthermore.' || GRhtCM 3.21-23:15 ||

children.text: tato'dhaḥpātanād raso bhasmākāro bhasmasadṛśo bhavet // GRhtCM_3.21-23:16 //
children.translated_text: Then, from the downward distillation, the mercury becomes ash-like (<s>bhasmākāra</s>), resembling ash. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:16 ||

children.text: sa ca bhasmākāro rasaḥ hemnā svarṇena sārdham ubhayamelane yujyate karmavidā iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.21-23:17 //
children.translated_text: And that ash-like mercury unites with gold (<s>hema</s>), that is, with <s>svarṇa</s> — it combines in the pairing of both — by one who knows the procedure: this is the completion. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:17 ||

children.text: athavā samuccaye avyayo rekārthasambandhāt pakṣāntare ca // GRhtCM_3.21-23:18 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, <s>ca</s> as a conjunction particle [indicates] connection with the meaning of the other interpretation, and [indicates] an alternative option. || GRhtCM 3.21-23:18 ||
[START GRht 3.24-25]

children.text: athavā gandhakapiṣṭiṃ paktvā drutagandhakasya madhye tu // GRht_3.24 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, having cooked the sulphur paste, in the midst of melted sulphur — || GRht 3.24 ||
<Mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (calcination), compound with gold>
that gold-paste too is cooked again in sulphur.

children.text: itthaṃ hemnā sūto milati dvaṃdve tathā kṣaṇānmriyate // GRht_3.25 //
children.translated_text: Thus mercury unites with gold in the pair, and dies (<s>mriyate</s>) in an instant thereby. || GRht 3.25 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: athavā hemnā saha pūrvarasavidhānena gandhapiṣṭiṃ kuryāt athavā drutagandhakasya dravībhūtagandhakasya madhye paktvā vahniyogena supakvaṃ kṛtvā rasaṃ piṣṭivat rasahemagandhapiṣṭiṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.24-25:1 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, one should make a sulphur-paste with gold in the manner previously described for mercury; or, having cooked [it] in the midst of melted sulphur — sulphur that has been liquefied — having thoroughly cooked it by the application of fire, one should make a paste of mercury-gold-sulphur like a regular paste: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 3.24-25:1 ||
He states the procedure for the previously mentioned pairing (<s>dvaṃdvamelana</s>), beginning with 'that' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.24-25:2 ||
<s>Ca</s> means 'furthermore.' || GRhtCM 3.24-25:3 ||

children.text: sā pūrvoktā hemapiṣṭiḥ rasahemagandhakṛtaretasoḥ sambandhaḥ sadātanaḥ // GRhtCM_3.24-25:4 //
children.translated_text: That previously mentioned gold-paste — the relationship between the pair made of mercury-gold-sulphur is eternal. || GRhtCM 3.24-25:4 ||

children.text: hemnā militā yā piṣṭimelanaviśet sā hemapiṣṭī bhūyaḥ punaḥ gandhake vipacyate yuktyā pākaḥ kāryaḥ pūrvavad gandhake // GRhtCM_3.24-25:5 //
children.translated_text: The paste united with gold — that gold-paste, mixed through the process of combination, is again cooked in sulphur — the cooking should be done skillfully, as before, in sulphur. || GRhtCM 3.24-25:5 ||

children.text: ittham uktavidhānena hemnā saha sūtaḥ pārado milati granthimeti kva sati dvaṃdve sati ubhayasaṃyoge sati // GRhtCM_3.24-25:6 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the stated procedure, mercury (<s>sūta</s>, <s>pārada</s>) unites with gold (<s>hema</s>), becomes knotted — where? When the pairing (<s>dvaṃdva</s>) exists, when the combination of both exists. || GRhtCM 3.24-25:6 ||

children.text: tathoktavidhānena dvaṃdve milati sati tatkālād alpakālato mriyate pañcatvamupayāti // GRhtCM_3.24-25:7 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, by the stated procedure, when the pairing occurs, from that very time, in a short time, it dies — reaches the state of the five elements [dissolution]. || GRhtCM 3.24-25:7 ||
The purport is that it becomes dead (calcined) through only a small additional operation. || GRhtCM 3.24-25:8 ||
Thus [ends] the procedure for wing-clipping (<s>pakṣaccheda</s>). || GRhtCM 3.24-25:9 ||
[START GRht 3.26]

children.text: itare pakṣacchedaṃ dvaṃdve rasamāraṇaṃ na vāñchanti /
children.translated_text: Others do not desire [merely] wing-clipping; they do not desire the killing of mercury in the paired [compound alone];

children.text: bījānāmapi pākaṃ hṛṣyanti ca tadanu tapyanti // GRht_3.26 //
children.translated_text: nor [do they desire merely] the cooking of metals — they first rejoice, and then they grieve. || GRht 3.26 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: etāvatā rasapakṣakartanena nālaṃ bhavitavyamityāha itare ityādi // GRhtCM_3.26:1 //
children.translated_text: He says that one should not be satisfied with just this much of mercury's wing-clipping, beginning with 'others' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.26:1 ||

children.text: ye puruṣā iti uktavidhānena pakṣacchedaṃ rasapakṣāpakartanaṃ vāñchanti punaḥ dvaṃdve rasamāraṇaṃ dvaṃdvena pūrvoktena rasahemagandhakena kṛtvā yadrasamāraṇaṃ tanna vāñchanti punarbījānāmapi raktābhrahemarasakādīnāmapi pākaṃ vahniyogena supakvakaraṇaṃ na vāñchanti te puruṣāḥ pūrvaṃ pakṣacchedaṃ jñātvā hṛṣyanti harṣayuktā bhavanti pakṣacchedaṃ vinānyakāryasiddhiṃ jñātvetyarthas tadanu ca kāryāsiddhau tapyanti paritāpayuktā bhavanti // GRhtCM_3.26:2 //
children.translated_text: Those persons who desire wing-clipping — the clipping of mercury's wings — by the stated procedure; furthermore, who do not desire the killing of mercury in the paired [compound] — the killing of mercury done by the previously described mercury-gold-sulphur pair; nor do they desire the cooking of metals (<s>bīja</s>) either — the thorough cooking by fire of red mica (<s>raktābhra</s>), gold, mercury-compounds, and such — those persons, first knowing the wing-clipping, rejoice, become delighted; knowing that without wing-clipping the accomplishment of other purposes [is impossible]: that is the meaning. And then, upon the non-accomplishment of [their further] purpose, they grieve — become full of sorrow. || GRhtCM 3.26:2 ||
[START GRht 3.27]
Thus, considering the <s>gagana-cāraṇa</s> (mica-assimilation) to be [beset] with many defects and requiring much labor,

children.text: nirdiśyate prakāraḥ karmaṇi śāstre'pi saṃvādī // GRht_3.27 //
children.translated_text: a [different] method is indicated [here] in this treatise, which is also in accordance with practice. || GRht 3.27 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Having indicated the mica-assimilation, praising another <s>saṃskāra</s>, he says beginning with 'thus' and so forth. || GRhtCM 3.27:1 ||

children.text: mayā granthakartrā asmin śāstre karmaṇyati saṃvādī prakāraḥ agrimaprakaraṇe sattvaniṣkāsanarūpaḥ nirdiśyate nirdeśaḥ kriyate // GRhtCM_3.27:2 //
children.translated_text: By me, the author of the treatise, in this treatise, a method that is fully in accordance with practice — in the form of essence-extraction (<s>sattvaniṣkāsana</s>) in the following section — is indicated, is declared. || GRhtCM 3.27:2 ||
<s>Saṃvādī</s> — meaning it is agreed upon, it is perfected by those who know the <s>saṃskāras</s>. || GRhtCM 3.27:3 ||

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā itthamuktaprakāreṇa anekairdoṣaiḥ anekakaṣṭaiḥ bahuśramairbahvāyāsairgaganacāraṇaṃ matvā abhrakacāraṇaṃ jñātvā // GRhtCM_3.27:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Thus, in the manner described, considering the mica-assimilation (<s>gagana-cāraṇa</s>) — having known the assimilation of mica — [to be beset] with many defects, many difficulties, and requiring much labor, great exertion. || GRhtCM 3.27:4 ||
After mica-assimilation, another more excellent method is indicated: this is the purport. || GRhtCM 3.27:5 ||
[START GRht 3.28]
Ungraspable, without residue, of subtle movement, all-pervading, imperishable — [such is] the <s>jīva</s> (life-force/soul);

children.text: yāvadviśati na yonau tāvadbandhaṃ kuto bhajate // GRht_3.28 //
children.translated_text: so long as it does not enter the womb, how can it experience bondage? || GRht 3.28 ||

Thus, in the treatise called <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>, composed by the <s>Paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācārya</s> (supreme wandering ascetic preceptor), the illustrious <s>Govinda Bhagavatpāda</s>, the third chapter (<s>avabodha</s>), consisting of faceless (<s>nirmukha</s>), impression (<s>vāsanā</s>), faced (<s>mukha</s>), inner-faced (<s>antarbhūta-samukha</s>), leaf-mica (<s>pattra-abhraka</s>), and <s>cāraṇa</s> (consumption) [procedures], is complete.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing another method, [the author] says 'ungraspable' and so forth. // GRhtCM 3.28:1 //

children.text: evaṃvidho harajo yāvadyonau abhrake na viśati na milati yāvadbandhaṃ bandhanaṃ kuto bhajate prāpnoti na kuto'pi yonāv apraviśati sati na bandhanamāpnotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.28:2 //
children.translated_text: Such a <s>Haraja</s> (mercury), so long as it does not enter the womb, i.e., the mica (<s>abhraka</s>), does not combine [with it] — how then can it attain binding (<s>bandhana</s>)? It does not obtain [binding] from anywhere. When it has not entered the womb, it does not attain binding — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 3.28:2 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭo harajaḥ agrāhyaḥ haraḥ kathamapi na gṛhyate 'navayavatvāt harajastadguṇa eva kāraṇānurūpaṃ kāryamiti nyāyāt /
children.translated_text: Of what quality is <s>Haraja</s> (mercury)? 'Ungraspable' (<s>agrāhya</s>) — <s>Hara</s> (Śiva/mercury) cannot be grasped by any means, because of [its] having no parts; <s>Haraja</s> (that born from Hara) has that same quality, by the principle that 'the effect conforms to the cause.'

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭo nirlepaḥ vaikārikair doṣaguṇairna lipyata iti doṣaguṇanivṛtteḥ // GRhtCM_3.28:3 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what quality? 'Unattached' (<s>nirlepa</s>) — it is not stained by modifications [such as] defects and qualities; because of the cessation of defects and qualities. // GRhtCM 3.28:3 //

children.text: punaḥ sūkṣmagatiḥ sūkṣmā gatir gamanaṃ pravartanaṃ vā yasya saḥ dhūmarūpāvalokanatvāt // GRhtCM_3.28:4 //
children.translated_text: Further, 'of subtle movement' (<s>sūkṣma-gati</s>) — that whose movement, motion, or operation is subtle; because it is perceived [only] in the form of smoke. // GRhtCM 3.28:4 //
Further, 'all-pervading' (<s>vyāpaka</s>) — because of its capacity to pervade the body, metals, and the like. // GRhtCM 3.28:5 //

children.text: punarakṣayaḥ na kṣayo yasyetyakṣayaḥ sarvadā bhāvarūpatvāt // GRhtCM_3.28:6 //
children.translated_text: Further, 'imperishable' (<s>akṣaya</s>) — that which has no decay is <s>akṣaya</s>; because of its eternally existing nature. // GRhtCM 3.28:6 //

children.text: punarjīvaḥ ajīve prakāśatvābhāvaḥ svatvaṃ vihāya malinopādhikatvānnirupādhāv upādhisampattiriti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.28:7 //
children.translated_text: Further, 'alive' (<s>jīva</s>) — in the lifeless [mercury], there is an absence of luminosity. Having abandoned its own nature, due to the condition of impure adjuncts (<s>malina-upādhika</s>), [it becomes lifeless]; in the unconditioned state, the acquisition of adjuncts [ceases] — this is the intended meaning. // GRhtCM 3.28:7 //
As per the <s>Vedānta</s> statement: 'Beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) has that [Ātman] as its support and that as its object.' // GRhtCM 3.28:8 //

Thus, in the <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>, the commentary on the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>, composed by <s>Caturbhuja</s>, the son of <s>Maheśa</s> of the illustrious <s>Kurala</s> lineage, [who was like] the moon [rising from] the ocean [of that family], the third chapter (<s>avabodha</s>), consisting of faceless, impression, faced, inner-faced, leaf-mica, and <s>cāraṇa</s>, is complete. // GRhtCM 3.28:9 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 4.1]

children.text: kṛṣṇo raktaḥ pīto yo 'bhraḥ syāt sthūlatārakārahitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Black, red, or yellow mica (<s>abhra</s>), which is free from thick flakes —

children.text: vajrī sa pītakarmaṇi pātitasattvo ghano yojyaḥ // GRht_4.1 //
children.translated_text: the <s>vajrī</s> (diamond-type [mica]), whose essence (<s>sattva</s>) has been extracted, dense — is to be employed in gold-related procedures. // GRht 4.1 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: adhunābhrasattvacāraṇaṃ tatra pītakarmaṇi gaganavarṇabhedānāha kṛṣṇa ityādi // GRhtCM_4.1:1 //
children.translated_text: Now [dealing with] the <s>cāraṇa</s> (consumption) of mica-essence (<s>abhra-sattva</s>); regarding the color-distinctions of mica for gold-related procedures, [the author] says 'black' and so forth. // GRhtCM 4.1:1 //

children.text: kṛṣṇo ghano rakto ghanaḥ pīto ghanaśceti trividhaḥ pātitasattvaḥ pātitaṃ sattvaṃ yasyeti samāsaḥ // GRhtCM_4.1:2 //
children.translated_text: Black, dense [mica]; red, dense [mica]; yellow, dense [mica] — thus [mica is] of three kinds. '<s>Pātita-sattva</s>' — that whose essence has been extracted — [this is] a compound. // GRhtCM 4.1:2 //

children.text: evaṃvidho vajrī pītakarmaṇi suvarṇakārye yojyaḥ // GRhtCM_4.1:3 //
children.translated_text: Such a <s>vajrī</s> (diamond-type) [mica] is to be employed in gold-related procedures (<s>pīta-karman</s>), i.e., in operations involving gold. // GRhtCM 4.1:3 //

children.text: vajriṇo lakṣaṇaṃ dhmāto'pi haṭhāgnau saṃyojito 'pi yaḥ sthūlatārakārahito bhavati sthūlāśca tāstārakāśca tābhī rahitaḥ dalasamuccayarūpāḥ sthūlatārakāḥ // GRhtCM_4.1:4 //
children.translated_text: The characteristic of <s>vajrī</s> (diamond-mica): even when blown [by bellows in a furnace], even when subjected to a forced fire, that which remains free from thick flakes — thick and distinct flakes (<s>sthūla-tārakā</s>), which are aggregate-forms of [mica] sheets — [is diamond-mica]. // GRhtCM 4.1:4 //

children.text: anukto'pi śvetavarṇo ghanaḥ śvetakarmaṇi yojyaḥ granthāntarasāmyād ayam abhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_4.1:5 //
children.translated_text: Though not mentioned [in the root text], white-colored dense [mica] is to be employed in silver-related procedures, by agreement with other texts — this is the intent. // GRhtCM 4.1:5 //

children.text: yathā granthāntare raktaṃ pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ śastaṃ hemakriyāsu gaganaṃ hi // GRhtCM_4.1:6 //
children.translated_text: As in another text: 'Red, yellow, and black mica is recommended in gold operations.' // GRhtCM 4.1:6 //

children.text: tārakriyāsu śuklaṃ rasāyane sarvameva tu śreṣṭham iti // GRhtCM_4.1:7 //
children.translated_text: 'In silver operations, white [mica]; for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), all [types] are excellent.' // GRhtCM 4.1:7 //

children.text: abhre 'pi vṛttikṛdviśeṣamāha kadācid girijā devī haraṃ dṛṣṭvā manoharam // GRhtCM_4.1:8 //
children.translated_text: Regarding mica, [the author of the source text] also states a mythological account: 'Once, the mountain-born goddess (<s>Girijā Devī</s>), seeing the captivating <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), // GRhtCM 4.1:8 //

children.text: amocayat tadā vīryaṃ tajjātaṃ śvetamabhrakam // GRhtCM_4.1:9 //
children.translated_text: released her vital fluid (<s>vīrya</s>) at that time; from that was born white mica.' // GRhtCM 4.1:9 //

children.text: śvetaṃ raktaṃ tathā pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tadbhūmisaṃgamāt /
children.translated_text: 'White, red, yellow, and black — from its contact with [different] earths;

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajrābhraṃ ca caturvidham // GRhtCM_4.1:10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pināka</s>, <s>Dardura</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, and <s>Vajra</s>-mica — thus [mica is] of four kinds.' // GRhtCM 4.1:10 //
'When blown in fire, <s>Pināka</s> [mica] abundantly releases a pile of flakes;

children.text: phūtkāraṃ bhujagaḥ kuryād darduraṃ bhekaśabdavat // GRhtCM_4.1:11 //
children.translated_text: the serpent [<s>Nāga</s>-mica] makes a hissing sound; <s>Dardura</s> [mica] sounds like a frog.' // GRhtCM 4.1:11 //

children.text: caturthaṃ khecaraṃ vajraṃ naivāgnau vikṛtiṃ bhajet /
children.translated_text: 'The fourth, the sky-moving <s>Vajra</s> [mica], does not undergo any change in fire;

children.text: tasmād vajrābhrakaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vyādhivārdhakyamṛtyujit iti // GRhtCM_4.1:12 //
children.translated_text: therefore, <s>Vajra</s>-mica is the best — it conquers disease, old age, and death.' // GRhtCM 4.1:12 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 4.2]

children.text: niścandrikaṃ hi gaganaṃ vāsitamapi vāsanābhir iha śatadhā /
children.translated_text: Mica without luster (<s>niścandrika</s>), even though impregnated a hundred times with impression-herbs (<s>vāsanā</s>) here —

children.text: tadapi na carati rasendraḥ sattvaṃ kathamatra yatnataḥ prabhavet // GRht_4.2 //
children.translated_text: even so, the king of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) does not consume it; how then can the essence (<s>sattva</s>) be properly extracted? // GRht 4.2 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: cāraṇāyām abhrapattre vaiṣamyaṃ sattve ca sugamatvaṃ sūcayannāha niścandrikam ityādi // GRhtCM_4.2:1 //
children.translated_text: Indicating the difficulty with mica-sheets in the <s>cāraṇa</s> (consumption process) and the ease with the essence (<s>sattva</s>), [the author] says '<s>niścandrika</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM 4.2:1 //

children.text: ihāsmin cāraṇāsaṃskāre niścandrikaṃ gaganaṃ tārakārahitam abhraṃ vāsanābhiḥ pūrvoktābhir vāsanauṣadhibhiḥ śatadhā śataprakāraṃ vāsitaṃ mathitam api rasendraḥ pāradas tadapi bahuśramaiḥ saṃskṛtamapyabhraṃ na carati grāsīkaroti // GRhtCM_4.2:2 //
children.translated_text: In this <s>cāraṇa</s>-process, mica without luster (<s>niścandrika gagana</s>) — mica devoid of flakes — even though impregnated (<s>vāsita</s>) a hundred times with the previously stated impression-herbs (<s>vāsanā-auṣadhis</s>), i.e., ground [with them], [even then] the king of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>), i.e., mercury (<s>pārada</s>), does not consume it, does not devour even that [mica] which has been processed with much labor. // GRhtCM 4.2:2 //

children.text: atra cāraṇe sattvaṃ yatnataḥ prayatnāt kathaṃ prabhavet kathamapi samarthībhavet sattvaṃ yatnataḥ samarthībhavedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.2:3 //
children.translated_text: In this <s>cāraṇa</s> (consumption), how can the essence (<s>sattva</s>) succeed by effort? How can it possibly become effective? The essence succeeds by effort — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 4.2:3 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 4.3]
Except for mica-essence (<s>abhra-sattva</s>) alone, no other [substance] is capable of clipping the wings (<s>pakṣa</s>) [of mercury];

children.text: tena niruddhaprasaro niyamyate badhyate ca sukham // GRht_4.3 //
children.translated_text: by it, [mercury] whose spread is restrained is controlled and easily bound. // GRht 4.3 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Praising the essence (<s>sattva</s>) for its ease and superior qualities, [the author] says 'except' and so forth. // GRhtCM 4.3:1 //

children.text: abhrasattvamekaṃ muktvā tyaktvā anyo 'paro rasapakṣāpakartanasamartho na pāradapakṣacchettā na tena sattvena sukhaṃ yathā syāttathā rasaḥ pārado niyamyate pāradasya niyamanaṃ bhavedityarthaḥ badhyate ca bandhanaṃ prāpyate raso baddho bhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.3:2 //
children.translated_text: Except for (<s>muktvā</s>) mica-essence alone, no other [substance] is capable of clipping the wings of mercury, i.e., cutting the wings of mercury (<s>pārada</s>). By that essence, the mercury is controlled — the control of mercury occurs — this is the meaning. And it is bound — binding is attained, i.e., the mercury becomes bound. Comfortably, i.e., in such a way that it becomes easy. // GRhtCM 4.3:2 //

children.text: kimbhūtaḥ san niyamanaṃ bandhanaṃ ca pnoti niruddhaprasaraḥ san niruddha ārundhittaḥ prasaraḥ prasaraṇaṃ prakṛṣṭena gamanaṃ yasya tādṛśaḥ san // GRhtCM_4.3:3 //
children.translated_text: In what condition does it attain control and binding? 'Whose spread is restrained' — that whose spread, i.e., extensive movement, is restrained, i.e., blocked — being in such a condition. // GRhtCM 4.3:3 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 4.4]
<Wing-clipping (<s>pakṣaccheda</s>)>
He who attempts to bind mercury without performing the wing-clipping (<s>pakṣaccheda</s>) —

children.text: bījaireva hi sa jaḍo vāñchatyajitendriyo mokṣam // GRht_4.4 //
children.translated_text: that fool, [trying merely] with seed-metals (<s>bījas</s>), is like an uncontrolled-sensed man desiring liberation. // GRht 4.4 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing the qualification for mercury-binding, [the author] says 'wing-clipping' and so forth. // GRhtCM 4.4:1 //

children.text: yo vādī abhrasattvagrasanena vinā pakṣacchedam kṛtvā pakṣāpakartanamavidhāya rasabandhaṃ kartuṃ pāradabandhanaṃ vidhātum īhate ceṣṭate sa vādī na kiṃtu jaḍa evam apaṇḍita iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_4.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Whatever practitioner (<s>vādī</s>), without performing the wing-clipping by means of consuming mica-essence (<s>abhra-sattva</s>), i.e., without accomplishing the wing-removal, attempts to perform the binding of mercury — that practitioner is not [wise] but rather foolish, i.e., a dullard — this is the purport. // GRhtCM 4.4:2 //

children.text: kaḥ kṛtvā rasabandhanaṃ kartumīhate bījaiḥ raktābhrahemarasakair ityādibhiḥ // GRhtCM_4.4:3 //
children.translated_text: Who attempts to perform the binding of mercury? With seed-metals (<s>bījas</s>) — red mica-essence, gold, silver (?), etc. // GRhtCM 4.4:3 //
'<s>Eva</s>' is an indeclinable that excludes other substances. // GRhtCM 4.4:4 //

children.text: pakṣacchedanaṃ kṛtvā bandhanaṃ kāryamayaṃ vidhiḥ anyathā tv avidhiḥ // GRhtCM_4.4:5 //
children.translated_text: Having performed the wing-clipping, binding is to be done — this is the rule; otherwise, it is a violation of the rule. // GRhtCM 4.4:5 //

children.text: avidher dṛṣṭāntamāha yathā ajitendriyo lampaṭaḥ pumān mokṣaṃ vāñchati // GRhtCM_4.4:6 //
children.translated_text: He gives an analogy for the violation: just as an uncontrolled-sensed, libertine man desires liberation. // GRhtCM 4.4:6 //
The uncontrolled-sensed and the foolish are equivalent. // GRhtCM 4.4:7 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 4.5]

children.text: nādhaḥ patati na cordhvaṃ tiṣṭhati yantre bhaved anudgārī /
children.translated_text: [Mercury that] does not fall downward, nor remains above in the apparatus, and produces no eructation —

children.text: abhrakajīrṇaḥ sūtaḥ pakṣacchinnaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ // GRht_4.5 //
children.translated_text: mercury that has digested mica (<s>abhrakajīrṇa</s>) — that is to be known as wing-clipped (<s>pakṣacchinna</s>). // GRht 4.5 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the characteristic of wing-clipped mercury, beginning with 'not' and so forth. // GRhtCM 4.5:1 //

children.text: evaṃvidhaḥ pāradaḥ sūto yaḥ sa pakṣacchinnaḥ pakṣau chinnau cheditau yasyeti samāsaḥ // GRhtCM_4.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Such mercury (<s>pārada</s>/<s>sūta</s>) which is wing-clipped — 'whose wings are clipped, cut' — [this is] a compound. // GRhtCM 4.5:2 //

children.text: sa kaḥ yo nādhaḥ patati adhaḥpātane kṛte ūrdhvato 'dhobhāgo na patati punaradhobhāgata ūrdhvapātane kṛte ūrdhvaṃ na yāti anudgārī acañcalo bhavet yantre svastha eva tiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.5:3 //
children.translated_text: What [mercury] is that? That which 'does not fall downward' — when downward distillation is performed, it does not fall from the upper to the lower part; and from the lower part, when upward distillation is performed, it does not go upward. 'Producing no eructation' (<s>anudgārī</s>) — it becomes motionless; it simply remains stable in the apparatus — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 4.5:3 //

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ abhrajīrṇaḥ abhrakaṃ jīrṇaṃ niḥśeṣatām āptaṃ yasmin rasa iti samāsaḥ // GRhtCM_4.5:4 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what quality? '<s>Abhrajīrṇa</s>' — that in which mica has been completely digested, i.e., reduced to nothing — [this is] a compound regarding mercury. // GRhtCM 4.5:4 //

children.text: grāsamātreṇa pakṣacchedo na jāyate yāvanna cāritamabhrakaṃ jaratīti dhvanyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.5:5 //
children.translated_text: By mere consumption (<s>grāsa</s>) alone, wing-clipping does not occur; only when the mica that has been consumed becomes fully digested — this is the implied meaning. // GRhtCM 4.5:5 //
That is wing-clipped mercury. // GRhtCM 4.5:6 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 4.6]
<Mica — Subtypes>
White and the other four colors [of mica] have been described — those free from thick flakes;
<Mica — Subtypes — Reaction to heating>

children.text: vajrī satvaṃ muñcatyapare dhmātāśca kācatāṃ yānti // GRht_4.6 //
children.translated_text: the <s>vajrī</s> (diamond-type) releases its essence; the others, when blown [by bellows], turn to glass. // GRht 4.6 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: vajrābhraṃ vihāya pinākanāgabhekāḥ satvamocane'samarthā iti darśayannāha śvetetyādi // GRhtCM_4.6:1 //
children.translated_text: Showing that except for <s>vajra</s>-mica, the <s>pināka</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>bheka</s> [types] are incapable of releasing essence, [the author] says 'white' and so forth. // GRhtCM 4.6:1 //

children.text: ye dhmātāḥ sthūlatārakārahitāḥ pattracayena varjitā raktapītakṛṣṇāḥ kathitāḥ pūrvaṃ varṇitāste śvetādicaturvarṇā bhavanti // GRhtCM_4.6:2 //
children.translated_text: Those which, when blown [by bellows], are free from thick flakes, i.e., devoid of layers of sheets — the red, yellow, and black [varieties] previously described — these are the four-colored [types], beginning with white. // GRhtCM 4.6:2 //

children.text: trayāṇāṃ raktapītakṛṣṇavarṇābhrāṇāṃ cet śvetavarṇa ādau yujyate tadā caturvarṇā bhavantītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.6:3 //
children.translated_text: If white is added first to the three — red, yellow, and black colored micas — then they become four-colored — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 4.6:3 //

children.text: teṣāṃ caturvarṇānāṃ madhye yo vajrī vajrasaṃjñako ghanaḥ sa satvaṃ muñcati dhmātaḥ san satvaṃ tyajati nānye // GRhtCM_4.6:4 //
children.translated_text: Among those four-colored [micas], the one named <s>vajrī</s> (diamond-mica), when blown [by bellows], releases its essence — it yields its essence; the others do not. // GRhtCM 4.6:4 //

children.text: apare pinākanāgabhekāhvayāḥ dhmātāḥ santaḥ kācatāṃ yānti kācākāratvam āpnuvanti na ca sattvanirgama iti // GRhtCM_4.6:5 //
