children.translated_text: The others — named <s>pināka</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>bheka</s> (frog) — when blown [by bellows], turn to glass, i.e., assume a glass-like form; but there is no emergence of essence. // GRhtCM 4.6:5 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 4.7]
<Mica — Subtypes — Potency>
Whatever dense [micas] of white, red, black, and yellow colors have been mentioned in the world —

children.text: alpabalā niḥsattvā vajrī śreṣṭhastu sarveṣām // GRht_4.7 //
children.translated_text: they are of little strength and devoid of essence; the <s>vajrī</s> (diamond-type) is the best of all. // GRht 4.7 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: sasattvabalavatvābhyām utkṛṣṭatvād vajrābhraṃ punaḥ praśaṃsati sitetyādi // GRhtCM_4.7:1 //
children.translated_text: Due to its possessing essence and strength, praising <s>vajra</s>-mica again for its superiority, [the author] says 'white' and so forth. // GRhtCM 4.7:1 //

children.text: loke saṃsāre ye kecit ghanā udāhṛtāḥ kathitāste alpabalāḥ alpaṃ balaṃ yeṣu te tathoktāḥ // GRhtCM_4.7:2 //
children.translated_text: In the world, whatever dense [micas] have been mentioned — those are of little strength, i.e., those in which strength is slight. // GRhtCM 4.7:2 //

children.text: niḥsattvāḥ satvavarjitāḥ dhmāteṣu teṣu satvābhāva ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.7:3 //
children.translated_text: Devoid of essence — lacking essence; when blown, there is an absence of essence in them — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 4.7:3 //

children.text: te ke ghanāḥ sitaraktāsitapītāḥ śvetaraktakṛṣṇapītavarṇāḥ nānye varṇāḥ santīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_4.7:4 //
children.translated_text: What are those dense [micas]? White, red, black, and yellow-colored — of white, red, black, and yellow colors; no other colors exist — this is the purport. // GRhtCM 4.7:4 //

children.text: sarveṣāṃ caturvarṇānāṃ madhye vajrī vajrasaṃjñakaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ pradhānaḥ // GRhtCM_4.7:5 //
children.translated_text: Among all the four-colored [micas], <s>vajrī</s>, the one named <s>vajra</s> (diamond), is the best, the chief. // GRhtCM 4.7:5 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 4.8]
<Mica — Inedible variants>

children.text: sūte'pi rasāyanināṃ yojyaṃ parikīrtitaṃ paraṃ satvam /
children.translated_text: Even in [the processing of] mercury, for practitioners of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), the supreme essence (<s>sattva</s>) has been proclaimed to be employed.

children.text: trividhaṃ gaganamabhakṣyaṃ kācaṃ kiṭṭaṃ ca pattrarajaḥ // GRht_4.8 //
children.translated_text: Threefold mica is inedible: glass-form (<s>kāca</s>), slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), and leaf-dust (<s>pattraraja</s>). // GRht 4.8 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the mica to be given [to mercury], beginning with 'even in mercury' and so forth. // GRhtCM 4.8:1 //

children.text: rasāyanināṃ rasāyanaṃ jarāvyādhividhvaṃsibheṣajaṃ vidyate yeṣāṃ yeṣu vā te rasāyaninaḥ teṣāṃ paraṃ pradhānaṃ satvamabhrasatvaṃ parikīrtitaṃ saṃkathitaṃ yathā granthāntare /
children.translated_text: For the practitioners of <s>rasāyana</s> — those who possess <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy), which is the medicine that destroys old age and disease, or those in whom it is [present] — the supreme, i.e., the chief, essence (<s>sattva</s>), meaning mica-essence (<s>abhra-sattva</s>), has been proclaimed. As in another text:
'The wise one who has properly purified [it] and who consumes [mica-] essence obtains the arresting of aging.'
Thus. // GRhtCM 4.8:2 //

children.text: abhrasatvaṃ sūte'pi pārade'pi paramamutkṛṣṭaṃ pakṣacchedanasamarthaṃ baladaṃ ca // GRhtCM_4.8:3 //
children.translated_text: Mica-essence is supreme even in [the treatment of] mercury — the most excellent, capable of wing-clipping, and strength-giving. // GRhtCM 4.8:3 //

children.text: punastrividhaṃ gaganam abhakṣyam abhojyaṃ rasāyanināṃ sūte'pi // GRhtCM_4.8:4 //
children.translated_text: Further, threefold mica is inedible, not to be consumed — [not] by practitioners of <s>rasāyana</s> nor by mercury. // GRhtCM 4.8:4 //

children.text: kiṃ tattrividham ekaṃ kācaṃ vahnau dhamanātkācākāratāṃ nītaṃ dvitīyaṃ kiṭṭaṃ yaddhamanātkiṭṭasvarūpaṃ prāptaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pattrarajaḥ patrāṇāṃ samāhitaṃ yadrajas tadevaṃ trividham abhakṣyaṃ sadoṣatvāt // GRhtCM_4.8:5 //
children.translated_text: What is that threefold [inedible mica]? The first is glass-form (<s>kāca</s>) — that which has been reduced to a glass-like state by blowing in fire. The second is slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) — that which has attained the form of slag through blowing. The third is leaf-dust (<s>pattraraja</s>) — the dust that has accumulated from the sheets. Thus, these three [forms of] mica are inedible, because they are defective. // GRhtCM 4.8:5 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 4.9]
<Mica — Essence (<s>sattva</s>)>

children.text: muñcati satvaṃ dhmātas tṛṇasāravikārakair ghanaḥ svinnaḥ /
children.translated_text: Dense [mica], when blown [by bellows], steamed with <s>tṛṇasāra</s> (bamboo) and its modifications, releases its essence.

children.text: parihṛtya kācakiṭṭaṃ grāhyaṃ sāraṃ prayatnena // GRht_4.9 //
children.translated_text: Having discarded the glass and dross (<s>kācakiṭṭa</s>), the essence (<s>sāra</s>) should be carefully collected.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Demonstrating the procedure for <s>sattva-pātana</s> (extraction of essence), he says, beginning with '<s>muñcati</s>' (releases) etc.

children.text: ghanas tṛṇasāravikārakaiḥ svinnaḥ tṛṇameva sāro yeṣāṃ te tṛṇasārāḥ teṣāṃ ye vikārakā viśeṣās tair auṣadhaiḥ sūryāvartakādibhiḥ kṛtvā svinnau vahnau dhmāto ghanaḥ satvaṃ muñcati sattvapātaṃ vidadhāti // GRhtCM_4.9:2 //
children.translated_text: The mica (<s>ghana</s>), sweated with the products of grass-essence plants — 'grass-essences' (<s>tṛṇasāra</s>) are those whose essential [part] is the grass; their 'products' (<s>vikāraka</s>) are the special [preparations]; with these herbs such as <s>sūryāvartaka</s> and others, having been sweated and then smelted in fire — the mica releases its essence (<s>sattva</s>), i.e., it performs the <s>sattva-pātana</s> (essence-extraction).

children.text: punaḥ kācaṃ kiṭṭaṃ ca parihṛtya sattvaṃ patitakācakiṭṭayuktaṃ yadā bhavati tadā prayatnena grāhyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.9:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, having discarded the glass (<s>kāca</s>) and dross (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) — when the fallen [essence] is mixed with glass and dross, then it should be carefully collected — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 4.10
<s>Abhraka</s> (mica) :: <s>sattva</s> (essence) :: <s>pātana</s> (extraction)>
[The mica] should be sweated, [then] having formed a ball (<s>piṇḍa</s>), with buffalo curd, milk, urine, dung, and ghee,

children.text: atha paṃcagavyayuktaḥ satvaṃ pātayati lohanibham // GRht_4.10 //
children.translated_text: then, combined with the five products of the cow (<s>pañcagavya</s>), it yields an essence (<s>sattva</s>) resembling metal (<s>lohanibha</s>).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states a different specific method, beginning with '<s>svedya</s>' (should be sweated) etc.

children.text: svedyo ghanaḥ pūrvoktaistṛṇasāravikāraiḥ sveditamabhraṃ svedavidhiruktaḥ punarghanasya piṇḍaṃ baddhvā kaiḥ saha māhiṣadadhidugdhamūtraśakṛdājyaiḥ kṛtvā mahiṣyā idaṃ māhiṣaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ yaddadhi dugdhaṃ mūtraṃ śakṛdviṣṭhā ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ caitaiḥ piṇḍaṃ baddhvā // GRhtCM_4.10:1 //
children.translated_text: The mica (<s>ghana</s>) should be sweated — mica sweated by the aforementioned grass-essence products; the sweating procedure has been stated. Then, having formed a ball of the mica — with what? With buffalo curd, milk, urine, dung, and ghee — that is, what belongs to the she-buffalo is '<s>māhiṣa</s>'; such curd, milk, urine, dung (<s>śakṛt</s> = feces), and ghee (<s>ājya</s> = clarified butter) — having formed a ball with these.
'<s>Atha</s>' [is used] in the sense of addition.

children.text: pañcagavyaiḥ gavāṃ dugdhadadhimūtraśakṛdājyaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ kāryaḥ piṇḍaṃ baddhvetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.10:3 //
children.translated_text: Combined with the five [products] of the cow (<s>pañcagavya</s>) — the milk, curd, urine, dung, and ghee of cows — the ball should be made — this is the meaning.

children.text: etatpiṇḍaṃ lohanibhaṃ muṇḍaprabhaṃ sattvaṃ pātayati pūrvasaṃbadhāt ghanasya ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_4.10:4 //
children.translated_text: This ball yields an essence resembling metal (<s>lohanibha</s>) — having a sheen like metal (<s>muṇḍa</s>) — it extracts the essence; by contextual connection, [this is the essence] of the mica — this is the implied supplement.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 4.11
<s>Sattva</s> (essence) :: extraction from cool minerals>
Minerals whose juices have been drunk by the heat of the sun release a small amount of essence (<s>sattva</s>);

children.text: svasthānasthāḥ santo muñcanti ta eva bhūyiṣṭham // GRht_4.11 //
children.translated_text: [but] those same [minerals], remaining in their own place [i.e., moist], release it abundantly.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: sūryātapapītarasā iti sūryātape savitṛgharme pītāḥ śoṣitā rasā dravā yaiḥ evaṃvidhā dhātavo dhmātāḥ santaḥ svalpaṃ īṣanmātraṃ sattvaṃ muñcanti tyajanti // GRhtCM_4.11:1 //
children.translated_text: 'Whose juices have been drunk by the sun's heat' — [that is], in the heat of the sun, [minerals whose] juices (<s>rasa</s>, fluids) have been drunk, i.e., dried up; such minerals, when smelted (<s>dhmāta</s>), release only a small, slight amount of essence (<s>sattva</s>).

children.text: punasta eva sūryātapapītarasā dhātavaḥ svasthānasthāḥ svakīyaṃ yatsthānaṃ draveṇa sthānapiṇḍaṃ rūpaṃ tasmin tiṣṭhantīti evaṃvidhāḥ santo bahalaṃ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ satvaṃ muñcanti dravantītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.11:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, those same minerals whose juices have been drunk by the sun's heat, [when they are] 'remaining in their own place' — their own station being the liquid state, remaining in a ball-form within the liquid — such [minerals], being substantial, release abundant, plentiful essence — that is, they flow [it out] — this is the meaning.

children.text: sūryātapapītarasā iti keṣāṃ sūryāvartakadalīvandhyākarkoṭakyādīnāṃ drāvakauṣadhīnām // GRhtCM_4.11:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Whose juices have been drunk by the sun's heat' — of which [herbs]? Of the dissolving herbs (<s>drāvakauṣadhī</s>) such as <s>sūryāvartaka</s>, <s>kadalī</s> (plantain), <s>vandhyākarkoṭakī</s>, and the like.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 4.12
Smelted long and deep, the cloud [of mica] rains down with streams of golden [essence];

children.text: devamukhatulyamamalaṃ patitaṃ satvaṃ tathā vindyāt // GRht_4.12 //
children.translated_text: the essence that has fallen, pure like the face of fire (<s>devamukha</s>), should be thus collected.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the characteristics of the extracted essence, beginning with '<s>bahugambhīram</s>' (long and deep) etc.

children.text: megho ghano bahugambhīraṃ yathā syāttathā dhmātaḥ san suvarṇadhārābhiḥ śobhanavarṇadhārābhiḥ vā suvarṇavat kanakavat varṇo yāsāṃ tābhiḥ nirmalatvāt prakāśakatvācca varṣati dhārāpātaṃ vidadhāti // GRhtCM_4.12:2 //
children.translated_text: The cloud (<s>megha</s>, i.e., mica), smelted so as to be [heated] long and deep, rains — that is, produces a shower of streams — with streams of golden color, or of beautiful color, [shining] like gold — because of [its] purity and luminosity.

children.text: kathaṃbhūtaṃ devamukhatulyaṃ vahninā tulyaṃ samaṃ amalaṃ nirmalaṃ haritapītaraktādidhūmarahitatvāt patitaṃ satvaṃ tathā vindyāt ghanasyetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.12:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? 'Like the face of fire (<s>devamukha</s>)' — equal to fire, similar [to it]; 'pure' (<s>amala</s>) — spotless, because of the absence of green, yellow, red, and other smoke-[colored impurities]; the essence that has thus fallen should be collected — of the mica — this is the meaning.
Similarly, in another text:
'With the fierce fire of bellows, in a blazing furnace,
when [the fire] is intensely burning, the coals become spent.
Then another [batch of fuel] — if not [added] on top, two or three times, the intelligent [practitioner should know] —

children.text: yadā dīpto bhavedvahniḥ śuddhajvālo mahābalaḥ // GRhtCM_4.12:5 //
children.translated_text: when the fire becomes intensely bright, with pure flames and great power,

children.text: patitaṃ tu tadā vindyāt tatsattvaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: then one should collect the fallen [essence]; there is no doubt in this.
The fallen [essence] should be separated, free from dross and charcoal.

children.text: nirguṇaṃ lakṣayitvā tu punar dhāmyo yathāvatā /
children.translated_text: Having observed [that it is] without qualities [i.e., impurities], one should again smelt it properly;

children.text: dvistrirevamaśeṣaṃ tu dhmātaḥ sattvaṃ vimuñcati // GRhtCM_4.12:7 //
children.translated_text: two or three times thus — [when] completely [smelted], [the mica] releases [its] essence.'
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 4.13-14
<s>Abhraka</s> (mica) :: <s>sattva</s> (essence) :: consumption [by mercury] without a '<s>mukha</s>' (face)>

children.text: yadi lohanibhaṃ patitaṃ jātaṃ gaganasya tadrasaścarati /
children.translated_text: If the essence of mica (<s>gagana</s>) has fallen resembling metal (<s>lohanibha</s>), mercury consumes it;

children.text: milati ca sarvadvandve hyauṣadhibhiścarati vināpi mukhaiḥ // GRht_4.13 //
children.translated_text: it combines in all [metal-]pairs, and with herbs it consumes even without a 'face' (<s>mukha</s>).
<s>Abhraka</s> (mica) :: <s>sattva</s> (essence) :: produces a '<s>mukha</s>' (face)>

children.text: mākṣikasahitaṃ gaganaṃ dhmātaṃ satvaṃ mukhapradaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Mica combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites), when smelted, produces a 'face'-giving (<s>mukhaprada</s>) essence;

children.text: tadanu ca nāgairvaṅgaiḥ sahitaṃ ca mukhapradaṃ satvam // GRht_4.14 //
children.translated_text: then also, combined with lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), the essence becomes 'face'-giving.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: mākṣikasatvāntarasaṃyogāt sattvasya guṇādhikyaṃ darśayannāha mākṣiketyādi // GRhtCM_4.13-14:1 //
children.translated_text: Demonstrating the superior quality of the essence through combination with the essence of <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites), he says, beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>' etc.

children.text: gagane bhavaṃ gaganaṃ aṇpratyayāntaṃ ṇito vā iti sūtreṇa na vṛddhiḥ gaganaṃ abhrasatvam // GRhtCM_4.13-14:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Gagana</s>' — born in <s>gagana</s> (sky/mica); by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>aṇ-pratyayānta</s>' or '<s>ṇito vā</s>', there is no <s>vṛddhi</s> [vowel strengthening]; '<s>gagana</s>' means mica-essence.

children.text: mākṣike bhavaṃ mākṣikaṃ mākṣikasatvaṃ tena sahitaṃ pūrvasatvaṃ cet dhmātaṃ tadubhayasatvaṃ mukhapradaṃ bhavati rasasya iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_4.13-14:3 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Mākṣika</s>' — born in <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites), i.e., the essence of copper pyrites; combined with that, the previous essence [of mica], when smelted, that combined essence of both becomes 'face'-giving (<s>mukhaprada</s>) — of mercury, this is the completion.
'<s>Mukha</s>' — 'gives [it] eminently' — this is the compound.

children.text: tadanu ca tatpaścācca nāgair vaṅgaiḥ sahitaṃ pūrvaṃ yadgaganaṃ abhrasatvaṃ mukhapradamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.13-14:5 //
children.translated_text: Then, after that, combined with lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), the previous mica-essence — that is, the mica-<s>sattva</s> — becomes face-giving — this is the meaning.

children.text: vā sukhapradaṃ iti pāṭhaḥ asmin yoge bahukleśaṃ vihāya sukhena cāraṇaṃ bhavatīti vikalpārthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.13-14:6 //
children.translated_text: Or, the reading '<s>sukhaprada</s>' (pleasure-giving) [is possible]; in this procedure, having avoided much difficulty, the <s>cāraṇa</s> (consumption) occurs easily — this is the alternative meaning.

children.text: <abhra:: sattva:: induction of garbhadruti, rañjana and bandhana>
children.translated_text: <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) :: <s>sattva</s> (essence) :: induction of <s>garbhadruti</s> (embryo-fusion), <s>rañjana</s> (coloring) and <s>bandhana</s> (binding)>
Through the combination with <s>mākṣika</s>-essence, mercury consumes all of the mica-essence (<s>ghanasattva</s>);

children.text: niyataṃ garbhadrāvī sa rajyate badhyate caivam // GRht_4.15 //
children.translated_text: it certainly becomes a <s>garbhadrāvī</s> (embryo-fuser), and thus it is colored (<s>rajyate</s>) and bound (<s>badhyate</s>).
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 4.15
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states <s>mākṣika</s>-essence as the primary [agent], beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>' etc.

children.text: sūtakaḥ pārado ghanasatvaṃ abhrasatvaṃ nikhilaṃ samastaṃ carati // GRhtCM_4.15:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury (<s>sūtaka</s>, i.e., <s>pārada</s>) consumes all, the entirety of the mica-essence (<s>ghanasattva</s>, i.e., <s>abhrasattva</s>).

children.text: kasmāt mākṣikasatve yogāt mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ tatsatve yo yogastasmāt // GRhtCM_4.15:3 //
children.translated_text: From what? From the combination with the essence of <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites) — '<s>mākṣika</s>' means gold-<s>mākṣika</s> (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>); from the combination with its essence — therefore.
'<s>Niyata</s>' means 'certainly.'

children.text: mākṣikasattvayogād ghanasattvaṃ carati raso garbhadrāvī garbhe drāvayati sattvaṃ dravarūpaṃ vidhatte yaḥ sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_4.15:5 //
children.translated_text: Through the combination with <s>mākṣika</s>-essence, [mercury] consumes the mica-essence and becomes a '<s>garbhadrāvī</s>' — one that melts [substances] in [its] womb (<s>garbha</s>), that renders the essence into a liquid form — [mercury] that is thus described.
In the belly of mercury, the essences of <s>mākṣika</s> and mica remain in a molten form — this is the meaning.

children.text: evamamunā vidhānena saha sūtakaḥ pārado rajyate rāgavān bhavati badhyate baddhaśca bhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.15:7 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this procedure, mercury (<s>pārada</s>) is colored (<s>rajyate</s>) — becomes endowed with color (<s>rāga</s>) — and is bound (<s>badhyate</s>) — becomes fixed (<s>baddha</s>) — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 4.16
<s>Abhraka</s> (mica) :: <s>sattva</s> (essence) :: for <s>bandhana</s> (binding) of mercury>

children.text: satvaṃ ghanasya kāntaṃ tālakayuktaṃ surundhitaṃ dhmātam /
children.translated_text: The essence of mica together with <s>kānta</s> (loadstone/magnetic iron), combined with <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), well-sealed and smelted,

children.text: vāraistribhiriha satvaṃ bhavati rasendrabandhakāri param // GRht_4.16 //
children.translated_text: in three rounds becomes an essence that effects the supreme binding of the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
After the <s>mākṣika</s>-procedure, another [method] is stated, beginning with '<s>sattva</s>' (essence) etc.

children.text: ghanasyābhrasya satvaṃ tathā kāntaṃ lohaviśeṣaṃ tālakayuktaṃ tālakena haritālena yuktaṃ surundhitaṃ dhmātaṃ sat trayamapi satvarūpaṃ bhavati yadaikavāradhamanena satvaṃ na milati tathā punardvistrivelābhir dhamanaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_4.16:2 //
children.translated_text: The essence of mica (<s>abhraka</s>), and <s>kānta</s> (a specific type of metal), combined with <s>tālaka</s> — that is, with orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>) — well-sealed and smelted, all three become of the nature of essence. If the essence does not combine by one round of smelting, then smelting should be done again two or three times.

children.text: samabhāgatālakayojanaṃ ghanasatvamākṣikasatvayogadrāvaṇāddhamitādatyarthaṃ tatsatvaṃ rakhe pārade bandhakāri bhavati paramamutkṛṣṭaṃ bandhanapradaṃ bhavati // GRhtCM_4.16:3 //
children.translated_text: The equal-proportion combination of orpiment, through the melting of mica-essence and <s>mākṣika</s>-essence — being smelted from that very combination — that essence, in mercury, becomes binding-effecting — that is, supremely excellent, bestowing fixation.

children.text: tatsattvasya cāraṇato raso bandhanamavāpnotīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_4.16:4 //
children.translated_text: Through the <s>cāraṇa</s> (consumption) of that essence, mercury attains fixation (<s>bandhana</s>) — this is the import.
The characteristics of <s>kānta</s> (loadstone/magnetic iron):

children.text: pātre yasmin praviśati jale tailabindurna sarpet hiṅgurgandhaṃ visṛjati nijaṃ tiktatāṃ nimbakalkaḥ /
children.translated_text: [That] in whatever vessel a drop of oil, when placed in water, does not spread; [where] asafoetida (<s>hiṅgu</s>) releases its own fragrance; [where] neem paste [exhibits] bitterness;

children.text: pāke dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākāratāṃ naiva bhūmau kāntaṃ lohaṃ viduriti ca tallakṣaṇoktaṃ na cānyat /
children.translated_text: [where] milk when heated forms peaks and does not [settle flat] on the surface — that metal is known as '<s>kānta</s>' (magnetic iron); its characteristics have been thus stated, and no other.
Thus.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 4.17
<s>Abhraka</s> (mica) :: <s>sattva</s> (essence) :: induction of <s>garbhadruti</s> (embryo-fusion)>
Metal (<s>loha</s>) and mica-essence, rendered into one body with an equal portion of orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), [mercury] consumes;
through the procedure of pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>), pressed with the finger, it melts in the womb (<s>garbha</s>).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for combining <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron), mica-essence, and orpiment, beginning with '<s>loha</s>' (metal) etc.
'<s>Ca</s>' [is used] in the sense of addition.

children.text: lohaṃ pūrvoktalakṣaṇaṃ muṇḍādikaṃ abhrasatvaṃ ca tālakasamabhāgasāritaṃ tālakasya samabhāgena pūrvavidhānena mukhādinā yatsāritaṃ ekaśarīratāṃ nītaṃ sṛ gatāvityasya dhāto rūpaṃ sāritaṃ pramilitam ityarthaḥ evaṃvidhaṃ kāntābhrasatvālaṃ rasaścarati // GRhtCM_4.17:3 //
children.translated_text: Metal — of the previously stated characteristics, such as <s>muṇḍa</s> (wrought iron) etc. — and mica-essence, 'rendered with an equal portion of orpiment' — rendered into one body by the previously described procedure of 'face' and the like, with an equal portion of orpiment; '<s>sārita</s>' — from the root <s>sṛ</s> meaning 'to go' — means brought into unified form, combined — this is the meaning. Such <s>kānta</s>-mica-essence-orpiment, mercury consumes.

children.text: ca punaḥ aṅgulimṛditaṃ aṅgulinā marditaṃ tat kāntābhrasatvālaṃ garbhe rasodare dravati tatsvarūpatvena milati // GRhtCM_4.17:4 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, 'pressed with the finger' — ground with the finger — that <s>kānta</s>-mica-essence-orpiment melts in the womb (<s>garbha</s>, i.e., the belly of mercury) — merges with its very nature.

children.text: kasmāt abhiṣavayogāt abhiṣavaḥ saṃmardanaṃ tadyogāt // GRhtCM_4.17:5 //
children.translated_text: From what? From the procedure of pressing (<s>abhiṣava-yoga</s>); '<s>abhiṣava</s>' means grinding/pressing — from that procedure.

children.text: lohasya trayo daśabhedānāṃ madhyāt kenāpi bhedena sahayogaḥ kārya iti lohaśabdena dhvanitam // GRhtCM_4.17:6 //
children.translated_text: Among the thirty varieties of metal, the combination should be made with any one variety — this is implied by the word '<s>loha</s>' (metal).
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 4.18
<s>Abhraka</s> (mica) :: <s>sattva</s> (essence) :: induction of <s>cāraṇa</s> (consumption)>
Tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), and then mica-essence, rendered [into one body] with a sixth portion of orpiment — [mercury] consumes;

children.text: abhiṣavayogāccarati vrajati raso nātra sandehaḥ // GRht_4.18 //
children.translated_text: through the pressing procedure (<s>abhiṣava</s>), mercury consumes [it] — proceeds — there is no doubt here.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Having stated the metal-procedure, he states the tin-procedure, beginning with '<s>vaṅga</s>' (tin) etc.

children.text: atha lohakathanānantaraṃ vaṅgaṃ khurasaṃjñakaṃ abhrakaṃ ca etaddvayaṃ tālakaṣaḍbhāgasāritaṃ tālakasya ṣaḍaṃśena ekaśarīratāṃ nītaṃ tatsvarūpaṃ rasaścarati // GRhtCM_4.18:2 //
children.translated_text: Then, after the statement about metal, tin — known by the name '<s>khura</s>' — and mica, this pair, 'rendered with a sixth portion of orpiment' — rendered into one body with a sixth part of orpiment — mercury consumes its very form.

children.text: kasmāt abhiṣavayogāt abhiṣavaḥ saṃmardanaṃ tadyogāt ṣuñ abhiṣave ityasya dhāto rūpaṃ abhiṣavaḥ // GRhtCM_4.18:3 //
children.translated_text: From what? From the pressing procedure (<s>abhiṣava-yoga</s>); '<s>abhiṣava</s>' means pressing/grinding — from that procedure; from the root '<s>ṣuñ abhiṣave</s>' (to press/extract), the form is '<s>abhiṣava</s>.'
Furthermore, mercury consumes — merges [with it].

children.text: cāritaṃ yat taddravati taddrutaṃ rase vrajati pṛthaktvāt saṃ milati nātrasandehaḥ niḥ saṃdigdhamiva // GRhtCM_4.18:5 //
children.translated_text: What has been consumed (<s>cārita</s>) melts, and that melted [substance] enters into the mercury, departing from separateness — it merges. 'There is no doubt here' — it is beyond doubt.

children.text: vaṅgasya laghudravitvāt ṣaḍaṃśayogastālakasya yuktaḥ lohajāteḥ kāṭhiṇyāt samabhāgatvaṃ uditam // GRhtCM_4.18:6 //
children.translated_text: Due to the lightness and fusibility of tin, a sixth-part proportion of orpiment is appropriate; due to the hardness of the iron-type [metals], equal proportion was stated.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 4.19-20
<s>Abhraka</s> (mica) :: <s>sattva</s> (essence) :: induction of <s>cāraṇa</s> (consumption)>

children.text: bahalaṃ suvarṇavarṇaṃ niculapuṭaiḥ patati pañcabhiḥ satvam /
children.translated_text: Dense, of golden color, with five <s>nicula</s>-leaf crucibles (<s>puṭa</s>), the essence falls;
[when mica is] made into pellets, killed (<s>mṛta</s>), [the essence is] stainless (<s>nirañjana</s>), free from dross.
Having powdered that, then, the mica (<s>ghana</s>), treated (<s>bhāvita</s>) many times with alkalines and sours,
ground with the three types of <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (emissions), water, <s>tumburu</s>, and [other] juices, [mercury] consumes it.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for mica-essence, beginning with '<s>bahala</s>' (dense) etc.

children.text: vaṭakīkṛtaṃ ca tanmṛtaṃ ca gaganaṃ tathoktaṃ na vaṭako vaṭakaḥ kriyata iti vaṭakīkṛtaṃ atra abhūtatadbhāve cviḥpratyayaḥ // GRhtCM_4.19-20:2 //
children.translated_text: Made into a pellet (<s>vaṭakīkṛta</s>) and calcined (<s>mṛta</s>) — that <s>gagana</s> (mica) is thus described. Not [merely] a pellet, but 'made into a pellet' — here the <s>cvi</s> suffix is in the sense of 'becoming what it was not before.' // GRhtCM_4.19-20:2 //

children.text: pañcabhirniculapuṭaiḥ pañcasaṃkhyābhirvetasavṛkṣadravabhāvanābhir bhāvitaṃ yanmṛtagaganaṃ mṛtābhraṃ vaṭakīkṛtaṃ satsatvaṃ patati taddrāvakauṣadhayogaṃ vidhāya vahninā vidhamanāditi śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_4.19-20:3 //
children.translated_text: With five <s>nicula</s> (castor-oil plant) calcinations, i.e., saturated with five rounds of <s>vetasa</s> (cane) tree-juice treatment — that calcined <s>gagana</s>, i.e., dead mica (<s>mṛtābhra</s>), made into pellets, being an essence-bearing substance (<s>sattva</s>), yields [when] the flux-herb preparation (<s>drāvaka-oṣadhi-yoga</s>) is applied and blown with fire — this is the remainder. // GRhtCM_4.19-20:3 //

children.text: kiyanmānaṃ satvaṃ patati bahalaṃ bahu anyavidheradhikam // GRhtCM_4.19-20:4 //
children.translated_text: How much essence falls out? Abundantly (<s>bahala</s>), i.e., copiously, more than by other methods. // GRhtCM_4.19-20:4 //

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ svarṇavarṇaṃ pītaśvetaṃ prakāśākhyaṃ punarnirañjanaṃ nirmalaṃ kiṭṭarahitaṃ ca // GRhtCM_4.19-20:5 //
children.translated_text: Of what kind? Gold-colored (<s>svarṇa-varṇa</s>), yellowish-white, called '<s>prakāśa</s>' (lustrous); furthermore, stainless (<s>nirañjana</s>), pure (<s>nirmala</s>), and free from dross (<s>kiṭṭa-rahita</s>). // GRhtCM_4.19-20:5 //
In this essence, there is an absence of glass-like dross (<s>kāca-kiṭṭa</s>). // GRhtCM_4.19-20:6 //
This is the most excellent of all methods — the meaning is: because of the abundant essence-extraction previously described. // GRhtCM_4.19-20:7 //
He describes the procedure for transmuting the pure essence alone — 'then' and so forth. // GRhtCM_4.19-20:8 //

children.text: tatastadabhrasatvapātanavidheranantaraṃ tadevābhrasatvaṃ cūrṇīkṛtya kalkaṃ vidhāya kṣārāmlairbhāvitaṃ kuryāt kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ amlā jambīrādayaḥ tairbahuśo bahuvāraṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.19-20:9 //
children.translated_text: Then, after that procedure of extracting the mica essence, that very mica essence, having been powdered and made into a paste, should be treated with alkalis and acids. The alkalis are <s>svarjikā</s> (soda ash) and others; the acids are <s>jambīra</s> (citron) and others. With these, it should be sun-dried many times, i.e., repeatedly — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_4.19-20:9 //

children.text: punaḥ sṛṣṭitrayanīrakaṇātumbururasamarditaṃ sṛṣṭiḥ pūrvoktā tattrayaṃ mūtraśukraśoṇitamiti nīrakaṇā jalapippalī tumbaru pratītaṃ eteṣāṃ rasena marditaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_4.19-20:10 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, 'ground with <s>sṛṣṭitraya</s>, <s>nīrakaṇā</s>, and <s>tumburu</s> juice': <s>sṛṣṭi</s> is as previously described; its triad is urine, semen, and blood. <s>Nīrakaṇā</s> is <s>jalapippalī</s> (water long-pepper). <s>Tumburu</s> is well-known [by that name]. With the juice of these, grinding should be done. // GRhtCM_4.19-20:10 //

children.text: abhrasattvamevaṃ kṛtaṃ sat carati grasati rasaḥ ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_4.19-20:11 //
children.translated_text: Mica essence prepared in this manner — 'mercury transmutes [it], i.e., devours [it]' is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_4.19-20:11 //
START GRht 4.21-22
<copper-mica (<s>śulvābhra</s>): production>
Mica essence, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite), combined in equal parts, thus mixed —

children.text: tacchulbābhraṃ kathitaṃ carati raso jīryati kṣipram // GRht_4.21 //
children.translated_text: that is called copper-mica (<s>śulvābhra</s>); mercury transmutes it and assimilates it quickly. // GRht_4.21 //
Thus, <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite) combined with copper, [and] the mica essence [are] ground in a heated iron mortar;
the lord of mercury transmutes [them], with <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented rice-water), <s>vetasa</s> (cane), <s>jambīra</s> (citron), and <s>bījapūra</s> (citron) acids. // GRht_4.22 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he describes copper-mica (<s>śulvābhra</s>) — '<s>ghana</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_4.21-22:1 //

children.text: ghanasatvaśulbamākṣikasamabhāganiyojitaṃ ghanasatvam abhrasatvaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ samabhāgena tulyabhāgena niyojitaṃ prayuktaṃ tanmilitaṃ sat śulbābhraṃ kathitam // GRhtCM_4.21-22:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Mica essence, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s> combined in equal parts': <s>ghanasattva</s> is mica essence, <s>śulba</s> is copper (<s>tāmra</s>), <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇa-mākṣika</s>) — combined in equal parts, i.e., in equal portions; when mixed, it is called copper-mica (<s>śulvābhra</s>). // GRhtCM_4.21-22:2 //
Here, what kind of copper should be used? He states:
Copper is of two kinds: <s>mleccha</s> (foreign) and <s>Nepāla</s> (Nepalese). In mercury-work, <s>Nepāla</s> is superior.
It withstands hammering, is unctuous, has red leaves (sheets), is pure, and soft. // GRhtCM_4.21-22:3 //
<s>Mleccha</s> [copper], however, when washed is black, is both rough and unctuous, does not withstand hammering,
[and] is mixed with lead and iron — it is not the best for mercury-work.
Therefore, <s>Nepāla</s> (Nepalese) [copper] should be selected — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_4.21-22:4 //

children.text: tacchulvābhraṃ rasaḥ kṣipraṃ carati punaḥ kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ tacchulbaṃ jīryati jāraṇamāpnoti // GRhtCM_4.21-22:5 //
children.translated_text: That copper-mica (<s>śulvābhra</s>) — mercury transmutes it quickly; furthermore, quickly, i.e., rapidly, that copper undergoes assimilation (<s>jāraṇā</s>), i.e., reaches the state of being assimilated. // GRhtCM_4.21-22:5 //

children.text: atra mākṣikayogaḥ śulbābhrasatvamelanārthaṃ rasaprītyeti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_4.21-22:6 //
children.translated_text: Here, the addition of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) is for the purpose of uniting the copper and mica essence, and for the delight of the mercury — this is the purport. // GRhtCM_4.21-22:6 //
He describes the procedure for copper-mica transmutation — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_4.21-22:7 //

children.text: iti pūrvoktaṃ tāpyaśulbasahitaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ nepālasaṃjñakaṃ tābhyāṃ sahitaṃ miśritaṃ ghanasatvaṃ taptalohakhalvake mṛditaṃ kāryaṃ mardanīyaṃ kaiḥ kṛtvā kāñjikavetasajambīrabījapūrāmlaiḥ kāñjikamuktavidhānaṃ sauvīraṃ vetasaṃ cukraṃ jambīraṃ prasiddhaṃ bījapūro mātuluṅgaḥ eteṣāmamlaiḥ dravarūpaiḥ // GRhtCM_4.21-22:8 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus,' i.e., as previously described, combined with <s>tāpya</s> and copper: <s>tāpya</s> is gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇa-mākṣika</s>), <s>śulba</s> is copper (<s>tāmra</s>), specifically the one called <s>Nepāla</s> — combined with these two, i.e., mixed, the mica essence should be ground in a heated iron mortar. With what? With <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented rice-water) — its preparation has been previously described — <s>vetasa</s> is <s>cukra</s> (tamarind), <s>jambīra</s> (citron) is well-known, <s>bījapūra</s> is <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron) — with the acid liquids of these. // GRhtCM_4.21-22:8 //

children.text: tataḥ śulvābhraṃ rasendraḥ pāradaścarati grasati // GRhtCM_4.21-22:9 //
children.translated_text: Then, the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>), i.e., <s>pārada</s>, transmutes, i.e., devours, the copper-mica. // GRhtCM_4.21-22:9 //

children.text: lohakhalvasya kathanāt taptakhalvake mardanaṃ kuryāditi tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.21-22:10 //
children.translated_text: Since the iron mortar is mentioned, the purport is that grinding should be done in a heated mortar. // GRhtCM_4.21-22:10 //
START GRht 4.23
<ash (of different metals): coloring (<s>rañjana</s>)>

children.text: iti tīkṣṇaśulbanāgaṃ mākṣikayuktaṃ ca tatkṛtaṃ khoṭam /
children.translated_text: Thus, iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), copper, and lead, combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) — the alloy (<s>khoṭa</s>) made from these,

children.text: tadbhasma ca puṭavidhinā nirvyūḍhaṃ satvarañjakaṃ bhavati // GRht_4.23 //
children.translated_text: its ash (<s>bhasma</s>), produced by the calcination method, when carried through the essence, becomes a coloring agent (<s>sattva-rañjaka</s>). // GRht_4.23 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_4.23:1 //

children.text: iti pūrvoktalakṣaṇaṃ tīkṣṇaśulbanāgaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tāmraṃ nāgaṃ ca etattrayaṃ mākṣikayuktaṃ svarṇamākṣikayutaṃ samaṃ tulyabhāgaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_4.23:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus,' i.e., of the aforementioned character — iron, copper, and lead, these three, combined with <s>mākṣika</s>, i.e., with gold-pyrite, should be made equal in parts. // GRhtCM_4.23:2 //

children.text: tatkṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ taiḥ sarvaiḥ piṣṭīstambhena khoṭabhasma kāryam // GRhtCM_4.23:3 //
children.translated_text: The alloy (<s>khoṭa</s>) made from these: from all of them, by the <s>piṣṭī-stambha</s> method (pellet-solidification), an alloy-ash should be prepared. // GRhtCM_4.23:3 //

children.text: puṭavidhinā vahnipuṭavidhānena tatkṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ bhasma kāryaṃ punaḥ tadbhasma satve nirvyūḍhaṃ nirvāhitaṃ sat satvarañjakaṃ bhavati khasatve abhrasatve rāgadāyi bhavati rañjitaṃ tatsatvaṃ rasarañjakaṃ bhavediti // GRhtCM_4.23:4 //
children.translated_text: By the calcination method, i.e., by the fire-calcination procedure, the alloy made from those should be reduced to ash. Furthermore, that ash, when carried through the essence, i.e., conveyed into it, becomes an essence-coloring agent (<s>sattva-rañjaka</s>), i.e., it becomes a color-giver to the mica essence — the colored essence then becomes a coloring agent for mercury. // GRhtCM_4.23:4 //
START GRht 4.24

children.text: cāryaṃ yatnena rase ghanasatvaṃ tadvidhaṃ ghanaṃ tasya /
children.translated_text: The mica essence of that kind, [and] the plain mica [substance] — combining these with all seeds,
one should carefully transmute [them] in mercury, through the mixing of pairs. // GRht_4.24 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He describes the transmutation of the colored mica essence — 'should be transmuted' and so forth. // GRhtCM_4.24:1 //

children.text: tadvidhaṃ pūrvarañjitaṃ ghanasatvam abhrasatvaṃ ca ghanaṃ kevalaghanodbhavaṃ satvaṃ arañjitaṃ rase pārade cāryaṃ grāsagrasanamānenaitad abhrasatvaṃ rase saṃyojyam // GRhtCM_4.24:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Of that kind' means the previously colored mica essence (<s>ghanasattva</s>), i.e., mica essence; and '<s>ghana</s>' means the essence derived solely from plain mica, i.e., uncolored — these should be transmuted in <s>rasa</s> (mercury), meaning made to be devoured by it. This mica essence should be combined with the mercury. // GRhtCM_4.24:2 //

children.text: vā satve sarvabījaṃ sarvaṃ rāgadāyi dravyaṃ saṃyojya nirvāhyaṃ nirvāhitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_4.24:3 //
children.translated_text: Or, in the essence, all seeds, i.e., all coloring substances, should be combined and carried through, i.e., made to be processed. // GRhtCM_4.24:3 //

children.text: kutaḥ dvandvasaṃkarataḥ dvandvānāṃ saṃkaro melāpaḥ saṅkaro'vakara ityamaraḥ // GRhtCM_4.24:4 //
children.translated_text: How? 'Through the mixing of pairs' — the mixing (<s>saṃkara</s>) of pairs (<s>dvandvas</s>); '<s>saṃkara</s>' means blending — '<s>saṅkaro'vakara</s>' says the <s>Amarakośa</s>. // GRhtCM_4.24:4 //

children.text: nirvāhyaṃ iti vaha prāpaṇe ityasya rūpaṃ pūrvavat // GRhtCM_4.24:5 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Nirvāhya</s>' (to be carried through) — from the root '<s>vaha</s>' meaning 'to convey' — its form as before. // GRhtCM_4.24:5 //
The prefix '<s>nir</s>' is in the sense of certainty — '<s>nir</s>' is used in the senses of certainty and prohibition — says the <s>Amarakośa</s>. // GRhtCM_4.24:6 //
START GRht 4.25
The transmutation of mica at the beginning, the <s>garbha-druti</s> (internal liquefaction) transmutation, and gold at the end —

children.text: yo jānāti na vādī vṛthaiva so'rthakṣayaṃ kurute // GRht_4.25 //
children.translated_text: an alchemist who does not know [these] merely wastes his wealth in vain. // GRht_4.25 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states what must be known in mercury transmutation — '<s>abhraka</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_4.25:1 //

children.text: yo vādī rasakartā ādau prathamaṃ abhracāraṇaṃ na jānāti yathā raso'bhrakaṃ carati grasati punaḥ tatpaścāt garbhadruticāraṇaṃ yadrasagarbhe drutaṃ dravarūpaṃ tiṣṭhatyabhrādikaṃ tasya cāraṇaṃ grasanaṃ punarante hemnaḥ svarṇasya cāraṇaṃ grasanaṃ na jānāti sa vṛthaiva mithyaiva arthakṣayaṃ dhananāśaṃ kurute kāryasiddherabhāvāt // GRhtCM_4.25:2 //
children.translated_text: An alchemist (<s>vādī</s>), i.e., a practitioner of mercury-work, who does not know, first of all, the transmutation of mica — how mercury transmutes, i.e., devours, mica; then after that, the <s>garbha-druti</s> transmutation — whereby that which has been dissolved into liquid form within the womb (interior) of mercury, the mica and other [substances], remains [there]; its transmutation, i.e., devouring; then, at the end, the transmutation, i.e., devouring, of gold (<s>heman</s>) — he who does not know [all these] merely wastes his wealth, i.e., causes the destruction of money, in vain, because the work cannot be accomplished. // GRhtCM_4.25:2 //

children.text: sarvajña eva rasakriyāyāṃ pravarteteti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_4.25:3 //
children.translated_text: Only an omniscient [practitioner] should engage in mercury-work — this is the purport. // GRhtCM_4.25:3 //
START GRht 4.26

children.text: <abhra:: sattva:: grāsa:: only abhra part is "eaten">
children.translated_text: <mica essence: <s>grāsa</s> (devouring): only the mica part is 'eaten'>
I shall declare one secret of <s>gagana-grāsa</s> (mica-devouring) — through the conjunction of mica essence and copper:
mercury devours with effort only the mica essence, not the entire [substance]. // GRht_4.26 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the secret of devouring — '<s>gagana</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_4.26:1 //

children.text: ahaṃ śrīmadgovindabhagavatpūjyapādācāryaḥ ekamadvitīyaṃ gaganagrāsarahasyaṃ abhrakakavalane grāsakautukaṃ vakṣyāmi kathayāmi // GRhtCM_4.26:2 //
children.translated_text: I, the revered <s>Śrīmad Govindabhagavatpūjyapāda Ācārya</s>, shall declare, shall explain, one unparalleled secret of <s>gagana-grāsa</s> (mica-devouring), the wonder of mica consumption. // GRhtCM_4.26:2 //

children.text: kasmāt ghanārkasaṃyogāt ghanaṃ abhrakasatvaṃ arkastāmraṃ etayoḥ saṃyogaḥ tasmāt ubhayasatvakṛtakhoṭaṃ cāryam // GRhtCM_4.26:3 //
children.translated_text: From what [conjunction]? From the conjunction of <s>ghana</s> and <s>arka</s>: <s>ghana</s> is mica essence, <s>arka</s> is copper — their conjunction; from that, the alloy made from both essences should be transmuted. // GRhtCM_4.26:3 //
The word 'now' (<s>atha</s>) indicates an alternative view. // GRhtCM_4.26:4 //

children.text: abhrasatvasya yasya dhāto rūpaṃ tena saha yasya dhātorvā saṃyogo bhavati dvandvabhāvāt saṅkarataḥ tatsaṃyuktamabhidhānaṃ bhavati yathā śulvābhraṃ nāgābhraṃ vaṅgābhraṃ mākṣikābhraṃ hemābhram iti evaṃ sarvatra saṃyogānnāmaniṣpattiḥ // GRhtCM_4.26:5 //
children.translated_text: The mica essence — whichever metal's form it takes, together with whichever metal it is conjoined — through the pair-nature, through the mixing, the combined designation comes about: such as copper-mica (<s>śulvābhra</s>), lead-mica (<s>nāgābhra</s>), tin-mica (<s>vaṅgābhra</s>), pyrite-mica (<s>mākṣikābhra</s>), gold-mica (<s>hemābhra</s>), and so forth. Thus, in all cases, the name arises from the conjunction. // GRhtCM_4.26:5 //

children.text: grastasya drāvaṇaṃ garbhe garbhadrutirudāhṛtā bahireva dravīkṛtya ghanasatvādikaṃ khalu /
children.translated_text: The liquefaction of that which has been devoured, within the womb [of mercury], is called <s>garbha-druti</s> (internal liquefaction). Having liquefied externally the mica essence and other substances indeed,
that [process] of assimilation (<s>jāraṇā</s>) for the lord of mercury is called <s>bāhya-druti</s> (external liquefaction). // GRhtCM_4.26:6 //
START GRht 5.1

children.text: yadi ghanasatvaṃ garbhe na patati no vā dravanti bījāni /
children.translated_text: If the mica essence does not fall into the womb [of mercury], or if the seeds do not liquefy,

children.text: na ca bāhyadrutiyogastatkathamiha badhyate sūtaḥ // GRht_5.1 //
children.translated_text: and there is no conjunction with external liquefaction — then how is <s>sūta</s> (mercury) bound here? // GRht_5.1 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Delight the moon-lotus (<s>janakaīrava</s>) with speech-rays heated by [eloquence],
and also [delight] the water-lilies (<s>kumudāni</s>) with the ever-lasting splendor rising from the pool of <s>kāsāra</s>. // GRhtCM_5.1:1 //
Now he praises <s>garbha-druti</s> (internal liquefaction) and <s>bāhya-druti</s> (external liquefaction) — 'if' and so forth. // GRhtCM_5.1:2 //

children.text: yadi ced ghanasatvam abhrasatvaṃ garbhe pāradasyāntarna patati dravatvaṃ nāpnoti vā bījāni śulbābhrādīni pāradasyodare no dravanti na rasarūpā bhavanti ca punaḥ bāhyadrutir na yujyate cedevaṃ na syāttarhi iha asyāṃ kriyāyāṃ prāptāyāṃ satyāṃ sūto rasaḥ kathaṃ badhyate anyathā na ko'pyupāyaḥ // GRhtCM_5.1:3 //
children.translated_text: If the mica essence (<s>ghanasattva</s>) does not fall into the womb, i.e., the interior of <s>pārada</s> (mercury), does not attain liquidity; or if the seeds — copper-mica and so forth — do not liquefy within the belly of mercury, do not become mercury-like; and furthermore, if external liquefaction is not applicable — if this is so, then in this procedure, when it has been reached, how is <s>sūta</s> (mercury) bound? There is no other means. // GRhtCM_5.1:3 //
START GRht 5.2
Even when devouring has been accomplished, without <s>garbha-druti</s> (internal liquefaction), it does not attain oneness;

children.text: ekībhāvena vinā na jīryate tena sā kāryā // GRht_5.2 //
children.translated_text: without becoming one, it is not assimilated — therefore that [<s>garbha-druti</s>] must be performed. // GRht_5.2 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing the superiority of <s>garbha-druti</s>, he says '<s>garbha</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_5.2:1 //

children.text: cīrṇo 'pi grāsaḥ cāraṇatāṃ prāpto 'pi kavalaḥ yadi garbhadrutyā rahito bhavet rasasyodare rasarūpakaraṇavarjito bhavet tadā ekatāṃ na yāti rasarūpo na bhavati // GRhtCM_5.2:2 //
children.translated_text: Even when devouring (<s>grāsa</s>) has been accomplished, i.e., even when [the substance] has reached the state of having been consumed (<s>cāraṇā</s>), if it is devoid of <s>garbha-druti</s> (internal liquefaction), i.e., devoid of the process of making it mercury-like within the belly of mercury — then it does not attain oneness, i.e., it does not become mercury-like. // GRhtCM_5.2:2 //

children.text: punarekībhāvena vinā grāso na jīryate jāraṇatvaṃ nāpnoti // GRhtCM_5.2:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, without achieving oneness, the devoured substance is not assimilated (<s>jīryate</s>), i.e., does not reach the state of assimilation (<s>jāraṇatva</s>). // GRhtCM_5.2:3 //

children.text: tena hetunā garbhadrutipūrvikā jāraṇā kāryā rasabandhe jāraṇaṃ heturiti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_5.2:4 //
children.translated_text: For that reason, <s>jāraṇā</s> (assimilation) preceded by <s>garbha-druti</s> must be performed — because <s>jāraṇā</s> is the cause of mercury-binding (<s>rasa-bandha</s>) — this is the purport. // GRhtCM_5.2:4 //
START GRht 5.3

children.text: bījānāṃ saṃskāraḥ kartavyaḥ ko'pi tādṛśaḥ prathamam /
children.translated_text: Some such special treatment of the seeds must first be performed,
by which they liquefy within the womb of the <s>Rasarāja</s> (King of Mercury) — with the acid group. // GRht_5.3 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states what must be done first for <s>jāraṇā</s> (assimilation) — 'of the seeds' and so forth. // GRhtCM_5.3:1 //

children.text: bījānāṃ śulbābhrādīnāṃ ko'pyanirvacanīyaḥ saṃskāro garbhe drutikārakaḥ prathamaṃ kartavyaḥ saṃskriyata iti saṃskāraḥ // GRhtCM_5.3:2 //
children.translated_text: Of the seeds — copper-mica and other substances — some indescribable preparation, one that produces liquefaction within the womb, must be performed first. '<s>Saṃskāra</s>' (preparation) means 'that by which [something] is refined.' // GRhtCM_5.3:2 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ tādṛśaḥ taiḥ bījaiḥ sadṛśaḥ yathā bījāni śaktimanti santi tathā saṃskāro 'pi śaktimān kartavya ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.3:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? 'Such,' i.e., befitting those seeds — just as the seeds are potent, so too the preparation must be potent — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_5.3:3 //

children.text: saṃskāraḥ kena kartavyaḥ amlavargeṇa jambīrādinā // GRhtCM_5.3:4 //
children.translated_text: By what should the preparation be done? By the acid group, i.e., with <s>jambīra</s> (citron) and others. // GRhtCM_5.3:4 //

children.text: yena saṃskāreṇa rasarājasya garbhe rasodare bījāni dhātūpadhātujātāni śulbābhrādīni dravantītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.3:5 //
children.translated_text: By which preparation, within the womb of the <s>Rasarāja</s>, i.e., within the belly of mercury, the seeds — the metals and subsidiary metals, such as copper-mica and others — liquefy — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_5.3:5 //
START GRht 5.4
<seed suitable for <s>garbha-druti</s> (1)>
Gold combined with equal <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) in the alloying [process], conjoined with equal <s>mākṣika</s> essence —

children.text: garbhe dravati ca jarati ca jaritaṃ badhnāti nānyathā sūtam // GRht_5.4 //
children.translated_text: it liquefies within the womb and is assimilated; [only] the assimilated [gold] binds <s>sūta</s> (mercury), not otherwise. // GRht_5.4 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He praises the gold seed — 'equal' and so forth. // GRhtCM_5.4:1 //

children.text: samamākṣikakṛtavāpaṃ samabhāgaṃ tulyāṃśaṃ hemnā yanmākṣikaṃ tasya kṛtvā vāpo vāraṃ vāram ākṣepo 'gniyogād yasmin tathoktaṃ punastaddhema samamākṣikasatvasaṃyutaṃ hemnā samaṃ tulyaṃ yanmākṣikasatvaṃ tena saṃyutaṃ kṛtakhoṭaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Having made the quenching (<s>vāpa</s>) with equal [portions of] pyrite — an equal share, i.e., equal portion of pyrite with gold — quenching it, i.e., repeatedly projecting [the pyrite] by conjunction with fire — that gold, endowed with equal pyrite-essence combined with gold, equal, i.e., the same amount of pyrite-essence as [gold] combined with it — one should make a fused alloy (<s>khoṭa</s>). || GRhtCM 5.4:2 ||
That gold in the form of a fused alloy melts (<s>dravati</s>) inside the womb (<s>garbha</s>), i.e., within the mercury. || GRhtCM 5.4:3 ||

children.text: punastaddrāvitaṃ hema jarati jīrṇatām āpnoti // GRhtCM_5.4:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that melted gold is digested (<s>jarati</s>), i.e., attains the state of being digested. || GRhtCM 5.4:4 ||

children.text: taddhema jaritaṃ sat sūtaṃ raseśvaraṃ badhnāti // GRhtCM_5.4:5 //
children.translated_text: That gold, having been digested, binds the mercury (<s>sūta</s>), the lord of mercury. || GRhtCM 5.4:5 ||

children.text: anyathā anyaprakāreṇa sūto bandhanaṃ nāpnoti // GRhtCM_5.4:6 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, by any other method, mercury does not attain binding. || GRhtCM 5.4:6 ||

children.text: mākṣikasya vāpo hemno varṇotkarṣaprada iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_5.4:7 //
children.translated_text: The quenching of pyrite enhances the color (<s>varṇa</s>) of gold — such is the purport. || GRhtCM 5.4:7 ||
START GRht 5.5
<s>tārāriṣṭa</s> (silver-auspiciousness)>
The essence of pyrite (<s>mākṣika-satva</s>), digested with gold in quarter portions and so forth, melted in mercury,
produces <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> (auspicious silver), making excellent gold by leaf-coating. || GRht 5.5 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the excellence of quality in mercury from the <s>cāraṇa</s> (ingestion) of pyrite-essence, saying 'pyrite-essence' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.5:1 ||

children.text: mākṣikasatvaṃ vahnyauṣadhayogadrutaṃ yaddhemamākṣikasāraṃ hemnā kanakena saha sūte pārade pūrvaṃ yadgutaṃ punaḥ pādādikajāritaṃ pādādikavibhāgena pādārdhasatvena niḥśeṣatāmāptaṃ sat ayaṃ sūtaḥ tārāriṣṭaṃ tāraṃ rūpyādi ariṣṭaṃ śubhaṃ varakanakaṃ kurute pūrṇavarṇamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.5:2 //
children.translated_text: The pyrite-essence — the core of gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>) melted through the conjunction of fire and medicinal substances — together with gold, first dissolved in mercury (<s>pārada</s>), then digested in quarter-portions and so forth, i.e., brought to completion by fractions of quarter, half, and full essence — this mercury produces <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>, i.e., makes silver and such auspicious, producing excellent gold (<s>varakanaka</s>), meaning gold of full color — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 5.5:2 ||

children.text: kena vidhānena pattralepanena patraṃ kaṇṭakabhedi tatra yo'sau lepaḥ vahniyogāditi śeṣaḥ tena // GRhtCM_5.5:3 //
children.translated_text: By what method? By leaf-coating (<s>pattralepa</s>) — a leaf (<s>patra</s>) that pierces [like] a thorn, upon which the coating is applied — through the conjunction of fire — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 5.5:3 ||

children.text: hemamākṣikasatvajāritasya rūpyapatralepena kanakaṃ syāditi vyaktārthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.5:4 //
children.translated_text: The clear meaning is: by coating silver-leaf with [mercury] that has digested gold-pyrite-essence, gold is produced. || GRhtCM 5.5:4 ||
START GRht 5.6
<s>garbhadruti</s> (womb-melting): test for it>
If [the swallowed substance] has attained the same consistency as mercury, passes through cloth, and is heavier on the balance,

children.text: grāso drutaḥ sa garbhe drutvāsau jīryate kṣipram // GRht_5.6 //
children.translated_text: that swallowed substance (<s>grāsa</s>) has melted in the womb (<s>garbha</s>); having melted, it is digested rapidly. || GRht 5.6 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the characteristic of <s>garbha-druti</s> (womb-melting), saying 'the same' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.6:1 ||

children.text: yadi grāsaḥ samarasatāṃ yāto bhavedrasatulyarūpatāṃ prāpto bhavet punarvastrādgalito bhavet caturguṇaśvetavastrānniḥsṛto bhavet punastulanāyāṃ tulākarmaṇi yadādhiko'pi syāttadā garbhe pāradasyāntar druto grāso jñātavyaḥ garbhadruto raso veditavya iti vyaktārthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.6:2 //
children.translated_text: If the swallowed substance (<s>grāsa</s>) has attained the same consistency as mercury, i.e., has reached a form equal to mercury; if it furthermore passes through cloth, i.e., emerges through a fourfold white cloth; and if furthermore on the balance, i.e., in the weighing operation, it is even heavier — then the <s>grāsa</s> melted within the womb, i.e., inside the mercury, should be recognized; the mercury should be known as womb-melted — this is the clear meaning. || GRhtCM 5.6:2 ||

children.text: punarasau raso drutvā dravarūpaṃ śīghraṃ prāpto jīryati dhātūnapi vidhāneneti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that mercury, having melted, i.e., having quickly attained a liquid form, digests — even metals, by the [proper] method — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 5.6:3 ||
START GRht 5.7
<Role of <s>tāpya-satva</s> (pyrite-essence)>

children.text: na biḍairnāpi kṣārairna snehairdravati hemaṃ tāraṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Neither by <s>viḍas</s> (acid-treated substances), nor by alkalis (<s>kṣāras</s>), nor by unctuous substances (<s>snehas</s>), does gold or silver melt,

children.text: mākṣikasatvena vinā tridinaṃ nihitena raktena // GRht_5.7 //
children.translated_text: without the essence of pyrite (<s>mākṣika-satva</s>), placed for three days, with the red [group]. || GRht 5.7 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the excellence of pyrite-essence, saying 'not' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.7:1 ||

children.text: mākṣikasatvena vinā svarṇamākṣikasāram antareṇa hema kanakaṃ vā tāraṃ rūpyaṃ na dravati // GRhtCM_5.7:2 //
children.translated_text: Without pyrite-essence, i.e., without the core of gold-pyrite, gold or silver (<s>tāra</s>) does not melt. || GRhtCM 5.7:2 ||

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā viḍaiḥ kṛtvā śaṅkhacūrṇārkakṣārādikṛtapiṇḍaiḥ kṛtvā granthāntare ca /
children.translated_text: Not even by what? By <s>viḍas</s>, i.e., by boluses prepared from conch powder, <s>arka</s>-plant alkali, and the like. And in another text:
'With salts, alkalis, <s>uparasas</s> (semi-metals), and these acids, <s>viḍa</s> is considered [made];

children.text: same garbhe tu saṃsthāpyo hyanenaiva dravībhavet /
children.translated_text: placed in the womb in equal [measure], with this alone melting occurs.'
Thus. || GRhtCM 5.7:3 ||

children.text: na kevalaṃ biḍaiḥ kiṃtu kṣārairapi na kṣāraiḥ svarjikāyavakṣāraṭaṅkaṇādyaiḥ // GRhtCM_5.7:4 //
children.translated_text: Not only by <s>viḍas</s>, but not even by alkalis — alkalis such as <s>svarjikā</s> (natron), <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.7:4 ||

children.text:
na kevalaṃ kṣāraiḥ kiṃtu snehairapi na snehāni yathā /
kaṅguṇikaṃ vinādoṣākarañjaśrīphalodbhavam /
kaṭuvātārisiddhārthasomarājīvibhītajam /

children.translated_text: from linseed (<s>atasī</s>), <s>mahākālī</s>, neem (<s>nimba</s>), and sesame (<s>tila</s>) likewise;
<s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera), <s>devadālī</s>, <s>dantī</s> (Baliospermum), castor (<s>tumbara</s>), and <s>vigraha</s>;
oils produced from the fruits of <s>aṅkola</s> (Alangium), datura (<s>unmatta</s>), and marking-nut (<s>bhallāta</s>).
Thus. || GRhtCM 5.7:5 ||
Even by oils it does not melt.
But by pyrite-essence, <s>garbha-druti</s> (womb-melting) occurs. || GRhtCM 5.7:6 ||
With what specific [quality] of pyrite-essence? With the red [group] (<s>rakta</s>), i.e., with the red class [of substances]. || GRhtCM 5.7:7 ||
Placed for three days (<s>tridina</s>), i.e., placed within the red group for a period of three days. || GRhtCM 5.7:8 ||

children.text: dāḍimaṃ kiṃśukaṃ caiva bandhūkaṃ ca kusumbhakam /
children.translated_text: Pomegranate (<s>dāḍima</s>), flame-of-the-forest (<s>kiṃśuka</s>), <s>bandhūka</s> (Pentapetes phoenicea), and safflower (<s>kusumbha</s>),
with equal [portion of] madder (<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>), turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>), and the like, combined with lac (<s>lākṣā</s>) juice,
joined with red sandalwood (<s>raktacandana</s>) — this is proclaimed as the red group.
Thus. || GRhtCM 5.7:9 ||
The red group (<s>raktavarga</s>) is as follows:
START GRht 5.8-12
<mercury: <s>cāraṇa</s>, <s>garbhadruti</s>>
Salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>), soaked in the juice of <s>devī</s> (Brāhmī), and betel leaf (<s>ahipatra</s>), ground on a stone,
this, well-calcined (<s>sumṛta</s>) by three <s>puṭas</s> (ignition cycles), should be placed in an iron vessel. || GRht 5.8 ||
A saucer (<s>kaṭorikā</s>), open and wide, with a depth of half a finger-breadth, serving as the mouth-support;
upon that, another saucer should be placed, with a height of one finger-breadth. || GRht 5.9 ||
Having three holes made [in it], recommended; at a height of four finger-breadths in the openings,
iron rods (<s>lohaśalākā</s>) should be inserted, and upon those, gold leaves. || GRht 5.10 ||
Having placed [them] and fumigated, one should kindle fire beneath the apparatus;
merely from the coating of smoke, the gold leaves become black. || GRht 5.11 ||
Those [leaves], having been heated by fire and afterwards killed in the apparatus by smoke,

children.text: pācitahemavidhānāccarati rasendro dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.12 //
children.translated_text: by the method of calcined-gold processing, the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) consumes [them] and melts [them] in the womb. || GRht 5.12 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the method of the gold-digestion apparatus, saying 'salt' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:1 ||

children.text: prathamaṃ lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ devīsvarasaplutaṃ kuryāt brāhmīsvakīyarasena saṃmiśraṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.8-12:2 //
children.translated_text: First, one should make the salt — rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) — soaked in the juice of <s>devī</s>, i.e., mixed with the juice of <s>Brāhmī</s>. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:2 ||

children.text: punar brāhmīrasaplutaṃ lavaṇaṃ ca ahipatraṃ tāmbūlidalaṃ tacca dvayaṃ śilayā vitatagrāveṇa cūrṇitaṃ peṣitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.8-12:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the salt soaked in <s>Brāhmī</s> juice and the betel leaf (<s>ahipatra</s>), i.e., the leaf of the betel vine (<s>tāmbūla</s>) — both of these should be ground, i.e., pulverized, on a stone slab (<s>vitatagāvara</s>). || GRhtCM 5.8-12:3 ||
Furthermore, this should be placed in an iron vessel, i.e., an iron container. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:4 ||

children.text: etat sthāpitaṃ dravyaṃ puṭatritayāt tripuṭakaraṇādagnisaṃyogena sumṛtaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_5.8-12:5 //
children.translated_text: This placed substance becomes well-calcined (<s>sumṛta</s>) from three <s>puṭas</s>, i.e., through the application of fire in three ignition cycles. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:5 ||

children.text: tasya devīsvarasaplutasya sumṛtasaindhavasya mukhādhārā sphuṭavikaṭakaṭorikā pātrī kāryā mukhameva ādhāro yasyāḥ sā evaṃvidhā sphuṭā prakaṭā vikaṭā viparītā adhomukhetyarthaḥ sā kaṭorikā vihitā kāryā ayaḥpātrasya // GRhtCM_5.8-12:6 //
children.translated_text: Of that well-calcined rock salt soaked in <s>devī</s>-juice, the mouth-support — an open, wide saucer (<s>kaṭorikā</s>) — should be made; that whose face itself is the support — such is described; open, i.e., uncovered; wide (<s>vikaṭa</s>), i.e., inverted, meaning face-down — that saucer should be made for the iron vessel. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:6 ||

children.text: tasyāḥ kaṭorikāyā upari ūrdhvabhāge eṣā kaṭorikā ādeyā sthāpyā // GRhtCM_5.8-12:7 //
children.translated_text: Above that saucer, i.e., on the upper part, this [second] saucer should be placed, i.e., positioned. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:7 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭā aṅgulotsedhā aṅgula utsedhaḥ parimāṇaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā // GRhtCM_5.8-12:8 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? 'Of one finger-breadth height' — that whose height, i.e., dimension, is one finger-breadth — so described. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:8 ||

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭā ardhāṅgulanimnā ardhāṅgulaparimāṇanimnā madhyagā // GRhtCM_5.8-12:9 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what character? 'With a depth of half a finger-breadth' — depressed in the middle to the measure of half a finger-breadth. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:9 ||

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭā vihitachidratritayā vihitāni kṛtāni chidratritayāni yasyāṃ sā evaṃvidhā śastā ca saṃtulavihitachidratritayā // GRhtCM_5.8-12:10 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what character? 'Having three holes made' — in which three holes have been made, i.e., created — such is described; and recommended, i.e., with evenly-made three holes. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:10 ||

children.text: caturaṅgulordhvā taduparibhāge kaṭorikā caturaṅgulipramāṇonnateti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_5.8-12:11 //
children.translated_text: 'Four finger-breadths high' — the saucer above that is raised to the measure of four finger-breadths — such is the purport. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:11 ||

children.text: punaśchidreṣu triṣu śalākā yojyā lohaśalākāḥ kṣepyāḥ punastatrāpi chidreṣu hemapatrāṇi kaṇṭakavedhīni kanakapatrāṇi yojyānīti // GRhtCM_5.8-12:12 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in the three holes, rods should be inserted — iron rods should be placed; and upon those too, in the holes, gold leaves — perforated-thorn-like gold leaves should be placed. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:12 ||

children.text: evaṃvidhe pūrvaṃ nirmite yantre hemapatrāṇi sthāpya vidhūpyante // GRhtCM_5.8-12:13 //
children.translated_text: In such a previously-constructed apparatus, having placed the gold leaves, they are fumigated. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:13 ||

children.text: tato'gniṃ pradīpayet yantrādhastād yantrādhobhāge vahniṃ prajvālayet tadā tāni hemapatrāṇi kṛṣṇāni śyāmavarṇāni bhavanti // GRhtCM_5.8-12:14 //
children.translated_text: Then one should kindle fire — beneath the apparatus, in the lower portion of the apparatus, one should ignite the fire. Then those gold leaves become black, i.e., of dark color. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:14 ||

children.text: kasmāt dhūmopalepamātrāt dhūmaścāsāvupalepaśca dhūmopalepas tanmātrāt tatpramāṇāt // GRhtCM_5.8-12:15 //
children.translated_text: From what? 'Merely from the coating of smoke' — smoke and that itself is the coating — the smoke-coating; merely from that, i.e., from that measure. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:15 ||

children.text: yenauṣadhena dhūpo niruktastenauṣadhenopalepaḥ kāryaḥ patreṣviti // GRhtCM_5.8-12:16 //
children.translated_text: The medicinal substance from which the fumigation is produced — with that very substance the coating should be applied on the leaves. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:16 ||

children.text: punaḥ kiṃbhūtāni hemapatrāṇi rasendro jarati agnitāpitāni santi vahniyogāttaptāni kṛtāni // GRhtCM_5.8-12:17 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what character are the gold leaves that the lord of mercury digests? They have been heated by fire, i.e., made hot through conjunction with fire. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:17 ||
This gold-digestion has been described. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:18 ||
Thus, a cluster (<s>kulaka</s>) of five verses. || GRhtCM 5.8-12:19 ||
START GRht 5.13
<silver: <s>garbhadruti</s> (in mercury)>
By that very method, having subjected the silver leaf (<s>tārapatra</s>) to sweating (<s>saṃsvedya</s>) through the apparatus,

children.text: jāyeta kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ tattāraṃ dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.13 //
children.translated_text: it becomes black in color; that silver melts in the womb [of mercury]. || GRht 5.13 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the digestion of silver, saying 'by that' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.13:1 ||

children.text: tenaiva vidhinā pūrvapidhānena tārapatraṃ rūpyadalaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ śyāmalaprabhaṃ jāyate // GRhtCM_5.13:2 //
children.translated_text: By that very method, i.e., as previously described, the silver leaf (<s>tārapatra</s>), i.e., the silver foil, becomes black in color, i.e., of dark lustre. || GRhtCM 5.13:2 ||

children.text: kena saṃsvedya yantrayogena saṃsvedaḥ prabalāgnis tasyedaṃ sambandhi yadyantraṃ yasya yo yogastena // GRhtCM_5.13:3 //
children.translated_text: By what? By sweating (<s>saṃsvedya</s>) through the apparatus — <s>saṃsveda</s> means intense fire; the apparatus associated with that, and the conjunction thereof — by that. || GRhtCM 5.13:3 ||

children.text: tattārapatraṃ punaḥ garbhe rasodare dravati jalatvamāpnoti // GRhtCM_5.13:4 //
children.translated_text: That silver leaf then melts in the womb, i.e., in the interior of mercury — attains a liquid state. || GRhtCM 5.13:4 ||

children.text: punastasmin yantre dravati caśabdāt rasendrastatpatraṃ jarati tārakṛṣṇīti // GRhtCM_5.13:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in that apparatus it melts, and by the word 'ca' (and), the lord of mercury digests that leaf — this is called <s>tārakṛṣṇī</s> (silver-blackening). || GRhtCM 5.13:5 ||
START GRht 5.14
<gold, silver: <s>garbhadruti</s>>
Or alternatively, tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) with potent [sulphur], and lead (<s>nāga</s>) by name, through the apparatus,

children.text: hemāhvaṃ tāraṃ vā dravati ca garbhe na sandehaḥ // GRht_5.14 //
children.translated_text: [make] gold-named [substance] or silver melt in the womb — there is no doubt. || GRht 5.14 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states an alternative method, saying 'or alternatively' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.14:1 ||
'Or alternatively' is used in the sense of accumulation, due to being directed toward the same purpose. || GRhtCM 5.14:2 ||

children.text: balinā gandhena saha vaṅgaṃ yantrayogena kṛṣṇaṃ jāyeta // GRhtCM_5.14:3 //
children.translated_text: Tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), together with potent [sulphur] (<s>gandha</s>), through the apparatus, becomes black. || GRhtCM 5.14:3 ||

children.text: kevalaṃ vaṅgaṃ punarnāgābhidhānena saha nāgavidhānamapyevaṃ syāditi vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_5.14:4 //
children.translated_text: Not only tin, but furthermore the procedure with lead (<s>nāga</s>) by name should also be similar — this is the clarification. || GRhtCM 5.14:4 ||

children.text: nāgābhidhāneneti nāganāmnā ākhyāhve abhidhānaṃ ca nāmadheyaṃ ca nāma ca ityamaraḥ // GRhtCM_5.14:5 //
children.translated_text: 'By the name of <s>nāga</s>' — as the <s>Amarakośa</s> states: '<s>ākhyā</s>, <s>abhidhāna</s>, <s>nāmadheya</s>, and <s>nāma</s>' [are synonyms for 'name']. || GRhtCM 5.14:5 ||

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ vaṅgaṃ vā nāgaṃ vā hemāhvaṃ hemapatraṃ vā tāraṃ tārapatraṃ vā etatsarvaṃ balinā kṛṣṇaṃ jāyeta mṛtaṃ ca sarvaṃ garbhe rasāntare dravati nātra saṃdehaḥ asaṃdigdhamidamuktam // GRhtCM_5.14:6 //
children.translated_text: Such tin or lead, or gold-leaf (<s>hemapatra</s>) or silver-leaf (<s>tārapatra</s>) — all of this, with the potent [sulphur], becomes black, i.e., calcined, and all of it melts in the womb, i.e., inside the mercury — there is no doubt about this; this has been stated without any ambiguity. || GRhtCM 5.14:6 ||
By the word 'ca' (and), [the substance] is digested (<s>jarati</s>), i.e., attains complete [absorption]. || GRhtCM 5.14:7 ||
START GRht 5.15
<s>rasaka</s> (zinc): <s>garbhadruti</s>>
<s>Rasaka</s> (zinc ore), combined with potent [sulphur], by the previously stated method and apparatus,

children.text: pakvaṃ cūrṇaṃ yāvadbhavati bhṛśaṃ dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.15 //
children.translated_text: should be calcined until it becomes powder; [then] it melts greatly in the womb [of mercury]. || GRht 5.15 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another application, saying '<s>rasaka</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.15:1 ||

children.text: rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ balinā gandhena saha yuktaṃ sat militaṃ sat samabhāgena iti śeṣaḥ kena kṛtvā pūrvoktavidhānayogena pūrvoktaṃ yadvidhānaṃ yantrādikaṃ tasya yo'sau yogastena kṛtvā tāvadbhṛśamatyarthaṃ pakvaṃ kāryaṃ yāvadaśarīratāṃ yāti taccūrṇaṃ garbhe rasodare dravati garbhadrutirbhavati caśabdājjarati ca // GRhtCM_5.15:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s>, i.e., <s>kharpara</s> (zinc carbonate), combined with potent [sulphur] (<s>gandha</s>), i.e., mixed in equal proportion — this is the remainder. Having done what? By the previously stated method and apparatus, i.e., the conjunction of the previously stated apparatus and the like — having done this, it should be calcined (<s>pakva</s>) to such an extent that it reaches bodilessness, i.e., until that powder [forms]; [then] it melts greatly, i.e., intensely, in the womb, i.e., in the interior of mercury — <s>garbhadruti</s> (womb-melting) occurs. By the word 'ca' (and), it is also digested. || GRhtCM 5.15:2 ||
START GRht 5.16
<gold: <s>garbhadruti</s>>
Now, the sulphur-stone (<s>gandhakāśman</s>), spread out, in a hundred-fold quantity, upon the finest gold — |

children.text: sūte ca bhavati piṣṭirdravati hi garbhe na vismayaḥ kāryaḥ // GRht_5.16 //
children.translated_text: and a paste forms in mercury — it melts in the womb (<s>garbha</s>) — no wonder should be made [of this]. || GRht 5.16 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method, beginning with '<s>vyūḍha</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.16:1 ||
'Then' (<s>atha</s>) means 'thereafter.' || GRhtCM 5.16:2 ||

children.text: gandhakāśmā gandhapāṣāṇaḥ śataguṇasaṃkhyaṃ yathā syāttathā uttame hemni pūrṇavarṇe vyūḍho nirvāhyaḥ tadgandhavyūḍhaṃ hema sūte pārade piṣṭirbhavati hi niścitaṃ garbhe rasāntardravati garbhadrutir bhavatītyatravismayo // GRhtCM_5.16:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhakāśmā</s> means sulphur-stone (<s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>); in a hundredfold quantity, it is to be <s>vyūḍha</s> (driven through/infused) into the finest gold (<s>uttama hema</s>) of full color. That sulphur-infused gold, in mercury (<s>sūta</s>), forms a paste — certainly — it melts in the womb (<s>garbha</s>), that is, the interior of mercury — <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) takes place: here no wonder [is needed]. || GRhtCM 5.16:3 ||
[START GRht 5.17]
<Gold: <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal) for <s>garbhadruti</s>>
Alternatively, the excellent <s>rasa-kavara</s> (mercury residue/calx), infused a hundredfold into pure gold — a supreme <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal);

children.text: bījaṃ jarati rasendre dravati ca garbhe na sandehaḥ // GRht_5.17 //
children.translated_text: the <s>bīja</s> is assimilated by the lord of <s>rasas</s> and melts in the womb — there is no doubt. || GRht 5.17 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method, beginning with 'alternatively' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.17:1 ||

children.text: athaveti samuccaye rasakavaraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kharparikaṃ śuddhahemni pūrṇavarṇe śatanirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt śataguṇanirvāhaḥ kāryaḥ ekaguṇasvarṇe śataguṇanirvāha iti yuktaṃ evaṃ kṛte sati varabījaṃ śreṣṭhabījaṃ bhavati tadbījaṃ garbhe rasodare dravati garbhe drutirbhavati rasendre pārade śīghraṃ avilambitaṃ jarati ca niḥśeṣatām āpnoti vidhānena iti śeṣaḥ atra dravaṇe jaraṇe ca na sandehaḥ // GRhtCM_5.17:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Alternatively' [is used] in a cumulative sense. <s>Rasakavara</s> means the excellent <s>kharparika</s> (mercury residue); one should infuse it a hundredfold into pure gold of full color — meaning one part gold receives a hundredfold infusion. When this is done, it becomes a supreme <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal). That <s>bīja</s> melts in the womb (<s>garbha</s>), that is, the interior of mercury — <s>garbhadruti</s> occurs. In the lord of <s>rasas</s>, <s>pārada</s>, it is rapidly assimilated — without delay it reaches complete absorption — according to the prescribed method: this is the completion. Here there is no doubt regarding the melting and assimilation. || GRhtCM 5.17:2 ||
[START GRht 5.18]
<Gold: <s>bīja</s> for <s>garbhadruti</s>>

children.text: athavā tālakasatvaṃ śilayā vā tacca hemni nirvyūḍham /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the essence of orpiment (<s>tālaka-sattva</s>), or with realgar (<s>śilā</s>) — that, infused a hundredfold into gold,

children.text: śataguṇamatha mūṣāyāṃ jarati rasendro dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.18 //
children.translated_text: in a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>), the lord of <s>rasas</s> assimilates [it] and it melts in the womb. || GRht 5.18 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method for the same purpose, beginning with 'alternatively' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.18:1 ||

children.text: tālakasatvaṃ haritālasāraṃ śataguṇaṃ śataguṇitaṃ hemni kanake nirvyūḍhaṃ andhamūṣāyāṃ vā prakāśamūṣāyāṃ vahniyogena iti śeṣaḥ tālakasatvasya hemni nirvāhaḥ kārya iti vyaktiḥ tacca tat sattvaṃ kevalaṃ vā śilayā manaḥśilayā sārdhaṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ kāryaṃ taddhema garbhe rasodare dravati atha rasendro rasarājaḥ drutaṃ jarati vidhāneneti // GRhtCM_5.18:2 //
children.translated_text: The essence of <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), that is, the extract of <s>haritāla</s>, in a hundredfold quantity, infused into gold (<s>kanaka</s>) — in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>) or an open crucible (<s>prakāśamūṣā</s>) — by the application of fire: this is the completion. The infusion of <s>tālaka</s>-essence into gold is to be performed: this is the clear meaning. And that essence alone, or together with realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>), should be infused. That gold melts in the womb, the interior of mercury. And the lord of <s>rasas</s> rapidly assimilates it — by the prescribed method. || GRhtCM 5.18:2 ||
[START GRht 5.19-21]
<Lead and Tin: combined <s>māraṇa</s> (calcination)>
Mercury, cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), mica (<s>abhraka</s>), pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), <s>vimalā</s> (gold-pyrite), nectar-copper (<s>amṛta-śulba</s>), iron (<s>loha</s>), [and] flakes (<s>parpaṭikā</s>) —
ground with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia) and <s>arka</s> (calotropis), combined with <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and realgar (<s>śilā</s>): [this is for] lead (<s>nāga</s>). || GRht 5.19 ||
Mica, orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), conch-shell (<s>śaṅkha</s>), and mercury combined — that, calcined again and again,
mixed with tamarind alkali (<s>ciñcākṣāra</s>) — tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) reaches a lifeless state. || GRht 5.20 ||

children.text: vidhinānena ca puṭitaṃ mriyate nāgaṃ nirutthatāṃ ca gatam /
children.translated_text: And calcined by this method, lead (<s>nāga</s>) dies and reaches the state of non-revival (<s>niruttha</s>);

children.text: vaṅgaṃ ca sarvakarmasu niyujyate tadapi gatajīvam // GRht_5.21 //
children.translated_text: and tin, also rendered lifeless, is employed in all operations. || GRht 5.21 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states another method, beginning with '<s>rasa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.19-21:1 ||

children.text: rasadaradābhrakatāpyamiti rasaḥ pāradaḥ darado hiṅgulaḥ abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ vimalā rukmamākṣikaṃ mṛtaṃ yacchulbaṃ tāmraṃ loho muṇḍādiśca eteṣāṃ rasādīnāṃ rasaparpaṭīvat parpaṭikā kāryā // GRhtCM_5.19-21:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasadaradābhrakatāpya</s>: <s>rasa</s> is mercury (<s>pārada</s>); <s>darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>); <s>abhraka</s> is well-known [mica]; <s>tāpya</s> is gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>); <s>vimalā</s> is copper-pyrite (<s>rukmamākṣika</s>); the calcined copper (<s>śulba</s>) is <s>tāmra</s>; <s>loha</s> (metal) is wrought iron (<s>muṇḍa</s>) and such. Of these, beginning with mercury, a <s>parpaṭikā</s> (flake) like a mercury-flake is to be prepared. || GRhtCM 5.19-21:2 ||

children.text: tayā yutaṃ nāgaṃ punaḥ kaṅkuṣṭhaśilāyutaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ haritapītavarṇo viṣaharapāṣāṇajātiḥ śilā manohvā tābhyāṃ yutaṃ miśritaṃ yannāgaṃ sīsakaḥ snuhyarkadugdhapiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ snuhī sehuṇḍaḥ arkaḥ prasiddho viṭapī tayordugdhena piṣṭaṃ pāṃśubhūtaṃ mṛtaṃ yannāgaṃ kukkuṭapuṭavidhāneneti śeṣaḥ etadapi bījaṃ siddhaṃ garbhe dravati ca pūrvasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_5.19-21:3 //
children.translated_text: Combined with that, lead (<s>nāga</s>, i.e., <s>sīsaka</s>) is further combined with <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and realgar (<s>śilā</s>) — <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is a yellow-green colored variety of poison-neutralizing stone; <s>śilā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar); combined with these two. That lead (<s>nāga</s>) is to be ground with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia) and <s>arka</s> (calotropis) — <s>snuhī</s> is a thorny plant; <s>arka</s> is the well-known tree — ground to powder with their milks, calcined, by the method of <s>kukkuṭa-puṭa</s> (hen's-nest calcination): this is the completion. This too becomes a perfected <s>bīja</s> that melts in the womb, due to the previous connection. || GRhtCM 5.19-21:3 ||
Now he states the procedure for the tin-<s>bīja</s>, beginning with '<s>abhraka</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.19-21:4 ||

children.text: ciñcākṣāravimiśraṃ yadvaṅgaṃ amlikākṣārayuktaṃ vaṅgaṃ abhrakatālakaśaṅkharasasahitaṃ abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ tālakaṃ haritālaṃ śaṅkhaṃ kambugrīvaṃ rasaḥ pāradaḥ etaiścaturbhiḥ sahitaṃ yathā syāttathā punaḥ punaḥ vāraṃ vāraṃ nirutthaṃ yāvat tāvatpuṭitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.19-21:5 //
children.translated_text: Mixed with tamarind alkali (<s>ciñcākṣāra</s>) — tin combined with tamarind-alkali, together with mica, orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>), conch (<s>kambugrīva</s>), and mercury (<s>pārada</s>) — combined with these four, it should be calcined (<s>puṭita</s>) again and again, repeatedly, until it reaches a non-revivable state. || GRhtCM 5.19-21:5 ||

children.text: etadauṣadhasyāṃśabhāgena saha puṭanādvaṅgaṃ nirjīvatāṃ yāti pañcatvamāpnoti etadapi bījaṃ siddhaṃ garbhadrāvaṇe jāraṇārthe ca pūrvasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_5.19-21:6 //
children.translated_text: Through calcination with these medicaments in proportional parts, tin reaches lifelessness — attains the state of the five elements [dissolution]. This too becomes a perfected <s>bīja</s> for womb-melting and assimilation, due to the previous connection. || GRhtCM 5.19-21:6 ||

children.text: nāgavaṅgayor etad auṣadhaṃ kāraṇamityāha vidhinetyādi // GRhtCM_5.19-21:7 //
children.translated_text: He states that this medicine is the cause [of calcination] for both lead and tin, beginning with 'by this method' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.19-21:7 ||

children.text: anena vidhinā uktavidhānena nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ puṭitaṃ sat mriyate mṛtaṃ bhavatīti vāmunā vidhānenaiva nirutthatāṃ gataṃ aśarīratāṃ prāptaṃ vaṅgaṃ sarvakarmasu cāraṇajāraṇabhakṣaṇādikāryeṣu niyujyate rasajñairiti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.19-21:8 //
children.translated_text: By this method, by the stated procedure, lead (<s>sīsaka</s>), when calcined, dies — becomes dead. And by this very procedure, tin, having reached a non-revivable state (<s>niruttha</s>) — having attained a bodiless state — is employed in all operations: <s>cāraṇa</s>, <s>jāraṇa</s>, <s>bhakṣaṇa</s>, and other processes — by those who know mercury: this is the completion. || GRhtCM 5.19-21:8 ||

children.text: nāgavaṅgamāraṇam ekavidham evoktam atas tadbhakṣaṇādiṣu parasparaṃ guṇādhikayogyaṃ natu jāraṇādiṣu // GRhtCM_5.19-21:9 //
children.translated_text: The calcination of lead and tin has been stated as a single method; therefore, in consuming and other [operations], each is especially suited according to its superior qualities — but not so in assimilation and other [processes]. || GRhtCM 5.19-21:9 ||
[START GRht 5.22]
<Gold: <s>bīja</s> for <s>garbhadruti</s>>
