children.text: mṛtanāgaṃ mṛtavaṅgaṃ mṛtavaraśulvaṃ mṛtaṃ tathā tīkṣṇam /
children.translated_text: Calcined lead, calcined tin, calcined best copper, and calcined steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) —

children.text: ekaikaṃ hemavare śatanirvyūḍhaṃ dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.22 //
children.translated_text: each one, infused a hundredfold into the finest gold, melts in the womb. || GRht 5.22 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for the assimilation of lead, tin, copper, and steel, beginning with 'calcined lead' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.22:1 ||

children.text: mṛtanāgamiti mṛtaṃ nirjīvatāṃ gataṃ yannāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tathānena vidhānena mṛtaṃ vaṅgaṃ tathā mṛtaṃ nirutthatāṃ gataṃ varaśulbaṃ tāmraṃ tathā ca mṛtaṃ tīkṣṇam arivargeṇeti śeṣaḥ eṣāṃ madhye ekaikaṃ nāgaṃ vā vaṅgaṃ vā śulbaṃ vā tīkṣṇaṃ vā pṛthaktvena hemavare pūrṇavarṇe svarṇe śatanirvyūḍhaṃ hemnaḥ śataguṇanirvāhitaṃ kuryāt tatsiddhaṃ garbhe rasodare dravati caśabdājjarati ca // GRhtCM_5.22:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Calcined lead' — lead (<s>sīsaka</s>) that has been calcined, rendered lifeless; likewise, by this same procedure, calcined tin; likewise, calcined best copper (<s>tāmra</s>); and likewise calcined steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) — with the enemy group [of herbs]: this is the completion. Among these, each one — whether lead, or tin, or copper, or steel — separately, infused a hundredfold into the finest gold of full color — meaning subjected to a hundredfold infusion relative to the gold — that perfected [metal] melts in the womb, the interior of mercury; and by the word '<s>ca</s>,' it is also assimilated. || GRhtCM 5.22:2 ||
[START GRht 5.23]
<Gold: <s>mahābīja</s> (great seed-metal)>

children.text: samagarbhe drutikaraṇaṃ hemno vakṣyāmyahaṃ paraṃ yogam /
children.translated_text: I shall declare the supreme method for effecting liquefaction in the womb (<s>samagarbhe drutikaraṇa</s>) of gold —
the powder of <s>bhrāmaka</s> (loadstone) and grain, infused a hundredfold: [this is] the <s>mahābīja</s> (great seed-metal). || GRht 5.23 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing the power of the <s>mahābīja</s>, he says beginning with '<s>samagarbha</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.23:1 ||

children.text: ihāsmiñśāstre vidhinā śāstroktarītyā yāni bījānyuktāni tāni kartavyāni sāmānyeneti bhāvaḥ paraṃ garbhadrutyarthaṃ ayaṃ vārttikendro yogaḥ vārttāsu kuśalā vārtikāḥ śāstropadeśarahitā ityarthaḥ atra bhāvādyarthe ikpratyayaḥ teṣu vārtikeṣu indraḥ pravaro yogaḥ tathānenaiva prakāreṇa ekamataścāyaṃ śāstropadeśikānāṃ śāstropadeśarahitānāṃ ca abhimata ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.23:2 //
children.translated_text: In this treatise, by the method prescribed in the scripture, whichever <s>bījas</s> (seed-metals) have been stated — those are to be prepared: this is the general purport. This supreme method for <s>garbhadruti</s> — this is the chief among <s>vārtika</s> methods — <s>vārtikas</s> means those skilled in practical techniques, those without scriptural instruction: that is the meaning. Here, by the <s>ik</s>-suffix in the sense of 'state,' the foremost among those <s>vārtikas</s> [is indicated as] the [best] method. Likewise, by this very procedure, this [method] is agreed upon by both the scripturally instructed and those without scriptural instruction: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 5.23:2 ||
[START GRht 5.24-26]
<<s>Garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction)>
Alternatively, the fume of sulphur, or the fume of orpiment, or of realgar and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine/zinc oxide) —
having placed an inverted crucible, a very elongated one, on half a potsherd (<s>kharpara</s>) — || GRht 5.24 ||

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ lagnā piṣṭī sudṛḍhā ca yathā tathā ca kartavyā /
children.translated_text: the paste stuck firmly at the top [of the crucible], as firmly as possible, is to be made [thus];
having placed [the substance] on the back of the potsherd, one should then burn [it with] <s>Daityendra</s> (sulphur, lit. 'lord of demons'). || GRht 5.25 ||

children.text: stokaṃ stokaṃ dattvā karṣāgnau dhmāpayenmṛdā liptām /
children.translated_text: Adding little by little, one should fan [the flame] over a cowdung fire; the [crucible] coated with clay —

children.text: garbhe dravati hi bījaṃ mriyate tathādhike dāhe // GRht_5.26 //
children.translated_text: the <s>bīja</s> melts in the womb, and likewise dies under increased heat. || GRht 5.26 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for melting the <s>bīja</s> in the belly of mercury, beginning with 'alternatively' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.24-26:1 ||
'Alternatively' [is used] in a cumulative sense. || GRhtCM 5.24-26:2 ||

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ dīrghatamamūṣāyantrasya talabhāge piṣṭī rasendrabījayor nirmitā piṣṭikā ca punaḥ sudṛḍhā yathā syāttathā lagnā kartavyā // GRhtCM_5.24-26:3 //
children.translated_text: At the top — on the base-plate of the elongated crucible-apparatus — the paste made from mercury and the <s>bīja</s>, the prepared <s>piṣṭikā</s>, should be attached very firmly. || GRhtCM 5.24-26:3 ||

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā kharparasyārdhe mṛnmayapātrasya khaṇḍārdhe khaṇḍaikadeśa ityarthaḥ dīrghatamāṃ adhobhāgamukhīṃ adhobhāge mukhaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā tāṃ dattvā // GRhtCM_5.24-26:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? On half a potsherd (<s>kharpara</s>) — on one broken portion of an earthen vessel, that is the meaning — having placed an elongated [crucible] with its mouth facing downward — [a crucible] whose opening is at the bottom: so described. || GRhtCM 5.24-26:4 ||

children.text: punaḥ kiṃ kṛtvā gandhakadhūmaṃ dattvā vā stokaṃ stokaṃ alpamalpaṃ tālakadhūmaṃ dattvā vā śilāhvarasakasya śilāhvā manaḥśilā rasakaḥ kharparaḥ cakavad bhāvasamāsaḥ tasya dhūmaṃ dattvā // GRhtCM_5.24-26:5 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, having done what? Having applied the fume of sulphur, or — adding little by little, in small quantities — having applied the fume of orpiment, or the fume of realgar (<s>śilāhvā</s>, i.e., <s>manaḥśilā</s>) and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine/zinc oxide) — '<s>kharpara</s>' [used here means calamine] in a <s>bahuvṛīhi</s> compound — having applied [the substance's] fume. || GRhtCM 5.24-26:5 ||

children.text: punastatkharparaṃ adhomukhamukhāṃ ca mṛdā liptāṃ mṛdveṣṭitāṃ karīṣāgnau dhmāpayet karīṣavahnāvityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.24-26:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that potsherd with the downward-facing [crucible], coated with clay — wrapped in clay — should be fanned over a cowdung fire (<s>karīṣāgni</s>): that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 5.24-26:6 ||

children.text: evaṃ adhomukhāṃ kharparaṃ ca dattvā daityendraṃ balināmānaṃ prastāvādgandhakaṃ tadanu tatkaraṇapaścād dāhayet // GRhtCM_5.24-26:7 //
children.translated_text: Thus, having placed the downward-facing [crucible] and the potsherd, [applying] <s>Daityendra</s> (<s>balināmā</s>, i.e., sulphur, named from the context) — then, after that operation, one should burn [it]. || GRhtCM 5.24-26:7 ||

children.text: evaṃ kṛte sati rasendramilitaṃ yadbījaṃ tadgarbhe rasendrāntardravati // GRhtCM_5.24-26:8 //
children.translated_text: When this is done, the <s>bīja</s> combined with mercury melts in the womb — in the interior of mercury. || GRhtCM 5.24-26:8 ||

children.text: punarbījasahito rasendro 'dhike dāhe sati mriyata ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.24-26:9 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the lord of mercury combined with the <s>bīja</s>, under increased heat, dies: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 5.24-26:9 ||
Due to the connection of the group of three verses, [this is] a specification. || GRhtCM 5.24-26:10 ||
[START GRht 5.27]
<<s>Viḍa</s> (flux): production>
Sulphur, orpiment, and bitumen (<s>śailā</s>); <s>sauvīraka</s> (antimony/white collyrium), calamine (<s>rasaka</s>), ochre (<s>gairika</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>);
alkalis, sours, and salts — [this is] the <s>viḍa</s> (flux), [made] with equal parts of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline), and <s>vimalā</s> (gold-pyrite). || GRht 5.27 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now, for the purpose of gold-assimilation, he describes the <s>viḍa</s> (flux), beginning with '<s>gandhaka</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.27:1 ||

children.text: gandhakatālakaśailā iti gandhakaṃ pratītaṃ tālakaṃ haritālaṃ śailaḥ śilājatuḥ dvaṃdvaḥ samāsaḥ tena tathoktāḥ samabhāgāḥ kāryāḥ // GRhtCM_5.27:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhakatālakaśailāḥ</s>: <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) is well-known; <s>tālaka</s> is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>); <s>śaila</s> is bitumen (<s>śilājatu</s>): a <s>dvandva</s> compound, therefore they are so called — to be taken in equal parts. || GRhtCM 5.27:2 ||

children.text: punaḥ sauvīrakaṃ śuklāñjanaṃ rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ gairikaṃ dhātugairikaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ atraikavadbhāvasamāsaḥ tattathoktaṃ samabhāgaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_5.27:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore: <s>sauvīraka</s> is white collyrium (<s>śuklāñjana</s>); <s>rasaka</s> is calamine (<s>kharparika</s>); <s>gairika</s> is mineral ochre (<s>dhātugairika</s>); <s>darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>): here there is a <s>bahuvṛīhi</s>-like compound (<s>ekavadbhāva-samāsa</s>); accordingly, these are to be taken in equal parts. || GRhtCM 5.27:3 ||

children.text: punaḥ kṣārāmlalavaṇāni kṣārā yavakṣārādayaḥ amlaṃ jambīrādi lavaṇāni saindhavādīni etānyapi samabhāgāni // GRhtCM_5.27:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore: <s>kṣārāmlalavaṇāni</s> — <s>kṣāras</s> (alkalis) are barley-alkali (<s>yavakṣāra</s>) and such; <s>amla</s> (sour) is lemon (<s>jambīra</s>) and such; <s>lavaṇāni</s> (salts) are rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) and such — these too are in equal parts. || GRhtCM 5.27:4 ||

children.text: kaiḥ saha mākṣikavaikrāntavimalasamabhāgaiḥ saha mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ vimalaṃ rukmamākṣikaṃ etāni samabhāgāni tairbiḍa ucyate sarvaiḥ samabhāgaiḥ sumarditair biḍaḥ kārya ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.27:5 //
children.translated_text: Together with what? With <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>vimalā</s> in equal parts — <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>); <s>vaikrānta</s> is tourmaline (<s>vajrabhūmija rajas</s>); <s>vimalā</s> is copper-pyrite (<s>rukmamākṣika</s>): these in equal parts — with all [ingredients] in equal parts and well-ground, the <s>viḍa</s> (flux) is to be prepared: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 5.27:5 ||
[START GRht 5.28]
<<s>Viḍa</s>: for <s>garbhadruti</s>>
Having made a gold-paste, ground and well-wrapped with this very [<s>viḍa</s>],

children.text: tripuṭaistapte khalve mṛditā garbhe tathā dravati // GRht_5.28 //
children.translated_text: ground in a heated mortar with three rounds of calcination — thus it melts in the womb. || GRht 5.28 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: biḍayogādyathā bījaṃ garbhe dravati tathāha kṛtvetyādi // GRhtCM_5.28:1 //
children.translated_text: He states how the <s>bīja</s> melts in the womb by means of the <s>viḍa</s> preparation, beginning with 'having made' and so forth. || GRhtCM 5.28:1 ||

children.text: pūrvoktā yā piṣṭī tāmanenaivoktabiḍayogena tapte khalve taptasaṃbandhāllohamaye tripuṭaiḥ karīṣāgnyātmakair mṛditā gharṣitā sati anenaiva ca veṣṭitā kāryā // GRhtCM_5.28:2 //
children.translated_text: The previously mentioned paste — [ground] with the stated <s>viḍa</s> preparation — in a heated mortar, heated by contact [with fire], in a metal [mortar], with three rounds of cowdung-fire calcination (<s>puṭa</s>), ground — rubbed — and furthermore, wrapped with this very [<s>viḍa</s>]. || GRhtCM 5.28:2 ||

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā suvarṇapiṣṭīṃ kanakapiṣṭīṃ vā anyasyāpi dhātoḥ suvarṇapiṣṭīṃ śobhanavarṇāṃ piṣṭīṃ kṛtvā // GRhtCM_5.28:3 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having made a gold-paste — a <s>kanaka</s>-paste — or for any other metal as well, having made a paste of excellent color (<s>suvarṇapiṣṭī</s>). || GRhtCM 5.28:3 ||

children.text: khalve mṛditā satī tathā tenaiva prakāreṇa natvanyaprakāreṇa garbhe rasodare dravati salilarūpā tiṣṭhati // GRhtCM_5.28:4 //
children.translated_text: When ground in a mortar, in the same manner — not by any other method — it melts in the womb (<s>garbha</s>), i.e., in the belly of mercury, and remains in a liquid form. // GRhtCM 5.28:4 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.29]
<<s>Viḍa</s> preparations :: for <s>garbhadruti</s> (embryo-fusion)>

children.text: rakte śatanirvyūḍhaṃ netrahitaṃ bhasma vaikrāntakaṃ cātha /
children.translated_text: The <s>bhasma</s> (calcinated ash) of <s>vaikrānta</s> (a mineral), processed a hundred times in the red group, beneficial for the eyes;

children.text: vimalaṃ śatanirvyūḍhaṃ grasati samaṃ dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.29 //
children.translated_text: and <s>vimala</s> (silver-pyrites), processed a hundred times — [mercury] consumes [them] equally, and they melt in the womb (<s>garbha</s>). // GRht 5.29 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the embryo-fusion with <s>vaikrānta</s>, beginning with '<s>rakta</s>' (red) and so forth. // GRhtCM 5.29:1 //

children.text: vaikrāntabhasma vajrabhūmijaṃ rajas tadudbhavaṃ bhasma rakte raktagaṇe śatanirvyūḍhaṃ śatavāraṃ nirvāhitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.29:2 //
children.translated_text: The <s>bhasma</s> of <s>vaikrānta</s> — the dust born from the <s>vajra-bhūmi</s> (diamond-earth), the <s>bhasma</s> derived from it — should be processed a hundred times in the red group (<s>rakta-gaṇa</s>). // GRhtCM 5.29:2 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ netrahitaṃ netrahitaśabdena maṇitvaṃ darśitaṃ maṇayo netrahitā iti // GRhtCM_5.29:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? 'Beneficial for the eyes' (<s>netra-hita</s>) — by the word '<s>netra-hita</s>' (eye-beneficial), its jewel-nature (<s>maṇitva</s>) is indicated, since jewels are said to be 'beneficial for the eyes.' // GRhtCM 5.29:3 //

children.text: vimalaṃ rūpyamākṣikaṃ śvetavarṇaṃ yanmākṣikaṃ raktagaṇe śatanirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.29:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s> means silver-pyrites (<s>rūpya-mākṣika</s>), a white-colored <s>mākṣika</s>; it should be processed a hundred times in the red group. // GRhtCM 5.29:4 //

children.text: tadubhayaṃ vaikrāntaṃ vimalaṃ ca raktaśatanirvyūḍhaṃ sat raso grāsavidhānaṃ vihāya samaṃ grasati kavalayati stadgrasitaṃ garbhe rasāntardravati jarati ca iti caśabdārthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.29:5 //
children.translated_text: Both of those — <s>vaikrānta</s> and <s>vimala</s> — when processed a hundred times in the red [group], mercury, setting aside the [usual] procedure of [gradual] consumption, consumes them equally, swallows them. What is thus consumed melts in the womb, i.e., inside the mercury, and is digested — the word '<s>ca</s>' conveys this additional meaning. // GRhtCM 5.29:5 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.30]
<<s>Viḍa</s> preparations :: for <s>garbhadruti</s> :: always with hundred-fold processing>
Whatever <s>viḍa</s>-preparations (corrective salts) [exist] — alkalines, sours, salts, and kindling groups —
all of them, processed a hundred times, are declared to be producers of embryo-fusion (<s>garbhadruti</s>). // GRht 5.30 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing the superiority of the red group, [the author] says '<s>ya</s>' (whatever) and so forth. // GRhtCM 5.30:1 //

children.text: ye kecidviḍayogā atra granthāntareṣvapi ca kathitāḥ tathā kṣārāmlalavaṇāni kathitāni kṣārā yavakṣārādayaḥ atha ca vṛkṣauṣadhisamudbhavāḥ amlā jambīrādayaḥ amlavṛkṣaśākasamudbhavāśca yānyetāni kathitāni ca punarye dīptavargāḥ kathitā dīptikarā yogā abhihitāḥ te sarve biḍakṣārāmlalavaṇadīptavargāḥ śatanirvyūḍhā garbhadrutikārakāḥ garbhe rasodare drutaṃ dravarūpaṃ kurvanti dhātumaṇiratnādīnīti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.30:2 //
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>viḍa</s>-preparations are described here and in other texts, and the alkalines, sours, and salts that are described — the alkalines being barley-alkali (<s>yava-kṣāra</s>) and others, and those derived from trees and herbs; the sours being lemon (<s>jambīra</s>) and others, and those derived from sour trees and vegetables — whatever these are that have been described; and further, whatever kindling groups (<s>dīpta-vargas</s>) are described, i.e., appetite-stimulating preparations that have been mentioned — all these <s>viḍa</s>-preparations, alkalines, sours, salts, and kindling groups, when processed a hundred times, are producers of embryo-fusion; they cause the metals, jewels, gems, and the like to assume a liquid form in the womb, i.e., the belly of mercury — [the rest is] supplied. // GRhtCM 5.30:2 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.31-32]
<Proportional dose: number of processings => amount of morsel consumed>
When processed a hundred times, [mercury consumes] an equal [quantity]; when processed seventy-five times, three-quarters;
at fifty, half; a quarter at twenty-five. // GRht 5.31 //
An eighth at half of that [i.e., twelve-and-a-half]; a sixteenth at half of that [i.e., about six] processings;
at half of that, a thirty-second; a sixty-fourth at half of that [number of] processings. // GRht 5.32 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the proportional rule beginning with 'equal' etc. for preparations processed a hundred times and so forth, beginning with '<s>śata</s>' (hundred) etc. // GRhtCM 5.31-32:1 //

children.text: śatanirvyūḍha iti śatavāraṃ nirvāhite raktagaṇe iti śeṣaḥ samaṃ tulyaṃ grasati rasa iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.31-32:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Processed a hundred times' — when the red group has been processed a hundred [times] — [the rest is] supplied. [Mercury] consumes an 'equal' [amount], i.e., an equal quantity — [the subject] 'mercury' is supplied. // GRhtCM 5.31-32:2 //

children.text: punaḥ pañcasaptativyūḍhe sati pādonaṃ caturthāṃśavarjitaṃ samagraṃ grasatīti // GRhtCM_5.31-32:3 //
children.translated_text: Further, when processed seventy-five times, [it consumes] 'three-quarters' (<s>pādonam</s>), i.e., a full [amount] minus a fourth — it consumes the entirety. // GRhtCM 5.31-32:3 //

children.text: punaḥ pañcāśannirvyūḍhe sati tadardhaṃ samasyārdhamiti // GRhtCM_5.31-32:4 //
children.translated_text: Further, when processed fifty times, [it consumes] 'half' — half of the equal amount. // GRhtCM 5.31-32:4 //
Further, at twenty-five [processings], a quarter, i.e., a fourth part. // GRhtCM 5.31-32:5 //

children.text: nyūnādhike nirvyūḍhe sati nyūnādhikāṃśo jñeya iti viśeṣārthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.31-32:6 //
children.translated_text: When processed more or fewer times, the proportional share should be understood as more or less — this is the specific meaning. // GRhtCM 5.31-32:6 //
He states the progression for lesser processings, beginning with 'an eighth' etc. // GRhtCM 5.31-32:7 //

children.text: tu punastadardhe sārdhadvādaśake nirvyūḍhe sati aṣṭāṃśaṃ tadardhe ṣaḍvāranirvyūḍhe sati ṣoḍaśāṃśamiti punastasyārdhe trivāranirvyūḍhe sati dvātriṃśadaṃśaṃ tadardhanirvyūḍhe ekadvivāranirvyūḍhe sati catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśaṃ raso grasatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.31-32:8 //
children.translated_text: Further, 'at half of that' — when processed twelve-and-a-half times, an eighth; at half of that, when processed six times, a sixteenth. Further, at half of that, when processed three times, a thirty-second; and at half of that number of processings, when processed once or twice, a sixty-fourth — mercury consumes [that proportional amount] — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 5.31-32:8 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.33]
<Embryo-fusion (<s>garbhadruti</s>)>
Thus, having understood the embryo-fusion as described, with the pressing procedure (<s>abhiṣava-yoga</s>) and the sour group,

children.text: svedanavidhinā jñātvā mṛditāṃ tapte tu khalvatale // GRht_5.33 //
children.translated_text: by the method of steaming — grind it on a heated mortar surface. // GRht 5.33 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states what is to be done when embryo-fusion has occurred, beginning with 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM 5.33:1 //

children.text: ityuktavidhānena gaditāṃ kathitāṃ garbhadrutiṃ jñātvā tapte khalvatale lohamaye karīṣāgninā uṣṇatāṃ nīte mṛditāṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.33:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus' — by the stated method, having understood the embryo-fusion as described, one should grind [it] on a heated mortar surface — a metallic [mortar] brought to heat by cow-dung fire. // GRhtCM 5.33:2 //

children.text: kena abhiṣavayogena abhiṣavaḥ saṃmardanaṃ tasya yogena na kevalamanena amlavargeṇa ca jambīrādinā na kevalamanenāpi svedanavidhinā ca svedanavidhiḥ svedanasaṃskāroktatvānnātrābhihitaḥ jāraṇahetoriti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.33:3 //
children.translated_text: By what means? By the pressing procedure (<s>abhiṣava-yoga</s>) — '<s>abhiṣava</s>' means pressing/grinding; by its procedure; not by this alone, but also with the sour group — lemon and the like; and not by this alone either, but also by the steaming method; the steaming method, since it has been described in the steaming <s>saṃskāra</s> (process), is not stated here. For the purpose of digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) — [the rest is] supplied. // GRhtCM 5.33:3 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.34]

children.text: <Durchfṃhrung von saṃskāra gemĪ“ den verwendeten bījas usw.>
children.translated_text: <Performing the process according to the seed-metals used, etc.>
Having understood the strength and weakness of the seed-metals, the grinding procedure applied to the king of mercury,

children.text: svedavidhānaṃ ca puṭaṃ yantraṃ vā vihitarasakarma // GRht_5.34 //
children.translated_text: the steaming method, the firing (<s>puṭa</s>), or the apparatus — [this constitutes] the procedure performed on mercury. // GRht 5.34 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing the prerequisite equipment for grinding and steaming, [the author] says 'having understood' and so forth. // GRhtCM 5.34:1 //

children.text: bījabalābalamardanayogaṃ kṛtaṃ jñātvā bījānāṃ dhātūpadhātuyogajanitānāṃ balābale nyūnādhike yo'sau mardanayogastameva kṛtaṃ jñātvā viditvā rasarāje svedavidhānaṃ kuryāt vā puṭaṃ vahniyogaṃ kuryāt vā yantraṃ vihitarasakarma kuryāt vihitaṃ kṛtaṃ rasasya karma saṃskārarūpaṃ yatra tathoktaṃ garbhayantrādikamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.34:2 //
children.translated_text: Having understood the grinding procedure [adjusted to] the strength and weakness of the seed-metals — the strength and weakness, i.e., more or less [potency], of the seed-metals (those produced from the combination of metals and sub-metals) — having understood that very grinding procedure as performed, in [the case of] the king of mercury, one should perform the steaming method; or one should perform the firing (<s>puṭa</s>), i.e., fire-treatment; or one should perform [the process using] an apparatus — one in which the mercury-procedure has been performed, i.e., an apparatus of the <s>garbha-yantra</s> (embryo-apparatus) type — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 5.34:2 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.35]

children.text: sūtavaraṃ lakṣayate bījaṃ nopekṣatāṃ yathā yāti /
children.translated_text: One should observe the excellent mercury, [ensuring] that the seed-metal does not go to waste;
accordingly, the procedure should be performed correctly, as directed by the feet of the <s>guru</s> (preceptor). // GRht 5.35 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Because mercury-procedures are difficult to comprehend, praising the <s>guru's</s> feet, [the author] says 'mercury' and so forth. // GRhtCM 5.35:1 //

children.text: yathā yena prakāreṇa sūtavaraṃ pāradaḥ lakṣayate jñāyate karmakṛteti śeṣaḥ punaryathā bījaṃ upekṣatāṃ na yāti samyak milati tadvattenaiva prakāreṇa gurupādanirdiṣṭaṃ karma ācāryavaryadarśitaṃ pūjyaṃ saṃskārarūpaṃ vidhinā ācāryoktavidhānena kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.35:2 //
children.translated_text: In whatever manner (<s>yathā</s>) the excellent mercury (<s>sūtavara</s>) is observed — it is known [whether] the procedure has been completed — [the rest is] supplied; and further, in whatever manner the seed-metal does not go to waste, i.e., combines properly — in that very manner, the procedure directed by the <s>guru's</s> feet, i.e., shown by the best of preceptors, [which is] revered, of the nature of processing, should be performed by the method taught by the preceptor. // GRhtCM 5.35:2 //
The characteristics of a <s>guru</s> (preceptor):
'One who is expert in all the specialties of the treatises, and skilled in mercury-procedures —
one possessing such characteristics becomes a <s>guru</s> in the science of mercury.'
Thus. // GRhtCM 5.35:3 //
Thus ends the section on embryo-fusion and digestion (<s>garbhadruti-jāraṇa</s>). // GRhtCM 5.35:4 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.36]
<External melting (<s>bāhyadruti</s>)>

children.text: bāhyadrutirati vimalā sphurati hi keṣāṃcideva siddhānām /
children.translated_text: External melting (<s>bāhyadruti</s>) — most pure — shines forth for only certain <s>siddhas</s> (perfected alchemists);

children.text: tebhyaḥ samyak jñātvā kalanāḥ kāryāstathā drutayaḥ // GRht_5.36 //
children.translated_text: from them, having properly learned, the [specific] proportions and meltings should be performed. // GRht 5.36 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Praising external melting, [the author] says '<s>bāhyadruti</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM 5.36:1 //
Melting (<s>druti</s>) has been stated as twofold: embryo-fusion (<s>garbhadruti</s>) and external melting (<s>bāhyadruti</s>). // GRhtCM 5.36:2 //
Embryo-fusion was stated previously; external melting is now described. // GRhtCM 5.36:3 //
Of what quality? 'Most pure' (<s>ativimalā</s>) — exceedingly stainless. // GRhtCM 5.36:4 //

children.text: eṣā ca punaḥ keṣāṃcideva siddhānāṃ sphurati siddhā rasavidyāpāragā nityanāthādayaḥ teṣāṃ te jānantīti // GRhtCM_5.36:5 //
children.translated_text: And this furthermore shines forth only for certain <s>siddhas</s> (perfected ones) — the <s>siddhas</s> who have mastered the science of mercury, such as <s>Nityanātha</s> and others — they know it. // GRhtCM 5.36:5 //
Being difficult to obtain, external melting is rare here [in this world]. // GRhtCM 5.36:6 //

children.text: tebhyaḥ samyak jñātvā tathā tenaiva siddhodeśavidhānena drutayo bāhyadrutayaḥ // GRhtCM_5.36:7 //
children.translated_text: From those [<s>siddhas</s>], having properly learned, by the very method taught by the <s>siddhas</s>, the external meltings should [be performed]. // GRhtCM 5.36:7 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.37-38]
<Digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) of lead>

children.text: varanāgaṃ rasarājaṃ bījavaraṃ sāritaṃ tathā tritayam /
children.translated_text: The best lead (<s>varanāga</s>), the king of mercury (<s>rasarāja</s>), and the best seed-metal (<s>bījavara</s>) — these three, rendered [into one body],
together with sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), and orpiment (<s>āla</s>) — become lead-free (<s>nirnāga</s>) by lamp-wick firing. // GRht 5.37 //

children.text: baddhvā sudṛḍhe vastre poṭalikāyāṃ śikhīkṛto dīpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having tied [it] in a strong cloth, in a poultice-bundle, a lamp with a wick [is placed below];

children.text: taile magnaṃ kṛtvā nirnāgaṃ jāyate kṣipram // GRht_5.38 //
children.translated_text: having immersed [the bundle] in oil, it quickly becomes lead-free (<s>nirnāga</s>). // GRht 5.38 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the digestion of lead, beginning with '<s>varanāga</s>' (best lead) and so forth. // GRhtCM 5.37-38:1 //

children.text: varanāgaṃ śreṣṭhajāti sīsakaṃ jāraṇayogyaṃ rasarājaṃ uktasaṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaṃ pāradaṃ bījavaraṃ hemabījaṃ etattrayaṃ sāritaṃ militaṃ kāryaṃ punargandhakaśilālasahitaṃ gandhakaṃ pratītaṃ śilā manaḥśilā ālaṃ haritālaṃ dvandvastāni taiḥ sahitaṃ ca kāryaṃ etat sarvaṣaṭkaṃ dīpavartitaḥ prajvālitadīpavartiyogāt nirnāgaṃ nāgavarjitaṃ bhavati nāgaṃ jaratītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.37-38:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Varanāga</s>' means lead (<s>sīsaka</s>) of the best variety, suitable for digestion; 'the king of mercury' means <s>pārada</s> (mercury) processed with the stated <s>saṃskāras</s>; 'the best seed-metal' means gold-seed (<s>hema-bīja</s>). These three should be rendered together, i.e., combined. Furthermore, 'together with sulphur, realgar, and orpiment' — <s>gandhaka</s> is well-known; <s>śilā</s> means realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>); <s>āla</s> means orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>); it should be combined with these. This entire group of six, through the process of a lit lamp-wick, becomes lead-free (<s>nirnāga</s>), i.e., devoid of lead; it digests the lead — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 5.37-38:2 //

children.text: yathā nirṇāgaṃ syāttathā vidhānam āha baddhvetyādi // GRhtCM_5.37-38:3 //
children.translated_text: He states the method for rendering it lead-free, beginning with 'having tied' and so forth. // GRhtCM 5.37-38:3 //

children.text: tatpūrvoktaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ sudṛḍhe vastre nūtane vastre atropaśleṣike 'dhikaraṇe saptamī poṭalikāyāṃ baddhvā punastaile tilodbhave tatṣaṭkaṃ magnaṃ nimajjitaṃ kṛtvā tadadhaḥ śikhīkṛto dīpo'vadhāryaḥ na śikhī śikhāyuktaḥ kṛtaḥ śikhīkṛtaḥ śikhāvānityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.37-38:4 //
children.translated_text: That previously described group of six, [tied] in a strong cloth — a new cloth; the seventh case-ending here is locative, indicating the container — tied in a poultice-bundle. Further, having immersed that group of six in oil, i.e., sesame oil, having submerged it — below it, a lamp with a wick should be placed. 'With a wick' (<s>śikhīkṛta</s>) — '<s>śikhī</s>' means 'possessing a flame'; 'made' — i.e., a lamp that has been given a flame — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 5.37-38:4 //

children.text: anena vidhinā kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ nirnāgaṃ syāditi // GRhtCM_5.37-38:5 //
children.translated_text: By this method, it quickly, i.e., swiftly, becomes lead-free. // GRhtCM 5.37-38:5 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.39-40]
<Digestion of lead>

children.text: kṛtvātra dīrghamūṣāṃ sudṛḍhāṃ dhmātaṃ tu bhasmagartāyām /
children.translated_text: Having made here a long, very strong crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>), [placed] in an ash-pit for smelting,

children.text: kṣiptvā śilālacūrṇaṃ paścātsūtaṃ tataḥ śilācūrṇaṃ // GRht_5.39 //
children.translated_text: put in the powder of realgar and orpiment, then mercury, then again the realgar-orpiment powder. // GRht 5.39 //
Having placed [it] and covered with ash, smelt it until it is naturally cool;

children.text: ākṛṣya tatra sūtaṃ jñātvā nāgaṃ subhakṣitaṃ sakalam // GRht_5.40 //
children.translated_text: then extract the mercury therein, knowing that all the lead has been well consumed. // GRht 5.40 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for lead-removal, beginning with 'having made' and so forth. // GRhtCM 5.39-40:1 //

children.text: tu punaḥ dīrghāṃ gostanākārāṃ sudṛḍhāṃ nirvraṇavajropamāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā tāṃ mūṣāṃ prati śilālacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā śilā manohvā ālaṃ haritālaṃ etayoścūrṇaṃ paścātsūtaṃ pūrvoktaṃ pāradaṃ kṣiptvā tato'nantaraṃ śilācūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā tāmeva rasasaṃyuktāṃ mūṣāṃ bhasmagartāyāṃ bhasmanā yuktā yā gartā tasyāṃ dhmātaṃ kuryāt punastāvadbhasmanā ācchādya yāvatsvāṅgaśītalaṃ svayameva śītalaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_5.39-40:2 //
children.translated_text: Further, having made a long, cow-udder-shaped, very strong crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>), flawless and diamond-like in hardness — into that crucible, first put the powder of realgar and orpiment: <s>śilā</s> means realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>), <s>āla</s> means orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>), their powder. Then put in mercury (<s>sūta</s>), the previously described <s>pārada</s>. Then afterward, put in realgar-orpiment powder. Then that same crucible containing mercury, in an ash-pit — a pit combined with ash — should be smelted. Further, cover it with ash until it becomes naturally cool, i.e., cool by itself. // GRhtCM 5.39-40:2 //

children.text: tatra tasyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ sakalaṃ samastaṃ nāgaṃ subhakṣitaṃ jīrṇatāṃ gataṃ jñātvā sūtaṃ ākṛṣya uddhārya nirnāgakaraṇavidhānam etat // GRhtCM_5.39-40:3 //
children.translated_text: Therein, in that crucible, knowing that the lead has been entirely, completely consumed — that is, has been digested — extract the mercury. This is the procedure for lead-removal. // GRhtCM 5.39-40:3 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.41]
<Seed-treatment of lead-digested mercury>

children.text: jñātvā nāgaṃ truṭitaṃ punarapi dadyādyathā bhavettriguṇam /
children.translated_text: Having ascertained that the lead is exhausted (<s>truṭita</s>), one should again add [lead], so that it becomes three times [the amount];
afterward, having purified [the mercury], one should then add the best seed-metal. // GRht 5.41 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states what is to be done after lead-removal, beginning with 'having ascertained' and so forth. // GRhtCM 5.41:1 //

children.text: nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ truṭitaṃ buddhvā punarapi nāgaṃ dahyāt pūrvoktavidhānena pārade iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.41:2 //
children.translated_text: Having ascertained that the lead (<s>sīsaka</s>) has been exhausted (<s>truṭita</s>), one should again feed lead [to the mercury] by the previously stated method — 'in mercury' is supplied. // GRhtCM 5.41:2 //

children.text: yathā nāgaṃ triguṇitaṃ bhavettathaiva kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.41:3 //
children.translated_text: One should do so in such a way that the lead becomes tripled. // GRhtCM 5.41:3 //

children.text: paścātsūtaṃ śuddhaṃ kṛtvā pāradaṃ nirnāgaṃ vidhāya tadanu nāgajāraṇānantaraṃ bījavaraṃ pūrvoktaṃ yojayet // GRhtCM_5.41:4 //
children.translated_text: Afterward, having purified the mercury, i.e., having made the <s>pārada</s> lead-free, then — after the lead-digestion — one should add the previously mentioned best seed-metal. // GRhtCM 5.41:4 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 5.42]
<Mercury :: Digestion of tin>

children.text: athavā tāraṃ vaṅgaṃ sūtaṃ saṃsārya vaṅgaparihīnam /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, having processed silver (<s>tāra</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) together with mercury, [making it] free from tin —
By the procedure of orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), likewise [render it] free from tin (<s>nirvaṅga</s>), by the crucible (<s>yantra</s>) procedure.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the silver procedure, beginning with '<s>athavā</s>' (or alternatively) etc.
'<s>Athavā</s>' (or alternatively) indicates an alternative procedure.

children.text: tāraṃ vaṅgaṃ sūtam iti tāraṃ rūpyaṃ vaṅgaṃ khurakaṃ sūtaṃ saṃskṛtapāradaṃ etattritayaṃ saṃsārya melanaṃ vidhāya vaṅgaparihīnaṃ kuryāt tathā tenaiva vidhānena tālasya yo'sau yogastena yantrayogena ca dīrghamūṣāyogena ca nirvaṅgaṃ vaṅgavivarjitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.42:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Silver, tin, mercury' — '<s>tāra</s>' means silver; '<s>vaṅga</s>' means tin (<s>khuraka</s>); '<s>sūta</s>' means purified mercury (<s>pārada</s>). These three, having been combined — having performed their union — one should make [the mixture] free from tin (<s>vaṅga</s>). By that same procedure, by the orpiment (<s>tāla</s>) method and the crucible (<s>yantra</s>) method — the long-crucible (<s>dīrghamūṣā</s>) method — one should make it free from tin (<s>nirvaṅga</s>), i.e., devoid of tin.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 5.43
<Mercury :: <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) of tin>
Or alternatively, tied in cloth, combined with mineral pitch (<s>girijatu</s>), well-wrapped with black gram (<s>māṣa</s>),

children.text: pakvaṃ taile vaṭakaṃ nirvaṅgaṃ jāyate nūnam // GRht_5.43 //
children.translated_text: cooked in oil, the pellet certainly becomes free from tin (<s>nirvaṅga</s>).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another procedure, beginning with '<s>athavā</s>' (or alternatively) etc.

children.text: athavā tāraṃ vaṅgaṃ vaṭakākāraṃ taile tilodbhave pakvaṃ kuryāt nūnaṃ niścitaṃ tadvaṭakaṃ tathā pakvaṃ kuryādyathā nirvaṅgaṃ jāyate vahniyogena iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.43:2 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, silver and tin, made into a pellet form, should be cooked in sesame oil (<s>tilodbhava</s>); certainly — [meaning] definitely — that pellet should be so cooked that it becomes free from tin, by the application of fire — this is the completion.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 5.44-46
<s>Bīja</s> (seed/transmutation agent) :: for <s>garbhadruti</s> (embryo-fusion)>
Having made an amalgam-lump (<s>piṣṭīstambha</s>), rendered [into one body] with the best seed (<s>bījavara</s>), thereafter —
<s>Bīja</s> (seed) :: for <s>garbhadruti</s> (embryo-fusion)>

children.text: athavā baddharasena tu sahitaṃ bījaṃ surañjitaṃ kṛtvā // GRht_5.44 //
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, having combined the seed with bound mercury (<s>baddharasa</s>), having made it well-colored (<s>surañjita</s>),

children.text: gandhakanihitaṃ sūtaṃ nihitānihitaṃ ca śṛṅkhalāyāṃ tat /
children.translated_text: mercury deposited in sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), deposited and un-deposited [alternately] in a chain (<s>śṛṅkhalā</s>) —
in mercury [thus] combined and processed, it certainly effects <s>garbhadruti</s> (embryo-fusion).

children.text: sūtakabhasmavareṇa tu bījaṃ kṛtvā rasendrake garbhe /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, having made the seed with the best mercury-ash (<s>sūtakabhasma</s>), in the womb of the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>),

children.text: mṛditā piṣṭī vidhinā hyabhiṣavayogāddravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.46 //
children.translated_text: the amalgam (<s>piṣṭī</s>), pressed according to procedure, by the pressing method (<s>abhiṣava-yoga</s>), melts in the womb.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states an alternative procedure, beginning with '<s>piṣṭī</s>' (amalgam) etc.

children.text: bījavareṇaiva pūrvakanakabījenaiva sāritaṃ militaṃ sat piṣṭīstambhaṃ khoṭastambhaṃ kṛtvā tadanu tatpaścāt athaveti prakārāntaraṃ darśayati tu punaḥ baddharasena khoṭabaddharasena sahitaṃ surañjitaṃ śobhanavidhānena varṇavṛddhīkṛtaṃ bījaṃ svarṇabījaṃ saṃyutaṃ kuryāt yoga eva kārya iti dvividhānam uktam // GRhtCM_5.44-46:2 //
children.translated_text: Having been rendered — combined — with the best seed, [meaning] the previously [described] gold-seed itself, making an amalgam-lump (<s>piṣṭīstambha</s>) — a solid amalgam (<s>khoṭa-stambha</s>); thereafter — after that. '<s>Athavā</s>' (or alternatively) shows another method. With bound mercury — mercury bound in solid form (<s>khoṭa</s>) — combined, well-colored — with color-enhancement done by excellent procedure — the gold-seed should be combined. Thus a twofold procedure is stated.
He states another [method], beginning with '<s>gandhaka</s>' (sulphur) etc.

children.text: gandhakanihitaṃ gandhake nihitaṃ sthāpitaṃ sūtaṃ ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ dattvā sūtaṃ madhyasthaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.44-46:4 //
children.translated_text: 'Deposited in sulphur' — deposited, i.e., placed in sulphur; having placed sulphur above and below, mercury should be made to remain in the middle — this is the meaning.

children.text: ca punarevaṃvidhaṃ sūtaṃ śṛṅkhalāyāṃ śṛṅkhalīkaraṇayoge nihitānihitaṃ yannihitaṃ tadanihitam ajāritaṃ kāryaṃ nihitānihitasaṃyogāt śṛṅkhaleyaṃ nūnaṃ niścitaṃ yojitanirvyūḍharase pūrvaṃ yojitaṃ paścānnirvāhitaṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ yatra tattasminnevaṃvidharase garbhadrutiḥ pāradasyodare bījāni dravanti // GRhtCM_5.44-46:5 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, such mercury, in the chain — in the chain-making (<s>śṛṅkhalīkaraṇa</s>) procedure — 'deposited and un-deposited' — what is deposited should be made as if un-deposited, i.e., un-digested; by the combination of deposited and un-deposited, this chain [operation]. Certainly — definitely — in mercury that has been [first] combined and then processed — i.e., worked through (<s>nirvāhita</s>) — the <s>garbhadruti</s> occurs: the seeds melt in the belly of mercury.
He states digestion by the amalgam method, beginning with '<s>sūtaka</s>' (mercury) etc.

children.text: tu punaḥ rasendrake garbhe rasendrakṛto yo'sau garbhastasmin bījaṃ kṛtvā vidhinā piṣṭīrvidheyā sā piṣṭī mṛditā kāryā kasmāt abhiṣavayogāt saṃmardanayogāt kena saha sūtakabhasmavareṇa saha sūtakasya yadbhasmavaraṃ tena sā piṣṭī garbhe dravati caśabdājjarati ca // GRhtCM_5.44-46:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in the womb of the lord of mercury — in the womb (<s>garbha</s>) produced by the lord of mercury — having placed the seed therein, amalgams (<s>piṣṭī</s>) should be prepared according to procedure; that amalgam should be pressed. By what? By the pressing procedure (<s>abhiṣava-yoga</s>) — by the grinding method. With what? With the best mercury-ash — with the ash (<s>bhasma</s>) that is the best [form] of mercury; that amalgam melts in the womb, and — by [the implied meaning of] 'ca' — is also digested (<s>jarati</s>).
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 5.47-49
<s>Bīja</s> (seed) :: for <s>garbhadruti</s> (embryo-fusion)>

children.text: patrābhrakaṃ ca satvaṃ kāṃkṣī vā kāntamākṣikaṃ puṭitam /
children.translated_text: Mica-leaf (<s>patrābhraka</s>) and its essence, or <s>kāṃkṣī</s>, and <s>kānta</s> (loadstone) and <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites), calcined (<s>puṭita</s>),
with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (five-leaved chaste tree), <s>gṛhakanyā</s> (aloe), <s>cāṅgerī</s> (wood-sorrel), and <s>palāśa</s> (flame-of-the-forest) vegetables;
calcined so many times until it becomes of the color of vermilion (<s>sindūra</s>);
that, with a quarter portion of salt, cooked firmly by the pot-cooking (<s>haṇḍikā-pāka</s>) method,
each one separately, processed a hundred times — becomes the best seed (<s>bījavara</s>). It should be digested in the womb of the lord of mercury;

children.text: garbhe dravati ca kṣipraṃ hyabhiṣavayogena mṛditamaṅgulyā // GRht_5.49 //
children.translated_text: it melts quickly in the womb, by the pressing procedure (<s>abhiṣava-yoga</s>), pressed with the finger.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for the best seed, beginning with '<s>patrābhraka</s>' (mica-leaf) etc.

children.text: patrābhrakamiti abhrakasya patrāṇi vābhrakasya satvaṃ punaḥ kāṃkṣī saurāṣṭrī kāntamākṣikaṃ kāntaścumbakaḥ mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ eteṣāṃ dvandva ekatvaṃ punaretat nirguṇḍīgṛhakanyācāṅgerīpalāśaśākaiḥ puṭitaṃ nirguṇḍī sephālikā gṛhakanyā kumārī cāṅgerī amlaśākaḥ palāśo brahmavṛkṣaḥ śāko vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ eteṣāṃ dvandvasamāsaḥ eteṣāṃ rasaṃ gṛhītvā pūrvauṣadhapuṭitaṃ kuryāt gharme iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.47-49:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Patrābhraka</s>' — the leaves of mica, or the essence of mica; furthermore, <s>kāṃkṣī</s> (i.e., <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, a type of chalcanthite); <s>kānta</s> means loadstone (<s>cumbaka</s>); <s>mākṣika</s> means gold-<s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites); the <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) of these [gives] a singular [form]. Furthermore, calcined with <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>gṛhakanyā</s>, <s>cāṅgerī</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, and vegetable [juices]: <s>nirguṇḍī</s> is the <s>sephālikā</s> plant; <s>gṛhakanyā</s> is aloe (<s>kumārī</s>); <s>cāṅgerī</s> is sour herb (<s>amlaśāka</s>); <s>palāśa</s> is the sacred tree (<s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>); <s>śāka</s> is a specific tree. The <s>dvandva</s> compound of these. Having taken the juice of these, one should perform calcination with the previous herbs — in sunlight — this is the completion.

children.text: tadauṣadhaṃ puṭitaṃ kṛtvā punastatpuṭitamauṣadhaṃ tatpādaśeṣaṃ caturthāṃśaṃ lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ dattvā haṇḍikāpākena haṇḍikāyāṃ mṛdbhājane yaḥ pākastena pācitaṃ vahnau puṭitaṃ tāvatkuryād yāvat sindūrasaṃprabhaṃ sindūratulyavarṇaṃ bhavati // GRhtCM_5.47-49:3 //
children.translated_text: That medicine, having been calcined, furthermore, that calcined medicine — with a quarter-portion residual — adding salt (<s>saindhava</s>), by pot-cooking — the cooking done in a pot (<s>haṇḍikā</s>), an earthen vessel — cooked, i.e., calcined in fire — one should do [this] so many times until it becomes of vermilion-like color — equal to the color of cinnabar.

children.text: kathaṃ pācitaṃ kuryāt sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā ekaikaṃ śatavyūḍhamiti // GRhtCM_5.47-49:4 //
children.translated_text: How should the cooking be done? Firmly, such that it becomes [solid]. 'Each one, processed a hundred times' — thus.

children.text: pūrvoktānāṃ sindūrīkṛtānām uparasānām adharāt ekaikaṃ ekaṃ ekaṃ pṛthaktvena śatavyūḍhaṃ śatavāraṃ vāhitaṃ bījavaraṃ jāyate kanake iti śeṣaḥ tadbījaṃ rasendrasya garbhe dravati caśabdāt kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ jarati ca // GRhtCM_5.47-49:5 //
children.translated_text: Of the aforementioned subsidiary minerals made into cinnabar-like [form], separately — each one individually, processed a hundred times — becomes the best seed; 'in gold' is the completion. That seed melts in the womb of the lord of mercury, and — from [the implied meaning of] 'ca' — is quickly digested also.

children.text: kathaṃ aṅgulyā anāmikayā yo 'bhiṣavayogaḥ saṃmardanayogasteneti viśeṣakam // GRhtCM_5.47-49:6 //
children.translated_text: How? With the finger — the ring finger — by the pressing procedure (<s>abhiṣava-yoga</s>) — the grinding method; this is the specific qualification.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 5.50
<Gold :: <s>bīja</s> (seed) with lead>
In the finest gold (<s>hemavara</s>), when it is being melted, lead (<s>nāga</s>) should be cast — [itself] to be melted — in the bright [gold];
with a counter-charge of triple-quantity arsenic (<s>śilā</s>) — that is called the 'serpent-seed' (<s>ahibīja</s>).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: nāgena bījakaraṇamāha ujjvalahemavare svarṇaśreṣṭhe āvartye samyagdrute nāgaṃ śuddhasīsakaṃ āvartyaṃ pradrāvyaṃ kiṃ kṛtvā samaṃ svarṇasamabhāgakṣepaṃ kṣiptvā punarnāgopari triguṇaśilāprativāpaṃ triguṇā yā śilā tasyā nirvāpaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.50:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the preparation of seed with lead. In the finest gold (<s>hemavara</s>) — the best gold — [when it is] being melted (<s>āvartya</s>), i.e., properly liquefied, lead (<s>nāga</s>) — pure lead (<s>śuddhasīsaka</s>) — should be melted [into it]. Having done what? Having cast [it] in equal proportion to the gold. Then, upon the lead, a counter-charge (<s>nirvāpa</s>) of triple-quantity arsenic (<s>śilā</s>) should be made — that is, arsenic three times [the amount].
'<s>Śilā</s>' means realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>).

children.text: tatsiddhaṃ ahibījaṃ nāgayogena bījaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ rasavidbhiḥ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.50:3 //
children.translated_text: That, [once] perfected, is called the 'serpent-seed' (<s>ahibīja</s>) — the seed [made] by the lead-procedure — [as] declared by the knowers of mercury — this is the completion.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 5.51
<Gold, silver :: <s>bīja</s> (seed) with tin>

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tu tena vidhinā hemavare kṣepya tālavāpena /
children.translated_text: Tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), by that same procedure, should be cast into the finest gold (<s>hemavara</s>), with a counter-charge of orpiment (<s>tāla</s>);

children.text: tāre vā nirvyūḍhaṃ bījavaraṃ truṭitasaṃyogāt // GRht_5.51 //
children.translated_text: or in silver (<s>tāra</s>) — processed — it becomes the best seed (<s>bījavara</s>), from the breaking of the combination (<s>truṭita-saṃyoga</s>).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the seed [made] by the tin-procedure, beginning with '<s>vaṅga</s>' (tin) etc.

children.text: tena pūrvoktena vidhinā vidhānena tu punaḥ hemavare pūrvavarṇite vaṅgaṃ kṣepya tālavāpena haritālanikṣepeṇa nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt vā tāre āvartye vaṅgaṃ nikṣipya nirvyūḍhaṃ nirvāhitaṃ sadbījavaraṃ bhavet // GRhtCM_5.51:2 //
children.translated_text: By that same — the previously stated — procedure, i.e., method; tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) should be cast into the previously described finest gold (<s>hemavara</s>), and with a counter-charge of orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>), it should be processed. Or, tin should be cast into silver (<s>tāra</s>) [that is being] melted, and the processed, i.e., worked-through [product], becomes the best seed.

children.text: kasmāt truṭitasaṃyogāt truṭitaṃ bhavati tathā bījavaramiti vaṅgabījaṃ tat pūrvavat dravati jarati ca // GRhtCM_5.51:3 //
children.translated_text: Why? 'From the breaking of the combination' — the [tin-gold/silver compound] becomes broken, and thus it becomes the best seed. That tin-seed, as before, melts [in mercury's womb] and is also digested.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 5.52
<<s>Rasāṅkuśa</s> (goad of mercury)>

children.text: yo niḥsṛto bhujaṅgād rasakeśarīvajrapañjaraḥ sa punaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which has emerged from the serpent (lead), the diamond-cage for the lion of mercury (<s>rasakeśarī-vajrapañjara</s>), it again —
due to the qualities of serpent (lead) and gold, [being] curved — is renowned by the name '<s>rasāṅkuśa</s>' (goad of mercury).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He praises the gold-named seed, beginning with '<s>ya</s>' (that which) etc.

children.text: bhujaṅgāt sīsakāt niḥsṛtaḥ bhujaṅgaśilāvāpena kṣayaṃ nītvā yaḥ pṛthagbhūtaḥ sa rasakesarīvajrapañjaraḥ kathitaḥ rasa eva kesarī siṃhaḥ tadarthaṃ vajrapañjaraḥ vajreṇa vyadhitaḥ pañjaro'tidṛḍhatvāt siṃharakṣaṇasamartha ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.52:2 //
children.translated_text: 'From the serpent (<s>bhujaṅga</s>)' — from lead (<s>sīsaka</s>), [the seed] has emerged — by the counter-charge of arsenic, having been brought to destruction [of impurities], that which has become separate; it is called the 'diamond-cage of the lion of mercury' — mercury itself is the lion (<s>kesarī</s>); for its sake, the diamond-cage — a cage pierced by diamond, extremely strong, capable of protecting the lion — this is the meaning.

children.text: punarviśeṣeṇocyate ayaṃ vajrapañjaro na kiṃtu ayaṃ rasāṅkuśaḥ raso gajarūpaḥ tasyāṅkuśaḥ vaśīkaraṇasamarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.52:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, it is specifically said: this is not merely a diamond-cage, but rather a '<s>rasāṅkuśa</s>' (goad of mercury) — mercury is in the form of an elephant; its goad — capable of bringing [it] under control.
'<s>Nāma</s>' (called) [is used] in the sense of probability.
'<s>Vikhyāta</s>' means 'celebrated.'

children.text: kasmāt kuṭilāt kimapi vastuharaṇāt kuṭilo vakro bhavati duṣṭasvabhāva eva anena hemnā nāgaharaṇaṃ kṛtam // GRhtCM_5.52:6 //
children.translated_text: Why? Because from the curved one — by stealing some substance — it becomes curved, i.e., bent, of a crooked nature; by this gold, the extraction of lead has been accomplished.

children.text: kathaṃbhūtāt kuṭilāt phaṇī bhujaṅgaḥ hema svarṇaṃ tayorguṇā vidyante yasmin evaṃvidhāt kuṭilādeśo yuktaḥ aṅkuśo'pi vakro bhavatīti // GRhtCM_5.52:7 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality is this curved one? '<s>Phaṇī</s>' — serpent (lead); '<s>hema</s>' — gold; the qualities of both are found in it — from such a curved one, the designation '<s>aṅkuśa</s>' (goad) is fitting, for the goad too is curved.

children.text: atra bhrāntimānalaṅkāraḥ hemabīje vajrapañjaragajāṅkuśadarśanād bhrāntirjāteti // GRhtCM_5.52:8 //
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>bhrāntimān</s> (confusion) figure of speech (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) [is employed]: upon seeing diamond-cage, elephant, and goad in the gold-seed, the confusion arises.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 5.53-58
<<s>Jāraṇa</s> (digestion) without preceding <s>garbhadruti</s> (embryo-fusion); external fusion??>

children.text: evaṃ pakvaṃ vidhinā bījavaraṃ sūtarāṭ tathāmlena /
children.translated_text: Thus, the best seed, cooked according to procedure, and the king of mercury, with sour [substances] —
sweating should be performed until a smooth amalgam (<s>piṣṭī</s>) forms.

children.text: tailena tena vidhinā svinnā piṣṭī bhavedakhilam /
children.translated_text: By oil, by that same procedure, the amalgam, when sweated, becomes complete;

children.text: athavā ślakṣṇaṃ śilayā nighṛṣṭabījaṃ bhavetpiṇḍī // GRht_5.54 //
children.translated_text: or alternatively, the seed, smoothly ground on stone, becomes a solid lump (<s>piṇḍī</s>).
Cooking should be done by the pellet method (<s>vaṭaka-vidhi</s>), with the oil procedure;

children.text: krāmaṇapiṇḍe kṣiptvā māṣaiśca syāt sudṛḍhapiṇḍatvam // GRht_5.55 //
children.translated_text: placing it in the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-lump and [coating it] with black gram (<s>māṣa</s>), it should become a firmly solid lump.
Cooked well over a gentle fire, until the lump is not [merely] burned;

children.text: ākṛṣya cātha sūtaṃ piṇḍe śeṣaṃ tathā punaḥ pācyam // GRht_5.56 //
children.translated_text: then, having extracted the mercury, the residue in the lump should be cooked again.
Or alternatively, in a herb-lump (<s>auṣadha-piṇḍa</s>), heated by the swing method (<s>dolā</s>), on a saucer (<s>kharpara</s>), by [proper] procedure;

children.text: punarapi piṇḍe kṣepyaṃ garbhe yāvaddrutirbhavati // GRht_5.57 //
children.translated_text: again and again it should be placed in the lump, until fusion (<s>druti</s>) occurs in the womb.

children.text: evaṃ drutaṃ hi garbhe bījavaraṃ jarati rasarāje /
children.translated_text: Thus, the best seed, fused in the womb, is digested by the king of mercury;

children.text: garbhadrutyā rahitaṃ biḍayogairjarati garbhe ca // GRht_5.58 //
children.translated_text: without embryo-fusion (<s>garbhadruti</s>), it is digested in the womb by the <s>biḍa</s>-procedures.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the amalgamation of this seed, beginning with '<s>evam</s>' (thus) etc.

children.text: evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa vidhinārthād upadeśena pakvaṃ yadbījavaraṃ tathā pūrvasaṃskṛtaḥ sūtarāṭ pāradaḥ amlena jambīrādinā saṃsvedyaḥ svedākhyo vidhiḥ kartavyaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method, [and] by the procedure — that is, by instruction — the best seed that has been cooked, and likewise the previously processed king of mercury (<s>pārada</s>), should be sweated with sour [substances] such as lemon (<s>jambīra</s>) and the like — the procedure called sweating (<s>sveda</s>) should be performed.

children.text: atra kimavadhistatkartavyo yāvat ślakṣṇā spaṣṭā piṣṭī ekaśarīratā bhavet rasabījayoriti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:3 //
children.translated_text: What is the limit here? That [sweating] should be done until a smooth — clear — amalgam (<s>piṣṭī</s>), a unified body, forms — of mercury and the seed — this is the completion.
He states an alternative procedure, beginning with 'with oil' (<s>tailena</s>) etc.

children.text: tena pūrvoktena vidhinā vadhavidhānena tilatailena svinnā sveditā satī piṣṭirbhavati vahnāviti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:5 //
children.translated_text: By that same — the previously stated — procedure, by the killing method, with sesame oil, the amalgam becomes sweated — having been steamed, the amalgam forms — in fire — this is the completion.
'<s>Athavā</s>' (or alternatively) shows another procedure.

children.text: śilayā dṛṣanmayayā nighṛṣṭabījaṃ nighṛṣṭaṃ gharṣitaṃ yadbījaṃ nāgākhyaṃ tat sūteneti śeṣaḥ akhilaṃ samastaṃ yathā syāttathā piṣṭirbhavatīti // GRhtCM_5.53-58:7 //
children.translated_text: The seed ground on stone — ground, i.e., rubbed on a grinding-stone — the lead-named [seed], that [is combined] with mercury — this is the completion; [so that] the whole, the entirety, becomes an amalgam (<s>piṣṭī</s>).

children.text: yathā vaṭakaḥ pācyastathāha pāka ityādi // GRhtCM_5.53-58:8 //
children.translated_text: He states how the pellet is to be cooked, beginning with '<s>pāka</s>' (cooking) etc.

children.text: vaṭakavidhinā māṣavaṭakavidhinā tailayogena pākaḥ kartavyaḥ vahnau pācanaṃ vidheyamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:9 //
children.translated_text: By the pellet procedure — the black-gram pellet (<s>māṣavaṭaka</s>) procedure — with the oil method, cooking should be done — cooking in fire should be performed — this is the meaning.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā krāmaṇapiṇḍe kṣiptvā biḍapiṇḍamadhye sthāpya ca punarmāṣair annaviśeṣair dṛḍhapiṇḍatvaṃ syāt māṣacūrṇaveṣṭitaṃ krāmaṇapiṇḍaṃ dṛḍhaṃ bhavediti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:10 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having placed [the mercury] in the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-pellet (<s>krāmaṇa-piṇḍa</s>), positioned within the <s>biḍa</s>-pellet, and furthermore [coated] with black-gram flour (<s>māṣa</s>), a type of grain, so that the pellet becomes firm — the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-pellet wrapped in black-gram flour becomes solid — this is the clarification. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:10 //
He states its procedure — 'gentle' and so forth. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:11 //

children.text: māṣacūrṇitajātaṃ krāmaṇapiṇḍaṃ tāvat supakvaṃ kartavyaṃ yāvaddagdhaṃ na bhavet // GRhtCM_5.53-58:12 //
children.translated_text: The <s>krāmaṇa</s>-pellet made with black-gram flour should be cooked well to the extent that it does not become burnt. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:12 //

children.text: kena supakvaṃ mṛdvagninā komalavahninā puṭaḥ tatpiṇḍataḥ śeṣaṃ śiṣṭaṃ taṃ nirmalapāradaṃ ākṛṣya gṛhītvā piṇḍamanyasmin piṇḍe tathā pūrvaprakāreṇa pācyamiti // GRhtCM_5.53-58:13 //
children.translated_text: By what should it be well-cooked? By a gentle fire (<s>mṛdvagni</s>), i.e., a soft flame. The <s>puṭa</s> (calcination) — the remainder from the pellet, the pure mercury, having extracted it, i.e., taken it out, the pellet should be cooked in another pellet in the same manner as before. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:13 //
He states another [method] — 'or alternatively' and so forth. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:14 //
'Or alternatively' indicates an alternative method. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:15 //

children.text: punarapi piṣṭīrdolātapte auṣadhapiṇḍe dolayottapte uṣṇatāṃ nīte krāmaṇauṣadhānāṃ piṇḍe kṣepya madhye sthāpya kasyopari kharpare mṛnmayapātropari // GRhtCM_5.53-58:16 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the pellets [should be placed] in a <s>dolā</s>-heated (swing-heated) medicinal pellet — a pellet of <s>krāmaṇa</s>-herbs that has been heated in a swing-apparatus, i.e., brought to warmth — having placed [them] in the middle; on what? On a <s>kharpara</s> (earthen saucer), i.e., on an earthenware vessel. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:16 //

children.text: kena vidhinā pūrvoktena tailena vā amleneti // GRhtCM_5.53-58:17 //
children.translated_text: By what method? By the previously described oil or acid. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:17 //

children.text: kiyatkālaṃ yāvadgarbhe rasodare piṣṭī dravati tāvadbiḍāntare piṇḍāntare kṣepyeti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:18 //
children.translated_text: For how long? Until the pellet liquefies in the womb, i.e., inside the mercury — for that duration it should be placed within the <s>biḍa</s> — this is the purport. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:18 //
He states another [method] — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:19 //

children.text: evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa garbhe rasodare jarati niḥśeṣatvaṃ rasodare prāpnoti ca punargarbhadrutyā rahitaṃ draveṇa varjitaṃ bījavaraṃ biḍairjarati drutabījamāraṇasamartho biḍa ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:20 //
children.translated_text: In this manner, by this method, it is assimilated within the womb, i.e., within the belly of mercury, reaching completeness within mercury's interior; and furthermore, the seed (<s>bīja</s>), devoid of <s>garbha-druti</s> (internal liquefaction), i.e., deprived of liquid, that excellent seed is assimilated by the <s>biḍas</s> — the <s>biḍa</s> is capable of killing the liquefied seed — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:20 //
The measure of liquefied devouring (<s>druta-grāsa</s>), through the application of the <s>biḍa</s>-apparatus and so forth,
is called <s>jāraṇā</s> (assimilation); its varieties exist in tens of millions —
'varieties of apparatuses' is the remainder to be supplied. // GRhtCM_5.53-58:21 //
The divisions of <s>jāraṇā</s> are:
The transmutation (<s>cāraṇā</s>) of the devoured [substance], the melting within the womb (<s>garbha-drāvaṇa</s>), and assimilation (<s>jāraṇā</s>) —
thus, <s>jāraṇā</s> has been declared to be threefold by the best among commentators.
START GRht 6.1-7
<s>jāraṇā</s> (assimilation): method>
Having made [mercury] transmute the devoured [substance] and then [having accomplished] <s>garbha-druti</s> (internal liquefaction), thereafter, on a birch-bark (<s>bhūrja</s>)
coated with salt, alkali, acid, lime (<s>sudhā</s>), and cow-urine, // GRht_6.1 //
bound externally with a firm cloth, one should assimilate the devoured [substance] by the <s>dolā-sveda</s> (swing-sweating method),
in a pot half-filled with <s>sauvīra</s> (fermented rice-water), or with alkali and urine-solutions. // GRht_6.2 //
By this sequence, in three-day intervals, one should assimilate the devoured [substance].
He describes the <s>garbha-druti jāraṇā</s> (internal-liquefaction assimilation) — 'devoured' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:1 //

children.text: pūrvoktaprakāreṇa grāsaṃ kavalaṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ cārayitvā punargarbhadrutiṃ kṛtvā tatastadanantaraṃ tadgarbhadrutaṃ sūtaṃ bhūrje bhūrjavṛkṣatvakpuṭake sthāpayedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.1-2:2 //
children.translated_text: By the previously described method, having made [mercury] transmute the appropriate quantity of devoured material (<s>grāsa</s>, morsel), and having performed <s>garbha-druti</s> (internal liquefaction), thereafter, i.e., after that, that mercury with internal liquefaction should be placed on birch-bark (<s>bhūrja</s>), i.e., in a pouch made from the bark of the birch tree — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:2 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭe bhūrje lavaṇakṣārāmlasudhāsurabhimūtreṇa kṛtalepe lavaṇāni saindhavādīni kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ amlo jambīrādiḥ sudhā śukticūrṇaṃ surabhī dhenustanmūtraṃ etena yogena kṛtvā kṛto lepo yasmin // GRhtCM_6.1-2:3 //
children.translated_text: On what kind of birch-bark? Coated with salt, alkali, acid, lime, and cow-urine: salts are <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) and others; alkalis are <s>svarjikā</s> (soda ash) and others; the acid is <s>jambīra</s> (citron) and such; lime (<s>sudhā</s>) is oyster-shell powder (<s>śukti-cūrṇa</s>); '<s>surabhi</s>' is the cow, and its urine — with this combined preparation, a coating has been made on which [the birch-bark is treated]. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:3 //
The mercury endowed with internal liquefaction (<s>udara-druti</s>) should be placed [therein] — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:4 //
He describes the assimilation procedure — 'firm' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:5 //

children.text: dṛḍhavastrabāhyabaddhe iti dṛḍhaṃ nūtanaṃ ghanaṃ ca yadvastraṃ tena bāhye sarvato baddhe saṃyate pūrvoktena dolāsvedena dolāyantravidhinā yaḥ svedastaṃ kṛtvā grāsaṃ rasāntardrutaṃ kavalaṃ jārayet // GRhtCM_6.1-2:6 //
children.translated_text: 'Bound externally with firm cloth' — 'firm' means new and dense; with such cloth, bound on the outside, i.e., tied all around — by the previously described <s>dolā-sveda</s> (swing-sweating method), i.e., by the procedure of the swing-apparatus (<s>dolā-yantra</s>), performing the sweating — having done this, one should assimilate the devoured material (<s>grāsa</s>), i.e., the morsel dissolved within the mercury. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:6 //

children.text: kutra kumbhe kalaśe kiṃviśiṣṭe sauvīreṇārdhapūrṇe sauvīreṇa svedanasaṃskāroditakāñjikena kṛtvā ardhapūrṇe // GRhtCM_6.1-2:7 //
children.translated_text: Where? In a pot (<s>kumbha</s>), i.e., a pitcher. Of what kind? Half-filled with <s>sauvīra</s>, i.e., the <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented rice-water) described in the sweating preparation — [filled] halfway. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:7 //
'Or alternatively' indicates an alternative procedure. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:8 //

children.text: sakṣāramūtrakaiḥ saha kṣāraḥ svarjikādibhiḥ vartante yāni mūtrāṇi go'jāvinārīṇāmiti śeṣaḥ etaiḥ ardhabhṛte kumbhe jārayedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.1-2:9 //
children.translated_text: 'With alkali and urine-solutions' — together with alkali, i.e., <s>svarjikā</s> and others, and the urines of cows, goats, sheep, and women — the remainder; in a pot half-filled with these, one should assimilate [the grāsa] — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:9 //
Now he states the time-calculation for mercury-assimilation — 'by this' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:10 //

children.text: amunā krameṇeti uktaprakāreṇa tribhistribhirdivasaiḥ tribhiḥ saṃkhyākairdivasaiḥ grāse jāte anyagrāsaḥ kriyate garbhadrutagrāsaḥ kriyate garbhadrutagrāsaḥ tridivasairjaratīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_6.1-2:11 //
children.translated_text: 'By this sequence,' i.e., by the described method — in three-day intervals, i.e., by threes of days: when one devoured morsel (<s>grāsa</s>) has been [assimilated], another morsel is prepared — the internally-liquefied morsel, i.e., the morsel that has undergone internal liquefaction, is assimilated in three days — this is the purport. // GRhtCM_6.1-2:11 //
START GRht 6.3-7
The characteristic of that which has been assimilated — now [this] should be known, having extracted [it] from the apparatus. // GRht_6.3 //
<Examination whether <s>jāraṇā</s> (assimilation) has taken place>
The extracted [mercury] should be washed in a vessel with <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented rice-water); then,

children.text: samalaṃ ca kāṃjikamato haraṇārthaṃ vastrayogena // GRht_6.4 //
children.translated_text: the impure <s>kāñjika</s> — for the purpose of removing [impurity], by means of cloth-straining. // GRht_6.4 //

children.text: tadanu sukhoṣṇe pātre saṃmardyo'sau yathā na hīye /
children.translated_text: Then, in a pleasantly warm vessel, it should be ground such that it does not diminish,
for as long as all the <s>kāñjika</s> adhering to it dries up completely. // GRht_6.5 //
Thus, with the water dried off, made thoroughly clean by hand-rubbing,
[it] should be pressed over a vessel through a cloth folded in four layers. // GRht_6.6 //

children.text: yadi parigalitaḥ sakalo vastrād grāsena caikatāṃ yātaḥ /
children.translated_text: If it has all passed through the cloth, having attained oneness with the devoured [substance],

children.text: na bhavati yadi daṇḍadharo jīrṇagrāsastadā jñeyaḥ // GRht_6.7 //
children.translated_text: [and] if it does not become rod-holding (<s>daṇḍa-dhara</s>), then it should be known as having a fully assimilated morsel. // GRht_6.7 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: atheti tridinasvedānantaraṃ jīrṇasya rasasya lakṣaṇaṃ jñeyaṃ grāso jīrṇo na veti jñātavyaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:1 //
children.translated_text: 'Now,' i.e., after the three-day sweating — the characteristic of the assimilated mercury should be known, i.e., whether the morsel has been assimilated or not, this should be ascertained. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:1 //

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā yantrāddolikābhidhānād uddhṛtya yantrād bahir gṛhītveti // GRhtCM_6.3-7:2 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having extracted from the apparatus, i.e., from the swing (<s>dolikā</s>), having taken [it] out from the apparatus. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:2 //
He describes the removal of mercury's impurity — 'extracted' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:3 //

children.text: uddhṛtamātramiti yantrād bahir gṛhītamātraṃ tatpātre bhājane mṛnmaye kāñjikena prakṣālya // GRhtCM_6.3-7:4 //
children.translated_text: 'Merely upon extraction' — merely upon being taken out from the apparatus, in a vessel (<s>pātra</s>), i.e., an earthenware container, wash [it] with <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented rice-water). // GRhtCM_6.3-7:4 //

children.text: punar ato rasātsamalaṃ malasaṃyutaṃ kāñjikaṃ haraṇīyaṃ bahiḥ kāryam // GRhtCM_6.3-7:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, from the mercury, the impure, i.e., contaminated, <s>kāñjika</s> should be removed, i.e., taken out. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:5 //

children.text: kena kṛtvā vastrayogena vastre kṣiptaṃ sat tadeva tiṣṭhati na kāñjikam // GRhtCM_6.3-7:6 //
children.translated_text: By what means? By cloth-straining — when cast upon cloth, it [mercury] alone remains, not the <s>kāñjika</s>. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:6 //
He describes its procedure — 'thereafter' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:7 //

children.text: tadanu vastrayogānantaraṃ sukhoṣṇe pātre asau rasaḥ saṃmardyaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:8 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, i.e., after the cloth-straining, in a pleasantly warm vessel, that mercury should be ground. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:8 //

children.text: kathaṃ yathā na hīyate nāśaṃ nāpnuyāt atyauṣṇyāt vā kāṃsyatāmranāgavaṅgakanakatārapātrāt vā dṛḍhakaraghātād raso hīna eva syāt ato'sau pāradas tāvan saṃmardyo yāvallagnakāñjikaṃ rasasaṃsargasauvīraṃ śuṣyati niḥśeṣatāṃ yātītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:9 //
children.translated_text: How? Such that it does not diminish, i.e., does not suffer loss — from excessive heat, or from vessels of bell-metal, copper, lead, tin, gold, or silver, or from forceful hand-striking, the mercury would indeed suffer loss. Therefore, that mercury should be ground only until the adhering <s>kāñjika</s>, i.e., the <s>sauvīra</s> that has come in contact with the mercury, dries up, i.e., reaches complete exhaustion — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:9 //
He describes its procedure — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:10 //

children.text: itthaṃ amunā prakāreṇa karamardanataḥ hastatalamardanataḥ sunirmalībhūto malarahitaḥ śoṣitajalo rasaścaturguṇena vastreṇa kṛtvā pānasyopari pīḍyaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:11 //
children.translated_text: Thus, i.e., by this method — through hand-rubbing, i.e., rubbing with the palm of the hand, made thoroughly clean, i.e., free from impurity, the mercury with its water dried off should be pressed over a vessel through a cloth folded in four layers. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:11 //
He states the characteristic of an assimilated morsel — 'if' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:12 //

children.text: tadā pārado jīrṇagrāso jñeyaḥ jīrṇo niḥśeṣatvamāpanno grāso yasmin sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:13 //
children.translated_text: Then the mercury should be known as having an assimilated morsel (<s>jīrṇa-grāsa</s>), i.e., the morsel has reached completeness within it — one in whom this [obtains] is thus described. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:13 //

children.text: yadi sakalaḥ sarvaḥ vastrātparigalitaḥ caturguṇavastrāt cyuto bhavati pātre iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:14 //
children.translated_text: If all of it, i.e., the entirety, has passed through the cloth, i.e., has descended from the four-layered cloth — into the vessel, is the remainder. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:14 //

children.text: punaryadi grāsena saha ekatāṃ yātaḥ san militaḥ san raso daṇḍadharo na bhavati sthirarūpo na syāt tadā jīrṇagrāso jñātavya ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:15 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, if, having attained oneness with the morsel, i.e., having merged with it, the mercury does not become rod-holding (<s>daṇḍa-dhara</s>), i.e., does not become solid in form — then it should be understood as having an assimilated morsel — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_6.3-7:15 //
START GRht 6.8
<unassimilated morsel (<s>grāsa-ajīrṇa</s>): treatment>
The unassimilated pellet from the morsel — having extracted [it] from the mercury, one should separate it by distillation;

children.text: svastho bhavati rasendro grāsaḥ pakvaḥ punarjarati // GRht_6.8 //
children.translated_text: the lord of mercury becomes healthy [again]; the morsel, [once] cooked, is again assimilated. // GRht_6.8 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the characteristic of mercury-indigestion — 'from the morsel' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.8:1 //

children.text: grāsāt kavalasaṃyogāt ajīrṇapiṣṭīṃ ajīrṇā aparipakvā yā piṣṭī pūrvoktalakṣaṇā tāṃ sūtāt rasāt yantre pātanakarmocite pātayet // GRhtCM_6.8:2 //
children.translated_text: From the morsel (<s>grāsa</s>), i.e., from the conjunction with the devoured substance — the unassimilated pellet (<s>ajīrṇa-piṣṭī</s>), i.e., the pellet that is unassimilated, uncooked, having the previously described characteristics — that should be separated from the mercury by distillation in the appropriate apparatus. // GRhtCM_6.8:2 //

children.text: evaṃ grāsātpṛthakkṛtya patitaḥ svastho nirmalo bhavati // GRhtCM_6.8:3 //
children.translated_text: Having thus separated [the unassimilated pellet] from the morsel, the dropped [mercury] becomes healthy, i.e., pure. // GRhtCM_6.8:3 //

children.text: punargrāsaḥ pakvo vahnitale dattvā pakvaḥ kṛtastaṃ rasendro jaratīti // GRhtCM_6.8:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the morsel, once cooked, i.e., placed over fire and cooked — that the lord of mercury assimilates. // GRhtCM_6.8:4 //
START GRht 6.9
In the swing-apparatus (<s>dolā</s>), four morsels should be assimilated, in due sequence.

children.text: śeṣāḥ kacchapayantre yāvad dviguṇādikaṃ jarati // GRht_6.9 //
children.translated_text: The remaining [morsels] in the tortoise-apparatus (<s>kacchapa-yantra</s>) — until [mercury] assimilates double [its weight] and more. // GRht_6.9 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the apparatus and so forth for morsel-assimilation — 'in the swing' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.9:1 //

children.text: yathākrameṇaiva catuḥṣaṣṭyādinaiva catvāro grāsā dolāyāṃ jāryāḥ śeṣā grāsāścatvāraḥ asaṃkhyā vā kacchapayantre jalayantre ca jāryāḥ // GRhtCM_6.9:2 //
children.translated_text: In due sequence, i.e., by the sixty-four [proportion] and so forth, four morsels should be assimilated in the swing-apparatus; the remaining morsels — four [more], or an unlimited number — should be assimilated in the tortoise-apparatus (<s>kacchapa-yantra</s>), i.e., the water-apparatus. // GRhtCM_6.9:2 //

children.text: śeṣāścatvāraḥ kutaḥ yato 'nyaśāstreṣu aṣṭaiva grāsāḥ // GRhtCM_6.9:3 //
children.translated_text: The remaining four — from where? Because in other treatises, eight morsels are prescribed. // GRhtCM_6.9:3 //

children.text: jāraṇe kimavadhiḥ yāvaddviguṇādikaṃ jarati pāradāddviguṇitaṃ ādiśabdena dviguṇānnyūnaṃ na kāryaṃ adhikamadhikaṃ ca bhavatu // GRhtCM_6.9:4 //
children.translated_text: What is the limit for assimilation? Until [mercury] assimilates double [its weight] and more — double the weight of the mercury. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and so forth), not less than double should be done, but more and more may be [done]. // GRhtCM_6.9:4 //

children.text: śaktyavatare'ṣṭau bṛhacchāstre kvacid aṣṭau grāsā uktāḥ kvacidviṃśatigrāsā iti // GRhtCM_6.9:5 //
children.translated_text: In the chapter on potency-reduction (<s>śaktyavatara</s>), in the major treatise, sometimes eight morsels are prescribed, sometimes twenty morsels. // GRhtCM_6.9:5 //
START GRht 6.10-12

children.text: <Īussere Merkmale des Hg nach jāraṇa einer best. Menge abhra>
children.translated_text: <External characteristics of mercury after assimilation of a certain amount of mica>
At the outset, a fixed quantity-rule for the morsel cannot be established here;

children.text: grasate na hi sarvāṅgaṃ gaganamato lakṣaṇairjñeyam // GRht_6.10 //
children.translated_text: for [mercury] does not devour the entire body of <s>gagana</s> (mica) — therefore, it should be known by external signs. // GRht_6.10 //

children.text: yadi hi catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśān grasati rasastadā dhareddaṇḍam /
children.translated_text: If mercury devours one-sixty-fourth [of its weight], then it holds a rod (<s>daṇḍa-dhara</s>);
upon the entry of a fortieth part, it becomes milk-like (<s>pāyasa-ākāra</s>). // GRht_6.11 //
It becomes leech-shaped (<s>jalaukā-ākāra</s>) from a thirtieth part; and immovable (<s>avipluṣa</s>) from a twentieth;

children.text: chedīva ṣoḍaśāṃśādata ūrdhvaṃ durjaro grāsaḥ // GRht_6.12 //
children.translated_text: cuttable (<s>chedī</s>) from a sixteenth part — and above that, the morsel is difficult to assimilate. // GRht_6.12 //
Showing that the quantity of the morsel is not fixed, he says 'not' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:1 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: atrāsmin śāstre ādau prathamaṃ grāsapramāṇaniyamaḥ kartuṃ na śakyaḥ // GRhtCM_6.10-12:2 //
children.translated_text: In this treatise, at the outset, i.e., initially, a fixed quantity-rule for the morsel cannot be established. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:2 //

children.text: yataḥ kāraṇāt gaganamabhraṃ sarvāṅgaṃ na grasate rasa iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_6.10-12:3 //
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because mercury does not devour the mica entirely, i.e., in its complete form — 'mercury' is the remainder to be supplied. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:3 //
That mica, [whether] entirely devoured or not, should be ascertained by its characteristics alone — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:4 //
He states the form of mercury after devouring from one-sixty-fourth onward — 'if' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:5 //

children.text: yadi cedrasaḥ catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśān pramāṇato grāsaṃ grasati hi niścitaṃ tadā daṇḍaṃ dhārayet vastrānna kṣaratītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.10-12:6 //
children.translated_text: If mercury devours a one-sixty-fourth portion by measure, certainly then it holds a rod, i.e., it does not flow through cloth — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:6 //

children.text: punaścatvāriṃśadbhāgapraveśato rasodare iti śeṣaḥ tadā pāyasākāraḥ kvathitadugdhākāro bhavet nibiḍatvāt // GRhtCM_6.10-12:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, from the entry of a fortieth portion into the mercury's belly — the remainder — then it becomes milk-like (<s>pāyasa-ākāra</s>), i.e., like boiled milk in appearance, due to its density. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:7 //
He elaborates on that — 'becomes' and so forth. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:8 //

children.text: viṃśadbhāgāt triṃśadbhāgasya jāraṇato jalaukākāro bhavet rasa ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_6.10-12:9 //
children.translated_text: From the assimilation of a thirtieth to a twentieth portion, it becomes leech-shaped (<s>jalaukā-ākāra</s>) — 'mercury' is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:9 //

children.text: punaḥ viṃśatyā viṃśadbhāgajāraṇena avipluṣo bhaved āsanānna calati // GRhtCM_6.10-12:10 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, from a twentieth part, i.e., from the assimilation of a twentieth portion, it becomes immovable (<s>avipluṣa</s>), i.e., it does not move from its seat. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:10 //

children.text: punaḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśāt ṣoḍaśāṃśabhāgajāraṇataḥ chedī bhavet kṣurikādibhiḥ chede kṛte pṛthaktvamāpnoti // GRhtCM_6.10-12:11 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, from a sixteenth portion, i.e., from the assimilation of a sixteenth part, it becomes cuttable (<s>chedī</s>), i.e., when cut with a blade and the like, it separates. // GRhtCM_6.10-12:11 //

children.text: ataḥ ṣoḍaśabhāgādūrdhvaṃ grāso durjaro bhavet // GRhtCM_6.10-12:12 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, a swallowing (<s>grāsa</s>) beyond the sixteenth part becomes difficult to digest. || GRhtCM 6.10-12:12 ||
START GRht 6.13
Having digested the dense essence (<s>ghana-satva</s>) first with these five swallowings,

children.text: garbhadrāve nipuṇo jārayati bījaṃ kalāṃśena // GRht_6.13 //
children.translated_text: one skilled in womb-melting (<s>garbhadrāva</s>) digests the seed (<s>bīja</s>) in fractional portions (<s>kalāṃśa</s>). || GRht 6.13 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
That he states, saying 'with five' and so forth. || GRhtCM 6.13:1 ||

children.text: evaṃ uktaprakāreṇa punargarbhadrāve nipuṇaḥ rasodare abhradhātvādīnāṃ drutikaraṇe pravīṇaḥ pumān kalāṃśena grāsaṃ yojayet // GRhtCM_6.13:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the method described, a person skilled in womb-melting (<s>garbhadrāva</s>), i.e., proficient in causing the melting of mica, metals, and such in the interior of mercury, should apply the swallowing in fractional portions (<s>kalāṃśa</s>). || GRhtCM 6.13:2 ||

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā pañcabhiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ grāsaiścāru yathā syāttathā ghanasatvamādau jārayitvā pañcabhirgrāsair ghanasatvajāraṇānantaraṃ ṣoḍaśabhāgena bījaṃ jārayedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.13:3 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having first digested the dense essence with the five previously mentioned swallowings, in such a way that it becomes beautiful — after the digestion of the dense essence with the five swallowings, one should then digest the seed in sixteenth portions — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 6.13:3 ||
START GRht 6.14-15

children.text: <Ōnderung von phys. Eig. von Hg nach jāraṇa>
children.translated_text: <Change of physical properties of mercury after <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion)>
Smoky, making a crackling (<s>ciṭiciṭi</s>) sound, [moving with] a frog-like gait, and trembling,
[then] becoming still — the mercury should be known as mica-digested. || GRht 6.14 ||

children.text: kapilo'tha nirudgārī vipluṣabhāvaṃ ca muñcate sūtaḥ /
