children.translated_text: Tawny (<s>kapila</s>), then without emission (<s>nirudgārī</s>), and giving up the state of droplets (<s>vipluṣa</s>),
motionless, devoid of movement — it should be known as mica-digested. || GRht 6.15 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the characteristics of mica-digested mercury, saying 'smoky' and so forth. || GRhtCM 6.14-15:1 ||

children.text: abhrajīrṇarasa evaṃvidho bhavati abhraṃ jīrṇaṃ yasmin sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_6.14-15:2 //
children.translated_text: Mica-digested mercury is of such a character — that in which mica has been digested is so called. || GRhtCM 6.14-15:2 ||

children.text: vahniyogāt prathamaṃ dhūmro dhūmrābho bhavati punaściṭiciṭiśabdo bhavati tato maṇḍūkagatirbhavati punastathā tena prakāreṇa dhṛte sati sakampo bhavati punarvahnau niṣkampaḥ svastho bhavati abhrasatvadrutasya lakṣaṇamiti // GRhtCM_6.14-15:3 //
children.translated_text: From conjunction with fire: first it becomes smoky (<s>dhūmra</s>), of smoke-like hue; then it makes a crackling (<s>ciṭiciṭi</s>) sound; then it develops a frog-like gait; furthermore, in that manner, when held [in fire], it becomes trembling; then again in fire, it becomes still (<s>niṣkampa</s>), i.e., stable — this is the characteristic of [mercury in which] the mica-essence has been melted. || GRhtCM 6.14-15:3 ||
That itself he states, saying 'tawny' and so forth. || GRhtCM 6.14-15:4 ||
Furthermore, mercury of such character should be known as mica-digested. || GRhtCM 6.14-15:5 ||

children.text: kīdṛśaḥ kapilaḥ varṇataḥ nirudgārī sthirabhāvaḥ punaḥ sa raso vipluṣabhāvaṃ cañcalatvaṃ muñcate // GRhtCM_6.14-15:6 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? Tawny (<s>kapila</s>) in color; without emission (<s>nirudgārī</s>), i.e., of stable nature; furthermore, that mercury gives up the state of droplets (<s>vipluṣa-bhāva</s>), i.e., [gives up] instability. || GRhtCM 6.14-15:6 ||

children.text: punarniṣkampaḥ svasthaḥ punargatirahitaḥ pakṣacchinnaḥ iti lakṣaṇānyabhrajīrṇasya bhavanti // GRhtCM_6.14-15:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, motionless (<s>niṣkampa</s>), i.e., stable; furthermore, devoid of movement (<s>gatirahita</s>), i.e., with wings clipped — these are the characteristics of mica-digested [mercury]. || GRhtCM 6.14-15:7 ||
START GRht 6.16-18
<s>kacchapayantra</s> (tortoise apparatus)>
In the midst of a water-filled vessel, having placed a wide earthen shard (<s>ghaṭakharpara</s>),

children.text: tadupari madhyagataḥ sūtaḥ sthāpyastataḥ kuḍye // GRht_6.16 //
children.translated_text: upon that, the mercury, placed in the center, [should be set]; then in a furnace (<s>kuḍya</s>). || GRht 6.16 ||
Having covered with a light iron saucer, sealed with cloth-and-clay joint-coating,
that earthen shard, filled to the brim, with charcoals mixed with cow-dung and husks; || GRht 6.17 ||
through sweating and grinding, the mercury stationed in the tortoise apparatus (<s>kacchapayantra</s>) digests [the swallowed substance];
then, by the force of fire alone, womb-melting (<s>garbhadruti</s>) of all metals [occurs]. || GRht 6.18 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He describes the tortoise apparatus, saying 'water' and so forth. || GRhtCM 6.16-18:1 ||

children.text: jalapūrṇapātramadhye iti jalapūrṇaṃ yatpātraṃ tasya madhye suvistīrṇaṃ sundarāyataṃ ghaṭakharparaṃ kumbhakhaṇḍaṃ dattvā tadupari kharparopari biḍamadhyagataḥ sūtaḥ sthāpyaḥ // GRhtCM_6.16-18:2 //
children.translated_text: 'In the midst of a water-filled vessel' — in the middle of a vessel that is full of water, having placed a well-extended, broad earthen shard (<s>ghaṭakharpara</s>), i.e., a pot-fragment — upon that, above the shard, the mercury, located in the center with <s>viḍa</s> (acid-treated substance), should be placed. || GRhtCM 6.16-18:2 ||

children.text: kutra kuḍye mṛdā vinirmite viśālamukhe laghulohakaṭorikayā atilaghvī yā lohasya muṇḍādeḥ kaṭorikā pātraviśeṣaḥ tayā viḍāvṛtaṃ sūtaṃ ācchādya ā samantāt saṃrudhya // GRhtCM_6.16-18:3 //
children.translated_text: Where? In a furnace (<s>kuḍya</s>), made of clay, with a wide mouth — with a light iron saucer, i.e., a very light saucer of <s>muṇḍa</s> (cast iron) or similar metal, a particular vessel — having covered, i.e., enclosed on all sides, the mercury wrapped in <s>viḍa</s>. || GRhtCM 6.16-18:3 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭayā kṛtapaṭamṛtsandhilepayā kṛtaḥ paṭamṛdbhyāṃ sandherlepo rodho yasyāḥ sā tayā // GRhtCM_6.16-18:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what character [is the saucer]? 'With cloth-and-clay joint-coating made' — that in which the sealing of the joint has been made with cloth and clay — with such [a saucer]. || GRhtCM 6.16-18:4 ||

children.text: punastatkuḍyāntargataghaṭakharparaṃ aṅgāraiḥ pūrṇaṃ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ karīṣatuṣamiśraiḥ karīṣo gomayasya cūrṇaṃ tuṣāḥ śālyāderdhānyasya tair miśritairiti // GRhtCM_6.16-18:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that earthen shard within the furnace, filled with charcoals — of what character? Mixed with cow-dung and husks — <s>karīṣa</s> is the powder of cow-dung, <s>tuṣa</s> are the husks of rice and such grain — mixed with those. || GRhtCM 6.16-18:5 ||

children.text: kacchapayantre yadvihitaṃ tadāha svedanata ityādi // GRhtCM_6.16-18:6 //
children.translated_text: What is accomplished in the tortoise apparatus, that he states, saying 'through sweating' and so forth. || GRhtCM 6.16-18:6 ||

children.text: kacchapayantrastho raso jarati grāsaṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_6.16-18:7 //
children.translated_text: The mercury stationed in the tortoise apparatus digests — the swallowed substance — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 6.16-18:7 ||
From what? Through sweating (<s>svedana</s>), i.e., through heating in fire. || GRhtCM 6.16-18:8 ||

children.text: na kevalaṃ svedanato mardanataśca viḍādinā ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_6.16-18:9 //
children.translated_text: Not only through sweating, but also through grinding — with <s>viḍa</s> and such — this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 6.16-18:9 ||

children.text: tato 'gnibalenaiva sarvalohānāṃ svarṇādīnāṃ asminnantarāle garbhadrutirbhavati atrāgnibalameva mukhyaṃ // GRhtCM_6.16-18:10 //
children.translated_text: Then, by the force of fire alone, the womb-melting of all metals — gold and such — occurs in this interval. Here, the force of fire alone is paramount. || GRhtCM 6.16-18:10 ||
START GRht 6.19

children.text: evaṃ dattvā jīryati na kṣayati raso yathā tathā kāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus added [the swallowed substance], the mercury digests [it] — the procedure should be done so that the mercury does not diminish;
it diminishes through alkalis and <s>viḍas</s>; but with <s>uparasas</s> (semi-metals), it belches forth the swallowed substance. || GRht 6.19 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the twofold procedure in digestion, saying 'thus' and so forth. || GRhtCM 6.19:1 ||

children.text: evamamunā prakāreṇa kacchapayantre nidhāya jīryati grāsaṃ rasa iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_6.19:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method, having placed [the substance] in the tortoise apparatus, the mercury digests — the swallowed substance — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 6.19:2 ||

children.text: yathā raso na kṣayati kṣayaṃ nāpnoti tathā kāryo vidhiḥ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_6.19:3 //
children.translated_text: The procedure should be done in such a way that the mercury does not diminish, i.e., does not attain diminution — the procedure — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 6.19:3 ||
For the protection of the substrate of the operation — such is the purport. || GRhtCM 6.19:4 ||

children.text: punaḥ kṣārabiḍaiḥ kṣayameti nāśamāpnoti grāsa ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_6.19:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, through alkalis and <s>viḍas</s>, [the swallowed substance] diminishes, i.e., reaches destruction — the swallowed substance — this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 6.19:5 ||

children.text: punaḥ sa rasa uparasairgandhādibhiḥ grāsaṃ utprāvalyena girati gilatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.19:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that mercury, with <s>uparasas</s> such as sulphur and the like, belches forth (<s>girati</s>) the swallowed substance with force — meaning it swallows [again]. || GRhtCM 6.19:6 ||
With alkalis, acids, sulphur and such, urines, and pungent [substances] indeed —
for the purpose of digesting the mercury's swallowed substance, <s>viḍa</s> is so proclaimed.
Thus the technical definition (<s>paribhāṣā</s>). || GRhtCM 6.19:7 ||
By the word '<s>viḍa</s>', a bolus (<s>piṇḍa</s>) [is meant]. || GRhtCM 6.19:8 ||
START GRht 7.1
<s>viḍa</s>: positive effects>

children.text: grāsaṃ na muñcati na vāñchati taṃ ca bhūyaḥ kāṃścidguṇānbhajati bhuktavibhuktimātrāt /
children.translated_text: [Mercury] does not release the swallowed substance, nor does it desire another [substance] again; it acquires certain qualities merely from the act of swallowing and digesting;

children.text: yajjīryate pracurakevalavahniyogāt tasmādviḍaiḥ suniviḍaiḥ saha jāraṇā syāt // GRht_7.1 //
children.translated_text: since it is digested by the conjunction of abundant pure fire alone, therefore digestion (<s>jāraṇā</s>) should be performed with well-compact <s>viḍas</s>. || GRht 7.1 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the ease of digestion with <s>viḍas</s>, saying 'the swallowed substance' and so forth. || GRhtCM 7.1:1 ||

children.text: grāsaṃ na muñcati ca punastam evānyagrāsaṃ na vāñchati bhūyaḥ punaḥ bhuktavibhuktimātrāt kāṃścidguṇān nityaṃ bhajati dadhāti grāsagrasanamātrāt guṇaṃ karotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_7.1:2 //
children.translated_text: [Mercury] does not release the swallowed substance, and furthermore does not desire another swallowed substance again. Furthermore, merely from the act of swallowing and digesting, it always acquires certain qualities, i.e., produces [good] qualities merely from the swallowing of the swallowed substance — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 7.1:2 ||

children.text: yato hetorbiḍairvakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇaiḥ kṛtvā jīryate grāsamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_7.1:3 //
children.translated_text: Since, by reason of the <s>viḍas</s> whose characteristics will be described, [mercury] digests — the swallowed substance — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 7.1:3 ||

children.text: kutaḥ pracurakevalavahniyogāt pracura udagro yaḥ kevalavahniyogaḥ śuddhāgniyogastasmāt // GRhtCM_7.1:4 //
children.translated_text: From what? From the conjunction of abundant pure fire — <s>pracura</s> means intense; the conjunction of pure fire alone — from that. || GRhtCM 7.1:4 ||
Of what character [are the <s>viḍas</s>]? Well-compact (<s>sunibiḍa</s>), i.e., dense. || GRhtCM 7.1:5 ||

children.text: yato biḍāḥ śreṣṭhās tasmādviḍair eva jāraṇā syāt sugamatvāditi bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_7.1:6 //
children.translated_text: Since <s>viḍas</s> are excellent, therefore digestion should be performed with <s>viḍas</s> alone — because of the ease — such is the purport. || GRhtCM 7.1:6 ||
START GRht 7.2
<s>viḍa</s>: for digestion of copper leaves>
With <s>viḍas</s> [made of] <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt), the three pungents (<s>kaṭukatraya</s>), <s>kākṣī</s> (Saurashtra earth), <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), and sulphur,
soaked a hundred times in the juice of <s>śigru</s> (drumstick tree) — [mercury] digests even copper leaves. || GRht 7.2 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for <s>viḍa</s>, saying '<s>sauvarcala</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 7.2:1 ||

children.text: tāmradalānyapi jārayati buddhimān iti śeṣaḥ svarṇabījādīnāṃ kā katheti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_7.2:2 //
children.translated_text: An intelligent person [causes mercury to] digest even copper leaves — this is the remainder. What to speak then of gold-seed and such — this is the purport. || GRhtCM 7.2:2 ||
With what? With <s>viḍas</s>. || GRhtCM 7.2:3 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭair biḍaiḥ sauvarcalakaṭukatrayakāṃkṣīkāsīsagandhakaiḥ sauvarcalaṃ rucakaṃ kaṭutrayaṃ śuṇṭhīmaricapippalyātmakaṃ kākṣī saurāṣṭrī kāsīsaṃ puṣpakāsīsaṃ gandhakaṃ lelitakaṃ etānyauṣadhāni yeṣu viḍeṣu santi te tathoktāḥ taiḥ // GRhtCM_7.2:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what character are the <s>viḍas</s>? [Containing] <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt), the three pungents (<s>kaṭukatraya</s>) — consisting of dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>), black pepper (<s>marica</s>), and long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>) — <s>kākṣī</s>, which is Saurashtra earth — <s>kāsīsa</s>, which is flower-vitriol — sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), which is <s>lelitaka</s> — those <s>viḍas</s> in which these medicinal substances are present are so called — with those. || GRhtCM 7.2:4 ||

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ śigro rasaśatabhāvyaiḥ śigroḥ saubhāñjanasya rasena śatavāraṃ bhāvyāḥ ye biḍāstaiḥ evaṃ niṣpannairviḍairniścitaṃ jāraṇā syāditi bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_7.2:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what character? 'Soaked a hundred times in the juice of <s>śigru</s>' — those <s>viḍas</s> soaked a hundred times with the juice of <s>śigru</s>, i.e., the <s>saubhāñjana</s> (Moringa) tree — with such well-prepared <s>viḍas</s>, the digestion will certainly occur — such is the purport. || GRhtCM 7.2:5 ||
START GRht 7.3
<s>viḍa</s>: for digestion of gold>
The ash of radish (<s>mūlaka</s>) burnt with all its parts, filtered with fragrant cow-urine,

children.text: śatabhāvyaṃ balivasayā tatkṣaṇato jāryate hema // GRht_7.3 //
children.translated_text: soaked a hundred times with potent fat (<s>bali-vasā</s>) — from that very instant, gold is digested. || GRht 7.3 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another <s>viḍa</s>, saying 'all' and so forth. || GRhtCM 7.3:1 ||

children.text: sarvāṅgadagdhamūlakabhasma pratigālitamiti sarvāṅgena mūlatvakpatrapuṣpaphalena saha dagdhaṃ bhasmatāṃ prāptaṃ yanmūlakakandaṃ tadbhasma surabhimūtreṇa gojalena gālitaṃ kāryaṃ kṣāro grāhya ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_7.3:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Ash of radish burnt with all its parts and filtered' — the radish root, burnt with all its parts (root, bark, leaves, flowers, and fruits), having attained the state of ash — that ash should be filtered, i.e., strained, with fragrant cow-urine, i.e., with cow-water — the alkali should be taken — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 7.3:2 ||

children.text: punarbalivasayā balamukhyā yā jalaukā maṇḍūkādīnāṃ vasā yathā ca /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with 'potent fat' (<s>bali-vasā</s>), i.e., the principal [one being] the fat of aquatic creatures such as leeches, frogs, and the like. As the verse states:
The fat of frogs, fish, or of roosters,

children.text: bhāvyam ebhiḥ kramādgandhaṃ śiśumāravasāpi vā // GRhtCM_7.3:3 //
children.translated_text: or the fat of the crocodile (<s>śiśumāra</s>) — sulphur should be soaked with these in sequence. || GRhtCM 7.3:3 ||

children.text: ekā balivasā samyak sūtasya bandhinī param /
children.translated_text: A single [application of] potent fat is the supreme binder of mercury;
and it also produces coloring (<s>rañjana</s>), by the procedure of the crucible (<s>maṇimūṣā</s>) method.
Thus. || GRhtCM 7.3:4 ||

children.text: balivasayā śataṃ śatavāraṃ kṣārabhūtaṃ bhasma bhāvyaṃ punaḥ tacchatabhāvyam auṣadhaṃ tatkṣaṇataḥ tatkālato hema svarṇaṃ jāryate raso grāsabhūtaṃ hema jaratīti biḍayogāditi bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_7.3:5 //
children.translated_text: With potent fat, the ash that has become alkali should be soaked a hundred times (<s>śata</s>) — furthermore, with that hundred-times-soaked medicine, from that very instant, gold is digested — the mercury digests gold that has become the swallowed substance — by means of the <s>viḍa</s> application — such is the purport. || GRhtCM 7.3:5 ||
START GRht 7.4-7
<s>viḍa</s>: for digestion>

Banana (<s>kadalī</s>), <s>palāśa</s> (Butea), sesame (<s>tila</s>), <s>nicula</s> (Barringtonia), datura (<s>kanaka</s>), <s>suradālī</s> (Devadālī), <s>vāstuka</s> (Chenopodium), and castor (<s>eraṇḍa</s>);
together with <s>varṣābhū</s> (Boerhavia), <s>vṛṣa</s> (Adhatoda), and <s>mokṣaka</s> — the alkali [should be made] as available. || GRht 7.4 ||

children.text: ānīya kṣāravṛkṣān kusumaphalaśiphātvakpravālairupetān kṛtvātaḥ khaṇḍaśastān vipulataraśilāpiṣṭagātrātiśuṣkān /
children.translated_text: Having brought the alkali-trees, equipped with flowers, fruits, roots, bark, and tender shoots, having cut them into pieces, their bodies well-ground on broad stones and thoroughly dried,

children.text: dagdhvā kāṇḍaistilānāṃ karisurabhihayāmbhobhir āsrāvya vastrair bhasma tyaktvā jalaṃ tanmṛduśikhini pacedvaṃśapākena bhūyaḥ // GRht_7.5 //
children.translated_text: having burnt them with sesame stalks, having filtered with cow-urine and horse-water through cloths, discarding the ash, one should cook the liquid on a gentle fire with the bamboo-cooking method again. || GRht 7.5 ||

children.text: tacchuṣyamāṇaṃ hi sabāṣpabudbudān yadā vidhatte kṣaṇabhaṅgurān bahūn /
children.translated_text: When that, while drying, produces many momentary bubbles with steam,

children.text: tadā kṣipettryūṣaṇahiṃgugandhakaṃ kṣāratrayaṃ ṣaḍlavaṇāni bhūkhagau // GRht_7.6 //
children.translated_text: then one should add the three pungents (<s>tryūṣaṇa</s>), asafoetida (<s>hiṅgu</s>), sulphur, the three alkalis (<s>kṣāratraya</s>), the six salts (<s>ṣaḍlavaṇa</s>), and <s>bhūkhaga</s> (earth and sky [substances]). || GRht 7.6 ||

children.text: dravyāṇi saṃmiśrya nivṛtya bhūtale vyavasthitaṃ śastrakaṭorikāpuṭe /
children.translated_text: Having mixed the substances, removing [the vessel from fire], and placing it on the ground,
one should store [the <s>viḍa</s>] in a steel saucer-<s>puṭa</s> for seven days in grain; it should be employed for the digestion of mercury and such. || GRht 7.7 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the specific alkali-trees, shrubs, and medicinal plants, saying 'banana' and so forth. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:1 ||

children.text: yathālābhaṃ lābham anatikramya eṣāṃ kṣāraḥ kartavyaḥ // GRhtCM_7.4-7:2 //
children.translated_text: 'As available' — not exceeding availability — the alkali of these should be made. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:2 ||

children.text: te ke kadalīpalāśatilaniculakanakasuradālivāstukairaṇḍāḥ kadalī rambhā palāśo brahmavṛkṣaḥ tilāḥ pratītāḥ niculo vetasavṛkṣaḥ kanako dhattūraḥ suradālī devadālī vāstukaṃ kṣāraśākaṃ eraṇḍo vātāriḥ ete kṣārasaṃbhavāḥ // GRhtCM_7.4-7:3 //
children.translated_text: Who are they? Banana (<s>kadalī</s>), i.e., the plantain; <s>palāśa</s>, i.e., the <s>Brahmavṛkṣa</s> (Butea frondosa); sesame (<s>tila</s>), well-known; <s>nicula</s>, i.e., the <s>vetasa</s>-tree (willow-like); <s>kanaka</s>, i.e., datura (<s>dhattūra</s>); <s>suradālī</s>, i.e., <s>devadālī</s>; <s>vāstuka</s>, i.e., the alkali-herb (Chenopodium); castor (<s>eraṇḍa</s>), i.e., <s>vātāri</s> — these are the sources of alkali. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:3 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭā ete varṣābhūvṛṣamokṣakasahitāḥ varṣābhūḥ punarnavā vṛṣo vāsakaḥ mokṣako mokhāvṛkṣa iti pratītaḥ etaiḥ saṃyutā ityuddeśaḥ // GRhtCM_7.4-7:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what character are these? 'Together with <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, and <s>mokṣaka</s>' — <s>varṣābhū</s> is <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia diffusa); <s>vṛṣa</s> is <s>vāsaka</s> (Adhatoda vasica); <s>mokṣaka</s> is known as the <s>mokhā</s>-tree — combined with these — thus the enumeration. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:4 ||
He states the procedure for making the alkali, saying 'having brought' and so forth. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:5 ||

children.text: prathamaṃ kṣāravṛkṣān pūrvoktān ānīya vanāntarādgṛhītvā // GRhtCM_7.4-7:6 //
children.translated_text: First, having brought, i.e., having obtained from the forest, the previously mentioned alkali-trees. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:6 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭān kusumaphalaśiphātvakpalāśairupetān kusumāni prasūnāni pratītāni śiphā mūlaṃ tvaktvacā pravālā nūtanapallavāḥ etaiḥ pañcāṅgāhvayair upetān saṃyutān // GRhtCM_7.4-7:7 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? Equipped with flowers, fruits, roots (<s>śiphā</s>), bark (<s>tvak</s>), and leaves (<s>palāśa</s>) — <s>kusuma</s> means blossoms, well-known; <s>śiphā</s> means root; <s>tvak</s> means bark; <s>pravāla</s> means fresh shoots — equipped with these, called the five parts (<s>pañcāṅga</s>), meaning combined [with them]. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:7 ||
Having cut into pieces — making many fragments. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:8 ||

children.text: na kevalaṃ khaṇḍaśaḥ vipulataraśilāpiṣṭagātrātiśuṣkān kṛtvā vipulatarā ativistīrṇā yā śilā tasyāṃ piṣṭāni gātrāṇi yeṣāṃ te'śuṣkā nirasāḥ tānevaṃvidhān kṛtvā // GRhtCM_7.4-7:9 //
children.translated_text: Not merely into pieces — having made them with limbs ground on a very broad stone and thoroughly dried — ground on a very extensive stone, whose limbs are powdered, [and made] juiceless — having made them in such a condition. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:9 ||

children.text: punastāneva ca tilānāṃ kāṇḍairnālaiḥ saha dagdhvā // GRhtCM_7.4-7:10 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, having burned those same [plants] together with the stalks of sesame. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:10 ||

children.text: punaḥ karisurabhihayāmbhobhiḥ hastigo'śvānāṃ mūtrairāsrāvya āplutya tadbhasma tyaktvā vastrair jalaṃ grāhyamiti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_7.4-7:11 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with the urines of cows and horses (<s>kari-surabhi-hayāmbhas</s>) — the urines of elephants, cows, and horses — having washed [the ash]; that ash is to be discarded, and the water [filtrate] should be collected through cloth: this is the completion. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:11 ||

children.text: tajjalaṃ mṛduśikhini komalāgnau pacet kena vaṃśapākena vaṃśānāṃ samavahnitvāt // GRhtCM_7.4-7:12 //
children.translated_text: That water should be cooked over a gentle fire (<s>mṛduśikhi</s>), a mild flame — by what [method]? By the bamboo-cooking method (<s>vaṃśapāka</s>), due to bamboo having an even heat. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:12 ||
He states the characteristic of the cooking of alkali-water, beginning with 'that' and so forth. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:13 ||

children.text: tajjalaṃ kṣārapānīyaṃ śuṣyamāṇaṃ sat niścitaṃ yadā sabāṣpabudbudān vidhatte saha bāṣpeṇa jalātyayadhūmena vartante ye budbudāstān tadā kṣāro niṣpanno jñeyaḥ // GRhtCM_7.4-7:14 //
children.translated_text: That water — the alkali-water — when it is drying, certainly, when it produces bubbles with steam — when bubbles that exist together with steam, the smoke of water's departure — then the alkali should be known as prepared. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:14 ||

children.text: punastadā tryūṣaṇaṃ śuṇṭhīmaricapippalyaḥ hiṅgu rāmaṭhaṃ gandhakaṃ lelītakaṃ punaḥ kṣāratrayaṃ sarjikāyavāgrajaṭaṅkaṇāhvayaṃ lavaṇāni ṣaṭ saindhavādīni bhūḥ tuvarī khagaṃ kāsīsaṃ etāni kṣipet etatkṣāreṇārdreṇa saha miśraṃ kāryamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_7.4-7:15 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, at that point [add]: <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> (the three pungents) — dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>), black pepper (<s>marica</s>), and long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>); asafoetida (<s>hiṅgu</s>); <s>rāmaṭha</s>; sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>); <s>lelītaka</s>; furthermore the three alkalis (<s>kṣāratraya</s>) — called <s>sarjikā</s> (natron), barley-alkali (<s>yavāgraja</s>), and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>); the six salts beginning with rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>); <s>bhūḥ</s> meaning <s>tuvarī</s> (a type of legume); <s>khaga</s> meaning green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>) — these should be added; meaning they should be mixed together with this still-moist alkali: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:15 ||

children.text: tathā ca dravyāṇi tryūṣaṇādīni saṃmiśrya ekīkṛtya nivṛtya ca saṃmardya śastrakaṭorikāpuṭe lohamayapātrasaṃpuṭe vyavasthitaṃ saptadināni dhānyagataṃ kasyaciddhānyasya madhyagataṃ sthāpayet kutra bhūtale pṛthivyā āsthāne tato'nantaraṃ tatsiddhaṃ rasajāraṇādikaṃ prati prayojyaṃ etadbiḍarūpaṃ rasajāraṇādiṣu praśastamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_7.4-7:16 //
children.translated_text: And thus, having mixed the substances beginning with the three pungents, having unified them, and then having ground them thoroughly, it should be placed in a sealed metal vessel (<s>śastrakaṭorikāpuṭa</s>) — an enclosed metal container — established [therein], for seven days, placed within some grain — stored in the middle of some grain — where? On the ground, at a place on the earth. Thereafter, that perfected [<s>viḍa</s>] is to be employed for assimilation of mercury and such purposes. This <s>viḍa</s>-form [preparation] is excellent for mercury-assimilation and other [operations]: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 7.4-7:16 ||
[START GRht 7.8]
<<s>Viḍa</s>: for <s>garbhadruti</s>>
From the combination of lemon (<s>jambīra</s>), citron (<s>bījapūra</s>), sorrel (<s>cāṅgerī</s>), and cane-sour (<s>vetasāmla</s>),

children.text: kṣārā bhavanti nitarāṃ garbhadrutijāraṇe śastāḥ // GRht_7.8 //
children.translated_text: alkalis that are exceedingly excellent for <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) and <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) are produced. || GRht 7.8 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the alkali-procedure for assimilation, beginning with '<s>jambīra</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 7.8:1 ||

children.text: kṣārā uktavṛkṣodbhavāḥ nitarām atiśayena garbhadrutijāraṇe rasāntargrāsajāraṇe śastā utkṛṣṭā bhavanti // GRhtCM_7.8:2 //
children.translated_text: Alkalis produced from the stated trees are exceedingly — supremely — excellent in <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) and <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) — meaning assimilation within mercury's womb. || GRhtCM 7.8:2 ||

children.text: kutaḥ jambīrabījapūrakacāṅgerīvetasāmlasaṃyogāt jambīraḥ pratītaḥ bījapūrako mātuluṅgaḥ cāṅgerī amlapatrikā vetasāmlaṃ cukrakaṃ eṣāṃ yo rasastasya saṃyogāt etairbhāvitāḥ kṣārā biḍavatkāryakarā iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_7.8:3 //
children.translated_text: From what? From the combination of lemon, citron (<s>bījapūraka</s>, i.e., <s>mātuluṅga</s>), sorrel (<s>cāṅgerī</s>, i.e., <s>amlapatrikā</s>), and cane-sour (<s>vetasāmla</s>, i.e., <s>cukraka</s>); from the juice of these, by combination [with the alkalis]; alkalis treated with these are efficacious like <s>viḍa</s>: this is the purport. || GRhtCM 7.8:3 ||
[START GRht 7.9]
<<s>Viḍa</s>: how to use>
Having placed <s>viḍa</s> above and below at the outset, with one-eighth the [quantity of] mercury,
one should perform <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation); thus, step by step, one should increase the fire. || GRht 7.9 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the application of <s>viḍa</s> to mercury, beginning with '<s>viḍa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 7.9:1 ||

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ sūtasya rasasyāṣṭamāṃśena pūrvanirmitaṃ viḍaṃ adharottaraṃ adha uparibhāgaṃ ca dattvā evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa jāraṇaṃ kuryāt punaḥ kramyate aneneti kramo biḍarūpaḥ tatkramaḥ paraṃparā tasmāt agniṃ vivardhayet karmakṛt ityadhyāhāraḥ vāraṃvāraṃ biḍasaṃprayogādagnirvardhate // GRhtCM_7.9:2 //
children.translated_text: At the outset — first — with one-eighth the quantity of mercury, having placed the previously prepared <s>viḍa</s> above and below — on the lower and upper portions — by this method, one should perform <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation). Furthermore, the <s>viḍa</s>-form is the step-by-step procedure (<s>krama</s>); from that step-by-step progression, the practitioner should increase the fire — this is to be understood. With each repeated application of <s>viḍa</s>, the fire increases. || GRhtCM 7.9:2 ||
[START GRht 8.1-2]
<<s>Rañjana</s> (coloring): color according to mica type>
Mercury that has assimilated mica (<s>jīrṇābhraka</s>) displays a hue corresponding to the mica —

children.text: kṛṣṇāṃ raktāṃ pītāṃ sitāṃ tathā saṃkarairmiśrām // GRht_8.1 //
children.translated_text: black, red, yellow, white, and likewise mixed [hues] from combinations. || GRht 8.1 ||
With black mica, the lord of mercury is united with strong dark colors;

children.text: śvetai raktaiḥ pītairvahneḥ khalu varṇato jñeyaḥ // GRht_8.2 //
children.translated_text: with white, red, or yellow [micas] — it should be known by the color, indeed according to the fire. || GRht 8.2 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
The moon shines in the sky with brilliance when mica is assimilated;

children.text: tatheha tāmupāśritya śālate manujeṣu ca // GRhtCM_8.1-2:1 //
children.translated_text: likewise, here [on earth], having resorted to that [brilliance], it excels among humans. || GRhtCM 8.1-2:1 ||
Through the assimilation of well-perfected <s>viḍa</s>, metals, and other [substances] into mercury,
the production of yellow and other colors is called <s>rañjana</s> (coloring).
Thus the definition. || GRhtCM 8.1-2:2 ||

children.text: abhrasya chāyāviśeṣam āha jīrṇābhraka ityādi // GRhtCM_8.1-2:3 //
children.translated_text: He states the particular hue-differences of mica, beginning with '<s>jīrṇābhraka</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 8.1-2:3 ||

children.text: rasendro yadā jīrṇābhro bhavati tadā ghanānurūpiṇīṃ jīrṇābhrasamavarṇāṃ chāyāṃ darśayati // GRhtCM_8.1-2:4 //
children.translated_text: When the lord of mercury has assimilated mica (<s>jīrṇābhra</s>), then it displays a hue corresponding to the mica — a color matching the assimilated mica. || GRhtCM 8.1-2:4 ||

children.text: kṛṣṇe jīrṇe kṛṣṇāṃ rakte'bhre jīrṇe raktāṃ pīte pītāṃ tathā site śubhre sitāṃ evaṃ caturvidhāṃ chāyāṃ darśayati // GRhtCM_8.1-2:5 //
children.translated_text: When black [mica] is assimilated, [it shows] a black [hue]; when red mica is assimilated, a red [hue]; with yellow, a yellow [hue]; likewise with white, a white [hue] — thus it displays a fourfold hue. || GRhtCM 8.1-2:5 ||

children.text: punardvayostrayāṇāṃ vā caturṇāṃ saṃkare melāpe sati dvitricaturṇām anurūpiṇīṃ chāyāṃ darśayatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.1-2:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, when there is a mixture (<s>saṅkara</s>) — a blending — of two, three, or four [types], it displays a hue corresponding to the two, three, or four: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 8.1-2:6 ||
He states the particular color-differences arising from mica-combination, beginning with '<s>kṛṣṇa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 8.1-2:7 ||

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakeṇa jīrṇena raso balavān bhavet tu punaḥ asitarāgaiḥ kṛṣṇarāgairyujyate // GRhtCM_8.1-2:8 //
children.translated_text: With black mica, when assimilated, mercury becomes powerful; and furthermore, it is united with dark colors — black colors. || GRhtCM 8.1-2:8 ||

children.text: tathā śvetena śvetai rāgair yujyate raktena raktaiḥ pītena pītaiḥ kapilāgnerdivyasyāpi sarvasyādarśanarūpaṃ kṣayakarasya balairdravyāṇāṃ tādṛśo varṇo rasavarṇato varṇakovidairjñeyaḥ // GRhtCM_8.1-2:9 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, with white [mica], it is united with white colors; with red, with red colors; with yellow, with yellow colors. By the tawny fire (<s>kapilāgni</s>) — the divine [fire] that destroys all, including the invisible — such a color in mercury should be known by those expert in colors, according to the color of [the resulting] mercury. || GRhtCM 8.1-2:9 ||
[START GRht 8.3]

children.text: <mercury transfers own colour on other substances>
children.translated_text: <Mercury transfers its own color onto other substances>

children.text: atha nijakarme varṇaṃ na jahāti yadā sa rajyate rāgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, in its own operation, it does not abandon the color; when it is colored with [particular] hues,

children.text: kramaśo hi vakṣyamāṇairnirṇikto raṃjanaṃ kurute // GRht_8.3 //
children.translated_text: step by step, indeed, by those [hues] to be described, when properly cleansed, it effects coloring [of other substances]. || GRht 8.3 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the praise of colored mercury, beginning with 'now' and so forth. || GRhtCM 8.3:1 ||

children.text: athānantaraṃ rasaḥ rasendro yadā vakṣyamāṇaiḥ śvetādibhiḥ rāgaiḥ rajyate tadā nijakarme varṇaṃ svakīyameva svābhāvikaṃ rūpaṃ na jahāti na tyajati punastaireva rāgaiḥ nirṇikto raktaḥ san rañjanaṃ kurute rāgadāyī bhavatīti // GRhtCM_8.3:2 //
children.translated_text: Then, thereafter, when the lord of mercury is colored by the hues to be described — white and such — then in its own operation it does not abandon its color, does not give up its own natural form. Furthermore, colored — dyed — by those very hues, it effects coloring — becomes a giver of color. || GRhtCM 8.3:2 ||

children.text: tathā no rakto na rañjanaṃ kurute avidyamānatvānniṣedhaḥ // GRhtCM_8.3:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus, [mercury that is] not colored does not effect coloring — the negation is due to its non-existence [in that state]. || GRhtCM 8.3:3 ||
[START GRht 8.4]
<Substances that induce various <s>saṃskāras</s>>
Strength resides in mica-essence; <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) and <s>rāga</s> (coloring) are established in steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>);
binding (<s>bandha</s>) [resides] in pure iron (<s>sāraloha</s>); and <s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing) [resides] in lead and tin. || GRht 8.4 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: abhrasatvādīnāṃ yoge rase vyavasthāmāha balamityādi // GRhtCM_8.4:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the established role of mica-essence and other [substances] when combined with mercury, beginning with 'strength' and so forth. || GRhtCM 8.4:1 ||

children.text: abhrakasatve'dhikaraṇe balamāste abhrasatvasaṃyogena raso balamāpnotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.4:2 //
children.translated_text: In the substrate of mica-essence — strength resides; meaning through the combination with mica-essence, mercury attains strength. || GRhtCM 8.4:2 ||

children.text: punastīkṣṇe lohabhede jāraṇarāgā jāraṇena tīkṣṇasthā rāgāḥ pratiṣṭhitā bhavantītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.4:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), a type of metal — <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) and <s>rāga</s> (coloring) — by assimilation of steel, the colors become established: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 8.4:3 ||

children.text: sāraṇamatha nāgavaṅgābhyām iti nāgavaṅgābhyāṃ duḥsaraṇaṃ sāraṇadravyaṃ sarata iti // GRhtCM_8.4:4 //
children.translated_text: And <s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing/spreading) [resides] in lead and tin — from lead and tin, the substance of difficult flowing, the <s>sāraṇa</s> agent, flows out. || GRhtCM 8.4:4 ||
[START GRht 8.5]
<Potency of steel (<s>tīkṣṇaloha</s>)>

children.text: krāmati tīkṣṇena rasastīkṣṇena ca jīryate kṣaṇādgrāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury pervades (<s>krāmati</s>) by means of steel; and by steel, the bolus (<s>grāsa</s>) is assimilated instantly;

children.text: hemno yonistīkṣṇaṃ rāgān gṛhṇāti tīkṣṇena // GRht_8.5 //
children.translated_text: steel is the source (<s>yoni</s>) of gold; mercury takes on colors through steel. || GRht 8.5 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that steel is the cause of everything, beginning with '<s>krāmati</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 8.5:1 ||

children.text: tīkṣṇena lohabhedena rasaḥ krāmati krāmaṇaṃ vidadhāti punas tīkṣṇena kṛtvā grāsaḥ kṣaṇādalpakālato jīryate jāraṇam āpnoti punarhemnaḥ suvarṇasya yonirutpattisthānaṃ tīkṣṇamasti punaḥ rāgān rañjanabhāvān tīkṣṇena kṛtvā raso gṛhṇāti svasmin rāgān dadhātītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Through steel, a type of metal, mercury performs <s>krāmaṇa</s> (pervading); furthermore, through steel, the bolus (<s>grāsa</s>) is assimilated in an instant — a brief time — it attains <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation). Furthermore, steel is the source (<s>yoni</s>), the place of origin, of gold (<s>suvarṇa</s>). Furthermore, mercury, through steel, takes on colors — meaning it holds the coloring capacities within itself: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 8.5:2 ||
[START GRht 8.6]
<Steel: <s>cāraṇa</s> and <s>jāraṇa</s>>

children.text: tadapi ca daradena hataṃ kṛtvā mākṣikeṇa ravisahitam /
children.translated_text: That [steel] too, killed (<s>hata</s>) with cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) and copper (<s>ravi</s>),

children.text: vāsitamapi vāsanayā ghanavaccāryaṃ ca jāryaṃ ca // GRht_8.6 //
children.translated_text: and treated (<s>vāsita</s>) with the treating agent (<s>vāsanā</s>), should be assimilated and digested like mica. || GRht 8.6 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the superior quality of steel through combination with cinnabar, beginning with 'that too' and so forth. || GRhtCM 8.6:1 ||

children.text: api niścayena tat tīkṣṇaṃ daradena hiṅgulena hataṃ māritaṃ vā mākṣikena svarṇamākṣikena ravisahitaṃ tāmrasaṃyutaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ hataṃ māritaṃ punarvāsanayā vāsanauṣadhena vāsitaṃ paribhāvitaṃ ghanavad abhravat cāryaṃ jāryaṃ ca satvābhravat nānyathā // GRhtCM_8.6:2 //
children.translated_text: Indeed (<s>api</s>, expressing certainty), that steel, killed (<s>hata</s>, calcined) with cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>), or [combined] with <s>mākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite) and copper (<s>tāmra</s>, indicated by <s>ravi</s>) — the steel killed [thus]; furthermore, treated (<s>vāsita</s>, impregnated) with treating medicine (<s>vāsanauṣadha</s>) — should be assimilated and digested like mica (<s>ghana</s>) — like mica-essence: not otherwise. || GRhtCM 8.6:2 ||
[START GRht 8.7]
<<s>Rañjana</s> (coloring): suitable substances>

children.text: kāntaṃ vā tīkṣṇaṃ vā kāñcīṃ vā vajrasasyakādīnām /
children.translated_text: Loadstone (<s>kānta</s>), or steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), or <s>kāñcī</s> (gold-pyrite), or from diamond (<s>vajra</s>), grain-stones (<s>sasyaka</s>), and others —

children.text: ekatamaṃ sarvaṃ vā rasaraṃjane saṃkaro'bhīṣṭaḥ // GRht_8.7 //
children.translated_text: any single one, or all [of them] — a mixture is desirable for the coloring of mercury. || GRht 8.7 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states [substances] similar to steel, beginning with '<s>kānta</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 8.7:1 ||

children.text: rasarañjane rasendre rāgakarmaṇi kāntaṃ cumbakapāṣāṇotthaṃ lohaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ veti samuccaye tīkṣṇaṃ lohabhedo vā kāñcīṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ vā vajrasasyakādīnāṃ vajrasasyakāvādiryeṣāṃ te teṣāṃ hīrakacapalādīnāṃ ekatamaṃ tanmadhyādekatamaṃ sarvaṃ vā atrābhīṣṭaśabdasya pratyekaṃ saṃbandhaḥ hīrakādīni ratnāni sasyakādyā upadhātavaḥ // GRhtCM_8.7:2 //
children.translated_text: For the coloring of mercury — in the coloring operation of the lord of mercury — <s>kānta</s>, the metal produced from loadstone, is excellent; 'or' [indicates] accumulation; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is a type of metal; or <s>kāñcī</s> is gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>); or from among diamond (<s>vajra</s>), grain-stone (<s>sasyaka</s>), and others — these beginning with <s>vajra</s> and <s>sasyaka</s> — of diamond (<s>hīraka</s>), <s>capala</s> (bismuth), and others: any single one from among them, or all of them. Here the word '<s>abhīṣṭa</s>' (desirable) has a connection with each one. Diamonds and such are gems (<s>ratna</s>); <s>sasyaka</s> and such are sub-metals (<s>upadhātu</s>). || GRhtCM 8.7:2 ||

children.text: vā rasarañjane ayameva saṃkaraḥ sarveṣāṃ kāntādīnāṃ melāpaḥ sarvatrābhīṣṭaḥ // GRhtCM_8.7:3 //
children.translated_text: Or, for the coloring of mercury, this very mixture — the blending of all, from loadstone onwards — is desirable in all cases. || GRhtCM 8.7:3 ||
[START GRht 8.8-9]
<Chemical potencies of various substances>

children.text: kuṭile balamabhyadhikaṃ rāgastīkṣṇe tu pannage snehaḥ /
children.translated_text: In curved [metal] (<s>kuṭila</s>, i.e., copper), strength is greatest; coloring [is greatest] in steel; in lead (<s>pannaga</s>), unctuousness (<s>sneha</s>);

children.text: rāgasnehabalāni tu kamale śaṃsanti dhātuvidaḥ // GRht_8.8 //
children.translated_text: coloring, unctuousness, and strength — all three in copper (<s>kamala</s>): so declare the knowers of metals. || GRht 8.8 ||
<Mercury: <s>rañjana</s> (coloring)>
With all these metals, killed with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) and likewise melted in the womb (<s>garbha</s>),

children.text: viḍayogena tu jīrṇo rasarājo rāgamupayāti // GRht_8.9 //
children.translated_text: the king of <s>rasas</s>, assimilated with the <s>viḍa</s>-procedure, attains coloring (<s>rāga</s>). || GRht 8.9 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: sve sve vikāre vakṣyamāṇamāha balamityādi // GRhtCM_8.8-9:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the respective special properties to be described, beginning with 'strength' and so forth. || GRhtCM 8.8-9:1 ||
The knowers of metals — the physicians of <s>rasa</s> — so declare. || GRhtCM 8.8-9:2 ||

children.text: iti kiṃ kuṭile balaṃ abhyadhikaṃ sarvādhikaṃ punastīkṣṇe'bhyadhiko rāgaḥ rañjanaṃ tu punaḥ pannage nāge'bhyadhikaṃ snehaḥ snigdhatvaṃ tu punaḥ rāgasnehabalāni trīṇyevoktāni kamale tāmre kuṭilatīkṣṇapannagānāṃ jāraṇādrase yathā balarāgasnehā bhavanti tathaikatāmrajāraṇāt trayo bhavantītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.8-9:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus, what? In curved metal (<s>kuṭila</s>, copper), strength is greatest — surpassing all. Furthermore, in steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), coloring (<s>rāga</s>) is greatest. Furthermore, in lead (<s>pannaga</s>, <s>nāga</s>), unctuousness (<s>sneha</s>) is greatest. Furthermore, coloring, unctuousness, and strength — these three just mentioned — [are found] in copper (<s>kamala</s>, <s>tāmra</s>): just as by the assimilation of curved metal, steel, and lead into mercury, strength, coloring, and unctuousness arise respectively, so by the assimilation of copper alone, all three arise: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 8.8-9:3 ||
He states the means for binding mercury, beginning with 'with all' and so forth. || GRhtCM 8.8-9:4 ||

children.text: biḍayogena pūrvoktena jīrṇo jāraṇamāpanno rasarājo bandhamupayāti bandhanamādatte // GRhtCM_8.8-9:5 //
children.translated_text: Through the previously described <s>viḍa</s>-procedure, when assimilated — when <s>jāraṇa</s> has been attained — the king of <s>rasas</s> attains binding (<s>bandha</s>) — receives fixation. || GRhtCM 8.8-9:5 ||

children.text: kaiḥ saha jīrṇaḥ ebhiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ sarvair lohairdhātubhiḥ // GRhtCM_8.8-9:6 //
children.translated_text: Assimilated with what? With all these previously mentioned metals (<s>dhātu</s>). || GRhtCM 8.8-9:6 ||
Of what character? Killed (<s>nihata</s>) with <s>mākṣika</s> — calcined with gold-pyrite. || GRhtCM 8.8-9:7 ||

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ garbhe rasodare drutairvidrutairiti // GRhtCM_8.8-9:8 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what character? Melted (<s>druta</s>) in the womb (<s>garbha</s>) — liquefied in mercury's belly. || GRhtCM 8.8-9:8 ||
[START GRht 8.10-11]
<Mercury: <s>rañjana</s> (coloring with a <s>kṛṣṭi</s>)>
With orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), realgar (<s>darada</s>), and arsenic (<s>śilā</s>), together with oils, alkalines, sours, and salts —
by firing (<s>puṭa</s>), one should process tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), iron (<s>śastra</s>), and the like in equal, double, or triple [proportions]. // GRht 8.10 //
By pouring red [group substances] and oils, [one should complete] the remainder; this is the 'attraction' (<s>kṛṣṭi</s>) of mercury —
merely by consumption (<s>cāraṇa</s>) and digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>), it makes mercury resemble the <s>indragopa</s> (a brilliant red insect). // GRht 8.11 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the calcination (<s>māraṇa</s>) procedure for the metals about to be described, beginning with '<s>tālaka</s>' (orpiment) and so forth. // GRhtCM 8.10-11:1 //

children.text: vaṅgaśastrādīn vaṅgaṃ trapuṣaṃ śastraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ te ādiryeṣāṃ te tān // GRhtCM_8.10-11:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Vaṅga-śastra</s>-etc.' — <s>vaṅga</s> means tin (<s>trapuṣa</s>); <s>śastra</s> means iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>); 'etc.' [includes others]. // GRhtCM 8.10-11:2 //

children.text: kābhiḥ saha puṭo vahet tālakadaradaśilābhiḥ tālakaṃ haritālaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ śilā manaḥśilā tābhiḥ // GRhtCM_8.10-11:3 //
children.translated_text: With what should the firing be done? With orpiment (<s>tālaka</s> = <s>haritāla</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s> = <s>hiṅgula</s>), and realgar (<s>śilā</s> = <s>manaḥśilā</s>). // GRhtCM 8.10-11:3 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭābhiḥ snehakṣārāmlalavaṇasahitābhiḥ snehaḥ tailaṃ kaṅguṇitumbinyādīnāṃ kṣāraḥ svarjikādiḥ amlaṃ jambīrādi lavaṇāni saindhavādīni etaiḥ sahitābhiḥ // GRhtCM_8.10-11:4 //
children.translated_text: With what further qualities? 'Together with oils, alkalines, sours, and salts' — oil means sesame oil, or [oil] from <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus), gourd (<s>tumbinī</s>), and the like; alkaline means <s>svarjikā</s> (natron) and the like; sour means lemon (<s>jambīra</s>) and the like; salts mean rock-salt (<s>saindhava</s>) and the like — together with these. // GRhtCM 8.10-11:4 //

children.text: ekadhātuto dvādaśāṃśād ārabhya yāvatsamakadviguṇatriguṇabhāgāḥ samāpyante tāvatpuṭo vahediti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_8.10-11:5 //
children.translated_text: Beginning with a twelfth portion of one metal, up to equal, double, and triple proportions — until these are exhausted, firing should be done — this is the explanation. // GRhtCM 8.10-11:5 //
He states what is to be done with the fired metal, beginning with '<s>rakta</s>' (red) and so forth. // GRhtCM 8.10-11:6 //

children.text: uktadhāturgarbhitaṃ rasaṃ raktasnehaniṣekaiḥ rakto raktavargaḥ snehaḥ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ anayorniṣekāḥ siñcanāni taiḥ śeṣaṃ dhātuvarjitaṃ kuryāt iyaṃ rasasya kṛṣṭiḥ rasasya guṇākarṣaṇaṃ punariyaṃ kṛṣṭiḥ rasendraṃ indragopanibhaṃ kurute atiriktavarṇaṃ kurute // GRhtCM_8.10-11:7 //
children.translated_text: The mercury that has consumed (<s>garbhita</s>) the stated metals — by pouring the red group and oils: 'red' means the red group [of substances]; 'oils' means [the oils] of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and the like; by pouring these, one should complete the remainder [of the process], making [it] free from metals. This is the 'attraction' (<s>kṛṣṭi</s>) of mercury — the drawing out of mercury's qualities. Furthermore, this 'attraction' makes the king of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) resemble the <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect) — produces an exceedingly [red] color. // GRhtCM 8.10-11:7 //

children.text: kutaḥ cāraṇajāraṇamātrāt punaḥ puṭitadhātūnāṃ cāraṇaṃ ca jāraṇaṃ jīrṇaṃkaraṇaṃ ca tanmātrāt vā cāraṇasya dravyasya jāraṇaṃ tanmātrāt ubhayoḥ pakṣayoreka evārthaḥ paramuktiviśeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_8.10-11:8 //
children.translated_text: From what [process]? Merely from consumption (<s>cāraṇa</s>) and digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) — the consumption and the causing-to-digest of the fired metals; or, from the digestion of the material [used for] consumption; in both interpretations, the meaning is the same — the specific distinction is [simply] in liberation [of the mercury]. // GRhtCM 8.10-11:8 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 8.12]
<Mercury :: Coloring (<s>rañjana</s>)>

children.text: athavā kevalam amalaṃ kamalaṃ daradena vāpitaṃ kurute /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, pure, stainless copper (<s>kamala</s>), alone, treated (<s>vāpita</s>) with cinnabar (<s>darada</s>),

children.text: triguṇaṃ hi cīrṇajīrṇaṃ lākṣārasasannibhaṃ sūtam // GRht_8.12 //
children.translated_text: in triple quantity, consumed and digested — makes mercury resemble the juice of lac (<s>lākṣā-rasa</s>). // GRht 8.12 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the praise of copper as the primary [coloring agent], beginning with 'alternatively' and so forth. // GRhtCM 8.12:1 //

children.text: athaveti vidhānāntare kevalaṃ śuddhaṃ vānyasaṃyogena varjitaṃ amalaṃ jātapūrvaśodhanaṃ triguṇaṃ cīrṇajīrṇaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ pūrvaṃ cīrṇaṃ cāraṇamāptaṃ paścājjīrṇaṃ jāraṇamāpannaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ tāmraṃ sūtaṃ lākṣārasasannibhaṃ alaktakaprabhaṃ kurute // GRhtCM_8.12:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Alternatively' — in another procedure; 'alone' — pure, or free from combination with other [substances]; 'stainless' — having previously undergone purification; [the copper should be] consumed and digested in triple quantity — this is the meaning. First consumed (<s>cīrṇa</s>), i.e., having undergone consumption (<s>cāraṇa</s>); then digested (<s>jīrṇa</s>), having undergone digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>); such copper makes mercury (<s>sūta</s>) resemble lac-juice (<s>lākṣā-rasa</s>) — having the luster of lac (<s>alaktaka</s>). // GRhtCM 8.12:2 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 8.13]
<Mercury :: Coloring (<s>rañjana</s>)>
Copper-pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and realgar (<s>śilā</s>) — impregnated with animal-fluid (<s>paśu-jala</s>) melted through the red group —

children.text: ekena vāpitamṛtaṃ kamalaṃ rañjayati rasarājam // GRht_8.13 //
children.translated_text: by any one of these, [when copper (<s>kamala</s>) is] treated [with it] and killed (<s>mṛta</s>), [it] colors the king of mercury. // GRht 8.13 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method, beginning with '<s>rakta</s>' (red) and so forth. // GRhtCM 8.13:1 //

children.text: raktagaṇena dāḍimakiṃśukabandhūkādinā pūrvoktena galitaṃ yat paśujalaṃ gomūtraṃ tena bhāvitā yās tāpyagandhakamanaḥśilās tāsāṃ madhyād ekena tāpyena svarṇamākṣikena vā gandhakena vā śilayā vāpitamṛtaṃ sat kamalaṃ tāmraṃ rasaṃ rañjayati rāgaṃ dadātītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.13:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Melted through the red group' — by the previously described red group of pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, <s>bandhūka</s>, and the like — that which has melted, i.e., animal-fluid (<s>paśu-jala</s> = cow's urine) — [that] with which the copper-pyrites (<s>tāpya</s> = gold <s>mākṣika</s>), sulphur, and realgar have been impregnated; by any one of these — by copper-pyrites, or sulphur, or realgar — when [copper] is treated and killed (<s>mṛta</s>), it colors the mercury, i.e., gives it coloration — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 8.13:2 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 8.14]
<Duration of coloring according to substance>
The coloring by sulphur is external [i.e., impermanent]; [that by] realgar and orpiment produces an unstable color;

children.text: mākṣikasatvarasakau dvāveva hi rañjane śastau // GRht_8.14 //
children.translated_text: only two — <s>mākṣika</s>-essence and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine) — are recommended for [permanent] coloring. // GRht 8.14 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the [substances] qualified for coloring — sulphur and the others. // GRhtCM 8.14:1 //

children.text: tatra gandhakaḥ kīdṛśaṃ rāgaṃ dadāti tatsvarūpamāha bāhya ityādi // GRhtCM_8.14:2 //
children.translated_text: There, what kind of color does sulphur give? He states its nature, beginning with 'external' and so forth. // GRhtCM 8.14:2 //

children.text: gandhakarāgo bāhyo bahirbhavaḥ punarmanaḥśilātāle manaḥśilā manohvā tālaṃ haritālaṃ tāvubhe vilulitarāge cañcalarāge punar mākṣikasatvarasakau svarṇamākṣikasatvakharparikau dvāveva rañjane rasarāge śastau gandhakamanaḥśilātālebhyaḥ pradhānau atyadhikāvityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.14:3 //
children.translated_text: The color from sulphur is 'external' (<s>bāhya</s>), i.e., only on the surface. Furthermore, [regarding] realgar and orpiment: <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) and <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment) — both of these produce an unstable (<s>vilulita</s>) color, a wavering color. But <s>mākṣika</s>-essence (gold-pyrites essence) and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine) — these two alone are recommended for coloring, for the [permanent] coloring of mercury — they are superior to sulphur, realgar, and orpiment, i.e., exceedingly more effective — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 8.14:3 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 8.15]
<Coloring agent for mercury (15)>
Copper (<s>ravi</s>) and calamine (<s>rasaka</s>), [processed] in sequential procedure, well-purified, smelted in a sealed crucible (<s>mūka-mūṣikā</s>) —

children.text: triguṇaṃ cīrṇo jīrṇo hemābho jāyate sūtaḥ // GRht_8.15 //
children.translated_text: consumed and digested in triple quantity — mercury becomes gold-hued. // GRht 8.15 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for the two principal [agents] — copper and calamine, beginning with 'in sequential procedure' and so forth. // GRhtCM 8.15:1 //

children.text: kramavṛttau ravirasakau saṃśuddhau viśeṣavidhānena śodhitau vā uttamajātīyau mūkamūṣikādhmātau andhamūṣāyāṃ dhmātau vahniyogīkṛtau kāryau etattriguṇaṃ yathā syāttathā cīrṇo jīrṇaśca sūtaḥ hemanibho jāyate etena cāraṇamāpannaḥ paścāttenaiva jāraṇām āpanno rasaḥ svarṇaprabho bhavedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.15:2 //
children.translated_text: Copper and calamine, 'well-purified' — purified by a special method, or of the finest variety — 'smelted in a sealed crucible' — smelted in a blind crucible (<s>andha-mūṣā</s>), i.e., subjected to fire-treatment; this should be done in such a way that it becomes triple. Consumed (<s>cīrṇa</s>) and digested (<s>jīrṇa</s>) — the mercury becomes gold-hued. By this, [mercury] that has undergone consumption and subsequently by that very [substance] has undergone digestion, becomes golden in luster — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 8.15:2 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 8.16]
<Coloring agent for mercury (16)>

children.text: atha kṛṣṇābhrakacūrṇaṃ puṭitaṃ raktaṃ bhavettathā sakalam /
children.translated_text: Now, black mica powder, when fired, becomes entirely red;

children.text: triguṇaṃ cīrṇo jīrṇo hemadrutisannibhaḥ sūtaḥ // GRht_8.16 //
children.translated_text: consumed and digested in triple quantity — mercury [becomes] like molten gold. // GRht 8.16 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the mica-procedure, beginning with 'now' and so forth. // GRhtCM 8.16:1 //

children.text: atha rasakayogānantaraṃ kṛṣṇavarṇābhrakacūrṇaṃ śyāmavarṇābhrakarajaḥ tathā ravirasakavidhānena kharparakeṇa sahitaṃ puṭitaṃ sat sakalaṃ samastaṃ raktaṃ bhavet tadraktabhūtamabhraṃ triguṇaṃ yathā syāttathā cīrṇaḥ cāraṇamāpannas tato jīrṇo jāraṇamāpannaśca san sūto hemadrutisannibhaḥ svarṇadravasadṛśo bhaved ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.16:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Now' — after the calamine-procedure; black-colored mica powder, i.e., dust of dark-colored mica, combined with calamine (<s>kharpara</s>) by the same method as the copper-calamine procedure, when fired, becomes entirely red. That reddened mica, consumed and digested in triple quantity — the mercury becomes like molten gold (<s>hema-druti</s>), i.e., resembling the liquid of gold — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 8.16:2 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 8.17-18]
<Mercury :: Coloring (<s>rañjana</s>)>

children.text: triguṇena mākṣikeṇa tu kanakaṃ ca mṛtaṃ rasakatālayutam /
children.translated_text: Gold, killed (<s>mṛta</s>) with triple-quantity <s>mākṣika</s> (copper-pyrites), combined with calamine and orpiment,
together with salt, cooked in a pot until [it resembles] the <s>indragopa</s> (red insect). // GRht 8.17 //

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ sūtavare triguṇaṃ cīrṇaṃ hi jīrṇaṃ tu /
children.translated_text: That powder, consumed and digested in triple quantity in the excellent mercury —

children.text: drutahemanibhaḥ sūto rañjati lohāni sarvāṇi // GRht_8.18 //
children.translated_text: mercury becomes like molten gold and colors all metals. // GRht 8.18 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the killing of gold, beginning with 'triple-quantity' and so forth. // GRhtCM 8.17-18:1 //

children.text: tu punaḥ triguṇena mākṣikeṇa svarṇatriguṇitena tāpyena yatkanakaṃ mṛtaṃ tatkanakaṃ indragopako varṣākālīno raktavarṇo jīvaviśeṣaḥ tadvannibhā dīptiryasya tadindragopanibhaṃ bhavatīti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_8.17-18:2 //
children.translated_text: Further, with triple-quantity <s>mākṣika</s> — copper-pyrites three times [the amount of] gold — the gold that is killed (<s>mṛta</s>); that gold [becomes] like the <s>indragopa</s> — a rainy-season red-colored creature — whose luster is like that — [it becomes] <s>indragopa</s>-like; the rest is supplied. // GRhtCM 8.17-18:2 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ kanakaṃ mṛtaṃ rasakatālayutaṃ rasakaṃ kharparaṃ tālaṃ haritālaṃ tābhyāṃ yutaṃ miśritaṃ sat yanmṛtaṃ pañcatvamāptamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.17-18:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality is the gold that is killed? Combined with calamine (<s>rasaka</s> = <s>kharpara</s>) and orpiment (<s>tāla</s> = <s>haritāla</s>); when mixed with these and killed, i.e., when it has attained the state of quintuple [i.e., total dissolution] — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 8.17-18:3 //

children.text: punaḥ paṭusahitaṃ lavaṇamiśritaṃ punar haṇḍikayā bhājanena pakvaṃ vahnipuṭitaṃ tadapi pūrvavat // GRhtCM_8.17-18:4 //
children.translated_text: Further, 'together with salt' — mixed with salt; further, 'cooked in a pot' — fired in a vessel — that too, as before. // GRhtCM 8.17-18:4 //

children.text: mṛtakanakacūrṇaṃ sūtavare pārade triguṇaṃ cīrṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ cāritaṃ jāritaṃ ca sat sūto drutahemanibho bhavet galitasvarṇaprabha ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.17-18:5 //
children.translated_text: The powder of the killed gold, consumed and digested in triple quantity in the excellent mercury — the mercury becomes like molten gold (<s>druta-hema</s>), i.e., having the luster of liquefied gold — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 8.17-18:5 //

children.text: evaṃ rañjito rasaḥ sarvalohāni dhātūni kṛtrimākṛtrimāni navavidhāni rañjati svarṇarūpāṇi karotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.17-18:6 //
children.translated_text: Mercury thus colored transforms all metals (<s>lohas</s>) — the nine [types of] metals, both artificial and natural — into the form of gold — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 8.17-18:6 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 8.19]
<The greatness of seed-digestion>
Essence (<s>sattva</s>) is eight times [more potent] than sheet (<s>patra</s>); melting (<s>druti</s>) is eight times [more] than essence;

children.text: druteraṣṭaguṇaṃ bījaṃ tasmādbījaṃ tu jārayet // GRht_8.19 //
children.translated_text: seed (<s>bīja</s>) is eight times [more] than melting — therefore, one should [make mercury] digest the seed. // GRht 8.19 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: sarveṣāṃ dhāturasānāmuttarottaraṃ viśeṣatvam āha patrādityādi // GRhtCM_8.19:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the progressively superior quality of all the metal-preparations, beginning with 'than sheet' and so forth. // GRhtCM 8.19:1 //

children.text: patrādaṣṭaguṇaṃ satvaṃ abhrapatre jīrṇe sati rase yo guṇastasmādaṣṭaguṇo guṇastatsatve ityarthaḥ punaḥ sattvāt drutistaddravarūpā aṣṭaguṇā punardruter bījaṃ dhātūparasasaṃyogajanitaṃ pūrvopavarṇitaṃ tadaṣṭaguṇaṃ tataḥ sarvotkṛṣṭatvādbījaṃ jārayennatvanyat // GRhtCM_8.19:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Essence is eight times [more potent] than sheet' — the quality [derived from] digesting mica-sheet in mercury is eight times less than the quality [derived from digesting] its essence — this is the meaning. Further, melting (<s>druti</s>) — the liquid form thereof — is eight times [more potent] than essence. Further, seed (<s>bīja</s>) — produced from the combination of metals and sub-metals, as previously described — is eight times more than melting. Therefore, because of its supreme excellence, one should make [mercury] digest the seed, and nothing else. // GRhtCM 8.19:2 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 9.1]
<Seed (<s>bīja</s>) — Definition>

children.text: iti rakto'pi rasendro bījena vinā na karmakṛdbhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus, even a colored king of mercury, without a seed, does not become an agent of action;
that [seed] is twofold — yellow and white — [only] the perfected one is to be employed. // GRht 9.1 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
'Like the moon in its luster, like the sun in its radiance,

children.text: niśāhnoriva kartā ca durjanaiḥ sahanālayaḥ // GRhtCM_9.1:1 //
children.translated_text: like day and night as an agent — not [to be] associated with the wicked.' // GRhtCM 9.1:1 //
'When, by a special quenching procedure, it attains that color,
[being] soft and of variegated treatment — that is called a seed (<s>bīja</s>).' // GRhtCM 9.1:2 //
This is the technical definition (<s>paribhāṣā</s>). // GRhtCM 9.1:3 //
He states the praise of the seed, beginning with 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM 9.1:4 //

children.text: ityuktavidhānena rakto'pi rasendro bījena vinā karmakṛnna bhavati bījenaiva karmakārī syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_9.1:5 //
children.translated_text: By the procedure thus stated, even a colored king of mercury, without a seed, does not become an agent of action — only with a seed would it become an effective agent — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 9.1:5 //

children.text: tadbījaṃ dvividhaṃ dviprakāraṃ pītasitaṃ ekaṃ pītaṃ aparaṃ sitaṃ śvetaṃ svarṇarūpyakriyāyogyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_9.1:6 //
children.translated_text: That seed is twofold, of two kinds — yellow and white; one is yellow, the other is white — fit for gold-procedures and silver-procedures respectively — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 9.1:6 //

children.text: tadbījaṃ siddhaṃ sarvalakṣaṇopetaṃ rase pārade niyojyaṃ nāsiddhamiti // GRhtCM_9.1:7 //
children.translated_text: That seed, [only when] perfected — endowed with all characteristics — is to be employed in mercury; not an imperfected one. // GRhtCM 9.1:7 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 9.2]
<Seed :: Purification necessary>
Its purification [is done] in many ways, with powders of mica, <s>mahārasas</s> (great minerals), <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals), and metals;

children.text: dvividhaṃ bījaṃ tairapi nāśuddhaiḥ śudhyate vai tat // GRht_9.2 //
children.translated_text: the twofold seed is not purified even by those [powders] if they are impure. // GRht 9.2 //
'Of that' and so forth. // GRhtCM 9.2:1 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: tasya bījasya viśuddhiḥ śodhanaṃ bahudhā bahuprakāraiḥ kṛtvā rasoparasadhātūnāṃ bahuvidhatvāt // GRhtCM_9.2:2 //
children.translated_text: Of that seed, the purification — the cleansing — is to be done in many ways, by many methods, because of the manifold nature of the <s>mahārasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, and metals. // GRhtCM 9.2:2 //

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā gaganarasalohacūrṇaiḥ gaganamabhraṃ rasā vaikrāntādayo'ṣṭau vakṣyamāṇāḥ uparasā gandhakādayaḥ lohā dhātavaḥ teṣāṃ cūrṇāni taiḥ // GRhtCM_9.2:3 //
children.translated_text: By what [substances] is it done? With the powders of mica (<s>gagana</s> = <s>abhra</s>), <s>rasas</s> (the eight [great minerals] such as <s>vaikrānta</s> etc., to be described), <s>uparasas</s> (such as sulphur etc.), and metals (<s>lohas</s> = <s>dhātus</s>) — with their powders. // GRhtCM 9.2:3 //

children.text: ca punaḥ tair gaganarasoparasalohacūrṇair aśuddhaiḥ śuddhivarjitaistadbījaṃ na śudhyate śuddhihīnaṃ syāt kāraṇānurūpaṃ kāryamitinyāyāt // GRhtCM_9.2:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, by those — by the powders of mica, <s>mahārasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, and metals — if impure, i.e., lacking purification, that seed is not purified, i.e., would remain lacking in purity — by the principle that 'the effect conforms to the cause.' // GRhtCM 9.2:4 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 9.3]
He who performs procedures with these [substances] when they are impure — the mercury that results for him

children.text: avyāpakaḥ pataṃgī na rase rasāyane yogyaḥ // GRht_9.3 //
children.translated_text: becomes non-pervading, volatile (<s>pataṃgī</s>) — not fit for mercury or for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). // GRht 9.3 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the effect of impure seed, beginning with 'he who' and so forth. // GRhtCM 9.3:1 //

children.text: punarviśeṣeṇa yaḥ saṃskārakṛdetairgaganādyair aśuddhaiḥ kṛtvā rasasya karma kurute tasya puruṣasya rasaḥ pārado 'vyāpako 'saraṇaśīlo bhavet pataṅgī ūrdhvagāmī ca bhavet yantrasyādhobhāge na tiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_9.3:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, specifically, he who performs procedures — the one doing the processing — having used these [substances] such as mica etc. when impure, if he performs the procedure on mercury, then for that person, the mercury becomes non-pervading, i.e., having an unyielding nature; and [it becomes] volatile (<s>pataṃgī</s>), i.e., upward-moving — it does not remain in the lower part of the apparatus — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM 9.3:2 //
[Beginning of <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> 9.4]
<Great minerals (<s>Mahārasas</s>)>

<s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s> (loadstone), <s>sasya</s> (lapis lazuli?), <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrites), <s>vimala</s> (silver-pyrites), mountain-born (<s>adri</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), and calamine (<s>rasaka</s>) —

children.text: aṣṭau rasāstathaiṣāṃ sattvāni rasāyanāni syuḥ // GRht_9.4 //
children.translated_text: these are the eight <s>rasas</s> (great minerals); and their essences (<s>sattvas</s>) are [the means for] <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). // GRht 9.4 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: ete vakṣyamāṇā aṣṭau rasāḥ rasasaṃjñakāḥ syuḥ // GRhtCM_9.4:1 //
children.translated_text: These eight, about to be described, are the <s>rasas</s> — [substances] designated by the name '<s>rasa</s>' (great minerals). // GRhtCM 9.4:1 //

children.text: ete ke vaikrāntakāntasasyakamākṣikavimalādridaradarasakāś ceti vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ kāntaṃ cumbakotthaṃ sasyakaṃ capalaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ vimalā raupyamākṣikaṃ adri śilājatu daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ rasakaḥ kharparikaḥ ete rasasaṃjñikā jñeyāḥ // GRhtCM_9.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Which are these? <s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vimala</s>, <s>adri</s>, <s>darada</s>, and <s>rasaka</s> — thus: '<s>vaikrānta</s>' is the dust born of diamond-earth; '<s>kānta</s>' is [the substance] derived from loadstone (<s>cumbaka</s>); '<s>sasyaka</s>' is quicksilver (<s>capala</s>); '<s>mākṣika</s>' is copper pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>); '<s>vimala</s>' is silver-<s>mākṣika</s> (silver pyrites); '<s>adri</s>' is mineral pitch (<s>śilājatu</s>); '<s>darada</s>' is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>); '<s>rasaka</s>' is calamine (<s>kharpārikā</s>). These should be known as having the designation '<s>rasa</s>' (mineral-substance).

children.text: tathā eṣāṃ satvāni sārāṇi rasāyanāni jarāvyādhināśanāni syuriti // GRhtCM_9.4:3 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, their essences (<s>sattva</s>) — their <s>sāras</s> (extracts) — are <s>rasāyanas</s> (rejuvenators), destroyers of old age and disease.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.5-6

<<s>Uparasa</s> (subsidiary mineral)>
Sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), ochre (<s>gairika</s>), arsenic (<s>śilā</s>), orpiment (<s>āla</s>), alum (<s>kṣiti</s>), green vitriol (<s>khecara</s>), collyrium (<s>añjana</s>), and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> —
He states those designated as <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals), beginning with '<s>gandhaka</s>' (sulphur) etc.
The following [substances] are designated as <s>uparasas</s>.

children.text: kimidaṃ gandhakagairikaśilālakṣitikhecaram iti gandhakaṃ pratītaṃ gairikaṃ dhātugairikaṃ śilā manohvā ālaṃ haritālaṃ kṣitiḥ sphaṭikā khecaraṃ kāsīsaṃ etat sarvamiti ca punaḥ añjanaṃ nīlāñjanaṃ punaḥ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ ityaṣṭau uparasasaṃjñakā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_9.4:3 //
children.translated_text: What are these? '<s>Gandhaka-gairika-śilā-āla-kṣiti-khecara</s>' — '<s>gandhaka</s>' is well known [as sulphur]; '<s>gairika</s>' is mineral ochre (<s>dhātugairika</s>); '<s>śilā</s>' is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>); '<s>āla</s>' is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>); '<s>kṣiti</s>' is alum (<s>sphaṭikā</s>); '<s>khecara</s>' is green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>); all these — and furthermore, '<s>añjana</s>' is collyrium (<s>nīlāñjana</s>); furthermore, '<s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>' is <s>viraṅga</s> — thus eight are designated as <s>uparasas</s> — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.5-6
This is designated as <s>uparasa</s>. '<s>Śikhi</s>' (fire/peacock) and '<s>śaśin</s>' (moon) are called '<s>sāra-lohas</s>' (noble metals).
<<s>Sāraloha</s> (noble metals)>
<<s>Pūtiloha</s> (base metals)>
Copper (<s>tāmra</s>), bronze (<s>āra</s>), steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), loadstone (<s>kānta</s>), mica-essence (<s>abhrasattva</s>), iron (<s>loha</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), and lead (<s>nāga</s>) —
these are said to bear the designation '<s>pūti</s>' (base); their purification should be performed.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
'<s>Śikhi</s>' (fire/gold) and '<s>śaśin</s>' (moon/silver) — gold and silver — are called '<s>sāra-lohas</s>' (noble metals); they bear the designation of noble metals — this is the meaning.
He states those bearing the designation '<s>pūti</s>' (base), beginning with '<s>tāmra</s>' (copper) etc.

children.text: tāmrāratīkṣṇakāntābhrasatvalohānīti tāmraṃ nepālakaṃ āraṃ rājarītiḥ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ kāntaṃ cumbakodbhavaṃ abhrasatvaṃ gaganasāraṃ lohaṃ muṇḍaṃ etānīti punarvaṅganāgau ete pūtisaṃjñakāḥ kathitāḥ // GRhtCM_9.5-6:3 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Tāmra-āra-tīkṣṇa-kānta-abhrasattva-lohas</s>': '<s>tāmra</s>' is Nepalese copper; '<s>āra</s>' is <s>rājarīti</s> (bell-metal/bronze); '<s>tīkṣṇa</s>' is steel (<s>sāra</s>); '<s>kānta</s>' is that derived from loadstone (<s>cumbaka</s>); '<s>abhrasattva</s>' is the extract of mica (<s>gaganasāra</s>); '<s>loha</s>' is wrought iron (<s>muṇḍa</s>). These — and furthermore, tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) and lead (<s>nāga</s>) — these are said to bear the designation '<s>pūti</s>' (base).

children.text: teṣāṃ pūtilohasaṃjñakānāṃ śodhanaṃ samyaṅmalāpanayanaṃ kāryamiti // GRhtCM_9.5-6:4 //
children.translated_text: The purification (<s>śodhana</s>) of those bearing the '<s>pūti-loha</s>' designation — the proper removal of impurities — should be performed.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.7

<<s>Ṣaḍlavaṇa</s> (six salts)>
<s>Sauvarcala</s>, <s>saindhava</s>, <s>kacūlika</s>, <s>sāmudra</s>, <s>romaka</s>, and <s>biḍa</s> —
He states those designated as salts and alkalies, beginning with '<s>sauvarcala</s>' etc.

children.text: etāni vakṣyamāṇāni lavaṇasaṃjñānyāhuḥ ācāryāḥ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_9.6:2 //
children.translated_text: The following [substances] are designated as salts — [say] the masters — this is the completion.

children.text: kāni sauvarcalasaindhavakacūlikasāmudraromakabiḍānīti sauvarcalaṃ rucakaṃ saindhavaṃ maṇikamanthāhvayaṃ cūlikaṃ kācalavaṇaṃ sāmudraṃ kṣārābdhijaṃ romakaṃ pratītaṃ biḍaṃ lavaṇaviśeṣaḥ etānīti // GRhtCM_9.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Which? '<s>Sauvarcala-saindhava-kacūlika-sāmudra-romaka-biḍa</s>': '<s>sauvarcala</s>' is digestive salt (<s>rucaka</s>); '<s>saindhava</s>' is also called <s>maṇikamantha</s> (rock salt); '<s>cūlika</s>' is glass-salt (<s>kācalavaṇa</s>); '<s>sāmudra</s>' is sea-salt (<s>kṣārābdhija</s>); '<s>romaka</s>' is well known; '<s>biḍa</s>' is a specific salt-variety. These are [the six].
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.7
These are the six salts. <s>Svarjī</s> (washing soda), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley alkali) [are the three alkalies].
<<s>Trikṣāra</s> (three alkalies)>
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: punaḥ svarjī sarjikā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ yavakṣāraḥ pratītaḥ ete kṣārāḥ kṣārasaṃjñikāḥ rasakarmaṇi ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_9.7:1 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, '<s>svarjī</s>' is <s>sarjikā</s> (soda ash); '<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>' is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax); '<s>yavakṣāra</s>' is well known. These are the alkalies (<s>kṣāras</s>), bearing the designation of alkali — in mercury operations — this is the implied supplement.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.8-9
<<s>Uparasa</s> :: purification, essence-extraction>

children.text: sūryāvartaḥ kadalī vandhyā kośātakī ca suradālī /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūryāvarta</s> (sunflower/heliotrope), <s>kadalī</s> (plantain), <s>vandhyā</s> (barren) [<s>karkoṭī</s>], <s>kośātakī</s> (luffa), and <s>suradālī</s> (a climbing plant),

children.text: śigruśca vajrakando nīrakaṇā kākamācī ca // GRht_9.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>śigru</s> (drumstick tree), <s>vajrakanda</s> (adamantine tuber), <s>nīrakaṇā</s> (water-pepper), and <s>kākamācī</s> (nightshade).
By the juice of [any] one of these, treated many times with salts, alkalies, and sours,

children.text: śudhyanti rasoparasā dhmātāḥ sattvāni muñcanti // GRht_9.9 //
children.translated_text: the <s>rasas</s> (minerals) and <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals) are purified; when smelted, they release their essences (<s>sattva</s>).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the dissolving and purifying group, beginning with '<s>sūryāvarta</s>' etc.

children.text: sūryaṃ prati āvartako bhramaṇaṃ yasyetyevaṃvidhaḥ kadalī rambhā vandhyā phalarahitā karkoṭī kośātakī jālinī suradālī devadālī śigruḥ saubhāñjanaṃ vajrakando vadasūraṇakandaḥ nīrakaṇā jalapippalī kākamācī vāyasī iti gaṇaḥ śodhanadrāvaṇayogya iti // GRhtCM_9.8-9:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Sūryāvarta</s>' — that which turns toward the sun — such [a plant]; '<s>kadalī</s>' is plantain; '<s>vandhyā</s>' means fruit-less, i.e., the barren <s>karkoṭī</s>; '<s>kośātakī</s>' is the luffa vine (<s>jālinī</s>); '<s>suradālī</s>' is the <s>devadālī</s> plant; '<s>śigru</s>' is the drumstick tree (<s>saubhāñjana</s>); '<s>vajrakanda</s>' is the tuber of <s>vadasūraṇa</s>; '<s>nīrakaṇā</s>' is water-pepper (<s>jalapippalī</s>); '<s>kākamācī</s>' is <s>vāyasī</s> (nightshade). This group is suitable for purification and dissolution.
He states the purification and dissolution procedure for the purifying-dissolving [agents], beginning with '<s>āsām</s>' (of these) etc.

children.text: āsāṃ pūrvauṣadhīnāṃ madhyāt ekarasena ekasyā rasena rasoparasā vaikrāntādayo'ṣṭau rasāḥ gandhakādayo 'ṣṭāvuparasāḥ bahuśo'nekavāraṃ bhāvitā gharmapuṭitāḥ kāryāḥ punarlavaṇakṣārāmlabhāvitāśca lavaṇāni sauvarcalādīni ṣaṭ kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ amlā jambīrādayaḥ tairbahuvāraṃ bhāvitās tīvragharmapuṭitā rasoparasāḥ śudhyanti doṣavarjitā bhavanti punaste dhmātāḥ santaḥ satvāni svīyasārāṇi muñcanti tyajantīti // GRhtCM_9.8-9:4 //
children.translated_text: Of these, the previously stated herbs — by the juice of one — the <s>rasas</s> (minerals), viz. the eight [substances] such as <s>vaikrānta</s> etc., and the <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals), viz. the eight such as <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) etc. — should be treated many times, i.e., repeatedly, and calcined in sunlight. Furthermore, treated with salts, alkalies, and sours — the six salts such as <s>sauvarcala</s>, the alkalies such as <s>svarjikā</s>, the sours such as lemon — by these, treated many times, calcined in strong sunlight, the minerals and subsidiary minerals are purified — become free from defects. Furthermore, they, when smelted, release their essences — their own extracts — [that is], they emit [them].
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.10-11

children.text:
<vaikrānta:: śodhana>
svinnaṃ sakṣārāmlairdhmātaṃ vaikrāntakaṃ haṭhād dravati /
children.translated_text:
<<s>Vaikrānta</s> :: purification>
Sweated with alkalies and sours, when smelted, <s>vaikrānta</s> forcibly (<s>haṭhāt</s>) liquefies.
He states the purification of the minerals in order, beginning with '<s>svinna</s>' (sweated) etc.

children.text: sakṣārāmlairvaikrāntakaṃ svinnaṃ dolābhidhānena sveditaṃ kuryāt tat svinnaṃ vaikrāntaṃ haṭhāt prābalyāt dhmātaṃ sat dravati sāraṃ muñcati drutamātraṃ satvanirgamamātrameva śudhyati pūrvasaṃbandhāt dravati // GRhtCM_9.9:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>, sweated with alkalies and sours — sweated by the method called <s>dolā</s> (swing) — should be prepared. That sweated <s>vaikrānta</s>, when smelted forcibly (<s>haṭhāt</s>), i.e., with great power, liquefies — it releases its extract; at the very moment of liquefaction — at the very moment of essence-emergence — it is purified; by contextual connection, it liquefies.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.10-11

children.text: tad drutamātraṃ śudhyati kāntaṃ śaśaraktabhāvanayā // GRht_9.10 //
children.translated_text: That, at the very moment of liquefaction, is purified. <s>Kānta</s> (loadstone) [is purified] by treatment with hare's blood (<s>śaśarakta</s>).
<<s>Kānta</s> (loadstone) :: purification>
<<s>Sasyaka</s> (quicksilver/capala) :: purification>
<s>Sasyaka</s> also, well-treated with the red group [of herbs], sprinkled with oil and coloring [agents],

children.text: śudhyati vāraiḥ saptabhirataḥ paraṃ yujyate kārye // GRht_9.11 //
children.translated_text: is purified in seven rounds; thereafter it is fit for use in operations.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with '<s>sasyaka</s>' etc.

children.text: sasyakamapi capalamapi raktagaṇairdāḍimakiṃśukabandhūkādibhiḥ subhāvitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_9.10-11:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sasyaka</s> — also <s>capala</s> — should be well-treated with the red group [of herbs] — pomegranate (<s>dāḍima</s>), <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame-of-the-forest), <s>bandhūka</s> (midday flower), and the like.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ sneharāgasaṃsiktaṃ snehaḥ kaṅguṇitumbunyādīnāṃ rāgo raktavarṇadravaḥ tābhyāṃ vahnau taptaṃ sasyakaṃ saṃsiktaṃ secitamiti ghṛtaiḥ saṃsiktaṃ komalaṃ bhāvanāyogyaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_9.10-11:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? 'Sprinkled with oil and coloring [agents]' — 'oil' [refers to that] of <s>kaṅguṇi</s>, <s>tumbuṇī</s>, and the like; '<s>rāga</s>' is a red-colored liquid; by both of these, the <s>sasyaka</s>, heated in fire, should be sprinkled — doused. [When sprinkled] with ghee, it becomes soft and suitable for treatment.

children.text: katibhirvāraiḥ subhāvitaṃ kuryāt saptabhiḥ saptasaṃkhyākaiḥ // GRhtCM_9.10-11:4 //
children.translated_text: In how many rounds should it be well-treated? In seven — seven in number.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ kārye bījādike yujyate // GRhtCM_9.10-11:5 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, it is fit for use in operations such as seed-making and the like.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.12
<<s>Vimala</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>darada</s>, <s>mākṣika</s> :: purification>
First with alkalies and oils, then treated with sour [substances], <s>vimala</s> (silver pyrites)

children.text: śudhyati tathā ca rasakaṃ daradaṃ mākṣikamapyevam // GRht_9.12 //
children.translated_text: is purified; and likewise <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), <s>darada</s> (cinnabar), and <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites) also [are purified] in this way.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with '<s>kṣāraiḥ</s>' (with alkalies) etc.

children.text: vimalaṃ raupyamākṣikaṃ ādau prathamaṃ kṣāraiḥ svarjikādibhiḥ snehaistailaiḥ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ bhāvitaṃ kuryāt paścādamlena jambīrādinā bhāvitaṃ kuryāt evaṃvidhaṃ kṛtaṃ sat śudhyati // GRhtCM_9.12:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s> — silver pyrites (<s>raupyamākṣika</s>) — should first be treated with alkalies such as <s>svarjikā</s> (soda ash) and oils; then afterward treated with sour [substances] such as lemon and the like. Having been thus prepared, it is purified.

children.text: tathā tenaiva vidhinā rasakaṃ kharparakaṃ śudhyati daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ caivaṃ mākṣikamapyeva śudhyati // GRhtCM_9.12:3 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, by that same procedure, <s>rasaka</s> — calamine (<s>kharparaka</s>) — is purified; <s>darada</s> — cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>) — also thus; and <s>mākṣika</s> also is similarly purified.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.13
<Copper :: coloring (<s>rañjana</s>), purification>
Even a thin leaf [of gold/silver], anointed with salts, alkalies, sours, and the milks of <s>arka</s> (swallow-wort) and <s>snuhī</s> (milkweed),

children.text: dhmātaṃ nirguṇḍīrasasaṃsiktaṃ bahuśo bhaveddhi raktaṃ ca // GRht_9.13 //
children.translated_text: smelted, sprinkled many times with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (five-leaved chaste tree) juice, becomes truly red.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the purification of gold and silver, beginning with '<s>tanu</s>' (thin) etc.
'<s>Lavaṇa</s>' etc.:

children.text: lavaṇāni sauvarcalādīni kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ amlāḥ jambīrādayaḥ ravirarkaḥ snuhī sudhā tayoḥ kṣīrāṇi etaiḥ tanurapi sūkṣmamapi patraṃ dalaṃ sāralohākhyayoḥ iti śeṣaḥ liptaṃ dhmātaṃ sat bahuśo'nekavāraṃ nirguṇḍīrase saṃsiktaṃ śephālīdrave siñcitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_9.13:3 //
children.translated_text: Salts — <s>sauvarcala</s> and the rest; alkalies — <s>svarjikā</s> and the rest; sours — lemon and the rest; '<s>ravi</s>' is <s>arka</s> (swallow-wort); '<s>snuhī</s>' is <s>sudhā</s> (milkweed); the milks of both. By these, even a thin — even a fine — leaf (<s>dala</s>) of the noble metals (<s>sāra-lohas</s>) — this is the completion — should be anointed. When smelted, it should be sprinkled many times — repeatedly — with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice, i.e., doused with <s>sephālikā</s> extract.
