children.text: tarhi svarṇaṃ rūpyaṃ ca raktaṃ āraktachaviyutaṃ bhavedityarthaḥ caśabdācchudhyati // GRhtCM_9.13:4 //
children.translated_text: Then, gold and silver become red — endowed with a deep red color — this is the meaning. And, by [the implied meaning of] 'ca,' [they are also] purified.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.14
<Lead, tin, bronze, copper :: purification>

children.text: śudhyati nāgo vaṃgo ghoṣo raviṇā ca vāramapi munibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Lead (<s>nāga</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), and bronze (<s>ghoṣa</s>) are purified — with <s>ravi</s> (copper) also — seven times, by the sages;
by sprinklings of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice and counter-charges of its root-powder.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the purification of metals, beginning with '<s>śudhyati</s>' (is purified) etc.

children.text: nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ nirguṇḍīrasasekaiḥ śephālīrasaṃsecanaiḥ śudhyati nirdoṣo bhavati vaṅgaśca śudhyati // GRhtCM_9.14:2 //
children.translated_text: Lead (<s>nāga</s>), i.e., <s>sīsaka</s> — by sprinklings of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice, i.e., by sprinkling with <s>sephālikā</s> extract — is purified, becomes free from defects. Tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) also is purified.

children.text: evaṃ raviṇā tāmreṇa saha ghoṣo'pi kāṃsyamapi śudhyati // GRhtCM_9.14:3 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, with '<s>ravi</s>' (copper/sun), bronze (<s>ghoṣa</s>) — that is, bell-metal (<s>kāṃsya</s>) also — is purified.

children.text: kativāraṃ secanaiḥ munibhiḥ saptasaṃkhyākaiḥ tanmūlarajaḥ nirguṇḍīśiphācūrṇaṃ tatpravāpaiḥ galiteṣu nāgavaṅgaravighoṣeṣu rajo nikṣepaṇaiśca catvāraḥ śudhyantīti // GRhtCM_9.14:4 //
children.translated_text: In how many rounds of sprinkling? Seven — seven in number. And by the counter-charges of its root-powder — the powder of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> root (<s>śiphā-cūrṇa</s>) — by casting [this] powder into the melted lead, tin, copper, and bronze — the four are purified.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.15
<<s>Tīkṣṇaloha</s> (steel) :: coloring>
Steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), treated with the red group [of herbs], [combined with] cow's urine, and calcined, is indeed colored (<s>rajyate</s>);
<<s>Tīkṣṇaloha</s> (steel) :: purification>
it is purified [by being] treated with plantain (<s>kadalī</s>) and <s>śikhi</s> (leadwort) juices and calcined, in three rounds.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with '<s>raktagaṇa</s>' (red group) etc.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ sārākhyaṃ raktagaṇagalitapaśujalabhāvitaṃ puṭitaṃ sat raktagaṇena saha galitaṃ militaṃ yat paśujalaṃ gomūtraṃ tena bhāvitaṃ tato vahnipuṭitaṃ sat rajyate rāgamāpnoti // GRhtCM_9.15:2 //
children.translated_text: Steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), also called '<s>sāra</s>' — treated with the red group [of herbs] and cow's urine, and calcined: combined with the red group, whatever cow's urine (<s>gomūtra</s>) [is used] — treated with that, then fire-calcined — it acquires color (<s>rāga</s>).

children.text: punastīkṣṇaṃ kadalīśikhirasabhāvitapuṭitaṃ vā rambhācitrakarasabhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ tato vahnipuṭitaṃ ca sat tribhirvāraiḥ śudhyatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_9.15:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, steel, treated with plantain (<s>rambhā</s>) and leadwort (<s>citraka</s>) juices, heat-calcined — then fire-calcined — is purified in three rounds — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 9.16
<Metals :: purification>

children.text: sarvaṃ śudhyati loho rajyati suragopasannibho vāpāt /
children.translated_text: All metals are purified, colored like an <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect/firefly), by the counter-charge of

children.text: mākṣikadaradena bhṛśaṃ śulvaṃ vā gandhakena mṛtam // GRht_9.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites) and <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) intensely; or copper (<s>śulva</s>), killed by sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: sāmānyena sarvalohānāṃ śodhanamāraṇamāha sarva ityādi // GRhtCM_9.16:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the general purification and killing of all metals, beginning with '<s>sarva</s>' (all) etc.

children.text: sarvo loho dhātuvargaḥ śudhyati mṛtaśca bhavati punaḥ rajyati ca // GRhtCM_9.16:2 //
children.translated_text: All metals — the group of mineral substances — are purified and also killed; furthermore, they are colored.

children.text: kena bhṛśaṃ atyarthaṃ yathā syāttathā mākṣikadaradena tāpyahiṅgulena kṛtvā yo vāpaḥ galiteṣu loheṣu mākṣikadaradaprakṣepaṇaṃ tasmāt suragopasaṃnibha indragopasadṛśaḥ sarvo loho bhavet // GRhtCM_9.16:3 //
children.translated_text: By what? Intensely — very thoroughly — by <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>darada</s>, i.e., copper pyrites and cinnabar; the counter-charge (<s>vāpa</s>) — the casting into melted metals of <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>darada</s> — by that, all metals become like an <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect) — resembling a firefly.

children.text: vā śulbaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣikadaradavāpena suragopasannibhaṃ syāt vā gandhena gandhakavāpena mṛtamapyeva syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_9.16:4 //
children.translated_text: Or, copper (<s>śulva</s>), i.e., <s>tāmra</s>, would become like an <s>indragopa</s> by the counter-charge of <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>darada</s>; or it would become killed (<s>mṛta</s>) by the counter-charge of sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 10.1
Now, the extraction of essence (<s>sattva-nirgama</s>) will be described.
<<s>Sattva</s> (essence) :: importance>
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s> (loadstone), <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites), <s>vimala</s> (silver pyrites), and the rest — without their essence (<s>sattva</s>),

children.text: śuddhā api no dvandve milanti na ca tān raso grasati // GRht_10.1 //
children.translated_text: even when purified, they do not combine in pairs, nor does mercury consume them.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
[The text that] has always granted happiness to the pure, and to the wicked likewise
suffering — even to the point of death — acting equally with anger.

children.text: vaikrāntādīnāṃ rasasaṃjñikānāṃ sattvapraśaṃsanam āha vaikrāntamityādi // GRhtCM_10.1:2 //
children.translated_text: He states the praise of the essence of the mineral substances designated as <s>rasa</s>, such as <s>vaikrānta</s> and the rest, beginning with '<s>vaikrānta</s>' etc.

children.text: vaikrāntakāntasasyakamākṣikavimalādayaḥ śuddhā api dvandve na milanti // GRhtCM_10.1:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vimala</s>, and the rest — even when purified, do not combine in pairs.

children.text: vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ sasyakaścapalaḥ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ vimalā raupyamākṣikam ityādayo gandhakādayaścoparasaṃjñakā na milanti ekaśarīratāṃ nāpnuvanti // GRhtCM_10.1:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline), <s>vajra</s> (diamond-type) mica born of the earth, <s>rajas</s>, <s>kānta</s> (magnet), <s>cumbaka</s> (lodestone), <s>sasyaka</s> (copper sulphate), <s>capala</s> (bismuth), <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite), <s>vimalā</s> (silver-pyrite) — the <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals) beginning with sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) and so forth — they do not merge, i.e., do not attain unity of body. // GRhtCM_10.1:4 //
Where? In the pair-combination (<s>dvandva</s>), i.e., in the fusion of both [substances]. // GRhtCM_10.1:5 //

children.text: punastān śuddhānapi rasaḥ sūto na grasati // GRhtCM_10.1:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, even purified, mercury (<s>sūta</s>) does not devour them. // GRhtCM_10.1:6 //
START GRht 10.2-3
Called '<s>nāga-nāsikā</s>' (serpent's nose), [it possesses] moon-water (<s>candrodaka</s>), [is] nectar-like (<s>amṛta</s>), [and has] acquired hardness;

children.text: rasavaikrāntakam evaṃ badhnāti rasaṃ svasattvena // GRht_10.2 //
children.translated_text: such <s>rasa-vaikrāntaka</s> binds mercury by means of its own essence. // GRht_10.2 //
<Mountain-water (<s>śailodaka</s>)>
Of varied forms, born on the peak of the summit of the mountain of the gods (<s>nirjara-śikhari</s>),

children.text: dhārodambhasi śreṣṭhaṃ tadaśma śailodakaṃ prāpya // GRht_10.3 //
children.translated_text: that stone, having obtained the mountain-water (<s>śailodaka</s>), is the best in rain-water. // GRht_10.3 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the preeminence of <s>vaikrānta</s> — '<s>nāga</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.2-3:1 //
<s>Vaikrāntaka</s> of such characteristics should be known. // GRhtCM_10.2-3:2 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ nāganāsikābhidhānaṃ nāgānāṃ phaṇināṃ nāsikā eva abhidhānaṃ saṃjñā yasya tat // GRhtCM_10.2-3:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? Called '<s>nāga-nāsikā</s>' — '<s>nāga</s>' means serpent; their nose (<s>nāsikā</s>) itself is the designation (<s>abhidhāna</s>) of which — that [substance] is so called. // GRhtCM_10.2-3:3 //

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ candrodakaṃ candramasaḥ sambandhi yadudakaṃ balaṃ tasmādevāmṛtaṃ // GRhtCM_10.2-3:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what character? '<s>Candrodaka</s>' — the water associated with the moon, [meaning] the potency [derived from] that, hence '<s>amṛta</s>' (nectar-like). // GRhtCM_10.2-3:4 //

children.text: āptakāṭhinyaṃ prāptaṃ kāṭhinyaṃ yena pūrvametacca mṛdūtpannamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.2-3:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Acquired hardness' — it has acquired hardness; but previously, it arose as a soft [substance] — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.2-3:5 //

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ rasavaikrāntaṃ rasasaṃjñakaṃ vaikrāntaṃ rasaṃ sūtaṃ badhnāti // GRhtCM_10.2-3:6 //
children.translated_text: Such <s>rasa-vaikrānta</s>, i.e., the <s>vaikrānta</s> designated as '<s>rasa</s>' — it binds <s>rasa</s>, i.e., mercury (<s>sūta</s>). // GRhtCM_10.2-3:6 //
By what? By its own essence (<s>sva-sattva</s>), i.e., by its own core-substance. // GRhtCM_10.2-3:7 //
He states the varieties of <s>vaikrānta</s> — 'of various' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.2-3:8 //

children.text: pūrvamupavarṇitaṃ vaikrāntaṃ nānāvidhasaṃsthānamasti nānāvidhamanekaprakāraṃ saṃsthānaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yasya tat saṃsthānaṃ vyañjanaṃ liṅgaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cihnamākṛtiḥ iti mādhavanidānaṃ sitāsitaraktapītavarṇatvān nānāvidhasaṃsthānam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.2-3:9 //
children.translated_text: The previously described <s>vaikrānta</s> is of varied forms: '<s>nānāvidha</s>' means of many kinds; '<s>saṃsthāna</s>' means defining characteristic — as the <s>Mādhava-nidāna</s> states: '<s>saṃsthāna</s>, <s>vyañjana</s>, <s>liṅga</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, <s>cihna</s>, <s>ākṛti</s>' [are synonyms]. Due to being of white, dark, red, and yellow colors — 'of varied forms' — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.2-3:9 //

children.text: punarnirjaraśikhariśikharasambhūtaṃ nirjarāṇāṃ devānāṃ yaḥ śikharī parvatastasya śikharaṃ śṛṅgaṃ tatra sambhūtam utpannam // GRhtCM_10.2-3:10 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, 'born on the peak of the mountain of the gods' — <s>nirjara</s> means the gods; their mountain (<s>śikharī</s>), its peak (<s>śikhara</s>), i.e., summit — born there, i.e., produced. // GRhtCM_10.2-3:10 //

children.text: nānāvidhasaṃsthānaṃ kutaḥ dhārodambhasi dhārābhirudanta unmattamambho yatra samaye tasmin varṣākāle śailodakaṃ śilāsaṃbandhi yadudakaṃ jalaṃ tat prāpya śreṣṭhaṃ tadaśma vaikrāntābhidhānaṃ nānāvarṇaṃ bhavati yataḥ śilodakasya nānāvidhatvam // GRhtCM_10.2-3:11 //
children.translated_text: Why of varied forms? Having obtained mountain-water (<s>śailodaka</s>), i.e., water connected with rock — at the time when the waters rise and become agitated through rain-streams — in that rainy season, that stone, the one called <s>vaikrānta</s>, becomes of various colors, because the mountain-water itself is of various kinds. // GRhtCM_10.2-3:11 //
START GRht 10.4-5
<s>vaikrānta</s>: essence (<s>sattva</s>) extraction>
With a pair of bellows, forcefully, one should blow [upon the] <s>vaikrānta</s> well-bound with the five buffalo-products;
having added one-tenth [proportion of] alkalis of <s>svarjikā</s> (soda ash), <s>paṭu</s> (salt), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>guñjikā</s> (red seeds). // GRht_10.4 //
It attains hardness and releases essence in the form of sparks —

children.text: muktānikaraprāyaṃ grāhyaṃ tat kācam adhivarjya // GRht_10.5 //
children.translated_text: resembling a heap of pearls; that should be collected, discarding the glass [waste]. // GRht_10.5 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the extraction of the <s>vaikrānta</s> essence — 'bellows' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.4-5:1 //

children.text: tadvaikrāntaṃ pañcamāhiṣasubaddhaṃ dadhidugdhājyamūtraśakṛdbhiḥ pañcasaṃkhyākair māhiṣaiḥ saha subaddhaṃ piṇḍākṛti kṛtaṃ sat bhastrādvayena khallayugmena haṭhato balāt dhmātavyam // GRhtCM_10.4-5:2 //
children.translated_text: That <s>vaikrānta</s>, well-bound with the five buffalo-products — i.e., with curds, milk, ghee, urine, and dung, five in number, of the buffalo — well-bound, made into a pellet form, should be blown forcefully, i.e., with vigor, by a pair of bellows, i.e., by a pair of <s>khalla</s> (forge-bellows). // GRhtCM_10.4-5:2 //

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā daśāṃśasarjikapaṭuṭaṅkaṇaguñjikākṣārān dattvā daśāṃśavibhāgena sarjikālavaṇasaubhāgyaraktikāyavakṣārān piṣṭavaikrānte kṣepyetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.4-5:3 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having added one-tenth [proportion of] alkalis of <s>sarjikā</s>, <s>paṭu</s> (salt), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>guñjikā</s> — in one-tenth proportion, <s>sarjikā</s> (soda ash), <s>lavaṇa</s> (salt), <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax), <s>raktikā</s> (guñjā seeds), and barley alkali should be cast into the ground <s>vaikrānta</s> — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.4-5:3 //

children.text: dhmātaṃ sat kiṃ syāttadāha tadityādi // GRhtCM_10.4-5:4 //
children.translated_text: When blown, what happens? He says 'that' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.4-5:4 //

children.text: sphuliṅgakākāraṃ vahnikaṇanibhaṃ satvaṃ sāraṃ muñcati // GRhtCM_10.4-5:5 //
children.translated_text: It releases essence (<s>sattva</s>), i.e., core-substance, in the form of sparks (<s>sphuliṅgaka</s>), resembling fire-particles. // GRhtCM_10.4-5:5 //

children.text: punastatsatvaṃ kaṭhinatvaṃ gacchati kaṭhinaṃ syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.4-5:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that essence attains hardness, i.e., becomes hard — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.4-5:6 //

children.text: tatsatvaṃ ākārato muktānikaraprāyaṃ mauktikarāśisadṛśaṃ syāt evaṃvidhaṃ satvaṃ kācaṃ adhivarjya dūrīkṛtya tat nirmalaṃ grāhyamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.4-5:7 //
children.translated_text: That essence in form resembles a heap of pearls (<s>muktā-nikara</s>), i.e., is like a mass of pearls. Such essence, discarding, i.e., removing, the glass [waste] (<s>kāca</s>), should be collected as pure — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.4-5:7 //
A pair [of verses]. // GRhtCM_10.4-5:8 //
START GRht 10.6
<s>vaikrānta</s>: binding of mercury>
The <s>rasa-vaikrāntaka</s> essence, thus mixed equally with gold, combined in pair-form,

children.text: nirvyūḍhaṃ ghanasatvaṃ tena raso bandhamupayāti // GRht_10.6 //
children.translated_text: the mica essence carried through with it — by that, mercury attains bondage. // GRht_10.6 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the application of the <s>vaikrānta</s> essence — '<s>rasa</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.6:1 //

children.text: tadrasavaikrāntakaṃ sattvaṃ hemnā samaṃ svarṇena samabhāgaṃ dvandvānvitaṃ sat dvandvamelāpakauṣadhasahitaṃ sat evamamunā vidhānena milati rase iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_10.6:2 //
children.translated_text: That <s>rasa-vaikrāntaka</s> essence, equal with gold, i.e., in equal parts with gold, combined in pair-form, i.e., equipped with pair-combination medicines — in this manner, by this procedure, it merges in mercury — the remainder to be supplied. // GRhtCM_10.6:2 //

children.text: punastena satvena saha ghanasatvamabhrasāraṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ nirvāhitaṃ sat tenobhayasatvasaṃyogena rasaḥ sūto bandhamupayāti bandhanamāpnoti // GRhtCM_10.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with that essence, the mica essence (<s>ghanasattva</s>), i.e., the core of mica, carried through, i.e., processed — by the combination of both essences, mercury (<s>sūta</s>) attains bondage, i.e., achieves the state of being bound. // GRhtCM_10.6:3 //
START GRht 10.7
<minerals: essence extraction (<s>sattva-pātana</s>)>
Of all metals beginning with diamond-type mica (<s>vajrābhra</s>), magnet (<s>kānta</s>), copper sulphate (<s>sasyaka</s>), and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>),

children.text: pātayati satvameṣāṃ piṇḍī dhmātā dṛḍhāṅgāraiḥ // GRht_10.7 //
children.translated_text: a pellet blown [upon] with firm charcoals extracts the essence of these. // GRht_10.7 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for essence extraction — '<s>vajra</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.7:1 //

children.text: dṛḍhāṅgārair iti dṛḍhakathanāt khadirādīnāṃ pūrvoktatvādbhastrādvayena ca dhmātā satī vajrābhrakāntasasyakamākṣikaprabhṛtisakaladhātūnāṃ vajrasaṃjñakaṃ yadabhraṃ tadvajrābhraṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ sasyakaṃ capalā mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ itiprabhṛtayaḥ sakaladhātavaḥ sarvoparasāsteṣāṃ piṇḍī satvaṃ pātayati // GRhtCM_10.7:2 //
children.translated_text: 'With firm charcoals' — since firm [charcoal] is specified, [it refers to] those of <s>khadira</s> (acacia) and others as previously described; blown with a pair of bellows — being in that condition — of all metals beginning with diamond-type mica (<s>vajrābhra</s>), magnet (<s>kānta</s>), copper sulphate (<s>sasyaka</s>), and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>): the mica called <s>vajra</s>-type is <s>vajrābhra</s>; <s>kānta</s> is the lodestone; <s>sasyaka</s> is <s>capalā</s> (bismuth); <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite — 'and so forth' [indicates] all metals, all subsidiary minerals — their pellet extracts the essence. // GRhtCM_10.7:2 //
START GRht 10.8
<s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) essence: special alchemical potency>
Except for the <s>mākṣika</s> essence, none of the others possesses the power to destroy metals;

children.text: na patati tāvatsatvaṃ bhastrānte na yāvad āhriyet // GRht_10.8 //
children.translated_text: the essence does not fall as long as [the bellows] are not brought close to the end [of the blowing]. // GRht_10.8 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He praises the <s>mākṣika</s> essence for its potency — 'except for' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.8:1 //

children.text: mākṣikasatvaṃ tāpyasāraṃ hitvā tyaktvā anyeṣāṃ rasoparasānāṃ śaktiḥ sāmarthyaṃ nāsti // GRhtCM_10.8:2 //
children.translated_text: Except for the <s>mākṣika</s> essence, i.e., the core of <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite) — setting it aside, the others, the <s>rasas</s> and <s>uparasas</s>, do not possess the power, the capacity. // GRhtCM_10.8:2 //

children.text: kiṃbhūtā śaktiḥ lohaghnīti lohān hantīti vigrahaḥ // GRhtCM_10.8:3 //
children.translated_text: What kind of power? '<s>Loha-ghnī</s>' — one that destroys metals — this is the analysis. // GRhtCM_10.8:3 //

children.text: punastāvatsattvaṃ na patati yāvadbhastrā ante satvasamīpe na āhrīyeta na prāpyeta tasmādalpenāgninā satvāpravṛttirityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.8:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the essence does not fall out as long as the bellows are not brought near the essence at the end [of blowing]. Therefore, with insufficient fire there is no extraction of essence — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.8:4 //
START GRht 10.9
<s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) essence: physical properties>

children.text: raktaṃ mṛdu nāgasamaṃ satvaṃ yasmāddhi mākṣikātpatitam /
children.translated_text: Red, soft, lead-like — such is the essence that falls from <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite);
from <s>gandhāśman</s> (sulphur-stone) likewise — one should carefully make it soft. // GRht_10.9 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Having set aside the <s>mākṣika</s> essence, he states the behavior of other essences — 'red' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.9:1 //

children.text: raktaṃ lohitaṃ nāgasamaṃ sīsakatulyaṃ mṛdu komalaṃ evaṃvidhaṃ satvaṃ yasmāddhetor mākṣikāt patati tāpyāt nirgacchati tadvattasmāddhetor vā tasmādvidhānataḥ gandhāśmano gandhakasya yatnena mṛdubhāvaṃ kāryaṃ yathā gandhako'pi mṛdurbhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.9:2 //
children.translated_text: Red, i.e., crimson; lead-like (<s>nāga-sama</s>), i.e., similar to <s>sīsaka</s> (lead); soft (<s>mṛdu</s>), i.e., tender — such essence falls from <s>mākṣika</s>, i.e., emerges from <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite). Likewise, i.e., from that very procedure, <s>gandhāśman</s> (sulphur-stone) should be carefully made soft, so that sulphur too becomes soft — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.9:2 //
START GRht 10.10
<s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) essence: extraction procedure>
<s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite) well-calcined with salt and acid, ground with acid according to procedure,

children.text: muñcati soṣṇe grāsam āyasapātre tu piṣṭikā bhavati // GRht_10.10 //
children.translated_text: releases [its] morsel when hot, in an iron vessel — a pellet forms. // GRht_10.10 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for <s>mākṣika</s> essence — 'salt' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.10:1 //

children.text: mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ lavaṇāmlena lavaṇaṃ mukhyatvāt granthāntarasāmyācca saindhavaṃ amlo jambīrādiḥ tena marditaṃ punaramlena jambīrādinā vidhinā uktarītyā puṭitaṃ vahnau pratāpitaṃ sat muñcati pūrvaślokasaṃbandhāt sattvaṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_10.10:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>, i.e., <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite), with salt and acid: salt, being primary and by analogy with other texts, is <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt); acid is <s>jambīra</s> (citron) and such — ground with these. Furthermore, with acid, i.e., <s>jambīra</s> and such, by the procedure, i.e., by the described method, calcined, i.e., heated in fire — it releases essence, the remainder being connected with the previous verse. // GRhtCM_10.10:2 //
The essence thus extracted should be collected. // GRhtCM_10.10:3 //
With salt and acid, sulphur too becomes soft. // GRhtCM_10.10:4 //

children.text: tu punaḥ soṣṇe āyasapātre vahnau tāpite lohapātre piṣṭikā bhavati raktavarṇarajorūpety arthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.10:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, when hot, i.e., in an iron vessel heated in fire, a pellet forms — of red-colored powdery form — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.10:5 //
START GRht 10.11
<essences: colors of different types>

children.text: tutthāddhi tāpyajasamaṃ samasṛṣṭaṃ patati vai satvam /
children.translated_text: From <s>tuttha</s> (blue vitriol) indeed, an essence equal to <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) [in appearance], produced in equal mixture, falls;
of mica, <s>vaikrānta</s>, magnet, and such — their [essence] resembles iron. // GRht_10.11 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the essence extraction of <s>tuttha</s> and others — '<s>tuttha</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.11:1 //

children.text: tutthāt tutthaṃ śikhigrīvaṃ tasmāt tāpyajasamamiti mākṣikasatvavat mākṣikasatvavidhānenāsya satvapāta ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.11:2 //
children.translated_text: From <s>tuttha</s> — <s>tuttha</s> is 'peacock-neck' [colored blue vitriol] — from that, 'equal to pyrite-born' means: by the same procedure as for <s>mākṣika</s> essence, its essence is extracted — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.11:2 //

children.text: samasṛṣṭaṃ samaṃ tāpyena tulyaṃ varṇamārdavābhyāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ kathitamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.11:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Equally produced' — equal to <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), similar in both color and softness — thus described — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.11:3 //
Such <s>tutthaka</s> (blue vitriol) essence falls [out]. // GRhtCM_10.11:4 //

children.text: abhraketyādi abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ vaikrāntaṃ rasavaikrāntaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ itiprabhṛtīnām ityādīnāṃ tattvaṃ patrasatvapātanayoge lohanibhaṃ muṇḍavarṇam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.11:5 //
children.translated_text: Of mica and so forth: mica is well-known; <s>vaikrānta</s> is <s>rasa-vaikrānta</s>; <s>kānta</s> is the lodestone — 'and such' means and other [minerals] — their essence, by the foil-essence-extraction method, resembles iron (<s>loha</s>), i.e., is of the color of <s>muṇḍa</s> (iron) — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_10.11:5 //
START GRht 10.12
<gold-pyrite (?): essence extraction (?))>
Treated with the milk of <s>strīvajrī</s> (female Euphorbia) and treated with castor oil, blown a hundred times,

children.text: evaṃ tribhiriha vāraiḥ śulvasamaṃ bhavati rañjakaṃ haimam // GRht_10.12 //
children.translated_text: thus, in three rounds here, it becomes copper-like, golden, and a coloring agent. // GRht_10.12 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another procedure for <s>mākṣika</s> — '<s>strī</s>' and so forth.

children.text: tāpyaṃ strīvajrīdugdhabhāvitaṃ strī nārī vajrī sehuṇḍaḥ tayordugdhaṃ tena bhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_10.12:1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite) should be treated with the milk of <s>strīvajrī</s>: '<s>strī</s>' means woman, '<s>vajrī</s>' is the <s>sehuṇḍa</s> (Euphorbia) plant; their milk — treated with that, i.e., sun-dried after saturation. // GRhtCM_10.12:1 //

children.text: punareraṇḍasnehena śataṃ śatavāraṃ bhāvitaṃ ca kuryāt // GRhtCM_10.12:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with castor oil (<s>eraṇḍa-sneha</s>), treated a hundred times, i.e., saturated a hundred times. // GRhtCM_10.12:2 //

children.text: tato vāraistribhireva dhmātaṃ sat haimaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ tasyedaṃ haimaṃ satvaṃ śulbasamaṃ tāmranibhaṃ bhavati rañjakaṃ rase rāgadāyī syātkanake'pi ca // GRhtCM_10.12:3 //
children.translated_text: Then, blown only three times — the golden [substance], i.e., gold-pyrite — its essence becomes copper-like (<s>śulba-sama</s>), i.e., resembling copper; it becomes a coloring agent (<s>rañjaka</s>) — it gives color to mercury, and also to gold. // GRhtCM_10.12:3 //
START GRht 10.13
<s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>rasaka</s> (zinc): essence extraction>
<s>Tāpya</s> (pyrite), treated a hundred times with banana (<s>kadalī</s>) juice, cooked with honey and castor oil,

children.text: tāpyaṃ muñcati satvaṃ rasakaṃ caivaṃ trisantāpaiḥ // GRht_10.13 //
children.translated_text: releases its essence; <s>rasaka</s> (zinc) too, in this manner, with three heatings. // GRht_10.13 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another procedure — 'banana' and so forth. // GRhtCM_10.13:1 //

children.text: tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ kadalīrasaśatabhāvitamadhvairaṇḍatailaparipakvam iti prathamaṃ rambhādraveṇa śatavāraṃ bhāvitaṃ paścāt madhvairaṇḍatailābhyāṃ saha paripakvaṃ samyak pācitaṃ sat satvaṃ muñcati // GRhtCM_10.13:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpya</s>, i.e., <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), treated a hundred times with banana juice, cooked with honey and castor oil: first, saturated a hundred times with plantain juice; then, well-cooked with honey and castor oil together — it releases its essence. // GRhtCM_10.13:2 //

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā trisaṃtāpaiḥ trivāraṃ dhamanaiḥ // GRhtCM_10.13:3 //
children.translated_text: By what means? With three heatings (<s>trisaṃtāpa</s>), i.e., three rounds of blowing. // GRhtCM_10.13:3 //

children.text: evaṃ rasakaṃ kharparakamapi satvaṃ muñcatīti // GRhtCM_10.13:4 //
children.translated_text: In this manner, <s>rasaka</s>, i.e., <s>kharpara</s> (zinc carbonate), also releases essence. // GRhtCM_10.13:4 //
START GRht 10.14
<minerals: essence extraction>
With wool (<s>ūrṇā</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), <s>purā</s> (?), lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), and <s>sarjarasa</s> (sal resin), [together] with all metals, ground,

children.text: chāgīkṣīreṇa kṛtā piṇḍī śastā hi satvavidhau // GRht_10.14 //
children.translated_text: a pellet made with goat's milk — this is recommended in the essence-extraction procedure. // GRht_10.14 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He describes the bolus for essence-extraction (<s>satva-pātana</s>), saying 'wool' and so forth. || GRhtCM 10.14:1 ||

children.text: ūrṇā iti ūrṇā meṣaroma ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ guḍaḥ pratītaḥ puro gugguluḥ lākṣā jatu sarjaraso rālaḥ etaiḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ sarvadhātubhiḥ rasoparasairvā svarṇādibhiḥ saha piṣṭaiḥ peṣitaiḥ punaḥ chāgīkṣīreṇa ajāpayasā kṛtā yā piṇḍī sā satvavidhau satvapātanakarmaṇi śastā pradhānā // GRhtCM_10.14:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Wool' (<s>ūrṇā</s>) means sheep's wool; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is borax (<s>saubhāgya</s>); <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) is well-known; <s>pura</s> is <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium resin); <s>lākṣā</s> is shellac; <s>jatu</s> is <s>sarjarasa</s> (sal resin); <s>rāla</s> is dammar resin. With these, of what character? Ground together with all metals (<s>dhātus</s>), <s>rasas</s> (minerals) and <s>uparasas</s> (semi-metals), gold and such — furthermore, the bolus (<s>piṇḍī</s>) made with goat's milk (<s>chāgīkṣīra</s>), i.e., the milk of a she-goat — that is recommended, i.e., paramount, in the essence-procedure (<s>satva-vidhi</s>), i.e., in the operation of extracting essence. || GRhtCM 10.14:2 ||
It indeed causes the essence of metals, minerals, and semi-metals to fall [i.e., to be extracted]. || GRhtCM 10.14:3 ||
START GRht 10.15-17
<minerals: <s>satva</s> (essence): extraction>
Having carefully collected the powdered essence-material of thirty <s>palas</s> (measures),
combined with seven <s>palas</s> of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and joined with three <s>palas</s> of <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seeds); || GRht 10.15 ||
mixing with [equal] <s>palas</s> of sesame powder and iron-slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), with small fish, stirring, and with double portions,
the bolus bound with wheat [flour] and soaked repeatedly in the five cow-products (<s>gopañcaka</s>); || GRht 10.16 ||
by the method of blowing in a smelting furnace (<s>koṣṭhaka</s>), with intense bellows-fire, the essence falls,

children.text: saṃdravati cābhrasattvaṃ tathaiva sarvāṇi satvāni // GRht_10.17 //
children.translated_text: and the mica-essence (<s>abhrasatva</s>) melts; likewise all essences. || GRht 10.17 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method, saying 'powdered' and so forth. || GRhtCM 10.15-17:1 ||

children.text: cūrṇitasatvasamānaṃ cūrṇitaṃ piṣṭaṃ yat satvaṃ sāraṃ tatsamānaṃ viśuddhatvāt satvasamānaṃ dhāturasoparasacūrṇaṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_10.15-17:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Powdered essence-material' — the powdered, i.e., ground, essence (<s>satva</s>), i.e., core, that which is equal to it — meaning pure, equal to the essence in purity — the powder of metals, minerals, and semi-metals — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 10.15-17:2 ||

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ viśuddhaṃ cūrṇaṃ ādareṇa prītyā ādau saṃgṛhya ṭaṅkaṇapalasaptayutaṃ kuryāt saubhāgyasya palaiḥ saptasaṃkhyākaiḥ sahitaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.15-17:3 //
children.translated_text: Such purified powder, having first collected it with care, i.e., with affection — should be combined with seven <s>palas</s> of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), i.e., combined with seven <s>palas</s> of <s>saubhāgya</s> — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 10.15-17:3 ||

children.text: viśuddhe cūrṇe triṃśatpale saptapalaṃ saubhāgyaṃ yojyaṃ evaṃ ṭaṅkaṇavidhānena ca punaḥ guñjāpalatritayena raktikāpalatritayaparimāṇena yojitaṃ kuryād iti // GRhtCM_10.15-17:4 //
children.translated_text: In thirty <s>palas</s> of purified powder, seven <s>palas</s> of borax should be added. Likewise, by the borax method, furthermore, with three <s>palas</s> of <s>guñjā</s>, i.e., with the measure of three <s>palas</s> of <s>raktikā</s> (red seeds), it should be combined. || GRhtCM 10.15-17:4 ||

children.text: tilacūrṇakakiṭṭapalaiḥ tilaṃ pratītaṃ teṣāṃ cūrṇakaṃ kiṭṭaṃ muṇḍādīnāṃ malaṃ tayoḥ palaiḥ palamānairgodhūmabaddhapiṇḍī bahuśo bahuvāraṃ gopañcakabhāvitaṃ gavāṃ kṣīrājyadadhimūtraviṭkena bhāvitā kiṃ kṛtvā matsyair āloḍya matsyaiḥ kṣudrajalacarair āloḍya saṃmiśryetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.15-17:5 //
children.translated_text: With <s>palas</s> of sesame powder and iron-slag — sesame is well-known; their powder, and <s>kiṭṭa</s> which is the impurity of <s>muṇḍa</s> (cast iron) and such — with <s>palas</s> of both. The bolus bound with wheat, soaked repeatedly, i.e., many times, in the five cow-products (<s>gopañcaka</s>): cow's milk, ghee, curd, urine, and dung. Having done what? Having stirred, i.e., mixed, with small fish (<s>matsya</s>), i.e., small aquatic creatures — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 10.15-17:5 ||

children.text: koṣṭhake koṣṭhikāyantre dhamanavidhinā utkṣipyotkṣipya dhamanena bhastrānalena tat satvaṃ patati pūrvasaṃbandhāt tāpyādīnāṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_10.15-17:6 //
children.translated_text: In the smelting furnace (<s>koṣṭhaka</s>), i.e., the <s>koṣṭhikā</s>-apparatus, by the method of blowing, i.e., by repeated blowing with bellows-fire — that essence falls, i.e., of pyrites and such — from the previous context — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 10.15-17:6 ||
And furthermore, the mica-essence, i.e., the core of mica, melts. || GRhtCM 10.15-17:7 ||

children.text: tathaivoktavidhānena sarvāṇi samastāni satvāni sārāṇi patanti anuktānāṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_10.15-17:8 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, by the stated method, all, i.e., the totality of, essences fall — including those not [separately] mentioned — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 10.15-17:8 ||
START GRht 11.1-2
Now the process of seed-extraction (<s>bīja-nirvāhaṇa</s>) begins.
<gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>): for production of gold>

children.text: svīkṛtya sarvasarito gaṅgā jaladhau yathā tathā haimam /
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, having absorbed all rivers, enters the ocean, so the gold[-pyrite essence],

children.text: praviśati rase gṛhītvā saṃmiliti sarvalohaguṇān // GRht_11.1 //
children.translated_text: having taken in and combined all metal-qualities, enters the mercury. || GRht 11.1 ||

children.text: jīryati milati ca śulbe tatsatvaṃ kiṭṭatāṃ yāti /
children.translated_text: [When the gold-pyrite essence] is digested and merges with copper, its essence turns to slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>).
Well-rounded, undertaking righteous activities, wise, a knower of signs,
he was indeed a knower of wealth and <s>dharma</s>, a robber of the riches of [others'] gardens. || GRhtCM 11.1:1 ||
First he states the praise of gold[-pyrite essence], saying 'having absorbed' and so forth. || GRhtCM 11.1:2 ||

children.text: haimaṃ svarṇamākṣikasatvaṃ saṃmiliti kiṃkṛtvā sarvalohaguṇān sarvaloheṣu samastadhātuṣu saṃmilitā miśritāḥ ye guṇās tān gṛhītvā tathā rase praviśati yathā gaṅgā sarvā nadyaḥ saritaḥ svīkṛtya aṅgīkṛtya jaladhau samudre praviśati // GRhtCM_11.1:3 //
children.translated_text: The gold[-pyrite essence] (<s>haima</s>), i.e., the essence of gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika-satva</s>), merges — having done what? Having taken in the qualities of all metals, i.e., the qualities that are mixed in all metals — having taken those in, it enters the mercury, just as the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, having absorbed (<s>svīkṛtya</s>), i.e., having accepted, all rivers, enters the ocean. || GRhtCM 11.1:3 ||
He states the application of pyrite-essence (<s>tāpya-satva</s>), saying 'is digested' and so forth. || GRhtCM 11.1:4 ||

children.text: tat haimaṃ tāpyasatvaṃ śulbe tāmre milati sati sattvaṃ jīryati jāraṇatvamāpnoti rase iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_11.1:5 //
children.translated_text: That gold[-pyrite], i.e., the pyrite-essence, when it merges with copper (<s>śulba</s>), i.e., with <s>tāmra</s> — the essence is digested, i.e., attains the state of being digested — in the mercury — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 11.1:5 ||

children.text: tasmin satve śulbe milati sati kiṭṭatāṃ yāti lohamalasadṛśaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_11.1:6 //
children.translated_text: When that essence merges with copper, it turns to slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), i.e., becomes like the impurity of metal. || GRhtCM 11.1:6 ||
START GRht 11.2

children.text: hemakriyāsu kariṇā trapuṇā tārakriyāsu nirvyūḍham // GRht_11.2 //
children.translated_text: For gold-operations, [the seed] should be extracted (<s>nirvyūḍha</s>) with lead (<s>karin</s>); for silver-operations, with tin (<s>trapu</s>). || GRht 11.2 ||
<appropriate substances for gold-work and silver-work>
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: prathamaṃ tatsatvaṃ kariṇā nāgena saha hemakriyāsu svarṇakāryeṣu nirvyūḍhaṃ rase nirvāhitaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.2:1 //
children.translated_text: First, that essence, together with lead (<s>nāga</s>), for gold-operations, i.e., in gold-work — should be extracted (<s>nirvyūḍha</s>), i.e., accomplished in the mercury — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 11.2:1 ||

children.text: punastrapuṇā vaṅgena saha tārakriyāsu rūpyakāryeṣu nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt nāgavaṅgau sarvatra pītasitakāryeṣu praśastāvityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.2:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), for silver-operations, i.e., in silver-work — should be extracted. Lead and tin are recommended everywhere for yellow and white operations respectively — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 11.2:2 ||
START GRht 11.3
<preparation of a seed (<s>bīja</s>)>

children.text: ghanasatvaṃ khalu raviṇā rasāyane dvaṃdvakaṃ yojyam /
children.translated_text: The dense essence (<s>ghana-satva</s>), indeed, with copper (<s>ravi</s>), for the elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>), should be combined as a pair (<s>dvaṃdvaka</s>),
with bitite (<s>girijatu</s>), pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), ochre (<s>gairika</s>), and cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), processed by immersion in the red group. || GRht 11.3 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the application of mica-essence, saying 'dense essence' and so forth. || GRhtCM 11.3:1 ||

children.text: khalu niścaye vākyālaṅkāre vā ghanasatvam abhrasāraṃ raviṇā tāmreṇa saha rasāyane jarāvyādhināśane dvaṃdvakaṃ ghanasatvatāmraṃ yojyaṃ punaḥ raktagaṇapātabhāvitagirijatumākṣikagairikadaradaiḥ raktagaṇasya yaḥ pātaḥ pātanaṃ nikṣepo vā tena bhāvitāni gharmapuṭitāni girijatumākṣikagairikadaradāni girijatu śilājatu mākṣikaṃ pratītaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ etairbījaśeṣaṃ kuryād ityāgāmiślokājjñeyam // GRhtCM_11.3:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Indeed' (<s>khalu</s>) — used for emphasis or as an ornament of speech. The dense essence, i.e., the mica-core, together with copper (<s>ravi</s>), i.e., <s>tāmra</s>, for the elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>), i.e., for the destruction of old age and disease, should be combined as a pair, i.e., the mica-essence-and-copper pair. Furthermore, with bitite, pyrite, ochre, and cinnabar — processed by the immersion, i.e., the projection or sprinkling, of the red group, i.e., heated in a <s>puṭa</s> with those. With these, the remaining seed should be made — this is to be understood from the following verse. || GRhtCM 11.3:2 ||
START GRht 11.4
<gold: seed (<s>bīja</s>)>
Soft Nepali copper, magnetic iron (<s>kānta</s>), dense mica-essence, calcined lead (<s>nāga</s>), wrought iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), and gold —
one should make the remaining seed by quenching with cinnabar, <s>śilā</s> (realgar), orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), and pyrite. || GRht 11.4 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method, saying 'soft' and so forth. || GRhtCM 11.4:1 ||

children.text: mṛdulaṃ nepālasaṃjñikaṃ tāmraṃ kāntaṃ lohajāti ghanasatvamabhrasāraṃ punarmṛtaṃ nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ lohajāti kanakaṃ hema etattrayaṃ bījaṃ śulbāditrayaṃ ca bījasaṃjñakaṃ daradaśilātālamākṣikairvāpāt daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ śilā manohvā tālaṃ haritālaṃ etaiḥ kṛtvā vāpaḥ vahnitapte parikṣepaḥ tasmāt bījaśeṣaṃ kurvīta ubhayorbīje abhrasatvahemnaḥ śeṣe kuryādityarthaḥ vā evaṃ kṛte yaccheṣaṃ tiṣṭhati tadbījamiti // GRhtCM_11.4:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Soft' (<s>mṛdula</s>) means Nepali copper; <s>kānta</s> is a type of iron; dense essence (<s>ghana-satva</s>) is mica-core; furthermore, calcined lead (<s>mṛta-nāga</s>), i.e., <s>sīsaka</s>; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is a type of iron; <s>kanaka</s> is gold — these three are [one] seed, and the triad beginning with copper is also called seed. With cinnabar, <s>śilā</s> which is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>), orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>) — by quenching (<s>vāpa</s>) with these, i.e., projection into fire-heated [mercury] — one should make the remaining seed, i.e., in both seeds, of mica-essence and gold, the remainder should be made — that is the meaning. Or: the residue that remains after doing this is the seed. || GRhtCM 11.4:2 ||
START GRht 11.5
<gold, silver: seed>

children.text: mṛtanāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ vā śulvaṃ ghanasatvatārakanakaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Calcined lead, or tin, or copper, or dense mica-essence, silver, or gold —
all of that should be smelted (<s>dhmāta</s>) with bitite (<s>giri</s>), by means of further purifications through quenching. || GRht 11.5 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method, saying 'calcined lead' and so forth. || GRhtCM 11.5:1 ||

children.text: mayannāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tanmṛtanāgaṃ ca mṛtaṃ yadvaṅgaṃ raktagaṇāvāpamṛtaṃ ca yacchulvaṃ vā ghanasatvatārakanakaṃ ghanasatvamabhrasāraṃ tāraṃ rūpyaṃ kanakaṃ hema etannadugaṇasarvaṃ vā pratyekaṃ pṛthak giriṇā śilājatunā saha dhmātaṃ kuryāt adhikaśodhanaiḥ daradaśilātālairvāpāt bījaśeṣaṃ kuryāditi pūrvasaṃbandhaḥ // GRhtCM_11.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Lead, i.e., <s>sīsaka</s> — that calcined lead; and tin that has been calcined, quenched with the red group; and copper; or dense mica-essence, silver, and gold — all of these, or each one individually, should be smelted together with bitite (<s>śilājatu</s>); by means of further purifications, i.e., quenching with cinnabar, realgar, and orpiment, the remaining seed should be made — this is the connection with the previous [verse]. || GRhtCM 11.5:2 ||
START GRht 11.6-7
<gold: seed>

children.text: raktagaṇaṃ pītaṃ vā mākṣikarājāvartam atho vimalam /
children.translated_text: The red group, or the yellow [group], or pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli), or alternatively pure [silver-pyrite],
or any one of ochre (<s>gairika</s>), <s>kunaṭī</s> (realgar), <s>kṣiti</s> (crystal), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and <s>khaga</s> (vitriol); || GRht 11.6 ||
with these very [substances] extracted [into mercury], mercury acquires coloring (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, and attains binding (<s>bandha</s>);
with calcined metals, semi-metals, and such extracted, the chain-seed (<s>śṛṅkhalā-bīja</s>) is produced. || GRht 11.7 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
The red group means pomegranate, flame-of-the-forest, and such; or the yellow group, as follows:
'Flame-of-the-forest (<s>kiṃśuka</s>), <s>karṇikāra</s> (Pterospermum), and the pair of turmerics (<s>haridrā-dvitaya</s>),
this is proclaimed as the yellow group for the operations of the king of mercury.' || GRhtCM 11.6-7:1 ||

children.text: vā mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ vā rājāvartaṃ rājavarto lājavarada iti bhāṣāyāṃ atha vimalaṃ tāramākṣikaṃ ityekatamaṃ sarvameva vā gairikakunaṭīkṣitigandhakakhagaiḥ gairikaṃ pratītaṃ kunaṭī manohvā kṣitiḥ sphaṭakī gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ khagaḥ kāsīsaṃ etairiti // GRhtCM_11.6-7:2 //
children.translated_text: Or pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), i.e., <s>tāpya</s>; or <s>rājāvarta</s>, which in the vernacular is called <s>lājavarda</s> (lapis lazuli); or alternatively pure [silver-pyrite] (<s>vimala</s>), i.e., <s>tāramākṣika</s> (silver pyrite) — or any one of these; or [combined with] ochre, <s>kunaṭī</s> which is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>), <s>kṣiti</s> which is crystal (<s>sphaṭakī</s>), sulphur which is well-known, and <s>khaga</s> which is vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>) — with these. || GRhtCM 11.6-7:2 ||

children.text: etaiḥ pūrvoktaireva rase nirvyūḍhe raso rāgādi rañjanādi gṛhṇāti ādiśabdāt sāraṇaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ punarbandham upayāti bandhanamāpnoti punaḥ mṛtalohoparasādyaiḥ mṛtāśca te lohāśca dhātavaśca ta eva uparasā gandhakādyāḥ ādyaśabdāt rasā api tairnirvyūḍhaiḥ kṛtvā śṛṅkhalābījaṃ uttarottaraṃ rañjakaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.6-7:3 //
children.translated_text: With these very previously-stated [substances] extracted in mercury, the mercury acquires coloring (<s>rāga</s>) and the like — by the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), <s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing/liquefaction) is also to be understood. Furthermore, it attains binding, i.e., reaches the state of being bound. Furthermore, with calcined metals and semi-metals such as sulphur and the like — by the word 'and the like', minerals (<s>rasas</s>) are also [included] — with these, having been extracted, the chain-seed (<s>śṛṅkhalā-bīja</s>), i.e., successively [more powerful] coloring agents, is produced — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 11.6-7:3 ||
START GRht 11.8

children.text: <bīja for rañjana and bandhana of mercury>
children.translated_text: <seed for coloring and binding of mercury>
With iron rods, and with [substances] called 'non-paired' (<s>advandva</s>) and called 'mixed' (<s>saṅkara</s>),
extracted with mineral-metals — [the seed] becomes suitable for the operation of digestion. || GRht 11.8 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: rasalohairiti rasā vaikrāntādayo lohā dhātavaḥ pratītās tair nirvyūḍhaṃ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ advandvākhyaiḥ ekātmaiḥ saṃkarairvā sarvaiḥ saṃkaro'vakare ityamaraḥ evaṃ niṣpanne bījaṃ jāraṇayogyaṃ sadityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.8:1 //
children.translated_text: 'Mineral-metals' — <s>rasas</s> are <s>vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline) and such; <s>lohas</s> are metals, well-known — with those, extracted; of what character? 'Non-paired' (<s>advandva</s>), i.e., singular; or mixed (<s>saṅkara</s>), i.e., all [combined together] — 'saṅkara means refuse,' as the <s>Amarakośa</s> states. In the seed thus produced, [it] becomes suitable for digestion — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 11.8:1 ||
START GRht 11.9
This seed, immersed in the red group, having been quenched with it,
[when mercury is] merely fed and digested [with this seed], it colors the mercury and binds it. || GRht 11.9 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states a specific alternative method, saying 'the seed' and so forth. || GRhtCM 11.9:1 ||

children.text: idaṃ niṣpannabījaṃ raktagaṇe niṣecitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_11.9:2 //
children.translated_text: This produced seed should be immersed in the red group. || GRhtCM 11.9:2 ||

children.text: punastena raktagaṇena kṛtavāpaṃ kṛto vāpo yasmin tat // GRhtCM_11.9:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with that red group, quenching should be performed — that in which quenching has been done. || GRhtCM 11.9:3 ||

children.text: punastadbījaṃ cāritajāritamātraṃ pūrvaṃ ca paścāt jāritaṃ santaṃ sūtaṃ rañjayati rāgaṃ prāpayati badhnāti ceti // GRhtCM_11.9:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that seed, when merely fed and digested — first [fed], then digested — colors the mercury, i.e., brings about coloring (<s>rāga</s>), and binds [it]. || GRhtCM 11.9:4 ||
START GRht 11.10
<seed: further processing>
With calcined metals, minerals, and such that have been purified by the red unctuous [group], for all

children.text: bījānāṃ kuru vāpaṃ raktasnehe niṣekaṃ ca // GRht_11.10 //
children.translated_text: seeds, perform the quenching and the immersion in the red unctuous [group]. || GRht 11.10 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
That he states, saying 'red' and so forth. || GRhtCM 11.10:1 ||

children.text: raktasneha iti raktagaṇo dāḍimakiṃśukādikaḥ snehaḥ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ etairviśodhitāḥ paścānmṛtā ye dhātavo rasādayaśca rasoparasāstaiḥ sarveṣāṃ bījānāṃ pūrvoktānāṃ vāpaṃ kuru rase iti śeṣaḥ vā rakte raktavarṇe snehe snehavarge niṣekaṃ ca vidhānadvayamidam // GRhtCM_11.10:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Red unctuous' — the red group means pomegranate, flame-of-the-forest, and such; unctuous (<s>sneha</s>) means the oils of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and such; purified with these, and then calcined metals, minerals, <s>uparasas</s>, and such — with those, for all seeds previously mentioned, perform the quenching — in the mercury, this is the remainder. Or: in the red, i.e., red-colored, unctuous, i.e., unctuous group, [perform] the immersion as well — this is a twofold procedure. || GRhtCM 11.10:2 ||
START GRht 11.11
<silver: seeds>
Tin-mica, mica-silver, white-mountain-slag-struck, and white tin;
the red [group], struck with white pyrite-essence — [mercury then] delights in the extracted tin-mica. || GRht 11.11 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: pītakriyāyāṃ bījānyuktāni atha śvetakriyāyāṃ bījānyāha vaṅgetyādi // GRhtCM_11.11:1 //
children.translated_text: Seeds for yellow operations have been stated; now he states the seeds for white operations, saying 'tin' and so forth. || GRhtCM 11.11:1 ||

children.text: vaṅgābhramiti vaṅgaṃ raṅgaṃ abhraṃ gaganaṃ ete bījahetave iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_11.11:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Tin-mica' — <s>vaṅga</s> is tin; <s>abhra</s> is mica — these serve as the seed — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 11.11:2 ||

children.text: punarabhratāraṃ abhraṃ gaganaṃ tāraṃ rūpyaṃ iti ca sitaṃ śvetaṃ yacchailamalaṃ śilājatu tena āhatau samyak mṛtau sitavaṅgau tāraraṅgau kāryau punaḥ raktaṃ hema sitaṃ tāraṃ tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ tābhyāṃ hataṃ māritaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_11.11:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>abhratāra</s> — <s>abhra</s> is mica (<s>gagana</s>), <s>tāra</s> is silver (<s>rūpya</s>); and <s>sita</s> means white; and <s>śailamala</s> means bitumen (<s>śilājatu</s>): with that, [the metals] having been properly killed, white tin-sheets (<s>sitavaṅga</s>, i.e., <s>tāraraṅga</s>) should be prepared. Furthermore, red [means] gold, white [means] silver, <s>tāpya</s> [means] <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) — with these two, [the tin] should be killed, calcined. || GRhtCM 11.11:3 ||

children.text: punastāraṃ rūpyaṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ vaṅgaṃ cābhraṃ ca yatra tadevaṃvidhaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_11.11:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, silver (<s>tāra</s>) infused, and tin and mica wherever [present] — such [a preparation] should be made. || GRhtCM 11.11:4 ||
All this is to be employed in the silver-related operations on mercury: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 11.11:5 ||
[START GRht 11.12]
This infusion procedure (<s>nirvāhaṇa-vidhi</s>) has been set forth for the removal of all defects;
for the <s>bījas</s> (seed-metals) too, in the same way, mica-essence is to be combined first. || GRht 11.12 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that mica-essence is primary in the <s>bīja</s>, beginning with '<s>nirvāhaṇa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 11.12:1 ||

children.text: eṣaḥ kimarthaḥ aśeṣadoṣaśamanāya dhātvādīnāṃ samastadoṣanāśanāyetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.12:2 //
children.translated_text: This — for what purpose? For the removal of all defects — meaning for the destruction of all defects in metals and such: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 11.12:2 ||

children.text: evamamunā prakāreṇa yathā dhātunirvāhaṇavidhistathā bījānāṃ rase nirvāhaṇaṃ kuryāt sarvabījanirvāhaṇe abhrakasatvaṃ prathamaṃ nirvāhyamiti jñeyam // GRhtCM_11.12:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method — just as the metal-infusion procedure [is performed], so the infusion of <s>bījas</s> (seed-metals) into mercury should be done. In the infusion of all <s>bījas</s>, mica-essence is to be infused first: this should be known. || GRhtCM 11.12:3 ||
[START GRht 11.13]
<Crucible for <s>bījanirvāhaṇa</s> (seed-metal infusion)>
Having made a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>) fashioned from goat-bone ash, in the shape of a <s>mallaka</s> (cup),
with dense perforations suitable for leaf-joining (<s>dalayoga</s>), coated with a paste of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), poison (<s>viṣa</s>), and rosary pea (<s>guñjā</s>) — || GRht 11.13 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the infusion procedure, beginning with '<s>chāga</s>' (goat) and so forth. || GRhtCM 11.13:1 ||

children.text: evaṃvidhāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā dhātunirvāhaṇaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_11.13:2 //
children.translated_text: Having made such a crucible, the metal-infusion should be performed: this is the completion. || GRhtCM 11.13:2 ||

children.text: kiṃbhūtāṃ chāgāsthibhasmanirmitamūṣāmiti chāgo bastastasyāsthīni tadbhasmanā nirmitā kṛtā yā mūṣā tām // GRhtCM_11.13:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what kind? A crucible made from goat-bone ash — <s>chāga</s> is a goat; its bones; a crucible fashioned from the ash of those [bones]: that [crucible]. || GRhtCM 11.13:3 ||
Furthermore, of what kind? In the shape of a <s>mallaka</s> — resembling a cow's udder. || GRhtCM 11.13:4 ||
Furthermore, of what character? With dense perforations (<s>ghanarandhra</s>) — with closely-spaced holes. || GRhtCM 11.13:5 ||

children.text: punaḥ ṭaṅkaṇaviṣaguñjākṛtalepāṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ viṣaṃ saktukaṃ guñjā raktikā tābhiḥ kṛto lepo yasyāṃ sā tām // GRhtCM_11.13:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, coated with a paste of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, i.e., <s>saubhāgya</s>), poison (<s>viṣa</s>, i.e., <s>saktuka</s>), and rosary pea (<s>guñjā</s>, i.e., <s>raktikā</s>) — that which has a coating made from these: that [crucible]. || GRhtCM 11.13:6 ||

children.text: evaṃbhūtā mūṣā dalayoge patramelane kāryetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.13:7 //
children.translated_text: Such a crucible is to be made for <s>dalayoga</s> (leaf-joining) — for the joining of metal sheets: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 11.13:7 ||
[START GRht 12.1]
Now, <s>dvandvamelana</s> (pairing/alloying) will be described.
<Motivation for <s>dvandvamelana</s>>

children.text: yāvan nāṅgāṅgatayā na milanti lohāni sarvasattveṣu /
children.translated_text: So long as metals do not combine limb to limb in all essences (<s>sattva</s>),

children.text: tāvatsarvāṅgaṃ na ca carati raso dvandvayogena // GRht_12.1 //
children.translated_text: so long mercury does not pervade the whole body — [this is accomplished] by the <s>dvandva</s> (paired) method. || GRht 12.1 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He who, by the grace of speech, produces a likeness of nectar —
the very manhood that is dependent on the two-tongued one of nectar — this is not a fault. || GRhtCM 12.1:1 ||
Now he states the method of <s>dvandvayoga</s> (pairing), beginning with '<s>yāvat</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 12.1:2 ||
'<s>Yāvat</s>' [is used] in the sense of a limit. || GRhtCM 12.1:3 ||

children.text: lohāni hemādīni nāgāṅgatayā bhujaṅgaśarīratayā na milanti sugamatvena ekaśarīratāṃ nāpnuvanti // GRhtCM_12.1:4 //
children.translated_text: Metals such as gold and others, without becoming limb to limb — body to body like a serpent — do not combine easily, do not attain the state of being one body. || GRhtCM 12.1:4 ||

children.text: keṣu sarvasattveṣu abhrādīnāṃ sāreṣu sattvasya kāṭhinyādvinopāyaṃ naikatāṃ yānti lohāni // GRhtCM_12.1:5 //
children.translated_text: In what? In all essences (<s>sattva</s>) — in the extracts of mica and others; due to the hardness of the essence, without a method, the metals do not become one. || GRhtCM 12.1:5 ||
Therefore, until then, mercury does not pervade the whole body. || GRhtCM 12.1:6 ||

children.text: kena kṛtvā satveṣu lohāni milanti dvandvayogena daradādinā vā guḍapuraṭaṅkaṇādineti // GRhtCM_12.1:7 //
children.translated_text: By what means do metals combine in the essences? By the <s>dvandvayoga</s> (pairing method), or by cinnabar and such, or by jaggery, borax, and such. || GRhtCM 12.1:7 ||
[START GRht 12.2]
<Metals: preparation for <s>dvandva</s> (pairing)>
Metal, quenched with any one of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), <s>sasyaka</s> (vitriol), or <s>darada</s> (cinnabar),

children.text: saṃtyajati nibiḍabhāvaṃ satve saṃmilati sudhmātam // GRht_12.2 //
children.translated_text: abandons its dense state; when well-smelted, it combines with the essence. || GRht 12.2 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for combining with essence, beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 12.2:1 ||
<s>Loha</s> (metal) means gold and others. || GRhtCM 12.2:2 ||

children.text: mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ sasyakaṃ capalā daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ etena catuṣkeṇa vā ebhyo 'nyatamenoktarasoparasena vāpitaṃ sudhmātaṃ śobhanayuktyā dhmātaṃ ca sat niviḍabhāvaṃ saṃtyajati sattve saṃmilati ca // GRhtCM_12.2:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>); <s>rasaka</s> is calamine (<s>kharparika</s>); <s>sasyaka</s> is <s>capalā</s> (bismuth); <s>darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>). By this set of four, or by any one among these minerals and sub-minerals, quenched (<s>vāpita</s>) — well-smelted (<s>sudhmāta</s>), excellently fused — the metal abandons its dense state and combines with the essence. || GRhtCM 12.2:3 ||
[START GRht 12.3]
<<s>Dvandvamelāpaka</s> (pairing agent): preparation>
With jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), guggulu (<s>pura</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), and <s>sarjarasa</s> (resin), combined with equal portions of <s>dhātakī</s> (woodfordia),

children.text: strīstanyena tu piṣṭaiḥ rasāyane dvaṃdvitaṃ yojyam // GRht_12.3 //
children.translated_text: ground with woman's milk (<s>strīstanya</s>), the paired [metal] is to be employed for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). || GRht 12.3 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method, beginning with '<s>guḍa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 12.3:1 ||

children.text: idaṃ dvaṃdvitaṃ dvaṃdvīkṛtaṃ lohaṃ sattvena militaṃ rasāyane jarāvyādhināśane yojyam // GRhtCM_12.3:2 //
children.translated_text: This paired (<s>dvaṃdvita</s>) [metal] — made into a pair with its essence — is to be employed for <s>rasāyana</s>, the destruction of old age and disease. || GRhtCM 12.3:2 ||
By which pairing agents is it made into a pair? He says, beginning with '<s>guḍa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 12.3:3 ||

children.text: guḍaḥ pratītaḥ puro gugguluḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ lākṣā jatu sarjaraso rālā etaiḥ dhātakīsamāyuktaiḥ dhātakī pratītā tatsamāyuktaiḥ punaḥ strīstanyena nārīdugdhena piṣṭairmarditaiḥ etairdvandvamelāpakaiḥ kṛtvā // GRhtCM_12.3:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Guḍa</s> (jaggery) is well-known; <s>pura</s> is <s>guggulu</s>; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is borax (<s>saubhāgya</s>); <s>lākṣā</s> is lac; <s>sarjarasa</s> is resin (<s>rālā</s>). With these, combined with equal portions of <s>dhātakī</s> — <s>dhātakī</s> is well-known — combined with equal [parts of it]; furthermore, ground (<s>piṣṭa</s>) with woman's milk (<s>strīstanya</s>, i.e., <s>nārīdugdha</s>) — rubbed [together]; with these pairing agents, [the alloying] is done. || GRhtCM 12.3:4 ||
[START GRht 12.4]
<<s>Dvandvamelāpaka</s> (pairing agent)>
With wool (<s>ūrṇā</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), bitumen (<s>girijatu</s>), earwax (<s>karṇākṣimala</s>), cochineal insects (<s>indragopa</s>), and crabs (<s>karkaṭaka</s>),

children.text: nārīpayasā piṣṭaiḥ sarve dvandveṣu hi milanti // GRht_12.4 //
children.translated_text: ground with woman's milk — all [metals] combine in pairs. || GRht 12.4 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: sarve dvandveṣu satvaṃ prati dvandveṣu milanti ekībhavanti lohāni iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_12.4:1 //
children.translated_text: All [metals] combine in pairs — in pairs with respect to the essences — meaning the metals become one: this is the completion. || GRhtCM 12.4:1 ||
With which [substances]? With wool and so forth. || GRhtCM 12.4:2 ||

children.text: ūrṇā pratītā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ girijatu śilājatu karṇākṣimalaṃ manuṣyasya indragopako jīvaviśeṣaḥ karkaṭakaścakulīraḥ syātkulīraḥ karkaṭakaḥ ityamaraḥ etaiḥ // GRhtCM_12.4:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ūrṇā</s> (wool) is well-known; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is borax (<s>saubhāgya</s>); <s>girijatu</s> is bitumen (<s>śilājatu</s>); <s>karṇākṣimala</s> is the ear-dirt of a human; <s>indragopa</s> is a particular insect (<s>jīvaviśeṣa</s>); and <s>karkaṭaka</s> is a crab — '<s>kulīra</s> is a <s>karkaṭaka</s>' [says] the <s>Amarakośa</s>. With these. || GRhtCM 12.4:3 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ nārīpayasā strīdugdhena piṣṭaiḥ kalkitaiḥ trayo'pi dvandvamelāpakayogā iti // GRhtCM_12.4:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? Ground (<s>piṣṭa</s>) with woman's milk — made into a paste with woman's milk. All three <s>dvandvamelāpaka</s> (pairing agent) formulations [have been stated]. || GRhtCM 12.4:4 ||
[START GRht 12.5]

children.text: <dva.~ of rasavaikrānta and gold => bandhana of mercury>
children.translated_text: <<s>Dvandva</s> (pairing) of mercury-tourmaline (<s>rasavaikrānta</s>) and gold → binding of mercury>
Thus <s>rasavaikrānta</s> (mercury-tourmaline), endowed with the pairing [agent], combines equally with gold;

children.text: nirvyūḍhaṃ tatsatvaṃ tena raso bandhamupayāti // GRht_12.5 //
children.translated_text: that essence, infused [into gold], [causes] mercury to attain binding (<s>bandha</s>). || GRht 12.5 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method, beginning with '<s>rasa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 12.5:1 ||

children.text: evamuktavidhānena rasavaikrāntakaṃ dvandvānvitaṃ svakīyadvandvasahitaṃ milati pṛthagbhāvaṃ tyajati // GRhtCM_12.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the stated procedure, <s>rasavaikrāntaka</s> (mercury-tourmaline), endowed with its own pairing [agent], combines — abandons its separate state. || GRhtCM 12.5:2 ||
With what equally? Together with gold. || GRhtCM 12.5:3 ||

children.text: tadrasavaikrāntasattvaṃ hemnā saha nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt tena rasavaikrāntasattvahemayogena raso bandhamupayāti baddho bhavatīti // GRhtCM_12.5:4 //
children.translated_text: That <s>rasavaikrānta</s>-essence, infused with gold, should be prepared; by that combination of mercury-tourmaline-essence and gold, mercury attains binding — becomes fixed. || GRhtCM 12.5:4 ||
[START GRht 12.6]
<<s>Dvandvamelāpaka</s> (pairing agent)>
Recommended for all pairings: with bitumen (<s>girijatu</s>), sulphur (<s>lelītaka</s>), cochineal (<s>indragopa</s>), and others,
with buffalo earwax (<s>mahiṣīkarṇamala</s>) and others — the <s>bīja</s> is [made] with borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), orpiment (<s>āla</s>), and mineral poison (<s>viṣa</s>). || GRht 12.6 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states another specific method, beginning with '<s>śasta</s>' (recommended) and so forth. || GRhtCM 12.6:1 ||

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ bījaṃ śastaṃ kva sarvadvandve // GRhtCM_12.6:2 //
children.translated_text: Such a <s>bīja</s> is recommended — where? In all pairings. || GRhtCM 12.6:2 ||

children.text: punaretaiḥ kṛtvā bījaṃ śastaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_12.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>bīja</s> prepared with these [agents] would be recommended. || GRhtCM 12.6:3 ||

children.text: kaiḥ girijatulelītakendragopādyaiḥ girijatu śilājatu lelītako gandhakaḥ indragopaḥ surendragopo jīvaviśeṣaḥ ete ādyā yeṣāṃ taiḥ // GRhtCM_12.6:4 //
children.translated_text: With what? With bitumen (<s>girijatu</s>, i.e., <s>śilājatu</s>), sulphur (<s>lelītaka</s>, i.e., <s>gandhaka</s>), cochineal insect (<s>indragopa</s>, i.e., <s>surendragopa</s>, a particular insect) and others — these are the initial ones (<s>ādya</s>) of those [ingredients]: with them. || GRhtCM 12.6:4 ||

children.text: na kevalametair mahiṣīkarṇamalādyaiśca mahiṣyāḥ karṇayormala ādyo yeṣāṃ te ādyaśabdānnāsākṣimalaṃ ca // GRhtCM_12.6:5 //
children.translated_text: Not only with these, but also with buffalo earwax (<s>mahiṣīkarṇamala</s>) and others — the wax from the ears of a she-buffalo; by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (and others), nose- and eye-dirt also [is included]. || GRhtCM 12.6:5 ||

children.text: punaṣṭaṅkaṇālaviṣaiḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ ālaṃ haritālaṃ viṣaṃ kandajaṃ etaiḥ piṣṭairdvandvamelāpaḥ syāditi punaḥ saṃbandhaḥ // GRhtCM_12.6:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, i.e., <s>saubhāgya</s>), orpiment (<s>āla</s>, i.e., <s>haritāla</s>), and mineral poison (<s>viṣa</s>, i.e., <s>kandaja</s>): with these, ground, the <s>dvandvamelāpa</s> (pairing) would result — this is the further connection. || GRhtCM 12.6:6 ||
[START GRht 12.7]
<<s>Dvandvamelāpaka</s>>
With these [agents] combined with honey, silver and mica combine, and also pyrite and gold;
with castor oil (<s>eraṇḍataila</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, realgar (<s>śilā</s>), and cochineal (<s>indragopa</s>) — || GRht 12.7 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method, beginning with '<s>madhu</s>' (honey) and so forth. || GRhtCM 12.7:1 ||

children.text: etaiḥ pūrvoktair yogaiḥ madhusahitaiḥ kṣaudrayutaiḥ tārābhraṃ rūpyagaganaṃ milati // GRhtCM_12.7:2 //
children.translated_text: With these — the previously stated formulations — combined with honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>), silver-mica (<s>tārābhra</s>, i.e., silver and mica) combines. || GRhtCM 12.7:2 ||

children.text: ca punastāpyakanakaṃ mākṣikasvarṇaṃ idaṃ dvandvaṃ ca milati // GRhtCM_12.7:3 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, pyrite-gold (<s>tāpyakanaka</s>, i.e., <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>svarṇa</s>) — this pair also combines. || GRhtCM 12.7:3 ||

children.text: na kevalaṃ pūrvoktayogair milati punaretair eraṇḍatailaṭaṅkaṇakaṅkuṣṭhaśilendragopaiśca eraṇḍatailaṃ vātārisnehaḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ śilā manohvā indragopako jīvaviśeṣaḥ etaiśca madhusahitaiḥ kṛtvā dvandvaṃ milatītyavaśyam // GRhtCM_12.7:4 //
children.translated_text: Not only do they combine by the previously stated formulations, but also with these — castor oil (<s>eraṇḍataila</s>, i.e., castor oil), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (a specific poison-neutralizing mineral), realgar (<s>śilā</s>, i.e., <s>manaḥśilā</s>), and cochineal insect (<s>indragopa</s>) — with these, combined with honey, the pairing occurs: without doubt. || GRhtCM 12.7:4 ||
[START GRht 12.8]
<Pairing of mercury, gold, and mica>
Having ground pure gold with mercury, and having made it combined with equal mica,
one-fourth [part of] any one of the previously stated pairing [agents] should be prepared. || GRht 12.8 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that procedure, beginning with '<s>sūtena</s>' (with mercury) and so forth. || GRhtCM 12.8:1 ||

children.text: prathamaṃ sūtena rasena saha śuddhakanakaṃ niṣpiṣya saṃmardya punaḥ samābhrayojitaṃ kṛtvā samaṃ ca tadabhraṃ ca tena yojitaṃ kṛtvā paścātpādena caturthāṃśavibhāgena pūrvoktadvandvānyatamakaṃ kalpyaṃ pūrvoktadvandvam eraṇḍatailādikaṃ girijatvādikaṃ ca tebhyo 'nyatamakaṃ dvandvaṃ yojyamiti // GRhtCM_12.8:2 //
children.translated_text: First, having ground pure gold with mercury (<s>sūta</s>), having rubbed [them together]; furthermore, having made it combined with equal mica — equal [parts of] mica, combined [therewith]; thereafter, in a one-fourth proportion, any one of the previously stated pairing [agents] should be prepared — the previously stated pairing agents such as the castor-oil formula or the bitumen formula — any one pairing [agent] from among them is to be employed. || GRhtCM 12.8:2 ||
[START GRht 12.9-10]
<Pairing of gold and mica>
Having added twice the amount of purified <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) to gold, from among the minerals and sub-minerals,
one should grind it with the juice of <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade) and plantain stem (<s>rambhākanda</s>). || GRht 12.9 ||
This preparation, made into a ball, combines gold and mica in a diamond crucible (<s>vajramūṣā</s>).
He states another method, beginning with '<s>rasa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 12.9:1 ||

children.text: rasoparasasya vaikrāntagandhakādermadhye śuddhamākṣikaṃ nirdoṣaṃ tāpyaṃ hemno dviguṇaṃ kanakāddviguṇitaṃ dattvā dviguṇamākṣikayutaṃ hema dattvetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_12.9:2 //
children.translated_text: From among the minerals and sub-minerals such as tourmaline (<s>vaikrānta</s>), sulphur, and others — purified <s>mākṣika</s>, faultless pyrite, twice the amount of gold (<s>kanaka</s>), should be added — meaning gold with twice its amount of pyrite is added: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 12.9:2 ||

children.text: etadrasoparasādikaṃ kākamācyā vāyasyāḥ svarasena mṛdnīyāt mardanaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_12.9:3 //
children.translated_text: This mineral-and-sub-mineral preparation should be ground with the juice of <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade, <s>vāyasī</s>). || GRhtCM 12.9:3 ||
And also with plantain stem (<s>rambhākanda</s>, i.e., <s>kadalīkanda</s>): that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 12.9:4 ||
This preparation with the aforementioned herbs should be made into a ball-shaped [pellet]. || GRhtCM 12.9:5 ||

children.text: itividhānena hemābhraṃ milati hematāpyaṃ ceti // GRhtCM_12.9:6 //
children.translated_text: By this procedure, gold-mica (<s>hemābhra</s>) combines, as does gold-pyrite (<s>hematāpya</s>). || GRhtCM 12.9:6 ||
Where? In a diamond crucible (<s>vajramūṣā</s>). || GRhtCM 12.9:7 ||
Accordingly he says:
Three parts of clay, one part each of hemp-fiber (<s>śaṇa</s>) and <s>laddi</s>, and one part of burned husk-stone (<s>nirdagdhatuṣopala</s>),
half a part of iron slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) — having mixed [these], one should prepare the diamond crucible for essence-extraction.
Thus. || GRhtCM 12.9:8 ||
[START GRht 12.10]
With copper (<s>ravi</s>), silver (<s>śaśi</s>), and steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), thus, mica-essence and other essences combine. || GRht 12.10 ||
<Pairing of mica-essence with different substances>
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: evam amunā vidhinā raviśaśitīkṣṇaiḥ saha ravistāmraṃ śaśī rūpyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ lohajātiḥ etaiḥ sārdhaṃ gaganādisatvāni abhrādīnāṃ sārāṇi milantīti yugmam // GRhtCM_12.10:1 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method, with copper (<s>ravi</s>, i.e., <s>tāmra</s>), silver (<s>śaśi</s>, i.e., <s>rūpya</s>), and steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>, a type of metal) — together with these, the essences of mica and others, the extracts of <s>abhra</s> and others, combine: [this is] the pair-verse. || GRhtCM 12.10:1 ||
[START GRht 12.11]
<Pairing for <s>saṅkarabījas</s> (mixed seed-metals)>
The procedure for <s>saṅkarabījas</s> (mixed seed-metals) too [proceeds] thus, by combination with mica-essence —
Other [substances] than <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites) must be necessarily combined by the <s>mākṣika</s>-procedure everywhere.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the authority of mica-essence, beginning with '<s>saṅkara</s>' (mixed) etc.

children.text: saṅkarabījānāmapi vidhānaṃ kartavyārthopadeśa iti yāvat // GRhtCM_12.11:2 //
children.translated_text: The procedure for mixed seeds (<s>saṅkara-bīja</s>) is also to be stated — an instruction for what should be done — to that extent.

children.text: ityādi pūrvoktaṃ tu punaḥ gaganasatvayogena abhrakasattvena sārdhaṃ mākṣīkayogād anyaṃ yojyaṃ abhrasatvena saha mākṣīkaṃ na syāditi vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_12.11:3 //
children.translated_text: And so forth, as previously stated. But furthermore, with the mica-essence combination — together with mica-essence — by the <s>mākṣika</s>-procedure, other [substances] are to be combined; [the point is] that <s>mākṣika</s> should not be [combined] with mica-essence — this is the clarification.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 12.12
<s>Kānta</s> (loadstone) serves as the 'face' (<s>mukha</s>) for all essences; the first combination (<s>melaka</s>)
[consists of] the previously described paste combined with <s>mākṣika</s>, killed lead (<s>mṛta-nāga</s>), orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), and realgar (<s>śila</s>).

Thus ends the twelfth chapter (<s>avabodha</s>), dealing with the topic of pairs (<s>dvandva</s>), in the <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Govindabhagavatpāda</s>, the <s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya</s>.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Beginning with '<s>kānta</s>' etc.

children.text: mākṣikeṇa mṛtaṃ yannāgaṃ tālaṃ haritālaṃ śilā manohvā ca tattathā pūrvoktakalkasahitaṃ yatkalkaṃ rasoparasādīnāṃ tena sahitaṃ yuktaṃ kāntamukhaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text:
'<s>Mākṣika</s>-killed' — lead (<s>nāga</s>) killed by <s>mākṣika</s>; '<s>tāla</s>' is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>); '<s>śilā</s>' is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>). That, combined with the previously described paste — the paste of minerals, subsidiary minerals, and the like — along with <s>kānta</s> as the 'face.' As [stated]:
'In the absence of mica-essence, one should apply <s>kānta</s>-essence;
In the absence of mica-essence, <s>kānta</s>-essence should be employed;
and in the absence of <s>kānta</s>-essence, steel (<s>tīkṣṇa-loha</s>) should be employed.'
Thus.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 13.1
<s>Mākṣika</s>-<s>kānta</s>-steel; steel-<s>mākṣika</s>-mica is a seed;
<s>mākṣika</s>-<s>kānta</s>-copper; steel-mica is a <s>mahābīja</s> (great seed).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: madhuni mādhava eva madhuvrataḥ prakurute mudito madhuraṃ ravam /
children.translated_text: In honey, the <s>mādhava</s>-bee itself, the honey-seeker, delightedly produces a sweet hum;

children.text: vararavo'pi satāṃ ca samāgamaṃ śabalatā kimupaiti na cārutām // GRhtCM_13.1:1 //
children.translated_text: does not even a fine voice, and the company of the virtuous, attain loveliness when mixed?
Among the mixed seeds, he states those designated as <s>mahābīja</s> (great seeds), beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>' etc.

children.text: etattrikaṃ mahābījaṃ kimetat mākṣīkakāntatīkṣṇaṃ mākṣīkakāntaśulbaṃ tīkṣṇābhrakaṃ ca mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ lohajātir abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ etattritayaṃ bījaṃ mahābījaṃ etattritrimukhaṃ pratyekaṃ mahāsaṃjñam // GRhtCM_13.1:3 //
children.translated_text: This triad is the <s>mahābīja</s>. What is it? <s>Mākṣika</s>-<s>kānta</s>-steel, <s>mākṣika</s>-<s>kānta</s>-copper, and steel-mica. '<s>Mākṣika</s>' is copper pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>); '<s>kānta</s>' is loadstone (<s>cumbaka</s>); '<s>śulba</s>' is copper (<s>tāmra</s>); '<s>tīkṣṇa</s>' is a type of iron; '<s>abhraka</s>' is mica (<s>gagana</s>). This triad constitutes a seed, a <s>mahābīja</s>. Each of these three-faced [combinations] individually bears the designation '<s>mahā</s>' (great).
The specific [point] here:
'I shall state the cooking of the seed for the purpose of digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) of mercury.',
'This is the <s>sūtra</s>-sequence: by a seed that has been uniformly digested, [mercury] is purified.'
Thus.

children.text: avāntaratvena ca pratyekaṃ dravyaṃ bījasaṃjñābhimatam // GRhtCM_13.1:5 //
children.translated_text: And in a subsidiary sense, each individual substance is considered to bear the designation of 'seed.'
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 13.2
<s>Mākṣika</s>-<s>kānta</s>-copper, copper-mica-<s>mākṣika</s> also,
<s>kānta</s>-mica-<s>mākṣika</s>, <s>tāpya</s>-copper-mica — [these are] <s>mahābījas</s> (great seeds).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>' etc.

children.text: mākṣīkakāntaśulbaṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ etadapi mahābījaṃ jñeyam // GRhtCM_13.2:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>-<s>kānta</s>-copper: '<s>mākṣika</s>' is copper pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>); '<s>kānta</s>' is loadstone (<s>cumbaka</s>); '<s>śulba</s>' is copper (<s>tāmra</s>). This also should be known as a <s>mahābīja</s>.

children.text: punaḥ śulbābhrakamākṣīkaṃ punaḥ kāntābhrakamākṣīkaṃ kāntaṃ kāntapāṣāṇaṃ abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ tathā tāpyakaśulbābhrakaṃ etadapi ca mahābījaṃ jñeyamiti // GRhtCM_13.2:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, copper-mica-<s>mākṣika</s>; and furthermore, <s>kānta</s>-mica-<s>mākṣika</s>: '<s>kānta</s>' is loadstone; '<s>abhraka</s>' is mica (<s>gagana</s>); '<s>mākṣika</s>' is copper pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>). And likewise, <s>tāpya</s>-copper-mica — this also should be known as a <s>mahābīja</s>.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 13.3
<s>Mākṣika</s>-steel-copper, steel-copper-mica — [these are] <s>mahābījas</s>;
<s>mākṣika</s>-<s>kānta</s>-gold, gold-copper-<s>mākṣika</s> — [these are] <s>mahābījas</s>.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>' etc.

children.text: mākṣīkatīkṣṇaśulbaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāralohajātiḥ śulbaṃ tāmram // GRhtCM_13.3:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>-steel-copper: '<s>mākṣika</s>' is copper pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>); '<s>tīkṣṇa</s>' is a type of iron/steel (<s>sāra-loha-jāti</s>); '<s>śulba</s>' is copper (<s>tāmra</s>).

children.text: punastīkṣṇaśulbābhrakaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ abhrakaṃ gaganam // GRhtCM_13.3:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, steel-copper-mica: '<s>tīkṣṇa</s>' is steel (<s>sāra</s>); '<s>śulba</s>' is copper (<s>tāmra</s>); '<s>abhraka</s>' is mica (<s>gagana</s>).

children.text: punarmākṣīkakāntakanakaṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ kāntaṃ kāntapāṣāṇaṃ kanakaṃ svarṇam // GRhtCM_13.3:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>mākṣika</s>-<s>kānta</s>-gold: '<s>mākṣika</s>' is copper pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>); '<s>kānta</s>' is loadstone (<s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s>); '<s>kanaka</s>' is gold (<s>svarṇa</s>).

children.text: punaḥ kanakāruṇamākṣikaṃ kanakaṃ svarṇaṃ aruṇaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ ceti catuṣṭayaṃ mahābījaṃ pravarabījam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_13.3:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, gold-copper-<s>mākṣika</s>: '<s>kanaka</s>' is gold (<s>svarṇa</s>); '<s>aruṇa</s>' is copper (<s>tāmra</s>); '<s>mākṣika</s>' is gold-<s>mākṣika</s> (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>). Thus this group of four [are each] <s>mahābījas</s> — the finest seeds — this is the meaning.
Each of the four individually bears the designation of <s>mahābīja</s>.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 13.4
<s>Mākṣika</s>-steel-silver, silver-copper-<s>mākṣika</s>, and likewise

children.text: kāntaṃ tu śulbatāpyaṃ śulbābhratāpyakāṃcanaṃ cāpi // GRht_13.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>kānta</s> with copper and <s>tāpya</s>, and copper-mica-<s>tāpya</s>-gold also.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>-steel-silver.'

children.text: mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ tāraṃ rūpyam // GRhtCM_13.4:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Mākṣika</s>' is copper pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>); '<s>tīkṣṇa</s>' is steel (<s>sāra</s>); '<s>tāra</s>' is silver (<s>rūpya</s>).

children.text: punastārāruṇamākṣikaṃ evamuktavidhānena idamapi tāraṃ rūpyaṃ aruṇaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyam // GRhtCM_13.4:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, silver-copper-<s>mākṣika</s>: by the same described procedure, this also — '<s>tāra</s>' is silver (<s>rūpya</s>); '<s>aruṇa</s>' is copper (<s>tāmra</s>); '<s>mākṣika</s>' is copper pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>).

children.text: punaḥ kānte cumbake'bhivyāpake adhikaraṇe śulbaṃ tāmraṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ yat prayuktam // GRhtCM_13.4:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in <s>kānta</s> (loadstone) — that is, in the all-pervading [medium of] loadstone (<s>cumbaka</s>) — copper (<s>śulba</s>, i.e., <s>tāmra</s>) and <s>tāpya</s> (gold-<s>mākṣika</s>) are employed.
'Api' (also/indeed) [is used] in the sense of certainty.

children.text: śulbābhratāpyakāñcanaṃ vā śulbaṃ tāmraṃ abhraṃ gaganaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ kāñcanaṃ hema etaccatuṣṭayamapi mahābījaṃ jñeyam // GRhtCM_13.4:6 //
children.translated_text: Copper-mica-<s>tāpya</s>-gold: or '<s>śulba</s>' is copper (<s>tāmra</s>); '<s>abhra</s>' is mica (<s>gagana</s>); '<s>tāpya</s>' is gold-<s>mākṣika</s>; '<s>kāñcana</s>' is gold (<s>hema</s>). This group of four also should be known as <s>mahābījas</s>.
The <s>mahābīja</s> designation applies to each individually — this is the clarification.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 13.5
<s>Kānta</s>-silver-<s>sasyaka</s>-<s>tāpya</s>, and <s>kānta</s>-mica-steel-<s>mākṣika</s> also;
gold-mica-copper-<s>tāpya</s>, and gold-mica-copper-<s>mākṣika</s> or [the like].
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with '<s>kānta</s>-silver-<s>sasyaka</s>-<s>tāpya</s>.'

children.text: kāntaṃ kāntapāṣāṇaṃ industāraṃ sasyaṃ capalā tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ ceti // GRhtCM_13.5:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kānta</s>' is loadstone (<s>kāntapāṣāṇa</s>); '<s>indu</s>' is silver (<s>tāra</s>); '<s>sasya</s>' is quicksilver (<s>capalā</s>); '<s>tāpya</s>' is gold-<s>mākṣika</s>.

children.text: punaḥ kāntābhrakatīkṣṇamākṣikaṃ tathā hemābhraśulbatāpyaṃ punarhemābhrakaśulbamākṣikaṃ vā hema kanakaṃ abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ etaccatuṣṭayamapi mahābījaṃ jñeyam // GRhtCM_13.5:3 //
