children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>kānta</s>-mica-steel-<s>mākṣika</s>; and gold-mica-copper-<s>tāpya</s>; and gold-mica-copper-<s>mākṣika</s>: or '<s>hema</s>' is gold (<s>kanaka</s>); '<s>abhraka</s>' is mica (<s>gagana</s>); '<s>śulba</s>' is copper (<s>tāmra</s>); '<s>mākṣika</s>' is copper pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>). This group of four also should be known as <s>mahābījas</s>.
The designation of 'seed' applies to each individual substance as well — this is the implied meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 13.6
<s>Kānta</s>-mica-copper-<s>tāpya</s> — [these are] the mixed seeds (<s>saṅkara-bīja</s>); sixty-four [in total].
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with '<s>kānta</s>' etc.

children.text: kāntābhraśulbatāpyaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ ityapi mahābījam // GRhtCM_13.6:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s>-mica-copper-<s>tāpya</s>: '<s>kānta</s>' is loadstone (<s>cumbaka</s>); '<s>abhraka</s>' is mica (<s>gagana</s>); '<s>śulba</s>' is copper (<s>tāmra</s>); '<s>tāpya</s>' is <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites). This also is a <s>mahābīja</s>.

children.text: eteṣāṃ mahābījānāṃ cet saṃkarabījaṃ pratyekaṃ dravyasya bījasaṃjñā sā tarhi catuḥṣaṣṭipramāṇā syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_13.6:3 //
children.translated_text: If the mixed seeds of these <s>mahābījas</s> — the designation of 'seed' for each individual substance — [are counted], then they number sixty-four — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 13.7
<<s>Mahābīja</s> (great seed) :: production>
For all seeds, having first made the combination as prescribed,

children.text: śatavāpyaṃ yadvahnau drāvitaṃ hi bījaṃ viśuddhamidaṃ // GRht_13.7 //
children.translated_text: that which, when counter-charged a hundred times in fire, is liquefied — that indeed is the purified seed.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the seed-procedure, beginning with '<s>sarveṣām</s>' (of all) etc.

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ sarveṣāṃ bījānāṃ yathoktaṃ saṃyogaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭīnāṃ uktasaṃjñānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ saṃyogaṃ ekatrīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā yadekatrīkṛtaṃ vahnau drāvitaṃ bhavati tatsarvaṃ śatavāpyaṃ bījaṃ siddhaṃ prayatnena syāditi śabdārthaḥ // GRhtCM_13.7:2 //
children.translated_text: First — initially — for all sixty-four seeds with their stated designations, having made the prescribed combination — having unified [the substances] — that which, when unified and liquefied in fire, [and] counter-charged a hundred times — then all [of it] becomes the perfected seed — [this] should be [done] with effort — this is the meaning of the words.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 13.8

children.text: <cāraṇa, garbha- and bāhyadruti necessary for bandhana>
children.translated_text: <<s>Cāraṇa</s>, <s>garbha</s>- and <s>bāhya-druti</s> (internal and external fusion) are necessary for <s>bandhana</s> (binding)>

children.text: na patati yadi ghanasatvaṃ garbhe no vā dravanti bījāni /
children.translated_text: If mica-essence does not fall into the womb [of mercury], or if the seeds do not melt in the womb,

children.text: na ca bāhyadrutiyogastatkathamiha badhyate sūtaḥ // GRht_13.8 //
children.translated_text: and if there is no external fusion (<s>bāhya-druti</s>) procedure — then how can mercury be bound here?
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the causes for the binding of mercury, beginning with 'not' (<s>na</s>) etc.

children.text: yadi garbhe rasodare ghanasattvaṃ abhrakasāraṃ na patati na prāpnoti vā garbhe bījāni asminnadhyāye abhihitāni mākṣikakāntaśulbādīni yāvanno dravanti ca punarbāhyadrutistasyā yogo rase drutimelanaṃ na syāt tattasmāddhetoḥ sūta ihāsyāṃ kriyāyāmasatyāṃ kathaṃ badhyate ghanatvaṃ dhatte // GRhtCM_13.8:2 //
children.translated_text: If mica-essence — the extract of mica — does not fall into, i.e., does not reach, the womb (belly of mercury); or if the seeds — those described in this chapter, such as <s>mākṣika</s>-<s>kānta</s>-copper and the like — do not melt in the womb; and furthermore, if there is no external fusion (<s>bāhya-druti</s>), and its combination — the merging of [external] fusion with mercury — does not occur — then, from that cause, how can mercury, in this operation, when it does not exist [without these conditions], be bound — attain solidity?
The import is: mercury is certainly bound through [both] embryo-fusion (<s>garbha-druti</s>) and external fusion (<s>bāhya-druti</s>).
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 14.1
<Production of gold :: preparing the mercury>

children.text: samād adhi ca yajjīrṇaṃ bījaṃ tenaiva cāvartatā kāryā /
children.translated_text: That seed which has been digested in equal [proportion] or more, with that very [seed], the melting (<s>āvarta</s>) should be performed;

children.text: kartavyaṃ tatkaraṇaṃ yasmātkhalu jāyate hema // GRht_14.1 //
children.translated_text: that procedure should be executed, from which indeed gold is produced.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: śaradi śāradamegho varṣati varṣāsu vārṣiko vārdaḥ /
children.translated_text: In autumn, the autumnal cloud rains; in the rainy season, the monsoon-born [cloud rains];

children.text: madhusamaye parapuṣṭaḥ pravarajavaḥ śobhate satatam // GRhtCM_14.1:1 //
children.translated_text: in the spring season, the cuckoo (<s>parapuṣṭa</s>), finest in speed, always shines.
He states what results from seed-digestion, beginning with '<s>samāt</s>' (from equal) etc.

children.text: samaṃ sūtatulyaṃ adhiśabdād aparimitaṃ samādadhikaṃ yajjīrṇaṃ jāraṇamāptaṃ bījaṃ niṣpannabījaṃ tenaiva jīrṇena bījena saha āvartatā kāryā āvarta iti āvartaḥ // GRhtCM_14.1:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Equal' (<s>sama</s>) means equal to the mercury; 'from <s>adhi</s>' (more) means unlimited — [i.e.,] equal or more; the seed that has been digested — that has undergone digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) — the perfected seed; with that very digested seed, the melting (<s>āvarta</s>) should be performed — '<s>āvarta</s>' means the melting [process].

children.text: kiṃ tat yasmādvidhānāddhema kanakaṃ jāyate khalu niścayena tatkaraṇaṃ tasya vidhānasya karaṇam // GRhtCM_14.1:4 //
children.translated_text: What is that? That procedure from which gold (<s>kanaka</s>) is produced — certainly, without doubt; 'that procedure' means the execution of that method.

children.text: samādijīrṇasya sūtasya rūpyādiṣu prayogātkanakaṃ bhavediti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_14.1:5 //
children.translated_text: The clarification: from the application of mercury that has digested [seed in] equal [or greater proportion] to silver and other [metals], gold would result.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 14.2-9
<<s>Rasabīja</s> (mercury-seed) :: production>
Having melted [the substance] in a steel vessel, one should add mercury with a quarter-portion of sulphur (<s>gandha</s>);

children.text: svarasena cauṣadhīnāṃ vaṭikāṃ niṣpiṣya kurvīta // GRht_14.2 //
children.translated_text: grinding with the juice of herbs, one should make a tablet (<s>vaṭikā</s>).

children.text: saṃsthāpya lohaphalake chāyāśuṣkāṃ tu tāṃ vaṭikām /
children.translated_text: Having placed it on an iron plate, [letting] that tablet [become] shade-dried,
covering it with a small metal cup (<s>kaṭorikā</s>), one should seal it firmly.
The [cup], anointed with salt-moistened clay, should be made firm — to block smoke;
having placed firm coals, with the fire of two bellows alone, in a smokeless [state],
smelt until the amalgam (<s>khoṭikā</s>) becomes reddish in appearance.

children.text: apanīya tato'ṅgārān svabhāvaśītāṃ kaṭorikāṃ matvā // GRht_14.5 //
children.translated_text: Then, having removed the coals, and considering the cup to be naturally cooled,
having dug out [the contents] from the cup again and again, the mercury should be collected.

children.text: eṣaḥ mṛtasūtarājo golakavadbhavati ca sa sukhādhmātaḥ // GRht_14.6 //
children.translated_text: This is killed mercury (<s>mṛta-sūtarāja</s>); it becomes like a ball (<s>golaka</s>); and it, easily smelted,
becomes of peacock-throat [color], homogeneous; excessively smelted, with glass (<s>kāca</s>) and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>),

children.text: triguṇaṃ vaṅgaṃ dadyātkrameṇa nāgam alpālpadānena // GRht_14.7 //
children.translated_text: one should add triple-quantity tin (<s>vaṅga</s>); progressively, lead (<s>nāga</s>) in small increments.
Afterward, it should be combined with gold — [this is] the <s>rasabīja</s> (mercury-seed), the binder of mercury.
He states the procedure for killing mercury, beginning with '<s>pradrāvya</s>' (having melted) etc.
'In a steel vessel' — in a vessel made of steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), in the sense of a container; the seventh [case-ending is] in the locative sense.

children.text: gandhapādena gandhasya turyāṃśavibhāgena sūtakaṃ dadyāt tatpātroparibhāge dattaṃ pradrāvya vahninā iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_14.2-7:3 //
children.translated_text: With a quarter-portion of sulphur (<s>gandha</s>) — with a quarter-part division of sulphur — mercury should be given [into the vessel]; given upon the upper part of that vessel; 'having melted' [means] by fire — this is the completion.

children.text: punaḥ oṣadhīnāṃ svarasena auṣadhyo granthāntare yathā /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with the juice of herbs; the herbs [are], as in another text:
'One should grind [mercury] until the paste becomes collyrium-like;'
'then, of the regulating [herbs] — <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>kandukī</s>, <s>sudhā</s> (milkweed), and the like.'
Thus.

children.text: śatāvaryādīnāṃ svakīyarasena niṣpiṣya pramardya vaṭikāṃ badarākarāṃ kurvīteti // GRhtCM_14.2-7:5 //
children.translated_text: With the juice of <s>śatāvarī</s> and the rest, having ground — having pressed [into a paste] — one should make a tablet of the size of a jujube (<s>badara</s>).
He states that, beginning with '<s>saṃsthāpya</s>' (having placed) etc.

children.text: tāṃ pūrvoktāṃ vaṭikāṃ chāyāśuṣkāṃ lohaphalake śastrapātre saṃsthāpya punaḥ laghulohakaṭorikayā pūrvoktalohaphalakāt laghvī yā lohakaṭorikā tayā sthagayitvā ācchādya dṛḍhaṃ gāḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā lepayet vakṣyamāṇeneti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_14.2-7:7 //
children.translated_text: Having placed that aforementioned pellet, dried in shade, on an iron plate — a metal vessel — and then covering it with a small iron bowl (<s>laghu-loha-kaṭorikā</s>), which is smaller than the aforementioned iron plate, one should seal it firmly and tightly with [the substance] to be described — this is the remainder. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:7 //
He states that — 'with salt' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:8 //

children.text: tāṃ pūrvoditāṃ laghulohakaṭorikāṃ sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā lavaṇārdramṛdā lavaṇena saindhavādinā yutā yā ārdrā jalasiktā mṛt tayā liptāṃ kurvīta // GRhtCM_14.2-7:9 //
children.translated_text: That aforementioned small iron bowl should be made firmly sealed with salt-moistened clay — clay that is moist, i.e., sprinkled with water, combined with salt such as <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) and others. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:9 //

children.text: kimarthaṃ dhūmrarodhāya yathā yantrādbahirdhūmodgamo na syāt // GRhtCM_14.2-7:10 //
children.translated_text: For what purpose? For the prevention of smoke — so that smoke does not escape outward from the apparatus. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:10 //

children.text: punaḥ sudṛḍhāṅgārān khadirādīnāṃ dattvā bhastrādvayavahninā khalu dvayāgninā dhamyād iti agrimaślokasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_14.2-7:11 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, having placed firm charcoals of <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu) and such, one should blow with the fire of two bellows (<s>bhastra-dvaya</s>), i.e., with double-bellows fire — this connects with the next verse. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:11 //

children.text: kva sati nirdhūme sati rase dhūmaniḥsaraṇavarjite sati // GRhtCM_14.2-7:12 //
children.translated_text: When? When the mercury is smoke-free, i.e., when [the apparatus is] devoid of smoke emission. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:12 //
He states that — 'until' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:13 //

children.text: sandhiliptā pūrvoktā lohaśarāvikā tāvadavadhau dhmātā kāryā yāvatkālapramāṇaṃ raktābhā raktadyutiyuktā khoṭikā bhavati khoṭasyeva ākṛtiryasyāḥ sā khoṭikā // GRhtCM_14.2-7:14 //
children.translated_text: The aforementioned joint-sealed iron bowl should be blown until such time as the <s>khoṭikā</s> (small ingot) becomes red-hued, i.e., endowed with crimson brilliance — a <s>khoṭikā</s> being that which has the form of a <s>khoṭa</s> (ingot). // GRhtCM_14.2-7:14 //

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ kaṭorikāṃ svabhāvaśītalāṃ svato himāṃ matvā jñātvā punaraṅgārānapanīya apasārya kaṭorikāmutkhanya raso grāhya iti śeṣaḥ āgamiślokasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_14.2-7:15 //
children.translated_text: Then, after that, having determined that the bowl has become naturally cool, i.e., cold by itself, one should remove the charcoals, push them aside, dig out the bowl, and collect the mercury — this is the remainder, connecting with the next verse. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:15 //
He states that — 'digging out' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:16 //

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ laghulohakaṭorikāṃ pūrvavarṇitāṃ utkhanyotkhanya prabalatvenotpāṭya rasaḥ sūto grāhyaḥ // GRhtCM_14.2-7:17 //
children.translated_text: Then, after that, having vigorously dug out the aforementioned small iron bowl — forcefully extracting it — mercury (<s>rasa</s>, i.e., <s>sūta</s>) should be collected. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:17 //
The repetition 'digging out, digging out' is either due to extreme hardness or expresses emphasis through iteration. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:18 //

children.text: kutaḥ kaṭorikāsakāśāt eṣa itthamutpanno mṛtasūtarājo jñeyaḥ // GRhtCM_14.2-7:19 //
children.translated_text: From where? From the bowl — this mercury thus produced should be known as 'killed mercury' (<s>mṛta-sūta-rāja</s>). // GRhtCM_14.2-7:19 //

children.text: sa ca sukhādhmātaḥ san golakavadbhavati vajramūṣāyāṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_14.2-7:20 //
children.translated_text: And that [mercury], when easily blown, becomes like a ball (<s>golaka</s>) — in a diamond crucible (<s>vajra-mūṣā</s>), this is the remainder. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:20 //

children.text: kācaḥ pratītaḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ tataḥ raso 'ti maryādāmatikramya dhmātaḥ san ekaraso bhavati samarasa ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_14.2-7:21 //
children.translated_text: Glass (<s>kāca</s>) is well-known; borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>) is <s>saubhāgya</s>; then mercury, exceeding the limit, when blown, becomes of uniform essence (<s>ekarasa</s>) — meaning homogeneous. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:21 //

children.text: keṣāṃ śikhigalatāṃ śikhini galantīti vigrahaḥ śikhigalatāṃ dhātūnāṃ evaṃ galite rase triguṇaṃ vaṅgaṃ raṅgaṃ dadyāt tato vaṅgadānānantaraṃ krameṇa alpamalpadānena nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ ca dadyāditi // GRhtCM_14.2-7:22 //
children.translated_text: Of which [metals]? <s>Śikhi-galatām</s> — parsed as 'those that melt in fire' — of such metals; when mercury has thus melted, one should add tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) in triple quantity, and then after adding tin, gradually, by adding small amounts at a time, one should add lead (<s>nāga</s>, i.e., <s>sīsaka</s>). // GRhtCM_14.2-7:22 //
He states that — 'afterward' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.2-7:23 //

children.text: paścāt triguṇasīsakadānānantaraṃ hemnā kanakena saha rasabījaṃ mahābījaṃ yojyaṃ hemnā sārdhaṃ mahābījaṃ kīdṛgbhavati // GRhtCM_14.2-7:24 //
children.translated_text: Afterward, after adding triple-quantity lead, the <s>rasa-bīja</s> (mercury-seed), i.e., the great seed (<s>mahā-bīja</s>), should be combined with gold (<s>heman</s>, i.e., <s>kanaka</s>) — what kind of great seed combined with gold? // GRhtCM_14.2-7:24 //
START GRht 14.8-9

children.text: tālakasūtenāpi ca kṛtvā vaṭikāṃ niyāmakauṣadhibhiḥ // GRht_14.8 //
children.translated_text: Having also made a pellet with orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>) and mercury (<s>sūta</s>), with restraining herbs (<s>niyāmaka-auṣadhi</s>), // GRht_14.8 //
<mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (killing)>

children.text: evaṃ nigṛhya dhūmaṃ sudhiyā rasamāraṇaṃ kāryam /
children.translated_text: thus restraining the smoke, the wise one should perform the killing of mercury (<s>rasa-māraṇa</s>).

children.text: rasabandhakaraṃ pāradabandhapradaṃ ca punaḥ tālakaṃ haritālaṃ sūto rasaḥ tenāpi niyāmakauṣadhibhiśca śatāvaryādibhiḥ pūrvoktābhir guṭikāṃ kṛtvā nigṛhya dhūmaṃ rundhitadhūmaṃ yathā syāttathā sudhiyā matimatā rasajñena evamamunā vidhinā rasamāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ pāradabandhaḥ kārya ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_14.8:1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa-bandhakara</s> (that which produces the binding of mercury): <s>tālaka</s> means <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment); <s>sūta</s> means mercury — with that too, and with restraining herbs (<s>niyāmaka-auṣadhi</s>) such as <s>śatāvarī</s> and the previously mentioned ones, having made a pellet, restraining the smoke — making it so that smoke is blocked — the wise one, i.e., the intelligent one who knows mercury, should perform the killing of mercury (<s>rasa-māraṇa</s>) by this method — meaning the binding of mercury should be done. // GRhtCM_14.8:1 //
START GRht 14.9
<mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (killing)>

children.text: athavā śilayā sūto mākṣikayogena vā siddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, mercury accomplished with realgar (<s>śilā</s>) or with the addition of pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>),

children.text: jāyeta śuklavarṇo dhūmarodhena tābhyāṃ vā // GRht_14.9 //
children.translated_text: becomes white-colored through smoke-restraint, or with both of those. // GRht_14.9 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [method] — 'alternatively' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.9:1 //

children.text: athavā vidhyantare śilayā manohvayā kṛtvā vā mākṣikayogena tāpyasaṃyogaṃ kṛtvā sādhitastālakayogavat sūto rasaḥ śuklavarṇo jayeta // GRhtCM_14.9:2 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, in another procedure — with realgar (<s>śilā</s>), called <s>manaḥ</s> (-<s>śilā</s>), having performed [the procedure], or with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) combination, i.e., having made a conjunction with <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite), accomplished as in the orpiment procedure — mercury (<s>sūta</s>, i.e., <s>rasa</s>) becomes white-colored. // GRhtCM_14.9:2 //

children.text: kena dhūmarodhena saindhavārdramṛdā lepena vā tābhyāṃ śilāmākṣikābhyām ubhābhyāṃ tālakayogavat sādhitaḥ san sūtaḥ śuklavarṇo bhaved iti // GRhtCM_14.9:3 //
children.translated_text: By what means? Through smoke-restraint, i.e., by sealing with salt-moistened clay; or with both of those — both realgar and pyrite — accomplished as in the orpiment procedure, mercury becomes white-colored. // GRhtCM_14.9:3 //
START GRht 14.10
<mercury: <s>mṛta</s> (killed): medicinal use>
Powder of killed copper (<s>śulba</s>) and killed pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), combined with lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) — with that, one should color the ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>);
well-extracted, combined with dense essence (<s>ghana-satva</s>) and gold — that should be employed in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). // GRht_14.10 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [procedure] — 'killed' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.10:1 //

children.text: mṛtaśulbatāpyacūrṇaṃ mṛtaṃ ca yat śulbaṃ tāmraṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ ca taccūrṇaṃ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ kāntayutaṃ cumbakamiśritaṃ tena mṛtaśulbatāpyacūrṇena kāntayutena pūrvaṃ niṣpannaṃ khoṭaṃ rañjayet // GRhtCM_14.10:2 //
children.translated_text: Powder of killed copper and pyrite — <s>mṛta</s> (killed) copper (<s>śulba</s>, i.e., <s>tāmra</s>) and <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite, <s>svarṇa-mākṣika</s>) — that powder, of what quality? Combined with <s>kānta</s> (lodestone), i.e., mixed with magnet — with that powder of killed copper and pyrite combined with lodestone, one should color the previously produced ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>). // GRhtCM_14.10:2 //
Of what quality? Combined with dense essence and gold (<s>ghana-satva-hema-yuta</s>), i.e., mixed with mica-essence (<s>abhra-satva</s>) and gold. // GRhtCM_14.10:3 //

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ tatkhoṭaṃ rasāyane jarāvyādhināśane yojyam // GRhtCM_14.10:4 //
children.translated_text: Such a <s>khoṭa</s> (ingot) should be employed in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), i.e., for the destruction of old age and disease. // GRhtCM_14.10:4 //
START GRht 14.11-12

children.text: balinā triguṇena rasāt parpaṭikayutena marditaṃ sūtam /
children.translated_text: Mercury ground with triple-quantity sulphur (<s>balin</s>) combined with metal foil (<s>parpaṭikā</s>),
with restraining divine herbs — a pellet made [and] shade-dried. // GRht_14.11 //
Concealed in the middle of a crucible-held foil, firmly sealed with hidden [substance],

children.text: dhmātaṃ gacchati khoṭaṃ hemayutaṃ sūtabandhakaram // GRht_14.12 //
children.translated_text: when blown, [mercury] becomes an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) — combined with gold, it produces the binding of mercury. // GRht_14.12 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [method] — 'sulphur' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.11-12:1 //

children.text: triguṇena balinā gandhakena saha rasaṃ sūtaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā marditaṃ kuryāt ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_14.11-12:2 //
children.translated_text: With triple-quantity sulphur (<s>balin</s>, i.e., <s>gandhaka</s>), mercury (<s>rasa</s>, i.e., <s>sūta</s>) should be firmly ground — this is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_14.11-12:2 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭena balinā parpaṭikayutena parpaṭiko lohaparpaṭikaḥ pratītastena yutena militena niyamasaṃskāroktāḥ niyamakāḥ divyauṣadhayaḥ śatāvarīpramukhās tābhiḥ tato vaṭikā chāyāśuṣkā kāryā chāyāgharmarūpā śuṣkā nīrasā tathā kāryā iti // GRhtCM_14.11-12:3 //
children.translated_text: With what kind of sulphur? Combined with foil (<s>parpaṭikā-yuta</s>) — <s>parpaṭika</s> is well-known as metal foil — combined with that; the restraining herbs (<s>niyamaka</s>) are the divine herbs (<s>divya-auṣadhi</s>) headed by <s>śatāvarī</s> as mentioned in the restraining procedure — with those; then a pellet should be made shade-dried, i.e., dried in shade-heat, rendered moisture-free — thus it should be made. // GRhtCM_14.11-12:3 //
He states another [step] — 'crucible' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.11-12:4 //

children.text: mūṣādhṛtaparpaṭikā mūṣāyāṃ yā parpaṭikā pūrvoktalohaparpaṭikā sā nigūḍhasudṛḍhena nigūḍhaścāsau sudṛḍhaśca tena mūlakādikṣārabiḍena kṛtvā madhye svāntaḥ ācchādya dhmātaṃ kriyate punas tadūdhmātaṃ sat khoṭaṃ gacchati khoṭatvamāpnoti // GRhtCM_14.11-12:5 //
children.translated_text: Crucible-held foil (<s>mūṣā-dhṛta-parpaṭikā</s>) — the foil that is in the crucible, being the aforementioned metal foil — firmly sealed with hidden [substance] (<s>nigūḍha-su-dṛḍha</s>), hidden and firm — meaning with alkali-<s>viḍa</s> of radish and such; having concealed [the pellet] inside, in the middle, it is blown; and that which is thus blown becomes an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>), i.e., attains ingot-form. // GRhtCM_14.11-12:5 //

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ hemayutaṃ svarṇamilitaṃ sūtabandhakaraṃ syāt rasabandhanapradam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_14.11-12:6 //
children.translated_text: That ingot, combined with gold (<s>hema-yuta</s>), i.e., mixed with gold, would produce the binding of mercury (<s>sūta-bandhakara</s>) — meaning it grants the immobilization of mercury. // GRhtCM_14.11-12:6 //
START GRht 14.13-14
<mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (killing), <s>khoṭa</s> (ingot)>
A foil combined with sulphur (<s>balin</s>), ground, saturated with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) — a pellet [is made];

children.text: madhye gartā kāryā sūtabhṛtācchāditā tadanu // GRht_14.13 //
children.translated_text: a cavity should be made in the middle, filled with mercury, and then covered. // GRht_14.13 //

children.text: bāhye dattvā nigaḍaṃ suliptamūṣodare dṛḍhaṃ nyastam /
children.translated_text: On the outside, having applied a fetter (<s>nigaḍa</s>), firmly placed in the belly of a well-sealed crucible,

children.text: sūtaḥ puṭito mriyate dhmātaḥ khoṭaṃ bhavatyeva // GRht_14.14 //
children.translated_text: mercury, when fired (<s>puṭita</s>), dies; when blown, it becomes an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) indeed. // GRht_14.14 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states an alternative procedure — 'sulphur' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.13-14:1 //

children.text: pūrvoktā yā parpaṭikā lohaparpaṭikā baliyuktā gandhakamiśritā snuhyarkabhāvitā ca snuhī vajrī arko mandāras tābhyāṃ bhāvitā plutā etayoḥ payaseti bhāvaḥ mṛditā ca gharṣitā ca evaṃ kṛtavidhānā parpaṭikā sati guṭikā vaṭikā kāryā madhye guṭikāntaḥ gartā kāryā sā gartā tataḥ sūtabhṛtā sūtapūritā satī tadanu gartakaraṇānantaraṃ ācchāditā kāryā parpaṭikayeti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_14.13-14:2 //
children.translated_text: The aforementioned metal foil (<s>parpaṭikā</s>), combined with sulphur (<s>balin</s>, i.e., <s>gandhaka</s>), and saturated with [the milks of] <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> — <s>snuhī</s> is <s>vajrī</s> (Euphorbia), <s>arka</s> is <s>mandāra</s> (Calotropis) — saturated with those, i.e., soaked; the sense is 'with the milks of these two'; and ground, i.e., triturated — the foil thus prepared, a pellet should be made; in the middle, i.e., inside the pellet, a cavity should be made; that cavity then filled with mercury (<s>sūta-bhṛtā</s>); then after making the cavity, it should be covered — with foil, this is the sense. // GRhtCM_14.13-14:2 //
He states that — 'on the outside' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.13-14:3 //

children.text: bāhye sūtodaraguṭikopari nigaḍaṃ dattvā suliptamūṣodare suliptā sāraṇakarmābhihitauṣadhīriti śeṣaḥ evaṃvidhā yā mūṣā tasyā yadudaraṃ tasmindṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā nigaḍaṃ nyastaṃ sthāpitaṃ kuryāditi śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_14.13-14:4 //
children.translated_text: On the outside, i.e., on top of the mercury-containing pellet, having applied a fetter (<s>nigaḍa</s>), in the belly of a well-sealed crucible — 'well-sealed' means coated with the herbs mentioned in the <s>sāraṇa</s> (streaming) procedure, this is the remainder — in the belly of such a crucible, firmly, so that it stays secure, the fetter should be placed — this is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_14.13-14:4 //

children.text: mūṣodaraguṭikāntasthaḥ sūtaḥ puṭito vahniyogāt mriyate pañcatvamāpnoti // GRhtCM_14.13-14:5 //
children.translated_text: The mercury situated inside the pellet within the crucible's belly, when fired (<s>puṭita</s>), i.e., through contact with fire, dies — attains the five-fold [dissolution]. // GRhtCM_14.13-14:5 //

children.text: punaḥ dhmātaḥ san khoṭo bhavati // GRhtCM_14.13-14:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, when blown, it becomes an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>). // GRhtCM_14.13-14:6 //
The particle <s>eva</s> (indeed) is used to exclude other [methods]. // GRhtCM_14.13-14:7 //
START GRht 14.15
<mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (killing), <s>khoṭa</s> (ingot)>
Thus, with orpiment (<s>tāla</s>) and realgar (<s>śilā</s>), and with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>rasaka</s> (zinc), together with <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) and <s>śikhi</s> (fire/mica),

children.text: mriyate puṭasaṃyogād dhmātaṃ khoṭaṃ kṛtaṃ vimalam // GRht_14.15 //
children.translated_text: [mercury] dies through <s>puṭa</s> (firing) combination; when blown, an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) is made, [rendered] pure. // GRht_14.15 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [method] — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.15:1 //

children.text: evaṃ lohaparpaṭikāvidhānena tālaśilābhyāṃ dhmātaṃ sat yutaṃ yat khoṭaṃ tadvimalaṃ malavarjitaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_14.15:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the metal-foil procedure, that which is blown together with orpiment (<s>tāla</s>) and realgar (<s>śilā</s>) — the resulting ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) becomes pure (<s>vimala</s>), i.e., free from impurity. // GRhtCM_14.15:2 //

children.text: ca punaḥ mākṣikarasakaistāpyakharparikaiḥ daradaśikhisahitaiśca hiṅgulaśikhimilitaiśca karaṇarūpairvimalaṃ ca punaḥ puṭayogād vahnisaṃparkāt dhmātaṃ mriyate // GRhtCM_14.15:3 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) and <s>rasaka</s> (zinc), i.e., <s>tāpya</s> and <s>kharpara</s>; together with <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) and <s>śikhi</s> (mica), i.e., combined with <s>hiṅgula</s> and <s>śikhi</s> — these being the operative substances — [the ingot] becomes pure; and furthermore, through <s>puṭa</s>-combination (firing), i.e., through contact with fire, when blown, [mercury] dies. // GRhtCM_14.15:3 //
The characteristics of impurity were stated earlier. // GRhtCM_14.15:4 //
START GRht 14.16
<mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (killing)>
Through the combination of slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) and <s>pura</s> (guggulu resin), when blown, from the slag, an essence (<s>satva</s>) [forms];

children.text: nipatati satvaṃ rasasākaṃ janayati tadbhasma tasyāpi // GRht_14.16 //
children.translated_text: the essence falls; the mercury-combined [essence] produces ash (<s>bhasma</s>) — and from that [ash], too [an essence falls]. // GRht_14.16 //
He states that — 'through the combination of slag and <s>pura</s>.' // GRhtCM_14.16:1 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: kiṭṭaṃ lohamalaṃ puro gugguluḥ tayoḥ saṃyogāt dhmātaiḥ mākṣikarasadaradarūpaiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ kiṭṭo bhavet punaḥ kiṭṭato rasasākaṃ sūtamiśritaṃ sattvaṃ sāraṃ nipatati tatsattvaṃ bhasma janayati utpādayati // GRhtCM_14.16:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kiṭṭa</s> is metal slag (<s>loha-mala</s>); <s>pura</s> is <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium resin) — through the combination of these two, when blown with the aforementioned substances in the form of <s>mākṣika</s>, mercury, and <s>darada</s> (cinnabar), slag forms; then from the slag, a mercury-combined essence (<s>rasa-sāka</s>), i.e., an essence (<s>sattva</s>) mixed with mercury, falls; that essence produces ash (<s>bhasma</s>), i.e., generates [it]. // GRhtCM_14.16:2 //

children.text: tasyāpi bhasmanaḥ sattvaṃ ca nipatatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_14.16:3 //
children.translated_text: From that ash too, an essence falls — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_14.16:3 //
START GRht 14.17
<s>rañjana</s> (coloring) with smoke and without mercury (????)>
Tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), mercury (<s>rasa</s>), sulphur (<s>gandha</s>), and orpiment (<s>tāla</s>) — through combination with chalk (<s>khaṭikā</s>), [become] an excellent foil;

children.text: rañjayati satvatālaṃ dhūmena vināpi sūtam // GRht_14.17 //
children.translated_text: [it] colors [with] orpiment-essence (<s>satva-tāla</s>) by smoke — even without mercury (<s>sūta</s>). // GRht_14.17 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states an alternative procedure — 'tin, mercury, sulphur, orpiment.' // GRhtCM_14.17:1 //

children.text: vaṅgaṃ trapu rasaḥ sūtaḥ gandhako baliḥ tālaṃ haritālaṃ etaccatuṣṭayaṃ khaṭikāyā yogataḥ khaṭikā citrakarajastasyā yogataḥ suparpaṭikāṃ pūrvoktāṃ lohaparpaṭikāṃ rañjayati sūtena vināpi kimuta rasamilitena tālasattveneti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_14.17:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaṅga</s> is tin (<s>trapu</s>); <s>rasa</s> is mercury (<s>sūta</s>); <s>gandha</s> is sulphur (<s>bali</s>); <s>tāla</s> is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>) — this fourfold [combination], through combination with <s>khaṭikā</s> — <s>khaṭikā</s> is chalk (<s>citraka-rajas</s>) — through combination with that, colors the aforementioned metal foil (<s>su-parpaṭikā</s>) — even without mercury, how much more so when combined with mercury — and with orpiment-essence, this is the clarification. // GRhtCM_14.17:2 //
START GRht 14.18
<s>bīja</s> (seed-metal): for <s>rañjana</s> (coloring)>

children.text: evaṃ khoṭaṃ bījaṃ kṛtvā rañjanavidhinā surañjanaṃ kāryam /
children.translated_text: Thus having made the ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) into a seed (<s>bīja</s>), excellent coloring (<s>su-rañjana</s>) should be performed by the coloring procedure;

children.text: triguṇaṃ rasasya hema saṃyojyaṃ tasya varabījam // GRht_14.18 //
children.translated_text: triple-quantity gold should be combined with mercury — that is its excellent seed (<s>vara-bīja</s>). // GRht_14.18 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: mahābījānāṃ bījānāṃ ca viśeṣavidhānamāha evamityādi // GRhtCM_14.18:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the specific procedure for great seeds (<s>mahā-bīja</s>) and [ordinary] seeds (<s>bīja</s>) — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_14.18:1 //

children.text: evam uktavidhānena bījaṃ vidhāya rañjanavidhinā rañjanavidhānena surañjanaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_14.18:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the described procedure, having prepared the seed (<s>bīja</s>), excellent coloring (<s>su-rañjana</s>) should be performed by the coloring procedure (<s>rañjana-vidhāna</s>). // GRhtCM_14.18:2 //

children.text: tatkārye rasasya sūtasya triguṇaṃ hema saṃyojyaṃ punas tasya hemnaḥ triguṇaṃ varabījaṃ yojyaṃ iti viśeṣavidhiḥ // GRhtCM_14.18:3 //
children.translated_text: In that procedure, three times the amount of gold should be combined with the mercury (<s>sūta</s>), and furthermore, three times the gold's [amount] of the excellent seed should be added — this is the special procedure. // GRhtCM_14.18:3 //
START GRht 15.1

children.text: <abhra:: sattva:: druti:: causes bandhana of mercury>
children.translated_text: <mica essence: <s>druti</s> (liquefaction): causes binding of mercury>
I shall describe the pure <s>druti</s> (liquefaction) from mica essence — the foundation of all hosts of qualities;

children.text: sā hi nibadhnāti rasaṃ saṃmilitā milati ca sukhena // GRht_15.1 //
children.translated_text: for it indeed binds mercury when combined, and it merges easily. // GRht_15.1 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

O <s>Bhāratī</s>, adorning the land of <s>Bhārata</s>, may the bliss-cluster
and the water-lily communities be delighted by speech-rays, with ever-lasting splendor. // GRhtCM_15.1:1 //

children.text: kastayā na rasamalaṃ kuto jayā vakrapadmamadhisthayā sadā // GRhtCM_15.1:1 //
children.translated_text: (Invocatory verse of the commentator.)
He states the praise of external liquefaction (<s>bāhya-druti</s>) — 'I shall describe' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.1:2 //

children.text: ahaṃ kaviḥ abhrakasattvādgaganasārato vimaladrutiṃ pakṣe vimalā cāsau drutiśceti vigrahaḥ // GRhtCM_15.1:3 //
children.translated_text: I, the author, [shall describe] the pure <s>druti</s> (liquefaction) from mica essence, i.e., from the core of <s>gagana</s> (mica). In an alternative reading: '<s>vimalā</s>' and '<s>druti</s>' as a compound — this is the analysis. // GRhtCM_15.1:3 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāṃ akhilaguṇagaṇādhārām akhilāśca te guṇagaṇāśca guṇapaṭalāśca teṣāṃ yā ādhārā tāṃ bahavo guṇās tiṣṭhantyasyāmiti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_15.1:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? 'The foundation of all hosts of qualities' — 'all' and 'hosts of qualities,' i.e., assemblies of qualities — whose foundation it is. The clarification: many qualities reside in it. // GRhtCM_15.1:4 //

children.text: sā rasabhūtā drutiḥ rasaṃ sūtāṃ nibadhnāti niścayena badhnātītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_15.1:5 //
children.translated_text: That <s>druti</s>, become mercury-like, binds mercury (<s>sūta</s>), i.e., certainly binds [it] — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_15.1:5 //
In what condition? // GRhtCM_15.1:6 //

children.text: militā satī tulyamiśritā satī punaḥ drutiḥ sukhena milati patrāder durmilāpatvāt // GRhtCM_15.1:7 //
children.translated_text: When combined (<s>militā</s>), i.e., when equally mixed. Furthermore, the <s>druti</s> merges easily — because leaves and such are difficult to merge [with mercury]. // GRhtCM_15.1:7 //
START GRht 15.2
<mica essence: <s>druti</s>: production>
<s>Gagana</s> (mica) ground with <s>vajravallī</s> juice, combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt),
cooked with <s>nicula</s> (Barringtonia) calcinations, becomes free from coating and mercury-like in form. // GRht_15.2 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the <s>druti</s> procedure — '<s>vajravallī</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.2:1 //

children.text: vajravallyāḥ svarasena svakīyena rasena gaganamabhrasattvaṃ sauvarcalānvitaṃ rucakasahitaṃ piṣṭaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_15.2:2 //
children.translated_text: With the juice of <s>vajravallī</s>, i.e., with its own juice, <s>gagana</s>, i.e., mica essence, combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> (<s>rucaka</s>, black salt), should be ground — the remainder is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_15.2:2 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ gaganaṃ niculapuṭair vetasadravabhāvanābhiḥ pakvaṃ vahnipuṭitaṃ tatpakvaṃ san nirlepaṃ saṃparkavarjitaṃ rasarūpaṃ bhavati pāradasya rūpamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_15.2:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what character is the <s>gagana</s>? Cooked, i.e., fire-calcined, with <s>nicula</s> calcinations, i.e., with saturations using <s>vetasa</s> (cane) tree-juice. That cooked [mica], being free from coating, i.e., free from contact [with impurities], becomes mercury-like in form, i.e., it takes the form of mercury — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_15.2:3 //
START GRht 15.3
<mica essence: <s>druti</s>: production>
Merely by the addition (<s>vāpa</s>) of <s>kapitinduka</s> powder saturated a hundred times with goat-water,
the liquefied mica essence, in the crucible, becomes mercury-like. // GRht_15.3 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another procedure — '<s>aja</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.3:1 //

children.text: drujātarabhrakasattvaṃ abhrakasatvaṃ gaganasāraṃ mūṣāyāṃ vajrasaṃjñāyāṃ drutaṃ sat rasasaṃnibhaṃ bhavati pāradabhūtam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_15.3:2 //
children.translated_text: The liquefied mica essence, i.e., the core of mica (<s>gagana</s>), in the crucible called <s>vajra</s>-type, when liquefied, becomes mercury-like, i.e., takes the nature of mercury — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_15.3:2 //

children.text: kena ajajalaśataparibhāvitakapitindukacūrṇavāpamātreṇa ajaḥ chāgastasya jalena mūtreṇa śataṃ śatavāraṃ paribhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ yatkapitindukacūrṇaṃ tasya vāpamātreṇa drute'bhrasattve vāpe // GRhtCM_15.3:3 //
children.translated_text: By what? Merely by the addition of <s>kapitinduka</s> powder saturated a hundred times with goat-water: <s>aja</s> is a goat; with its water, i.e., urine; saturated a hundred times, i.e., sun-dried; the <s>kapitinduka</s> powder [thus prepared]; merely by its addition (<s>vāpa</s>) into the liquefied mica essence. // GRhtCM_15.3:3 //
START GRht 15.4
<mica essence: <s>druti</s>: production>
With the addition of powder from <s>kañcukī</s>-tubers saturated a hundred times with its own juice,
the mica essence remains liquefied, and likewise all metals. // GRht_15.4 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: abhrakasattvaṃ vahniyogena drutaṃ āste dravarūpamevāvatiṣṭhate // GRhtCM_15.4:1 //
children.translated_text: The mica essence, when liquefied by fire, remains in a liquid state. // GRhtCM_15.4:1 //

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ sattvaṃ nijarasaśataparibhāvitetyādi nijarasena svakīyadraveṇa paribhāvitaṃ yatkañcukikandotthacūrṇaṃ tasya āvāpena yathā śatabhāvitakañcukikandotthacūrṇena sattvaṃ drutamāste tadvatsarvāṇi lohāni drutāni tiṣṭhanti // GRhtCM_15.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Of what character is the essence? Saturated a hundred times with its own juice, etc. — by its own liquid, saturated; the powder from <s>kañcukī</s>-tubers [so treated]; by its addition, just as with the <s>kañcukī</s>-tuber powder saturated a hundred times, the essence remains liquefied; likewise, all metals also remain in a liquefied state. // GRhtCM_15.4:2 //
START GRht 15.5
<mica essence: <s>druti</s>: production>
<s>Gagana</s> (mica), rubbed with hair-oil, coated with cow-dung, in a diamond-type crucible,
well-blown — in this case, the essence floats water-like in a short time. // GRht_15.5 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [method] — '<s>gagana</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.5:1 //

children.text: gaganaṃ abhrasāraṃ cikuratailaghṛṣṭaṃ cikuratailaṃ keśatailaṃ pratītaṃ grantheṣu tena ghṛṣṭaṃ marditaṃ gomayaliptaṃ gomayena liptaṃ yathā syāttathā kuliśamūṣāyāṃ vajrābhidhānāyāṃ sudhmātaṃ sat acireṇālpakālena jalākāraṃ bhavatītyanvayaḥ // GRhtCM_15.5:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gagana</s>, i.e., the mica core, rubbed with hair-oil — 'hair-oil' (<s>cikura-taila</s>) is well-known as 'hair-oil' in the texts — rubbed, i.e., ground, with it; coated with cow-dung, i.e., smeared with cow-dung as appropriate; in a diamond-type crucible (<s>kuliśa-mūṣā</s>); well-blown — in a short time it becomes water-like — this is the syntactical connection. // GRhtCM_15.5:2 //
START GRht 15.6
<mica essence: <s>druti</s>: general rule>

children.text: gaganadrutiriha satve jñeyo hi rasasya sampradāyo 'yam /
children.translated_text: The liquefaction of <s>gagana</s> (mica) here, in the essence — this should be known as the tradition of mercury;

children.text: prathamaṃ nipātya satvaṃ deyo vāpo drute tasmin // GRht_15.6 //
children.translated_text: first, having extracted the essence, the addition should be given when it is in the liquefied state. // GRht_15.6 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the general procedure for mica liquefaction — '<s>gagana</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.6:1 //

children.text: ihāsmin śāstre sattve gaganasāre jāte sāṅgatayā gaganadrutiḥ bhavatītyadhyāhāryam // GRhtCM_15.6:2 //
children.translated_text: In this treatise, when the mica core (<s>gagana-sāra</s>) has been [extracted], the liquefaction of mica follows as a necessary accompaniment — this is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_15.6:2 //

children.text: ayaṃ pratyakṣāntargataḥ hi niścitaṃ rasasya sūtasya saṃpradāyo jñeyaḥ // GRhtCM_15.6:3 //
children.translated_text: This tradition of mercury (<s>sūta</s>), accessible through direct [experience], should be known with certainty. // GRhtCM_15.6:3 //

children.text: punaḥ prathamādau sattvaṃ abhrasāraṃ nipātya tasmindrute sattve vahninā dravarūpe sati vāpaḥ kāryaḥ kathitauṣadhīnāṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_15.6:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, first, i.e., at the beginning, having extracted the mica core, when that essence is in a liquefied state, i.e., in liquid form through fire, the addition (<s>vāpa</s>) should be made — of the previously mentioned herbs — the remainder. // GRhtCM_15.6:4 //
START GRht 15.7
<gold: <s>druti</s> (liquefaction)>
The powdered body of the <s>suragopa</s> insect (<s>indragopa</s>), together with <s>suradālī</s> (Devadālī) fruits in equal parts, should be given

children.text: vāpo drute suvarṇe drutamāste tadrasaprakhyam // GRht_15.7 //
children.translated_text: as an addition to liquefied gold — [the gold] remains liquefied, resembling mercury. // GRht_15.7 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the procedure for gold liquefaction — 'body-powder of <s>suragopa</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.7:1 //

children.text: indragopaśarīracūrṇaṃ suradālīphalaiḥ samāṃśakaiḥ suragopacūrṇatulyabhāgaiḥ kṛtvā vāpo deyaḥ drute satyuparikṣepa iti suvarṇe vāpe kṛte suvarṇaṃ drutamāste kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ rasaprakhyaṃ jalatulyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_15.7:2 //
children.translated_text: The body-powder of <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect), together with <s>suradālī</s> fruits in equal parts, i.e., equal in portion to the <s>suragopa</s> powder — having prepared these, the addition should be given. When [added to] the liquefied gold, i.e., the projection from above — when the addition is made to the gold, the gold remains liquefied. Of what character? Mercury-like, i.e., water-like — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_15.7:2 //
START GRht 15.8
<gold: <s>druti</s>>
Now, merely by the addition of <s>suradālī</s> (Devadālī) powder saturated with its own juice a hundred times,

children.text: drutamevāste kanakaṃ labhate bhūyo na kaṭhinatvam // GRht_15.8 //
children.translated_text: gold remains in a liquefied state and never again acquires hardness. // GRht_15.8 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [method] — 'now' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.8:1 //

children.text: athendragopadevadālīyogakathanānantaraṃ kanakaṃ hema nijarasaparibhāvitaṃ yat suradālīcūrṇaṃ tasya vāpamātreṇa galite hemni kṣepamātreṇa drutamevāste galitam evāvatiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ punaḥ kanakaṃ kāṭhinyaṃ sthiratvaṃ na labhate iti cirakālaprayojanam // GRhtCM_15.8:2 //
children.translated_text: Now, after the description of the <s>indragopa</s>-<s>devadālī</s> combination: gold (<s>kanaka</s>), i.e., gold (<s>hema</s>) — by the addition of <s>suradālī</s> powder saturated with its own juice, when projected into liquefied gold, merely by the projection — it remains liquefied, i.e., it persists in a molten state — this is the meaning. Furthermore, the gold does not acquire hardness, i.e., solidity — this serves a long-term purpose. // GRhtCM_15.8:2 //
START GRht 15.9
<iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>): <s>druti</s>>
The ash of <s>suradālī</s>, liquefied [and filtered] twenty-one times with cow-water, [and then] dried —

children.text: vāpena salilasadṛśaṃ kurute mūṣāgataṃ tīkṣṇam // GRht_15.9 //
children.translated_text: by its addition, [one] makes iron in the crucible water-like. // GRht_15.9 //
Now he states the procedure for iron — '<s>suradālī</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.9:1 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: suradālībhasmagalitaṃ suradālī devadālī tasyāḥ bhasma dāhasambhūtaṃ tena galitaṃ trisaptakṛtvā ekaviṃśativāraṃ gojalaṃ surabhimūtraṃ bhāvitaṃ kuryādityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_15.9:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Liquefied with <s>suradālī</s> ash' — <s>suradālī</s> is <s>devadālī</s>; its ash, produced by burning; liquefied with that, twenty-one times (three times seven); cow-water, i.e., cow-urine — it should be saturated — this is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_15.9:2 //

children.text: atha mūṣāgataṃ vajrasaṃjñāyāṃ sthitaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ vāpena nikṣepaṇena jalasadṛśaṃ jalatulyaṃ kurute karmaviditi śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_15.9:3 //
children.translated_text: Now, the iron placed in the crucible called <s>vajra</s>-type — the core (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), i.e., [steel] essence — by the addition, i.e., by projection, [one skilled in] the art makes it water-like, i.e., like water — the remainder is 'the one skilled in the art.' // GRhtCM_15.9:3 //
START GRht 15.10
<s>mākṣika</s>-essence liquefaction>
Quenched with the bones of tortoise (<s>kūrma</s>), bitumen (<s>śilājatu</s>), [and bones of] ewe (<s>meṣī</s>), deer (<s>mṛga</s>), and cow —

children.text: jalasadṛśī bhavati sadā vāpo deyo drutāyāṃ tu // GRht_15.10 //
children.translated_text: the <s>kāñcī</s> (gold-pyrite) becomes permanently water-like; the addition should be given when it is in the liquefied state. // GRht_15.10 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the procedure for <s>mākṣika</s> liquefaction — '<s>kūrma</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.10:1 //

children.text: kūrmāsthi śilājatukaṃ pratītaṃ meṣī meṣapatnī mṛgo hariṇaḥ gauḥ pratītā pratīto vā teṣāṃ yānyasthīni tair nirvāpitā yā kāñcī svarṇamākṣikaṃ sā jalasadṛśī bhavati kiyatkālaparimāṇaṃ sadā nityaṃ punaḥ drutāyāṃ galitāyāṃ vāpo deyaḥ vāpo nikṣepaṇam // GRhtCM_15.10:2 //
children.translated_text: Tortoise bones; <s>śilājatu</s> (bitumen) is well-known; <s>meṣī</s> is the wife of a ram; <s>mṛga</s> is a deer; <s>go</s> is the cow, well-known — with the bones of these, quenched — that <s>kāñcī</s>, i.e., gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇa-mākṣika</s>), becomes water-like. For how long? Permanently, i.e., always. Furthermore, when it is in the liquefied, i.e., molten, state, the addition (<s>vāpa</s>), i.e., projection, should be given. // GRhtCM_15.10:2 //
START GRht 15.11
<mica <s>druti</s>: alchemical properties>
Mica <s>druti</s> (liquefaction), even ordinary and non-specific, prepared by the procedure, free from coating,

children.text: āroṭaṃ rasarājaṃ badhnāti hi dvandvayogena // GRht_15.11 //
children.translated_text: combined in equal [parts] — it indeed binds <s>āroṭa</s> mercury by the pair-combination method. // GRht_15.11 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the general authority of mica <s>druti</s> — 'mica <s>druti</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.11:1 //

children.text: gaganadravaḥ aviśeṣā sāmānyāpi vidhānena kṛtā nirlepā asparśā samā sūtatulyabhāgayojitā satī āroṭaṃ rasanajaṃ pūrvasaṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaṃ sūtaṃ badhnāti kena dvandvayogena ubhayamelāpakauṣadhena // GRhtCM_15.11:2 //
children.translated_text: The mica liquid (<s>gagana-drava</s>), even ordinary, i.e., non-specific, prepared by the procedure, free from coating, i.e., contactless, combined in equal parts, i.e., equal to the mercury — being in that condition — it binds <s>āroṭa</s> mercury, i.e., the mercury prepared through previous treatments (<s>rasanaja</s>). By what [means]? By the pair-combination method (<s>dvandva-yoga</s>), i.e., with the pair-merger medicine. // GRhtCM_15.11:2 //
The particle '<s>hi</s>' is in the sense of established meaning. // GRhtCM_15.11:3 //
START GRht 15.12

children.text: <receipe for dvandvana of druti and mercury>
children.translated_text: <recipe for pair-combination (<s>dvandvana</s>) of <s>druti</s> and mercury>
With black <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) and musk-camphor, garlic, sugar, and asafoetida — these <s>drutis</s> (liquefied [essences]),

children.text: soṣṇe milanti rasena mṛditāḥ strīkusumapalāśabījarasaiḥ // GRht_15.12 //
children.translated_text: when warm, merge with mercury [when] ground with menstrual fluid and <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) seed-juice. // GRht_15.12 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the merging of the previously mentioned [substances] — '<s>kṛṣṇa</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.12:1 //

children.text: imā drutayaḥ soṣṇatuṣakarīṣādinā tāpite khalve mṛditāḥ satyo milanti rasena saha tathā kāryam // GRhtCM_15.12:2 //
children.translated_text: These <s>drutis</s>, when ground in a mortar heated by hot husks, cow-dung fuel, and the like, merge with mercury — thus it should be done. // GRhtCM_15.12:2 //
With what? With black <s>aguru</s>-musk-camphor combined. // GRhtCM_15.12:3 //

children.text: kṛṣṇāgarukastūrikāghanasāraiḥ kṛtvā na kevalametaiḥ rasonasitarāmaṭhaiśca laśunaśarkarāhiṅgubhiḥ punaḥ strīkusumapalāśabījarasaiḥ strīkusumaṃ ca palāśasya bījāni ca rasaśceti dvaṃdvaḥ etaistribhiryogaiḥ pṛthagbhūtairmilanti sarvaiśceti // GRhtCM_15.12:4 //
children.translated_text: Black <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood), <s>kastūrikā</s> (musk), <s>ghanasāra</s> (camphor) — having prepared [these]; not with these alone [but also] with garlic, sugar, and <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida); furthermore, with menstrual fluid (<s>strī-kusuma</s>) and <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) seed-juice — '<s>strī-kusuma</s>' and '<s>palāśa</s> seeds' and 'juice' — a <s>dvandva</s> compound; with these three preparations, separately or all together, they merge. // GRhtCM_15.12:4 //
START GRht 15.13
<mercury bound: causes longevity>
Thus, the bound <s>Rasarāja</s> (King of Mercury), consumed daily in the amount of one <s>guñjā</s> (seed),

children.text: ekenaiva palena tu kalpāyutajīvitaṃ kurute // GRht_15.13 //
children.translated_text: with just one <s>pala</s> (measure), grants a lifespan of ten thousand <s>kalpas</s>. // GRht_15.13 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the greatness of the bound <s>Rasarāja</s> — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.13:1 //

children.text: iti pūrvoktena drutividhānena baddho rasarājaḥ sūtaḥ ekena palena ṣoḍaśikayā kalpāyutaṃ jīvitaṃ kurute kalpānām ayutaṃ sahasraparimāṇaṃ jīvitamiti // GRhtCM_15.13:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the previously described <s>druti</s> procedure, the bound <s>Rasarāja</s>, i.e., mercury (<s>sūta</s>), with one <s>pala</s> (a sixteenth measure), grants a lifespan of ten thousand <s>kalpas</s>, i.e., a lifespan measured by ten thousand (a thousand) <s>kalpas</s>. // GRhtCM_15.13:2 //

children.text: kasmāt nityaṃ yathā syāttathā guñjāmātropayogataḥ dinaṃ dinaṃ prati raktikāparimāṇasya rasasya yo'sau upayogastena // GRhtCM_15.13:3 //
children.translated_text: Why? Through daily consumption: such that it is regular — by the consumption of mercury in the measure of one <s>guñjā</s> (raktikā seed), day after day — by that [practice]. // GRhtCM_15.13:3 //
START GRht 15.14
Now, when mercury is digested according to the previously described sequence of morsels, properly,
these previously [described] <s>drutis</s> become fruit-giving [in conjunction] with the <s>Rasarāja</s>. // GRht_15.14 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: vidhinā grāsajārito raso guṇavānityāha athetyādi // GRhtCM_15.14:1 //
children.translated_text: He states that mercury digested according to the procedure is endowed with qualities — 'now' and so forth. // GRhtCM_15.14:1 //

children.text: atha drutiyogānantaraṃ rasaḥ sūtaḥ pūrvoktagrāsakramāt yojitakavalakramāt vidhivat śāstroktavidhānena biḍādinā jarate ca punaretāḥ pūrvoktadrutayo rasarājaphaladā bhavanti sūte prayuktāḥ phaladāḥ syurityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_15.14:2 //
children.translated_text: Now, after the <s>druti</s> application, mercury (<s>sūta</s>), from the previously described sequence of morsels, i.e., from the sequence of applied morsels, properly, i.e., according to the procedure described in scripture, with <s>biḍa</s> and so forth, is digested. Furthermore, these previously described <s>drutis</s>, when applied to <s>sūta</s> (mercury), become fruit-giving, i.e., yield results — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_15.14:2 //
START GRht 15.15
<s>druti</s>-<s>jāraṇā</s> (liquefaction-assimilation) → <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) potency>

children.text: samajīrṇaḥ śatavedhī dviguṇena rasaḥ sahasravedhī ca /
children.translated_text: When digested in equal [proportion], [mercury] pierces a hundred-fold; with double [the melted substance], mercury becomes a thousand-fold piercer;
progressively indeed a ten-million-fold piercer, from the ingestion of successively doubled meltings. || GRht 15.15 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: adhikadruter jāraṇād adhikaguṇe raso bhavatītyāha samajīrṇa iti // GRhtCM_15.15:1 //
children.translated_text: He states that from additional melting and digestion, the mercury becomes of higher quality, saying 'when digested in equal' and so forth. || GRhtCM 15.15:1 ||

children.text: iti samā tulyabhāgā drutirjīrṇā yasminniti // GRhtCM_15.15:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Equal' means a melting in equal portions that has been digested. || GRhtCM 15.15:2 ||

children.text: drute dviguṇā yā drutiḥ tasyāścaraṇāt kramaśaḥ koṭivedhī koṭyaṃśena vedhakaḥ syāt // GRhtCM_15.15:3 //
children.translated_text: The melting that is doubled — from the ingestion of that, progressively, [mercury] becomes a ten-million-fold piercer, i.e., one that pierces in a proportion of one to ten million. || GRhtCM 15.15:3 ||

children.text: drutibhāgo vṛddhau hyadhikaḥ syāditi vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_15.15:4 //
children.translated_text: The proportion of melting increases progressively — this is the clarification. || GRhtCM 15.15:4 ||
START GRht 15.16
When sixteen, or thirty-two, or sixty-four swallowings have been digested,

children.text: vidhyati tadā rasendro lohaṃ dhūmāvalokanataḥ // GRht_15.16 //
children.translated_text: then the lord of mercury pierces metal merely by observing smoke. || GRht 15.16 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the qualities [achieved] through increase of swallowings, saying 'sixteen' and so forth. || GRhtCM 15.16:1 ||

children.text: yadā ṣoḍaśagrāsā vā dvātriṃśadgrāsā vā catuḥṣaṣṭigrāsā jīrṇā jāraṇamāpannā bhavanti tadā rasendraḥ sūtaḥ lohaṃ dhātusaṃjñakaṃ vidhyati vedhaṃ karoti kutaḥ dhūmāvalokanataḥ dhūmasya yadavalokanaṃ darśanaṃ // GRhtCM_15.16:2 //
children.translated_text: When sixteen swallowings, or thirty-two swallowings, or sixty-four swallowings have been digested, i.e., have attained the state of digestion, then the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>), i.e., <s>sūta</s>, pierces metal (<s>loha</s>), i.e., the substance called <s>dhātu</s>, i.e., performs <s>vedha</s> (transmutation). From what? From mere observation of smoke — from the seeing, i.e., the perception, of smoke. || GRhtCM 15.16:2 ||
START GRht 16.1
<s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing/liquefaction): motivation>
Thus, even though the lord of mercury is colored (<s>rakta</s>) and has digested the seed (<s>bīja</s>), if devoid of <s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing),

children.text: vyāpī na bhavati dehe loheṣvapyathavāpi hi ṣaṇḍhatāṃ yāti // GRht_16.1 //
children.translated_text: it does not become pervasive in the body or even in metals; or rather, it becomes impotent (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>). || GRht 16.1 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
With a mind extended by wisdom, the self-extended one should perform action benefitting others;

children.text: arcīva śobhāṃ labhate parātparāṃ parāpavādādapi saṃnivṛttaḥ // GRhtCM_16.1:1 //
children.translated_text: like a flame, he obtains the most supreme splendor, having withdrawn even from the censure of others. || GRhtCM 16.1:1 ||
The projection of gold and such into mercury stationed in the oil-apparatus —
that which increases the transmuting power in metal — is proclaimed as <s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing).
Thus the technical definition (<s>paribhāṣā</s>). || GRhtCM 16.1:2 ||
Considering <s>sāraṇa</s> to be supreme, he praises it, saying 'thus' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.1:3 ||

children.text: iti pūrvoktena vidhānena rakto'pi rāgavānapi rasendraḥ sūtaḥ jaritabījo'pi jāritāni bījāni yasminniti sāraṇarahitaḥ sāraṇā vakṣyamāṇasaṃskārastena varjitaḥ vyāpī na bhavati dehe lohe ca vyāpako na syāt hi niścitaṃ athavāpi sāraṇārahito rasendraḥ ṣaṇḍhatāṃ yāti nirvīryatvam āpnoti // GRhtCM_16.1:4 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus,' by the previously stated method — even though colored (<s>rakta</s>), i.e., possessing coloring; even though having digested the seed — the lord of mercury, i.e., <s>sūta</s>, devoid of <s>sāraṇa</s>, i.e., lacking the processing to be described — does not become pervasive in the body or in metal, i.e., would not become a pervader. Indeed, certainly, or rather, the lord of mercury devoid of <s>sāraṇa</s> attains impotence (<s>ṣaṇḍhatā</s>), i.e., reaches a state of powerlessness. || GRhtCM 16.1:4 ||
START GRht 16.2-5
<s>sāraṇā</s> oil>
Of frogs, fish, turtles, rams, leeches, serpents, boars, and the like,
combining the fat of any one of them, then one should cook the <s>sāraṇā</s> oil. || GRht 16.2 ||
The oil of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> (Celastrus), <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia), <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia), and bitter gourd (<s>kaṭutumbī</s>) from one [source],
with double the [amount of] red-group decoction, one should cook with four times [the amount of] milk. || GRht 16.3 ||
<red group (<s>raktavarga</s>)>
With pomegranate (<s>dāḍima</s>), <s>palāśa</s> (Butea), <s>bandhūka</s> (Pentapetes) flowers, turmeric (<s>rajanī</s>), and red-colored [substances],
along with madder (<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>), lac juice (<s>lākṣārasa</s>), and red sandalwood — this is the red group. || GRht 16.4 ||
Coral (<s>vidruma</s>), earthworm excrement (<s>bhūnāga-mala</s>), and the droppings of flies, crows, and moths,

children.text: karṇamalaṃ mahiṣīṇāṃ krameṇa kalkaṃ kalāṃśena // GRht_16.5 //
children.translated_text: and the ear-wax of she-buffaloes — as a paste, in a sixteenth portion, in sequence. || GRht 16.5 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the fat-oil for <s>sāraṇa</s>, saying 'frogs' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:1 ||

children.text: maṇḍūko bhekaḥ matsyo jalacaraviśeṣaḥ kacchapaḥ kamaṭhaḥ pratītaḥ jalaukāḥ pratītāḥ ahiḥ sarpaḥ sūkaro varāhaḥ ādiśabdād gomahiṣagajoṣṭrakharanarakarkaṭaśiśumārā api grāhyāḥ // GRhtCM_16.2-5:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇḍūka</s> is a frog; <s>matsya</s> is a specific aquatic creature; <s>kacchapa</s> is a turtle, well-known; <s>jalaukā</s> (leeches) are well-known; <s>ahi</s> is a serpent; <s>sūkara</s> is a boar. By the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), the fat of cow, buffalo, elephant, camel, donkey, human, and crocodile (<s>śiśumāra</s>) should also be taken. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:2 ||

children.text: atha teṣāṃ madhye ekaikasya pṛthaktvena vasāṃ saṃyojya sāraṇaṃ tailaṃ sāraṇameva tailaṃ tatpacediti vahninā iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_16.2-5:3 //
children.translated_text: Now, combining the fat of each one of them individually, one should cook the <s>sāraṇa</s> oil — the oil that is itself <s>sāraṇa</s> — with fire — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:3 ||
He states the specific <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, saying '<s>jyotiṣmatī</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:4 ||

children.text: jyotiṣmatīvibhītakakarañjakaṭutumbītailaṃ jyotiṣmatī kaṅguṇī vibhītakaḥ kalidrumaḥ karañjaḥ pratītaḥ kaṭutumbī kaṭukā yā tumbī etāsāṃ tailaṃ ekaṃ ato dviguṇito yo raktakaṣāyaḥ raktagaṇasya kvāthaḥ taṃ niyojya pūrvasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_16.2-5:5 //
children.translated_text: 'The oil of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>karañja</s>, and bitter gourd' — <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> is <s>kaṅguṇī</s>; <s>vibhītaka</s> is the <s>kalidrama</s> tree; <s>karañja</s> is well-known; <s>kaṭutumbī</s> is the bitter gourd — the oil of these. One part of this; with double the amount of the red-group decoction, i.e., the decoction of the red group — combining [this] from the previous context. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:5 ||

children.text: kena saha caturguṇavasayā tathā tailataḥ caturguṇitena dugdhena saha pacet pākaṃ kuryāditi // GRhtCM_16.2-5:6 //
children.translated_text: With what? With four times the fat; likewise, with four times as much milk as the oil — one should cook, i.e., perform the cooking. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:6 ||
For the procedure of <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, he describes the red group, saying 'pomegranate' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:7 ||

children.text: dāḍimaṃ pratītaṃ palāśo brahmavṛkṣaḥ bandhūkapuṣpaṃ madhyāhnavikāśikusumaṃ rajanī haridrā etābhiḥ aruṇasahitābhiḥ aruṇaṃ āraktaṃ yaddravyaṃ kārpāsakusumādikaṃ tatsahitābhiḥ // GRhtCM_16.2-5:8 //
children.translated_text: Pomegranate is well-known; <s>palāśa</s> is the <s>Brahmavṛkṣa</s>; <s>bandhūka</s> flower is the flower that blooms at midday; <s>rajanī</s> is turmeric. With these, 'along with red-colored [substances]' — reddish substance such as cotton-flower and the like — along with those. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:8 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭo'yaṃ raktavargaḥ mañjiṣṭhālākṣārasacandanasahitaḥ mañjiṣṭhā pratītā lākṣārasaḥ alaktakaḥ candanaṃ raktacandanam // GRhtCM_16.2-5:9 //
children.translated_text: Of what character is this red group? 'Along with madder, lac juice, and sandalwood' — madder (<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>) is well-known; lac juice is <s>alaktaka</s> (lac dye); sandalwood means red sandalwood. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:9 ||
He states the paste for the <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, saying 'coral' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:10 ||

children.text: vidrumaṃ latāmaṇir bhūnāgamalaṃ gaṇḍūpadapurīṣaṃ makṣikādhvāṅkṣaśalabhānāṃ makṣikā jīvaviśeṣaḥ dhvāṅkṣāḥ kākāḥ śalabhaḥ pataṅgaḥ iti haimaḥ teṣāṃ viṭ śakṛt punarmahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalaṃ krameṇa kalāṃśena ṣoḍaśāṃśena kalkaṃ prativāpaṃ dattvā pūrvatailamuttārayet // GRhtCM_16.2-5:11 //
children.translated_text: Coral (<s>vidruma</s>) is the creeper-gem; earthworm excrement (<s>bhūnāga-mala</s>) is the feces of earthworms; of flies — a specific kind of insect; crows (<s>dhvāṅkṣa</s>); and moths (<s>śalabha</s>) — these are gold-related; their excrement (<s>viṭ</s>). Furthermore, the ear-wax of she-buffaloes. In sequence, in a sixteenth portion, i.e., in a one-sixteenth share — adding this paste as the subsidiary ingredient (<s>prativāpa</s>), one should prepare the aforementioned oil. || GRhtCM 16.2-5:11 ||
START GRht 16.6-8
<s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing process)>
Having taken [the oil] filtered through cloth, [pour] the mercury into a full, elongated crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>);

children.text: tadanu khalu taptataile pradrāvya samaṃ kṣiped bījam // GRht_16.6 //
children.translated_text: then, having melted [mercury] in the heated oil, one should add the seed in equal [proportion]. || GRht 16.6 ||
The mouth of the crucible should be covered with a cloth-soaked-in-oil, stretched and tied with two creeper-strips,

children.text: tailārdrapaṭena tato bījaṃ prakṣipya samakālam // GRht_16.7 //
children.translated_text: then, having inserted the seed simultaneously. || GRht 16.7 ||
Mercury, applied by the <s>sāraṇa</s> method with seeds in proportion to the flesh (<s>piśita</s>),

children.text: akṣīyamāṇo milati ca bījair baddho bhavatyeva // GRht_16.8 //
children.translated_text: without diminishing, merges with the seeds — it indeed becomes bound. || GRht 16.8 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the operation with the prepared oil, saying 'cloth' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.6-8:1 ||

children.text: tatsiddhatailaṃ paṭagālitaṃ vastrapūtaṃ gṛhītvā tadanu tatpaścāt // GRhtCM_16.6-8:2 //
children.translated_text: That prepared oil, filtered through cloth, i.e., purified through a cloth-strainer — having taken [it]; then, i.e., after that. || GRhtCM 16.6-8:2 ||

children.text: sampūrṇadīrghamūṣāyāṃ gostanākārāyāṃ taptataile koṣṇasāraṇataile sūtaṃ kṣipet // GRhtCM_16.6-8:3 //
children.translated_text: In a full, elongated crucible, i.e., in a cow-udder-shaped [crucible], [having placed] the mercury into the heated oil, i.e., into the warm <s>sāraṇa</s> oil — one should cast [it]. || GRhtCM 16.6-8:3 ||

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā bījaṃ samaṃ samabhāgaṃ rasatulyaṃ yadbhāvyaṃ mahābījaṃ tat bhāvitaṃ kṛtvetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.6-8:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? The seed in equal proportion — equal in share, i.e., equal to the mercury — the great seed that is to be soaked — having prepared that — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 16.6-8:4 ||
He states the construction of the <s>sāraṇa</s> apparatus, saying 'crucible' and so forth.

children.text: samakālam ekakālaṃ yathā syāttathā bījaṃ mūṣāntarnikṣipya tato'nantaraṃ mūṣāvaktraṃ sthagayet ācchādayet // GRhtCM_16.6-8:5 //
children.translated_text: Simultaneously, i.e., at one time, in such a way — having cast the seed inside the crucible, then immediately thereafter, the mouth of the crucible should be covered, i.e., sealed. || GRhtCM 16.6-8:5 ||
With what? With an oil-soaked cloth, i.e., with a cloth moistened with <s>sāraṇa</s> oil. || GRhtCM 16.6-8:6 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭena latādvayena vastracīradvayena protaṃ ca tadvitataṃ vistīrṇaṃ ca tat naddhaṃ baddhaṃ tena // GRhtCM_16.6-8:7 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? Threaded through two creeper-strips, i.e., two cloth-bands, and spread out, i.e., extended, and tied, i.e., bound — with that. || GRhtCM 16.6-8:7 ||

children.text: akṣīyamāṇo milati na kṣīyata ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.6-8:8 //
children.translated_text: 'Without diminishing, merges' — meaning it does not diminish. || GRhtCM 16.6-8:8 ||

children.text: sūte milati baddho jñeyaḥ bījaiḥ saha milito baddho bhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.6-8:9 //
children.translated_text: Mercury merges — bound — [this] should be understood; merged with seeds, it becomes bound — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 16.6-8:9 ||
By the mention of yellow and other colors, [the capacity] to produce [those colors] is also indicated. || GRhtCM 16.6-8:10 ||
START GRht 16.9
<mercury: <s>pratisāraṇa</s> (counter-flowing)>
Similarly, in a deep crucible, the king of mercury, still moist with <s>sāraṇa</s> oil,
[adding] gold in double the amount of mercury — one should then perform counter-flowing (<s>pratisāraṇa</s>). || GRht 16.9 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
After the <s>sāraṇa</s> of mercury and seed, he states the <s>sāraṇa</s> of gold, saying 'similarly' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.9:1 ||

children.text: tadvat pūrvavidhānena gabhīramūṣe dīrghamūṣāyāṃ sāraṇatailārdraṃ sāraṇatailāplutaṃ eva niścayena rasarājaṃ kuryāditi śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_16.9:2 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, by the previous method, in a deep crucible, i.e., in an elongated crucible — moist with <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, i.e., saturated with <s>sāraṇa</s> oil — indeed, with certainty — the king of mercury should be [prepared] — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 16.9:2 ||

children.text: tadanu tatpaścātsūtāddviguṇaṃ yatkanakaṃ hema tadatra dattvā pratisārayetsāraṇaṃ kuryātpūrvavat // GRhtCM_16.9:3 //
children.translated_text: Then, thereafter — gold in double the amount of mercury — that gold (<s>kanaka</s>), having been added here, should be counter-flowed (<s>pratisārayet</s>), i.e., the <s>sāraṇa</s> should be performed as before. || GRhtCM 16.9:3 ||
START GRht 16.10
<mercury: <s>anusāraṇa</s> (after-flowing)>
With seed in triple the amount, one should perform after-flowing (<s>anusāraṇa</s>) on the mercury placed in the exposed [crucible].
He states another method, saying 'with seed' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.9:1 ||

children.text: prakāśasthaṃ prakāśamūṣāgataṃ sūtaṃ triguṇena bījena anusārayet pratisārayet // GRhtCM_16.9:2 //
children.translated_text: The mercury placed in the exposed crucible (<s>prakāśamūṣā</s>) — with triple the seed, one should perform after-flowing (<s>anusāraṇa</s>), i.e., counter-flowing (<s>pratisāraṇa</s>). || GRhtCM 16.9:2 ||
START GRht 16.10

children.text: īṣannāgaṃ deyaṃ trividhāyāṃ sāraṇāyāṃ tu // GRht_16.10 //
children.translated_text: A small amount of lead (<s>nāga</s>) should be added in the threefold <s>sāraṇa</s>. || GRht 16.10 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā īṣadalpaṃ nāgaṃ dattvā trividhāyāṃ sāraṇāyāmevaṃ vidheyam iti // GRhtCM_16.10:1 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having added a slight, small [amount of] lead — in the threefold <s>sāraṇa</s>, thus it should be done. || GRhtCM 16.10:1 ||
START GRht 16.11-12
<s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus>

children.text: kṛtvā mūṣāṃ dīrghāṃ bandhitatribhāgapraṇālikāṃ tāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Having made an elongated crucible with a channel sealed at one-third [of its length],
at its end, an open crucible (<s>prakaṭamūṣā</s>) with a hole, firmly coated with clay. || GRht 16.11 ||
Having cast the mercury into that, moistened with <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, when heated,

children.text: pradrāvya tulyakanakaṃ kṣipte'smin milati rasarājaḥ // GRht_16.12 //
children.translated_text: having melted an equal [amount of] gold and cast it in — the king of mercury merges [with it]. || GRht 16.12 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He describes the <s>sāraṇa</s> apparatus, saying 'having made' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.11-12:1 ||

children.text: prathamaṃ dīrghāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā ca punaḥ tāṃ bandhitatribhāgapraṇālikāṃ bandhitā tribhāge praṇālikā yasyāḥ sā tāṃ ca kṛtvā tasyāgre yantrasyāgre praṇālikāyāṃ mūṣāntarityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.11-12:2 //
children.translated_text: First, having made an elongated crucible, and furthermore, that [crucible] with a channel sealed at one-third — in which the channel is sealed at the one-third mark — having made such [a crucible]; at its end, i.e., at the end of the apparatus, in the channel, meaning inside the [second] crucible — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 16.11-12:2 ||

children.text: sudṛḍhamṛttikāliptā sacchidrā randhrasahitā prakaṭamūṣā prakāśamūṣā kāryeti yantram // GRhtCM_16.11-12:3 //
children.translated_text: Firmly coated with clay, with a hole, i.e., possessing an opening — the open crucible (<s>prakaṭamūṣā</s>), i.e., the exposed crucible, should be made — thus is the apparatus. || GRhtCM 16.11-12:3 ||

children.text: tasminyantre sāraṇatailānvitaṃ rasaṃ prakṣipya tato'nantaraṃ tulyaṃ kanakaṃ pradrāvya gālayitvā tasminneva tapte yantre kṣipte sati raso milati ekatāṃ yāti // GRhtCM_16.11-12:4 //
children.translated_text: In that apparatus, having cast the mercury moistened with <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, then thereafter, having melted an equal [amount of] gold, having strained [it], and cast [it] into that very heated apparatus — the mercury merges, i.e., attains unity. || GRhtCM 16.11-12:4 ||
START GRht 16.13-16
<s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus>
Having made an elongated tube (<s>nalikā</s>) of six finger-breadths, resembling a datura flower,

children.text: mūṣāpyadho vilagnā kartavyā vai mṛdā lepyā // GRht_16.13 //
children.translated_text: a crucible attached below must also be made, and it should be coated with clay. || GRht 16.13 ||

children.text: aparā sūkṣmā nalikā kāryā saptāṃgulā sudṛḍhā /
children.translated_text: Another fine tube should be made, of seven finger-breadths, sturdy,

children.text: madhye praviśati ca yathā tadvatkāryā ca dṛḍhamukhā // GRht_16.14 //
children.translated_text: made so that it fits into the middle [of the first tube], with a firm mouth. || GRht 16.14 ||
Mercury is cast into that, moistened with <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, its mouth sealed with datura [paste];

children.text: tadanu bṛhattamayā hema pradrāvya hemakoṣṭhikayā // GRht_16.15 //
children.translated_text: then, having melted gold with a large [apparatus], in a gold-furnace (<s>hemakoṣṭhikā</s>), || GRht 16.15 ||
having cast [the gold] into the middle of that, one should turn the tube-end face-down;

children.text: antarūrdhvaṃ bhārākrāntāṃ sarati raso nātra saṃdehaḥ // GRht_16.16 //
children.translated_text: inside, upward, pressed down by weight — the mercury flows — there is no doubt about this. || GRht 16.16 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another apparatus, saying 'having made' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.13-16:1 ||

children.text: pūrvavaddīrghāṃ dhūrtakusumasaṃkāśāṃ dhattūrapuṣpasaṃkāśāṃ pūrvayantranalikāyāḥ sthāne evaṃvidhāṃ ṣaḍaṅgulāṃ nalikāṃ kuryād iti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_16.13-16:2 //
children.translated_text: As before, elongated, resembling a datura flower — such a tube of six finger-breadths should be made, in place of the tube of the previous apparatus — this is the clarification. || GRhtCM 16.13-16:2 ||

children.text: mūṣāpi adho vilagnā nalikāyāstalabhāge mūṣā vilagnā saṃlagnā kāryā // GRhtCM_16.13-16:3 //
children.translated_text: A crucible also, attached below, i.e., at the bottom of the tube — a crucible joined, i.e., connected — should be made. || GRhtCM 16.13-16:3 ||

children.text: sā ca mṛdā mṛtsnayā lepyā // GRhtCM_16.13-16:4 //
children.translated_text: And that should be coated with clay (<s>mṛtsnā</s>). || GRhtCM 16.13-16:4 ||

children.text: punarapi aparā sūkṣmā nālikā saptāṅgulā saptāṅgulaparimāṇā sudṛḍhā manoharakaṭhinā kāryā yathā madhye ṣaḍaṅgulanālikāntaḥ praviśati tadvattathā kāryā // GRhtCM_16.13-16:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, another fine tube, of seven finger-breadths, i.e., of seven-finger-breadth measure, sturdy, i.e., beautifully firm — should be made so that it fits into the middle of the six-finger-breadth tube — in that manner it should be constructed. || GRhtCM 16.13-16:5 ||

children.text: kiṃbhūtā dṛḍhamukhā dṛḍhaṃ mukhaṃ yasyāḥ sā evaṃrūpā tasmin saṃsiddhe yantre sāraṇatailānvitaḥ sūtaḥ kṣiptaḥ san madanaruddhamukhaḥ kāryaḥ madanena sikthakena ruddhaṃ mudritaṃ mukhaṃ yasya saḥ // GRhtCM_16.13-16:6 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? With a firm mouth (<s>dṛḍhamukha</s>) — having a firm opening. In such a perfected apparatus, mercury combined with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil, having been placed, should be made with its mouth sealed with wax (<s>madana</s>, i.e., <s>sikthaka</s>) — meaning the mouth is sealed, closed with wax. || GRhtCM 16.13-16:6 ||

children.text: tadanu tatpaścāt hemakoṣṭhikayā hemno yā koṣṭhī eva koṣṭhikā tayā hema svarṇaṃ pradrāvya drāvayitvā tatra kṣipet ityadhyāhāryam // GRhtCM_16.13-16:7 //
children.translated_text: Then, after that, with a gold-chamber (<s>hemakoṣṭhikā</s>) — the <s>koṣṭhī</s> (furnace) that is for gold, that is the <s>koṣṭhikā</s> — with that, having melted gold (<s>svarṇa</s>), one should cast [it] therein: this is to be supplied [from context]. || GRhtCM 16.13-16:7 ||

children.text: tasminyantre madhye'ntaḥ nalikāgraṃ nalikāyāḥ saptāṅgulāyā agrabhāgaṃ kṣiptvā adhomukhīṃ kuryāt punarūrdhvaṃ bhārākrāntāṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_16.13-16:8 //
children.translated_text: In the middle of that apparatus, inside, the tip of the tube (<s>nalikāgra</s>) — the front portion of the seven-<s>aṅgula</s> tube — having been placed [therein], it should be made facing downward; furthermore, at the top, it should be made weighed down. || GRhtCM 16.13-16:8 ||

children.text: iti kṛte sati rasaḥ sarati hemnā milati na saṃdehaḥ niyatamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.13-16:9 //
children.translated_text: When this is done, mercury flows (<s>sarati</s>) — it combines with gold — there is no doubt; meaning it is certain. || GRhtCM 16.13-16:9 ||
[START GRht 16.17-18]
<<s>Sāraṇā-yantra</s> (spreading apparatus)>
Having made an eight-<s>aṅgula</s> crucible, resembling a <s>dhūrta</s> (thorn-apple) flower, firm and smooth —

children.text: aparā madhyagatāpi ca sacchidrā ca saptāṃgulā kāryā // GRht_16.17 //
children.translated_text: another [crucible], placed in the middle, with a hole, seven <s>aṅgulas</s> [long], should be made. || GRht 16.17 ||

children.text: niruddhatāṃ ca kṛtvā sūtaṃ prakṣipya tailasaṃyuktam /
children.translated_text: Having sealed it and placed mercury combined with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil [within],

children.text: nirdhūmaṃ karṣāgnau sthāpya mūṣāṃ susaṃdhitāṃ kṛtvā // GRht_16.18 //
children.translated_text: placing the well-joined crucible in a smokeless cowdung fire — || GRht 16.18 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another apparatus-procedure, beginning with 'having made' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.17-18:1 ||

children.text: aṣṭāṅgulamūṣāṃ aṣṭāṅgulaparimāṇadīrghāṃ dhūrtakusumopamāṃ kanakapuṣpasadṛśāṃ dṛḍhāṃ kaṭhināṃ ślakṣṇāṃ masṛṇāṃ evaṃvidhāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā aparā dvitīyā saptāṅgulā saptāṅgulaparimāṇadīrghā sacchidrā randhrayuktā sā madhyagatā antaḥpraviṣṭā kāryā apītyavaśyaṃ iti mūṣādvayayantraṃ siddham // GRhtCM_16.17-18:2 //
children.translated_text: An eight-<s>aṅgula</s> crucible — eight <s>aṅgulas</s> in length; resembling a <s>dhūrta</s> (thorn-apple) flower, i.e., like a <s>kanakapuṣpa</s>; firm — hard; smooth — polished. Having made such a crucible, a second one, seven <s>aṅgulas</s> [long] — seven <s>aṅgulas</s> in length — with a hole — having an opening — placed in the middle — inserted inside [the first] — should be made. 'And' [indicates] certainly. Thus the double-crucible apparatus is complete. || GRhtCM 16.17-18:2 ||

children.text: taccāha pūrvoktāyāmantaḥpraviṣṭāyāṃ saptāṅgulāyāṃ sūtaṃ tailasaṃyuktaṃ sāraṇatailasahitaṃ prakṣipya niruddhatāṃ ca kṛtvā nirdhūmaṃ yathā syāt tathā karṣāgnau mūṣāṃ sthāpya punaḥ kiṃ kṛtvā susaṃdhitāṃ sandhimudritāṃ kṛtvā pūrvavatsārayedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.17-18:3 //
children.translated_text: That he states: in the previously mentioned [crucible] that has been inserted inside — the seven-<s>aṅgula</s> one — having placed mercury combined with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil — accompanied by <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil — and having sealed it; so that it would be smokeless, in a cowdung fire, the crucible should be placed; and furthermore, having done what? Having made it well-joined — sealed at the junction — then one should perform <s>sāraṇa</s> as before: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 16.17-18:3 ||
[START GRht 16.19-21]
<<s>Sāraṇā-yantra</s>>
A tube of one <s>vitasti</s> (span) in length should also be made; two crucibles, firm, at its front —

children.text: uttānaikā kāryā niśchidrā chidramudritā ca tanau // GRht_16.19 //
children.translated_text: one should be made upright, without holes; with a sealed hole in the [wall of the] slender [crucible]. || GRht 16.19 ||

children.text: dattvā sūtaṃ pūrvaṃ sāraṇatailānvitaṃ nidhāpya bhuvi /
children.translated_text: Having first placed mercury combined with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil, depositing [it] on the ground,

children.text: uttānāyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ tasyāṃ bījaṃ samāvṛtya // GRht_16.20 //
children.translated_text: in the upright crucible, having covered the <s>bīja</s> (seed-metal) — || GRht 16.20 ||

children.text: svacchaṃ jñātvā ca tatastadbījaṃ chidrasaṃsthitaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: Having ascertained it to be clear [i.e., properly melted], then one should place that <s>bīja</s> in the hole;
the <s>bīja</s> falls upon the mercury — it binds [it], without doubt. || GRht 16.21 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another apparatus-procedure: two crucibles should be made. || GRhtCM 16.19-21:1 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭe tadagrato vitastimātranalike vitastiparimāṇe nalike yayoste evaṃvidhe sudṛḍhe ubhe kārye ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_16.19-21:2 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? At its front, with <s>vitasti</s>-length tubes — tubes of one <s>vitasti</s> (span) in measurement — these two, of such a character, should be made very firm: this is the intent. || GRhtCM 16.19-21:2 ||
