children.text: tayormadhye ekā mūṣā uttānā kāryā aparā nimneti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_16.19-21:3 //
children.translated_text: Between those two, one crucible should be made upright; the other [should be] inverted: this is the purport. || GRhtCM 16.19-21:3 ||

children.text: uttānā kiṃviśiṣṭā niśchidrā nirvraṇā chidramudritā chidraṃ mudritaṃ yasyāṃ tanau mūṣāśarīre iti // GRhtCM_16.19-21:4 //
children.translated_text: The upright one — of what character? Without holes — without perforations; with a sealed hole in the [wall of the] slender body of the crucible. || GRhtCM 16.19-21:4 ||

children.text: taccāha pūrvaṃ prathamaṃ sūtaṃ yantre pūrvokte sāraṇatailānvitaṃ dattvā bhuvi nidhāpya tasyāṃ uktāyāṃ uttānāyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ bījaṃ mahābījaṃ samāvṛtya dravīkṛtya dattvetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.19-21:5 //
children.translated_text: That he states: first, in the previously described apparatus, having placed mercury combined with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil; having deposited [it] on the ground; in the said upright crucible, having covered the <s>bīja</s> — the <s>mahābīja</s> — having melted [it] and placed [it]: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 16.19-21:5 ||

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ bījaṃ svacchamamalaṃ dravarūpaṃ jñātvā chidrasaṃsthitaṃ kuryāt chidrāntaḥ kṣipedityabhiprāyaḥ chidrāntaḥkṣepaṇāt bījaṃ rasasyopari patati sati sūtaṃ asaṃdehaṃ yathā syāttathā badhnāti bīje chidrāntaḥkṣepaṇānantaraṃ chidramacchidraṃ syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.19-21:6 //
children.translated_text: Then, after that, having ascertained the <s>bīja</s> to be clear — pure, in liquid form — one should place it in the hole — the intent is to cast it inside the hole. From the casting inside the hole, the <s>bīja</s> falls upon the mercury; then mercury, without doubt — certainly — becomes bound. After casting the <s>bīja</s> inside the hole, the hole should become [sealed as if] without a hole: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 16.19-21:6 ||
[START GRht 16.22-23]
<<s>Sāraṇā</s> (6th procedure)>
That open crucible (<s>prakāśamūṣā</s>), [placed] inverted, inserted by half an <s>aṅgula</s> —

children.text: nalikā kāryā vidhinā ūrdhve sūtastvadho bījam // GRht_16.22 //
children.translated_text: a tube should be made by the [proper] method; mercury above, <s>bīja</s> below. || GRht 16.22 ||

children.text: mūṣāṃ nirudhya vidhinā dhmātā koṣṭhe drutaṃ bījam /
children.translated_text: Having sealed the crucible by the [proper] method and smelted [it] in a furnace (<s>koṣṭha</s>), the <s>bīja</s>, once melted,

children.text: jñātvā parivartya tato nibadhnāti sūtarājaṃ ca // GRht_16.23 //
children.translated_text: having been ascertained [as ready], then inverted — it binds the king of mercury. || GRht 16.23 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Beginning with 'that' and so forth: || GRhtCM 16.22-23:1 ||

children.text: punaḥ sā vitastimātranalikā prakāśamūṣā ardhāṅgulasuniviṣṭā mūṣāntaḥ praviṣṭā nyubjā adhomukhī kāryā tasyāḥ prakāśamūṣāyāḥ nalikā praṇālikā vidhinā śāstravārtikasaṃpradāyena kāryā yathordhve sūto bhavedadho bījamityarthaḥ mūṣām ityādi // GRhtCM_16.22-23:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that <s>vitasti</s>-length tube — the open crucible (<s>prakāśamūṣā</s>) — inserted by half an <s>aṅgula</s> into the interior of the crucible, made inverted — facing downward; its tube, the channel, should be made according to the tradition of scripture and practice, such that mercury would be above and the <s>bīja</s> below: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 16.22-23:2 ||

children.text: mūṣāṃ nirudhya randhraṃ dūrīkṛtya vidhinā koṣṭhe koṣṭhīyantre sā mūṣā dhmātā kāryā drutaṃ dravarūpaṃ kṛtaṃ bījaṃ jñātvā parivartya ca mūṣāyāṃ bījasya parivartanaṃ kṛtvā tato bījaṃ sūtarājaṃ badhnātīti // GRhtCM_16.22-23:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Having sealed the crucible' — having closed the opening; by the [proper] method; in a furnace (<s>koṣṭhī-yantra</s>), that crucible should be smelted. Having ascertained the melted <s>bīja</s> — rendered into liquid form — and having inverted [it] — performing the inversion of the <s>bīja</s> in the crucible — then the <s>bīja</s> binds the king of mercury. || GRhtCM 16.22-23:3 ||
[START GRht 16.24]
<<s>Sāraṇā</s> with <s>ḍamaru-yantra</s> (drum-shaped apparatus)>
Alternatively, in a <s>ḍamaruka-yantra</s> (drum-shaped apparatus), mercury employed by the <s>sāraṇa</s> method —

children.text: sarati rasendro vidhinā jñātvā tatkarmakauśalyam // GRht_16.24 //
children.translated_text: the lord of mercury flows by the [proper] method, when one knows the skill of that operation. || GRht 16.24 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states another apparatus, beginning with 'alternatively' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.24:1 ||

children.text: vidhinā sāraṇavidhānena ḍamarukayantre uktalakṣaṇapātanakaraṇocite yantre sūto niyojitaḥ san sarati bījena milati // GRhtCM_16.24:2 //
children.translated_text: By the method of <s>sāraṇa</s>-procedure, in a <s>ḍamaruka-yantra</s> — an apparatus suited for the previously described distillation operation — mercury, when employed therein, flows — combines with the <s>bīja</s>. || GRhtCM 16.24:2 ||
[START GRht 16.25]
<<s>Jāraṇā</s> after <s>sāraṇā</s> → <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) potency>
That <s>sārita</s> (spread/flowed) lord of mercury should then be assimilated by the <s>grāsa</s> (swallowing) method;

children.text: punarapi sāritasūto vidhyati koṭyaṃśataḥ śulbam // GRht_16.25 //
children.translated_text: furthermore, the <s>sārita</s> mercury transmutes (<s>vidhyati</s>) copper in a proportion of one-<s>koṭi</s> (ten million). || GRht 16.25 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā rasendro niyojitaḥ jñātvā tatkarmakauśalyaṃ rasendrakarmaprāvīṇyaṃ jñātveti // GRhtCM_16.25:1 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Mercury is employed — having known the skill of that operation, the proficiency in mercury-work: having known [this]. || GRhtCM 16.25:1 ||
[START GRht 16.26]
<<s>Sāraṇā</s> with <s>krāmaṇa</s>-fat>
Through the combination of <s>krāmaṇa</s>-fat and other [agents], mercury flows by the [proper] method;
due to its fickleness and excessive lightness, the <s>bīja</s> — therefore, drops (<s>vipluṣa</s>) must be made [i.e., stabilized]. || GRht 16.26 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states [this] to reinforce the previous [point], beginning with '<s>krāmaṇa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.26:1 ||

children.text: sūto vidhinoktavidhānena krāmaṇocitā yā vasā maṇḍūkādīnāṃ tā eva ādayo yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ yogātsarati sāraṇā syāt punarbījayuto'pi sūtaḥ capalatvātilaghutvāt capalatvaṃ cañcalatvaṃ ca atilaghutvaṃ ca tasmāddhetoḥ avipluṣaḥ sthiraḥ kāryaḥ // GRhtCM_16.26:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury, by the stated method, through the combination of the fats suited for <s>krāmaṇa</s> — the fats of frogs and such — these being the initial [agents] of those [combinations] — flows: <s>sāraṇā</s> occurs. Furthermore, mercury combined with the <s>bīja</s>, due to fickleness — restlessness — and excessive lightness — for that reason, should be made into stable drops (<s>avipluṣa</s>), i.e., immobile. || GRhtCM 16.26:2 ||
[START GRht 16.27]
<<s>Sāraṇa</s> and <s>krāmaṇa</s> with lead and others>

children.text: sarati sukhena ca sūto dahati mukhaṃ naiva hastapādādi /
children.translated_text: Mercury flows easily and does not burn the face, hands, feet, or other [body parts];
mercury pervades (<s>kramati</s>) through the combination with lead (<s>phaṇi</s>), along with pyrite-combined gold and ochre (<s>gairikā</s>). || GRht 16.27 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the previously described qualities, beginning with 'flows' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.27:1 ||

children.text: pūrvavidhānā sūtaḥ sarati sāritaḥ sūto mukhaṃ na dahati hastapādādi ca aṅgavibhāgaṃ naiva dahati // GRhtCM_16.27:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury, [processed] by the previous method, flows — the <s>sārita</s> mercury does not burn the face, and it does not burn the hands, feet, or other limb-divisions either. || GRhtCM 16.27:2 ||

children.text: punaḥ phaṇiyogāt nāgasaṃyogataḥ mākṣikayutahemagairikayā saha tāpyamilitasvarṇagairikayā sārdhaṃ krāmati // GRhtCM_16.27:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, through the combination with lead (<s>phaṇi</s>, i.e., <s>nāga</s>), together with pyrite-combined gold and ochre (<s>gairikā</s>) — together with <s>tāpya</s>-infused gold and mineral ochre — it pervades (<s>krāmati</s>). || GRhtCM 16.27:3 ||
[START GRht 16.28]
<<s>Druti</s> (liquefaction) and <s>sāraṇā</s>>
Through the combination with pyrite-essence and through the combination with lead (<s>phaṇi</s>), [mercury] melts rapidly, like lead;

children.text: dravati ca kanake sūtaḥ saṃsāryate vidhinā // GRht_16.28 //
children.translated_text: mercury melts in gold and is caused to flow (<s>saṃsāryate</s>) by the [proper] method. || GRht 16.28 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the easy <s>sāraṇa</s> method, beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.28:1 ||

children.text: kanakaṃ hema mākṣikasattvayogāt phaṇisaṃyogānnāgasaṃyogācca śīghraṃ dravati kanake dravati sati vidhinā sāraṇatailādinā saṃsāryate sāraṇā kriyata iti // GRhtCM_16.28:2 //
children.translated_text: Gold (<s>hema</s>) — through the combination with pyrite-essence, and through the combination with lead (<s>phaṇi</s>, i.e., <s>nāga</s>) — quickly melts. When it melts in gold, by the method of <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil and such, it is caused to flow (<s>saṃsāryate</s>) — <s>sāraṇā</s> is performed. || GRhtCM 16.28:2 ||
[START GRht 16.29]
<Mercury: preparation for <s>vedha</s> (transmutation)>

children.text: tasmād dravyavidhāyī sūto bījena sārito laghunā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, mercury, the producer of substances (<s>dravyavidhāyī</s>), when flowed (<s>sārita</s>) with a large <s>bīja</s> —
when equally flowed (<s>samasārita</s>) and well-bound, in the crucible would [undergo] melting (<s>samāvarta</s>). || GRht 16.29 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the qualities of mercury through <s>sāraṇā</s>, beginning with 'therefore' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.29:1 ||

children.text: tasmāddhetoḥ sūto dravyavidhāyī syāt iti śeṣaḥ dravyakartetyartha // GRhtCM_16.29:2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, for that reason, mercury would become a producer of substances: this is the completion; meaning a maker of substances. || GRhtCM 16.29:2 ||

children.text: alaghunā bījena analpaparimāṇena mahābījena sāritaḥ san samasāritaḥ san baddho bhavet ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_16.29:3 //
children.translated_text: When flowed (<s>sārita</s>) with a not-small <s>bīja</s> — with a <s>mahābīja</s> of not-small quantity — and being equally flowed (<s>samasārita</s>), it would become bound: this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 16.29:3 ||

children.text: mūṣāyāṃ samāvarto dravaṇaṃ syāt vahnidhamanāt iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_16.29:4 //
children.translated_text: In the crucible, <s>samāvarta</s> means melting — this would [occur] through the blowing of fire: this is the completion. || GRhtCM 16.29:4 ||
[START GRht 16.30]
<(<s>Prati-sāraṇā</s> and <s>anu-sāraṇā</s>)>
Mercury that has been flowed and turned — which combines with an equal <s>bīja</s> is called <s>sārya</s> (flowable);

children.text: dviguṇena pratisāryaḥ sa cānusāryaśca triguṇena // GRht_16.30 //
children.translated_text: with double [<s>bīja</s>], it is <s>pratisārya</s> (counter-flowable); and with triple, it is <s>anusārya</s> (sequentially-flowable). || GRht 16.30 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the graduated sequence of <s>sāraṇā</s>, beginning with '<s>sarati</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.30:1 ||

children.text: sāritavartitasūtaḥ sāritaścāsau vartitaś ceti vigrahaḥ // GRhtCM_16.30:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sāritavartitasūtaḥ</s> — 'that which has been flowed and that which has been turned': this is the analysis of the compound. || GRhtCM 16.30:2 ||

children.text: yaḥ samānabījena tulyamahābījena milati sa sāryaḥ yo dviguṇena milati saḥ pratisāryaḥ yaśca triguṇena so'nusārya iti sāraṇākramo darśitaḥ // GRhtCM_16.30:3 //
children.translated_text: That which combines with an equal <s>bīja</s> — an equal <s>mahābīja</s> — is <s>sārya</s>; that which combines with a double [<s>bīja</s>] is <s>pratisārya</s>; and that which [combines] with a triple [<s>bīja</s>] is <s>anusārya</s>: thus the graduated sequence of <s>sāraṇā</s> has been shown. || GRhtCM 16.30:3 ||
[START GRht 16.31]
<<s>Sāraṇa</s> ↔ <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) potency>
The <s>sārya</s> [mercury] transmutes a hundredfold; the <s>pratisārita</s> becomes a thousandfold transmuter;

children.text: anusārito'yutena ca vidhināpi balābalaṃ jñātvā // GRht_16.31 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>anusārita</s>, ten-thousandfold — [all this] by the method, having assessed the strength and weakness. || GRht 16.31 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the qualities of the graduated <s>sāraṇā</s> sequence, beginning with 'hundred' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.31:1 ||

children.text: yaḥ sāryaḥ samasāritaḥ sa śatavedhī syād ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_16.31:2 //
children.translated_text: That which is <s>sārya</s> — equally flowed — would be a hundredfold transmuter: this is the intent. || GRhtCM 16.31:2 ||

children.text: punaḥ pratisāritaḥ dviguṇabījena sārito yaḥ sūtaḥ sa sahasravedhī syāt // GRhtCM_16.31:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>pratisārita</s> — the mercury flowed with a double-quantity <s>bīja</s> — would be a thousandfold transmuter. || GRhtCM 16.31:3 ||

children.text: ca punaḥ anusāritaḥ triguṇabījena sāritaḥ sa ayutena ayutavedhī syāditi vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_16.31:4 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, the <s>anusārita</s> — flowed with a triple-quantity <s>bīja</s> — would be a ten-thousandfold transmuter: this is the clear meaning. || GRhtCM 16.31:4 ||
'By the method' means by the stated procedure. || GRhtCM 16.31:5 ||

children.text: balābalaṃ jñātvā nyūnādhikyaṃ matvā vidhinā yukta iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_16.31:6 //
children.translated_text: 'Having assessed the strength and weakness' means having considered the degrees of less and more — [and applied] the method accordingly: this is the completion. || GRhtCM 16.31:6 ||
[START GRht 16.32]

children.text: anusāritena tu samaḥ svacchaḥ sūtaḥ sāritastadanu /
children.translated_text: Mercury that has been <s>anusārita</s> and [then] equally flowed (<s>sārita</s>) — the pure mercury — thereafter

children.text: sa bhavati lakṣavedhī pratisāritaḥ prayutavedhī ca // GRht_16.32 //
children.translated_text: becomes a hundred-thousandfold (<s>lakṣa</s>) transmuter; the <s>pratisārita</s> becomes a millionfold (<s>prayuta</s>) transmuter. || GRht 16.32 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the special distinction of the <s>anusārita</s> over the <s>sārita</s> and <s>pratisārita</s>, beginning with '<s>anu</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 16.32:1 ||

children.text: tu punaḥ svacchaḥ pradhānasaṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaḥ sūtaḥ anusāritena samaḥ triguṇabījena sārito'nusāritastena tulyo yadi syātsa ca lakṣavedhī syāt // GRhtCM_16.32:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the pure mercury — processed with the primary <s>saṃskāras</s> — when equal to the <s>anusārita</s>, i.e., flowed with a triple-quantity <s>bīja</s> and thus made equal to that [level] — if it becomes so, then it would be a hundred-thousandfold transmuter. || GRhtCM 16.32:2 ||

children.text: evaṃ pratisāritaḥ sūtaḥ samena sārito 'yutavedhī syāt // GRhtCM_16.32:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>pratisārita</s> mercury, when flowed with an equal [<s>bīja</s>], would be a ten-thousandfold transmuter. || GRhtCM 16.32:3 ||

children.text: evaṃ svecchātisvacchavṛddhau vedhasyāpi vṛddhiḥ syāditi rahasyam // GRhtCM_16.32:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus, with the progressive increase in purity, the increase in transmutation [potency] would also [occur]: this is the secret. || GRhtCM 16.32:4 ||
[START GRht 16.33]
Mercury, even [when merely] <s>anusārita</s>, transmutes one <s>koṭi</s> (ten million); and [when further] flowed with <s>bīja</s> —
the <s>pratisārita</s> and then <s>anusārita</s> mercury transmutes ten <s>koṭi</s> (one hundred million). || GRht 16.33 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the superior quality of the further-processed essence (<s>uttara-sattva</s>), beginning with '<s>koṭi</s>' (ten million) etc.

children.text: sūte sarito bījena grāsanyāyaṃ vihāya samena bījenānusārito yaḥ sa koṭisaṃkhyāṃ dhātūnāmiti śeṣaḥ sūto vidhyati // GRhtCM_16.33:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury (<s>sūta</s>), processed (<s>sārita</s>) with seed by the equal [proportion] method — setting aside the consumption (<s>grāsa</s>) rule — [when] further-processed (<s>anusārita</s>) with equal seed, transmutes (<s>vidhyati</s>) metals — numbering in the tens of millions (<s>koṭi</s>) — this is the completion.

children.text: yathoktasārite sūte daśaguṇavṛddhiḥ sarvatraiveti veditavyam // GRhtCM_16.33:3 //
children.translated_text: In mercury processed as stated, a tenfold increase [in potency] should be understood everywhere.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 16.34
The counter-processed (<s>pratisārita</s>) [mercury transmutes] a hundred million (<s>abja</s>); and the further-processed (<s>anusārita</s>) is a <s>kharva</s>-transmuter (ten billion);

children.text: evaṃ sāraṇayogātkurute vedhaṃ yathepsitaṃ vidhinā // GRht_16.34 //
children.translated_text: thus, by the processing (<s>sāraṇa</s>) procedure, it performs transmutation (<s>vedha</s>) as desired, according to [proper] method.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states a further distinction, beginning with '<s>prati</s>' etc.

children.text: pratisāritaḥ sūto dviguṇabījena vāraikena sārito rasaḥ abjasaṃkhyāṃ vidhyati // GRhtCM_16.34:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury that has been counter-processed (<s>pratisārita</s>) — processed once with double-quantity seed — transmutes metals numbering in the hundred millions (<s>abja</s>).

children.text: tu punar anusāritaḥ triguṇena bījena vāraikena sāritaḥ sūtaḥ kharvavedhī syāt kharvasaṃkhyāke dravyasaṃbandhaṃ karotītyabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_16.34:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the further-processed (<s>anusārita</s>) — processed once with triple-quantity seed — mercury would be a <s>kharva</s>-transmuter (ten-billion range); the import is that it effects a connection with substances numbering in the <s>kharva</s> range.

children.text: evamuktaprakāreṇa vidhinā śāstrajñavārtikasaṃpradāyena sāraṇayogāt yathepsitaṃ vedhaṃ kurute yathāvāñchitam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.34:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the manner stated, by [proper] method — by the tradition of those learned in the treatise — by the processing (<s>sāraṇa</s>) procedure, [mercury] performs transmutation as desired — as wished — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 16.35
[Mercury] processed with the further-processed [seed] transmutes copper numbering in the <s>nikharva</s> (hundred billion) range;

children.text: pratisāritastu vidhyati padmaṃ svanusāritaḥ śaṅkham // GRht_16.35 //
children.translated_text: and the counter-processed one transmutes a <s>padma</s> (trillion); its further-processed [form transmutes] a <s>śaṅkha</s> (ten trillion).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states a further distinction, beginning with '<s>anu</s>' etc.

children.text: anusāritena triguṇaprathamagrāsanyāyena bījena sāritaḥ sūto nikharvasaṃkhyākaṃ śulbaṃ vidhyati tu punaḥ pratisāritaḥ ṣaḍguṇaprathamagrāsanyāyena sāritaḥ sūtaḥ padmasaṃkhyākaṃ vidhyati // GRhtCM_16.35:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury processed with the further-processed [seed] — with seed [given] according to the triple first-consumption rule — transmutes copper numbering in the <s>nikharva</s> (hundred billion) range. Furthermore, the counter-processed — processed according to the sixfold first-consumption rule — mercury transmutes metals numbering in the <s>padma</s> (trillion) range.

children.text: punar anusārito navaguṇagrāsanyāyena bījena sāritaḥ sūtaḥ śaṅkhasaṃkhyāṃ vidhyatīti // GRhtCM_16.35:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the further-processed — mercury processed with seed according to the ninefold consumption rule — transmutes [metals] numbering in the <s>śaṅkha</s> (ten trillion) range.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 16.36
<Lead :: transmutation (<s>vedha</s>)>
It would transmute double the substance; having added lead (<s>nāga</s>), one should process it gradually;
until it produces all the divine gold.

Thus ends the sixteenth chapter (<s>avabodha</s>), dealing with processing (<s>sāraṇa</s>), in the <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Govindabhagavatpāda</s>, the <s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya</s>.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states a further distinction, beginning with '<s>vidhyet</s>' (would transmute) etc.

children.text: kanakaṃ hema dattvā śanakair nīcais tāvadanuvāhayet yāvaddivyaṃ pravaraṃ kanakaṃ bhavediti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_16.36:2 //
children.translated_text: Having added gold (<s>kanaka</s>, i.e., <s>hema</s>), one should gradually, slowly, process [mercury] until divine — excellent — gold results — this is the completion.

children.text: punaryāvatsakalaṃ samastaṃ nāgaṃ pronmīlayenniḥśeṣaṃ kuryādityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_16.36:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, until all, the entire lead (<s>nāga</s>), is completely eliminated — [meaning] one should make [it] entirely [free of lead] — this is the import.

children.text: punastatkanakaṃ dviguṇaṃ svato dravyaṃ vidhyet vā sūtakena sāritaṃ sat dravyaṃ kanakaṃ śatasahasrādisaṃkhyāto dviguṇasaṃkhyākaṃ dravyaṃ śulbādikaṃ vidhyed iti rahasyam // GRhtCM_16.36:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that gold — double the substance — [mercury] would transmute; or, mercury having been processed [with seed], the substance — gold — [numbering] in the hundreds of thousands and more — double that number of substance, such as copper and the like, [mercury] would transmute — this is the secret.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 17.1
Thus, even the king of mercury, though having undergone the processing (<s>sāraṇa</s>) procedure and being powerful, due to the operation-procedure (<s>kriyā-yoga</s>),

children.text: saṃveṣṭya tiṣṭhati lohaṃ no viśati krāmaṇārahitaḥ // GRht_17.1 //
children.translated_text: merely wraps around the metal and does not penetrate — [being] devoid of <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation/penetration).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Words that are well-refined, situated within the mouth, clear, and beneficial in meaning,

children.text: tathā parocitāḥ pūtā bhavantyamarajā giraḥ // GRhtCM_17.1:1 //
children.translated_text: and moreover suitable for others and pure, become [like] those born of immortals.
Now he states the praise of <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation), beginning with '<s>iti</s>' (thus) etc.

children.text: uktavidhānena kṛtaḥ sāraṇasya vidhir yasmin sūtarāje evaṃvidhiḥ sūtarāṭ balavān bhavediti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_17.1:3 //
children.translated_text: The king of mercury in whom the processing (<s>sāraṇa</s>) procedure has been performed by the stated method — such a king of mercury becomes powerful — this is the completion.
From what? From the operation-procedure (<s>kriyā-yoga</s>) — from the performance of the work.

children.text: yādṛk kṛtyaṃ kriyate tādṛk balavān syād ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_17.1:5 //
children.translated_text: The import is: according to the quality of the work performed, accordingly [mercury] would become powerful.

children.text: evaṃvidho'pi krāmaṇārahitaḥ krāmaṇavarjito lohaṃ na viśati lohāntaḥpraveśaṃ na karoti tato hetor lohaṃ dhātuṃ saṃveṣṭya pariveṣṭanaṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhati bāhyarāgadāyī syāditi // GRhtCM_17.1:6 //
children.translated_text: Even such [mercury], when devoid of <s>krāmaṇa</s> — lacking permeation — does not penetrate the metal — does not enter inside the metal. For that reason, it merely wraps around — surrounds — the metal substance, and remains [thus]; it would be merely an external coloring agent.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 17.2

children.text: annaṃ vā dravyaṃ vā yathānupānena dhātuṣu kramate /
children.translated_text: Just as food or medicine, with a [proper] vehicle (<s>anupāna</s>), penetrates (<s>kramate</s>) the bodily tissues (<s>dhātus</s>),
so too, by the <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation) procedure, the king of mercury penetrates metals.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the similarity between body and metal, beginning with '<s>anna</s>' (food) etc.
'<s>Yathā</s>' (just as) [is used] in the sense of analogy.

children.text: annaṃ godhūmādikaṃ vā dravyaṃ auṣadhaṃ anupānena saha jalādinā sārdhaṃ dhātuṣu māṃsādiṣu saptasu kramate vyāpnoti tathā amunā vakṣyamāṇavidhānena krāmaṇayogāt krāmaṇāya yogaḥ kunaṭīmākṣikaviṣādis tataḥ sūtarājo loharūpyādiṣu viśati bāhyābhyantaraṃ vidhyatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_17.2:3 //
children.translated_text: Food — wheat and the like — or medicine (<s>dravya</s>) — herbal preparations — with a vehicle (<s>anupāna</s>), i.e., together with water and the like, penetrates (<s>kramate</s>) — pervades — the seven <s>dhātus</s> (bodily tissues) such as flesh and the rest. Likewise, by the permeation procedure (<s>krāmaṇa-yoga</s>) to be described — the procedure for permeation, [using] <s>kunaṭī</s>-<s>mākṣika</s>-poison and the like — the king of mercury penetrates metals such as iron, silver, and the like; it transmutes [them] both externally and internally — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 17.3-5
<<s>Krāmaṇa-yoga</s> (permeation formula) (1)>
<s>Kānta</s> (loadstone), poison (<s>viṣa</s>), calamine (<s>rasaka</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), the red group, oils, cochineal (<s>indragopika</s>), and the like —

children.text: krāmaṇametacchreṣṭhaṃ lepe kṣepe sadā yojyam // GRht_17.3 //
children.translated_text: this is the best <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation formula); it should always be employed in anointing (<s>lepa</s>) and casting (<s>kṣepa</s>).
<<s>Krāmaṇa-yoga</s> (2)>
<s>Kunaṭī</s> (a plant), <s>mākṣika</s> (copper pyrites), poison, human blood, crow's excrement,

children.text: mahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalaṃ strīkṣīraṃ krāmaṇe balakṛt // GRht_17.4 //
children.translated_text: she-buffalo's ear-wax, woman's milk — [these are] strengtheners for <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation).
<<s>Krāmaṇa-yoga</s> (3)>
Borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), <s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>rāmaṭha</s> (a type of salt), and <s>bhūmilatā</s> (ground-vine), combined with great blood (<s>mahārudhira</s>) —

children.text: krāmaṇametatkathitaṃ lepe kṣepe sadā yojyam // GRht_17.5 //
children.translated_text: this <s>krāmaṇa</s> [formula] has been declared; it should always be employed in anointing and casting.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the <s>krāmaṇa</s> formula, beginning with '<s>kānta</s>-poison' etc.

children.text: kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ viṣaṃ kandajaṃ viṣaṃ kandaviṣāṇi kālakūṭādīni trayodaśa daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ taiḥ ca punaḥ raktatailendragopādyaiḥ rakto raktakavargaḥ tailaṃ kaṅguṇyādeḥ indragopo jīvaviśeṣaḥ ityādyāḥ krāmaṇocitās tacca // GRhtCM_17.3-5:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kānta</s>' is loadstone (<s>cumbaka</s>); '<s>viṣa</s>' means tuber-born poisons (<s>kandaviṣa</s>) — the thirteen [poisons] such as <s>kālakūṭa</s> and the rest; '<s>darada</s>' is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>). With these, and furthermore, with the red [herbs], oils, and cochineal: 'red' is the red-group [of herbs]; 'oil' is [oil] of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and the rest; '<s>indragopa</s>' is a specific living creature [cochineal insect]. These and the like are suitable for permeation.

children.text: etat śreṣṭhaṃ sarvottamaṃ krāmaṇaṃ anena sūtaḥ krāmati viśati loheṣviti vyāptiḥ tatkrāmaṇaṃ kathitam // GRhtCM_17.3-5:3 //
children.translated_text: This is the best, the most excellent <s>krāmaṇa</s>; by this, mercury permeates — enters — metals. The permeation has been described.
That should be employed in anointing (<s>lepa</s>) and casting (<s>kṣepa</s>) — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 17.6

children.text: śilayā nihato nāgo vaṅgaṃ vā tālakena śuddhena /
children.translated_text: Lead (<s>nāga</s>) killed by realgar (<s>śilā</s>), or tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) [killed] by pure orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>),
respectively for golden [operations] and for silver [operations] — this <s>krāmaṇa</s> has been prescribed.
<<s>Krāmaṇa-yoga</s> (4): for gold/silver production>
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [formula], beginning with '<s>śilā</s>' (realgar) etc.

children.text: nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ śilayā manohvayā nihato māritaḥ punaḥ vaṅgaṃ śuddhena doṣavarjitena tālena nihataṃ kramaśaḥ krameṇa pīte hemakarmaṇi śukle rūpyakarmaṇi etatkrāmaṇaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ samyak prakāśitaṃ pītakarmaṇi nāgaḥ śuklakarmaṇi vaṅgaṃ ca niyojitavyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_17.6:2 //
children.translated_text: Lead (<s>nāga</s>), i.e., <s>sīsaka</s>, killed by realgar (<s>manohvā</s>); and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), killed by pure — defect-free — orpiment (<s>tāla</s>); respectively, for golden [operations] (gold-making) and for silver [operations] (silver-making), this <s>krāmaṇa</s> has been well-declared. For golden operations, lead [should be employed]; for silver operations, tin — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 17.7
<<s>Krāmaṇa</s> (permeation)>

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ daradena hataṃ śulbaṃ vā tāpyamāritaṃ vidhinā /
children.translated_text: Steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) killed by cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), or copper (<s>śulba</s>) killed by <s>tāpya</s> (copper pyrites) according to procedure —
this <s>krāmaṇa</s> has been declared; <s>kānta</s> (loadstone) as the 'face,' with <s>mākṣikas</s> (copper pyrites) or [the like].
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [formula], beginning with '<s>tīkṣṇa</s>' (steel) etc.

children.text: daradena hiṅgulena hataṃ māritaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāro vidhinā arivargavidhānena tāpyena svarṇamākṣikena māritaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ etadapi krāmaṇaṃ kathitaṃ vā kāntamukhaṃ kāntaṃ lohajāti uktaṃ granthādau tat mukhaṃ pradhānaṃ yasya tat mākṣikairvā māritaṃ niyojyaṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_17.7:2 //
children.translated_text: Steel (<s>sāra</s>), killed by cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>), by the method of the enemy-group (<s>arivarga</s>); copper (<s>tāmra</s>), killed by <s>tāpya</s> (gold-<s>mākṣika</s>) — this also is a <s>krāmaṇa</s> that has been declared. Or, <s>kānta</s>-faced — '<s>kānta</s>' is a type of metal stated at the beginning of the treatise, and that [serves as] the 'face' (<s>mukha</s>), i.e., the primary [agent] — killed by <s>mākṣikas</s>, it should be employed — this is the completion.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 17.8

children.text: mākṣikasattvaṃ nāgaṃ vihāya na krāmaṇaṃ kimapyasti /
children.translated_text: Aside from <s>mākṣika</s>-essence and lead (<s>nāga</s>), there is no <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation agent) whatsoever;

children.text: dalasiddhe rasasiddhe vidhāvasau bhavati khalu saphalaḥ // GRht_17.8 //
children.translated_text: in the leaf-<s>siddhi</s> (leaf-transmutation) [method] and in the <s>rasa-siddhi</s> (mercury-perfection) procedure, that [permeation] indeed becomes fruitful.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specific procedure, beginning with '<s>mākṣika-sattva</s>' (copper-pyrites essence) etc.

children.text: mākṣikasattvaṃ tāpyasāraṃ nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ taṃ vihāya nānyatkimapyasti krāmaṇaṃ na krāmaṇamiti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_17.8:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika-sattva</s> — the extract of copper pyrites (<s>tāpya</s>); '<s>nāga</s>' is lead (<s>sīsaka</s>). Setting aside these [two], there exists no other <s>krāmaṇa</s> whatsoever — there is no [effective] permeation — this is the sense.
'<s>Khalu</s>' [is used] in the sense of inquiry.

children.text: dalasiddhe vidhau saṃskāraiḥ pūrṇatāṃ nīte sati asau vidhiḥ saphalaḥ // GRhtCM_17.8:4 //
children.translated_text: When the leaf-<s>siddhi</s> (leaf-transmutation) procedure has been brought to completion through the [proper] processes, that procedure becomes fruitful.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 18.1
<Greatness of <s>vedha</s> (transmutation)>

children.text: anayā khalu sāraṇayā krāmaṇena ca viśati yojito vidhivat /
children.translated_text: By this very processing (<s>sāraṇa</s>) and by permeation (<s>krāmaṇa</s>), [mercury], when properly combined, penetrates;

children.text: asati vedhavidhau na rasaḥ svaguṇānprakāśayati // GRht_18.1 //
children.translated_text: [but] in the absence of the transmutation (<s>vedha</s>) procedure, mercury does not manifest its own qualities.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
'Mercury cast into a substance equipped with intermediary medicines —

children.text: vedha ityucyate tajjñaiḥ sa ca naikavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: that is called <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) by the experts; and that is said to be of many kinds.'
This is the technical definition (<s>paribhāṣā</s>).
He states the authority of the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-process, beginning with '<s>anayā</s>' (by this) etc.

children.text: anayā uktayā sāraṇayā saha krāmaṇasaṃskāre kṛte sati raso viśati krāmati punarvedhavidhau kṛte sati rasaḥ svaguṇān prakāśayatīti veditavyam // GRhtCM_18.1:3 //
children.translated_text: By this — the stated — processing (<s>sāraṇa</s>), together with the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-process being performed, mercury penetrates — permeates. Furthermore, when the transmutation (<s>vedha</s>) procedure is performed, mercury manifests its own qualities — this should be understood.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 18.2
<<s>Hemakṛṣṭi</s> (gold-attraction/gold-making)>
Mercury, cinnabar, <s>tāpya</s> (copper pyrites), sulphur, realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>), lapis lazuli (<s>rājāvartta</s>), and <s>vimala</s> (silver pyrites) —
copper, killed by calcination [with these], [then cast] into silver, when processed — this is <s>hemakṛṣṭi</s> (gold-attraction).
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the transmutation procedure, beginning with '<s>rasa</s>' (mercury) etc.

children.text: rasaḥ sūtaḥ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ manaḥśilā manohvā rājavarttakaṃ rājāvartaṃ vimalaṃ raupyamākṣikaṃ ekavadbhāvadvandvaḥ // GRhtCM_18.2:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Rasa</s>' is mercury (<s>sūta</s>); '<s>darada</s>' is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>); '<s>tāpya</s>' is copper pyrites (<s>mākṣika</s>); '<s>gandhaka</s>' is well known [as sulphur]; '<s>manaḥśilā</s>' is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>); '<s>rājavarttaka</s>' is lapis lazuli (<s>rājāvarta</s>); '<s>vimala</s>' is silver pyrites (<s>raupyamākṣika</s>). The <s>dvandva</s> compound [of these gives them] a singular [collective] form.
'Copper killed by calcination' — killed by the calcination (<s>puṭa</s>) [process using the above substances] — this is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ śulbaṃ tāre nirvāhitaṃ iyaṃ hemakṛṣṭiḥ svarṇakaraṇamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.2:4 //
children.translated_text: Such copper, processed (<s>nirvāhita</s>) in silver (<s>tāra</s>) — this is <s>hemakṛṣṭi</s> (gold-making) — this is the meaning.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 18.3
Ninety-eight parts of silver (<s>tāra</s>), and one part of gold (<s>kanaka</s>),
and one part of mercury — this hundredth-part method (<s>śatāṃśa-vidhi</s>) is renowned.
<<s>Śatāṃśa-vidhi</s> (hundredth-part transmutation method) (1)>
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the transmutation procedure, beginning with 'ninety-eight' (<s>aṣṭānavati</s>) etc.

children.text: eṣa rasadaradetyādiśatāṃśavedhavidhiḥ kathaṃ atra śatāṃśe aṣṭānavatirbhāgāstārasya rūpyasya punariha kanakabhāgaḥ syāt eka eveti punaḥ sūtasya daradādimilitarasasyaiko bhāgaḥ ekāṃśaḥ iti sarve śatāṃśāḥ śatāṃśena vedha iti // GRhtCM_18.3:2 //
children.translated_text: This hundredth-part transmutation method, beginning with 'mercury-cinnabar' etc. — how? In this hundredth-part [formula]: ninety-eight parts of silver (<s>rūpya</s>); furthermore, here, one part only of gold; furthermore, one part of mercury — mercury combined with cinnabar and the rest — one part. Thus all [total] one hundred parts; transmutation is by the hundredth-part.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 18.4
<<s>Śatāṃśa-vidhi</s> (2)>
Forty-nine parts of silver here, and likewise of copper,
one part of gold, and transmutation by one [part] of mercury.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [formula], beginning with 'forty-nine' (<s>ekonapañcāśat</s>) etc.

children.text: ekonapañcāśadbhāgāḥ tārasya rūpyasya kāryāḥ tathaiva śulvasya tāmrasya ekonapañcāśadbhāgāśca kāryāḥ punaḥ kanakasya hemnaśca eko bhāgaḥ kāryaḥ sūtasya ca ekena bhāgena vedha iti eṣo'pi śatāṃśavidhiḥ // GRhtCM_18.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Forty-nine parts of silver (<s>rūpya</s>) should be prepared; and likewise of copper (<s>tāmra</s>), forty-nine parts should also be prepared. Furthermore, one part of gold (<s>hema</s>) should be prepared. And by one part of mercury, transmutation [is effected]. This too is a hundredth-part method.
START <s>Rasa-hṛdaya-tantra</s> 18.5
<Definition of thousand-fold transmuter and higher>
Thus, a thousand-fold transmuter (<s>sahasra-vedhī</s>) is employed, and a ten-million-fold transmuter (<s>koṭi-vedhī</s>) also;

children.text: jāraṇabījavaśena tu sūtasya balābalaṃ jñātvā // GRht_18.5 //
children.translated_text: according to the seed-digestion (<s>jāraṇa-bīja</s>), knowing the strength and weakness of mercury.
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states a distinction from the previously stated method, beginning with '<s>evam</s>' (thus) etc.

children.text: evaṃ śatāṃśavedhanyāyena daśavṛddhivibhāgena sahasravedhī syāt // GRhtCM_18.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the principle of hundred-part penetration (<s>śatāṃśa-vedha</s>), with a tenfold progressive division, it would become a thousand-fold penetrator (<s>sahasra-vedhī</s>). // GRhtCM_18.5:2 //

children.text: evaṃ ca jāraṇabījavaśena jāraṇāyāṃ yadbījaṃ kiyadguṇajāritamiti bhāvaḥ tadvaśena koṭivedhī ca syāt // GRhtCM_18.5:3 //
children.translated_text: And thus, by virtue of the digestion-seed (<s>jāraṇa-bīja</s>) — the sense is: what seed was digested and to what degree of potency — by that virtue, it would become a ten-million-fold penetrator (<s>koṭi-vedhī</s>). // GRhtCM_18.5:3 //

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā tenaiva jāraṇabījavaśena yattasya balābalaṃ nyūnādhikyaṃ tat jñātvetyabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_18.5:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? By virtue of that very digestion-seed — having ascertained its strength or weakness (<s>balābala</s>), i.e., its degree of lesser or greater [potency] — this is the intended meaning. // GRhtCM_18.5:4 //
START GRht 18.6
<<s>kunta-vedha</s> (lance-penetration)>
Having first added the charge (<s>prativāpa</s>), with saturation by lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), fish-bile and such,

children.text: tāre vā śulbe vā tārāriṣṭe tathā kṛṣṭau // GRht_18.6 //
children.translated_text: into silver (<s>tāra</s>), or into copper (<s>śulba</s>), or into inferior gold (<s>tārāriṣṭa</s>), and likewise in gold-making (<s>kṛṣṭau</s>). // GRht_18.6 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure for penetration in particular — 'having added' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.6:1 //

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ lākṣāmatsyādipittabhāvanayā lākṣā pratītā matsyādipittāni matsyamāhiṣamayūrājasūkarasaṃbhavāni pittāni teṣāṃ bhāvanayā kṛtvā prativāpaṃ galite nikṣepaṃ tattāre dattvā athavā śulbe prativāpaṃ kuryāt athavā kṛṣṭau hemakaraṇe vāpaṃ dattvā niyuñjyāditi śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.6:2 //
children.translated_text: First, i.e., at the beginning, with saturation by lac and fish-bile and such: <s>lākṣā</s> (lac) is well-known; the biles of fish and others — those being biles derived from fish, buffalo, peacock, goat, and pig — with saturation by these, having made the charge (<s>prativāpa</s>), i.e., the addition into the molten [metal] — that [is added] into silver (<s>tāra</s>); alternatively, one should make the charge into copper (<s>śulba</s>); alternatively, having added the charge into gold-making (<s>kṛṣṭau</s>), i.e., the production of gold, one should employ [it] — this is the remainder. // GRhtCM_18.6:2 //
START GRht 18.7
Then, [the mercury] ground with <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetration-agent), with that very paste, with consolidated mercury,

children.text: atividrute ca tasmin vedho'sau kuntavedhena // GRht_18.7 //
children.translated_text: and when that [metal] is thoroughly melted — that penetration is by the lance-method (<s>kunta-vedha</s>). // GRht_18.7 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states further specifics — 'then' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.7:1 //

children.text: tadanu lākṣāmatsyādipittabhāvanāyā anantaraṃ tasmin lākṣādikalke krāmaṇamṛdite kāntarasakadaradaraktatailendragopādyair mṛdite sati punastatkalkena taccūrṇenāpi piṇḍitarasena vedhaḥ kartavya iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.7:2 //
children.translated_text: Then, i.e., after the saturation with lac and fish-bile and such, when that lac-paste has been ground with the <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetration-agent) — ground with lodestone (<s>kānta</s>), <s>rasaka</s> (zinc), <s>darada</s> (cinnabar), red oil, <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal) and such — then with that very paste, i.e., with that powder, penetration should be performed with consolidated mercury — this is the remainder. // GRhtCM_18.7:2 //

children.text: kasmin tāre vā śulbe vā vidrute jalarūpe kārya ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.7:3 //
children.translated_text: Into what? Into silver (<s>tāra</s>) or copper (<s>śulba</s>) when melted, i.e., in liquid form — this should be done, is the meaning. // GRhtCM_18.7:3 //
START GRht 18.8
<<s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetration)>
One should cover that [substance to be penetrated] with an oil-moistened cloth, or with flesh (<s>palala</s>), or with ash;
the substance to be penetrated [is prepared] according to procedure, for the purpose of making the king of mercury penetrate (<s>rasa-rāja-krāmaṇa</s>). // GRht_18.8 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specifics — 'that' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.8:1 //

children.text: vedhyaṃ vedhocitaṃ dravyaṃ rasarājakrāmaṇārthaṃ yathā raso viśati tadarthaṃ taṃ tailārdrapaṭena sāraṇatailārdravastreṇa sthagayet ācchādayet vā palalena kenacinmāṃsena vā bhasmanā ācchādayedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.8:2 //
children.translated_text: The substance to be penetrated (<s>vedhya</s>), i.e., the substance suitable for penetration, for the purpose of making the king of mercury penetrate (<s>rasa-rāja-krāmaṇa</s>), i.e., so that mercury enters — one should cover that [substance] with an oil-moistened cloth, i.e., a cloth moistened with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil; or with flesh (<s>palala</s>), i.e., with some [piece of] meat; or one should cover it with ash — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_18.8:2 //
START GRht 18.9

children.text: iti sāritasya kathitaṃ rasasya vedhādi krāmaṇaṃ karma /
children.translated_text: Thus has been described the penetration and <s>krāmaṇa</s> procedure for mercury that has been streamed (<s>sārita</s>).
He states the specifics — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.8:1 //

children.text: sāritasya uktavidhānena sāraṇākṛtasya vedhādi krāmaṇaṃ karma vedhavidhānoditakrāmaṇaṃ karma kathitam // GRhtCM_18.8:2 //
children.translated_text: For mercury that has been streamed (<s>sārita</s>), i.e., subjected to the <s>sāraṇā</s> procedure by the described method, the <s>krāmaṇa</s> procedure of penetration, i.e., the penetration-making operation described in the penetration procedure, has been stated. // GRhtCM_18.8:2 //
START GRht 18.9
[Mercury] whose seed has been digested in quarter-proportion and such is suitable for foil-paste (<s>patra-lepa</s>). // GRht_18.9 //
<<s>lepa-vedha</s> (paste-penetration) / <s>patra-rañjana</s> (foil-coloring)>
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: pādādijīrṇabījaḥ pādādinā pādārdhena samato nyūnena ca jīrṇaṃ bījaṃ yasmin saḥ patralepena yujyate ataḥ patrarañjanaṃ syādityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_18.9:1 //
children.translated_text: [Mercury] whose seed has been digested in quarter-proportion and such (<s>pādādi-jīrṇa-bīja</s>) — 'quarter and such' meaning by a quarter, a half, equal, or lesser [proportion], the seed digested in which — that [mercury] is suitable for foil-paste (<s>patra-lepa</s>); therefore foil-coloring (<s>patra-rañjana</s>) would result — this is the intended meaning. // GRhtCM_18.9:1 //
START GRht 18.10
<<s>patra-rañjana</s> (foil-coloring, method 2) by paste>
A foil of silver (<s>tāra</s>), inferior gold (<s>ariṣṭa</s>), and such, rubbed with acid and such, thoroughly purified,

children.text: ālipya rasena tataḥ krāmaṇalipte puṭeṣu viśrāntam // GRht_18.10 //
children.translated_text: smeared with mercury, then with the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-paste applied, rested in firings (<s>puṭa</s>). // GRht_18.10 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: atiśuddhaṃ nirmalaṃ amlādyudvartitaṃ tārāriṣṭaśabdātsitaṃ svarṇaṃ grāhyaṃ tataḥ rasenālipya tataḥ kramaṇālipte krāmaṇapiṇḍena lepe kṛte sati puṭeṣu utpalāgnau viśrāntaṃ sthāpitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.10:1 //
children.translated_text: Thoroughly purified (<s>atiśuddha</s>), i.e., spotless; rubbed with acid and such — from the word '<s>tārāriṣṭa</s>' (silver and inferior gold), white and gold [foils] should be understood; then, having smeared with mercury, then when the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-paste has been applied, i.e., when the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-pellet coating has been made, [the foil should be] rested, i.e., placed, in firings (<s>puṭa</s>), i.e., in <s>utpala</s>-fire (lotus-fire). // GRhtCM_18.10:1 //
This is the procedure for foil-coloring (<s>patra-rañjana</s>). // GRhtCM_18.10:2 //
START GRht 18.11
<Further processing of the foil; <s>varṇa-puṭa</s> (color-firing)>

children.text: ardhena miśrayitvā hemnā jyeṣṭhena taddalaṃ puṭitam /
children.translated_text: Having mixed by half with superior gold (<s>heman</s>), that foil is fired

with [a paste of] crystal (<s>kṣiti</s>), yellow iron-sulphate (<s>khaga</s>), rock salt (<s>paṭu</s>), and red clay (<s>rakta-mṛd</s>) — this is the color-firing (<s>varṇa-puṭa</s>); then it should be applied. // GRht_18.11 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the procedure for gold — 'by half' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.11:1 //

children.text: ardhena ardhavibhāgena rañjitadalādita iti jñeyam // GRhtCM_18.11:2 //
children.translated_text: 'By half' (<s>ardhena</s>) — by a half-portion, it should be understood [to mean] from the colored foil onward. // GRhtCM_18.11:2 //

children.text: jyeṣṭhena hemnā pravarakanakena taddalaṃ rañjitapatraṃ miśrayitvā puṭitaṃ kuryāt yathā milati // GRhtCM_18.11:3 //
children.translated_text: With superior gold (<s>jyeṣṭha-heman</s>), i.e., excellent gold, that foil, i.e., the colored sheet, having been mixed, should be fired so that they unite. // GRhtCM_18.11:3 //

children.text: punaḥ kṣitikhagapaṭuraktamṛdā kṛtvā kṣitiḥ sphaṭikaḥ khagaḥ pītakāsīsaṃ paṭu saindhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ raktamṛt gairikaṃ ekavadbhāvadvandvaḥ tena kṣityādinopari liptaṃ dalaṃ prati ayaṃ puṭo deyaḥ vanopalair iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.11:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with crystal-bird-salt-red-clay (<s>kṣiti-khaga-paṭu-rakta-mṛd</s>): <s>kṣiti</s> is crystal (<s>sphaṭika</s>); <s>khaga</s> is yellow iron-sulphate (<s>pīta-kāsīsa</s>); <s>paṭu</s> is rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>); <s>rakta-mṛd</s> (red clay) is ochre (<s>gairika</s>) — this is a collective compound, treated as a unity; with these substances headed by crystal, the foil being coated on top — this firing (<s>puṭa</s>) should be applied to the foil, with forest-lotuses [as fuel] — this is the remainder. // GRhtCM_18.11:4 //
START GRht 18.12
<<s>vedha</s> (transmutation): white gold to red gold>
Powder of lapis lazuli (<s>bhūpati-vartaka</s>), saturated many times with <s>śirīṣa</s>-flower (<s>Albizia</s>) juice,

children.text: sadyaḥ karoti raktaṃ sitakanakam aśītibhāgena // GRht_18.12 //
children.translated_text: instantly makes white gold red, in eighty-part proportion. // GRht_18.12 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the color procedure — '<s>bhūpati</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.12:1 //

children.text: bhūpativartakacūrṇaṃ rājāvartarajaḥ bahuśo bahuvāraṃ śirīṣapuṣparasabhāvitaṃ kuryāt ityadhyāhāryam // GRhtCM_18.12:2 //
children.translated_text: Powder of lapis lazuli (<s>bhūpati-vartaka-cūrṇa</s>), i.e., the dust of <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli) — one should saturate it many times, i.e., repeatedly, with <s>śirīṣa</s>-flower juice — this is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_18.12:2 //

children.text: bhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitamiti vidhānavit iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.12:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Saturated' means sun-dried after saturation — one who knows the procedure [understands this], this is the remainder. // GRhtCM_18.12:3 //
START GRht 18.13
<<s>vedha</s> (transmutation): silver to gold>
Mercury (<s>rasa</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), <s>vimala</s>, pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), rock salt (<s>paṭu</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), <s>mākṣīka</s> (pyrite), and lapis lazuli (<s>nṛpa</s>);
coral (<s>pravāla</s>), <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and ochre (<s>gairika</s>) — charged into white gold (<s>sita kanaka</s>). // GRht_18.13 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [method] — 'mercury' and so forth.

children.text: rasaḥ sūtaḥ daradaṃ hiṅgulaḥ vimalaṃ tāpyabhedaḥ paṭu saiṃdhavaṃ śilā manohvā mākṣikaṃ pratītaṃ vaṇigdravyaṃ nṛpo rājāvartaḥ pravālaṃ vidrumaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ gairikaṃ pratītaṃ etaiḥ prativāpitaṃ sitadravyaṃ kanakaṃ bhavet ityadhyāhāryam // GRhtCM_18.13:1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is mercury (<s>sūta</s>); <s>darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>); <s>vimala</s> is a variety of pyrite (<s>tāpya-bheda</s>); <s>paṭu</s> is rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>); <s>śilā</s> is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>); <s>mākṣika</s> is well-known; the merchant-substance — <s>nṛpa</s> is lapis lazuli (<s>rājāvarta</s>); <s>pravāla</s> is coral (<s>vidruma</s>); <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s>; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax); <s>gairika</s> (ochre) is well-known — charged with these, the white substance becomes gold (<s>kanaka</s>) — this is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_18.13:1 //
START GRht 18.14
<coloring of gold>
Ground with <s>tāpī-bhava</s> (pyrite-born essence), lapis lazuli (<s>nṛpāvarta</s>), and <s>bījapūra</s> (citron) juice,
through firing (<s>puṭa-pāka</s>), it makes gold vermilion-like (<s>sindūra-sannibha</s>). // GRht_18.14 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [method] — '<s>tāpī-bhava</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.14:1 //

children.text: tāpībhavaṃ mākṣikasattvaṃ nṛpāvartaṃ rājāvartakaṃ etaddvayaṃ bījapūrarasārditaṃ mātuluṅgarasamarditaṃ kuryāt etadubhayoryogāt kanakaṃ puṭapākena vahnividhānena kanakaṃ pūrvoktaṃ yatkanakaṃ vā hīnavarṇakanakaṃ sindūrasannibhaṃ karoti // GRhtCM_18.14:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpī-bhava</s> is pyrite-essence (<s>mākṣika-sattva</s>); <s>nṛpāvarta</s> is lapis lazuli (<s>rājāvartaka</s>) — these two, ground with <s>bījapūra</s> (citron, i.e., <s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice, should be prepared; through the combination of these two, by firing (<s>puṭa-pāka</s>), i.e., by the fire-procedure, the gold — either the aforementioned gold or inferior-colored gold — becomes vermilion-like (<s>sindūra-sannibha</s>), i.e., makes [it so]. // GRhtCM_18.14:2 //
The compound is: 'that whose appearance is like vermilion.' // GRhtCM_18.14:3 //
START GRht 18.15
<silver: improvement of color>
Tin-mica (<s>vaṅgābhra</s>), white <s>mākṣīka</s> (pyrite), or mineral pitch (<s>śaila</s>) — one should drive into white [silver];

children.text: tattāraṃ ca daśāṃśena tārotkarṣaṃ karoti hi // GRht_18.15 //
children.translated_text: that silver, [treated] with a tenth part, produces the enhancement of silver (<s>tārotkarṣa</s>). // GRht_18.15 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the procedure for silver color — '<s>vaṅga</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.15:1 //

children.text: vaṅgābhramiti vaṅgaṃ trapu abhraṃ śvetābhraṃ punaḥ sitamākṣīkaṃ vimalaṃ śailaṃ śvetaśilājatu vā site tāre vāhayet // GRhtCM_18.15:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Tin-mica' (<s>vaṅgābhra</s>): <s>vaṅga</s> is tin (<s>trapu</s>); <s>abhra</s> is white mica; furthermore, white <s>mākṣīka</s> is <s>vimala</s>; <s>śaila</s> is white mineral pitch (<s>śveta-śilājatu</s>) — one should drive [these] into white [metal], i.e., into silver (<s>tāra</s>). // GRhtCM_18.15:2 //

children.text: punardaśāṃśena etadauṣadhanicayaṃ tārato daśamavibhāgena kṛtvā hi niścitaṃ tārotkarṣaṃ karoti hīnavarṇata uttamaṃ karotītyabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_18.15:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with a tenth part — having made this collection of medicines in a tenth portion relative to the silver — indeed certainly, it produces the enhancement of silver (<s>tārotkarṣa</s>), i.e., makes [silver] of inferior color superior — this is the intended meaning. // GRhtCM_18.15:3 //
START GRht 18.16
<<s>nirvāhaṇa</s> (extraction) of different substances: physical results>

children.text: nāgaḥ karoti mṛdutāṃ nirvyūḍhastāṃ ca raktatāṃ ca raviḥ /
children.translated_text: Lead (<s>nāga</s>) when extracted produces softness; copper (<s>ravi</s>) [produces] both that [softness] and redness;

children.text: tāṃ pītatāṃ ca tīkṣṇaṃ kācastatkālikavināśaṃ ca // GRht_18.16 //
children.translated_text: iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) [produces] both that [redness] and yellowness; glass (<s>kāca</s>) [produces] temporary destruction of [color]. // GRht_18.16 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specifics regarding silver — 'lead' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.16:1 //

children.text: nāgaḥ sīsakas tāre nirvyūḍho mṛdutāṃ komalatvaṃ karoti // GRhtCM_18.16:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s>, i.e., lead (<s>sīsaka</s>), when extracted into silver, produces softness (<s>mṛdutā</s>), i.e., tenderness. // GRhtCM_18.16:2 //

children.text: punaḥ ravistāmraṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ sat tāṃ mṛdutāṃ ca punaḥ raktatāṃ lohitanibhāṃ karoti // GRhtCM_18.16:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, copper (<s>ravi</s>, i.e., <s>tāmra</s>), when extracted, produces both that softness and redness (<s>raktatā</s>), i.e., crimson appearance. // GRhtCM_18.16:3 //

children.text: ca punastīkṣṇaṃ tāranirvyūḍhaṃ tāṃ raktatāṃ pītatāṃ ca karoti // GRhtCM_18.16:4 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), when extracted into silver, produces both that redness and yellowness (<s>pītatā</s>). // GRhtCM_18.16:4 //

children.text: punaḥ kācaḥ pratīto loke sa kālikavināśaṃ karotīti tāre nirvyūḍha iti saṃbandhaḥ // GRhtCM_18.16:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, glass (<s>kāca</s>) — well-known in the world — it produces the temporary destruction [of color] — the connection being 'when extracted into silver.' // GRhtCM_18.16:5 //
START GRht 18.17
<gold: improvement>
Gold and copper in equal parts with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), flooded with <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia) oil, blown —

children.text: pāte pāte daśa daśa vindati yāvaddhi koṭimapi // GRht_18.17 //
children.translated_text: at each addition, [it gains] tenfold — indeed up to ten million (<s>koṭi</s>). // GRht_18.17 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specifics regarding gold — 'gold and copper' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.17:1 //

children.text: kanakaṃ hema aruṇaṃ tāmraṃ samaṃ tulyabhāgaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ ayaṃ gaṇaḥ karañjatailapluto dhmātaḥ kāryaḥ // GRhtCM_18.17:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kanaka</s> is gold (<s>hema</s>); <s>aruṇa</s> is copper (<s>tāmra</s>); <s>sama</s> means in equal portions; <s>mākṣika</s> is pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>) — this group, flooded with <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia) oil, should be blown. // GRhtCM_18.17:2 //

children.text: punaḥ pāte pāte vāraṃvāraṃ nikṣepe sati daśa daśa guṇotkarṣaṃ vidanti dhmāta ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_18.17:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, at each addition (<s>pāte pāte</s>), i.e., at each successive charge, they gain tenfold quality-enhancement — 'blown' is to be supplied. // GRhtCM_18.17:3 //
'Indeed' (<s>hi</s>) means certainly. // GRhtCM_18.17:4 //
For how long? Until it attains the <s>koṭi</s>-count [ten million]. // GRhtCM_18.17:5 //
START GRht 18.18
<gold: seed for improvement of color>
And that [preparation], when thoroughly melted, sprinkled repeatedly with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus) oil,
with the addition of pyrite-essence (<s>mākṣīka</s>) and copper (<s>ravi</s>), penetrates gold in hundredth-part proportion. // GRht_18.18 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specifics — 'that' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.18:1 //

children.text: saḥ karañjatailapluto yogo bahuśo vāraṃvāraṃ kaṅguṇītailena secito yathā syāttathāyaṃ ati vilīnaḥ san mākṣikaravinivāpāṃ punaḥ kārya evaṃvidhaṃ ca kanakaṃ śatāṃśena śatavibhāgena vidhyati sitakanakam iti // GRhtCM_18.18:2 //
children.translated_text: That [preparation] flooded with <s>karañja</s> oil, sprinkled repeatedly, i.e., again and again, with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil so that it [absorbs it] — this [preparation] being thoroughly melted, should again be made with the addition of pyrite-essence and copper (<s>ravi</s>); and such gold, in hundredth-part proportion (<s>śatāṃśena</s>), penetrates white gold. // GRhtCM_18.18:2 //
START GRht 18.19
<gold: seed for improvement>
Struck with copper (<s>śulba</s>), killed by mercury and sulphur (<s>rasa-gandha</s>), [combined with] yellow iron-sulphate (<s>khaga-pīta</s>) — in tenth-part proportion,

children.text: vidhyati kanakaṃ kurute tannirvyūḍhaṃ marditaṃ sudṛḍham // GRht_18.19 //
children.translated_text: it penetrates gold; that [preparation], well-extracted, firmly ground, makes [gold]. // GRht_18.19 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specifics — 'copper' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.19:1 //

children.text: śulbahataṃ śulbena saha hataṃ rasagandhaṃ sūtagandhaṃ tena āhataṃ pañcatvam āpannaṃ yatkhagapītaṃ pītakāsīsaṃ etadauṣadhasamuccayaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā marditaṃ kuryāt punastat nirvyūḍhaṃ daśāṃśena vidhyati sitakanakaṃ kurute svarṇamiti viśeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.19:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Struck with copper' (<s>śulba-hata</s>) — struck together with copper; 'killed by mercury and sulphur' (<s>rasa-gandha-āhata</s>) — reduced to the five-fold state by mercury and sulphur; the yellow iron-sulphate (<s>khaga-pīta</s>), i.e., <s>pīta-kāsīsa</s> — this collection of medicines should be firmly ground; then that, well-extracted (<s>nirvyūḍha</s>), in tenth-part proportion penetrates white gold — 'makes gold' is the specific point. // GRhtCM_18.19:2 //
START GRht 18.20
<<s>vedha</s> (transmutation)>
Gold, well-blown with equal <s>rasaka</s> (zinc), consumed; then with sun-and-moon paste (<s>arka-candra-lepa</s>),

children.text: mākṣikasattvaṃ hemnā karoti jīrṇo rasaḥ śatāṃśena // GRht_18.20 //
children.translated_text: pyrite-essence (<s>mākṣika-sattva</s>) with gold — when mercury is digested, [it penetrates] in hundredth-part proportion. // GRht_18.20 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [method] — '<s>rasaka</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_18.20:1 //

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ arkacandralepena kanakaṃ rasakasamaṃ dhmātaṃ kuryāt punaretadauṣadhaṃ bhuktvā kanakaṃ syāt punarmākṣikasattvaṃ hemnā saha jīrṇaṃ rasaṃ śatāṃśena vidhyatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.20:2 //
children.translated_text: Then, after that, with sun-and-moon paste (<s>arka-candra-lepa</s>), gold should be blown with equal <s>rasaka</s> (zinc); furthermore, having consumed this medicine, it becomes gold; furthermore, pyrite-essence (<s>mākṣika-sattva</s>) with gold — mercury digested [with these] penetrates in hundredth-part proportion — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_18.20:2 //
START GRht 18.21
<<s>vedha</s> (transmutation): silver to gold>
Eight-fold killed copper (<s>mṛta-śulba</s>), coated with silver (<s>kaladhauта</s>) in a sealed crucible (<s>mūka-mūṣā</s>),
that [copper], digested in sixteenth-part [of mercury], penetrates silver in fiftieth-part proportion. // GRht_18.21 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another, saying 'eightfold' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.21:1 ||

children.text: aṣṭaguṇaṃ mṛtaśulbaṃ arivargeṇa saha hataṃ yat śulbaṃ tāmraṃ tataḥ kaladhautena ṣoḍaśāṃśena jīrṇaṃ śatārdhena pañcāśadvibhāgena tāraṃ vidhyati kanakaṃ karotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.21:2 //
children.translated_text: Eightfold calcined copper — copper that has been struck with the hostile group (<s>arivarga</s>) — then, with one-sixteenth [proportion of] silver (<s>kaladhautam</s>), when digested, it transmutes silver by one-fiftieth part, i.e., produces gold — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.21:2 ||
START GRht 18.22
<s>vedha</s> (transmutation): one-tenth; silver to gold>

children.text: āvṛtya kanakakariṇau śilayā prativāpitau tato bhuktvā /
children.translated_text: Having smelted gold and lead together, quenched with realgar (<s>śilā</s>), then having [mercury] consume them
in the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swinging apparatus), [mercury] digested with sulphur becomes a one-tenth transmuter of silver. || GRht 18.22 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another, saying 'having smelted' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.22:1 ||

children.text: kanakakariṇau samahemanāgau āvṛtya gālayitvā śilayā manohvayā prativāpitau tato'nantaraṃ dolāyantre kanakakariṇau bhuktvā gandhakajīrṇo yo rasaḥ sa tāre daśāṃśavedhī syāt daśāṃśena vidhyatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.22:2 //
children.translated_text: Gold-and-lead (<s>kanakakariṇau</s>), i.e., gold and lead in equal amounts — having smelted, i.e., filtered; quenched with realgar (<s>śilā</s>), i.e., <s>manohvā</s>; then, in the <s>dolāyantra</s>, having consumed the gold-and-lead; [mercury] that has been digested with sulphur — that mercury becomes a one-tenth transmuter of silver, i.e., it transmutes in a proportion of one-tenth — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.22:2 ||
START GRht 18.23
<s>vedha</s>: one-hundredth; bronze to gold>
[Mercury that has] digested the six metals killed by the hostile group, stored in grain for four months,

children.text: sahitaḥ purasurābhyāṃ vidhyati ghoṣaṃ śatāṃśena // GRht_18.23 //
children.translated_text: combined with <s>guggulu</s> and wine — transmutes bronze (<s>ghoṣa</s>) by one-hundredth. || GRht 18.23 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another, saying 'killed by the hostile group' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.23:1 ||

children.text: ripunihatalohaṣaṭkaṃ ripubhir arivargair nihataṃ māritaṃ yat lohaṣaṭkaṃ svarṇatāratāmranāgavaṅgalohābhidhānaṃ tat caturmāsaṃ yathā syāttathā dhānyasthito'nnakoṣṭhīdhṛto raso jīrṇaḥ // GRhtCM_18.23:2 //
children.translated_text: The six metals killed by the hostile group — killed, i.e., calcined, by enemies, i.e., the hostile group — the six metals, namely gold, silver, copper, lead, tin, and iron — that [mercury which has digested those], stored in grain, i.e., kept in a grain-container, for four months in such a way — is the digested mercury. || GRhtCM 18.23:2 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭo dhānyasthitaḥ purasurābhyāṃ guggulumadirābhyāṃ sahito militaḥ śatāṃśena ghoṣaṃ kāṃsyaṃ vidhyati kanakaṃ karotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.23:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what character is [the mercury] stored in grain? Combined with <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) and wine (<s>surā</s>), i.e., mixed [with them] — it transmutes bronze (<s>ghoṣa</s>), i.e., <s>kāṃsya</s> (bell-metal), by one-hundredth, i.e., produces gold — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.23:3 ||
START GRht 18.24

children.text: vakṣye samprati samyagyad bījaṃ samarase jīrṇam /
children.translated_text: I shall now properly describe the seed which, when digested in equal mercury,
[performs] the procedures of <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste), <s>stambha</s> (fixation), and so forth, being revealed — O wise ones, listen! || GRht 18.24 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specific [method], saying 'I shall describe' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.24:1 ||

children.text: bho budhāḥ mayā prakāśyamānaṃ sat śṛṇuta sāvadhānā ityadhyāhāryam // GRhtCM_18.24:2 //
children.translated_text: O wise ones! Being revealed by me — listen attentively — this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 18.24:2 ||

children.text: tatkiṃ saṃprati yad bījaṃ samarase tulyasūte samyak jīrṇaṃ jāraṇamāpannaṃ tadahaṃ govindanāmā vakṣye kathayāmi // GRhtCM_18.24:3 //
children.translated_text: What is that? Now, the seed which has been properly digested, i.e., has attained digestion, in equal mercury, i.e., in an equal amount of <s>sūta</s> — that I, <s>Govinda</s> by name, shall describe, i.e., shall narrate. || GRhtCM 18.24:3 ||

children.text: punaḥ piṣṭistambhādividhiṃ piṣṭistambha ādir yasya vidhestaṃ vidhiṃ pāṭakhoṭajalaukākhyaṃ ca vakṣye // GRhtCM_18.24:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the procedure of <s>piṣṭī</s> (paste), <s>stambha</s> (fixation), and so forth — the procedure whose beginning is <s>piṣṭī</s> and <s>stambha</s> — that procedure, known as <s>pāṭa</s>, <s>khoṭa</s>, and <s>jalaukā</s>, I shall describe. || GRhtCM 18.24:4 ||
START GRht 18.25-40
<s>vedha</s>; bronze-drawn [copper] to gold>
With lapis lazuli (<s>rājāvarta</s>), silver-pyrite (<s>vimala</s>), yellow mica (<s>pītābhra</s>), sulphur (<s>gandha</s>), gold-pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), and <s>rasaka</s> (zinc ore),
and with <s>kāṅkṣī</s> (Saurashtra earth), vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), and cinnabar (<s>darada</s>) — lead combined [with these]. || GRht 18.25 ||

children.text: ahimārarasaiḥ puṭitaṃ māraya nāgaṃ nirutthakaṃ yāvat /
children.translated_text: Calcinated with oleander (<s>ahimāra</s>) juices, kill the lead until it is non-revivable;

children.text: tadanu ca tasya hi madhye śulbaṃ gandhaṃ ca lavaṇakaṃkuṣṭham // GRht_18.26 //
children.translated_text: then, in the midst of that, [add] copper, sulphur, salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>), and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (zinc vitriol). || GRht 18.26 ||
Soak all that a hundred times with the juices of cooked <s>arka</s> (milkweed) leaves;
and in bronze-drawn copper (<s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa-śulba</s>), extract the powder hundreds of times. || GRht 18.27 ||

children.text: śulbena tena hi samaṃ rasakapītābhrasatvavimalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Equal to that copper: <s>rasaka</s> (zinc), yellow mica-essence, and silver-pyrite (<s>vimala</s>),
ochre (<s>gairika</s>), pyrite-essence (<s>mākṣika-satva</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), lead, and combined with iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>). || GRht 18.28 ||
Making a pair with these, one should color the copper by quenching with pyrite,
even twenty times; and after it is melted, one should then sprinkle [it]. || GRht 18.29 ||
Having made a combination of the juices of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex), <s>kākamācī</s> (Solanum nigrum), and aloe (<s>kanyā</s>),

children.text: vārān sapta ca vidhinā tadapi ca nirvāpayeddhemni // GRht_18.30 //
children.translated_text: quench seven times by the method, and then also quench in gold. || GRht 18.30 ||
Until it becomes the excellent seed coloring twenty-four-fold,

children.text: pakvaṃ mākṣikameva hi tena ca vidhinā tadapi caturviṃśatiguṇam // GRht_18.31 //
children.translated_text: cook it with pyrite alone indeed; and by that method, [it colors] twenty-four-fold again. || GRht 18.31 ||
That seed, in a small amount, into the king of mercury previously processed,

children.text: mūṣāyāṃ khalu dattvā daśaguṇaṃ ca gandhakaṃ dāhyam // GRht_18.32 //
children.translated_text: having placed [it] in a crucible, and ten times the amount of sulphur should be burnt. || GRht 18.32 ||
Or alternatively, in a sturdy sand-bath apparatus (<s>vāluka-yantra</s>), in a crucible of fourteen finger-breadths,

children.text: madhye sūtaṃ muktvā laghutarapuṭayogataḥ pihitā // GRht_18.33 //
children.translated_text: having released the mercury in the middle, sealed with a light <s>puṭa</s> application. || GRht 18.33 ||

children.text: tena samaṃ bījavare piṣṭiḥ pādāṃśataḥ kāryā /
children.translated_text: With that, in equal [amount of] the excellent seed, a paste (<s>piṣṭī</s>) should be made in a quarter-portion;

children.text: aṃgulinavaparimāṇe mūṣāmadhye ca piṣṭikāṃ dattvā // GRht_18.34 //
children.translated_text: and in a crucible of nine-finger measure, having placed the paste, || GRht 18.34 ||
[the paste should be covered with] <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>gojihvā</s> (ox-tongue plant), <s>dugdhikā</s> (milky spurge), red [substances],
aloe (<s>gṛhakanyā</s>), honey, and rock-salt boluses — covered completely on all sides. || GRht 18.35 ||
The <s>puṭa</s> application should be done until it attains firmness;
[then] six times the amount of sulphur, orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), salt, and alkali, || GRht 18.36 ||
and pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>) — all in equal amount — should be given externally as a medicine-bolus;

children.text: ṣaḍguṇaṣaḍguṇasahitaṃ piṣṭīṃ yantre'tha kacchape dattvā // GRht_18.37 //
children.translated_text: combined with six times, then six times [again]; having placed the paste in the tortoise apparatus, || GRht 18.37 ||

children.text: svedyaṃ puṭayogena tu tridinaṃ ghaṭikātrayaṃ yāvat /
children.translated_text: it should be sweated by <s>puṭa</s> application for three days, up to three <s>ghaṭikās</s> (periods);

children.text: uddhṛtya tato yatnāt piṣṭvā sucūrṇitāṃ kṛtvā // GRht_18.38 //
children.translated_text: then, extracting carefully, grinding, and making into fine powder, || GRht 18.38 ||

children.text: samabījena tu sāryo nāgaṃ triguṇaṃ tataḥ samuttārya /
children.translated_text: [it] should be flowed with equal seed; then, having extracted the lead in triple [amount],

children.text: pratisāraṇā ca kāryā jāritasūtena bījayuktena // GRht_18.39 //
children.translated_text: counter-flowing (<s>pratisāraṇā</s>) should also be performed with digested mercury endowed with seed. || GRht 18.39 ||
And after-flowing (<s>anusāraṇā</s>) afterwards — where the seed is triple;
as previously stated, upon that, calcined lead should be carried in a hundred-fold [amount];

children.text: tena ca ghoṣākṛṣṭe śulbe vedho'tha saptaśataiḥ // GRht_18.40 //
children.translated_text: and with that, in bronze-drawn copper (<s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa-śulba</s>), transmutation occurs in seven hundred [parts]. || GRht 18.40 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states [the preparation of] lead, saying 'lapis lazuli' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.25-40:1 ||

children.text: rājāvartakaṃ prasiddhaṃ vimalaṃ śvetamākṣikaṃ pītābhraṃ pītavarṇaṃ yadabhraṃ gandho gandhakaḥ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ etaiḥ punaretaiḥ kāṅkṣī kāhīti loke kāsīsaṃ pītakāsīsaṃ śilā manohvā daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ taiśca samanvitaṃ militaṃ nāgaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.25-40:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvarta</s> is well-known; <s>vimala</s> is white pyrite; <s>pītābhra</s> is yellow-colored mica; <s>gandha</s> is sulphur; <s>tāpya</s> is gold-pyrite; <s>rasaka</s> is zinc carbonate. With these; furthermore, with these: <s>kāṅkṣī</s> — <s>kāhī</s> in the vernacular; <s>kāsīsa</s> is yellow vitriol; <s>śilā</s> is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>); <s>darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>) — combined, i.e., mixed, with those — one should prepare the lead — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.25-40:2 ||
That he states, saying 'snake' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.25-40:3 ||

children.text: pūrvauṣadhasaṃyutaṃ nāgaṃ ahimārarasaiḥ karavīradrāvaiḥ puṭitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.25-40:4 //
children.translated_text: The lead combined with the aforementioned medicines — with oleander (<s>ahimāra</s>) juices, i.e., with oleander (<s>karavīra</s>) extracts — should be calcinated. || GRhtCM 18.25-40:4 ||

children.text: nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tāvanmāraya yāvannirutthakaṃ yathā punarutthitaṃ na syāt // GRhtCM_18.25-40:5 //
children.translated_text: Kill the lead, i.e., <s>sīsaka</s>, until it is non-revivable (<s>nirutthaka</s>), i.e., so that it cannot be revived again. || GRhtCM 18.25-40:5 ||

children.text: tadanu tatpaścāt tasya nāgasya madhye śulbaṃ tāmraṃ gandhaṃ pratītaṃ lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ etatsarvaṃ miśritaṃ kuryāt ityadhyāhāryam // GRhtCM_18.25-40:6 //
children.translated_text: Then, i.e., after that, in the midst of that lead: copper, i.e., <s>tāmra</s>; sulphur, well-known; salt, i.e., rock salt; and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, i.e., <s>viraṅga</s> (zinc vitriol) — all this should be mixed — this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 18.25-40:6 ||
START GRht 18.41-46
<s>kṣepavedha</s> (projection-transmutation)>
This <s>krāmaṇa</s> (progressive treatment), as described previously too — with pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and realgar (<s>śilā</s>),
with lapis lazuli (<s>rājāvarta</s>), silver-pyrite (<s>vimala</s>), coral (<s>pravāla</s>), <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (zinc vitriol), blue vitriol (<s>tuttha</s>), and poison (<s>viṣa</s>); || GRht 18.41 ||
with magnetic iron (<s>kānta</s>), ochre (<s>gairika</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), <s>bhūmilatā</s> (earthworm), blood (<s>rudhira</s>), cochineal (<s>śakragopa</s>), and minerals (<s>rasas</s>);

children.text: mahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalair mṛtalohaṃ vāyasasya viṣṭhā ca // GRht_18.42 //
children.translated_text: with the ear-wax of she-buffaloes, calcined metal, and the excrement of crows; || GRht 18.42 ||

children.text: pārāvatasya viṣṭhā strīpayaḥ sarvam ekataḥ kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: the excrement of pigeons, and woman's milk — having combined all into one,
this <s>krāmaṇa</s> paste — [soaked] a hundred times with the red and yellow groups; || GRht 18.43 ||
should be soaked in <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil; seven soakings with <s>krauñcī</s> (crane-plant) bile;

children.text: kalkenānena pacet sāritapiṣṭiṃ ca haṇḍikāyāṃ hi // GRht_18.44 //
children.translated_text: with this paste, one should cook the flowed paste (<s>sārita-piṣṭī</s>) in a cooking-pot; || GRht 18.44 ||

children.text: yāvadraktā bhavati hi gacchati nāgaṃ samuttārya /
children.translated_text: until it becomes red and the lead is removed — having extracted [the lead],
one should project (<s>kṣepa</s>) the projection in everything, beginning with <s>sāraṇa</s>. || GRht 18.45 ||

children.text: evaṃ hi koṭivedhī rasarājaḥ krāmito bhūtvā /
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, the king of mercury, having been progressively treated (<s>krāmita</s>), becomes a ten-million-fold transmuter;
becoming a bestower of the elevation of virility and the like, it grants enjoyments. || GRht 18.46 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the <s>krāmaṇa</s>, saying '<s>krāmaṇa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:1 ||

children.text: prāgapīti pūrvādhyāye'pi proktaṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.41-46:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Previously too' — meaning it has been stated in the previous chapter as well — this is the remainder. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:2 ||
Furthermore, the quality of <s>krāmaṇa</s> to be described should be prepared — this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:3 ||
How is that? That he states, saying 'pyrite' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:4 ||

children.text: mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ śilā manohvā tābhiḥ // GRhtCM_18.41-46:5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite; <s>darada</s> is cinnabar; <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) is well-known; <s>śilā</s> is realgar — with these. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:5 ||
Furthermore, 'lapis lazuli' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:6 ||

children.text: rājāvartakaṃ lājavarada iti bhāṣāyāṃ vimalaṃ sitamākṣikaṃ pravālaṃ vidrumaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ tutthakaṃ śikhigrīvaṃ viṣaṃ saktukādikandajaṃ etaiśca // GRhtCM_18.41-46:7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvarta</s> — <s>lājavarda</s> in the vernacular; <s>vimala</s> is white pyrite; <s>pravāla</s> is coral; <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s> (zinc vitriol); <s>tutthaka</s> is copper sulphate, [colored like] peacock-neck; <s>viṣa</s> (poison) is derived from tubers such as <s>saktuka</s> and the like — with these as well. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:7 ||

children.text: kāntetyādi kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ gairikaṃ pratītaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ bhūmilatā bhūnāgaḥ rudhiraṃ śakragopaḥ raso viṣaṃ punaruktādviṣamatra dviguṇaṃ taiḥ // GRhtCM_18.41-46:8 //
children.translated_text: 'Magnetic' and so forth — <s>kānta</s> is magnetite; <s>gairika</s> (ochre) is well-known; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is borax (<s>saubhāgya</s>); <s>bhūmilatā</s> is the earthworm (<s>bhūnāga</s>); <s>rudhira</s> is blood; <s>śakragopa</s> — <s>rasa</s> means minerals; <s>viṣa</s> is repeated, indicating double the amount here — with those. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:8 ||

children.text: ca punar mahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalair hayāripatnīnāṃ śravaṇayor malāni taiḥ saha mṛtalohaṃ mṛtaṃ ca tallohaṃ ceti vāyasasya kākasya viṣṭhā śakṛt // GRhtCM_18.41-46:9 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, with the ear-wax of she-buffaloes, i.e., the ear-impurities of the wives of water-buffaloes — with those; and calcined metal (<s>mṛtaloha</s>), i.e., that which has been calcined and is [still] metal; and the excrement of crows (<s>vāyasa</s>), i.e., the dung of crows. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:9 ||

children.text: pārāvatasya viṣṭhā kapotaśakṛt strīpayo nārīkṣīraṃ etatsarvaṃ mākṣikādistrīkṣīrāntam ekataḥ kṛtvā miśritaṃ vidhāya ca punaretatkrāmaṇakalkaṃ raktapītagaṇaiḥ kiṃśukādiharidrādyaiḥ śatavārān bhāvayedityāgāmiślokasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_18.41-46:10 //
children.translated_text: The excrement of pigeons (<s>pārāvata</s>), i.e., pigeon-dung; woman's milk, i.e., the breast-milk of women. All this, from pyrite to woman's milk, having been combined into one, i.e., mixed and prepared; furthermore, this is the <s>krāmaṇa</s> paste; with the red and yellow groups, i.e., with flame-of-the-forest and such, and turmeric and such — one should soak a hundred times — from the connection with the following verse. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:10 ||
He states the method of the <s>sāraṇa</s> paste, saying 'should be soaked' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:11 ||

children.text: pūrvoktasāraṇakalkaṃ kaṅguṇītaile jyotiṣmatīsnehe bhāvyaṃ tataḥ krauñcīpittabhāvanāḥ sapta deyāḥ dātavyāḥ // GRhtCM_18.41-46:12 //
children.translated_text: The aforementioned <s>sāraṇa</s> paste should be soaked in <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil, i.e., in <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> unctuous substance; then seven soakings of <s>krauñcī</s> (crane-plant) bile should be given, i.e., applied. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:12 ||

children.text: punaḥ sāritapiṣṭiṃ sāritā yā rasendrabījapiṣṭis tām anena kalkena haṇḍikāyāṃ pacet vahninā pākaḥ kartavyaḥ // GRhtCM_18.41-46:13 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the flowed paste (<s>sārita-piṣṭī</s>), i.e., the paste of mercury-and-seed that has been flowed — that, with this paste, should be cooked in a cooking-pot — the cooking should be done with fire. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:13 ||
He states the cooking of the <s>sāraṇa</s> paste, saying 'until' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:14 ||

children.text: pūrvakalkasaṃyutāṃ piṣṭiṃ kiyatkālaṃ pacet yāvadraktā bhavati nāgaṃ ca gacchati nāganāśaḥ syāt nāge gacchati sati samuttārya punastāvatsarvasminsāraṇādau ca kṣepakrameṇa kṣepaṃ kṣipet // GRhtCM_18.41-46:15 //
children.translated_text: The paste combined with the previous paste — for how long should it be cooked? Until it becomes red, and the lead is removed, i.e., the destruction of lead occurs; when the lead is removed, then, extracting [the mercury]; then projecting the projection (<s>kṣepa</s>) in everything, beginning with <s>sāraṇa</s>, by the method of projection. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:15 ||
The purport is that it grants enjoyments from virility and such up to flying through the sky. || GRhtCM 18.41-46:16 ||
START GRht 18.47-48
<silver to gold>
Mica, pyrite, and gold, combined with lead, mixed by the method,

children.text: sūte piṣṭiḥ kāryā divyauṣadhiyogataḥ puṭitā // GRht_18.47 //
children.translated_text: [in] mercury, a paste should be made, calcinated with the application of divine medicines. || GRht 18.47 ||
Burning with six times the sulphur, and extracting the lead with realgar,
in silver, the gold-extraction (<s>hemākṛṣṭi</s>) would occur in a mixed one-sixteenth proportion. || GRht 18.48 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method of paste-[transmutation], saying 'mica' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.47-48:1 ||
