children.text: abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ kanakaṃ hema nāgayutaṃ nāgena sīsakena yutaṃ sahitaṃ vidhinā kartavyopadeśena etatsarvaṃ sūte militaṃ sat piṣṭiḥ kāryā divyauṣadhiyogataḥ puṭitā piṣṭiḥ kāryā iti // GRhtCM_18.47-48:2 //
children.translated_text: Mica is well-known; <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite; <s>kanaka</s> is gold; combined with lead, i.e., with <s>sīsaka</s>, joined, i.e., combined — by the method, i.e., by the instruction of what is to be done — all this, when mixed in mercury, a paste should be made, calcinated with the application of divine medicines. || GRhtCM 18.47-48:2 ||
He states the gold-extraction from silver, saying 'six' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.47-48:3 ||

children.text: pūrvoktāyāṃ piṣṭyāṃ ṣaḍguṇagandhakadāhaḥ kāryaḥ punaḥ ṣaḍguṇaśilayā kṛtvā nāgaṃ samuttārya sīsakamapahāya sā niṣpannā piṣṭī ṣoḍaśāṃśena tāre rūpye militā satī hemākṛṣṭiḥ syātkanakoddhāraṇaṃ bhavet tāmranāgādiṣu dhātuṣu hema sthitameva tata ākṛṣṭiśabdo yuktaḥ // GRhtCM_18.47-48:4 //
children.translated_text: In the aforementioned paste, burning with six times the sulphur should be done; furthermore, with six times the realgar; having extracted the lead, i.e., having removed the <s>sīsaka</s> — that accomplished paste, mixed in a one-sixteenth proportion in silver, i.e., in <s>rūpya</s> — gold-extraction (<s>hemākṛṣṭi</s>) would occur, i.e., the extraction of gold would happen. Gold indeed exists in metals such as copper, lead, and the like — from them, 'extraction' (<s>ākṛṣṭi</s>) is the appropriate term. || GRhtCM 18.47-48:4 ||
START GRht 18.49-50
<silver to gold>

children.text: mākṣikanihataṃ śulbaṃ śilayā nihataṃ ca nāgatulyāṃśam /
children.translated_text: Copper killed by <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), and lead (<s>nāga</s>) killed by <s>śilā</s> (realgar), in equal parts —
calcited with lemon juice together with rock-salt, one should cook in an earthen pot. || GRht 18.49 ||
That powder, together with ghee, honey, and borax, in a sealed crucible (<s>guptamūṣā</s>) —
projected threefold into silver, a divine gold-attraction (<s>hemākṛṣṭi</s>) would result. || GRht 18.50 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the method for killing lead (<s>nāga</s>), beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.49-50:1 ||

children.text: mākṣikeṇa nihataṃ māritaṃ yat śulvaṃ śilayā manaḥśilayā nāgaṃ ca nihataṃ māritaṃ ubhayaṃ tulyāṃśaṃ samabhāgaṃ kāryaṃ punar jambīrarasaiḥ jambīradrāvaiḥ saindhavasahitam ubhayaṃ puṭitaṃ bhāvitaṃ satpacedvahninā pakvaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.49-50:2 //
children.translated_text: That which is killed (<s>nihata</s>), i.e., calcined (<s>mārita</s>), by <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) — that is the copper; and lead (<s>nāga</s>) killed, i.e., calcined, by <s>śilā</s>, i.e., <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) — both should be made in equal parts (<s>tulyāṃśa</s>), i.e., equal measures (<s>samabhāga</s>); furthermore, calcited (<s>puṭita</s>), i.e., saturated (<s>bhāvita</s>), with lemon juices (<s>jambīradrāva</s>) together with rock-salt, one should cook (<s>pacet</s>), i.e., make cooked (<s>pakva</s>), by fire. || GRhtCM 18.49-50:2 ||
Where? In an earthen pot (<s>sthālī</s>), meaning an earthen vessel (<s>mṛdbhājana</s>). || GRhtCM 18.49-50:3 ||
[START GRht 18.51-52]
<copper + silver → gold>

children.text: śulbaṃ balinā nihataṃ tīkṣṇaṃ daradena nihatasamabhāgam /
children.translated_text: Copper killed by <s>balin</s> (sulphur), and iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) killed by cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), in equal parts —
combining them together, one should calcite and cook with <s>mātārasa</s> (woman's milk) alone. || GRht 18.51 ||
Projected threefold into silver, it becomes resembling a cat's eye;

children.text: liptaṃ rasena puṭitaṃ hemārdhena mātrayā tulyam // GRht_18.52 //
children.translated_text: smeared with mercury and calcited, it equals half the measure of gold in proportion. || GRht 18.52 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the method of gold-attraction in lead and silver, beginning with 'copper' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.51-52:1 ||

children.text: balinā gandhakena nihataṃ sat samabhāgaṃ tulyāṃśaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.51-52:2 //
children.translated_text: Killed by <s>balin</s>, i.e., <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur), it being in equal parts (<s>samabhāga</s>), one should make it in equal shares (<s>tulyāṃśa</s>): this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 18.51-52:2 ||

children.text: ubhayamekīkṛtya saṃmiśrya mātārasenaiva nārīkṣīreṇa puṭayet paced iti ślokārthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.51-52:3 //
children.translated_text: Combining both together, i.e., mixing them, one should calcite and cook with <s>mātārasa</s> alone, i.e., with woman's milk (<s>nārīkṣīra</s>): this is the verse's meaning. || GRhtCM 18.51-52:3 ||
He states the method of gold-attraction, beginning with 'in silver' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.51-52:4 ||

children.text: pūrvoktaṃ cūrṇaṃ śulbajaṃ tīkṣṇajaṃ vā tāre triguṇaṃ vyūḍhaṃ vāhitaṃ sat mārjārākṣasaṃnibha otunetrābhaṃ tāraṃ bhavet // GRhtCM_18.51-52:5 //
children.translated_text: The aforementioned powder — derived from copper or from iron — projected threefold into silver, the silver becomes resembling a cat's eye (<s>mārjārākṣa</s>), i.e., having the appearance of a cat's pupil (<s>otunetrābha</s>). || GRhtCM 18.51-52:5 ||

children.text: hemārdhena mātrayā tārārdhabhāgena parimāṇena hemnā tulyam anyūnādhikaṃ rasena payasā // GRhtCM_18.51-52:6 //
children.translated_text: With half the measure of gold — with a quantity equal to half of the silver — [it becomes] equal to gold (<s>heman</s>), neither less nor more; [smeared] with mercury (<s>rasa</s>), i.e., with <s>payas</s> (liquid mercury). || GRhtCM 18.51-52:6 ||
[START GRht 18.53-55]
<lead → gold>

children.text: liptaṃ tadanu puṭitaṃ nāgaṃ hi rasena pādayuktena /
children.translated_text: Smeared and then calcited, lead indeed [treated] with mercury in a quarter portion,

children.text: kharparakasthaṃ kṛtvā kāryaṃ vidhinā dṛḍhaṃ tāpyam // GRht_18.53 //
children.translated_text: placed in a potsherd vessel (<s>kharpara</s>), should be made strongly heated by the [proper] method. || GRht 18.53 ||
Saturated with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo) juice and calcited, rolled smooth with realgar (<s>śilā</s>) —
it should be ground and calcited repeatedly until it attains the state of being free from rise (<s>niruttha</s>). || GRht 18.54 ||
Projected into silver until it becomes a pleasing yellow color,

children.text: hemasamena ca militaṃ mātrātulyaṃ bhavetkanakam // GRht_18.55 //
children.translated_text: and combined with an equal measure of gold, [all] becomes gold in equal proportion. || GRht 18.55 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He again states the method for lead, beginning with 'smeared' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.53-55:1 ||

children.text: triguṇaṃ yathā syāt tathā pādayuktena rasena caturthāṃśasahitasūtena saha nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ kharparakasthaṃ mṛdbhājanakhaṇḍasthitaṃ kṛtvā vidhinā rasajñopadeśena dṛḍhaṃ tāpyaṃ vahniyutaṃ sat nihataṃ kuryāditi vākyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.53-55:2 //
children.translated_text: So that it becomes threefold, with mercury in a quarter portion, i.e., combined with mercury (<s>sūta</s>) having a fourth part added — lead (<s>nāga</s>), i.e., tin (<s>sīsaka</s>), placed in a potsherd vessel (<s>kharpara</s>), i.e., placed in an earthen vessel fragment (<s>mṛdbhājanakhaṇḍa</s>) — should be made strongly heated by fire by the method, i.e., by the instruction of one skilled in mercury (<s>rasajña</s>) — it should be calcined: this is the sentence's meaning. || GRhtCM 18.53-55:2 ||
He states that, beginning with '<s>nirguṇḍī</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.53-55:3 ||

children.text: pakvaṃ nāgacūrṇaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ śreṣṭhavidhānaṃ yathā syāttathā śilayā vartitaṃ san nirguṇḍīrasabhāvitapuṭitaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ paścātpuṭitaṃ vahnipuṭitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.53-55:4 //
children.translated_text: The cooked lead powder, smooth, i.e., of excellent preparation — rolled with realgar (<s>śilā</s>) so that it becomes so — saturated and calcited with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice, i.e., fully saturated (<s>bhāvita</s>) and heat-calcited (<s>gharmapuṭita</s>), and afterward fire-calcited (<s>vahnipuṭita</s>) — one should do this. || GRhtCM 18.53-55:4 ||

children.text: punaryāvannirutthabhāvaṃ aśīratvaṃ vrajet tāvanmṛditapuṭitaṃ marditapācitaṃ kuryād ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.53-55:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, until it attains the state of being free from rise (<s>niruttha</s>), i.e., free from lead-ness (<s>aśīratva</s>), one should grind and calcite it, i.e., pound and cook: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.53-55:5 ||
He states that, beginning with 'in silver' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.53-55:6 ||

children.text: tannirutthanāgacūrṇaṃ yāvatpītaṃ pītavarṇaṃ tāraṃ bhavet tāvadvāraṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.53-55:7 //
children.translated_text: That rise-free lead powder — until the silver becomes yellow (<s>pīta</s>), i.e., golden-colored — should be projected that many times. || GRhtCM 18.53-55:7 ||

children.text: punarhemasamena kanakatulyāṃśena mātrātulyaṃ militaṃ sat ruciraṃ manoramaṃ kanakaṃ sarvaṃ bhavedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.53-55:8 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, combined with an equal measure of gold, i.e., with a portion equal to gold — it being pleasing and beautiful — everything becomes gold: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.53-55:8 ||
[START GRht 18.56-63]
<<s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold pyrite) → gold>

children.text: tāpyaṃ cāṃgulisaṃjñaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tadantare dattvā /
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpya</s>, known as '<s>aṅguli</s>' — having made it into powder, and having placed that inside,

children.text: śulbasya guptamūṣā kāryā puṭitāpyatha ca dhmātā // GRht_18.56 //
children.translated_text: a sealed crucible (<s>guptamūṣā</s>) of copper should be made, calcited and then blown. || GRht 18.56 ||
Combined with gold by the method, it becomes equal in measure.
He states the method for <s>tāpya</s>, beginning with '<s>tāpya</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.56:1 ||

children.text: aṅgulisaṃjñaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tadantare taccūrṇam antare madhye dattvā śulbasya tāmrasya guptamūṣā andhamūṣā kāryā tatra nale ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_18.56:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpya</s> known as <s>aṅguli</s>, i.e., <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold pyrite) — having made it into powder, and having placed that inside, i.e., in the middle — a sealed crucible (<s>guptamūṣā</s>), i.e., a blind crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>), of copper, i.e., of <s>tāmra</s> — should be made there at the tube (<s>nala</s>): this is the intent. || GRhtCM 18.56:2 ||

children.text: sā mūṣā puṭitā dhmātā kāryeti vidhānam uktam // GRhtCM_18.56:3 //
children.translated_text: That crucible, calcited and blown, should be made: thus the procedure has been stated. || GRhtCM 18.56:3 ||
He states that, beginning with 'with gold' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.56:4 ||
The cooked pyrite powder — combined with gold, having done so — || GRhtCM 18.56:5 ||
[START GRht 18.57-63]
In mercury that has assimilated a quarter and so forth, one should smear the leaves of gold-attractions. || GRht 18.57 ||
<gold: <s>rañjana</s> (coloring) method>

children.text: krāmaṇayogena tato vilipya vidhinā nidhāya tulyādhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, by means of a <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetration) compound, having smeared by the method and having placed [it] equally underneath,

children.text: paścāddhemnā sahitaṃ dhmātaṃ mūṣodare samāvartya // GRht_18.58 //
children.translated_text: afterward, combined with gold and blown, having rolled it in the belly of a crucible — || GRht 18.58 ||
the apparatus in a pot, cooked with five clays (<s>pañcamṛd</s>), and calcite-cooked.

children.text: pādādijīrṇasūte pādādinā pādārdhasamānadinā jīrṇo yo'sau sūtaḥ tasmin hemakṛṣṭīnāṃ patrāṇi kaluṣakanakānāṃ patrāṇi lihyāt krāmaṇayogena lepayedityāgāmiślokāt // GRhtCM_18.57-58:1 //
children.translated_text: In mercury that has assimilated a quarter and so forth — a quarter, half, equal, and so forth — the mercury (<s>sūta</s>) in which [morsels] have been assimilated — on the leaves of gold-attractions, i.e., the leaves of impure gold — one should smear, i.e., coat, with a <s>krāmaṇa</s> compound: from the forthcoming verse. || GRhtCM 18.57-58:1 ||
He states that, beginning with '<s>krāmaṇa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.57-58:2 ||

children.text: tato rasalepānantaraṃ krāmaṇayogena kunaṭīmākṣikaviṣam ityādinoktena vilipya tulyādhaḥ tulyaṃ yathā syāttathā adhobhāge nidhāya mūṣodare dhmātaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.57-58:3 //
children.translated_text: Then, after the mercury coating, by means of a <s>krāmaṇa</s> compound — 'consisting of <s>kunaṭī</s>, pyrite, poison,' and so forth as stated — having smeared, with equal [quantity] placed underneath, having placed it in the lower part, one should blow it in the belly of a crucible. || GRhtCM 18.57-58:3 ||

children.text: punaḥ paścāddhemnā kanakena sahitaṃ āvartya dhmātaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.57-58:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, afterward combined with gold, i.e., with gold (<s>kanaka</s>), having rolled it, one should blow: this should be done. || GRhtCM 18.57-58:4 ||
[START GRht 18.59-63]
<gold: production method>

children.text: vakṣyāmi cālepavidhiṃ kramati ca sūto yathā hi patreṣu /
children.translated_text: I shall state the method of coating (<s>ālepa</s>) by which mercury penetrates into the leaves,

children.text: rañjati yena vidhinā samāsataḥ sūtarājastu // GRht_18.59 //
children.translated_text: and by which method, in brief, the king of mercury (<s>sūtarāja</s>) bestows color (<s>rañjana</s>). || GRht 18.59 ||
Having made a cloth [dyed with] lac (<s>ālaktaka</s>), smeared with oil (<s>sneha</s>) afterward, [covered] above with powder,

children.text: avacūrṇitaṃ tu kṛtvā gandhakaśilayā vidhānena // GRht_18.60 //
children.translated_text: having made it sprinkled with sulphur-realgar powder by the method — || GRht 18.60 ||

children.text: tadupari śṛtaṃ ca dattvā gandhakaśilācūrṇaṃ ca sūtavare /
children.translated_text: on top of that, having placed melted [material], and sulphur-realgar powder upon the excellent mercury (<s>sūtavara</s>) —

children.text: paścādvartiḥ kāryā pātre dhṛtvāyase ca same // GRht_18.61 //
children.translated_text: afterward a wick should be made, placed upon an iron vessel on a level [surface]. || GRht 18.61 ||

children.text: dīpaṃ pratibodhya tatastailaṃ dattvā tataḥ stokam /
children.translated_text: Having kindled the lamp, then adding oil little by little,

children.text: pākaṃ yāmasyārdhaṃ svāṅge śītaṃ tataḥ kāryam // GRht_18.62 //
children.translated_text: cooking for half a <s>yāma</s> (one and a half hours), thereafter it should be cooled on its own body. || GRht 18.62 ||
One should then collect the mercury-attraction (<s>sūtakṛṣṭi</s>); smeared then with that,

children.text: krāmaṇayogairliptvā puṭitā sā hemni nirdhmātā // GRht_18.63 //
children.translated_text: coated with <s>krāmaṇa</s> compounds and calcited, that is blown upon gold. || GRht 18.63 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with 'apparatus' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:1 ||

children.text: vā yantraṃ pañcamṛdā valmīkamṛt gairikaṃ khaṭikā saindhavaṃ iṣṭikā ceti pañcamṛdaḥ tayā kṛtvā haṇḍyāṃ sthālyāṃ pakvaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_18.59-63:2 //
children.translated_text: Or, the apparatus — with five clays (<s>pañcamṛd</s>): anthill clay (<s>valmīkamṛt</s>), ochre (<s>gairika</s>), chalk (<s>khaṭikā</s>), rock-salt (<s>saindhava</s>), and brick-dust (<s>iṣṭikā</s>) — these are the five clays; having done [so] with these, [it should be] cooked in a pot (<s>haṇḍī</s>), i.e., an earthen vessel (<s>sthālī</s>). || GRhtCM 18.59-63:2 ||
Furthermore, calcite-cooked means it should be cooked by an elephant-sized calcination furnace (<s>gajapuṭa</s>) and the like: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:3 ||

children.text: lepanavidhiṃ vakṣyāmi yathā patreṣu lepaḥ kāryaḥ punar yathā patreṣu kramati svaguṇān prakāśayati punaryena vidhinā rañjanaṃ rāgaṃ dadāti samāsataḥ saṃkṣepataḥ vidhinā vidhānataḥ sūtarāja evaṃvidho bhavet tamupāyaṃ vakṣyāmīti // GRhtCM_18.59-63:4 //
children.translated_text: I shall state the method of coating — how the coating should be applied on the leaves, and furthermore how [mercury] penetrates (<s>kramati</s>), i.e., manifests its qualities, in the leaves; and furthermore by which method it bestows coloring (<s>rañjana</s>), i.e., tinge (<s>rāga</s>) — in brief, i.e., concisely, by the method, i.e., by the procedure — the king of mercury (<s>sūtarāja</s>) would be of such nature: I shall state that means. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:4 ||

children.text: atha lepakrāmaṇaṃ rañjanavidhānamāha kṛtvālaktakavastram ityādi // GRhtCM_18.59-63:5 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the method of coating, penetration (<s>krāmaṇa</s>), and coloring (<s>rañjana</s>), beginning with 'having made a lac cloth' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:5 ||

children.text: prathamaṃ ālaktakaṃ vastraṃ alaktena rañjitaṃ yadvastraṃ tad ālaktakaṃ anu paścāt snehaṃ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ tailaṃ liptaṃ kāryaṃ tattailaliptavastropari vakṣyamāṇauṣadhānāṃ cūrṇena avacūrṇanaṃ kuryāt tailaliptavastraṃ gandhakaśilayā avacūrṇitaṃ kṛtvā tadupari dātavyaṃ darśayati // GRhtCM_18.59-63:6 //
children.translated_text: First, a lac cloth (<s>ālaktaka vastra</s>) — a cloth dyed with lac is the lac-cloth; after that, oil (<s>sneha</s>), i.e., oil of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and such, should be smeared. On that oil-smeared cloth above, one should sprinkle (<s>avacūrṇana</s>) with the powder of the medicines to be described. The oil-smeared cloth, having been sprinkled with sulphur-realgar, should be placed above: he shows this. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:6 ||

children.text: punastadupari gandhakaśilācūrṇopari śṛtaṃ dattvā punargandhakaśilācūrṇaṃ sūtavare sūtarājopari dattvā paścāttatkaraṇānantaraṃ vartiḥ kāryā sā vartir āyase lohamaye same samabhūmau pātre dhṛtvā tatropari kāryā // GRhtCM_18.59-63:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, on top of that — above the sulphur-realgar powder — having placed the melted [material], and again having placed sulphur-realgar powder upon the excellent mercury (<s>sūtarāja</s>), afterward, i.e., after doing that, a wick should be made; that wick should be placed upon an iron vessel, i.e., one made of metal (<s>lohamaya</s>), on a level ground (<s>samabhūmi</s>), and the [wick] should be placed on top. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:7 ||
He shows the further procedure, beginning with 'lamp' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:8 ||

children.text: tato varteḥ pātropari karaṇānantaraṃ dīpaṃ pratibodhya prajvālya tato vāraṃvāraṃ stokamalpaṃ tailaṃ dattvā yāvadyāmasya praharasya ardhaṃ syāttāvatpākaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.59-63:9 //
children.translated_text: Then, after the placing upon the vessel, having kindled the lamp, i.e., having ignited [it], then repeatedly, little by little, i.e., in small [amounts], one should add oil, until half a <s>yāma</s>, i.e., half a <s>prahara</s> (about one and a half hours) — one should cook for that long: this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:9 ||

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ tatpatitaṃ tailaṃ svāṅgaśītaṃ kāryaṃ aṅge tailadravarūpe śarīre yathāsvaṃ svayameva śītaṃ yathā syāttathā kāryam // GRhtCM_18.59-63:10 //
children.translated_text: Then afterward, the fallen oil should be cooled on its own body (<s>svāṅga</s>) — so that in its body, i.e., in its oil-liquid form (<s>tailadravarūpa</s>), of its own accord it becomes cool — one should do it thus. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:10 ||
He states that, beginning with 'one should collect' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:11 ||
Now, after the cooling process — || GRhtCM 18.59-63:12 ||

children.text: sūtakṛṣṭīṃ ca gṛhṇīyāt karmavit iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.59-63:13 //
children.translated_text: One should collect the mercury-attraction (<s>sūtakṛṣṭi</s>): the one skilled in the procedure [should do so] — this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:13 ||

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ sā sūtakṛṣṭī tena patreṇa liptā satī krāmaṇayogair liptvā hemni suvarṇe nirdhmātā kāryeti // GRhtCM_18.59-63:14 //
children.translated_text: Then afterward, that mercury-attraction, smeared with that leaf, coated with <s>krāmaṇa</s> compounds, should be blown upon gold (<s>suvarṇa</s>): this should be done. || GRhtCM 18.59-63:14 ||
[START GRht 18.64-67]
<gold: production>
Alternatively, with cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), orpiment (<s>āla</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), calcined pyrite (<s>mākṣīka</s>), calcined lead (<s>mṛtanāga</s>) —
together with <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (costus root) and coral (<s>pravāla</s>), ground in <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus) oil — || GRht 18.64 ||

children.text: madhye sūto yukto mṛditaḥ khalve tathāyase vidhinā /
children.translated_text: mercury joined in the midst, ground in an iron mortar by the method,

children.text: saṃsvedya vaṃśanalikāṃ dolāyantreṇa sveditaṃ tridinam // GRht_18.65 //
children.translated_text: after steaming, [placed] into a bamboo tube, sweated by means of a swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>) for three days. || GRht 18.65 ||
Having coated [the leaf] with these black [substances], by the previously stated method,

children.text: nāgaṃ dattvā prakaṭaṃ stokaṃ stokaṃ krameṇaiva // GRht_18.66 //
children.translated_text: having added lead openly, little by little, in sequence — || GRht 18.66 ||

children.text: bhavati hi kanakaṃ divyamakṣīṇaṃ devayogyaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: there results divine, imperishable gold worthy of the gods;

children.text: evaṃ jāritasūte sakalāḥ khalu haṇḍikāḥ sarvāḥ // GRht_18.67 //
children.translated_text: thus, with mercury that has [undergone] assimilation (<s>jārita</s>), indeed all the preparations (<s>haṇḍikā</s>) are [accomplished]. || GRht 18.67 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states an alternative method, beginning with 'alternatively' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:1 ||

children.text: darado hiṅgulaḥ śilā manohvā ālaṃ haritālaṃ taiḥ gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ mākṣikaṃ yatpakvaṃ sindūrīkṛtaṃ mṛtanāgaśca taiḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>); <s>śilā</s> is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>); <s>āla</s> is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>) — with these; sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) is well-known; <s>mākṣika</s> which is cooked, i.e., made into <s>sindūra</s> (red oxide); and calcined lead (<s>mṛtanāga</s>) — with these. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:2 ||

children.text: punaḥ kaṅkuṣṭhapravālasahitaiḥ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ pravālaṃ vidrumaṃ tābhyāṃ sahitaiḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, together with <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and coral — <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s> (costus root), <s>pravāla</s> is coral (<s>vidruma</s>) — together with these two. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:3 ||

children.text: punaretaiḥ kaṅguṇītaile jyotiṣmatītaile piṣṭaiś cūrṇīkṛtaiḥ madhye sūto yuktaḥ kārya ityagrimaślokasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_18.64-67:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with these — ground in <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil, i.e., in <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> oil — made into powder; mercury should be placed in the midst: connected with the next verse. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:4 ||
He states that, beginning with 'in the midst' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:5 ||

children.text: pūrvoktairauṣadhaiḥ kṛtvā madhye auṣadhāntaḥ sūto yuktaḥ kāryaḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:6 //
children.translated_text: With the aforementioned medicines, having placed [them], mercury should be joined in the midst, i.e., within the medicines. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:6 ||

children.text: punarmardayitvā vaṃśanalikāṃ riktodarāṃ prati saṃvedya dinatrayaṃ dolāyantreṇa sveditaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, having ground it, into a bamboo tube (<s>vaṃśanalikā</s>), i.e., one with an empty belly — having steamed [it], one should sweat [it] for three days by means of a swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>): this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:7 ||
He states that, beginning with 'having coated' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:8 ||

children.text: etāni sveditauṣadhāni saṃyuktāni taiḥ kṛṣṇaiḥ kṛṣṇalavaṇaiḥ pūrvoktavidhānena sūtakṛṣṭīvidhānena patraṃ liptvā punaḥ prakaṭaṃ yathā syāt tathā stokaṃ alpamalpaṃ krameṇa nāgaṃ dattvā kanakaṃ jāyate ityagrimaślokasaṃbandhaḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:9 //
children.translated_text: These steamed medicinal substances, combined with those black [salts] — black salt — by the previously stated procedure, the mercury-transmutation procedure, having coated the metal sheet; furthermore, so that it becomes manifest, adding lead little by little, in small amounts, step by step — gold is produced: this is the connection with the following verse. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:9 ||

children.text: evaṃ kṛte sati akṣīṇaṃ akṣayaṃ divyaṃ pravaraṃ devayogyaṃ devā indrādayastadyogyaṃ kanakaṃ bhavati // GRhtCM_18.64-67:10 //
children.translated_text: When this is done, the gold that results is imperishable (<s>akṣīṇa</s>), eternal, divine, excellent — worthy of the gods; the gods such as <s>Indra</s> and others — worthy of them. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:10 ||
This meaning is fitting. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:11 ||

children.text: evaṃ jāritasūte jāritakarmakṛte rase khalu niścitaṃ sarvā haṇḍikāḥ sarve dhātvādyāḥ sakalāḥ saprasavāḥ syurityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:12 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in mercury that has undergone assimilation — in mercury that has had the assimilation operation performed — certainly, all the vessels (<s>haṇḍikā</s>), all the metals and such — all become productive [of gold]: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.64-67:12 ||
[START GRht 18.68]
<Relation between <s>bīja</s> and gold [production]>
Without <s>bīja</s> — when assimilated equally, [only] by one-fourth; with a sixteenth part,

children.text: ardhena pādayogaṃ pādenaikena tulyakanakaṃ ca // GRht_18.68 //
children.translated_text: by half, a quarter-combination; by a full one-fourth, equal gold. || GRht 18.68 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specification, beginning with 'without <s>bīja</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.68:1 ||

children.text: nirbījaṃ yathā syāttathā samajīrṇaṃ pādena turyāṃśena phalaṃ dadāti tathā ardhena jīrṇena ṣoḍaśāṃśena phalaṃ dadāti ca punastadardhena jīrṇena tatpādayogaṃ tatpādena ekena tatpādayogaṃ phalaṃ dadātīti sarvatra vācyam // GRhtCM_18.68:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Without <s>bīja</s>' — so that it would be seedless — when equally assimilated, by one-fourth, by a quarter-portion, it gives a result. Likewise, when assimilated by half, with a sixteenth part, it gives a result. And furthermore, when assimilated by half of that, with a quarter-combination of that, by one single quarter of that, it gives a result of that quarter-combination: this should be stated in all cases. || GRhtCM 18.68:2 ||

children.text: tulyakanakaṃ ca jīrṇaṃ pūrṇaṃ phalaṃ dadātīti // GRhtCM_18.68:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Equal gold' — when fully assimilated, it gives the complete result. || GRhtCM 18.68:3 ||
[START GRht 18.69]
<<s>Tārākṛṣṭi</s> (silver-transmutation)>
I shall describe the <s>tārākṛṣṭi</s> (silver-transmutation): calcined tin combined with an equal portion of orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>),

children.text: lambitamatha nirdhmātaṃ tāmraṃ tārachaviṃ vahati // GRht_18.69 //
children.translated_text: spread out and then smelted — the copper assumes a silver luster (<s>tārachavi</s>). || GRht 18.69 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: hemākṛṣṭyanantaraṃ tārākṛṣṭiṃ vakṣye ahaṃ kaviḥ kathayāmi mṛtavaṅgaṃ māritaṃ vaṅgaṃ tālakena haritāleneti // GRhtCM_18.69:1 //
children.translated_text: After the gold-transmutation (<s>hemākṛṣṭi</s>), I — the poet — shall describe the silver-transmutation (<s>tārākṛṣṭi</s>). Calcined tin — killed tin — with orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>). || GRhtCM 18.69:1 ||

children.text: atha tāmraṃ tulyāṃśaṃ lambitaṃ vistīrṇaṃ yathā syāt tathā nirdhmātaṃ sat tārachaviṃ vahati rūpyadyutiṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.69:2 //
children.translated_text: Then, copper in equal portion, spread out — made extended — when smelted, assumes a silver luster — attains the brilliance of silver: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.69:2 ||
[START GRht 18.70]
Afterward, lead should be added in open crucibles, until it becomes pure;

children.text: tāvad dhmātaṃ vidhinā sunirmalaṃ nistaraṅgaṃ tu // GRht_18.70 //
children.translated_text: it should be smelted by the method until thoroughly pure and free of waves (<s>nistaraṅga</s>). || GRht 18.70 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
That he states, beginning with 'afterward' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.70:1 ||

children.text: paścādvaṅgatāmrayogānantaraṃ prakāśamūṣāsu yāvat nirmalaṃ malavarjitaṃ syāttāvannāgaṃ deyaṃ punaryāvannirmalam ujjvalaṃ nistaraṅgaṃ nāgormivarjitaṃ syāt tāvadvidhinā dhmātaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.70:2 //
children.translated_text: Afterward — after the combination of tin and copper — in open crucibles, lead should be added until it becomes pure — free from impurity. Furthermore, it should be smelted by the method until it is pure, brilliant, and free of waves (<s>nistaraṅga</s>) — free of lead-waves: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.70:2 ||
[START GRht 18.71-72]
<[Transmutation details]>
With orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), and natron (<s>sarjikā</s>), with rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) combined with eye-salve (<s>nayanahita</s>) —

children.text: ekaikaṃ sahitaṃ vā vedhaṃ dattvā punaḥ śulbe // GRht_18.71 //
children.translated_text: each one [separately], or all combined, having applied <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) to copper once more — || GRht 18.71 ||
cow-dung (<s>chagaṇa</s>), buffalo buttermilk (<s>māhiṣatakra</s>), with milkweed (<s>snuhī</s>) milk, ghee (<s>sarpiṣā</s>), step by step,
mixed with jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), milk, and honey — step by step, sprinkling during the <s>vedha</s>. || GRht 18.72 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specification, beginning with '<s>tāla</s>' (orpiment) and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.71-72:1 ||

children.text: tālaṃ haritālaṃ śilā manohvā sarjikā pratītā tābhiḥ saindhavaṃ ca tat lavaṇaṃ ca tena nayanahitasahitaiḥ etaiḥ kṛtvā ekaikaṃ pṛthaktvena vā sahitam ekatvena punaḥ śulve tāmre vedhaṃ pratidadhyāditi // GRhtCM_18.71-72:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tāla</s> is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>); <s>śilā</s> is realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>); <s>sarjikā</s> is well-known [natron]: with these; and <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) — and eye-salve (<s>nayanahita</s>) combined [therewith]; with these [agents], each one separately, or combined as one — one should apply <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) to copper once more. || GRhtCM 18.71-72:2 ||
He states the sprinkling for silver-transmutation, beginning with '<s>chagaṇa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.71-72:3 ||

children.text: chagaṇaṃ vanotpannaṃ māhiṣaṃ takraṃ mahiṣyāḥ idaṃ māhiṣaṃ snuhikṣīreṇa sehuṇḍadugdhena saha punaḥ sarpiṣā ghṛtena saha guḍadugdhamadhubhir miśraiḥ militaṃ kṛtvā kramaśo vedhakarmaṇi niṣekaḥ kāryaḥ // GRhtCM_18.71-72:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Chagaṇa</s> is wild-growing [cow-dung]; <s>māhiṣa takra</s> is buffalo buttermilk; with <s>snuhī</s>-milk (milkweed milk); furthermore, with ghee (<s>ghṛta</s>); mixed with jaggery, milk, and honey — having unified [them]; step by step, in the <s>vedha</s> operation, sprinkling (<s>niṣeka</s>) should be performed. || GRhtCM 18.71-72:4 ||
[START GRht 18.73]
<<s>Tārākṛṣṭi</s>: copper → silver>

children.text: kāñcī brāhmī kuṭilaṃ tālakaṃ samabhāgayojitaṃ dhmātam /
children.translated_text: <s>Kāñcī</s> (gold-pyrite), <s>brāhmī</s> (soma-plant), <s>kuṭila</s> (lead), and orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), combined in equal portions and smelted —
copper transmuted with this becomes a divine silver-transmutation (<s>tārākṛṣṭi</s>). || GRht 18.73 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the silver-transmutation, beginning with '<s>kāñcī</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.73:1 ||

children.text: kāñcī svarṇamākṣikaṃ brāhmī somāhvā kuṭilaṃ sīsaṃ tālakaṃ pratītaṃ etatsamayojitaṃ samāṃśamelitaṃ sat dhmātaṃ kuryāt punaranena kāñcyādigaṇena viddhaṃ śulbaṃ divyā manoramā tārākṛṣṭirbhavet // GRhtCM_18.73:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāñcī</s> is gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>); <s>brāhmī</s> is <s>somāhvā</s> (soma-plant); <s>kuṭila</s> is lead (<s>sīsa</s>); <s>tālaka</s> is well-known [orpiment]. These, combined in equal portions — merged in equal parts — should be smelted. Furthermore, copper transmuted with this group of <s>kāñcī</s> and others becomes a divine — beautiful — silver-transmutation. || GRhtCM 18.73:2 ||
[START GRht 18.74-75]
<Silver: optimization>
Thus the silver-transmutation, coated and transmuted with <s>sārita</s> (flowed) mercury —

children.text: tāraṃ karoti vimalaṃ lepaṃ vā pādajīrṇādi // GRht_18.74 //
children.translated_text: produces pure silver; or with a coating, by quarter-assimilation and so forth — || GRht 18.74 ||
thus mixed and transmuted, pervaded, and equal to the original [silver] —
the silver sheet becomes faultless by the tests of cutting, hammering, and touchstone. || GRht 18.75 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the silver-transmutation, beginning with 'thus' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.74-75:1 ||

children.text: evaṃ uktavidhānena sāritena sāraṇākarmakṛtena liptvā viddhā satī tārākṛṣṭirbhavet // GRhtCM_18.74-75:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the stated procedure, coated and transmuted with <s>sārita</s> (flowed) mercury — mercury that has undergone the <s>sāraṇā</s> operation — the silver-transmutation would result. || GRhtCM 18.74-75:2 ||

children.text: punariyaṃ tārākṛṣṭiḥ tāraṃ vimalaṃ malavarjitaṃ karoti vā pādajīrṇādi pādena jīrṇaṃ yasmin ādiśabdād ardhasamagrahaṇaṃ kāryaṃ tat lepamiti // GRhtCM_18.74-75:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, this silver-transmutation produces silver that is pure (<s>vimala</s>) — free from impurity; or, with a coating of quarter-assimilation and so forth — the word '<s>ādi</s>' includes half and full assimilation: that coating [produces the result]. || GRhtCM 18.74-75:3 ||
He states the specification, beginning with 'thus' and so forth. || GRhtCM 18.74-75:4 ||

children.text: iti pūrvoktavidhānena miśrīkṛtaṃ militaṃ viddhaṃ kramitaṃ mātṛkātulyaṃ samāṃśaṃ sat tāradalaṃ rūpyapatraṃ bhavati tadrūpyadalaṃ chedanatāḍananikaṣaiḥ chedanaṃ khaṇḍanaṃ tāḍanaṃ ghanaghātaḥ nikaṣaṃ śilopari parīkṣaṇaṃ tairiti tāpaiśca nirdoṣaṃ tadbhavati // GRhtCM_18.74-75:5 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the previously stated procedure, mixed — blended — transmuted, pervaded, and equal to the original (<s>mātṛkātulya</s>) — in equal proportion — the silver sheet (<s>tāradala</s>), the silver leaf, results. That silver leaf, by the tests of cutting, hammering, and touchstone — cutting means breaking; hammering means striking with a heavy [tool]; touchstone means testing on stone — by these tests, it becomes faultless. || GRhtCM 18.74-75:5 ||
[START GRht 18.76]
Thus, the <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) procedure [is to be performed] by one who knows the method of the treatise, who is skilled in the operations —
having learned the instruction of the <s>guru</s>, it is to be carried out by one proficient in the operations. || GRht 18.76 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa śāstravidhijñena śāstrasya vidhiṃ jānātīti saḥ tena karmanipuṇena saṃskārapravīṇena kuśalena kartrā gurūpadeśaṃ gururuktalakṣaṇo granthādau tasya upadeśaṃ jñātvā vedhavidhānaṃ kartavyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.76:1 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method — by one who knows the method of the treatise, i.e., one who knows the procedure of the scripture — by one proficient in the operations, skilled in the <s>saṃskāras</s> — the <s>guru</s> is the one whose characteristics were described at the beginning of the treatise; having learned his instruction, the <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) procedure is to be carried out: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 18.76:1 ||
[START GRht 19.1]

children.text: iti rasarājasya vidhau vedhavidhānaṃ prasaṃgataḥ proktam /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the procedure of the king of <s>rasas</s>, the <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) method has been described incidentally;

children.text: adhunā proktānapi vakṣyāmi rasāyane yogān // GRht_19.1 //
children.translated_text: now I shall also describe formulations for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) that have been [previously] taught. || GRht 19.1 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the <s>bhakṣaṇa</s> (ingestion) procedure, beginning with 'thus' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.1:1 ||

children.text: rasarājasya vidhau rasendrakarmavidhāne vedhavidhānaṃ prasaṅgataḥ prastāvataḥ proktaṃ na tu svaprajñāsamam // GRhtCM_19.1:2 //
children.translated_text: In the procedure of the king of <s>rasas</s> — in the procedural arrangement of mercury-operations — the <s>vedha</s> method has been described incidentally — from context — but not at the level of [the author's] own full knowledge. || GRhtCM 19.1:2 ||

children.text: adhunā proktānapi api śabdādanubhūtānapi rasāyane jarāvyādhināśanavidhau yogān dravyasamudāyātkān vakṣyāmi kathayāmītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.1:3 //
children.translated_text: Now, also those that have been taught — by the word '<s>api</s>,' also those that have been experienced — for <s>rasāyana</s>, the method of destroying old age and disease — formulations (<s>yoga</s>), meaning combinations of substances — which ones — I shall describe, shall tell: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.1:3 ||
[START GRht 19.2-4]
<<s>Kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (body purification)>

children.text: ādau prātaḥ prātaḥ saindhavayuktaṃ ghṛtaṃ pibettridinam /
children.translated_text: First, morning after morning, one should drink ghee combined with rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) for three days;

children.text: tadanu kvāthaṃ tridinaṃ yuñjīyāt ketakītanujam // GRht_19.2 //
children.translated_text: then afterward, for three days, one should take a decoction of the root of <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine). || GRht 19.2 ||
The body should be sweated by the method, by the chief of practitioners (<s>vārtikendra</s>);
a decoction of <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s> (picrorhiza) should be administered as a purgative afterward. || GRht 19.3 ||

children.text: tadanu ca śuddhādūrdhvaṃ śleṣmānte recite sakalam /
children.translated_text: Then, after purification from above [i.e., emesis], when at the end all phlegm (<s>śleṣma</s>) has been evacuated,
one should take barley-gruel (<s>yāvaka</s>) with <s>pathyā</s> (chebulic myrobalan) for three days, combined with ghee. || GRht 19.4 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the purification of the body, beginning with 'first' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.2-4:1 ||

children.text: prathamaṃ prātaḥ prātaḥ pratyūṣe tridinaṃ saindhavamilitaṃ ghṛtam ājyaṃ pibet // GRhtCM_19.2-4:2 //
children.translated_text: First, morning after morning — at dawn — for three days, one should drink ghee (<s>ājya</s>) combined with rock salt. || GRhtCM 19.2-4:2 ||

children.text: anyasaṃyogamāha tadanu ghṛtasaindhavānantaraṃ ketakītanujaṃ kvāthaṃ ketakyāḥ tanuḥ śarīraṃ tasmājjātaṃ ketakīmūlasaṃbhavam ityarthaḥ aṅge'pyanukte vihitaṃ tu mūlaṃ iti nyāyāt tridinaṃ prayuñjīyādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.2-4:3 //
children.translated_text: He states another combination: then, after the ghee-and-salt [treatment], a decoction of <s>ketakī</s>'s offspring — <s>ketakī</s>'s <s>tanu</s> (body), from which is born: meaning originating from <s>ketakī</s>'s root, that is the meaning. By the rule 'when the limb is not specified, the root is intended,' for three days one should take [it]: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.2-4:3 ||
He states another method, beginning with 'by the method' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.2-4:4 ||

children.text: tato vidhinā svedavidhānena dehaḥ śarīraṃ vārtikendreṇa rasasaṃpradāyavidā svedyaḥ svinnaḥ kartavyaḥ // GRhtCM_19.2-4:5 //
children.translated_text: Then, by the method — by the sweating procedure — the body should be sweated — made to perspire — by the chief of practitioners (<s>vārtikendra</s>), one who knows the tradition of mercury-practice. || GRhtCM 19.2-4:5 ||

children.text: anyatkiṃ kaṭurohiṇyāḥ tiktāyāḥ kvathitaṃ prasādhitaṃ samyak śuddhikaraṇaṃ anuprayuñjīta svedānantaram ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_19.2-4:6 //
children.translated_text: And what else? A decoction of <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s> (<s>tiktā</s>, picrorhiza), well-prepared — should be administered as a thorough purgative — after the sweating: this is the intent. || GRhtCM 19.2-4:6 ||
He states another method, beginning with 'then' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.2-4:7 ||

children.text: tadanu kaṭukarohiṇīsevanānantaraṃ śuddhād ūrdhvaṃ yathā syāt tathā śleṣmāntarecite sati yathā śleṣmaṇo'ntaḥ syāttathā recite sati tridinaparimāṇaṃ yāvakapathyaṃ ghṛtasahitaṃ prayuñjīteti // GRhtCM_19.2-4:8 //
children.translated_text: Then, after the administration of <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>, from above the purification, so that [the body] be [purged]; when at the end of phlegm all has been evacuated — when all phlegm has been purged — for a three-day duration, barley-gruel with <s>pathyā</s> (chebulic myrobalan), combined with ghee, should be taken. || GRhtCM 19.2-4:8 ||
[START GRht 19.5-7]

children.text: punarapi ca pānayogaṃ vakṣyāmi ca sakalabhuvanahitakṛtaye /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, I shall also describe a drinking formulation, for the benefit of the entire world —

children.text: pītvā prathame yāme coṣṇodakasamamidaṃ cūrṇam // GRht_19.5 //
children.translated_text: having drunk in the first watch [of the night], this powder, with warm water: || GRht 19.5 ||

Of <s>pathyā</s> (chebulic myrobalan), rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), <s>dhātrī</s> (Indian gooseberry), black pepper (<s>marica</s>), sweet flag (<s>vacā</s>), jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (embelia), turmeric (<s>rajanī</s>),

children.text: śuṇṭhīpippalyor api cūrṇaṃ tridinaṃ prayuñjīta // GRht_19.6 //
children.translated_text: and also dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>) and long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>) — the powder should be taken for three days. || GRht 19.6 ||
By this [treatment], with a purified body, with the defects of [humoral] association overcome, [one becomes] strong;

children.text: pītvā payasā sahitaṃ yāvakamamunā bhavecchuddhaḥ // GRht_19.7 //
children.translated_text: having drunk barley-gruel (<s>yāvaka</s>) with milk, by this [treatment] one becomes purified. || GRht 19.7 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method, beginning with 'furthermore' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.5-7:1 ||

children.text: punarapīti yāvakapathyayogānantaraṃ ca punaḥ pānayogaṃ vakṣyāmi kimarthaṃ sakalabhuvanahitakṛtaye samastasaṃsārahitakaraṇāya idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ cūrṇaṃ pathyādyaṃ uṣṇodakasamaṃ taptajalena saha prathamayāme prathamapraharāntaḥ pītvā śuddhaśarīro bhaved ityāgāmiślokasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_19.5-7:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Furthermore' — after the barley-<s>pathyā</s> combination — and furthermore, the drinking formulation — I shall describe. For what purpose? For the benefit of the entire world — for the sake of benefiting all of <s>saṃsāra</s>. This forthcoming powder of <s>pathyā</s> and others, with warm water — with hot water — in the first watch — within the first <s>prahara</s> [of the night] — having drunk [it], one would become of purified body: this is from the connection with the following verse. || GRhtCM 19.5-7:2 ||
He states the purificatory powder, beginning with '<s>pathyā</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.5-7:3 ||

children.text: pathyā harītakī saindhavaṃ pratītaṃ dhātrī āmalakaṃ marīcam ūṣaṇaṃ vacā ugragandhā guḍaḥ pratītaḥ viḍaṅgaṃ kṛmighnaṃ rajanī haridrā śuṇṭhīpippalyor apīti śuṇṭhī nāgaraṃ pippalī māgadhī āsāṃ auṣadhīnāṃ cūrṇaṃ tridinaṃ prayuñjīta // GRhtCM_19.5-7:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pathyā</s> is chebulic myrobalan (<s>harītakī</s>); <s>saindhava</s> is well-known [rock salt]; <s>dhātrī</s> is Indian gooseberry (<s>āmalaka</s>); <s>marica</s> is black pepper (<s>ūṣaṇa</s>); <s>vacā</s> is sweet flag (<s>ugragandhā</s>); <s>guḍa</s> is well-known [jaggery]; <s>viḍaṅga</s> is the worm-killer (<s>kṛmighna</s>); <s>rajanī</s> is turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>); <s>śuṇṭhī</s> is dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>); <s>pippalī</s> is long pepper (<s>māgadhī</s>). The powder of these herbs should be taken for three days. || GRhtCM 19.5-7:4 ||
'With warm water' — this should be understood. || GRhtCM 19.5-7:5 ||
Beginning with 'by this' and so forth:

children.text: amunā vakṣyamāṇavirecanena yāvakādinā śuddhaśarīraḥ san parihatasaṃsargadoṣabalī bhavati saṃsargeṇa ye doṣāḥ śarīrābhyantarāste saṃsargadoṣāḥ te parihatā jitā yena saḥ parihatasaṃsargadoṣaḥ tena balī balayuktaḥ doṣanivṛttau guṇapravṛttir ityavaśyam // GRhtCM_19.5-7:6 //
children.translated_text: By this — by the forthcoming purgative of barley-gruel and such — with a purified body, one becomes strong with the defects of [humoral] association overcome. The defects that are internal to the body through [humoral] association — those are the <s>saṃsargadoṣas</s>; one in whom they have been overcome — defeated — becomes strong — endowed with strength. When defects are removed, the manifestation of good qualities [follows]: this is inevitable. || GRhtCM 19.5-7:6 ||

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā parihatadoṣaḥ amunā payasā uṣṇodakena yāvakaṃ alaktaṃ pītvā śuddho bhavedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.5-7:7 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? With defects overcome — by this, having drunk barley-gruel (<s>yāvaka</s>, i.e., <s>alakta</s>) with milk — with warm water — one becomes purified: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.5-7:7 ||
[START GRht 19.8]
If a person takes <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy) without having performed <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (body purification),

children.text: tasya krāmati na rasaḥ sa rasaḥ sarvāṅgadoṣakṛdbhavati // GRht_19.8 //
children.translated_text: mercury does not pervade him; that mercury causes defects in all limbs. || GRht 19.8 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the fault of not performing purification — 'without doing' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.8:1 //

children.text: yo naraḥ pumān akṛtakṣetrīkaraṇe dehe iti śeṣaḥ na kṛtaṃ akṛtaṃ kṣetrīkaraṇaṃ yasmin tasminsati rasāyanaṃ jarāvyādhivināśanauṣadhaṃ prayuñjīta tasya puṃso raso na krāmati svaguṇānna prakāśayati tarhi kiṃ sarvāṅgadoṣakṛdbhavati bāhucaraṇādiṣu ṣaṭsvaṅgeṣu vikārakṛt syāt // GRhtCM_19.8:2 //
children.translated_text: The man (<s>pumān</s>) who, without having performed <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (body-preparation) — 'in the body' is to be supplied — that is, in whom the body-preparation has not been done, [if he] employs a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating medicine) that destroys old age and disease, for that man mercury does not permeate, does not manifest its qualities; then what happens? It becomes the cause of defects in all limbs — it produces disorders in the six limbs such as arms, legs, and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.8:2 //
START GRht 19.9
Thus purified and having gained strength [through] rice-gruel, barley-water, and green-gram soup,
having prepared one's own body as a field (<s>kṣetrīkṛta</s>), one should properly undertake the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen. // GRht_19.9 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the qualification for <s>rasāyana</s> — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.9:1 //

children.text: pūrvoktavidhānena śuddhaḥ san yo jātabalo bhavati sa kṣetrīkṛtanijadehaḥ akṣetraṃ kṣetraṃ kriyata iti kṣetrīkṛto nijadehaḥ śarīraṃ yena saḥ matimān rasāyanaṃ vidhivatprakurvīta // GRhtCM_19.9:2 //
children.translated_text: One who, being purified by the previously stated procedure, has gained strength — he, having made his own body a prepared field (<s>kṣetrīkṛta</s>), that is, the body that was not a field has been made into a field — such a wise person should properly undertake the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen. // GRhtCM_19.9:2 //

children.text: kaiḥ jātabalaḥ śālyodanaṃ ca yāvakākhyaṃ ca mudgāśca taiḥ // GRhtCM_19.9:3 //
children.translated_text: By what means has strength been gained? By rice-gruel (<s>śālyodana</s>), barley-water (<s>yāvaka</s>), and green-gram (<s>mudga</s>) — by these. // GRhtCM_19.9:3 //
START GRht 19.10-11
Having churned together the oil of the divine tree (<s>surataru</s>), ghee, honey, <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalakī) juice, and milk,
a man who drinks [this] becomes purified in the bowels, internally cleansed. // GRht_19.10 //

children.text: māsena kāntimedhe dvābhyāṃ praśamayati doṣanikaraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Within a month, [he gains] radiance and intellect; within two months, he quells the mass of diseases;
and within three months, [he attains] a body like that of an immortal, of great splendor. // GRht_19.11 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another method — 'divine tree' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.10-11:1 //

children.text: antaritaśuddhaḥ antaritaṃ śuddhaṃ yasya saḥ grahaṇīrogādivarjita ityarthaḥ etāni auṣadhāni nirmathya pītvā viśuddhakoṣṭho bhavati viśuddhaṃ malavarjitaṃ koṣṭhaṃ udaraṃ kasyetyevaṃvidho bhavati // GRhtCM_19.10-11:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Internally cleansed' (<s>antaritaśuddha</s>) — one whose interior is purified, meaning free from digestive disorders (<s>grahaṇī</s>) and the like; having churned these medicines and drunk them, one becomes purified in the bowels (<s>viśuddhakoṣṭha</s>), that is, the belly becomes free of impurities — such a person becomes of this kind. // GRhtCM_19.10-11:2 //

children.text: tāni kāni suratarutailetyādīni suratarur devavṛkṣaḥ tattailapeṣaṇaṃ tailamityarthaḥ ghṛtaṃ ājyaṃ madhu kṣaudraṃ dhātrīrasaḥ āmalakīsalilaṃ payo dugdhaṃ etāni sarvāṇi nirmathya ekīkṛtyetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.10-11:3 //
children.translated_text: What are those [medicines]? 'Divine tree oil' and so forth: <s>surataru</s> is the celestial tree (<s>devavṛkṣa</s>); its oil is obtained by grinding, this is the meaning of 'oil'; <s>ghṛta</s> is clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>); <s>madhu</s> is honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>); <s>dhātrī</s>-juice is the liquid of <s>āmalakī</s>; <s>payas</s> is milk — all these, having been churned together, made into one, is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.10-11:3 //
He states the benefits of consuming this medicine month by month — 'within a month' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.10-11:4 //

children.text: asya auṣadhasya māsena māsapramāṇena bhakṣaṇāt kāntir bhavati medhā ceti dvābhyāṃ dvimāsābhyāṃ doṣanikaraṃ gadasamudāyaṃ praśamayati śāntiṃ nayati punarmāsatritayena trimāsapramāṇena svāt svasāmānyaśarīrāt amaravapurdevaśarīro mahātejāḥ dīptimān syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.10-11:5 //
children.translated_text: By consuming this medicine for the duration of one month, radiance (<s>kānti</s>) arises and intellect (<s>medhā</s>) as well; within two months, it quells the mass of diseases (<s>doṣanikara</s>), i.e., brings the collection of ailments to peace; then within three months, from one's ordinary body, one [attains] a body like that of an immortal (<s>amaravapur</s>), of great splendor (<s>mahātejas</s>), meaning radiant — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.10-11:5 //
START GRht 19.12
<s>Devadāru</s> (Cedrus) oil combined with ghee and <s>triphalā</s> juice in equal parts —

children.text: pītaṃ tat saptāhānnayanavikāraṃ śamaṃ nayati // GRht_19.12 //
children.translated_text: when drunk, within seven days it brings eye diseases to peace. // GRht_19.12 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another formula — '<s>suradāru</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.12:1 //

children.text: suradārutailaṃ devadārutailaṃ ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ triphalārasasaṃyutaṃ triphalāyā rasena draveṇa saṃyutaṃ sahitaṃ ca punaḥ samabhāgaṃ tulyāṃśaṃ tatpītaṃ sat saptāhāt saptadinapramāṇataḥ nayanavikāraṃ netrasaṃbhavaṃ rogaṃ śamaṃ nayati śāntiṃ prāpayati // GRhtCM_19.12:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Suradāru</s>-oil is <s>devadāru</s> oil; <s>ājya</s> is ghee; combined with <s>triphalā</s>-juice, i.e., united with the liquid of the three fruits; and furthermore in equal parts (<s>samabhāga</s>), i.e., in equal proportions — when this is drunk, within seven days, that is, within a period of seven days, it brings eye diseases (<s>nayanavikāra</s>), i.e., ailments arising in the eyes, to peace, i.e., to cessation. // GRhtCM_19.12:2 //
START GRht 19.13

children.text: suratarutailaṃ saghṛtaṃ pītvā śālyodanaṃ ca sakṣīram /
children.translated_text: Having drunk <s>surataru</s> (divine tree) oil with ghee, and [eating] rice with milk,

children.text: jīrṇāhāre bhuktvā harati hi sakuṣṭhān pīnasādīṃśca // GRht_19.13 //
children.translated_text: eating when the previous meal is digested — it indeed removes skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) and rhinitis (<s>pīnasa</s>) and the like. // GRht_19.13 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another formula — '<s>surataru</s> oil' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.13:1 //

children.text: devadārutailaṃ saghṛtaṃ sājyaṃ etadubhayaṃ pītvā sakṣīraṃ śālyodanaṃ bhuktvā ṣaṣṭikaudanam ityabhiprāyaḥ punarjīrṇāhāre pratidinaṃ dināntavīradvaye veditavyam // GRhtCM_19.13:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Devadāru</s> oil with ghee (<s>saghṛta</s>), i.e., with clarified butter — having drunk both of these, and eating rice with milk (<s>sakṣīra</s>), the meaning being <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>-rice gruel; furthermore, when the previous meal is digested (<s>jīrṇāhāra</s>), this is to be understood as every day at the interval of two meal-periods at the end of the day. // GRhtCM_19.13:2 //

children.text: ca punaḥ sakuṣṭhān kuṣṭhaiḥ saha vartante evaṃvidhān pīnasādīn rogān harati dūrīkaroti // GRhtCM_19.13:3 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, it removes those accompanied by skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), i.e., such diseases as rhinitis (<s>pīnasa</s>) and the like — it eliminates them. // GRhtCM_19.13:3 //
START GRht 19.14
Combined with ghee, [<s>devadāru</s>-juice] destroys diseases caused by <s>pitta</s>; combined with oil, [it destroys] diseases arising from <s>vāta</s>;

children.text: guḍasahito madhunā vā kaphajān hantyamaradārurasaḥ // GRht_19.14 //
children.translated_text: combined with jaggery or with honey, the juice of <s>devadāru</s> destroys diseases caused by <s>kapha</s>. // GRht_19.14 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another formula — 'combined with ghee' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.14:1 //

children.text: amaradāruraso devadārujalaṃ ghṛtasahitaṃ ājyamiśritaḥ pittakṛtān rogān harati nāśayati // GRhtCM_19.14:2 //
children.translated_text: The juice of <s>amaradāru</s> (<s>devadāru</s>), i.e., the liquid of <s>devadāru</s>, combined with ghee (<s>ghṛtasahita</s>), i.e., mixed with clarified butter, destroys diseases caused by <s>pitta</s>, i.e., annihilates them. // GRhtCM_19.14:2 //

children.text: punastailayutastailena miśrito devadārurasaḥ vātasaṃbhavān rogān hanti // GRhtCM_19.14:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, combined with oil (<s>tailayuta</s>), i.e., the <s>devadāru</s>-juice mixed with oil, destroys diseases arising from <s>vāta</s>. // GRhtCM_19.14:3 //

children.text: punarguḍasahitaḥ vā madhunā kṣaudreṇa sahito devadārurasaḥ vātasaṃbhavān rogān hanti // GRhtCM_19.14:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, combined with jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), or with honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>), the <s>devadāru</s>-juice destroys diseases arising from <s>vāta</s>. // GRhtCM_19.14:4 //

children.text: punar guḍasahitaḥ vā madhunā kṣaudreṇa sahito devadārurasaḥ kaphajān rogān hantīti vākyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.14:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, combined with jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), or with honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>), the <s>devadāru</s>-juice destroys diseases caused by <s>kapha</s> — this is the meaning of the sentence. // GRhtCM_19.14:5 //
START GRht 19.15
One should take rice with milk, avoiding sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>) and vegetables,
in measures of two, four, or six <s>palas</s> — [corresponding to] the lowest, middle, and highest [doses]. // GRht_19.15 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states what should and should not be eaten during <s>rasāyana</s> — 'avoiding' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.15:1 //

children.text: varjitakāñjikaśākaṃ varjitaṃ kāñjikaṃ sauvīraṃ śākaṃ vāstukādi ca yasmin tattathā payasā kṣīreṇa saha śālyodanaṃ bhuñjīta // GRhtCM_19.15:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Avoiding sour gruel and vegetables' (<s>varjitakāñjikaśāka</s>) — that in which sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>, i.e., <s>sauvīra</s>) and vegetables (<s>śāka</s> such as <s>vāstuka</s> and the like) have been excluded — such rice with milk, i.e., with <s>kṣīra</s>, one should eat. // GRhtCM_19.15:2 //
Furthermore, how much rice? In measures of two, four, or six <s>palas</s>. // GRhtCM_19.15:3 //

children.text: atra mātrādhamamadhyamajyeṣṭhā dvicatuḥṣaṭpalapramāṇā adhamamadhyamottamabaleṣu prayojyetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.15:4 //
children.translated_text: Here, the lowest, middle, and highest doses (<s>mātrādhamamadhyamajyeṣṭhā</s>) of two, four, and six <s>pala</s> measures are to be applied for those of low, medium, and superior strength respectively — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.15:4 //
START GRht 19.16-19
Thereafter, one should consume mercury purified by distillation (<s>pātana</s>) — the <s>āroṭa</s> (distillate);
sweating (<s>svedana</s>), fainting (<s>mūrcchā</s>), reviving (<s>utthāpana</s>), distillation (<s>pātana</s>), arrest (<s>rodha</s>), and regulation (<s>niyama</s>) — // GRht_19.16 //
combined with mica, it should be distilled according to procedure until it becomes stable;

children.text: athavā mākṣikasahitaḥ pātyaḥ sūto vidhānena // GRht_19.17 //
children.translated_text: alternatively, mercury combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) should be distilled by the [proper] method. // GRht_19.17 //
Thus the <s>āroṭa</s> mercury is first employed in body-preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>).
Now he states the mercury formula — 'thereafter' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:1 //

children.text: tadanu pathyamātropayogānantaraṃ pātanaśuddhaṃ pātanena śuddhaṃ sūtakaṃ āroṭam eva sāmānyam evāśnīyāt bhakṣayet // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:2 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, i.e., after the use of the appropriate diet, one should consume the <s>āroṭa</s>, that is, ordinary [distilled] mercury purified by distillation (<s>pātanaśuddha</s>) — one should eat it. // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:2 //

children.text: ca punaḥ svedanamūrchotthāpanarodhāśca svedanaṃ ca mūrchā ca utthāpanaṃ ca pātanāni ca nirodhaśceti dvandvaḥ ete yadyapi santi niyamaśca yadyapyasti tathāpyāroṭaḥ pātanena syād ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:3 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, sweating, fainting, reviving, distillation, and arrest — these form a <s>dvandva</s> compound; and although these [operations] exist, and although regulation also exists, still the <s>āroṭa</s> is obtained by distillation — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:3 //
Incidentally, he states the distillation — 'with mica' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:4 //

children.text: sūtaḥ abhrakasahitaḥ gaganamilitaḥ san pātyaḥ // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:5 //
children.translated_text: Mercury, combined with mica (<s>abhraka</s>), should be distilled. // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:5 //
By what method? By means of the <s>ḍamaruka</s>-yantra (hourglass apparatus) and similar devices. // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:6 //
Furthermore, [it should be distilled] so many times until it becomes stable. // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:7 //

children.text: athavā vidhyantare sūto mākṣikasahitaḥ pātyo vidhānena ayamapi yāvatsthiro bhavati // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:8 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, by another method, mercury combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) should be distilled by the [proper] procedure — this too [should be done] until it becomes stable. // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:8 //
He states the method of <s>āroṭa</s> and other [preparations] of mercury for <s>rasāyana</s> — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:9 //

children.text: āroṭa iti pūrvoktena pātanakarmaṇā ūrdhvādhastiryagbhavena sādhita āroṭaḥ saḥ prathamaṃ yathā syāttathā rasāyane jarāvyādhināśane niyujyate iti // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:10 //
children.translated_text: The <s>āroṭa</s>, i.e., that which has been prepared by the previously stated distillation process — upward, downward, and oblique — that [āroṭa] is first employed in <s>rasāyana</s>, i.e., in the destruction of old age and disease — thus. // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:10 //

children.text: athavā kalkayogena rasādisambhūtena raso bhasma kṛtvā // GRhtCM_19.17:1 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, by means of a paste-formula (<s>kalkayoga</s>) produced from mercury and other [ingredients], mercury is reduced to ash (<s>bhasma</s>). // GRhtCM_19.17:1 //
START GRht 19.18-19

children.text: athavā bhasma ca kṛtvā baddho vā kalkayogena // GRht_19.18 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, having also made [mercury into] ash, or [mercury that is] bound, by means of a paste-formula — // GRht_19.18 //
combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch), iron powder, <s>harītakī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, ghee, and honey —
one should first employ mercury thus combined for body-preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>). // GRht_19.19 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: dvividhaṃ bhasma ūrdhvagaṃ talabhasma ca varṇabhedena ṣaḍvidhaṃ śvetaṃ bhasma pītaṃ bhasma haritaṃ bhasma raktaṃ bhasma kṛṣṇaṃ bhasma karburaṃ bhasma iti ṣaḍvidhaṃ tatkṛtvā kṣetrīkaraṇe niyujyate prathamam // GRhtCM_19.18cd-19:1 //
children.translated_text: The ash is of two kinds: upward-rising (<s>ūrdhvaga</s>) and bottom-ash (<s>talabhasma</s>); by distinction of color, it is sixfold: white ash, yellow ash, green ash, red ash, black ash, and variegated ash — thus sixfold; having made that, it is first employed in body-preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>). // GRhtCM_19.18cd-19:1 //
He states the mercury formula — '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.18cd-19:2 //

children.text: mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ śilājatu prasiddhaṃ lohacūrṇaṃ māritamuṇḍasya rajaḥ pathyā harītakī akṣo vibhītakaḥ viḍaṅgaṃ kṛmighnaṃ ghṛtam ājyaṃ madhu kṣaudraṃ etaiḥ samprayuktaṃ rasaṃ kṣetrīkaraṇāya prayuñjīteti vākyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.18cd-19:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>); <s>śilājatu</s> is well-known; iron powder (<s>lohacūrṇa</s>) is the dust of killed iron (<s>māritamuṇḍa</s>); <s>pathyā</s> is <s>harītakī</s>; <s>akṣa</s> is <s>vibhītaka</s>; <s>viḍaṅga</s> is the worm-destroying [herb]; <s>ghṛta</s> is clarified butter; <s>madhu</s> is honey — combined with these, one should employ mercury for body-preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>) — this is the meaning of the sentence. // GRhtCM_19.18cd-19:3 //
START GRht 19.20
Thus, mercury made into a paste (<s>kalkīkṛta</s>), combined with mica (<s>ghana</s>), loadstone (<s>kānta</s>), honey, ghee, and so forth —
having consumed [this], one attains immortality; this body-preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>) is the principal [step]. // GRht_19.20 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: ityuktavidhānena kalkīkṛtaṃ sūtaṃ bhuktvā amaratāṃ devatvaṃ gacchet // GRhtCM_19.20:1 //
children.translated_text: By the previously stated method, having consumed mercury made into a paste (<s>kalkīkṛta</s>), one attains immortality (<s>amaratā</s>), i.e., the state of a deity. // GRhtCM_19.20:1 //

children.text: iti kiṃ ghanakāntamadhughṛtādisaṃyuktaṃ ghano'bhrakaḥ kāntaṃ lohajāti madhu kṣaudraṃ ghṛtam ājyaṃ ādiśabdāt sitā grāhyā etaiḥ saṃyuktaṃ sat kalkīkṛtaṃ idaṃ ca pradhānaṃ kṣetrīkaraṇaṃ kṣetrī kriyate'neneti // GRhtCM_19.20:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus what? Combined with mica (<s>ghana</s>, i.e., <s>abhraka</s>), loadstone (<s>kānta</s>, i.e., the iron variety), honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>), ghee (<s>ājya</s>) — and by the word 'and so forth' (<s>ādi</s>), sugar (<s>sitā</s>) is to be understood — combined with these, having been made into a paste; and this is the principal body-preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>) — 'by which the body is made into a field' [is the etymology]. // GRhtCM_19.20:2 //
Thus [ends] the <s>āroṭa</s> procedure. // GRhtCM_19.20:3 //
START GRht 19.21

children.text: atha kṛṣṇaṃ vā pītaṃ vā saṃyojyaṃ ghanaṃ śikhiprabhaṃ bahuśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, black or yellow mica (<s>ghana</s>), with peacock-like brilliance, [should be heated] repeatedly,
quenched in cow's milk, freed from rocky impurities — [this] should be employed in <s>rasāyana</s>. // GRht_19.21 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now, the procedure for leaf-mica (<s>patrābhra</s>). // GRhtCM_19.21:1 //

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ śyāmavarṇaṃ ghanaṃ abhraṃ pītaṃ pītavarṇaṃ ghanaṃ vā bahuśo naikavāraṃ śikhiprabhaṃ agniprabhaṃ sat surabhīkṣīraniṣiktaṃ secitaṃ kāryaṃ punargatagiridoṣaṃ yathā syāttathā gatā girijā doṣā mahīdharasaṃbhavā doṣā yasmāt tadevaṃ saṃśodhayitvā tat ghanaṃ rasāyane jarāvyādhivināśakaraṇe yojyam // GRhtCM_19.21:2 //
children.translated_text: Black, i.e., dark-colored mica (<s>ghana</s>, i.e., <s>abhra</s>), or yellow-colored mica — repeatedly, i.e., not just once, heated to peacock-like brilliance (<s>śikhiprabha</s>), i.e., fire-brilliance, and quenched in cow's milk — this should be done; furthermore, [it should be done] so that the rocky impurities are removed (<s>gatagiridoṣa</s>), i.e., the defects arising from the mountain are gone — having thus purified it, that mica should be employed in <s>rasāyana</s>, i.e., in the destruction of old age and disease. // GRhtCM_19.21:2 //
START GRht 19.22
Even without luster (<s>niścandrika</s>), [mica that is] purified, combined with <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, ghee, and honey —

children.text: pratidivasaṃ palamekaṃ bhuktvā kṣīrāśano vidhinā // GRht_19.22 //
children.translated_text: eating one <s>pala</s> daily, on a diet of milk, according to the proper method — // GRht_19.22 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the mica formula — 'without luster' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.22:1 //

children.text: ghanaṃ niścandrikamapi śuddhaṃ candrikārahitamapi nirdoṣaṃ viḍaṅgatriphalājyamadhurasamāyuktaṃ kṛmighnaharītakīvibhītakāmalakaghṛtakṣaudramilitaṃ pratidivasaṃ pratidinaṃ ekapalapramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ bhuktvā vidhinā śuddhaśarīravidhānena kṣīrāśano bhavet kṣīreṇa saha śālyodanāśanaṃ samācaredityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.22:2 //
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>ghana</s>), even without luster (<s>niścandrika</s>), i.e., devoid of brilliance, [when] purified, i.e., rendered faultless, combined with <s>viḍaṅga</s> (worm-destroying herb), <s>triphalā</s> (<s>harītakī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>), ghee (<s>ājya</s>), and honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>) — eating daily in the measure of one <s>pala</s>, everything [combined], by the proper method, i.e., with the regimen of a purified body, one should maintain a diet of milk with rice — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.22:2 //
START GRht 19.23
Mica (<s>vyoman</s>) combined with the three pungents (<s>trikaṭuka</s>), <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), and <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) —

children.text: kṣīraudanam aśnīyājjīvati jantuḥ śataṃ varṣam // GRht_19.23 //
children.translated_text: [one who] eats rice with milk [with this], a living being lives for a hundred years. // GRht_19.23 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
On that, he says — 'three pungents' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.23:1 //

Sky (<s>vyoma</s>), i.e., mica (<s>abhraka</s>), combined with the three pungents (<s>trikaṭuka</s>), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia), the three fruits (<s>triphalā</s>), <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), and mineral pitch (<s>śilājatu</s>) — i.e., combined with long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>), black pepper (<s>marica</s>), dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>), <s>harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan), <s>vibhītaka</s> (beleric myrobalan), <s>āmalaka</s> (emblic myrobalan), honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>), and mineral pitch — one should eat, i.e., consume. // GRhtCM_19.23:2 //
Furthermore, one should eat milk-rice (<s>kṣīraudana</s>) as the wholesome diet (<s>pathya</s>). // GRhtCM_19.23:3 //

children.text: eva kṛte sati jantuḥ śataṃ jīvati jantujanyuśarīriṇaḥ ityamaraḥ // GRhtCM_19.23:4 //
children.translated_text: When this is done, the creature (<s>jantu</s>) lives a hundred [years] — '<s>jantu</s>, <s>janyu</s>, and <s>śarīrin</s>' [are synonyms for embodied being] according to <s>Amara</s> [Kośa]. // GRhtCM_19.23:4 //
Thus ends the procedure of foil-mica (<s>patrābhraka-prakriyā</s>). // GRhtCM_19.23:5 //
START GRht 19.24
Thus, these and other [preparations] combined with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>) have been described in many [texts];
such foil-mica preparations are to be avoided, for they lack proper reasoning (<s>niryuktika</s>). // GRht_19.24 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing the progressive [superiority] of mica, he states — 'thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.24:1 //

children.text: ityevamādayaḥ iti pūrvoktā yogā ādayo yeṣāṃ te anye kāñjikayuktāśca kāñjikenāranālena yuktāḥ yogīkṛtāḥ granthāntare rasāvatārādau bahuśaḥ kīrtitāḥ kathitāḥ te patrābhrakayogāḥ niryuktikāḥ niryukte bhavā ikpratyayāntās te varjyāḥ sevane'yogyā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.24:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus these and others' — 'thus' [refers to] the previously stated formulations; those which begin with them; 'others' combined with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), i.e., formulated with <s>kāñjika</s> (rice-water/gruel) — described in many [places] in other texts such as the <s>Rasāvatāra</s> and others, i.e., stated [therein]; those foil-mica formulations that lack proper reasoning (<s>niryuktika</s>) — derived from <s>niryukti</s> (rational basis), with the -<s>ik</s> suffix — those are to be avoided (<s>varjya</s>), i.e., unfit for consumption — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.24:2 //
START GRht 19.25
Those foil-mica formulations that have been proclaimed for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) purposes, according to procedure,
by those who do not know the properties of substances — by them, old age and death have been prescribed. // GRht_19.25 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: avidhinā patrābhrakayogo vikārāyetyata āha ya ityādi // GRhtCM_19.25:1 //
children.translated_text: Since foil-mica used improperly leads to pathology, he states — 'those' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.25:1 //

children.text: ye ajñātadravyaguṇaiḥ ajñātā dravyāṇāṃ abhrādināṃ guṇā yais tair evaṃvidhaiḥ puṃbhiḥ vidhinā sāmānyavidhānena patrābhrakayogāḥ rasāyanārthaṃ kīrtitās tair eva jarā mṛtyuśca upadiṣṭaḥ jarā pālityaṃ mṛtyur vyādhiḥ // GRhtCM_19.25:2 //
children.translated_text: Those [formulations] by persons who do not know the properties of substances — those whose knowledge of the properties of substances like mica and such is unknown — by such persons, by ordinary procedure alone, foil-mica formulations proclaimed for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) purposes — by those very [persons], old age and death have been prescribed: old age is premature greying; death is disease. // GRhtCM_19.25:2 //
START GRht 19.26
The dense [mica-essence], having not attained world-being (<s>loka-bhāva</s>), leads the digestive fire (<s>jaṭharāgni</s>) to extinction;

children.text: agniṃ vināpi naśyati paribhūto vividharogagaṇaiḥ // GRht_19.26 //
children.translated_text: even without fire, [the person] perishes, overcome by multitudes of various diseases. // GRht_19.26 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: jarāmṛtyorupadeśe hetumāha aprāptetyādi aprāptalokabhavaṃ yathā syāttathā asya kartuḥ ghanaḥ // GRhtCM_19.26:1 //
children.translated_text: Stating the reason for the prescription of old age and death — 'not attained' and so forth: the dense [mica], in a manner that achieves not-attaining-world-being, of this practitioner — // GRhtCM_19.26:1 //

children.text: jaṭharāgniṃ vināpi pumān naśyati nāśaṃ prāpnoti // GRhtCM_19.26:2 //
children.translated_text: even without the digestive fire, the person perishes, i.e., reaches destruction. // GRhtCM_19.26:2 //

children.text: kiṃbhūtaḥ san vividharogagaṇaiḥ nānārogasamūhaiḥ paribhūto vijitaḥ san iti vākyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.26:3 //
children.translated_text: In what condition? Being overcome, i.e., conquered, by multitudes of various diseases, i.e., by collections of manifold ailments — this is the sentence-meaning. // GRhtCM_19.26:3 //

children.text: kāṣṭhe sthitam api ghanapaṭalamadhye'pi abhre'bhrasattvaṃ sthitaṃ tadāha abhrasatvaṃ ghanasāraṃ ghanapaṭale sthitamapi nijakāryaṃ svakīyakṛtyaṃ tathā na kurute vahniragniḥ // GRhtCM_19.26:4 //
children.translated_text: Even while situated within the mica-layer (<s>ghana-paṭala</s>), the mica-essence (<s>abhra-sattva</s>) situated in its sheet-form does not perform its own function — fire (<s>vahni</s>) [does not perform its function]. // GRhtCM_19.26:4 //

children.text: kāṣṭhe dāruṇi sthitaḥ san nijakāryaṃ na kurute tu punaḥ yathā ghṛtaṃ payasi dugdhe sthitaṃ sat svīkāryaṃ na kurute cāgrahir iva dhanasthamiva madhye sthitaṃ kāryaṃ kurute'tiniḥsṛtaṃ sat pṛthagbhūtaṃ sat nijakāryaṃ kuruta iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_19.26:5 //
children.translated_text: Just as [fire] situated in wood (<s>kāṣṭha</s>), i.e., timber, does not perform its own function; moreover, just as ghee (<s>ghṛta</s>) situated in milk (<s>payas</s>), i.e., in cow's milk, does not perform its own function — like a seizure (<s>āgrahīr</s>), like [something] situated within wealth — when situated in the middle, it performs [its] function; when thoroughly extracted (<s>atiniḥsṛta</s>), i.e., when made separate, it performs its own function — this is the sense. // GRhtCM_19.26:5 //
START GRht 19.27
<mica (<s>abhra</s>): inedible [forms]>

children.text: abhrasya rasāyanināṃ bhakṣyamiha kīrtitaṃ paraṃ satvam /
children.translated_text: Of mica, for those pursuing <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), the supreme edible here proclaimed is the essence (<s>sattva</s>);

children.text: trividhaṃ gaganamabhakṣyaṃ kācaḥ kiṭṭaṃ ca pattrarajaḥ // GRht_19.27 //
children.translated_text: three forms of mica (<s>gagana</s>) are inedible: glass (<s>kāca</s>), slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), and foil-dust (<s>patra-rajas</s>). // GRht_19.27 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the edible and inedible [forms] of mica — 'of mica' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.27:1 //

children.text: abhrakasatvamiha kṣetrīkaraṇe rasāyanināṃ jarāvyādhivināśecchūnāṃ param utkṛṣṭaṃ bhakṣyaṃ aśanayogyaṃ kīrtitam // GRhtCM_19.27:2 //
children.translated_text: The essence of mica — here, in the domain of <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (body-field preparation) — for those pursuing <s>rasāyana</s>, i.e., those desiring the destruction of old age and disease — is proclaimed as the supreme, i.e., excellent, edible, i.e., fit for consumption. // GRhtCM_19.27:2 //

children.text: punastrividhaṃ triprakāraṃ gaganamabhraṃ abhakṣyaṃ abhojyam // GRhtCM_19.27:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, three-fold, i.e., of three kinds, mica (<s>gagana</s>) is inedible, i.e., unfit for consumption. // GRhtCM_19.27:3 //

children.text: kiṃ tat kācaḥ kācarūpaṃ kiṭṭaṃ malarūpaṃ pattrarajaḥ sāmānyābhracūrṇaṃ ceti trividhamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.27:4 //
children.translated_text: What are those? Glass (<s>kāca</s>), i.e., in glass form; slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), i.e., in impurity form; and foil-dust (<s>patra-rajas</s>), i.e., ordinary mica powder — thus three-fold, is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.27:4 //
START GRht 19.28-33
First, mica-essence and iron-dust, rubbed and saturated with <s>triphalā</s> (three-fruit) juice,
one should make it collyrium-like (<s>añjana-sadṛśa</s>), covered with cloth, [dried] by sun-rays. // GRht_19.28 //
Having thus made it smooth, equal to various lodestone and iron powders,

children.text: lohaghanaṃ ca tadevaṃ bhṛṅgeṇa ca sādhayed bahuśaḥ // GRht_19.29 //
children.translated_text: iron and mica-essence together — one should process with <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta) many times. // GRht_19.29 //
Mixed with <s>triphalā</s>, ghee, and honey — this is [like] ambrosia (<s>amṛta</s>), stored for a month in grain,
placed inside a sealed metal bowl (<s>śastra-kaṭorikā-sampuṭa</s>), consecrated with mantras. // GRht_19.30 //

children.text: māsena tu taduddhṛtya jñātvā balaṃ tatprayuñjīta /
children.translated_text: After a month, having extracted it and ascertained its potency, one should employ it;

children.text: kāntaṃ vinātha gaganaṃ gaganaṃ vinā tathā ca kāntam // GRht_19.31 //
children.translated_text: either lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) without mica, or mica (<s>gagana</s>) without lodestone, and likewise lodestone [alone]. // GRht_19.31 //
Obesity, cataract (<s>paṭala</s>), glaucoma (<s>kāca</s>), blindness (<s>timira</s>), tumors (<s>arbuda</s>), tinnitus (<s>karṇanāda</s>), colic (<s>śūla</s>),
it destroys piles (<s>arśas</s>), fistula (<s>bhagandara</s>), urinary disorders (<s>meha</s>), splenic disease (<s>plīhā</s>) and such, and premature greying (<s>pālitya</s>). // GRht_19.32 //
The wise one performing this should eat [a diet] primarily of cow's milk and buttermilk (<s>mastu</s>);
[meat from] arid regions (<s>jāṅgala</s>), green gram (<s>mudga</s>), ghee, milk, and <s>śāli</s>-rice — with celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>). // GRht_19.33 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the preparation of mica-essence with iron — 'at first' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:1 //

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ ghanaloharajaḥ ghanamabhrasatvaṃ loharajaḥ kāntacūrṇaṃ triphalārasabhāvanaiḥ harītakīvibhītakāmalakadravapuṭanair nirghṛṣṭaṃ sat añjanasadṛśaṃ sauvīrāñjanatulyaṃ kurvīta kaiḥ kṛtvā sūryakaraiḥ kena sthagitavastreṇa ācchāditapaṭena vastreṇācchādya sūryakarasannidhau dhāryamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:2 //
children.translated_text: First, i.e., at the beginning: mica-essence-and-iron-dust (<s>ghana-loha-rajas</s>) — <s>ghana</s> is mica-essence (<s>abhra-sattva</s>); iron-dust (<s>loha-rajas</s>) is lodestone powder (<s>kānta-cūrṇa</s>) — rubbed and saturated with <s>triphalā</s> juice, i.e., with repeated soaking in the decoction of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>vibhītakī</s>, and <s>āmalaka</s>, one should make it collyrium-like, i.e., resembling <s>sauvīrāñjana</s> (antimony collyrium); by what means? By sun-rays; how? With covered cloth — meaning covered with cloth and kept in the proximity of sunlight — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:2 //
'Thus' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:3 //

children.text: itthamamunā prakāreṇa ślakṣṇam añjanasannibhaṃ yathā syāt tathā ghanasatvakāntaṃ kṛtvā punarlohaghanaṃ lohaṃ muṇḍādi ghanaṃ abhrasatvaṃ etadubhayaṃ vividhakāntalohacūrṇasamaṃ vividhā nānājātayaḥ ayaskāntabhedāḥ teṣāṃ cūrṇaṃ tatsamaṃ kṛtvā bhṛṅgeṇa ca bahuśo'nekavāraṃ sādhayedbhāvayedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method, having made the mica-essence-and-lodestone smooth and collyrium-like, then iron-and-mica-essence (<s>loha-ghana</s>) — iron (<s>loha</s>) being <s>muṇḍa</s> (wrought iron) and such, mica-essence (<s>ghana</s>) being <s>abhra-sattva</s> — these two made equal to the powder of various lodestones, i.e., the various kinds of magnet (<s>ayaskānta</s>) varieties — having made their powder equal, one should process with <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta alba) many times, i.e., saturate repeatedly — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:4 //
He states that — '<s>triphalā</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:5 //

children.text: tadbhṛṅgarājena bahuśo bhāvitaṃ ghanasatvakāntaṃ idam amṛtaṃ sudhāsamaṃ na mṛtamamṛtaṃ tat triphalāmadhughṛtamiśritaṃ harītakīvibhītakāmalakaghṛtakṣaudramilitaṃ dhānye kasyacidannasyāntaḥ māsasthitaṃ kuryāt māsaikaparimāṇaṃ tatra vidhātavyamiti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:6 //
children.translated_text: That mica-essence-and-lodestone, saturated many times with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta) juice — this is ambrosia (<s>amṛta</s>), i.e., nectar-like — not dead but immortalizing; that, mixed with <s>triphalā</s>, honey, and ghee — combined with <s>harītakī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, ghee, and honey — should be stored in grain, i.e., inside some grain [heap], for a month; the clarification is: it should be kept there for the duration of one month. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:6 //
Of what quality? Consecrated with mantras. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:7 //
And the mantra is:
