To her whose locks are adorned with <s>mandāra</s> (coral tree) garlands, to him whose crest is decorated with a garland of skulls,

children.text: divyāmbarāyai ca digambarāya namaḥ śivāyai ca namaḥ śivāya /
children.translated_text: to her who wears divine garments, to him who is sky-clad (<s>digambara</s>) — homage to <s>Śivā</s> and homage to <s>Śiva</s>!
— and so forth with such [mantras]. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:8 //
He states that — 'after a month' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:9 //

children.text: dhānyānmāsena māsaikaparimāṇenoddhṛtya bahirnītvā punarapi balaṃ jñātvā prayuñjīta bhoktre dadyāt atha viśeṣaṃ darśayati kāntaṃ vinā abhrakasatvameva kṛtvā prayuñjīta ca punargaganaṃ vinā kāntaṃ kevalaṃ pūrvavidhānena sādhayitvā prayuñjītetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:10 //
children.translated_text: Having extracted from the grain after a month, i.e., after one month's duration, having brought it out, and then having ascertained its potency, one should employ it, i.e., give it to the patient. Then he shows the specifics: one may prepare and employ mica-essence alone without lodestone (<s>kānta</s>); or again, lodestone alone without mica, processed by the aforementioned procedure and employed — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:10 //
He states the results — 'obesity' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:11 //

children.text: sthaulyamiti medorogaḥ paṭalakācatimirāṇi netrarogāḥ arbudaṃ granthiviśeṣaḥ karṇanādaḥ pratītaḥ śūlamaṣṭavidhaṃ etāni hanti arśāṃsi gudajāni bhagandaramehaplīhādi bhagandaraḥ gudavraṇaṃ mehaḥ pramehaḥ bījavikāraḥ plīhā plīharogaḥ ete rogā ādiryasya tat hanti pālityaṃ jarāṃ ca nāśayatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:12 //
children.translated_text: 'Obesity' (<s>sthaulya</s>) means fatty disease; cataract (<s>paṭala</s>), glaucoma (<s>kāca</s>), and blindness (<s>timira</s>) are eye diseases; tumor (<s>arbuda</s>) is a specific type of growth; tinnitus (<s>karṇanāda</s>) is well-known; colic (<s>śūla</s>) is of eight kinds — these it destroys; piles (<s>arśas</s>) arise at the anus; fistula (<s>bhagandara</s>) is an anal ulcer; <s>meha</s> is <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorder), a seminal disorder; <s>plīhā</s> is splenic disease — those diseases and others beginning with these, it destroys; and it eliminates premature greying (<s>pālitya</s>) and old age (<s>jarā</s>) — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:12 //
He states the dietary regimen — 'this' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:13 //

children.text: etanniṣpannauṣadhabhakṣaṇaṃ kurvan matimān puruṣaḥ gorasamastupradhānaṃ goraso godugdhaṃ mastu dadhimastu evaṃpradhānamannamaśnīyāt bhuñjīta // GRhtCM_19.28-33:14 //
children.translated_text: The wise person performing this, i.e., the consumption of this prepared medicine, should eat food primarily consisting of cow's milk (<s>go-rasa</s>) and buttermilk (<s>mastu</s>) — cow's milk being <s>go-dugdha</s>, <s>mastu</s> being yogurt-whey — food consisting primarily of these. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:14 //

children.text: punarjāṅgalamudgājyapayo'śnīyāt jāṅgalasyedaṃ jāṅgalaṃ svalpāmbuśākhīdeśaḥ jāṅgalaḥ mudgaḥ pratīto'nnaviśeṣaḥ ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ payo dugdhaṃ vā salilaṃ yanmudgājyapayaḥ taccāśnīyāt // GRhtCM_19.28-33:15 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, one should eat [meat from] arid regions, green gram, ghee, and milk: '<s>jāṅgala</s>' — that which belongs to an arid region, an area with sparse water and vegetation; <s>mudga</s> (green gram) is a well-known grain; ghee (<s>ājya</s>) is <s>ghṛta</s>; <s>payas</s> is milk or water — that which is green-gram-ghee-milk, one should eat that. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:15 //
And furthermore, one should eat <s>śāli</s>-rice (<s>śālyodana</s>). // GRhtCM_19.28-33:16 //
All this should be done with celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) — this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.28-33:17 //
Thus ends the procedure of essence-mica (<s>sattvābhra-kriyā</s>). // GRhtCM_19.28-33:18 //
START GRht 19.34

[Mercury] in which a quarter of mica-essence (<s>ghana-sattva</s>) has been digested, in which lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) has been digested, and in which iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) has been digested in equal measure —
is supreme for <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (body-field preparation); even an ingot (<s>āroṭa</s>) is employed again. // GRht_19.34 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now, showing the superiority of mercury in which [substances] have been digested, he states — '<s>ghana</s>' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.34:1 //

children.text: ghanasatvaṃ pādapramāṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ yasmin saḥ // GRhtCM_19.34:2 //
children.translated_text: [Mercury] in which mica-essence in quarter-proportion has been digested — that is [the compound's meaning]. // GRhtCM_19.34:2 //
'Lodestone-digested' — the meaning is: in which lodestone in quarter-proportion has been digested. // GRhtCM_19.34:3 //

children.text: punastīkṣṇaṃ samaṃ jīrṇaṃ yasminnevaṃvidho rasaḥ // GRhtCM_19.34:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) digested in equal measure in which — mercury of such quality — // GRhtCM_19.34:4 //
is supreme for <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (body-field preparation), i.e., is preeminent everywhere — this is the meaning.

children.text: baddho yaḥ khoṭatāṃ yāto dhmāto dhmātaḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: 'That which, when bound, attains ingot-form; when blown repeatedly, undergoes diminution —

children.text: khoṭo bandhaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ śīghraṃ sarvagadāpahaḥ /
children.translated_text: such an ingot-binding (<s>khoṭa-bandha</s>) should be known; it quickly removes all diseases.'
— thus in another text. // GRhtCM_19.34:5 //
START GRht 19.35
Mica-essence, lodestone, and mercury, with killed gold, accompanied by <s>śatāvarī</s> (Asparagus) juice,

children.text: ghṛtamadhulīḍhaṃ varṣānnihanti mṛtyuṃ jarāṃ caiva // GRht_19.35 //
children.translated_text: licked with ghee and honey — after a year, it destroys death and old age. // GRht_19.35 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: ghanasatvam abhrasāraḥ kāntaṃ cumbakotthaṃ sūto rasaḥ ekavadbhāvo dvandvasamāsāt tathā mṛtaṃ hema pañcatvamāptaṃ kanakaṃ ca etaccatuṣkaṃ śatāvarīrasopetaṃ śatamūlīdravabhāvitaṃ punarghṛtamadhulīḍhaṃ ghṛtamadhubhyāṃ līḍhaṃ āsvāditaṃ sat varṣādvarṣaparimāṇāt mṛtyuvyādhiṃ jarāṃ ca hanti nāśayatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.35:1 //
children.translated_text: Mica-essence (<s>ghana-sattva</s>) is the extract of mica; <s>kānta</s> is that born from the lodestone; <s>sūta</s> is mercury — these form a collective compound (<s>dvandva</s>); likewise, killed gold (<s>mṛta-hema</s>), i.e., gold reduced to the five-fold state — this fourfold [combination], accompanied by <s>śatāvarī</s> juice, i.e., saturated with the decoction of <s>śatamūlī</s> (hundred-rooted Asparagus); furthermore, licked with ghee and honey — tasted together with ghee and honey — after a year, i.e., after the duration of one year, it destroys death-disease (<s>mṛtyu-vyādhi</s>) and old age — eliminates [them], this is the meaning. // GRhtCM_19.35:1 //
START GRht 19.36
Having first prepared one formulation from among these for the purpose of <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (body-field preparation),
one should employ it for a year or half-year (<s>ayana</s>), for the attainment of supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>). // GRht_19.36 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specifics — 'of these' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.36:1 //

children.text: eṣāṃ pūrvoktānāṃ yogānāṃ madhye ādita ārambhataḥ ekaṃ yogaṃ kṛtvā niḥśreyaso mokṣaḥ tatsiddhaye niṣpattaye saṃvatsaraṃ varṣaparimāṇaṃ ayanaṃ ṣaṇmāsaparyantaṃ yojyaṃ bhoktṛṣu iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_19.36:2 //
children.translated_text: From among these aforementioned formulations, from the beginning, i.e., from the start, having prepared one formulation, for the attainment of <s>niḥśreyasa</s> — <s>niḥśreyasa</s> is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) — for its accomplishment, one should employ [the formulation] for a year, i.e., for the duration of one year, or for a half-year (<s>ayana</s>), i.e., up to six months — to the patients, this is the remainder. // GRhtCM_19.36:2 //
'Liberation (<s>mukti</s>), <s>kaivalya</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, <s>śreyas</s>, <s>niḥśreyasa</s>, <s>amṛta</s>' — [are synonyms] according to <s>Amara</s> [Kośa]. // GRhtCM_19.36:3 //
START GRht 19.37-38
With mica (<s>abhraka</s>), iron-pyrite (<s>sasya</s>), <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>rasaka</s> (zinc), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), <s>vimala</s>, diamond (<s>vajra</s>), mineral pitch (<s>girija</s>),
<s>vaikrānta</s>, lodestone (<s>kānta</s>), iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), gold (<s>hāṭaka</s>), silver (<s>tāra</s>), and copper (<s>tāmra</s>) — // GRht_19.37 //
combined or separately, in groups of two, three, or four, as available,

children.text: jīrṇahato rasendro rasāyane śasyate sadbhiḥ // GRht_19.38 //
children.translated_text: the king of mercury, killed by digestion, is recommended by the wise for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). // GRht_19.38 //
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Enumerating many [substances], he states the specifics — 'mica' and so forth. // GRhtCM_19.37-38:1 //

children.text: abhrakaḥ prasiddhaḥ sasyakaś capalaḥ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ rasakaṃ kharparaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ vimalaṃ sitamākṣikaṃ vajrakaṃ hīrakaṃ girijatu śilājatu etaiḥ // GRhtCM_19.37-38:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) is well-known; <s>sasyaka</s> is <s>capala</s> (bismuth); <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite; <s>rasaka</s> is zinc carbonate (<s>kharpara</s>); <s>darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>); <s>vimala</s> is white pyrite (<s>sitamākṣika</s>); <s>vajraka</s> is diamond (<s>hīraka</s>); <s>girijatu</s> is bitite (<s>śilājatu</s>) — with these. || GRhtCM 19.37-38:2 ||

children.text: punar vaikrāntetyādi vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ kāntaṃ lohajāti tīkṣṇaṃ sāraḥ etaiśca // GRhtCM_19.37-38:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, '<s>vaikrānta</s>' and so forth — <s>vaikrānta</s> is tourmaline (<s>vajrabhūmija</s>); <s>rajas</s> is [iron] dust; <s>kānta</s> is a type of iron; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is wrought iron (<s>sāra</s>) — with these as well. || GRhtCM 19.37-38:3 ||

children.text: hāṭakatārāratāmraiś ca hāṭakaṃ hema tāraṃ rūpyaṃ āraṃ rājarītiḥ tāmraṃ śulbaṃ etaiśca etair uddiṣṭaiḥ abhrakāditāmrāntaiḥ samastair ekatrīkṛtair vyastairvā pṛthakkṛtairvā yathālābhaṃ lābhamanatikramya bhavatīti yathālābhaṃ dvitricaturbhirvā abhrādyairjīrṇahato rasendro jīrṇābhrādīnāṃ hatiryasmin sa tathoktaḥ rasāyane jarāvyādhivināśane rasaśāstramarmajñaiḥ śasyate abhrādayaḥ praśastā uktā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.37-38:4 //
children.translated_text: And with gold (<s>hāṭaka</s>), silver (<s>tāra</s>), brass (<s>āra</s>), and copper (<s>tāmra</s>) — <s>hāṭaka</s> is gold; <s>tāra</s> is silver; <s>āra</s> is <s>rājarīti</s> (brass); <s>tāmra</s> is copper. With these, i.e., with all the enumerated [substances] from mica to copper, combined together or separately, i.e., individually, as available — not exceeding availability. The lord of mercury struck by the digested [substances] — in which there is the striking of digested mica and such — so described — is praised, i.e., is commended as excellent, by those who know the secrets of alchemical science, for the purpose of the elixir (<s>rasāyana</s>), i.e., the destruction of old age and disease — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.37-38:4 ||
A pair [of verses]. || GRhtCM 19.37-38:5 ||
Mercury struck with diamond and such, and another [mercury] equal to the struck mercury,
would be called 'chain-bound' (<s>śṛṅkhalābaddha</s>) — an agent for [transformation of] body and metal;
through its power, pervading occurs swiftly, without doubt.
Thus in another text. || GRhtCM 19.37-38:6 ||
START GRht 19.39

children.text: viṣanāgavaṅgabaddho bhukto hi rasaḥ karoti kuṣṭhādīn /
children.translated_text: Mercury bound with poison, lead, and tin, when consumed, indeed produces leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) and such diseases;

children.text: uparasabaddhe tu rase sphuṭanti bhukte tathāṅgāni // GRht_19.39 //
children.translated_text: and when mercury is bound with <s>uparasas</s> (semi-metals), when consumed, the limbs of the body burst open. || GRht 19.39 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing the despicable procedure, he says 'poison' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.39:1 ||

children.text: viṣanāgavaṅgabaddho rasaḥ viṣaṃ saktukādikaṃ nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ vaṅgaṃ trapu etairbaddho bandhanamāptaḥ sa bhuktaḥ san hi niścitaṃ kuṣṭhādīn kuṣṭhajvarakṣayādīn // GRhtCM_19.39:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury bound with poison, lead, and tin — <s>viṣa</s> (poison) means <s>saktuka</s> and such; <s>nāga</s> is lead (<s>sīsaka</s>); <s>vaṅga</s> is tin (<s>trapu</s>) — bound with these, having attained binding, that [mercury], when consumed, indeed, certainly, [produces] leprosy and such diseases — leprosy, fever, consumption, and the like. || GRhtCM 19.39:2 ||

children.text: uparasabaddhe rase uparasair gandhādibhiḥ aṣṭabhiḥ baddho bandhanam āpanno yo'sau rasaḥ tasmin bhukte sati bhokturaṅgāni hastapādādīni sphuṭanti // GRhtCM_19.39:3 //
children.translated_text: When mercury is bound with <s>uparasas</s>, i.e., the eight [semi-metals] such as sulphur and the like, [mercury] that has attained binding — when that is consumed, the limbs of the consumer — hands, feet, and the like — burst open. || GRhtCM 19.39:3 ||
START GRht 19.40-41
Of mercury that has been fed and digested with dense mica-essence, magnetic iron (<s>kānta</s>), gold (<s>kāñcī</s>), copper (<s>bhāskara</s>), and wrought iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>),

children.text: sūtasya guñjāmātrā māṣakamekaṃ parā mātrā // GRht_19.40 //
children.translated_text: one <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seed weight) is the dose; one <s>māṣaka</s> is the maximum dose. || GRht 19.40 ||
For a hundred-fold transmuter, two <s>guñjās</s>; likewise for a thousand-fold single transmuter, one <s>guñjā</s>;

children.text: ardhā ca lakṣavedhinaḥ siddhārthaḥ koṭivedhinaḥ sūtāt // GRht_19.41 //
children.translated_text: and half [a <s>guñjā</s>] for a hundred-thousand-fold transmuter; one mustard-seed [weight] from a ten-million-fold transmuting mercury. || GRht 19.41 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the dose of digested mercury, saying 'dense' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.40-41:1 ||

children.text: etaiścīrṇajīrṇaṃ pūrvaṃ cīrṇaṃ kavalitaṃ paścājjīrṇaṃ jāraṇam āpannaṃ tasya sūtasya guñjā mātrā bhakṣaṇāya guñjā yathā /
children.translated_text: With these, fed and digested — first fed, i.e., swallowed, then digested, i.e., having attained digestion — of that mercury, one <s>guñjā</s> is the dose for consumption. A <s>guñjā</s> is as follows:
One barley-grain (<s>yava</s>) equals six mustard seeds (<s>sarṣapa</s>); one <s>guñjā</s> equals three barley-grains.
Thus. || GRhtCM 19.40-41:2 ||

children.text: parā anyā mātrā anyajīrṇasūtasya mātrā māṣamekaṃ māṣako yathā /
children.translated_text: The maximum (<s>parā</s>), i.e., other, dose — the dose of differently-digested mercury — is one <s>māṣaka</s>. A <s>māṣaka</s> is as follows:
A <s>māṣaka</s> was anciently declared by <s>Brahmā</s> to be ten <s>guñjās</s>.
Thus. || GRhtCM 19.40-41:3 ||

children.text: etaiḥ kaiḥ ghanasattvakāntakāñcībhāskaratīkṣṇaiḥ abhrakasattvacumbakatāpyatāmrasārair iti // GRhtCM_19.40-41:4 //
children.translated_text: With which [substances]? With dense mica-essence, magnetic iron (<s>kānta</s>), gold-pyrite (<s>kāñcī</s>), copper (<s>bhāskara</s>), and wrought iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) — i.e., with mica-essence, magnetite, pyrite, copper, and steel. || GRhtCM 19.40-41:4 ||
Now he states the measure according to the specific type of transmutation, saying 'hundred' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.40-41:5 ||

children.text: śatavedhinaḥ sūtasya guñjāpramāṇā mātrā jñeyā tathā tena prakāreṇa sahasraikavedhinaḥ sūtasyāpi guñjāmānameva lakṣavedhinaḥ sūtāt ardhā raktikā punaḥ koṭivedhinaḥ sūtāt siddhārthaḥ sarṣapamānā // GRhtCM_19.40-41:6 //
children.translated_text: The dose of hundred-fold transmuting mercury should be known as one <s>guñjā</s> in measure. Likewise, in the same manner, the dose of thousand-and-one transmuting mercury is also one <s>guñjā</s> measure. For hundred-thousand-fold transmuting mercury, half, i.e., one <s>raktikā</s> (half <s>guñjā</s>). Furthermore, from ten-million-fold transmuting mercury, one <s>siddhārtha</s>, i.e., one mustard-seed measure. || GRhtCM 19.40-41:6 ||

children.text: śatāṃśena vedho vidyate yasmin sa śatavedhī tasya śatavedhinaḥ // GRhtCM_19.40-41:7 //
children.translated_text: 'Hundred-fold transmuter' (<s>śatavedhī</s>) — that in which transmutation exists by a hundredth part — of that hundred-fold transmuter. || GRhtCM 19.40-41:7 ||
Thus it should be understood everywhere. || GRhtCM 19.40-41:8 ||
START GRht 19.42
Mercury combined with gold, a magnetic gem (<s>kāntamaṇi</s>), and various pills (<s>guṭikās</s>) —
a person devoted to <s>japa</s> (mantra recitation), <s>homa</s> (fire offerings), and worship of the deities should wear [them]. || GRht 19.42 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: japaḥ aghorādijapaḥ homastaddaśāṃśena havanaṃ devatārcanaṃ devatānāṃ gaṇeśaviṣṇuraviśivacaṇḍīnāṃ arcanaṃ eteṣu nirataḥ saktaḥ evaṃvidhiḥ pumān // GRhtCM_19.42:1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Japa</s> means the recitation of <s>Aghora</s> and other [mantras]; <s>homa</s> means fire-offering with a tenth [of the recitation count]; worship of the deities means the worship of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Ravi</s> (Sun), <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Caṇḍī</s> — one who is devoted, i.e., engaged, in these — such a person. || GRhtCM 19.42:1 ||

children.text: iti kiṃ hemaniyojitasūtaṃ dhārayet hemnā saha niyojito miśrito yaḥ sūtaḥ taṃ kāntamaṇiḥ kāntaścāsau maṇiśca vā kāntamaṇiḥ kāntasaṃjñako maṇiḥ ca punaḥ vividhaguṭikāḥ vividhāśca tā guṭikāśceti // GRhtCM_19.42:2 //
children.translated_text: What should he wear? Mercury combined with gold — the mercury (<s>sūta</s>) that has been combined, i.e., mixed, with gold — that; and a magnetic gem (<s>kāntamaṇi</s>) — <s>kānta</s> which is itself a gem, or a gem called <s>kānta</s>; and furthermore, various pills (<s>guṭikās</s>) — various and those are pills. || GRhtCM 19.42:2 ||
START GRht 19.43-44
Food made from <s>śāli</s> (fine rice) flour, ghee (<s>ājya</s>), with <s>mudga</s> (mung beans) and meat juices,

children.text: yavagodhūmānnāni ca gokṣīraṃ mastu ca viśeṣāt // GRht_19.43 //
children.translated_text: barley and wheat foods, and cow's milk and buttermilk — especially [recommended]. || GRht 19.43 ||

children.text: pāne jalamakṣāraṃ madhurāṇi yāni kāni śastāni /
children.translated_text: For drink, water that is non-alkaline; whatever sweets are commended;
and the beverage should be taken with a delighted face, fragrant with the four spices (<s>cāturjāta</s>) and camphor (<s>karpūra</s>). || GRht 19.44 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Now he states the wholesome diet (<s>pathya</s>), saying '<s>śāli</s> rice' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.43-44:1 ||

children.text: śāleḥ ṣaṣṭikādeḥ piṣṭodbhavabhojanaṃ piṣṭakotpannaṃ ca tadbhojanaṃ ceti // GRhtCM_19.43-44:2 //
children.translated_text: Of <s>śāli</s>, i.e., <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> (sixty-day rice) and such — food produced from flour, i.e., food made from ground [grain]. || GRhtCM 19.43-44:2 ||
<s>Ājya</s> is ghee (<s>ghṛta</s>). || GRhtCM 19.43-44:3 ||

children.text: kaiḥ saha mudgamāṃsarasaiḥ saha mudgāḥ pratītāḥ atra viśeṣāt māṃsāni bhojyāni gokṣīraṃ ca bhojyaṃ punarmastu gorasasaṃbhavaṃ viśeṣāt bhojyam // GRhtCM_19.43-44:4 //
children.translated_text: With what? With <s>mudga</s> (mung beans) and meat juices. <s>Mudga</s> is well-known. Here especially, meats are to be eaten. Cow's milk is also to be consumed. Furthermore, buttermilk (<s>mastu</s>), produced from cow's milk products, is especially to be consumed. || GRhtCM 19.43-44:4 ||

children.text: pāne akṣāraṃ jalaṃ miṣṭajalaṃ prayojyaṃ punaḥ yāni kāni miṣṭāni dravyāṇi atrānuktatamāni praśastāni śreṣṭhāni punaḥ caturjātakakarpūrāmodamuditamukhaṃ yathā syāt tathā dravyaṃ peyaṃ pātavyaṃ caturjātakaṃ tvakpatrailānāgakesaraṃ karpūraṃ ghanasāraṃ eṣām āmodena parimalena muditaṃ yanmukhaṃ vāsitamukham ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.43-44:5 //
children.translated_text: For drink: non-alkaline water, i.e., sweet water, should be used. Furthermore, whatever sweet substances, those not mentioned here that are excellent. Furthermore, the beverage should be drunk with a delighted face, [fragrant] with the four spices (<s>caturjātaka</s>) — bark (<s>tvak</s>, cinnamon), leaf (<s>patra</s>, bay leaf), cardamom (<s>elā</s>), and <s>nāgakesara</s> (Mesua ferrea) — and camphor (<s>karpūra</s>), i.e., <s>ghanasāra</s>; 'delighted face' means a mouth perfumed by the fragrance of these — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.43-44:5 ||
Conversation with a young woman should be had, and body-massage by a young woman;
merely by her touch, the mercury pervades the body.
Thus the specific instruction from another text. || GRhtCM 19.43-44:6 ||
START GRht 19.45

children.text: madyāranālapānaṃ tailaṃ dadhi vā rase neṣṭam /
children.translated_text: The drinking of liquor, sour gruel (<s>āranāla</s>), oil, or curd is not desired during [mercury] elixir treatment;

children.text: kaṭutailenābhyaṅgaṃ vapuṣi na kuryādrasāyane matimān // GRht_19.45 //
children.translated_text: a wise person should not apply anointing with pungent oil upon the body during the elixir [treatment]. || GRht 19.45 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the unwholesome [things], saying 'liquor' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.45:1 ||

children.text: madyāranāletyādi madyaṃ surā āranālaṃ kāñjikaṃ tayoḥ pānaṃ neṣṭaṃ na praśastaṃ vā tailaṃ dadhi na neṣṭaṃ tailaṃ tilodbhavaṃ dadhi dugdhavikāraḥ etayorapi pānaṃ na praśastaṃ kaṭutailena sarṣapatailena vapuṣi abhyaṅgaṃ mardanaṃ na kuryāt // GRhtCM_19.45:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Liquor and sour gruel' — <s>madya</s> is wine (<s>surā</s>); <s>āranāla</s> is sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>) — the drinking of both is not desired, i.e., not recommended. Oil and curd are also not desired — oil is produced from sesame; curd is a transformation of milk — the drinking of these two is also not recommended. One should not perform anointing, i.e., massage, upon the body with pungent oil, i.e., mustard oil. || GRhtCM 19.45:2 ||
A wise person — during the elixir [treatment] as the context — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.45:3 ||
START GRht 19.46

children.text: dagdham apakvam amadhuram uṣṇaṃ kṣīraṃ na naṣṭamāṃsaṃ tu /
children.translated_text: Burnt [food], uncooked, non-sweet, hot, milk that is not [fresh], and spoiled meat —

children.text: paryuṣitaṃ phalamūlaṃ bhakṣyaṃ naivātra nirdiṣṭam // GRht_19.46 //
children.translated_text: stale fruits and roots are not prescribed here as food. || GRht 19.46 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: dagdhaṃ dravyaṃ rasāyane neṣṭaṃ apakvaṃ ca neṣṭaṃ amadhuraṃ kaṭutiktakaṣāyāmlalavaṇaṃ ca neṣṭaṃ uṣṇaṃ vahnitaptamiti tu punaḥ naṣṭamāṃsaṃ ninditamāṃsaṃ neṣṭaṃ punaḥ paryuṣitaṃ saṃdhānīkṛtaṃ evaṃvidhaṃ phalamūlaṃ phalaṃ mūlaṃ ca atra rasāyane bhakṣyaṃ na nirdiṣṭaṃ kathitaṃ /

children.translated_text: Pumpkin (<s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>), cucumber (<s>karkaṭī</s>), watermelon (<s>kaliṅga</s>), bitter gourd (<s>kāravellaka</s>),
<s>kusumbhikā</s> (safflower), spiny gourd (<s>karkoṭī</s>), banana (<s>kadalī</s>), and nightshade (<s>kākamācikā</s>) —
these eight [items beginning with] 'ka' should be avoided by one who consumes mercury.
Thus from another text. || GRhtCM 19.46:1 ||

Burnt substances are not desired during the elixir. Uncooked is also not desired. Non-sweet, i.e., pungent, bitter, astringent, sour, and salty, is also not desired. Hot, i.e., heated by fire. Furthermore, spoiled meat, i.e., condemned meat, is not desired. Furthermore, stale, i.e., fermented — such fruits and roots, i.e., fruit and root — are not prescribed, i.e., not stated, as food in this elixir [treatment].
START GRht 19.47

children.text: atha laṅghanaṃ na kāryaṃ yāmādho bhojanaṃ naiva /
children.translated_text: Now, fasting (<s>laṅghana</s>) should not be done, nor should one eat before a <s>yāma</s> (three-hour period) [has passed];

children.text: ityapanīya niṣiddhaṃ rasarāje dhīmatā kāryam // GRht_19.47 //
children.translated_text: thus, having removed the forbidden [things], the wise person should act regarding the king of mercury. || GRht 19.47 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: asmin rasāyane laṅghanaṃ na kāryaṃ punar yāmādhaḥ praharamadhye bhojanaṃ na kāryam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.47:1 //
children.translated_text: In this elixir treatment, fasting should not be done; furthermore, eating should not be done within a <s>yāma</s>, i.e., within a <s>prahara</s> (three-hour period) — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.47:1 ||
START GRht 19.48
Having abandoned worry and anger, one should bathe with pleasantly warm water;
and one should not exorcise planets (<s>grahas</s>), fevers, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), or the <s>Mātṛ</s>-goddesses. || GRht 19.48 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
That he states, saying 'having abandoned' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.48:1 ||

children.text: varjitacintākopa iti cintā ca kopaśceti cintākopau tau varjitau yena saḥ evaṃvidhaḥ san sukhāmbunā sukhoṣṇāmbunā snānaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_19.48:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned worry and anger' — worry and anger — these being abandoned by whom — such [a person]; being of such character, one should bathe with pleasantly warm water, i.e., with comfortably warm water. || GRhtCM 19.48:2 ||

children.text: graharākṣasabhūtāni noccāṭayet grahaṇādgrahāḥ piśācādayaḥ jvaro rogarājaḥ rākṣasāḥ kravyādāḥ bhūtāni devayonayaḥ etāni noccāṭayet svasthānānna cālayet // GRhtCM_19.48:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Planets, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>' — one should not exorcise them. <s>Grahas</s> (seizing spirits), seized from seizing, are <s>piśācas</s> and the like; fever is the king of diseases; <s>rākṣasas</s> are flesh-eaters; <s>bhūtas</s> are of divine origin — these one should not exorcise, i.e., should not drive from their places. || GRhtCM 19.48:3 ||

children.text: punarmātṛdevīṃśca mātaraḥ saptamātaraḥ devyo dakṣiṇyādayaḥ tā api noccāṭayet // GRhtCM_19.48:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Mātṛ-devīs</s> — the mothers, the seven mothers; the <s>devīs</s>, <s>Dakṣiṇyā</s> and others — those too one should not exorcise. || GRhtCM 19.48:4 ||
START GRht 19.49
Absorbed in the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, with a tranquil mind, having attained equanimity,
reassuring the three goals [of life], having conquered [the senses], satisfied with the bliss of the elixir. || GRht 19.49 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: cintākopanirodhe hetum āha parame ityādi // GRhtCM_19.49:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the reason for the restraint of worry and anger, saying 'in the supreme' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.49:1 ||

children.text: rasāyanakartā parame brahmaṇi citsvarūpe līnaḥ tanmayatāṃ prāpto bhavet praśāntacittaśca viṣayebhyo nivṛttamanā bhavet samatvamāpannaḥ svasute śatrau ca nirvairo yathā syāt tathā trivargaṃ dharmārthakāmarūpaṃ vijitya rasānandaparitṛpto bhavet harṣaparipūrita ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.49:2 //
children.translated_text: The practitioner of the elixir should be absorbed in the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, i.e., in the form of consciousness, having attained identity with it; and of tranquil mind, i.e., with the mind withdrawn from sense objects; having attained equanimity, i.e., without enmity toward one's own son or toward an enemy; having conquered the three goals (<s>trivarga</s>) — <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> — he should be satisfied with the bliss of the elixir, i.e., filled with delight — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.49:2 ||
START GRht 19.50

children.text: yastyaktvā śāstravidhiṃ pravartate svecchayā rase mūḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, abandoning the procedure prescribed in scripture, proceeds by his own whim regarding mercury — that fool,
from his contrary conduct, indigestion arises exceedingly. || GRht 19.50 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Showing the fixed nature of the procedure, he says 'he who' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.50:1 ||

children.text: yaḥ pumān śāstravidhiṃ tyaktvā svecchayā ucchṛṅkhalamanasā rase sūte pravartate sa mūḍhaḥ jñānaśūnyaḥ tasya puṃsaḥ viruddhācārāt nitarāmatiśayena ajīrṇam utpadyate tadrasājīrṇamiti // GRhtCM_19.50:2 //
children.translated_text: The person who, having abandoned the scriptural procedure, proceeds by his own whim, i.e., with an unrestrained mind, regarding mercury (<s>sūta</s>) — he is a fool (<s>mūḍha</s>), devoid of knowledge; for that person, from contrary conduct, exceedingly, i.e., in an extreme degree, indigestion arises — that is mercury-indigestion (<s>rasājīrṇa</s>). || GRhtCM 19.50:2 ||
START GRht 19.51
In this [mercury] indigestion, there arises: excessive sleep, laziness, fever, stupor, burning sensation,
slight pain in the region of the navel, mental dullness, loss of appetite, and body-ache. || GRht 19.51 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the characteristics of mercury-indigestion, saying 'there arises' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.51:1 ||

children.text: iha rasāyane ajīrṇaṃ yadā sambhavati utpadyate tadā etāni lakṣaṇāni syuḥ // GRhtCM_19.51:2 //
children.translated_text: In this elixir [treatment], when indigestion arises, i.e., occurs, then these symptoms would be [present]. || GRhtCM 19.51:2 ||

children.text: nidrā atiśayena nidrā ālasyaṃ aṅgāṅgaśaithilyaṃ jvaraḥ prasiddhaḥ tamo mūrchā dāha ūṣmā punarnābhitale bastau alpamalpaṃ śūlaṃ jaḍatāsyasya aruciḥ nirabhilāpitā bhaṅgo'ṅgasya aṅgamardanaṃ bhokturetāni lakṣaṇāni rasājīrṇe syur ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.51:3 //
children.translated_text: Excessive sleepiness (<s>nidrā</s>); laziness (<s>ālasya</s>), i.e., looseness of all limbs; fever (<s>jvara</s>), which is well-known; stupor (<s>tamas</s>), i.e., fainting (<s>mūrchā</s>); burning sensation (<s>dāha</s>), i.e., heat. Furthermore, in the region of the navel, i.e., in the bladder area, slight, i.e., mild pain (<s>śūla</s>); mental dullness (<s>jaḍatā</s>) of the mouth; loss of appetite (<s>aruci</s>), i.e., absence of desire; body-ache (<s>bhaṅga</s>), i.e., body-massage-like [pain] — these symptoms would be [present] for the consumer in mercury-indigestion — that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.51:3 ||
START GRht 19.52
Having recognized thus the indigestion, this regimen (<s>yoga</s>) should be employed for its concealment;

children.text: kāryo divasatritayaṃ saṃtyajya rasāyanaṃ sudhiyā // GRht_19.52 //
children.translated_text: the wise person should abstain from the elixir [treatment] for three days. || GRht 19.52 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the remedy even in indigestion, saying 'having recognized' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.52:1 ||

children.text: ityevam uktaprakāreṇa nidrādilakṣaṇenājīrṇaṃ jñātvā dhīmatā puṃsā asyājīrṇasya pracchādanāya vināśāya rasāyanaṃ saṃtyajya divasatritayaṃ yogaḥ kāryaḥ // GRhtCM_19.52:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, having recognized indigestion (<s>ajīrṇa</s>) by the previously described characteristics such as sleepiness and the like, a wise person, for the concealment, i.e., the destruction, of that indigestion — having abandoned the <s>rasāyana</s> — should perform the [corrective] formulation for three days. || GRhtCM 19.52:2 ||
[START GRht 19.53]
One should drink the root-juice of <s>karkoṭī</s> (spiny gourd), a decoction, with rock-salt (<s>sindhu</s>) for three days;
or combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt), or combined with cow's urine, in case of mercury indigestion. || GRht 19.53 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with '<s>karkoṭī</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.53:1 ||

children.text: karkoṭīmūlarasaṃ karkoṭī yā vallī tasyāḥ mūlarasaṃ tridinaṃ pibet vātha kaṣāyaṃ kathaṃ sindhunā saindhavena sahitaṃ pibet vā tatkvāthaṃ gojalasahitaṃ gomūtramilitaṃ rasājīrṇe pibet sauvarcalasahitamiti sauvarcalasya prativāpaṃ karkoṭīrase nikṣipya pibet tridinaṃ sarvatretyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.53:2 //
children.translated_text: The root-juice of <s>karkoṭī</s> — <s>karkoṭī</s> is a certain creeper (<s>vallī</s>); its root-juice — one should drink for three days. Or alternatively, a decoction — how? With <s>sindhu</s>, i.e., with rock-salt (<s>saindhava</s>) combined, one should drink. Or alternatively, that decoction combined with cow's urine (<s>gomūtra</s>), in case of mercury indigestion one should drink. 'Combined with <s>sauvarcala</s>' means: having added <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt) as an adjunct into the <s>karkoṭī</s> juice, one should drink for three days in all cases: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.53:2 ||
[START GRht 19.54]

children.text: piṣṭvātha mātuluṅgīṃ pibati rasaṃ śuṇṭhisaindhavaṃ prātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having ground <s>mātuluṅgī</s> (citron plant), one who drinks the juice with dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>) and rock-salt in the morning,

children.text: kvathitaṃ gosalilena tu rakṣati samyak rasājīrṇam // GRht_19.54 //
children.translated_text: or a decoction boiled with cow's water — it properly protects [one] in mercury indigestion. || GRht 19.54 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states another [remedy], beginning with 'having ground' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.54:1 ||

children.text: mātuluṅgasyeyaṃ jaṭā mātuluṅgī tāṃ piṣṭvā tasyā rasaṃ śuṇṭhī saindhavaṃ ca yaḥ pumān prātaḥ pibati tu punaḥ kvathitaṃ tasyāḥ kaṣāyaṃ gosalilena yaḥ pibati rasājīrṇe taṃ puruṣaṃ rakṣati na vināśayatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.54:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mātuluṅgī</s> is the fibrous root of the citron (<s>mātuluṅga</s>). Having ground that, its juice together with dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>) and rock-salt — the person who drinks [this] in the morning; and furthermore, a decoction, i.e., a boiled extract (<s>kaṣāya</s>) of that, with cow's water — whoever drinks [this] in mercury indigestion, it protects that person, i.e., does not destroy [him]: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.54:2 ||
[START GRht 19.55]
If somehow, through ignorance, mercury tainted with lead (<s>nāga</s>) and the like has been consumed,
for its expulsion one should drink cow's urine, bitter gourd (<s>kaṭukā</s>), and <s>āravallī</s> roots. || GRht 19.55 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the remedy for one who has consumed mercury combined with lead and the like, beginning with 'somehow' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.55:1 ||

children.text: ca punaḥ yat yasmāt nāgādikalaṅkito rasaḥ nāgavaṅgasahito raso'jñānātkathamapi bhuktaḥ tannodanāya tasya nāgavaṅgāṅkitarasasya nodanāya gojalakaṭukāravalliśiphāḥ gojalaṃ gomūtraṃ kaṭutiktā kāravallīśiphā kāravallīlatāyāḥ śiphā jaṭā etadauṣadhaṃ pibet tena nāgavaṅgādidoṣo vinaśyati // GRhtCM_19.55:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, since mercury tainted by lead and the like — mercury combined with lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) — through ignorance, somehow has been consumed — for its expulsion, i.e., for the expulsion of that lead-and-tin-tainted mercury — one should drink cow's urine (<s>gojala</s>), i.e., cow's urine (<s>gomūtra</s>), bitter gourd (<s>kaṭutiktā</s>), and <s>kāravallī</s> roots, i.e., the fibrous roots (<s>śiphā</s>) of the <s>kāravallī</s> creeper. By this medicine, the defect of lead, tin, and the like is destroyed. || GRhtCM 19.55:2 ||
[START GRht 19.56]
<s>Śarapuṅkhā</s> (Tephrosia purpurea), <s>suradālī</s> (Luffa), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>bimbī</s> (Coccinia), and <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade) —

children.text: ekatamā ceduditā śṛtāmajīrṇe hi seveta // GRht_19.56 //
children.translated_text: whichever one of these is prescribed, when decocted, one should take it in indigestion. || GRht 19.56 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with '<s>śarapuṅkhā</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.56:1 ||

children.text: āsāṃ auṣadhīnāṃ madhye ekatamā yā uditā kathitā śṛtā kvathitā tāṃ hi niścitaṃ ajīrṇe seveta tena ajīrṇaṃ naśyatīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_19.56:2 //
children.translated_text: Among these medicines, whichever one is prescribed, i.e., recommended, when decocted, i.e., when boiled — that one should certainly be taken in indigestion; thereby indigestion is destroyed: this is the purport. || GRhtCM 19.56:2 ||

children.text: tāḥ kā auṣadhyaḥ śarapuṅkhā prasiddhā suradālī devadālī paṭolaṃ pratītaṃ nāma bimbī golā kākamācī prasiddhā etā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.56:3 //
children.translated_text: What are those medicines? <s>Śarapuṅkhā</s> is well-known; <s>suradālī</s> is <s>devadālī</s> (Luffa); <s>paṭola</s> is well-known by name; <s>bimbī</s> is <s>golā</s> (Coccinia grandis); <s>kākamācī</s> is well-known — these: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.56:3 ||
[START GRht 19.57]
By excessively sour, salty, and pungent [foods], mercury overflows (<s>saṃsrāva</s>) and aging (<s>jara</s>) occurs;
and by excessively sweet [foods] consumed constantly, the digestive fire (<s>jaṭharavahni</s>) is destroyed. || GRht 19.57 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states that, beginning with 'excessively sour' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.57:1 ||

children.text: atyamlaṃ cukrādi atilavaṇaṃ kṣārādi atikaṭukaṃ nimbakaṭukītyādi etai rasasaṃsrāvo jaro jāraṇakaro bhavati jaratīti jaraḥ // GRhtCM_19.57:2 //
children.translated_text: Excessively sour means tamarind (<s>cukra</s>) and the like; excessively salty means alkalis (<s>kṣāra</s>) and the like; excessively pungent means neem, <s>kaṭukī</s> (picrorhiza) and the like — by these, there is mercury overflow (<s>saṃsrāva</s>) and aging (<s>jara</s>), i.e., one becomes an agent of aging: '<s>jarati</s> therefore <s>jara</s>.' || GRhtCM 19.57:2 ||

children.text: punarapi madhuraiḥ ikṣurasādibhiḥ satatabhuktaiḥ jaṭharavahniḥ koṣṭhāgniḥ vinaśyati abhyāśrayo vinaśyatītyabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_19.57:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, by sweet [foods] — sugarcane juice and the like — constantly consumed, the digestive fire (<s>jaṭharavahni</s>), i.e., the abdominal fire (<s>koṣṭhāgni</s>), is destroyed; the intended meaning is that its support is destroyed. || GRhtCM 19.57:3 ||
[START GRht 19.58]

children.text: yaḥ punarevaṃ satataṃ karoti mūḍhaḥ samāhāram /
children.translated_text: The foolish one who constantly partakes of such a diet,

children.text: tasya vinaśyatyagnirna khalu krāmati raso bhaved vyādhiḥ // GRht_19.58 //
children.translated_text: his fire is destroyed; mercury indeed does not pervade, and disease results. || GRht 19.58 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the specific consequence, beginning with 'who' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.58:1 ||

children.text: yaḥ punar mūḍho mūrkho 'jīrṇānantaraṃ atyamlalavaṇakaṭukāhāraṃ satataṃ nirantaraṃ karoti tasyāgniḥ koṣṭhāgnir vinaśyati rasaśca na krāmati svaguṇānna prakāśayati // GRhtCM_19.58:2 //
children.translated_text: The foolish (<s>mūḍha</s>), i.e., ignorant person, who after indigestion constantly, i.e., without interruption, partakes of an excessively sour, salty, and pungent diet — his fire, i.e., abdominal fire (<s>koṣṭhāgni</s>), is destroyed; and mercury does not pervade, i.e., does not manifest its qualities. || GRhtCM 19.58:2 ||

children.text: tarhi kiṃ bhavedityāha vyādhirbhaved ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.58:3 //
children.translated_text: Then what would happen? He answers: disease would result — this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.58:3 ||
[START GRht 19.59]
But one who, by tolerance of the great fire, from mercury [achieves] the power to transmute hundreds, thousands, and <s>lakṣas</s> —

children.text: anayā kriyayā sidhyati sa yatnādrasakriyāyogāt // GRht_19.59 //
children.translated_text: that [mercury] is perfected by this procedure, through effort, by the method of mercury-operations. || GRht 19.59 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: rasācchatasahasralakṣavedhī bhavet sa yatnāt anayā pūrvoktakriyayā sidhyati // GRhtCM_19.59:1 //
children.translated_text: From mercury, one becomes a transmuter of hundreds, thousands, and <s>lakṣas</s> — that [mercury] is perfected through effort by this previously stated procedure. || GRhtCM 19.59:1 ||
[START GRht 19.60]
A transmuter of hundreds, thousands, <s>lakṣas</s>, <s>koṭis</s>, and then <s>arbuda</s> and <s>nirbuda</s> as well —

children.text: piṣṭaṃ bhuñjīta rasaṃ balisahitaṃ siddhido bhavati // GRht_19.60 //
children.translated_text: one should consume mercury ground and combined with <s>bali</s> (sulphur); it becomes a bestower of <s>siddhi</s>. || GRht 19.60 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the characteristics by the further procedure, beginning with 'hundred' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.60:1 ||
Mercury that transmutes hundreds, thousands, and <s>lakṣas</s> — || GRhtCM 19.60:2 ||

children.text: balisahitaṃ piṣṭaṃ rasaṃ bhuñjīta balinā gandhakena sahitam śatādārabhya sahasralakṣakoṭyarbudānāṃ krameṇa daśaguṇottaraṃ saṃkhyā jñātavyā // GRhtCM_19.60:3 //
children.translated_text: One should consume ground mercury combined with <s>bali</s>, i.e., with sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>). The numerical sequence from hundreds through thousands, <s>lakṣas</s>, <s>koṭis</s>, and <s>arbudas</s> should be understood as increasing tenfold in progression. || GRhtCM 19.60:3 ||

children.text: evaṃ kṛtaḥ san rasaḥ siddhido yathoktaguṇakṛdbhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.60:4 //
children.translated_text: Mercury thus prepared becomes a bestower of <s>siddhi</s>, i.e., producing the stated qualities: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.60:4 ||
[START GRht 19.61-64]

children.text: krāmati tato hi sūto janayati putrāṃśca devagarbhābhān /
children.translated_text: Then indeed mercury pervades, and [the practitioner] begets sons resembling divine embryos;

children.text: strīṣu ca niścalakāmo bhavati valīpalitanirmuktaḥ // GRht_19.61 //
children.translated_text: among women, [his] desire becomes unwavering; he becomes free from wrinkles and grey hair. || GRht 19.61 ||

children.text: buddhirbalaṃ prabhāvaḥ saha cāyuṣā vardhate rasāyaninaḥ /
children.translated_text: Intelligence, strength, and power increase together with the lifespan of the <s>rasāyanin</s> (practitioner of rejuvenation);

children.text: prāptasya divyabuddhiṃ divyāśca guṇāḥ pravardhante // GRht_19.62 //
children.translated_text: of one who has attained divine intellect, divine qualities flourish. || GRht 19.62 ||
Thus, one perfected through mercury, free from suffering, old age, and death, endowed with [all] virtues,

children.text: khegamanena ca nityaṃ saṃcarate sakalabhuvaneṣu // GRht_19.63 //
children.translated_text: by sky-walking (<s>khecara</s> movement), perpetually wanders through all the worlds. || GRht 19.63 ||
A giver in the three worlds, a creator like <s>Brahmā</s> (the Lotus-born) himself,
a sustainer like <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and a destroyer like <s>Rudra</s>. || GRht 19.64 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Praising the previous procedure, he says, beginning with 'pervades' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:1 ||

children.text: tataḥ pūrvavidhānataḥ sūtaḥ krāmati svaguṇān prakāśayati sūte krāmati sati devagarbhābhān putrān janayati devagarbhavat ābhā kāntir yeṣāṃ te tān punaḥ strīṣu niścalaḥ sadāsthāyī kāmo ratyabhilāṣo vā madano yasya sa tathoktaḥ punar valīpalitanirmuktaḥ valyaśca palitāni ca tair nirmukto vivarjitaḥ valiścarma jarākṛtaṃ ityamaraḥ palitaṃ keśaśvetatvaṃ evaṃvidho bhavati pumān iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_19.61-64:2 //
children.translated_text: Then, by the previous procedure, mercury pervades, i.e., manifests its qualities. When mercury pervades, [the practitioner] begets sons resembling divine embryos — sons whose radiance (<s>ābhā</s>) is like that of divine embryos; furthermore, among women, unwavering, i.e., perpetually enduring, desire (<s>kāma</s>), i.e., passion for love-making, or <s>Madana</s> — one who is such is so described; furthermore, free from wrinkles and grey hair — wrinkles and grey hair, freed from those, i.e., devoid [of them]; wrinkles are the skin-folds caused by old age, as per <s>Amara</s> [dictionary]; grey hair is the whitening of head-hair — such a person becomes: this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:2 ||
Furthermore, what else would occur? He says, beginning with 'intelligence' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:3 ||

children.text: rasāyaninaḥ rasāyanaṃ prāptasya hi puṃsaḥ buddhirvardhate balaṃ ca vardhate kena saha āyuṣā jīvitakālena saha punar divyabuddhiṃ prāptasya rasāyaninaḥ divyāḥ prakaraṇādguṇā medhādayaḥ pravardhante prakāśanta ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.61-64:4 //
children.translated_text: Of the <s>rasāyanin</s>, i.e., the person who has obtained <s>rasāyana</s> — intelligence increases, and strength increases — with what? Together with lifespan, i.e., with the duration of life; furthermore, of the <s>rasāyanin</s> who has attained divine intellect, divine qualities — by context, [such as] memory (<s>medhā</s>) and the like — flourish, i.e., manifest: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:4 ||
He states that, beginning with 'thus' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:5 ||

children.text: evamamunā prakāreṇa rasasaṃsiddhaḥ puruṣaḥ rasaḥ pāradaḥ saṃsiddhaḥ samyak siddho yasya vā rasena saṃsiddhaḥ jarāmaraṇavarjito bhavati vṛddhatvavyādhirahita ityarthaḥ guṇavāṃśca bhavati guṇā medhādayaḥ // GRhtCM_19.61-64:6 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method, the person perfected through mercury — mercury, i.e., <s>pārada</s>, is perfected, i.e., fully accomplished, for him; or, one perfected through mercury — becomes free from old age and death, i.e., devoid of decrepitude and disease: this is the meaning; and becomes endowed with virtues, i.e., qualities such as memory (<s>medhā</s>) and the like. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:6 ||

children.text: punaḥ khegamanena ākāśagamanena nityaṃ sakalabhuvaneṣu samastalokeṣu saṃcarate ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.61-64:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, by sky-walking (<s>khecara</s>), i.e., by movement through the sky (<s>ākāśagamana</s>), he perpetually wanders through all the worlds, i.e., through all the realms (<s>lokas</s>): this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:7 ||

children.text: dātā bhuvanatritaye svargamṛtyupātāle bhavati sarvādhika ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_19.61-64:8 //
children.translated_text: A giver in the three worlds — in heaven, the mortal realm, and the netherworld — he becomes supreme over all: this is the intent. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:8 ||

children.text: so'pi pumān iha bhuvanatritaye svargamṛtyupātāle sraṣṭā sarjako bhavati // GRhtCM_19.61-64:9 //
children.translated_text: That person, here in the three worlds — heaven, the mortal realm, and the netherworld — becomes a creator (<s>sraṣṭṛ</s>), a maker. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:9 ||
Like whom? Like the Lotus-born (<s>Padmayoni</s>), i.e., like <s>Brahmā</s>. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:10 ||

children.text: punaḥ bhartā pālanārthaṃ trikasya viṣṇuriva ca bhavati // GRhtCM_19.61-64:11 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, he becomes a sustainer (<s>bhartṛ</s>) of the triad, like <s>Viṣṇu</s>. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:11 ||

children.text: punaḥ saṃhartā rudravat bhavati sṛṣṭisthitivināśeṣu brahmādīnāṃ trayīva syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.61-64:12 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, he becomes a destroyer (<s>saṃhartṛ</s>) like <s>Rudra</s>. In creation, sustenance, and dissolution, he would be like the triad of <s>Brahmā</s> and the others: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.61-64:12 ||
[START GRht 19.65-66]
<<s>Amarasundarī Guṭikā</s> (Immortal-Beauty Pill)>
Loadstone (<s>kānta</s>), mica-essence (<s>abhrasattva</s>), gold (<s>hema</s>), silver (<s>tāra</s>), and copper (<s>arka</s>) — in equal parts by measure;

children.text: baddhaṃ sūtasamāṃśaṃ dhmātaṃ golaṃ kṛtaṃ khoṭam // GRht_19.65 //
children.translated_text: bound mercury in equal parts — blown [in a crucible], made into a ball, forming an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>). || GRht 19.65 ||

children.text: bāhye rasena liptaṃ vadanagataṃ śastravārakaṃ rogān /
children.translated_text: On the outside smeared with mercury, placed in the mouth, it repels weapons;

children.text: hanti hi śarīrasaṃsthān nāmnāmarasundarī guṭikā // GRht_19.66 //
children.translated_text: it destroys diseases residing in the body — [this is] the pill called <s>Amarasundarī</s> (Immortal Beauty). || GRht 19.66 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure and qualities of the <s>Amarasundarī Guṭikā</s>, beginning with '<s>kānta</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.65-66:1 ||
<s>Kānta</s> is loadstone (<s>cumbaka</s>); <s>abhra</s> is mica (the pair). || GRhtCM 19.65-66:2 ||

children.text: abhrakasattvaṃ pratītaṃ hema kanakaṃ tāraṃ ca tat ekavadbhāvo dvandvatvāt punararkaḥ tāmram eṣāṃ kāntādīnāṃ saṃkhyā gaṇanā samāṃśataḥ samabhāgato jñeyā // GRhtCM_19.65-66:3 //
children.translated_text: Mica-essence (<s>abhrakasattva</s>) is well-known; <s>hema</s> is gold (<s>kanaka</s>); and <s>tāra</s> (silver) — these being treated as a singular compound due to their <s>dvandva</s> nature; furthermore, <s>arka</s> is copper (<s>tāmra</s>). Of these — <s>kānta</s> and the rest — the measure (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), i.e., the enumeration, should be understood as from equal parts (<s>samabhāga</s>). || GRhtCM 19.65-66:3 ||

children.text: punaḥ sūtasamāṃśaṃ pāradena tulyabhāgaṃ dhmātaṃ kuryāt andhamūṣāyāṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_19.65-66:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in equal parts with mercury (<s>pārada</s>), i.e., in equal proportion — it should be blown in a blind crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>): this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 19.65-66:4 ||

children.text: kiṃkṛtaṃ sat bāhye baddhagolopari rasena māraṇāyām uktadraveṇa liptaṃ sat dhmātaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_19.65-66:5 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? On the outside, i.e., on top of the bound ball (<s>baddha-gola</s>), smeared with mercury, i.e., with the liquid prescribed for calcination — it should be blown. || GRhtCM 19.65-66:5 ||

children.text: itthaṃ kṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ piṣṭistambhaḥ golākāraṃ bhavati // GRhtCM_19.65-66:6 //
children.translated_text: Thus made, the ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>), i.e., the solidified mass, becomes ball-shaped. || GRhtCM 19.65-66:6 ||

children.text: tat vadanagataṃ mukhāntaḥsthitaṃ śastravārakaṃ syāt asmiṃśca vadanaṃ gate sati śarīre khaḍgādīnāṃ prahāro na lagati // GRhtCM_19.65-66:7 //
children.translated_text: That, placed in the mouth, i.e., situated inside the mouth, would repel weapons — and when it is placed in the mouth, the blows of swords and the like do not strike the body. || GRhtCM 19.65-66:7 ||

children.text: guṭir iyaṃ nāmnā abhidhānena amarasundarīguṭikā jñeyā // GRhtCM_19.65-66:8 //
children.translated_text: This pill, by name, i.e., by designation, should be known as the <s>Amarasundarī Guṭikā</s> (Immortal Beauty Pill). || GRhtCM 19.65-66:8 ||

children.text: iyaṃ śarīrasthā mukhe anyasthale vā sthitā satī śarīrasthān rogān hanti vināśayati // GRhtCM_19.65-66:9 //
children.translated_text: This [pill], residing in the body — situated in the mouth or in another place — destroys diseases residing in the body, i.e., annihilates [them]. || GRhtCM 19.65-66:9 ||
Although the measure is not stated, it should be understood as five <s>niṣkas</s> in weight: this is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.65-66:10 ||
Thus [ends] the <s>Amarasundarī Guṭikā</s>. || GRhtCM 19.65-66:11 ||

children.text: hemnā vā rajatena vāpi sahito dhmāto vrajatyekatāmakṣīṇo niviḍo guḍaśca guṭikāḥ karoti dīrghojjvalāḥ // GRhtCM_19.65-66:12 //
children.translated_text: Combined with gold or indeed with silver, blown, it attains unity — imperishable, dense, and [like] jaggery — it produces pills that are long and lustrous. || GRhtCM 19.65-66:12 ||

children.text: cūrṇaṃ tatpaṭuvatprayāti vihitaghṛṣṭo na muñcenmalaṃ nirgandho dravati kṣaṇātsa hi mato baddhābhidhāno rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Its powder moves about like salt; when rubbed, it does not release impurity; it is odorless and melts in an instant — that is considered mercury bearing the designation 'bound.' ||
Thus from another treatise. || GRhtCM 19.65-66:13 ||
[START GRht 19.67-72]
<<s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī Guṭikā</s> (Dead-Reviving Pill)>

children.text: yaḥ pūrvoktaḥ sūto lakṣādūrdhvaṃ ca vedhate lohān /
children.translated_text: The mercury described previously, which transmutes metals beyond a <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred thousand) —

children.text: baddhe sāraṇayogair mukhāsthe ca jārayedratnam // GRht_19.67 //
children.translated_text: when bound, through <s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing) methods, and placed in the mouth, one should assimilate a gem [into it]. || GRht 19.67 ||
Combined with equal parts of lead (<s>nāga</s>), and with essences of celestial metal (<s>suralohā</s>), iron (<s>ayas</s>), loadstone (<s>kānta</s>), and <s>tāpya</s> —
combined with mica-essence — [this is] the pill named <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s> (Reviver of the Dead). || GRht 19.68 ||

children.text: hemayutā gulucchake mukuṭe vā kaṇṭhasūtrakarṇe vā /
children.translated_text: Combined with gold, [placed] on a topknot or a crown, or on a neck-cord or ear —
[it wards off] the aggregate of death, fear, grief, disease, poison, weapons, old age, and constant suffering. || GRht 19.69 ||
One on whose body this pill named <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s> is placed —
he becomes most honored by <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Siddha</s>-lords of <s>Yoga</s>. || GRht 19.70 ||

children.text: prakṣālya toyamadhye guṭikā ghaṭikādvayaṃ tataḥ kṣiptvā /
children.translated_text: Having washed [the pill] and placing it in water for two <s>ghaṭikās</s> (48 minutes), then
this [pill], placed in the mouth [of a dead person], effects the revival (<s>utthāpana</s>) of the dead. || GRht 19.71 ||

children.text: toyaṃ tadeva pibati svasthaṃ pathyānvitastataḥ puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The person who drinks that very water [in which the pill was washed], being healthy and following a wholesome diet (<s>pathyānvita</s>) —

children.text: labhate divyaṃ sa vapurmṛtyujarāvarjitaḥ sudṛḍham // GRht_19.72 //
children.translated_text: attains a divine body, firm, free from death and old age. || GRht 19.72 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure and qualities of the <s>mṛtasaṃjīvanī guṭikā</s> (pill that revives the dead), beginning with 'that which' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.67-72:1 ||

children.text: yaḥ pūrvoktaḥ sūto lakṣādūrdhvaṃ koṭyarbudādi lohān rūpyādīn vedhate tasminbaddhe sūte mukhasthe prakāśamukhayantre sthāpite sāraṇayogaiḥ sāraṇatailādibhiḥ ratnaṃ vajrādikaṃ jārayet // GRhtCM_19.67-72:2 //
children.translated_text: That previously described mercury, which transmutes metals — silver and others — beyond one <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred thousand), up to <s>koṭi</s>, <s>arbuda</s>, and so forth: in that bound mercury, when placed in an open-mouth apparatus (<s>prakāśamukha-yantra</s>), with <s>sāraṇa</s> agents such as <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil, gems (<s>ratna</s>) such as diamond should be assimilated. || GRhtCM 19.67-72:2 ||

children.text: punaḥ samāṃśanāgais tulyāṃśasīsakaiḥ sūto yuktaḥ kāryaḥ suralohāyaskāntatāpyasattvaiśca yuktaḥ kāryaḥ suralohaṃ kanakaṃ ayaskāntaḥ kāntalohaṃ tāpyasattvaṃ mākṣikasāraṃ etaiḥ abhrakasattvasametā satī mṛtasaṃjīvanī nāma guṭikā bhavati punastatra mūṣāyāmiyaṃ hemayutā kāryā // GRhtCM_19.67-72:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, mercury should be combined with lead in equal portions — equal amounts of lead; and should be combined with the essences of divine metal (<s>suraloha</s>, i.e., gold), loadstone (<s>ayaskānta</s>), and pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>). <s>Suraloha</s> is gold; <s>ayaskānta</s> is magnetic iron; <s>tāpyasattva</s> is the essence of copper-pyrite. With these, together with mica-essence, the pill called <s>mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s> (reviver of the dead) comes into being. Furthermore, in that crucible, this [pill] should be made combined with gold. || GRhtCM 19.67-72:3 ||

children.text: punar iyaṃ guṭikā nityaṃ yasya gulucchake nihitā bhavati vā mukuṭe kirīṭe vā kaṇṭhasūtrakarṇe kaṇṭhasūtraṃ ca karṇaśca kaṇṭhasūtrakarṇaṃ tasmin vā aṅge hastapādādau tasya mṛtyubhayaśokarogaśastrajarāsatataduḥkhasaṃghātaṃ naśyati ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_19.67-72:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, this pill — for whomever it is constantly placed in a topknot (<s>gulucchaka</s>), or in a crown (<s>mukuṭa</s>), or on a necklace-and-ear [ornament] (<s>kaṇṭhasūtra</s> means necklace, <s>karṇa</s> means ear), or on any limb such as the hand, foot, and so forth — death, fear, sorrow, disease, weapons, old age, and the constant mass of suffering are destroyed: this is to be supplied. || GRhtCM 19.67-72:4 ||

children.text: eteṣu sthāneṣu yasyeyaṃ nihitā sthāpitā bhavati sa asurayakṣakinnarapūjyatamaḥ asurā daityāḥ yakṣā devayonayaḥ kinnarāḥ turaṅgavaktrāḥ teṣāṃ pūjyatamo bhavati atiśayena pūjyaḥ pūjyatamaḥ // GRhtCM_19.67-72:5 //
children.translated_text: For whomever this [pill] is placed — deposited — in those [aforementioned] locations, he becomes most worshipped by <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s>. <s>Asuras</s> are demons (<s>Daityas</s>); <s>Yakṣas</s> are semi-divine beings; <s>Kinnaras</s> are horse-faced [celestials]. He becomes most worshipped by them — exceedingly venerable. || GRhtCM 19.67-72:5 ||

children.text: siddhayogīndraiḥ pūjyatamaḥ siddhā devaviśeṣāḥ yogīndrā nāgārjunādayaḥ tato'nantaraṃ mṛtajīvanī jalamadhye kṣiptvā prakṣālya ghaṭikādvayaṃ vadanagatā satī mṛtakasya puruṣasyotthāpanaṃ prabodhanaṃ kurute yaḥ pumān puruṣaḥ tadeva toyaṃ guṭikākṣālanaṃ svacchaṃ nirmalaṃ pibati kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ pathyānvito hitāvahadravyabhakṣaṇayuktaḥ sa puruṣo divyaṃ vapuḥ devaśarīraṃ labhate kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ divyaṃ punaḥ mṛtyujarāvarjitaṃ vyādhipālityarahitaṃ punaḥ sudṛḍhaṃ vajravad guṭikāparimāṇaṃ pākavidhānaṃ ca pūrvavad ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.67-72:6 //
children.translated_text: Most worshipped by <s>Siddhas</s> and lords of <s>Yogins</s> — <s>Siddhas</s> are particular deities; lords of <s>Yogins</s> are <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and others. Then, after that, having placed the <s>mṛtajīvanī</s> (life-restorer) in water and washed it, for two <s>ghaṭikās</s>, when placed in the mouth, it effects the revival — the awakening — of the dead person. The man who drinks that very water — the washing-water of the pill — which is clear, pure — of what character? Following a wholesome diet (<s>pathyānvita</s>) — one endowed with the consumption of beneficial substances — that person attains a divine body, a body fit for the gods. Of what character is the divine [body]? Free from death and old age — free from disease and greying. Furthermore, very firm — like a thunderbolt. The size of the pill and the cooking procedure are as before: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.67-72:6 ||
Thus [ends] the <s>mṛtajīvanī guṭikā</s> (pill that restores the dead to life). || GRhtCM 19.67-72:7 ||
[START GRht 19.73-74]
<<s>Vajriṇī guṭikā</s> (diamond pill)>

children.text: kāntaghanasattvakamalaṃ hema ca tāraṃ yathā kṛtadvandvam /
children.translated_text: The essences of loadstone (<s>kānta</s>) and mica (<s>ghana</s>), copper (<s>kamala</s>), gold (<s>hema</s>), and silver (<s>tāra</s>), properly paired (<s>dvandva</s>) —

children.text: samajīrṇaṃ bījavaraṃ vajrayutaṃ vajriṇī guṭikā // GRht_19.73 //
children.translated_text: equally assimilated as a supreme <s>bīja</s>, combined with diamond (<s>vajra</s>): [this is] the <s>vajriṇī guṭikā</s> (diamond pill). || GRht 19.73 ||
This [pill], placed in the mouth-cavity, creates strength equal to nine young elephants;
and that body [of its bearer] becomes impenetrable, freed from death, old age, and disease. || GRht 19.74 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure and qualities of the <s>vajriṇī guṭikā</s>, beginning with '<s>kānta</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.73-74:1 ||

children.text: kāntaṃ ca ghanaṃ ca anayoḥ sattvaṃ kāntaghanasattvaṃ kāntasattvaṃ cumbakasattvaṃ ghanasattvaṃ abhrakasāraṃ kamalaṃ ceti kamalaṃ tāmraṃ ca punarhema svarṇaṃ tāraṃ ca rūpyaṃ pūrvavat yathā yena vidhānena kṛtadvandvaṃ kṛtaṃ ca tat dvandvaṃ ceti bījavaraṃ samajīrṇaṃ kāryaṃ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ bījavaraṃ vajrayutaṃ hīrakayutam iyaṃ guṭikā nāmato vajriṇī punareṣā vajriṇīguṭikā mukhakuharagatā satī mukhāntaḥprāptā satī navanāgatulyabalaṃ navasaṃkhyākā nāgāḥ hastinastaistulyaṃ tatsamaṃ yadbalaṃ tatkurute tadvapustasya mukhe guṭikādhāriṇo vapuḥ śarīraṃ durbhedyaṃ duḥkhena bhettuṃ śakyaṃ punarmṛtyujarāvyādhibhir nirmuktam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.73-74:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> and <s>ghana</s> — the essence of these two: <s>kāntasattva</s> is loadstone-essence; <s>ghanasattva</s> is mica-extract. <s>Kamala</s> is copper; and furthermore, <s>hema</s> is gold, <s>tāra</s> is silver. As before, by which procedure [they are] properly paired — 'made and that pair': a supreme <s>bīja</s>, equally assimilated, should be prepared. Of what character? The supreme <s>bīja</s> combined with diamond (<s>hīraka</s>). This pill is called <s>vajriṇī</s> by name. Furthermore, this <s>vajriṇī guṭikā</s>, when placed in the mouth-cavity — when it has entered inside the mouth — creates strength equal to nine young elephants — nine in number are the <s>nāgas</s> (elephants); equal to them, meaning the same as theirs, is the strength: that it creates. The body of that person — the one who bears the pill in his mouth — becomes impenetrable (<s>durbhedya</s>) — difficult to pierce. Furthermore, freed from death, old age, and disease — free from sickness and greying: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.73-74:2 ||
Thus [ends] the <s>vajriṇī guṭikā</s>. || GRhtCM 19.73-74:3 ||
[START GRht 19.75-76]
<<s>Khecarī guṭikā</s> (sky-roaming pill)>
In mercury that has been [processed with] smoke-transmutation, assimilated with the five great gems, and flowed (<s>sārita</s>) —
with a <s>bīja</s> combined with pyrite and loadstone, in mica-essence — || GRht 19.75 ||
the pill named <s>khecarī</s> (sky-roaming) — the mere moment it is placed in the mouth, it activates;
one becomes most worshipped by the hosts of gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Siddhas</s>, including <s>Indra</s> and others. || GRht 19.76 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
He states the procedure and qualities of the <s>khecarī guṭikā</s>, beginning with '<s>dhūma</s>' (smoke) and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.75-76:1 ||

children.text: dhūmāvalokite dhūmavedhini rase sūte pañcamahāratnajārite pañcasaṃkhyākair mahāratnair vajrādibhiḥ tathā ca /
children.translated_text: In mercury that has undergone smoke-transmutation (<s>dhūmavedha</s>), assimilated with the five great gems — the five in number, the great gems beginning with diamond. And thus:

children.text: vajraṃ ca mauktikaṃ caiva māṇikyaṃ nīlameva ca /
children.translated_text: Diamond, pearl, ruby, sapphire,
and emerald — these are known as the five great gems.
Thus. || GRhtCM 19.75-76:2 ||

children.text: punar mākṣikakāntaprayuktena tāpyacumbakamilitena bījena rase gaganasattve sārite sati khecarasaṃjñā guṭikā bhavati // GRhtCM_19.75-76:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with a <s>bīja</s> combined with pyrite and loadstone — combined with <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) and <s>cumbaka</s> (loadstone) — when mercury has been flowed (<s>sārita</s>) in mica-essence, the pill named <s>khecarī</s> (sky-roaming) comes into being. || GRhtCM 19.75-76:3 ||

children.text: tasmin guṭikārūpe rase kṣiptamātreṇa mukhe patati sati indrādyaiḥ devāsurasiddhagaṇaiśca pūjyatamo bhavati indro maghavā ādyo yeṣāṃ te taiḥ // GRhtCM_19.75-76:4 //
children.translated_text: In that mercury in the form of a pill, the mere moment it is placed in the mouth — when it has arrived inside the mouth — [one becomes] most worshipped by <s>Indra</s> and others, and by the hosts of gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Siddhas</s>. <s>Indra</s>, that is <s>Maghavā</s>, is the first among those: by those. || GRhtCM 19.75-76:4 ||

children.text: devā amarāḥ asurāḥ daityāḥ siddhā devaviśeṣāḥ teṣāṃ ye gaṇāḥ samūhāḥ taiḥ kṛtvā atiśayena pūjyo bhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.75-76:5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Devas</s> are the immortals; <s>Asuras</s> are the demons (<s>Daityas</s>); <s>Siddhas</s> are particular deities; their hosts — assemblies — by those, having [the pill], one becomes exceedingly worshipped: that is the meaning. || GRhtCM 19.75-76:5 ||
Thus [ends] the pill named <s>khecarī</s>. || GRhtCM 19.75-76:6 ||
[START GRht 19.77]
The science of mercury (<s>rasavāda</s>) is of infinite virtues, through the divisions of liquid, ball, and paste;

children.text: kalitaḥ pradhānasiddhairyair dṛṣṭaste jayanti narāḥ // GRht_19.77 //
children.translated_text: fashioned by the foremost <s>Siddhas</s> — those men by whom it was seen, they triumph. || GRht 19.77 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
Indicating the infinitude of the science of mercury, he says beginning with '<s>rasa</s>' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.77:1 ||

children.text: rasavādo 'nantaguṇaḥ anantā guṇā yasya sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_19.77:2 //
children.translated_text: The science of mercury is of infinite virtues — that which has infinite virtues is so called. || GRhtCM 19.77:2 ||
'Infinite' means unlimited. || GRhtCM 19.77:3 ||

children.text: kena kṛtvā rasavādo'nantaḥ dravagolakakalkānāṃ pratyekamanantatvāt rasavādo'pyanantaḥ // GRhtCM_19.77:4 //
children.translated_text: By what [reason] is the science of mercury infinite? Because of the individual infinitude of the liquid, ball, and paste [forms of mercury], the science of mercury too is infinite. || GRhtCM 19.77:4 ||

children.text: kiṃbhūtaḥ pradhānasiddhaiḥ nityanāthādibhiḥ kalitaḥ racitaḥ // GRhtCM_19.77:5 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? Fashioned — composed — by the foremost <s>Siddhas</s> such as <s>Nityanātha</s> and others. || GRhtCM 19.77:5 ||

children.text: yairmahadbhiḥ siddhaiḥ rasavādo dṛṣṭaste narā jayanti sarvotkarṣeṇa vartante // GRhtCM_19.77:6 //
children.translated_text: Those great <s>Siddhas</s> by whom the science of mercury was seen — those men triumph, that is, they exist in a state of supreme excellence. || GRhtCM 19.77:6 ||
[START GRht 19.78-79]
Born of the lunar dynasty (<s>śītāṃśuvaṃśa</s>), his glory of qualities born from the <s>Haihaya</s> lineage —

children.text: sa jayati śrīmadanaśca kirātanātho rasācāryaḥ // GRht_19.78 //
children.translated_text: the illustrious <s>Madana</s> triumphs — the lord of the <s>Kirātas</s>, the master of the science of mercury. || GRht 19.78 ||
In whom the science of mercury itself descended, the foundation of all auspiciousness,
the cause of supreme welfare — the welfare of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) first [arose through it]. || GRht 19.79 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:

children.text: atha granthakārayitur vaṃśavarṇanam āha śītāṃśuvaṃśetyādi // GRhtCM_19.78-79:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the lineage description of the patron, beginning with 'lunar dynasty' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.78-79:1 ||

children.text: śrīmadano madanābhidho rājā jayati sarvotkarṣeṇa vartate // GRhtCM_19.78-79:2 //
children.translated_text: The illustrious <s>Madana</s> — the king named <s>Madana</s> — triumphs, exists in supreme excellence. || GRhtCM 19.78-79:2 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ kirātanāthaḥ kirātāḥ bhillāsteṣāṃ svāmī // GRhtCM_19.78-79:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what character? The lord of the <s>Kirātas</s> — the <s>Kirātas</s> are tribal people (<s>Bhillas</s>); their ruler. || GRhtCM 19.78-79:3 ||

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ śītāṃśuvaṃśasaṃbhavahaihayakulajanmajanitaguṇamahimā śītāṃśuvaṃśe candravaṃśe saṃbhava utpattiryasya tat evaṃvidhaṃ yat haihayakulaṃ tatra kule janmanā udbhavena janito guṇānāṃ mahimā yena sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_19.78-79:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what character? 'Born of the lunar dynasty, his glory of qualities born from the <s>Haihaya</s> lineage' — born (<s>saṃbhava</s>) in the lunar dynasty (<s>candravṃśa</s>); of such character is the <s>Haihaya</s> lineage — in that lineage, by birth, the glory of virtues was generated in him: so described. || GRhtCM 19.78-79:4 ||

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭo madanaḥ rasācāryaḥ rasavidyājanaka ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.78-79:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what character is <s>Madana</s>? A master of the science of mercury (<s>rasācārya</s>) — meaning the progenitor of the knowledge of mercury. || GRhtCM 19.78-79:5 ||

children.text: atha cāsya kārayitur guṇavarṇanamāha yasyetyādi // GRhtCM_19.78-79:6 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the praise of the patron's qualities, beginning with 'in whom' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.78-79:6 ||

children.text: yasya kārayituḥ śrīmadanasaṃjñasya rasavidyā svayaṃ svarūpatvenāvatīrṇā prādurbhūtā // GRhtCM_19.78-79:7 //
children.translated_text: In this patron named <s>Śrī Madana</s>, the science of mercury itself (<s>svarūpatve</s>) descended — manifested. || GRhtCM 19.78-79:7 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭā rasavidyā sakalamaṅgalādhārā sakalāni ca tāni maṅgalāni uttamarūpāṇi teṣāmādhāraḥ āśrayo yasyāṃ sā // GRhtCM_19.78-79:8 //
children.translated_text: Of what character is this science of mercury? The foundation of all auspiciousness — all the auspicious things — excellent forms — whose support, whose foundation is this [science]. || GRhtCM 19.78-79:8 ||

children.text: eṣā rasavidyā śarīraṃ ajarāmaraṇaṃ ajarāmaraṃ kurute śarīraṃ ca dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ mūlaṃ ataḥ sakalamaṅgalādhāreti yuktam // GRhtCM_19.78-79:9 //
children.translated_text: This science of mercury makes the body free from old age and death — ageless and immortal. And the body is the root of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>. Therefore, 'the foundation of all auspiciousness' is fitting. || GRhtCM 19.78-79:9 ||

children.text: punaḥ rasavidyā śreyase muktau parama utkṛṣṭo hetuḥ kāraṇam // GRhtCM_19.78-79:10 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the science of mercury is the supreme (<s>parama</s>), the most excellent cause (<s>hetu</s>) of liberation (<s>śreyas</s>). || GRhtCM 19.78-79:10 ||

children.text: anayaiva rasavidyayā parameṣṭhino brahmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ prathamaṃ śreyo 'jarāmaraṇarūpaṃ saṃjātam // GRhtCM_19.78-79:11 //
children.translated_text: By this very science of mercury, in <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), first — in the beginning — welfare in the form of freedom from old age and death arose. || GRhtCM 19.78-79:11 ||
[START GRht 19.80]
Therefore, having obtained the high esteem of the <s>Kirāta</s> king, devoted to the work of mercury —
the monk <s>Govinda</s> (<s>Bhikṣu Govinda</s>) composed the treatise called <s>Rasahṛdaya</s> (Heart of Mercury). || GRht 19.80 ||
*Commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>:
The author, indicating the greatness of his own name, says beginning with 'therefore' and so forth. || GRhtCM 19.80:1 ||

children.text: idaṃ rasatantraṃ śāstraṃ viracitavān kṛtavāniti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_19.80:2 //
children.translated_text: This mercury-treatise, this scripture, was composed — was made: this is the purport. || GRhtCM 19.80:2 ||

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ idaṃ tantraṃ rasahṛdayākhyaṃ kiṃ kṛtvā tasmādityādi // GRhtCM_19.80:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what character is this treatise? Called <s>Rasahṛdaya</s> (Heart of Mercury). Having done what? 'Therefore' and so forth — || GRhtCM 19.80:3 ||
